documents.t: Brabo runs the full lifecycle of an application — from brief to deploy — with a team of AI agents working over a real git repository. Creative, PO, Architect, devs per module, Infra, QA, SecOps, Psychologist and Anamnesis. Final authority is yours, and that's not a slogan: it's a property of the architecture.
documents.s: What Brabo Is

documents.t: No action with external effect happens on its own. Terminal command, commit, push, PR, merge, token spend — everything is born as a proposed_action, passes through the project's policy (where deny always beats allow) and only then executes. Two cases even policy can't unlock: merge into a protected branch and changing an agent's instruction. Those are ceilings, not defaults. The agent is not trustworthy by construction, and the system assumes that. It's a language model: it can hallucinate, loop, or ask for something destructive. The limits are structural — an iteration ceiling, a ceiling on fixes per task, a budget that refuses the call, a closed catalog of what Anamnesis is allowed to profile. A prompt is not a guarantee; code is. Everything that happened is recorded and immutable. The event log is append-only, with dense numbering per session. That's what makes the Psychologist's evidence traceable, cost auditable, and backups verifiable. The team improves on its own, with you in the loop. The Psychologist analyzes sessions and proposes hypotheses anchored in real events; Anamnesis derives your proficiency profile and proposes versioned instruction patches. Every patch needs your approval, and reverting creates a new version instead of erasing history.
documents.s: What sets it apart from a code assistant

documents.t: Phases 1 through 26 complete, version v7.0.0. What exists: IAM/RBAC, sessions with an immutable event log, LLM router, metering and budget, an approval pipeline with permissions.json GitProvider for Local, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and generic under a single contract, with capability declared only when proven; idempotent Gitflow bootstrap and adoption of an existing repository with the plan as a gate Full Harness and an agent hierarchy by area — lead as external contact, private internal delegation, consolidated verdict; conversational Creative, PO, Architect and Dev Lead, devs per module in isolated worktrees, QA and SecOps as PR gates, proactive Infra, Psychologist and Anamnesis with a closed loop First-party auth (argon2id, Ed25519 access, refresh rotation with family revocation) — Keycloak is gone entirely; OpenAPI locked by type across controllers, with the reference generated Nine LLM providers over a single OpenAI-compatible base, catalog with manual curation and price frozen at metering time Non-root production images, Kustomize deploy with HPA per Oban queue, graceful shutdown, OpenTelemetry, backup with tested restore Mechanized release pipeline: version computed from the branch's function, approval-ladder, promote/tag-release and backmerge with automatic back-propagation The app: the eight design-handoff screens, a read-only Code tab (tree, file with its own syntax highlighting, search, PR diff, blame and PRs in the API), a Spend tab with two audiences, a tree-shaped timeline, per-project container decided by the Architect, and its C4 diagram in the Overview What came after Phase 15 didn't come from a roadmap — it came from using the product. Program 16–26 was born from the first real navigation of the app, and every finding from live testing sessions became a rule with file:line and a test. The whole chain was proven against a real GitHub — repository adoption, story promotion, a dev agent writing code, a PR opened, a gate judging and the verdict coming back. What doesn't exist yet is stated where it matters, and is meant to be read: the known technical debt is a section, not an omission; the real-execution findings record what remains open by decision — including the two cases where the conclusion was that the path to autonomy doesn't run through loosening policy; the per-project container lifecycle is a declared cut from Phase 25, not an oversight: until it goes live, the terminal policy in ADR 0055 keeps holding as-is.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: An ADR records why something was decided, at the moment it was decided. They are immutable: no ADR is edited after being accepted. When a decision changes, a new ADR is born that supersedes the previous one — that's what happened with 0018, which records the replacement of the NoopDevAgent decided in 0011. Practical consequence: an ADR can describe a state that is no longer current. For the current state, use Business rules, Architecture and the Runbook. For the reasoning, come here. Of the 61, all are accepted except those still waiting for implementation — today 0053, 0054 and 0056, marked proposed in the file itself. 0055 was accepted once it was implemented in Phase F. 0154 and 0155 took the same path: accepted on 2026-09-27, after Phase 30 exercised them, with an "acceptance notes" section naming where the text and the code diverge. No check verifies this sentence: it aged saying 48 when there were already 54, and again 58 when there were already 59, and it's the argument of ADR 0029 (gerar > verificar > lembrar) confirming itself against itself. The decisions are grouped by theme — the product front they decide about — and each ADR appears once, under its main theme. The theme lives in docs/adr/temas.yml, next to this page, and not in the ADR, because an accepted ADR is never edited (ADR 0202); pnpm docs:check fails an ADR without a theme or a row under the wrong section. The phase-by-phase story is in the phase history.
documents.s: Architectural decisions

documents.t: The git provider contract, the repository's birth and adoption, protection and the branch policy. # decision 0001 Format of the GitProvider's normalized contract: nine operations and declared capabilities, validated by a single contract suite 0002 Error normalization: six specific classes, with no common base class — the abstraction was considered and rejected for not paying for itself yet 0003 Automatic retry only on reads, never on mutations, with Full Jitter and 4 attempts 0004 Registration of git credentials: dedicated enum in the database, united with LLM providers only in type 0005 Gitflow bootstrap in six idempotent, resumable steps; skip is success 0028 Branch protection diverges between GitHub and GitLab — and that's why it's not the gate; the gate is the domain 0030 Mechanized branch policy: rule → mechanism, logic in a testable script, backmerge gate, and the cost of reintroducing each cut 0044 Adoption of an existing repository with origin (created|adopted) in both tables, and the PLAN as the gate: the dry-run is the check() from ADR 0005 without run(), the plan lives in the cursor (a snapshot, not a log), and nothing is changed while the decision is null — the Phase 2 runner goes out verbatim to a collaborator and is never filtered, just not called; "divergent protection" stays at the boolean level because that's all the contract exposes (ADR 0028) 0056 The engine works on a remote repository. get_local_repo_path/1 returns unsupported_provider for anything that isn't local, and four consumers stop along with it — the dev agent's worktree, the terminal executor, the diff that QA and SecOps judge, and the project context. The root cause is the asymmetry: the api speaks GitHub over HTTP (created the repo, committed, created the branches) and the engine works on the filesystem, only knowing a local bare repo; a remote project does the conversational half and stops at the construction half. That's what blocks Phase 13b from existing as writes. The git plumbing is already generic — init + remote add + fetch + checkout doesn't care whether the origin is a path or a URL —, so what's missing is a CREDENTIAL. The engine doesn't receive the master key: it asks the api for the working remote over the /internal/* channel that already exists, at the moment it needs it. And the token NEVER enters .git/config, a decision that's a direct consequence of 0055: writing https://x-access-token:TOKEN@… into origin puts the secret in plain text INSIDE the folder where RN-075 just granted the dev agent auto-approved read access — a cat .git/config would return the token, which would travel to the LLM provider on the next turn. Scope protects against reading outward, not against a secret the product placed inside. origin keeps the clean URL and authentication is injected per invocation. The credential is the OWNER's (RN-058), local stays identical, and credential failure fails with origin infra 0139 Promotion is --no-ff, and that rule was broken THREE times (#367, #394, #464) — the third being the very PR that fixed the first two. Investigating found the opposite of a detection gap: the check has existed since 2026-07-27 and fired correctly on both squashed promotions; the 2026-08-25 log says o merge em qa não é merge commit (1 pai) verbatim. What was missing was an ADDRESSEE — a push-triggered workflow failing on a permanent branch has no PR to turn red (the merge already happened), so it leaves a run in the Actions tab that nothing points at, and the repo had zero issues in its whole history. So tag-release gains an avisar job that opens an issue (and comments on the existing one rather than opening a second for the same branch, since a flood of identical issues is the fastest way to teach someone to ignore them), authenticating with github.token and never the PAT — an invalid BRABO_BOT_TOKEN is itself one of the failures it must report, and an alarm depending on what may be broken goes quiet exactly when needed. The rule also extends to dev, NARROWLY: dev takes work by squash on purpose, so "one parent is a defect" would fire on every PR; the defect there is only the PR that carried a NEW EDGE (its head was a merge whose second parent was not already in the base) — #464, whose entire delivery was that edge. Its benign twin, a work PR that pulled dev into itself, has a merge for a head too but its second parent is already in the base. Identifying the producing PR filters by merge_commit_sha, not .[0]: commits/{sha}/pulls returns every associated PR, and since dev is the head of the promotion PR that stays open all cycle, .[0].head.ref would read dev for every work-PR squash and fail the whole repository — an error made and caught against real data before shipping. Disabling squash repo-wide was measured and REFUSED: the six most recent dev merges are single-parent squashes and changelog.mjs runs git log --no-merges, so the fix would tax every work PR and change changelog generation. Prevention stays open and is a product decision: promote.yml performing the --no-ff merge itself would preserve authority while mechanizing method, but needs a ruling on whether a human dispatch counts as "manual merge" 0165 The project's repository is created when the handoff to the Architect is accepted, and execution refuses to start without one. A real v6.1.0 install (AT-092) showed the Architect proposing open_adr_pr three times before any repository existed, the Dev Lead handoff left offered, and POST .../execution/activate answering 201 on a project whose three git tables stayed empty forever. RN-522 had put the trigger on the Dev Lead handoff — AFTER the two agents that write to the repository (the Architect, and the Infra Lead it activates) — and that trigger was skippable, since activating execution never required it. The Architect can only be activated by an accepted handoff addressed to him (from the PO or a manual one), so the trigger moves into the same AcceptHandoffUseCase, before activateAgent, with the same mechanism (local, failure as an event). The Dev Lead acceptance stays as a second, idempotent door — the way out for projects that passed the Architect under the old rule, and the natural retry of a failed provisioning — and its idempotence is proven through both doors against Postgres and the real local provider. Activation without a repository becomes a 409 raised before any side effect, whose message is chosen from the project's handoffs (HandoffRepository.findByProject); the Overview makes the button inert and says why once in text, and the Dev Lead handoff card drops its activation shortcut. Declared: the git-bootstrap session now becomes the project's most recent session during the whole Architect phase 0217 While QA is in its test phase (QA_FASE_DE_TESTE=true), every merge into dev opens and merges the dev → qa promotion by itself, after all checks finish green; the approval ladder waives only that bot-opened pair, and qa → main stays manual
documents.s: Git, repository and branch policy

documents.t: How an agent runs — context, the tool loop, the conversational turn, the session and its states. # decision 0006 Deterministic context assembly: ordered layers, budget per layer, predictable truncation 0007 ToolLoop, tool catalog and ContextManager — the loop with a real LLM 0061 The session's type is creation-time data, and execution stays an event. Every session was born the same, and reaching the Creative agent meant opening it first and DISCOVERING a button in the top bar afterward — that's how the user reported the problem. The risk isn't the new field: it's that the product ALREADY knew how to tell an executing session apart, by derivation, and findActiveExecutionSession looks for the active session that carries execution.activated (that's what makes reactivating land on the session where the dev agents already are, finding #11 of the first dogfooding). Recording a type creates a SECOND source, and two sources diverge — here, over where the dev agents write. Deriving everything from the log doesn't work, and the reason is temporal: the intent exists BEFORE any event, in the click that opens the session, and a creative session nobody activated has no event to derive from. The decision is that the two coexist answering different questions — kind is creation INTENT and immutable, the event is execution STATE, and findActiveExecutionSession does NOT start looking at kind —, under the rule that keeps them from fighting: execution.activated on a consultiva session is 409, never silent conversion. The lock lives in the FUNNEL (AppendSessionEventUseCase), because both the user's route and the engine's /internal/* pass through it, and locking in the use case would leave the other open; and it runs before incrementSeq, so a rejected attempt doesn't consume seq. The field is mandatory at every creation point, including the four internal ones: optional would make the other callers silently inherit the default. The column's DEFAULT is consultiva (the type that can do less) and the BACKFILL is criativa, in the opposite direction and by the argument of 0046 — every existing row predates the distinction, and some are the sessions the dev agents are working in right now. Along with it come the friendly name, which is ADDED to the hashtag and never replaces it (the hashtag is what gets pasted into a URL; a person's name isn't unique), and the session screen's exit, which had none. The accepted price: the question "does this session execute?" now has two places to check 0098 The 413 request entity too large on PRs had its cause inside Brabo's own api, never the LLM provider (comments blaming the provider were wrong). Two ends close together (RN-412): apps/api/src/main.ts never configured Express's body limit (the 100 KB default applied, against the 8 MB Phoenix accepts on the heaviest engine→api leg, POST .../llm-turn) — it gained API_JSON_BODY_LIMIT (default 10 MB); and Engine.Harness.ContextManager.Default had compaction structurally unreachable before the overflow — estimate/1 didn't count toolCalls (they cost ~zero tokens) and the window used only context_window (128k, ~350 KB before compacting). The EFFECTIVE window becomes min(context_window, transport_cap), with the cut always at a ToolLoop iteration boundary so as to never separate an assistant with toolCalls from the tool messages that answer it 0163 The click that starts an agent turn answers on ACCEPTANCE, not when the turn ends, and a refusal stops being silent. Measured on a real v6.1.0 install (AT-089): answering the Criativo's question form took 97.3 s, confirming readiness 97.3 s and confirming the architecture 51.8 s — each click held for the WHOLE turn, because the conversational agent's handle_call only replied to the engine controller's synchronous GenServer.call when the turn's Task finished, and a turn past the 120/180 s ceiling became a 500 on a command that had worked. The same install shows the other half: a "Continue" typed during the Arquiteto's kickoff got {:error, :turno_em_andamento}, which the controller discarded before answering 202 — accepted, never read, no trace. Decision: TurnoAssincrono.iniciar/3 replies :ok as soon as the Task is up (after persisting agent.status: working, never before), generalizing what 0086 did only for the suspended Dev Lead — one mechanism for the six conversational agents, no second path. What the agent refuses BEFORE starting stays synchronous and gets its own status (409 turno_em_andamento/aguardando_aprovacao, 422 sem_regra_de_negocio), passed through by the api with the engine's sentence. The api's success contract does NOT change (201 { ok: true } always meant "accepted"). The screen stops reading "the call resolved" as "the turn ended" and follows the end through the channel plus the log tail. The Dev Lead handoff is HELD while the Arquiteto's closing turn runs, so it still lands after Infra's. Declared: the chat.message recorded before the engine refuses stays in the log (now explained), and an engine restart mid-turn leaves the strip up until "Stop". 0175 The Infra Lead converses through the composer and becomes the SEVENTH conversational agent (AT-141, maintainer's decision). RN-584 had left the question open and priced a "yes": the Infra Lead's whole turn ran INSIDE handle_call/handle_cast — no acceptance reply, no "Stop", no orphan-turn closing, a 180 s call ceiling below the 225 s of a container propose_action (RN-605), and a message sent during the kickoff waited in the process queue for the whole turn. So the turn moved FIRST: kickoff, gate correction and message all start through Engine.Agents.TurnoAssincrono, the same module as the other six — acceptance with working persisted before it, 409 turno_em_andamento, via_for("infra") for "Stop", TurnoOrfao, and toolloop.limit_reached at its own ceiling of 14. The Workflows consolidation runs inside the Task; a gate correction that arrives mid-turn is QUEUED and started when the turn closes, because TurnoAssincrono without from drops it. Only then message/2 gained its own infra clause (the named refusal left) and the web put infra in AGENTES_DE_CHAT, so it is the recipient when it is the most recently activated agent; its handoff keeps its own card (RN-499) and is excluded from the thread card by name. No new external effect: the same four tools, everything with effect still a proposed_action. SOLO_CONVERSATIONAL_AGENTS does not change — the Infra Lead is an area lead 0177 The language agents ANSWER in lives in three places — account, session and project — as an OPEN list of BCP-47 codes, never in users.locale (AT-162, maintainer's decisions in AT-168/AT-169). No enum: every place stores canonical text validated by normalizarIdiomaBcp47 (shape by Intl.getCanonicalLocales, language subtag known to the API's ICU, never und or private use, 35 chars max), because opening the response language needs no resource file and an enum would need a migration per language. Account: users.response_language (NULL is automatic, how every account starts) and the detected_language/detected_language_confirmed_at pair bound by a CHECK — detection only counts once confirmed (written by AT-163). Session: session_language_overrides, keyed by the {session, user} pair, configuration not event. Project: projects.language (AT-243, RN-619). Precedence for a turn with a human author, per PERSON: session override > account choice > confirmed detection > users.locale, so the chain always ends in a language; ResolverIdiomaDaRespostaUseCase returns winner, origin and chain. Declared: no turn changes yet — the transport to the model is AT-164 0179 The agent loop asks the Jev which tool fits each step, and the user's chat model is offered only the menu that is left (AT-238, HS-063, maintainer's decisions in AT-236 and of 2026-09-29). A router of its OWN, ToolRouter, outside the ADR 0041 provider contract and outside the models catalog: it only acts with an OpenRouter chat model and two or more tools, and it only RESTRICTS (policy P3: {the Jev's pick, the previous tool of the same run}; responder_sem_ferramenta or no previous tool leaves the whole catalog). The adoption criterion was lowered from 90% to 80% by the owner, with the numbers in front of him (menu coverage 91%, 85.1–94%; Jev top-1 73%); real validation is AT-239. Any failure — HTTP, timeout (2,000 ms), unexpected JSON, pick outside the options — falls to the whole catalog with a named reason, and the turn never fails because of the Jev. The Jev does not approve, deny or choose a model. Its cost goes to token_usage as the REAL usage.cost with an IMPLICIT price (cost ÷ tokens, price_implicit), on the agent's own actor so it enters the area budget; the kill switch is per workspace (migration 0066); a wrong menu is escaped by repeating the step once with the whole catalog. 0183 A CLOSED session can be REOPENED (AT-071): one exit from the terminal states, only to active, through its own route (POST .../sessions/:id/reopen) and its own state-machine check (canReopen) — the generic transition still refuses closed → active, and closing → active stays forbidden. The row goes back to active with closed_at/termination_reason cleared, and a NEW session.reopened event, in the same seq, keeps the previous closing; no event is edited, kind is untouched. Three PROVISIONAL defaults await the owner: maintainer minimum, no time limit, and a session with execution.activated refused with 409 sessao_com_execucao so findActiveExecutionSession cannot be diverted. The engine's SessionLifecycleWorker ignores a close the reopening already undid; the Psychologist's second automatic analysis stays blocked by alreadyAnalyzed 0184 The owner answers the three PROVISIONAL defaults of ADR 0183 (AT-337): reopening a closed session needs developer — the same role that closes it through the generic transition — instead of maintainer, with viewer still 403; no time limit and the 409 sessao_com_execucao refusal for a session with execution.activated are CONFIRMED. ADR 0183 is not edited 0191 A message that arrives while a conversational agent is mid-turn is no longer refused with 409 turno_em_andamento (AT-267, owner decision 01/10, revising ADR 0163 for MESSAGES only): it joins the agent's QUEUE in TurnoAssincrono — one queue for the seven, the servers only say how a message becomes a turn —, and when the turn ends the pending messages are read TOGETHER, in order, in ONE turn. The state lives in the event log (chat.message_queued/_delivered/_cancelled, all carrying the chat.message id), never in a table: init/1 rebuilds the queue and the boot wakes whoever has one pending. Ceiling of 10 per agent and session (409 fila_de_mensagens_cheia); the person who SENT a pending message can cancel it. The Dev Lead suspended for approval keeps refusing; non-message commands keep turno_em_andamento

documents.t: Which agents exist, what each delivers to whom, delegation inside an area and the handoff between them. # decision 0008 Conversational Creative agent (chat stops being a stateless echo) and the foundation of handoffs 0009 PO, three-level backlog and rule → story → task traceability; readiness becomes a domain validation 0010 Architect: ADRs per real PR, module_map and cross-validation 0014 Proposal-only InfraAgent (proposes via PR, never applies) and a live team panel over Phoenix channels 0015 Real Psychologist: hypotheses with evidence pointing to real events, and light/heavy triage by cost 0016 Anamnesis: a closed catalog of competencies, versioned instruction patches with rollback, and the cap that a patch is never auto-approvable 0022 Evidence that arrives, cost that shows up, analysis that survives a kill; termination cause as a deterministic classification 0023 A catalog that works, dedup that distinguishes who declined, and a queue that survives the round 0038 Area, lead and delegation: an external handoff only addresses a lead or an area-less agent, consolidation into a single artifact without changing the gates' external contract, cascading budget with a sub-cap per delegation, typed failure origin retrofitted across the whole system that already classified failure informally 0046 Story promotion goes back to being the user's: proposed_ready is a boolean and not a new enum value because the enum IS the claimNext gate; promoting reuses TransitionStoryUseCase (dead code from finding #13) and gets 12b's task.became_claimable for free; validation is unified in assertPromotable BEFORE the trigger becomes configurable, otherwise the two modes would be distinct rules with the same name; DIRECTED backfill (existing project goes to auto) because that behavior was already in use; the refusal is recorded before talking to the engine — the reverse of rearm, because the event asserts something about the USER, not about the engine 0053 Dev Lead as an area, and parallelism authorized by the user. Today one dev goes up per module plus an extra on a one-click accept, with no session cap at all: N modules × 2 agents, and spend rises without anyone authorizing it. 14d decides that the LEAD is the one who evaluates how many agents are worth it, and that going over two in the session becomes a proposed_action through the same pipeline as any action with external effect. The Dev Lead didn't exist and was forbidden, along with dynamic areas via module_map and the generic area apparatus — the three cuts fall together because dev area members are one per module_map module, decided by the Architect and different in each project: there's no way to hardcode them like qa and infra. agent_areas/agent_area_members come in per project, with max_parallel default 2, configurable per lead; the gates' external contract doesn't change and Phase 4's suite staying green with no modification is the acceptance criterion. Anamnesis proposes raising the cap when authorization becomes routine, and never raises it on its own — automating that would be the product raising its own spend cap 0068 C4 diagram (Context + Container, Simon Brown) from the Architect, rendered on the Overview. artifact.c4_diagram with no table, same design as artifact.project_image (ADR 0065): the Container level is DERIVED from the current module_map by the use case (never retyped by the model — avoids silent divergence between the diagram and the real map), and only the Context (system name + external actors) comes from the create_c4_diagram tool call. mermaid enters as a new RUNTIME dependency of apps/web (user's decision) — the first of its kind; isolated behind lib/mermaid-render.ts with a dynamic import(), confirmed by vite build that only the entrypoint loads eagerly and Mermaid's heavy chunks (cytoscape.esm 435 KB, katex 258 KB, used only by OTHER diagram types) stay on demand. ADR 0058's locked-down CSP confirmed intact: no Mermaid chunk uses eval/new Function, and style-src 'unsafe-inline' already covered the <style> the SVG might embed 0069 Conditional merge of accepting the handoff with activating execution. The Dev Lead's card had two clicks because they're two deliberately distinct authorizations (RN-137): accepting requires developer, activating requires maintainer because whoever activates becomes session.createdBy and resolves the EFFECTIVE role of the PRs the dev agents open afterward. The request doesn't lower that bar — for someone already maintainer/owner (read from the same useCurrentWorkspaceWithRole() that already authorizes "Auto mode" and Approvals/Settings), the second click protected nothing, just repeated a decision the role already authorized; handleAcceptHandoff now chains into the SAME handleActivateExecution the "Activate execution" button already calls (RN-137), reusing its error handling so as not to confuse "accept failed" with "activation failed after a successful accept". Backend untouched — RequireRole('maintainer') stays the same, it's a decision only in apps/web; developer keeps today's flow, with the two buttons separate 0085 docs/fluxo.yml records the RELATIONSHIPS between agent-team roles — who delivers what to whom — the third piece alongside the catalog (agent-areas.ts, PHASE 18) and the control (docs/gates.yml, ADR 0054), which until now only existed implicitly in prompts and use cases. Contracts per role (mission, typed inputs/outputs, an exit gate referencing gates.yml) with status active/planned/proposto/em-refinamento; a proposto role DECLARES who absorbs it today and the objective criterion for separation, so the target org chart becomes an activation sequence rather than an aspiration. docs/.docmap.yml gains the modelo-de-time rule at warn — the fluxo.yml × gates.yml × agent-areas.ts cross-check test is missing to promote it to block (backlog) 0086 The Dev Lead's execution plan becomes a real proposed_action, revising part of 0053 — the fluxo.yml × code audit found the flow already declared via: proposed_action for this output and the code was never adjusted to match. Direct precedent: 0052 and 0057, but both are triggered by cast and never waited on a synchronous reply — the Dev Lead is the FIRST conversational agent (GenServer.call of up to 180s) to suspend. TurnoAssincrono.tratar_resultado/2 gains a branch: state carrying the :aguardando_aprovacao key (non-nil value, not just present — the Dev Lead carries it since init/1) replies to the from the same way, at the same time, but emits only agent.status: awaiting_approval instead of agent.done. LiveBroadcast.agent_status/4 widened its guard to accept the new status. DevLeadServer subscribes to Engine.Dev.Wake under its own id (the same module QaLeadServer already reuses for QA subagents) and resumes via {:action_settled, ...}; a second user_message during the wait is refused with agent.error (origin politica), no new turn. propose_execution_plan was CONSIDERED and left out of decide.ts's absolute-cap block — unlike parallelize/raise_max_parallel, it can be configured to auto-approve. Accepted, declared gap: with no state table, a restart during the suspension loses the Wake subscription — the decision stays recorded and visible in Approvals, but the Dev Lead doesn't narrate the outcome on its own 0087 The UX Designer enters as the fifth conversational agent (Creative, PO, Architect, Dev Lead and now this one), SOLO with no area, ANTICIPATING the separation trigger docs/fluxo.yml (ADR 0085) had always declared for the role ("when the MANAGED project has its own interface to design") — a conscious decision by the product owner, not a misreading of the criterion. UxDesignerServer mirrors DevLeadServer (cap 14, bounded loop); the kickoff reads the Creative agent's artifact.product_brief, and the design system (design/tokens.css/COMPONENTS.md) is DESCRIBED in the identity — conversational agents have no repository-reading tool. The single tool, propose_prototype, writes artifact.prototipo_navegavel with NO dedicated api use case (unlike project_image/c4_diagram, which need one because their content is DERIVED or shares a domain refusal — neither applies here): shape validation lives in the engine (ArtifactSchemas) and writing goes through the generic append_event_returning. A single artifact, two handoffs over it (to "po" and to "dev-lead") — never a second artifact for "spec-visual", which IS the same prototype. Reuses the half of ADR 0086's design that survives without its suspension: success ends the turn, so as not to duplicate proposals 0088 The Staff (docs/fluxo.yml, camada_decisao_tecnica, status: planned since 0085) gets CODE before its automatic trigger exists — a conscious decision by the product owner, knowing Anamnesis (which would fire the handoff on "recurring systemic problem") is paused (ANAMNESE_ENABLED=false). Sixth solo conversational agent, mirroring the Architect (per-session GenServer, bounded loop, cap 14), with two differences: NO kickoff/1 (there's no session artifact to summarize — it stays idle until the first user_message) and activation via the GENERIC canActivateAgent path (a handoff accepted addressed to "staff"), without entering USER_STARTED_AGENTS — investigation confirmed no domain change was needed in the api, because assertHandoffTargetAllowed only refuses an area subagent, and Staff has no area. The single tool, propose_rfc (problem, options with trade-offs, recommendation, throwaway PoC), writes artifact.rfc_staff DIRECTLY via append_event_returning — the same tableless pattern as emit_insight, not the one for artifact.c4_diagram (0068), because the RFC derives nothing from the api side — and returns the handoff to the Architect in the SAME tool call, no proposed_action (recording a document isn't an external effect). Declared, not hidden: SessionPage.tsx/AGENTES_DE_CHAT were untouched — the same pattern already accepted for infra, a real lead that's also left out of that list 0089 analytics and delivery-metricas (docs/fluxo.yml, status: proposto) become status: active as a report SCRIPT — the product owner's decision to bring forward both roles without waiting for the organic trigger the flow itself already declared. apps/api/scripts/analise-funil.ts is the only new artifact, in the SAME shape as medir-execucao.ts (Phase 13b): pure Drizzle reads, zero writes, no GenServer, no LLM agent — the shape docs/fluxo.yml already prescribed ("never becomes an agent" for delivery-metricas). Measures a real funnel (session → commit → PR → merge, counting SESSIONS per step, only executed actions), real lead time (first commit to first merge, by the execution's updated_at, not the proposal's) and real deployment frequency (merges to a PROTECTED_BRANCHES branch, cross-referenced with the backmerge gate). Three metrics stay DECLARED absent, on purpose: the full product funnel from ideation → commit (sessions has no storyId, RN-230), evidence of adoption per feature (Brabo doesn't instrument what it builds — no path to that today, not just no data), and MTTR/change failure rate (they depend on a real incident signal, the same dependency as secops-runtime/platform) 0092 platform (docs/fluxo.yml, status: planned, activation tied to DEPLOY_ENABLED — which doesn't exist) is born as an on-demand report SCRIPT, neither an LLM agent nor a GenServer: pnpm --filter api relatorio:telemetria [--projeto <uuid>] reads the SAME questions DomainGaugesCollector already collects every METRICS_GAUGE_INTERVAL_MS for the Prometheus scrape — active/closing sessions per project, blocked tasks per project, the last backup's state (always GLOBAL, never per project) — but as a ONE-OFF, standalone read that ends after printing. The SQL queries are replicated, not imported from the collector: its methods are private and end up writing to a Prometheus gauge, with no pure "just the query" half to reuse without coupling a CLI script to an @Injectable's lifecycle. The output always links to what already exists, versioned (dashboards, alerts, runbook, pnpm dev:obs) instead of duplicating it, and declares — never invents — what it does NOT measure: a formal numeric SLO (none defined), postmortem (no real incident) and closed-loop telemetry back into the product (that's what would make platform active, and the trigger is still absent). The role's status: planned and gate_saida: operavel don't change; docs/fluxo.yml just gains a nota on the telemetria-consolidada output saying the manual version is already real 0093 The dbre role (docs/fluxo.yml, ADR 0085) becomes two mechanical scripts, brought forward by the product owner's decision without waiting for the trigger ("real data volume") — neither an LLM agent (there's no natural-language judgment to make) nor a GenServer (there's no long-lived loop or state), because neither deliverable needs that: lint-migracao.ts is STATIC analysis of SQL text (DROP TABLE/TRUNCATE/DROP COLUMN/ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE/ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL with no DEFAULT, pure logic separate from the I/O adapter, same design as pr-police.ts) and relatorio-backup.ts just READS backup_runs with the same logic as DomainGaugesCollector.collectBackup(), formatted as an on-demand report, citing the already-tested restore (docs/runbook.md#restore) instead of re-running it. The linter scans the WHOLE repository (not a PR's diff) and for that reason did NOT go into CI — running it today finds three occurrences in migrations already merged and accepted (0006, 0007, 0034), and a gate that fails the whole repository would fail every PR forever; turning it into a real gate requires scoping it to the diff, as pr-police.ts already does, for when dbre needs to BLOCK and not just opine. plano-de-capacidade/tuning stay a declared GAP: they depend on real data volume, and simulating one without load would be inventing a number (same rule as 0042/0077) 0094 The Dev Lead → dev-<module> delegation becomes DATA in delegations (area: 'dev'), closing finding B1 of the fluxo.yml × code audit and revoking the cut declared in 0053 item 5. Written from the API side, inside AcceptParallelizationUseCase.execute (covers both paths — direct and approved — for free, because both already converge there), unlike QA/Infra which write from the engine side because that's where the subagent produces a verdict. status: 'completed' is REDEFINED for this area: it means "the delegation was EFFECTED" (the agent came up), not "verdict issued" — and parecerArtifactId points at the id of the project's most recent artifact.module_map event (via SessionEventRepository.listByTypeForProject, an existing method, reused without generalizing), the artifact that justified the delegation decision. With no module_map in the project: it does NOT write a fake id, it just logs the unexpected state (RN-059) and moves on — and a RecordDelegationUseCase failure never brings down the activation, which is already a success by the time the write is attempted 0109 Manual handoff to an agent of choice, closing the backlog item ADR 0088 had named precisely ("the generic UI remains in the backlog"). No third handoff state: CreateHandoffUseCase (the only writer of toAgent, ADR 0038) gets an optional actor?: Actor so a human-initiated handoff.offered records {kind:'user'} instead of the default {kind:'agent'} — the existing accept/activation path picks it up unchanged. addressableAgents() (leads ∪ SOLO_CONVERSATIONAL_AGENTS) is stricter than assertHandoffTargetAllowed: a human picking from a dropdown gets a closed catalog, not just "not a subagent". Investigation before coding found ux-designer (ADR 0087) in the exact same reachable-only-by-internal-route situation as the Staff — both entered AGENTES_DE_CHAT together, no engine change needed for either 0182 A handoff OFFER gets a lifecycle: status superseded (migration 0064) with an immutable handoff.superseded event, and at most ONE offered per (project, target) — the same session with no new artifact returns the existing offer, a new artifact or another session replaces it (AT-291/292). Concurrency by a transaction-scoped advisory lock per target, not a partial unique index, so the duplicates already in the table converge WITH an event instead of being rewritten by the migration. Activating an agent by any path supersedes the offers to it; an offer to an agent already active in the project is 409 agente_ja_ativo, whose message is what the model reads; "architecture ready" and AppSec (seAusente, RN-636) stop duplicating offers 0185 ONE click — "I'm ready — the need is validated" — closes readiness, the necessidade-validada gate and the PO acceptance (AT-311/312), revising ADR 0095's SEPARATE click by owner decision. The same POST records readiness.confirmed (marked) and, once the engine accepts the turn, necessity.validated with productBriefId: null (the brief comes from the turn the click starts); the gate stays warn. The Creative→PO offer carrying the brief born after that click is accepted on the internal route that creates it, through the SAME AcceptHandoffUseCase: the same events, the person as actor, and an implicito mark in handoff.accepted/agent.activated. A failed implicit acceptance becomes a durable agent.error; the engine does not change 0186 The PO's handoff to the Architect is accepted by the SYSTEM, without a click, when the backlog is COVERED (at least one business rule and none without a story citing it — the same computeCoverage as the Backlog tab), the repository the accept touches is local with no git credential in the project, and whoever opened the session still has developer (AT-314). It builds on ADR 0165 without editing it: provisioning stays in AcceptHandoffUseCase, before activateAgent; the new use case only reads and decides, and records handoff.accepted with the system actor handoff-auto-accept and the criterion in the payload. A failure after deciding becomes handoff.auto_accept_failed; a remote repository or a git credential still asks for the click 0194 APPROVING the Dev Lead's propose_execution_plan is what activates execution, and accepting the Dev Lead's handoff only brings him in to PLAN (AT-263, owner decision 01/10, revising the ADR 0069 fusion, RN-161). The plan gets an executor in the api that rereads it against the current module_map, writes each task's MODULE and calls the SAME ActivateExecutionUseCase as the button, so the 409 without a repository, the 409 on a consultative session and findActiveExecutionSession stay as they were. Tasks get a module column (migration 0068), assigned by the Dev Lead in the plan (tarefas: [{ taskId, modulo }], AT-274); a task without a module or with a module outside the module_map is refused with a named 400 at proposal time. Only the dev of that module claims it; a task with no module is claimable only when its story has exactly one module 0212 A story can be ARCHIVED, and it is a column — stories.archived_at/archived_reason (migration 0069) — not a new story_status value, because the status is the claim gate and archiving is not a progress step (AT-406, owner decision 03/10 "PO and user"). Every read that DECIDES (backlog, coverage, promotion queue, the Dev Lead plan, claim) filters archived_at IS NULL, and the tasks leave with their story; nothing is deleted, and the new immutable backlog.story_archived/backlog.story_updated events record it. One rule for the PO tool and the Backlog tab: only draft with no task in execution, a named 409 otherwise 0213 The deliverable runs on the user's machine through the Infra's compose, never through a port published by the broker (AT-517, owner decision 11/10; ADR 0130 untouched). The compose builds the APP from the module Dockerfile with FROM = the decided image, on host port ${APP_PORT:-8080}, with a committed .env.example; propose_infra_pr gets a mandatory run payload (command, 1–5 localhost urls, envExample) that the api turns into the versioned artifact.run_instructions. Devs serve /openapi.json and /docs (Swagger from a CDN under network none), QA proves them INSIDE the container, and the Overview card says "declared by Infra, not verified on your machine" — the real docker compose up stays a declared gap

documents.t: The gate registry, the QA and SecOps verdicts and the golden-sets that measure them. # decision 0013 QA and SecOps gates with an immutable-order state machine 0020 Unlocking the gates: gitleaks on the working tree (not just the diff), verdicts validated as an artifact, tool call recovery from text 0021 Closing 4a: an infra gate that really validates, and a panel that tells the truth 0054 Gates as a declarative registry in docs/gates.yml. The flow's gates existed and had been validated by real execution, but were implicit — spread across agent prompt, pure rule, use case, test and CI —, and the Phase 10/13 lesson (metric extracted by script, never handwritten) has no way to apply to what isn't enumerable. This ADR is the top half of 0048: that one made an action's DECISION observable in the event log, this one makes the set ENUMERABLE. Each gate declares `evidencia: event_log 0057 The gate agent waits for approval, the way the dev agent does. ADR 0052 did this for the dev agent; the GATE agents were left out, and nobody noticed because no execution ever reached them — Phase 13b did. In the 6th real execution, qa-automacao ran `ls -la && find … 0067 The gate survives a restart. 0057 already declared "a restart mid-wait loses the loop" as a known limitation, but investigating again found a SECOND window, distinct from suspending on {:awaiting, ...}: DevAgentServer.correct/3 and Dispatcher.run_secops/2 are direct in-memory calls, made AFTER record_gate_verdict had already durably advanced gate_status on the api — a crash between the two locks the PR forever, and it's the EASIEST window to hit, not the rarest. gate_states (schema engine, key {project_id, task_id, gate}) records two steps: in_progress (no verdict recorded yet — no surgical resume of ctx, which doesn't survive a restart, but restarting the area from scratch is safe because the api rejects record_gate_verdict for a gate that's no longer the gate_status owner) and dispatch_pending (verdict already recorded, only the in-process call is missing). Engine.Gates.GateRescuer scans rows stuck for more than 15 min (generously, on purpose — QA's ToolLoop legitimately runs up to 60 iterations, and rescuing too early would duplicate a merely slow cycle), called at boot and by an Oban tick that reschedules itself, reusing the same queue mechanism the rest of the engine already uses. Two guards against duplicating work: a local Registry.lookup before any rescue, and the staleness threshold itself as a second line for what the first doesn't cover (a remote replica, Registry node-local, the same caveat as Engine.Dev.Wake since ADR 0045) — the worst outcome of a residual race is duplicated, cheap work, never inconsistent data 0090 Two "second moments" of the same conceptual design, each decided by the product owner to bring forward a trigger docs/fluxo.yml had already foreseen. The implementavel gate moves from planned to active: QA-strategy stops being a proposto role and becomes the SAME qa-lead, in a second MOMENT, same process (Engine.Gates.QaLeadServer.run_design/3, additive to the usual run/2), a separate deliverable — Engine.Gates.QaEstrategiaAgent (stateless, no Terminal, LIGHT context reusing list_backlog/get_infra_context with no new route) produces artifact.plano_de_teste PRE-DEV. The Dev Lead gains assess_implementability: with no plan yet, it triggers the assessment and returns an error asking for a retry (RN-163); with a plan, it proposes the verdict as a proposed_action, the SAME pattern as propose_execution_plan (0086). appsec (RN-360/361) follows the SAME pattern over secops: Engine.Gates.SecOpsAgentServer.run_design/2, in the same process as PR secops, produces artifact.threat_model (a STRIDE-lite checklist over the story's DESIGN) and creates a handoff to architect, dev-lead and infra. Neither agent EVER suspends — no tool goes through ActionPipeline — and the iteration cap stays at 8 (conversational) on purpose, the same reason as infra-workflows: with no token_budget_micros underneath, raising the cap would multiply the worst case with nothing to contain it. Both are ACTIONABLE, but the automatic trigger (assess_implementability calling appsec's run_design) still doesn't exist — out of scope for this delivery (RN-340/341/360/361) 0091 secops-runtime (docs/fluxo.yml, proposto role of the security layer) brought forward as a report SCRIPT, neither an LLM agent nor a GenServer — a conscious decision by the product owner, even with the declared trigger ("production with real traffic, post DEPLOY_ENABLED + platform active") still not having fired. pnpm --filter api relatorio:seguranca-runtime reads rate_limit_hits (the data ADR 0027's RateLimitGuard already records, including under dev/CI traffic) and produces a bucket ranking (user:<uuid>/ip:<address>, the only two formats ever recorded — no route or reason, which the table never stored) and a time distribution in fixed slices. Automatic incident detection, incident response and postmortem stay OUT — they depend on the same trigger that hasn't fired — and the report lists them in a permanent "not measured" section, with no example incident simulated and no invented number (same principle as ADRs 0041/0042/0077). The retained window is short (DomainGaugesCollector.pruneRateLimit erases hits older than 2 × RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS, 240s by default) and the report declares both windows — CONFIGURED and OBSERVED — never letting the second pass for a longer history than it is 0095 The necessidade-validada gate (docs/fluxo.yml, criativo role, proposto since ADR 0085) closes the LAST wave of the fluxo.yml × code audit (finding B2), with a SEPARATE human confirmation — never the Creative agent self-validating, the anti-pattern already recorded in modelo-de-time.md. A dedicated button in SessionPage.tsx (same pattern as "Confirm architecture ready", RN-160), route POST .../agents/criativo/validate-necessity, ValidateNecessityUseCase writing necessity.validated — enabled only AFTER confirm_readiness has already consolidated artifact.product_brief (can't validate what doesn't exist yet), and it doesn't signal the engine: the Creative→PO handoff already happened inside confirm_readiness itself, so this event is just the record of merit, not an activation trigger. docs/gates.yml gains the gate as active/warn (nothing today CHECKS its passage before letting the PO move on) 0123 Closes ADR 0020's own open finding — the QA gate's semantic step (matching business rule to test) is non-deterministic with a local model, closing on the 10th of 11 runs — with a golden-set of six regression cases run deliberately (mix golden_set.qa) against a REAL local LLM (Ollama), never CI (confirmed blocked: no ollama in workflows, no LLM secret, and the CI's own culture rejects silent allow-failure). Engine.Gates.QaAutomacaoAgent.run/5 is called directly, same as qa_automacao_agent_test.exs, but against the REAL EngineApiClient.Live — which needs the api and engine actually running, and a NEW cross-language System.cmd (Elixir calling pnpm/ts-node) to seed real project/session/model-binding rows the engine test's own isolated engine_test database can't reach. apps/api/scripts/seed-golden-set-qa.ts does its OWN git checkout (the worktree has to live inside projectScopeRoot for decide()'s path-scope cap to ever auto-approve npm test — found empirically) and seeds agent_areas (missing it 404s the first LLM turn's mandatory metering — found empirically too). The :golden_set_qa ExUnit tag is excluded PERMANENTLY, never by binary/service detection, because this machine already runs Ollama continuously and auto-inclusion would fire the suite inside any mix test. A floor.json ratchet (mirroring coverage-floor.ts, >= never >, human-edited only) replaces a binary pass/fail: measured real pass rates were qwen2.5-coder:latest 1–4/6 across four runs (dominant failure: empty terminal command arguments — the same tool-calling unreliability ADR 0020 already found with this model family) versus gpt-oss:20b 4–5/6 across two (4x slower per case) — gpt-oss:20b is the recommended default for any workflow depending on this judgment being trustworthy. CI wiring stays a declared TODO(humano) 0168 The QA Automation golden-set (ADR 0123) starts running in CI on .github/workflows/golden-set-qa.yml, the mold of ADR 0138 — SCHEDULED and WEEKLY (Saturday 01:17 UTC, plus workflow_dispatch), never on pull_request. Two measurements made it possible: AT-067 showed the clock fits a GPU-less ubuntu-latest (refuting the "new infrastructure" half of ADR 0123's sentence) but scored 0/6 by construction under RN-502; AT-076 made the seed bring each case's container up through the broker by the production path, scoring 3/6 twice against the 1/6 floor in 52 and 86 min. Weekly rather than nightly because a run costs 52–86 min and the score VARIES between runs (same total, different cases) — one run a week reads the trend the ratchet floor guards; timeout-minutes: 150 covers the 86 min measured plus the model's variance. The verdict is the test's own floor; the workflow adds only two instrument guards (the score line must exist, and no RN-502 refusal may appear in the event log) and, on failure, prints logs exactly like the RAG job — no issue. api, engine and broker run natively on the runner and only the broker talks to Docker; the image to pre-pull is read from the seed's own constant, so the job can never pull one image while the broker asks for another inside the 30 s control ceiling (RN-604). Declared: the CI broker lacks the compose's five containment layers (what remains is what it accepts), and a PR that edits the workflow does not run it 0192 The test plan is written AFTER the dev agent's delivery, from the delivered code, not at design time (AT-269, owner decision 01/10, the "(b)" exit that contradicts ADR 0090). It becomes the FIRST step of the qa-verificada cycle: QaLeadServer.run_area/3 runs QaEstrategiaAgent.run/6 on the dev's worktree with the files the delivery touched (git diff dev...HEAD), once per TASK (the correction round reuses the plan by taskId), and the plan reaches Automation as INPUT — the verdict rule and the one-verdict contract don't change, and a failed plan never holds the review. The implementavel gate stays (same owner, warn, human approval) and is judged by the Dev Lead on the story and the module_map already in its context: the verdict comes out on the FIRST call, without plan fields. run_design/3, run_qa_estrategia/3 and QaEstrategiaContext go away; artifact.plano_de_teste requires taskId; the iteration cap STAYS at 8, now with the task budget underneath; appsec stays at design time (RN-674) 0207 A gate cycle stalled for more than 2 hours since its last activity is parked with a gate.rescue_parked event and only a human gesture resumes it; the rescuer asks the lead about the TASK, not the project, and leaves alone a cycle with a pending human decision (AT-391, revises 0067). 0214 An open question to the user becomes a pending item with state in the log (artifact.open_question + open_question.answered + a decision_record), declared only by the declare_open_question tool and answered only by the session author; QA gains the needs_user_decision verdict, which does not consume the correction cycle and parks the gate through the ADR 0207 mechanism until the answer; the decision reaches dev-context and the QA cut, and the PO may correct a ready story from an answered question (AT-521, extends 0207, revises part of 0212). 0215 The openQuestionId of a gate verdict must exist in the project and be open (unknown is 404, already answered is 409 with the decision), afeta.regras accepts the exact rule title and stores the id, and dev-context also returns the project's other decisions as decisoesDoProjeto inside the same cap of 10 (AT-526, revises part of 0214). Acceptance criterion still open. 0020 explicitly records that the gates demo is "CLOSED, but NOT DETERMINISTIC" — it depends on the judgment of a local 7B model and doesn't serve as a regression test. 0021 has a section "Acceptance criterion status: NOT CLOSED". Both are honest on purpose; don't read them as finished.
documents.s: Gates, QA and security review

documents.t: The dev agent at work, proposed_action, the terminal policy, path scope, auto mode and the absolute ceilings. # decision 0011 Worktrees per dev agent, git executors and the merge lock: a protected branch is never auto-approvable 0012 Real DevAgent: ToolLoop in the worktree, budget per task, ReportDone requiring a green suite, blocking with diagnosis 0017 Workspace initialization lock, dev agent Monitor and cap inheritance for subagent corrections 0018 NoopDevAgent stops being scaffolding and becomes a permanent execution mode 0019 Unlocking the real DevAgent: writing, terminal, ADR per module and budget per project 0045 Event-driven dev agent rescheduling: outbox (not an in-process call) because it survives a restart between the gate's verdict and the wake; awaiting_gate holds the worktree per AGENT (not per task) until the gate finishes; delivery via PubSub (not Registry, node-local) with the at-most-once limit consciously accepted; the circuit breaker (RN-047) lives in the engine because actor.id of backlog.task_blocked doesn't identify an agent's sequence 0047 Closing Phase 12: validation is a SCRIPT that exits != 0, not a prose script, and evidence is extracted from the database instead of transcribed; runs local and LLM-free for two verified reasons (the fork was never named; gate judgment with a local model has not been deterministic since ADR 0020), and that's declared in the first paragraph, not the footer; the Noop entered the 12b state machine — finding #10 lived on inside the very measurement instrument —, moving it to AgentIo instead of copying it; Phase 10's harvest was written with the gaps as not measured 0048 Two findings revisited: an action's DECISION (created/approved/denied) becomes a domain event with the real actor — the outbox is transport, not memory, and events.md had documented the three since forever without them existing; status in the created payload is what distinguishes a human click from policy auto-approval, the metric Phase 10 couldn't collect. And D5: the cause wasn't the worktree being recycled, it was propose/3 discarding the status and the gate opening with no PR — QA swept the worktree, approved, and the task closed without a single line committed. With the order fixed, D5 dies as a consequence, and worktree-per-task (foreseen by ADR 0045) stops being necessary 0052 The dev agent waits for approval mid-loop, instead of burning iterations. The :pipeline tool pending returned the string proposed_action <id> status pending AS THE RESULT, and the ToolLoop kept going: the agent learned nothing about the command, tried something else, and died at toolloop.limit_reached {iteration: 8, max_iterations: 8} without writing a single line — approvals granted arrived after the loop had run out and were useless. The terminal allowlist doesn't solve it because it's a list of anticipated commands and the model invents commands: with read commands allowed, the same agent got stuck on git branch -a. :awaiting_approval ALREADY existed (Phase 12e, for the pr_open at the end of the task) with all the plumbing ready — outbox event, worker, Wake.deliver, worktree retention —, so what's missing is applying it mid-loop. It does NOT wait by blocking: the ToolLoop runs inside the GenServer callback, and blocking there locks the mailbox that would bring the decision itself 0055 Path scope in the terminal policy. The terminal approval ladder was MEASURED as unworkable: 15 turns, 209,031 input tokens against 4,546 output, 14 actions and ZERO lines written for the task, because almost every turn ended up waiting on a click. Two independent defects explain the "always asks": the agent emits cd <path> && <verb> and cd is in no allow list, and a composite command requires that ALL segments match (decide.ts:201), so the seeded allow is almost never reached; and "Always allow" records the WHOLE literal command, which never matches again because matching is by token prefix — the escape hatch doesn't escape. What the user is asking for, "always, as long as it's inside the project folder", is today inexpressible: only write_file has any notion of path, terminal doesn't. Execution exposed the aggravating factor: /workspace inside the executor IS the Brabo monorepo itself, and the hello-clean dev agent went as far as proposing to read git_executor.ex and context_builder.ex — there's no project boundary, and the reach is bigger than the project. Scope resolves by REALPATH and not by string prefix (a .. would escape), it PERMITS without exempting (network and install still ask; being in the folder doesn't make curl piped to a shell safe), deny still wins first, and outside the scope is require_approval, not deny. It's policy, not isolation: as long as the monorepo is mounted in the container that executes, the boundary depends on the policy getting it right 0102 Revision of ADR 0065, a GLOBAL decision by the product owner (explicitly confirmed after an automatic security warning): git push/PR/deploy (RN-106) and sudo/doas (new) move from unconditional deny to an ABSOLUTE CAP — unconditional require_approval, the same code pattern as the other caps, never auto-approvable by auto mode nor by permissions.json. The "always allow" loophole was closed AT THE SOURCE (ApproveAlwaysActionUseCase refuses to write a pattern for these commands) — without that, the cap would be decorative 0167 Auto mode frees the path-scope ceiling, and only that one. Measured on the owner's install (AT-226, project exp001, mounted with a running container): with the "*": auto_approve wildcard on, 51 terminal commands still asked for approval, 47 only because they cited /work or /tmp — the dev agent runs inside the container and ADR 0055's scope compares against the HOST root. Decided by the product owner: an agent in auto mode runs any terminal command without approval, even outside the project folder. decide() now receives the autonomy's ORIGIN (specific rule or wildcard) from the repository, which still owns the specific-over-wildcard precedence; only a wildcard resolved as auto_approve is auto mode. In auto mode the path-scope ceiling and the require_approval a compound command synthesises for an uncovered segment no longer apply; an ask written in permissions.json, every deny, the external-effect/privileged ceiling (RN-418), protected-branch merge, instruction_patch, parallelism and container_remove stay exactly as they were. The approval card and the agent card say, before the click, what auto mode frees and what still asks. Refuses: translating /work before the scope check, and freeing scope for any specific auto_approve 0189 Auto mode becomes the AUTOPILOT, and the path scope compares against the folder where the command RUNS (AT-259/255/258, owner decision 01/10). ADR 0167 is NOT revoked: the *: auto_approve wildcard approves everything — synthesized compound commands, paths outside the folder, git commit and LOCAL branch creation — except the absolute ceilings (push/PR/merge/deploy, sudo/doas, protected-branch merge, container_remove, instruction_patch, parallelism); deny still wins. A specific auto_approve written by "Always allow" under the wildcard resolves AS the wildcard, so it no longer turns the autopilot off. With a registered running container (container/mounted), the ADR 0055 scope root becomes /work plus the container's /tmp, with the host cwd translated like the engine does; without one it stays the host folder, /tmp outside. The UI shows one list of what the autopilot releases and what it does not, in the three places it is turned on. And "Always allow" records VERB + SUBCOMMAND, one pattern per command segment (AT-257, closing AT-170 and ADR 0055 point 6): verb + flag stays exact, and a unit that would prefix an RN-418 cap (git remote, gh pr) stays exact too. The containment that backs the decision is proved end to end in the broker, and what it does NOT cover is declared 0204 Auto mode releases git_push and pr_open (typed, and the same push/PR through the terminal command), by owner decision of 02/10 (AT-385, RN-713), revising ADR 0102 and RN-689 for push/PR only. ONLY the *: auto_approve wildcard releases them — a specific rule, "Always allow" and permissions.json still do not, and activation keeps seeding only git_commit. Protected-branch merge, deploy, sudo/doas, container_remove, instruction_patch and parallelism stay absolute ceilings; turning the toggle back to manual restores the approval
