And it is precisely that translation that identity makes unnecessary. projectScopeRoot (api) and Engine.Actions.Workspace.workspace_dir/2 (engine) discriminate the mode by the path's leading slash and use the column's value as is. With host == container, both remain correct without a single new line of code — and the terminal scope of ADR 0055, which is derived from that same root, keeps authorizing exactly the folder the user sees.
documents.s: Why IDENTITY ($X:$X), and not a fixed mount point

documents.t: BRABO_PROJECTS_HOST_BASE enters the broker service derived from BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE (which is already a host path by definition — it is what api/engine mount by identity), next to PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT and for the same reason as ADR 0130: the -v of a docker run is resolved by the DAEMON, against the host filesystem, and a path coming from inside the api would mount an empty folder. Containment remains configured in the broker, never asserted by the caller — which is that ADR's real invariant. Nothing consumes this variable yet: whoever resolves a mounted project against that root is the PR that gives a container to the Mounted folder mode. It is born here because the base is born here, and a host variable that appears half a release later is a variable nobody connects to the file that explains it.
documents.s: The broker gains a SECOND root

documents.t: scripts/dev/preflight.mjs now refuses to start when BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE overlaps the Brabo checkout, in both directions (the base contains the checkout; the checkout contains the base), using git rev-parse --show-toplevel. The preflight runs on the HOST. It can answer what the api cannot, and that is why the guard lives there and not in the domain: the api compares against process.cwd(), which is /workspace inside its container, and will never see the real path. The pure logic lives in scripts/dev/base-de-projetos.mjs, its own tested module — preflight.mjs runs await main() at the top, and importing it from a test would start the whole preflight.
documents.s: The /workspace guard, in the place where it is possible

documents.t: What gets better. Creating a mounted project no longer requires a compose edit and a restart of api + engine — it no longer costs every agent turn, terminal socket and in-flight LLM call of the installation. Configuration becomes an act of the OPERATOR, once, and not an act of the user, per project. And the ADR 0055 vector that no api validation reached now has a guard, with a message that explains why nothing else would catch it. Operator action required BEFORE the deploy, and that is why the branch is born breaking/ and the version goes up MAJOR: whoever already uses the mounted mode has the per-project bind-mount lines written by hand in the compose. They keep working — nothing removes them, and nothing in this PR starts refusing a mounted project outside the base (the base rule is a CREATION and CONVERSION rule, and enters in the next PR; the lexical predicate, which runs on every read, does not change). But from here on the supported path is the base, and continuing line by line per project is debt nobody maintains anymore. Declared cost 1: a symlink under the base resolves differently on both sides. A symbolic link inside the base pointing outside it is followed by the kernel INSIDE the container only if the target is also mounted — and it is not. The folder browser refuses to descend into a symlink (and counts how many it skipped, so as not to lie "empty folder"); whoever catches the divergence for real is the disk check at materialization time, as a NAMED failed. It is lexical containment with a known hole, the same one ADR 0055 already declares and for the same reason: resolving realpath would require I/O where the decision needs to be pure. Declared cost 2: code outside the base requires moving the folder. This v1 supports ONE base. Whoever has repositories scattered across several places on disk needs to move the project inside it — and the refusal message says exactly that, instead of suggesting there is a hidden configuration. A second base (or a list) is a product decision not taken before someone asks: each extra root is one more root the folder browser exposes and the broker needs to distinguish. What this ADR does NOT decide. It does not touch caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido nor projectScopeRoot — the requirement that a mounted project be inside the base belongs to the next PR, and deliberately goes to creation/conversion, not to the predicate that runs on every read (otherwise a legacy mounted project, outside the base, would start exploding when READ). It does not change the schema, has no migration, and the CHECK of the (modo, caminho) pair stays intact. And it does not give a container to a mounted project: that is another PR, and it is there that BRABO_PROJECTS_HOST_BASE gains a consumer.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: ADR 0141 decided WHERE a mounted project lives — inside BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, a single base mounted by identity in api and engine — and explicitly left the other half for the next PR: when that folder comes to exist, and who verifies that it works. The requirement that forces the question is the product owner's, and it is literal: se for Pasta montada, o bind-mount deve ser criado APÓS a decisão do arquiteto. Today's code makes that impossible. validarCaminhoDeWorkspaceLocal (project-workspaces-root.ts) runs at project CREATION and asks three disk questions — does the folder exist? is it a directory? can the process write to it? — and refuses with 400 when any of them fails (RN-170/RN-422). Project creation is the FIRST screen of the flow; the Arquiteto's (Architect's) decision (project_image, module_map, module_routing) happens many sessions later. Requiring the folder ready at creation is requiring it before any decision exists. And the problem is neither hypothetical nor aesthetic. It is what separates mounted from being a first-class choice: the creation wizard suggests <base>/<slug do nome>, and a folder suggested by us is, by construction, a folder that does not exist yet. The runner mode already solved exactly this tension, and solved it well (RN-423, ADR 0104): it validates only the LEXICON at creation — absolute, no .., outside system folders, not overlapping the Brabo checkout — and leaves the disk to whoever has authority over it, the CLI connecting on the user's machine. The difference between the two modes was never what counts as a valid path; it was when and who confirms the disk part.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: mounted now validates only the LEXICON plus the base at creation, and the folder is MATERIALIZED when someone with authority over the disk needs it.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: validarExecutionModeEWorkspacePath stops touching the disk in the mounted branch. What it now requires is two things: the same lexical predicate as runner (caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido), which holds forever and therefore also runs on every read; being inside BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE (dentroDaBaseDeProjetos, ADR 0141). The second is not extra rigor: the base is the only folder on the computer that the api and engine containers see, so a path outside it produces exactly the project that hangs later — which is the defect the creation validation exists to prevent. Without a configured base, the mode is not available in this installation, and the refusal says so instead of pretending the path was what was wrong. The project is born, like runner, with workspaceVerifiedAt: null.
documents.s: At creation and conversion: lexicon + base, zero I/O

documents.t: The deferred verification happens again in a single function, mkdir -p plus the usual three disk questions, with the refusal for being outside the base BEFORE the mkdir — otherwise a path written outside the product would make the api create a folder anywhere it reaches. 1. ExecuteContainerStartUseCase — the normal place. When Infra brings up the container of a mounted project, the folder is created, proven writable, and workspace_verified_at is stamped through the same path ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase uses. It is here that the requirement "after the Arquiteto's decision" is fulfilled literally: container_start only exists after there is a decided image. Failing at this is a NAMED failed, never a throw, never a 500 — the same discipline BrokerIndisponivelError/RunnerNaoConectadoError already follow in the same file —, and the lifecycle does not get marked provisioning. Marking provisioning and only then discovering it cannot be written would leave the project_containers row asserting a state that never existed. 2. ConvertProjectExecutionModeUseCase — the exception, and it is declared. Converting a project to mounted has no container step on which to hang the work: it is an isolated act, and right after it MOVES the permissions.json to permissionsFilePath(localNova), which in mounted is projectScopeRoot, which is the user's folder. Moving a file into a folder that does not exist fails. So the conversion materializes at decision time — before the transaction, so a refusal does not leave a transaction open — and becomes a 400 with the message that teaches.
documents.s: materializarWorkspaceMontado, and the two places that call it

documents.t: The base rule does not enter caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido. That predicate runs on EVERY READ, through projectScopeRoot, on a hot path: terminal scope (ADR 0055), permissions.json, Code tab. A LEGACY mounted project — created when the bind-mount was a compose line per project, therefore outside the base — would start exploding with LocalizacaoDeProjetoInvalidaError just by being READ, without anyone having touched it. The base is a creation and conversion rule, where there is someone in front of the screen who can still choose another path. The lexicon is forever. There is a non-regression test for this, and a comment in the function itself saying why.
documents.s: What does NOT change, and it is the easiest regression to cause here

documents.t: mounted keeps writing a NON-null workspace_path — the composed suggestion, <base>/<slug> —, so (execution_mode <> 'container') = (workspace_path IS NOT NULL) remains satisfied byte for byte. Deferring the VERIFICATION never touches the PAIRING invariant: they are different questions, and confusing them would be the shortest path to a migration this ADR does not need.
documents.s: No migration, and the database CHECK stays intact

documents.t: What gets better. The product owner's requirement becomes executable: the folder of a mounted project is created when the container comes up, and not before. The creation wizard can suggest a path — which is the point of mounted becoming a first-class choice — without the suggestion being refused for not existing. And the two modes with a user folder now have the SAME discipline at creation, which makes the difference between them (who confirms the disk) easier to explain than it was when one touched the disk and the other did not. The window between creating and materializing is real, and it is accepted. Between project creation and the container coming up, workspace_path points to a folder that may not exist. Nothing breaks because of it — projectScopeRoot is lexical, permissions.json degrades to EMPTY_PERMISSIONS_FILE (which is require_approval on everything, the safe side) —, but the screen needs to SAY it, and that is what the caveat "the folder is created when the container comes up" does, in the container readiness PR. A screen that shows a path without saying it does not exist yet is a screen asserting what it does not know. The error arrives later, and so it needs to be more explicit. Validation at creation had a virtue: the refusal happened on the screen where the decision was made. Now it can happen in a container_start approved hours later, and so the failed NAMES the variable (BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE=<valor>), the path, the probable cause (owner of the folder on the host — the images run non-root, ADR 0024) and what to do next ("approve container_start again"). A generic failed here would be worse than the old validation. The old message DIED, on purpose. comoMontar taught how to add - <caminho>:<caminho> to the api and engine services of docker-compose.yml. That remedy cost a restart of both services per project — every agent turn, terminal socket and in-flight LLM call of the installation — and ADR 0141 replaced it with a base configured once. Continuing to teach the old remedy would send the user to bring down the installation to solve a problem the base already solves. There is a test assertion about the ABSENCE of that text. workspaceVerifiedAt now has two emitters. It was only runner's (RN-423). Now mounted also stamps it, at materialization. The field keeps meaning exactly the same thing — someone with authority confirmed this path on disk, once —, and still is NOT a heartbeat: reconnecting does not rewrite it, and the screen keeps saying "folder confirmed on <data>", never "up" (RN-468). What changes is the OpenAPI description, which said "container/mounted never fill this field in" and now describes the code. What this ADR does NOT decide. It does not change the branching of ExecuteContainerStartUseCase between broker and runner — giving a container to the mounted mode through the BROKER is another PR, and this one touches the file only to add the materialization above the existing branching. It does not touch caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido, does not touch the CHECK, has no migration, and does not touch Engine.Actions.Workspace.ensure!/4 — the engine's gap in runner mode remains declared and open in CLAUDE.md.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted — 2026-09-04
documents.s: Status

documents.t: In a real execution of the exp001 project (2026-09-04), the thread went far: Gitflow bootstrap, product_brief, module_map and, at 18:00, the Arquiteto (Architect) delivering project_image, module_routing and the C4 diagram. Two ADRs became PRs, three merges went through. And then ten dev tasks hung at once, all with the same outcome: the dev agent's working tree had nowhere to be born. The finding that matters here is not the cause of that specific folder — it is that nothing ordered container before dev agent. No container_start was proposed, and the ten dev agents started anyway, to hang ten times. There was a second defect, quieter, in the same line of the flow. ADR 0134 (RN-492) made the dev agent's terminal command cross engine → api → broker and run INSIDE the real container — when there was one. When there was not, Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor.decisao_de_execucao/1 fell into :caminho_de_sempre, that is, System.cmd inside the engine process — the same process that talks to the database, to the api and to every other project of the installation. The isolation ADR 0134 exists to create held only on the happy path, and its absence did not refuse: it degraded, and degraded silently. This ADR closes both halves.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Engine.Dev.AgentIo.try_claim/2 — the SINGLE claim point — queries Engine.Containers.ProjectContainerLifecycle.running?/1 before calling claim_task/1. Without a REGISTERED running row in project_containers (ADR 0081), the agent falls into :idle, persists and emits dev.blocked_by_container — without calling the api. The predicate already existed: it is the same one TerminalExecutor has queried since ADR 0134. Nothing new was built to answer the question; what changed was who asks it, and when. The equivalent gate in the api (ActivateExecutionUseCase refusing with 400 without ciclo?.status === 'running') is the sibling PR's decision, and it is what gives the warning to the human at the moment of the click. It does not replace this guard, because the claim has a path no route covers: rehydration. Engine.Dev.DevRehydrator does not cast :work; whoever claims after an engine restart is DevAgentServer.init/1 → finish_restart_recovery/1 → try_claim/2, without going through any endpoint. A gate only at the HTTP boundary would let every rehydrated agent go back to work without a container — and the restart is exactly the situation in which nobody is watching. The guard comes before claim_task/1, and not after: claiming only to give it back right away would leave the task marked and without a living owner, which is the state AgentIo.block_task/4 exists to never produce.
documents.s: 1. The guard lives in try_claim, not only at the HTTP boundary

documents.t: The docblock of the {:error, reason} clause of try_claim/2 itself already recorded the reason, written when a permanent agent hang was fixed in Phase 12b: ":idle is the only state from which a wake still rescues". All the guards of handle_info/2 are matched against it — {:wake, :became_claimable} requires :idle, :rearm requires :idle_tripped, {:gate_resolved, …} requires a matching task_id. A :blocked_by_container invented here would be a state from which nothing rescues: the agent would stay stopped forever, recreating the symptom Phase 12b existed to eliminate. Whoever distinguishes "I stopped because the queue emptied" from "I stopped because there is no container" is the EVENT (dev.idle × dev.blocked_by_container), not the status — and the event is durable, in the RN-059 pattern.
documents.s: 2. :idle, and not a new status

documents.t: A read warns nobody. An agent already stopped in :idle would stay stopped until an unrelated event passed nearby — which is, in practice, "until someone reactivates the execution by hand". So RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase publishes: when recording the arrival at running, it adds, in the same transaction, a container.running outbox row. Engine.Outbox.Drain now drains a third aggregate_type ("container", next to "session" and "task"), and Engine.Workers.DevAgentWakeWorker delivers the message to the project's agents. Three choices within that: aggregateType: 'container', and not 'task'. The task aggregate was already drained, and reusing it would cost zero lines in the drain — but the event is not about any task. The graph_projection of ADR 0099 already established that aggregate_type is how different consumers do not race each other; lying about it to save a line of query ages badly. aggregateId is the PROJECT, not the project_containers row: whoever consumes wakes agents by project, and the row may have been recreated. {:wake, :became_claimable}, the message that already existed. Its semantics is already "there may be work now" — the comment of EngineWeb.ExecutionCommandController.acordar/4 uses it exactly like that for execution reactivation, which is also not about a specific task. A new message would require a new handle_info/2 clause in BOTH servers (real and Noop) with a guard identical to the existing one, with no different decision to make. The fan-out is per PROJECT (DevAgentState.list_by_project/1), not per module: the container belongs to the project, and the api has no way of knowing which modules exist on the engine side.
documents.s: 3. The wake comes through the outbox, in its own aggregate

documents.t: decisao_de_execucao/1 gains :recusar_container_ausente, mirroring the :recusar_nao_verificado/:recusar_runner_desconectado that the runner mode already had since ADR 0104. It is the same discipline — "the precondition is missing, so it runs nowhere" — applied to the mode that did not yet have it. mounted enters the same branch: with a running container, it crosses to the broker just like container; without one, it refuses. Treating it differently would be arbitrary after mounted started actually bringing up a container. And the catch-all _ -> :caminho_de_sempre shrinks to what it always should have been alone: nonexistent project or malformed project_id. No execution mode falls into it. The refusal is a normal failed_result, never a crash — the same failure contract as the module's other two refusals.
documents.s: 4. The terminal stops degrading silently

documents.t: A project without a container up stops working, and says why. That is what the decision exists to do, not a side effect. It is also why it can only come in AFTER the changes that give a container to the mounted mode: without them, a mounted project is left with no dev agent at all, with the only way out being the container mode. Every previous dev agent spec now needs a running container. There are nine test files in the engine, and the change was one setup line in each (Engine.DataCase.container_running!/1) — not a module swappable by config. It was a choice: a production seam that existed only so the suite would not fail would make the guard inert precisely where it is exercised. One question, two places that ask it. AgentIo.try_claim/2 and TerminalExecutor.decisao_de_execucao/1 both call the same ProjectContainerLifecycle.running?/1. They are not two derivations: it is one function, with two callers, answering different questions ("can I start?" and "where does this run?"). The wake delivery remains at-most-once, like all of Engine.Dev.Wake (its moduledoc has declared this since Phase 12b). If the agent is momentarily down when the broadcast happens, it stays :idle until the next event — including a manual reactivation of the execution, which delivers the same {:wake, :became_claimable}. REGISTERED running is still not OBSERVED running (RN-486). A container that died from outside still passes this guard; the agent claims, and the failure shows up on the first call to the broker, as a normal command failure. Merging the two would require a network call per claim, and RN-486 is explicit about not merging them.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: ADR 0081 — the project_containers table and the state machine ADR 0134 — the terminal command inside the container; this ADR is what makes it land ADR 0135 — the image gate now applies in all three modes ADR 0137 — mounted/runner bringing up a container on the user's machine RN-502
documents.s: References

documents.t: The broker (ADR 0130) is the only product process that talks to a Docker daemon on the server, and the thing that makes it contained is a single one: it does not accept a container specification. It receives a projectId and one of the five operations, goes to the api to READ the Arquiteto's (Architect's) decision and COMPOSES the image, network, resources and the single mount itself. No path crosses the network — the api sent workspaceDirName and the broker concatenated it with ITS root (PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT). That shape had one root because there was only one place where a project folder could be from the server's point of view: /data/project-workspaces, the folder MANAGED by the product, of the container mode. mounted and runner projects were left out, and the broker refused both at the source with ModoDeExecucaoNaoSuportadoError. ADR 0141 changed the fact of the world that sustained half of that refusal. Every project in the Mounted folder mode now lives under one base (BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE), mounted by identity in api and engine, and therefore reachable by the server's daemon. The broker's refusal was about GEOMETRY — "its code is on a machine I do not see" —, and the geometry of mounted stopped being that. That of runner did not change at all. This opens a question the single-root shape cannot answer: given a segment, against which root does it apply? The obvious temptation is for the api to send the absolute path and the broker to mount it. That would undo ADR 0130 entirely: the containment of a root-equivalent process on the host would again depend on the CALLER being correct, which is the definition of there being no containment. The second temptation is for the broker to guess — use the base when the mode is mounted. That works until the day there is a third place, and until then it hides the decision in an if over an enum the broker does not own.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The broker gains a SECOND root, BRABO_PROJECTS_HOST_BASE, and the api now sends a DISCRIMINATED locator that says against which of the two the segment applies. localizacao: | { tipo: 'gerenciada'; segmento: string } // PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT | { tipo: 'montada'; segmento: string } // BRABO_PROJECTS_HOST_BASE | { tipo: 'indisponivel'; motivo: string } // nenhuma raiz alcança The invariant stays exactly where it was. What crosses the network is still only the half the broker's root does not cover; the api does NOT know where those roots are on the host, and the broker knows nothing about the project. Neither side alone can write an arbitrary path — what changed is that the api now says WHICH root, instead of there being only one and the answer being implicit. Two variables and not one, and no inheritance between them. The managed root is named by workspace_dir_name (UNIQUE) and the base is named by the user. The same name points to different folders in the two, and nothing in the schema prevents the collision — it is the first reason ADR 0141 refused to conflate BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE with PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR, and it holds identically here. That is why BaseDeProjetosNaoConfiguradaError is its OWN class, in the same mold as RaizDeWorkspacesNaoConfiguradaError: origin infra, message naming the variable, no container touched. Falling back to the other root by omission would mount ANOTHER project's folder, and the container would come up — with the wrong code inside, with nothing indicating why. Three variants and not two. indisponivel is not a disguised null: it is the state in which no root of THIS server reaches the folder, and it has two different fixes. A runner project (the folder is on the user's machine — the fix is the brabo-runner, on that side) and a LEGACY mounted project created before the base (the fix is to move the folder). A null would send whoever operates to the wrong place half the time. A folder that IS the base itself falls here too, instead of becoming an empty segment: <raiz>/ would mount the whole base — the folder of all mounted projects — inside a single one's container. The list of modes the broker serves is an ALLOW list, not a deny list (container, mounted). A new mode in the api's enum is born refused, with a message, instead of being born silently accepted and falling into a composition with no root that resolves it. Three barriers over the concatenation, not one. The api refuses what is not under the base (segmentoSobABaseDeProjetos); packages/docker-port refuses the segment that is not relative (segmentoDeProjetoValidado: .., absolute, empty, double slash, NUL); and the result of raiz + segmento still goes through raizDeProjetoValidada before becoming -v, as it always did. Validating the segment and not validating the concatenation would be trusting string arithmetic — and the validation on the broker side exists precisely because it cannot presuppose that the api is correct. Consequence on the api side: the branching of container_start becomes by DESTINATION. container and mounted go to the broker; only runner goes to the runner. And container_stop/container_remove change together, necessarily: bringing up on the server and asking to stop on the user's machine would leave standing, with no way to stop it, what is standing. mounted ELECTS the image, like container. It is not symmetry: it is the only design that works on this side. The broker composes from artifact.project_image, going to FETCH it from the api — an Infra election that was not recorded in that artifact would be inert, and the container would come up with the Arquiteto's image while the payload approved by the human would say something else. It is literally the argument of ADR 0133, applied to a second mode. The runner path can read the current one because there the api SENDS the spec fields through the channel; the artifact is not the source the other side queries.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The Mounted folder mode no longer requires a connected brabo-runner to have a container. It was that requirement that made incoherent the sequence the product owner's plan asks for — choosing mounted at creation, and the container coming up before the dev agents. runner is left alone on the runner path, and that is the design, not a leftover: the broker (and the server) still do not see its folder. container remains the only mode that brings up a container on the server without depending on a base configured by the operator; mounted brings it up on the server when the base is there. Declared cost 1: an installation can have one root and not the other. That is a legitimate state, and each operation says which one is missing instead of both falling into a generic refusal. The price is two error classes where there could be one with a parameter — accepted, because whoever reads the error is whoever needs to know WHICH variable to set. Declared cost 2: the broker now knows a second segment format. gerenciada is a name without /; montada is a relative path, which may have levels. nomeDeWorkspaceValidado (which serves the container's NAME and refuses / on purpose) stops serving to validate a path, and segmentoDeProjetoValidado is born next to it. They are two questions that came to have different answers — "what is the container called" and "where is the folder" — and having them with a single function was what worked while they coincided. What this ADR does NOT decide. It materializes no folder at all (that is the deferred validation, neighboring PR). It does not change the image gate — RN-105 already applies to all three modes since RN-494/ADR 0135. It does not change who PROPOSES container_start: the Infra Lead can still propose it for a project without a connected runner and without a decided image, the gap declared since RN-494. It does not change the count of broker operations: they remain five, and a sixth remains a product decision with an ADR. And it does not publish the broker image on GHCR — the four of ADR 0119 remain four. References 0130 (the broker composes the spec), 0133 (the election must be recorded to have effect), 0137 (the other execution path) and 0141 (the base that made this possible). None of them is edited.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: The runner mode (ADR 0104) exists for code that lives in a user folder WITHOUT a bind-mount to the server, confirmed by a CLI (brabo-runner) running on their machine. Since ADR 0137 (RN-497), that same CLI also brings up a Docker container ON THE USER'S MACHINE, and Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor routes every approved terminal command to the runner whenever the workspace is VERIFIED and the runner is CONNECTED — without checking whether there is any running container. The host-vs-container choice was entirely INTERNAL to the runner (EstadoDoRunner.containerAtivo): with a container up, it ran via docker exec; without one, it silently fell back to the bare HOST, executing the command outside any isolation. That left runner inconsistent with container/mounted, which since ADR 0143 (RN-502) already REFUSE to run a terminal without a registered running container — they never degrade to local System.cmd. For runner, the "local" was the user's own host: the same silent fallback ADR 0143 closed for the other two modes remained open here, outside the server. A second defect, declared since RN-478 and never fixed: the materialization of the dev agent's working tree (Engine.Actions.Workspace.ensure!/4) tried a LOCAL File.mkdir_p!/System.cmd("git", ...), inside the engine process, against a path that only physically exists on the user's machine — the engine process has no bind-mount there at all. The previous fix only improved the MESSAGE of an inevitable failure; the dev agent still had nowhere to work. A third point, found during the investigation: container_start (the action that actually brings up the container, ADR 0130/0133) also served runner, but its payload (imagem/network/resources/rationale — Infra ELECTS a candidate from the Arquiteto's routing) never made sense for that path: the broker never reaches a runner project's folder, so there is no routing to elect against, and the image that comes up is simply the one already decided.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Docker becomes a real prerequisite of the runner mode, with no fallback to the host. The three preconditions runner needs for any command to reach the user's machine — workspace CONFIRMED, runner CONNECTED and container REGISTERED running (ProjectContainerLifecycle.running?/1, the SAME predicate as container/mounted) — live in a single function, Engine.Runners.RunnerReadiness, with two consumers: TerminalExecutor (which already checked the first two) and the new module below. Worktree materialization now happens INSIDE the project's real container, on the user's machine — through the SAME channel that already executes the terminal. Engine.Actions.Workspace.ensure!/4 forks by execution_mode: local for container/mounted (unchanged), via Engine.Actions.Workspace.RunnerGit (new) for runner. RunnerGit does git init/remote add/fetch/checkout, and the equivalents of File.dir?/ls/rm_rf that Engine.Dev.WorktreeManager needs, as normal shell commands, delivered by Engine.Runners.RunnerRouter.exec/5 — never a new mechanism, always after RunnerReadiness.verificar/1 confirms the three preconditions. WorktreeManager (create/3, remove/2, list/1, cleanup_orphans/2) forks by the same criterion, and the periodic job Engine.Dev.WorktreeCleanup now SKIPS (does not fail) a runner project without a runner ready RIGHT NOW, continuing normally for the others. The exec/exec_result protocol gains an optional env field. The authenticated git fetch needs the provider credential (ADR 0056), which can only travel in the child process's environment — never argv, never a file. Since that child process is now born on the user's machine, env (a Record<string,string>) enters the payload the engine dispatches; the runner MERGES that env on top of process.env before the spawn (never replaces it — it would lose PATH) and never passes it to the docker exec path (no env support in packages/docker-port, on purpose — see Consequences) nor prints it in any log. container_start migrates entirely to being exclusive to container/mounted (both through the broker, RN-503). container_start_via_runner is born, a new action type, exclusive to runner. Same caliber as container_start (maintainer, require_approval by default, configurable in permissions.json) — but the schema only has an optional rationale: it elects no candidate at all, it brings up the image already DECIDED (ObterSpecDeContainerUseCase). Engine.Infra.Tools. ProposeContainerStartViaRunner, the Infra Lead's new tool, is intercepted by the InfraLeadServer BEFORE calling propose_action — it LOCALLY queries (Project.get/1 + Engine.Runners.Registry.connected?/1, without HTTP, in the same BEAM process) the execution_mode and the presence of a connected runner, refusing with a named reason instead of proposing blindly.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: A runner project without a running container loses the terminal and the dev agent's worktree until someone proposes and approves container_start_via_runner. Accepted cost, MEASURED against the real precedent: the sibling change for container/mounted (ADR 0143, RN-502) already had the same shape — "now requires where it did not before" — and shipped as feature/, MINOR, without a breaking/ branch. No existing runner project had guaranteed isolation before this delivery (the silent fallback to the host is exactly what is being closed), so there is no prior correct behavior being taken away — only an unsafe behavior ceasing to exist. env only reaches the git fetch when the runner chooses the HOST path. If the runner already has an active container (EstadoDoRunner.containerAtivo), tratarExec routes EVERY exec — including those of RunnerGit — via docker exec, which has no env field (a measured decision of ADR 0130: keep the Docker port with a closed type, with no free -e). A git fetch dispatched in that state silently loses the credential for a private repository. Not solved in this delivery — extending packages/docker-port to accept env would touch BOTH of its consumers (runner and broker) and was out of scope; declared for when the volume of runner projects with a private repository justifies it. RunnerReadiness.verificar/1 runs again on each RunnerGit call (one more query per git/worktree operation) — acceptable because no function of this module is on the hot path (the same rule that already held for Engine.Actions.Workspace.ensure!/4 before this delivery). The gap RN-494 declared for propose_container_start (neither it nor GetInfraContextUseCase restrict by executionMode — the Infra Lead can propose blindly) remains exactly as it was for that tool. The NEW tool (container_start_via_runner) is born without that gap because it is born knowing how to refuse — but that is not retroactive: propose_container_start still cannot distinguish the mode, a separate decision, outside the API/domain scope.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: ADR 0141 created BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE: one base on the host, mounted by identity ($X:$X) in api and engine, where the folders of every project in the Mounted folder mode live. It solved the problem it set out to solve — the per-project bind-mount line in the compose is gone, and with it the restart that killed every in-flight agent turn to onboard ONE project. But it left the variable absent by default, and the consequence of that is the reason this phase exists. Without the variable the api reports projectsBase: null and the creation wizard does not offer the mode (docs/adr/0141-base-unica-dos-projetos-montados.md:68-72). The normal state of a freshly cloned installation is therefore: the only mode that puts the code in a folder the user opens in their editor does not appear on screen. container has no folder they see; runner requires a binary, chmod, pairing and — since ADR 0145 — Docker up on their machine. The product has three execution modes and none of them delivers, without configuration work nobody asked the user to do, the simplest thing they expect: to see the files. A gesture of consent is missing. Choosing where projects will live is a decision of the machine's owner, happens once, and happens on the host — not inside a container, not through the api, not through the web interface. The product already has exactly one place with those three properties: pnpm bootstrap (scripts/dev/bootstrap.sh), the menu that already creates the .env, fixes folder owners and reconfigures Ollama. There is a second fact of the world that changed since ADR 0130 and that this phase cannot ignore. The broker starts under profiles: ["container-broker"] and does not start by default, and the recorded justification is literal (docs/adr/0130-broker-de-container.md:131-135): Nada o chama para escrever ainda; dar acesso ao Docker do host a toda máquina de desenvolvimento em troca de nada seria uma mudança de postura sem contrapartida. The premise of that sentence — "nothing calls it" — stopped being true. ADR 0133 gave container_start a real caller; ADR 0136 added stop and remove; ADR 0134 added exec. And ADR 0144 made mounted bring up a container through the broker. A mounted project in a local compose without the profile on does not end in a configuration error: it ends in BrokerIndisponivelError, after the user has chosen the mode, created the project and talked to the Arquiteto (Architect).
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The proposed path is $HOME/projetos-brabo, always expanded to absolute before being written. ~ remains forbidden, and not by taste: Compose does not expand it on the side that matters, and writing it creates a folder called ~ (.env.example:225-229). Under $HOME because that is what Docker Desktop shares by default — /Users on macOS, the user profile on Windows. A default that requires the user to open Docker's settings before it works is not a default; it is a disguised question. Not $HOME/brabo, because the base cannot be (nor contain) Brabo's own checkout — scripts/dev/preflight.mjs:316 already refuses to start in that case — and whoever clones the product there would fall exactly into the refusal. And not $HOME/brabo-projetos, despite being the most natural name, because .env.example:202 already uses that path as a commented example of PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR — the root of the workspaces the PRODUCT manages. They are different variables with opposite owners, and ADR 0141 refused to conflate them precisely because the collision "breaks in a way that is hard to see": <base>/loja would collide with a container project whose workspace_dir_name was also loja, and the bootstrap would git init inside the other's project (.env.example:231-237). Proposing as default the path the documentation already suggests for the other variable would be walking into that trap through the front door. The name, however, is only the dodge. The protection is mechanism: the script refuses any base that is equal to, contains or is contained in PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR, reusing dentroDe from scripts/dev/base-de-projetos.mjs — the same function that already sustains baseSobrepoeOCheckout. The check applies to the typed path, not only to the default; a well-chosen default only prevents the refusal from being the first thing the user sees. Whoever writes it is scripts/dev/consentir-base.mjs, new, sibling of scripts/dev/base-de-projetos.mjs (which already hosts the pure normalization and overlap logic), called by a menu item of bootstrap.sh. It is not bash, and the two reasons are measured, not aesthetic. The first: bootstrap.sh does not have a helper to write a variable in the .env — garantir_env (scripts/dev/bootstrap.sh:91) only copies .env.example when the file does not exist. The only helper that updates a key in place, preserving comments and appending at the end when it does not exist, is escreverEnv (scripts/dev/preflight.mjs:128). The second, and the decisive one: a menu item cannot ask. Every menu command runs in the background with stdin coming from /dev/null (scripts/dev/bootstrap.sh:770), and the comment above the line explains why — without it, anything that reads stdin steals the user's arrow keys, and a command that waits for an answer hangs without ever showing the question. A consent step written in bash inside the menu would be, by construction, a step that cannot consent. An already present value is never overwritten without confirmation. And without a TTY, the script reports and does nothing — the literal precedent of perguntarUsoDoOllama (scripts/dev/preflight.mjs:208), which without a terminal applies the default and warns instead of hanging. A consent script that "consents" on its own in a CI pipe is the negation of the word. The folder is created with mkdir -p after the user accepts the default or types another path, never before.
documents.s: 1. The default base is $HOME/projetos-brabo, and Node writes it, not bash

documents.t: On macOS and Windows, a folder outside Docker Desktop's sharing list mounts empty or makes docker run fail — and the whole Mounted folder mode depends on that mount. Validation is mandatory, and its form is the verdict: It is proven by mounting, never by reading Docker Desktop's configuration. The test is a docker run --rm -v <base>:/sonda <imagem já presente> ls /sonda. Reading settings.json would be reading the declared intent in an undocumented structure, which changes between versions and between macOS and Windows, and which describes what the user configured — not what the daemon will do. Mounting measures the property. It is the same rule the product already applies to providers: a capability is only declared when proven by execution, never read from official documentation (ADR 0041/0042). Only on macOS and Windows, by process.platform. On Linux there is no sharing list: the check is existence and write permission, and nothing more. This makes the validation the second platform guard of the product — the first is validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux (apps/runner/src/guard.ts:240), which restricts --dir to $HOME only on Linux. The two are symmetric in principle: each restricts only where the restriction means something. It is worth recording that today no dev script detects the platform — neither bootstrap.sh nor preflight.mjs call uname or read process.platform —, so this ADR introduces the pattern, and that is why it is written here instead of becoming an ownerless if. Base outside the list: refusal with an actionable message, naming the tested path and where to add it (Docker Desktop → Settings → Resources → File sharing). It never writes the variable, never mounts silently. A base accepted and not shared produces a project the api accepts, creates and shows — and whose container comes up with the folder empty, far from the screen where the choice was made. It is the same lesson as RN-170, and the reason the refusal comes before the write.
documents.s: 2. Docker Desktop sharing is proven by MOUNTING

documents.t: Verdict: it leaves in docker/docker-compose.yml; it remains under profiles: ["container-broker"] in docker/docker-compose.prod.yml. The original justification (docs/adr/0130-broker-de-container.md:131-135, quoted in the Context) has two halves, and only the second survives. "Nothing calls it to write yet" is false since ADRs 0133/0134/0136 — the broker has four real callers. And "in exchange for nothing" stopped describing the trade: with this ADR making mounted the local default (point 4) and ADR 0144 making mounted come up through the broker, the disabled profile becomes what separates the default mode from ending in BrokerIndisponivelError. The counterpart exists, and it is the common path. What sustains the local↔production asymmetry is what the socket means on each side. Whoever runs pnpm dev already has the Docker socket — they are running docker compose, with the host's own daemon. The broker receiving it grants nothing the operator does not already have; the marginal surface is the broker's own HTTP, which publishes no port (docker/docker-compose.yml:486-487), lives on an internal: true network only the api reaches, and compares BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN in constant time. In production the calculation is the opposite: the socket is a real privilege boundary, the operator is not the developer, and nothing in this phase changes the default mode of a production installation. That is why the profile stays there. The five containment layers are not touched (docs/adr/0130-broker-de-container.md:171-176). This ADR changes when the broker runs, never what it accepts: it still receives a projectId and one of the five operations, still goes to the api to read the Arquiteto's decision, and still has no parameter at all where one could write privileged, cap_add, network: host or a free -v. Containment was never the profile. DOCKER_GID/group_add remains the fragile environmental point, and it now applies to every development machine instead of only to whoever turned on the profile — see Consequences.
documents.s: 3. The broker leaves profiles in the LOCAL compose, and only there

documents.t: Base present: mounted preselected, with the path suggested as <base>/<slug> and editable. Base absent (projectsBase: null): mounted is not offered and container remains the default. Neither half is a new rule. "Do not offer without a base" is RN-500 and docs/adr/0141-base-unica-dos-projetos-montados.md:68-72; "suggest <base>/<slug>" is RN-501 and ADR 0142, which deferred disk validation precisely so the wizard could propose a path that does not exist yet. What this ADR records is that neither was ever implemented on the client: GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/projects-base has no caller at all in the web, and the mode's card is offered unconditionally. The phase makes them true; it does not invent them. What is new is the preselection. It revises the default of ADR 0072, where container is "the normal one" and the local mode is an escape hatch — and revises it only for the local installation, where the base was consented by a human on the host. The projectExecutionModeEnum enum does not change, no new mode is born, and conversion between modes (ADR 0111) stays identical.
documents.s: 4. With a configured base, mounted is the wizard's default

documents.t: scripts/dev/consentir-base.mjs lives in the repository, enters the diff, goes through review and is the same file for everyone. Never generated dynamically by the api, never downloaded at runtime. It is the same supply chain that already pins every third-party action by commit SHA and verifies every downloaded binary with sha256sum -c: a script that configures the user's host, creates a folder and writes to the .env is precisely the artifact whose provenance needs to be auditable. A script generated by the api would be code that runs on the user's machine and that nobody reviewed, delivered through a channel whose integrity the product does not verify. Explicit corollary: the api gains no route that emits a host script. The GET /runner-releases/binary proxy that already exists is not a precedent for that — it serves an already published artifact from GitHub Releases, it does not generate one; and the absence of a signature on that path is exactly BRB-005, an open backlog item, not a pattern to imitate.
documents.s: 5. The consent script is versioned in the repository

documents.t: The user who clones Brabo and runs pnpm bootstrap ends up with a consented base, validated against the Docker they really have, and with the wizard offering by default the mode that puts the code in a folder they open in the editor. Sessions 2, 3 and 4 of this phase build, in that order, the bootstrap step, the wizard behavior and the profile change. What this ADR does NOT touch. decide.ts and the absolute ceilings remain identical — nothing here is an agent action. proposed_action remains the origin of every external effect. The immutability of the event log is not touched. The image gate applies to all three modes as ADR 0135 left it, and a mounted project without a decided artifact.project_image still answers 409 in the Code tab. The broker still has five operations and the specification computed, never accepted (ADR 0128/0130) — a sixth operation remains a product decision with its own ADR. Declared cost 1: DOCKER_GID now matters for everyone. While the broker only started under a profile, a wrong group_add affected whoever had turned on the profile on purpose. Now it starts by default in the local compose, and a wrong GID becomes a socket permission error for any developer. The default ${DOCKER_GID:-999} is right in many Linux distributions and wrong in others; session 4 should report this in preflight.mjs, together with the base state, instead of letting the failure appear only when someone proposes container_start. Declared cost 2: a single base, and it is browsable. ADR 0141 already declared both, and this ADR inherits them without improving them: a symlink under the base pointing outside resolves differently on the two sides, and code outside the base requires moving the folder. .env.example:239-241 already instructs choosing a dedicated folder — everything under the base becomes reachable from inside the product's containers —, and the consent step's message repeats that instruction instead of presuming it was read. Declared cost 3: the sharing probe costs one docker run. It runs once, at the consent gesture, and reuses an image already present so as not to pull from the network. If there is no local image at all, the step says so and asks the user to run pnpm dev once first — it never downloads an image on its own in order to test. Assumed gaps, with origin. The git credential is still discarded on the docker exec path in runner mode (apps/runner/src/index.ts:318-320; the Docker port has no env field, by the design of ADR 0130) — this phase does not close it. A symlink from inside the project pointing outside is still not detected by decide(), which is pure and does no I/O (docs/adr/0055-escopo-de-caminho-na-politica-de-terminal.md:9-15); apps/runner/src/guard.ts:9-31 remains best-effort by declared invariant. BRB-005 (signature of published artifacts) and BRB-031 (manual chmod +x) remain open: this phase touches them and does not solve them. Windows stays off the tested path. The sharing probe runs on Windows because process.platform includes it, but the product is still exercised only on Linux and macOS (.env.example:198-201), and nothing in this phase changes that. References 0130 (the profile and the five layers), 0141 (the base this ADR now consents), 0142 (the deferred validation that makes the suggestion possible), 0144 (mounted comes up through the broker) and 0072 (the default point 4 revises for the local installation). None of them is edited. 0147 is this phase's sibling and decides the other half: the local agent and its capabilities.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: brabo-runner (ADR 0104/0105) was born for a single thing: executing, on the user's machine, a command already approved by the proposed_action pipeline. Since then it has accumulated functions without the protocol saying anything about it — interactive PTY (apps/runner/src/pty.ts), folder browsing (apps/runner/src/fs-browser.ts), and since ADR 0137 the lifecycle of a Docker container ON THE USER'S MACHINE. PHASE 28 wants to add one more: a mirror, which copies the agents' work to a folder the user chose, outside the mounted base. The temptation is a second binary. It pays off badly: it would be two installations, two authentication models, two revocations, and two things for the user to stop when they wanted to stop. And the product already has the live process on the user's machine — the problem is not a lack of an agent, it is that the current agent cannot say what it knows how to do. Today the join is mute on both sides. The runner sends empty params — socket.channel(\terminal:${projectId}`, {}) (apps/runner/src/channel.ts:304) — and the server literally ignores them: def join("terminal:" <> project_id, _params, socket) (apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel.ex:99). All identity comes from the ticket: the role (:runneror:web) comes from the kind (terminal_channel.ex:110, papel_do_kind/1), and the server has no way of knowing whether the binary on the other side is a version that understands mirror_syncor one that will silently ignore the message. The only data the runner declares about itself is theworkspace_confirm pushed after the join (apps/runner/src/index.ts:530`). An agent that gains capabilities without negotiating them degrades in the worst possible way: the message arrives, the handler does not exist, and nothing happens — no error, no log, nobody knowing the mirror never ran.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: One local agent, with capabilities declared in the join and granted by the server. Three capabilities to start: exec, pty, espelho.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The runner declares in the place that is empty today: the join params (channel.ts:304). The server grants in autorizar_por_papel/2 (terminal_channel.ex:110-138) — the same point that already builds socket.assigns with :role, :pending_execs and :open_pty_refs —, computing the intersection between what the runner declared and what the project's execution_mode requires. The granted set lives in socket.assigns, never in a table. It is the same reasoning that keeps containerAtivo on the client side (apps/runner/src/index.ts:270-277: "a decisão é INTERNA ao runner, o engine não sabe disso e não precisa saber") and that makes the :global entry of Engine.Runners.Registry die together with the pid: a capability is a property of that connection, not of the project nor of the user. A table would create the possibility of the database asserting that a runner knows how to do something the process connected now does not. A required and undeclared capability refuses the join. The runner already treats JoinRecusadoError as fatal without retry (index.ts:725-732, with the comment that explains why: "Recusa não é transitória… encerra com mensagem clara, SEM laço automático"), and it is exactly the right shape — a runner too old for the project should not stay in backoff retrying with the same binary. It is also where the Registry already refuses the second runner of the same project (terminal_channel.ex:126-135), so the capability refusal is born next to a refusal the user already knows. Why in the join and not in a push afterwards, like workspace_confirm. That one talks about the workspace, which changes between executions and is confirmed by the runner that has authority over the disk (RN-423). Capability talks about the binary, which is fixed at the instant of the connection. Declaring after the join would mean a window in which the server has already accepted the connection and does not yet know what it knows how to do — and it is in that window that the first message arrives.
documents.s: 1. Where it is declared and where it is granted

documents.t: apps/runner/src/espelho-guard.ts (new), sibling of guard.ts, not an extension of it. It reuses realpathMaisProximo and the lexical-then-realpath double pass of validarCwdDentroDaRaiz (guard.ts:134-170) — the second pass is what today catches a symlink in a middle segment, with the TOCTOU caveat already written there. It refuses three things: a symlink that escapes the destination; a destination that contains the workspace; a destination inside the workspace. The last two are the same loop, in opposite directions: with the identity bind of ADR 0141, writing the mirror inside the origin makes the mirror copy the mirror itself. One direction only — workspace → destination. Never --delete, never unlink. A file deleted in the workspace remains in the destination. That is a decision, not carelessness: the user's folder is not a replica, it is an accumulation — and an agent that deletes a file in someone's personal folder because of a git clean on the other side is exactly the kind of surprise the whole product exists not to produce.
documents.s: 2. Mirror: one direction, never deletes, its own scope

documents.t: Engine.Runners.RunnerReadiness stays byte for byte as it is (apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/runner_readiness.ex:44-61), with its two usual consumers (TerminalExecutor and Engine.Actions.Workspace.RunnerGit). The mirror gains its own predicate, with the two preconditions it actually needs — workspace confirmed and runner connected — and never a RunnerReadiness with a parameter. A shared function with a "skip container" flag is precisely the mechanism by which the third precondition falls by accident for exec in a future refactor, and ADR 0145 exists so that third precondition does not fall. Why the mirror legitimately does not need it: the third exists because a command without a container fell onto the HOST silently (ADR 0145) — there were two possible executions and the wrong one was invisible. The mirror has no such ambiguity: it is a file copy on the user's machine by definition, with no container to fall from. Requiring Docker there would be importing a precondition without the defect that justifies it, and the cost would be real — the mirror is precisely the capability that must work for whoever does not want Docker.
documents.s: 3. The mirror does not require Docker

documents.t: The destination is per project, declared by the user, and travels to the runner inside the capability granted in the join. The runner refuses mirror_sync for a destination not granted to it in that connection. Never a global configuration in the runner, never an environment variable: a global destination would make project B's artifact land in project A's folder, and the user would find out from the content, not from an error.
documents.s: 4. Consent per project and per destination

documents.t: User level, always: systemd --user on Linux, LaunchAgent on macOS. Never a system service, never root. The runner runs with the user's privileges by design — guard.ts:9-31 declares that as the premise of the whole guard ("O runner roda NA máquina do usuário, com os privilégios DELE") — and a root service would break the invariant on which the three real boundaries of that docblock rest. Subcommands brabo-runner service install | uninstall | status. Removal is complete: unit file, brabo-runner.config.json and brabo-runner-device-key.jwk.json. The precedent is zero: there is no mention of systemd, launchd or LaunchAgent in apps/runner/; the model today is foreground, terminated by SIGINT/SIGTERM (index.ts:709-717). Windows stays out of scope, declared — the build matrix already produces the binary (ADR 0112), but a user service on Windows is a third mechanism, not a variation of the two. Desired side effect: BRB-031 (the manual chmod +x left over from ADR 0118) dies if installation comes from the versioned bootstrap of ADR 0146.
documents.s: 5. User service

documents.t: Revocation exists: DELETE /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys/:deviceKeyId (apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/runner-device-keys.controller.ts:82-83, developer, 204, idempotent). But there is no way to see what is being revoked. The controller's docblock (:39-40) declares the cut as "sem a visão de maintainer (listar/revogar de qualquer usuário) que o PAT tem" — and the real cut is bigger than it says. PersonalAccessTokensController has five routes: @Post(), @Get() and @Delete(':tokenId') for the user themselves (developer), plus @Get('all') and @Delete(':tokenId/admin') for maintainer (personal-access-tokens.controller.ts:63,86,97,113,127). The device key controller has two: @Post() and @Delete(':deviceKeyId'). It is not only the maintainer view that is missing — the owner's own listing is missing. Nobody revokes what they cannot see, and an orphan key (tab closed in the middle of the ADR 0118 flow) is today invisible and permanent. The ADR closes it with @Get() in the same shape the PAT already has, role developer. The maintainer view remains out of scope, now by decision and not by omission. Second hole, of the same size: revoking today only prevents a new ticket. An already connected runner keeps the channel until it drops on its own, with the key revoked. Revocation now brings down the live connection — Engine.Runners.Registry.whereis/1 (apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/registry.ex:45) already delivers the pid, and no new mechanism is needed to reach it.
documents.s: 6. Revocation stops being blind, and starts reaching the live connection

documents.t: The runner pushes the state on the channel, in the same shape as workspace_confirm (index.ts:530) — the only precedent of the runner telling something about itself. Stored together with the project's other runner facts, not in the event log: it is connection telemetry, not a session domain event, and session_events.session_id is NOT NULL. It is the same reasoning that made rag_searches become a table instead of an event (RN-479): when what one wants to measure has no session, the event log is the wrong place. Three fields — last sync, count, last error — and "never looked" never collapses into "looked and found nothing", the three states of RN-088. A mirror that never ran and a mirror that ran and copied nothing are different situations, and the screen needs to be able to say which of the two.
documents.s: 7. Visible state

documents.t: The engine pushes mirror_sync at named moments — end of an agent turn, commit. Never fs.watch. A watcher is unbounded work triggered by anything: by a dependency install, by a build, and — worse — by the mirror's own writes, which is a loop. Besides, it would run continuously on the user's machine without anyone having asked, which is the opposite of what "local agent" should mean.
documents.s: 8. Trigger by event, never a watcher

documents.t: Configuration consent is not action approval, and the mirror stays on the configuration side. The mirror's write does not go through proposed_action: it is not an agent asking to act, it is the system writing to a path the user declared when configuring the project. The opposite — syncing via a terminal command — would fall into ADR 0055's path scope, would become a queue of routine approvals and would erode precisely the ceiling that gives meaning to the click: a queue in which almost everything is routine trains the person to approve without reading. Invariants this ADR does not touch, and declares it does not touch: decide.ts and the absolute ceilings; proposed_action as the origin of every external agent effect; the immutability of the event log; the image gate in the three modes (ADR 0135); the five operations and the computed spec of the broker (ADR 0128/0130). An old runner connected to a project that requires espelho stops connecting. It is an explicit refusal in the join, with a message — not silent degradation. The cost is real: updating the binary becomes a prerequisite for using the new capability, and whoever installed through the ADR 0118 flow has no automatic update (BRB-005/BRB-031 touch the same point). The mirror destination accumulates. Without --delete, a file removed in the workspace remains there forever, and no automatic mechanism cleans it. It is the direct price of "never deletes in the user's folder", and the alternative is worse. Assumed gaps, not closed here: git credential discarded when the exec routes through docker exec — apps/runner/src/index.ts:311-320; packages/docker-port has no env field, on purpose (ADR 0130), and ADR 0145 already declared the cost; a symlink from inside the project pointing outside is not detected by the policy decision (ADR 0055), and guard.ts:9-31 is best-effort by invariant — espelho-guard.ts inherits the same TOCTOU caveat; exclusivity by {project_id, machine_id} remains deferred (ADR 0137), so the same project on two machines remains one runner at a time through the Registry, not one identity per machine; BRB-005: neither the images nor the runner binaries are signed. A local agent that gains the ability to write outside the base makes the binary's provenance more important, not less. Sibling of this phase: ADR 0146 decides the base consented at bootstrap and mounted as the local default. The two split like this: 0146 covers the folder the bind reaches, this one covers the destination it does not reach.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Every artifact the agents produce — the Criativo's (Creative's) brief, the PO's business rules, the Arquiteto's (Architect's) C4 diagram and module routing, the decisions of the six conversational agents — lives exclusively in the event log. Engine.Harness.Tools.EmitArtifact (apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/emit_artifact.ex:3-5) is explicit: "não há tabela de artefatos". The artifact IS the artifact.<tipo> event, immutable, with an author and a seq. That is the right decision for the SOURCE, and it is not touched here. The problem is another: that memory never reaches any place a person opens. It is readable through the session timeline, one line at a time, inside the product. Whoever opens the project folder in the editor — which is where the code will be — finds nothing of the reasoning that produced that code. The hole got bigger with the decision to defer git (deferred provisioning, in its own PR): between the project's creation and the Arquiteto's handoff to the Dev Lead, the project exists without any repository. In that interval, everything the product has accumulated about the project is in database rows, and the user's folder is empty. There is an exact precedent in the product to solve this, and it has already been discussed and accepted: the Neo4j graph (ADR 0099/ADR 0101), which is declaredly memory derived from the event log — never a source, able to be discarded and rebuilt. GraphProjector (apps/api/src/application/graph-projection/graph-projector.ts) drains outbox_events under its own aggregate_type and writes to an external destination, degrading without ever bringing down whoever feeds it. The question of this decision is not whether the folder should exist — the product owner asked, literally, "criar apenas uma pasta por ora chamada docs, onde os artefatos estarão de cada um dos agentes". It is with what mechanism, and what that requires guaranteeing.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The docs/ folder is a PROJECTION of the event log, in the same strict sense ADR 0101 gave the graph. The source remains the event; the folder can be deleted entirely and rebuilt; and nothing in the product reads from it to decide anything. It exists to be opened by a person. Everything else follows from that.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: ArtifactProjector (apps/api/src/application/artifact-projection/artifact-projector.ts) copies the shape that already solved this problem: its own poller (setInterval with .unref(), cleaned in onModuleDestroy), a public drainOnce() independent of the timer (it is the tests' entry point), a draining flag against overlapping cycles, a batch of 50, and markProcessed only after success. It is not code reuse, it is design reuse — the two projectors write to destinations with nothing in common. Copying the shape is what makes a reader who knows one understand the other without rereading.
documents.s: 1. The mechanism is that of GraphProjector, piece by piece

documents.t: AppendSessionEventUseCase writes a third outbox row, in the SAME transaction, for the types in ARTIFACT_PROJECTABLE_EVENT_TYPES. The aggregate_type is new for the same reason as the graph's (documented in domain/graph/graph-projection-events.ts:7-26): Engine.Outbox.Drain.run_once/0 only drains session, task and container, and the 'session' row every event already has is marked processed_at by it every ~2s. Reading the same aggregate_type would be racing the engine's drain and losing almost always. One deliberate difference relative to the graph: the aggregateId is the project, not the session. The folder belongs to the project, and the source event only carries sessionId — recording the projectId here spares the projector a query per artifact to discover something the use case already had in hand.
documents.s: 2. Its own aggregate_type, artifact_projection

documents.t: ARTIFACT_PROJECTABLE_EVENT_TYPES (apps/api/src/domain/artifacts/artifact-projection-events.ts) is an allow list, not a deny list: a new artifact type is born outside the projection and enters when someone decides it is a document — instead of appearing on its own in a folder the user reads. Left out are qa_verdict, secops_verdict, task_blocked and infra_delegation_files. They are operational outcomes, not product documents: a gate verdict per task, in a project with dozens of tasks, would fill docs/qa-lead/ with files nobody opens, and the folder would lose the property that makes it useful — fitting in one glance. They remain in the event log, which is the source, and remain in the timeline.
documents.s: 3. An ALLOW list, and four types deliberately out

documents.t: The layout is docs/<agente>/<arquivo>.md. Browsing the folder answers "what did the Arquiteto produce?" without opening anything. The four versioned types (module_map, module_routing, project_image, c4_diagram — the ones read by reduction to the highest version, see obter-container-do-projeto.use-case.ts:22-25) always write the same file, overwriting: the folder shows the CURRENT one, and the history remains whole in the event log. Projecting them as a file per version would produce c4-diagram-v1.md, c4-diagram-v2.md and would make whoever opens it have to figure out which one holds — exactly the work the reduction by version exists to spare. The others are append-only by nature (a decision does not replace the previous one: both happened) and each becomes its own file, with the event's seq in the name. The seq is gapless per session and already orders the event log, so it is the tie-break that requires no new state — and without it two artifacts of the same type with the same title would generate the same file, and the second would erase the first: the only way this projection could lose information the source has.
documents.s: 4. Per agent, and the versioned one overwrites

documents.t: The file name is derived from the title the model wrote — untrusted input in every sense of the term. The defense is not escaping what came, it is deriving a new name from a closed alphabet: slugDeArquivo has no way back in which a separator survives, and returns null when nothing is left (an empty name would collide with all other empty names). FsArtifactFileStore checks again, with relative(), before opening the file. It is not paranoia: the two answer different questions — the first is "what name do I derive from this", the second is "what am I actually going to open". Trusting only the first would make the security of this write depend on no future slug change ever letting a separator through, which is precisely the form of containment ADR 0130 rejects on principle: the one that depends on the caller being correct.
documents.s: 5. Two barriers against the filesystem, and the second is not redundant

documents.t: pastaDeArtefatosDoProjeto (apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts) is a sibling of permissionsFilePath and makes the same detour, for the same physical reason: whoever writes is the api, from inside its container, and a runner project is deliberately without a bind-mount. The runner's channel (exec/exec_result) only carries COMMANDS — there is no primitive to write content to a file —, so not even delegating the write would solve it without inventing a new mechanism.
documents.s: 6. In runner mode, the folder detours to the managed root

documents.t: And it is not an omission. proposed_action is the origin of every external effect of an agent asking to act. Here there is no agent asking for anything: the artifact has already been emitted and is already in the event log when this class runs. What happens afterwards is the system materializing, in a derived path, a readable copy of something that is already fact. Making the projection go through the approval queue would have the opposite effect of the one intended: it would fill the queue with routine decisions — one per artifact — and would erode precisely the ceiling that gives meaning to the click on the actions that are external effects.
documents.s: 7. The write does NOT go through proposed_action

documents.t: The user now has, in the project folder, a docs/ folder organized by agent with the reasoning that produced the code. It appears before git exists (the deferred provisioning), which is precisely the interval in which today there is nothing on disk. The projection never brings down the source. No throw escapes drainOnce: each item fails in isolation, is logged and stays processed_at IS NULL for the next cycle. A full disk, denied permission or unreachable folder cannot prevent an artifact from being EMITTED. outbox_events has neither attempts nor a dead-letter — the retry is implicit and infinite, exactly like the graph's. A deliberate difference relative to GraphProjector: there is no equivalent here to GraphUnavailableError that stops the whole batch. A write failure is usually the ITEM's (a strange name, a project whose folder disappeared), and not the destination's; stopping the batch because of one item would block all those behind it. An event that vanished from the event log is marked processed, not retried forever — retrying what no longer exists would have no effect at all, and the row would stay in the queue indefinitely. Declared cost 1: in runner mode, docs/ does not sit next to the code. Whoever opens the project folder on their own machine will not find it; it is in <PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT>/<workspace_dir_name>/docs/. It is a REAL loss in this mode, because the folder exists precisely to be opened together with the code. What it avoids is the worse alternative: the projection simply not happening, or failing silently on every artifact. Declared cost 2: the Markdown is generic. The file has a header (type, agent, when, seq) and the payload as a JSON block. There is no per-type renderer — it would be thirteen places to age when a schema changed, and what this folder needs to deliver is readable and traceable content, not layout. A richer per-type format is its own decision, when there is a real reading asking for it. Declared cost 3: the folder can diverge from the event log between one cycle and another, and after a persistent failure it can remain incomplete indefinitely without anything warning. It is the same cost the graph already accepts, and it is tolerable for the same reason: the source is intact and the projection is rebuildable. There is no reprojection command today — deleting docs/ does not rebuild it, because the outbox rows are already marked. It is the same gap BRB-018 already records for the graph, now with a second consumer. What this ADR does NOT touch. decide.ts and the absolute ceilings; proposed_action as the origin of every external agent effect (see point 7 — the projection is not one of them); the immutability of the event log; the engine's artifact schemas, which do not change at all; and the image gate (ADR 0135).
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Proposed. First ADR of PHASE 29. Nothing here changes what the images contain nor what the runner does — it changes what is published next to them and what becomes verifiable.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: The product signs nothing it publishes. Searching for cosign, sigstore, slsa and attestation in .github/, scripts/, docker/ and Makefile returns a single real occurrence, and it covers neither image nor binary: npm publish --provenance of the runner's npm package (.github/workflows/publish-runner.yml:188, with the id-token: write it requires at :27). What is left without provenance: The four GHCR images. release.yml builds and publishes with docker/bake-action (.github/workflows/release.yml:286-303), records the digests in .release/images.json (:308-319, via scripts/ci/images-manifest.ts) and attaches that manifest to the Release (:321-332). The workflow declares three permissions — contents: write, pull-requests: write, packages: write (:40-43) — and does not have id-token: write, which is what a keyless signature requires. The runner's five binaries. build-runner-binaries.yml builds the matrix (:58-74), builds and uploads each file with gh release upload (:227) — and nothing more. There is no checksums.txt, .sig, .asc nor a sha256 of our own artifact in any workflow. The sha256sum -c that exist (ci.yml:201,453,458,462, docker/engine/Dockerfile.prod:95,100,104) verify third-party binaries, and they are precisely the pattern the repository already knows how to apply and never applied to itself. The download path the product offers. GET /runner-releases/binary is @Public() (apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/runner-releases.controller.ts:73-74), validates the input (platform against a closed allowlist, :97) and streams GitHub's bytes straight to the client (:111-133). There is no checksum, signature or any integrity check. ADR 0146:208-212 already names this as BRB-005 — "not a pattern to imitate". This is BRB-005, and it is what blocked the one-line installer in PHASE 28: "a one-line installer without a signature is worse than the current download" (../explanation/fase-28-pasta-do-usuario.md:171-173). The order of PHASE 29 comes from there — without this ADR, ADR 0150 would be exactly the thing the previous phase refused.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: release.yml gains id-token: write and signs the four images by digest — the digest it already computed and already recorded in .release/images.json, never by tag, which is a moving pointer.
