Measured in the owner's database on 2026-09-26, project exp001 (mounted mode, container up): with automatic mode on in the dev agents, 51 terminal commands still asked for approval, and 47 only because they cited /work or /tmp. The dev agent runs INSIDE the container, where the project folder is /work, and the scope compares the command with the HOST root — so everything the agent writes the right way for where it runs becomes "outside the project folder". None of the 51 was git push, PR, deploy or sudo. There was a second request for the same reason, without the scope name: a COMPOUND command (cd /work && npm test) with a segment without a rule in permissions.json receives a require_approval SYNTHESIZED by the file — which exists to prevent a partial allow from promoting the whole command — and that verdict overwrote the autonomy's auto_approve. The owner asked: "once the user presses the automatic mode button, that agent should understand it can execute any command… it should only ask for approval again when the user sets the agents back to manual".
documents.s: Context

documents.t: decide() now knows the ORIGIN of the autonomy. The repository (AgentAutonomyRepository.resolve) returns the resolved mode AND whether it came from the type-specific rule or from the wildcard. The specific > wildcard precedence keeps living there, only once — findMode became a reading of resolve, not a second rule. decide() remains pure: it receives ctx.autonomyOrigin, and an absent origin counts as 'especifica' (whoever does not report it keeps the previous verdict). Automatic mode is exactly: the wildcard, resolved as auto_approve. "*": require_approval (the toggle off) and "*": deny gain no power at all. A type-specific rule (terminal: require_approval) beats the wildcard in the repository and arrives with origin 'especifica' — automatic mode does not override it. In automatic mode, the path scope ceiling does not apply. Nor the require_approval the compound command synthesizes per segment without a rule: it is the file WITHOUT an opinion, and a file without an opinion never downgrades a previous stage. An ask WRITTEN in permissions.json remains valid — it is the user's rule, and an explicit rule beats the wildcard, as in the repository. Everything else stays byte for byte. deny (from permissions.json, from the built-in defaults or from specific autonomy) still wins; the external effect/privileged command ceiling (git push, PR, deploy, sudo/doas, RN-418) runs BEFORE the scope one and does not look at the origin; merge into a protected branch, instruction_patch, parallelize/raise_max_parallel and container_remove remain never auto-approvable. The screen says, before the click, what the button releases and what still asks. The ApprovalCard note applies in both variants (chat and the Approvals queue), and the agent card shows a sentence under the toggle — only when the WILDCARD is on, because the toggle over the representative type writes a specific rule, which does not release the scope.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: An agent in automatic mode can read and write outside the project folder without asking. It is the chosen price: finding U (the agent reading the code of the platform that executes it, ADR 0055) becomes possible again FOR THAT AGENT, by explicit decision of the user who turned on the mode. The containment that remains is that of the place where the command runs — the container's mount namespace (container/mounted, ADR 0134) or the user's machine (runner) — plus deny and the effect ceilings. Switching the agent card's toggle back to "manual" rewrites the wildcard as require_approval and restores the scope ceiling on the next proposal. The card's toggle, when there is NO recorded wildcard, keeps editing the representative type (autonomyActionTypeFor) — a specific rule. Turning it on there is not automatic mode and does not release the scope; the screen does not say it releases. decide() stops being blind to the autonomy's origin, which was the proof by construction of RN-154. The proof remains valid for all ceilings except the scope one, and it is locked by tests: each of them with the wildcard on stays require_approval.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Translating /work to the host root before the scope. It would solve exp001's 47, but not /tmp nor what the owner asked ("any command"). And the translation lives in the engine, after the decision, on purpose (ADR 0134). Releasing the scope for every auto_approve autonomy, specific or not. Rejected: per-type terminal: auto_approve has existed since Phase 8d with the scope on top, and changing its meaning without anyone having asked would reopen finding U in projects that never turned on automatic mode. Letting the ask written in the file be ignored too. Rejected: it would be automatic mode overriding an explicit user rule, the inverse of the precedence the repository already applies.
documents.s: Alternatives considered

documents.t: Accepted. The cadence was decided by the maintainer on 2026-09-27 (AT-149): weekly. It references ADR 0123 (the golden-set of the QA's semantic judgment, born manual) and ADR 0138 (the RAG mold, which declared the QA one "entirely manual"). It edits neither.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: ADR 0123 left the QA golden-set as TODO(humano) for CI, saying that wiring it required "an API LLM secret or new infra (GPU)". ADR 0138 repeated the sentence when separating RAG (embedding, deterministic) from QA (chat, judgment). Two measurements changed the picture, and both are in docs/explanation/gates.md: AT-067 (2026-09-13): on an ubuntu-latest without a GPU, with qwen2.5-coder pulled into the job's own Ollama, the clock fits (19–23 min of mix golden_set.qa). The "new infra" half fell. But the score was 0/6 by construction: since RN-502 the npm test of a container project without a running container is refused, and the seed never brought one up. AT-076 (2026-09-27): the seed started bringing up the container through the production path (container_start proposed and approved, broker, state machine), without touching RN-502. Two runs in CI: 3/6 and 3/6 against the floor of 1/6, 52 and 86 min of job. With the instrument measuring, what was missing was the cadence. This workflow's proof run (run 36327281774, a temporary push trigger, removed before the PR) gave 3/6 again, through another set of cases, with zero RN-502 refusals, in 13 min 41 s of job — no case repeated a command up to the ceiling this time. The time goes from 14 to 86 min between runs.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: .github/workflows/golden-set-qa.yml, separate from ci.yml and from the RAG one, weekly schedule + workflow_dispatch, never pull_request. The same argument as ADR 0138: ci.yml is pull_request only, and a golden-set that judges with a chat model does not stay on the merge path. Saturday, 01:17 UTC: outside the RAG's daily window (06:00), the Sunday of the property proofs (04:00) and the Monday of the link check (06:00); Saturday so the red waits for the week to start; minute 17 because Actions' schedule is delayed and can drop triggers at the top of the hour. Weekly and not nightly. The RAG one costs ~20 min and is deterministic: a regression from yesterday is a regression. This one costs 52–86 min measured and VARIES — the two AT-076 runs gave the same total with different cases. One run per day would spend hours of runner per week to read the same trend signal with more noise; one per week is what the floor (ratchet) needs to flag a drop, and workflow_dispatch covers whoever touched the QA prompt and wants the answer right away. timeout-minutes: 150. The largest measured job took 86 min; the variance is the model's (one case repeated npm test 30 times before ending blocked(modelo)). 150 covers a run in which more than one case hits the iterations ceiling without turning red by clock, which is not what the job measures. The verdict is the test's. The ExUnit fails when the hits fall below the passRate of floor.json for the model, and when the api answers but the seed fails. The workflow adds two instrument guards, none of judgment: the score line must exist (the test SKIPS when the api does not answer, and skipping in a scheduled run is a green that did not measure), and the event log cannot have an RN-502 refusal (the known signature of AT-067). On failure, it does what the RAG one does: it prints the logs. It does not open an issue. Api, engine and broker native on the runner, and the Docker socket only in the broker. It is the design measured in AT-076. The same managed folder on all three sides, because api and engine run on the host (PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT = PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT). The cases' image is pulled before the seed, and the reference comes from the seed itself (IMAGEM_DO_GOLDEN_SET_QA, pinned by the index digest), not from a second literal in the workflow: the broker's docker run runs under the 30 s control ceiling of the Docker port (RN-604), and a divergence between what the job pulls and what the seed asks for would put the pull inside that ceiling.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: ADR 0123's TODO(humano) for CI closes. What remains with a human owner is what ADR 0123 itself already said: the floor (floor.json) is only written by a human, after measuring. This ADR does not touch it, nor the model. No gate changes. The QA golden-set has no gate of its own in the registry (docs/gates.yml); it is a trend signal of the semantic step of qa-verificada, and a scheduled job blocks no merge. The CI broker does not have the compose's five layers. On an ephemeral runner there is neither an internal network nor a closed port: what remains of containment is what the broker ACCEPTS (five operations, a spec computed by the api from the artifact). The runner is discarded at the end of the job and keeps no secret of this workflow (permissions: contents: read, a literal CI service token). Declared, not fixed here: the engine's heartbeat closes the seed's sessions (heartbeat_timeout) ~30 s after they are created, while the QA keeps proposing commands in them (it runs in the mix process, outside a session), with no visible effect on the AT-076 score. And a pull_request that touches this workflow does not execute it — green on the PR is not proof; the proof is the workflow_dispatch or the first Saturday.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. Decided on 2026-09-27 (AT-200, issue #633), by measurement, under the maintainer's delegation ("you measure and choose"). It references ADR 0027 (the S3 backup and the swap of mc for aws-cli) and ADR 0159 (third-party image by index digest). It edits neither.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: The Kubernetes local overlay brings up an S3 server inside the brabo namespace so that the backup exercised locally is the SAME as production's: the script always talks S3 and only the endpoint changes. That server was MinIO, pinned since ADR 0159 at quay.io/minio/minio@sha256:a1ea29fa… # RELEASE.2025-04-22T22-12-26Z. MinIO stopped publishing the community image. Measured on 2026-09-27, without authentication: reference response quay.io/v2/minio/minio/manifests/sha256:a1ea29fa… 401 quay.io/v2/minio/minio/tags/list 401 registry-1.docker.io/v2/minio/minio/manifests/RELEASE.2025-04-22T22-12-26Z 401 UNAUTHORIZED (repository nonexistent for anonymous) hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/minio/minio/tags 404 object not found The consequence was total, not partial: deploy/k8s/bootstrap.sh waits for rollout status deployment/minio BEFORE seeding and creating the bucket, so propriedades.yml died in the bootstrap and none of the property proofs ran — not even those that do not touch backup (rollout-test, hpa-test, test-reprojecao-k8s). The digest fulfilled what ADR 0159 promised — nobody swapped the bytes underneath — and that was not enough: a digest guarantees immutability, not availability. A pin survives the tag's owner moving the tag; it does not survive the registry's owner deleting the repository.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Server: deploy/k8s/overlays/local/minio/{minio,netpol}.yaml, listed in the local overlay's kustomization.yaml. Only the local overlay; staging and prod point to an external bucket. Client: it is NOT a MinIO image. mc left in Phase 5 (ADR 0027, decision 1b); backup, restore and bucket creation use the apk aws-cli inside brabo-backup (docker/backup/Dockerfile.prod), through the adapter docker/backup/lib.sh. The S3 operations it does are seven: s3 ls, s3 cp - (stdin, multipart), s3 cp (download), s3api head-object, s3 cp bucket→bucket (server-side copy), s3api list-objects-v2 and s3 rm — plus the bootstrap's s3 mb. Credentials: BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY/BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY of the brabo Secret, materialized by ESO into brabo-secrets. The server reads the SAME pair. Bootstrap: the BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT, the rollout status, the wait for the Endpoints and the ephemeral pod that creates the bucket. Network: two NetworkPolicies in the overlay (ingress into the server, egress of backup/restore), matching the POD's port. make test-restore (deploy/k8s/test-restore.sh) and the backup CronJob only see the endpoint. The compose (docker/backup/test-restore-compose.sh) uses disk, not S3, and is not affected.
documents.s: What depends on that S3 (mapped)

documents.t: The server becomes SeaweedFS, docker.io/chrislusf/seaweedfs 4.47, pinned by the INDEX digest (sha256:ce9e796f1fe6f06968f4c04bdaf8f678dad9c8acdfef3d244133d71bfa6bf882), running server -s3 -s3.port=9000. The resources are now called s3-local (Deployment, Service, PVC s3-local-data, label app.kubernetes.io/name) and the folder, overlays/local/s3/.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: candidate 1. official, anonymous, amd64+arm64 index 2. real backup flow 3. smallest change 4. license outcome SeaweedFS 4.47 (chrislusf/seaweedfs) yes — the author's Docker Hub (the README of seaweedfs/seaweedfs points to it; OCI labels with source/revision), anonymous 200, OCI index with amd64, arm64, arm/v7, 386; the tags have a published cosign signature (.sig) yes, measured (below) the server changes; client, script, Secret and port stay Apache-2.0 chosen Garage v2.1.0 (dxflrs/garage) yes — anonymous 200, index with amd64, arm64, arm, 386 not measured requires a configuration file (ConfigMap with rpc_secret) and, AFTER boot, garage layout assign + layout apply and garage key import <key-id> <secret> — a new administration step in the bootstrap. Garage documents its own key-id format (GK…), which would force changing BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY=brabo-backup (not measured here) AGPL-3.0 (no problem for unmodified use in a test overlay, but heavier than the first) discarded at criterion 3 MinIO from another source: bitnami/minio no — anonymous 404 (Bitnami also ended its free catalog) — — — discarded at criterion 1 MinIO from another source: bitnamilegacy/minio no as a live publication — FROZEN repository, last update 2025-08-19; it is a mirror without patches and without an active publisher — — — discarded at criterion 1 MinIO from another source: cgr.dev/chainguard/minio partial — amd64+arm64 index, anonymous, but only :latest is free: there is no stable tag for the pin's comment, and the publisher is whoever recompiles the source, not MinIO — — AGPL-3.0 discarded at criterion 1 (no fixed tag; unofficial publisher) original MinIO (quay.io/docker.io) no — 401/404 (Context) — — — it is the problem "Keep the first one that meets everything": SeaweedFS met all four, so Garage was not taken to the real flow — the measurement stopped where the rule says to stop, and the column says so instead of filling it.
documents.s: The candidates, by the criteria in the order the maintainer gave

documents.t: The brabo-backup built from this checkout (aws-cli/2.15.57, Alpine 3.20) ran the real adapter (docker/backup/lib.sh, destino_preparar and the destino_* functions) against weed server -s3 in a container as uid 1000, with the credential pair in the environment and /data limited to 4 GiB (the PVC's size): wrong secret → aws s3 ls refused (authentication holds); the bootstrap's s3 mb → created the bucket; destino_enviar of 30 MiB through stdin (multipart) → head-object returned 31457280, the download matched the sha256; destino_tamanho of a nonexistent object → 0; destino_copiar (server-side copy), destino_listar (3 keys, empty prefix without output) and destino_remover → correct; /healthz on the S3 port → 200 in ~1 s, without authentication (it is what the probes use); memory ~470 MiB after the upload, within the 1 GiB limit. And in the cluster, twice: CI, propriedades.yml by workflow_dispatch on the branch, run 36362479629: bootstrap, smoke-k8s, hpa-test, rollout-test, test-restore, test-restore-mutacao and test-reprojecao-k8s — all success, with no proof altered. Local, k3d on this machine: deploy/k8s/bootstrap.sh exited with 0 (the rollout status deployment/s3-local and the bucket creation passed), and make test-restore uploaded the 183 KB dump to s3-local…/brabo-backups/daily/…, downloaded it and restored 55 identical tables (exit 0); make test-restore-mutacao failed the break naming zz_mutacao_restore (exit 0). A detail UNRELATED to S3, recorded so it is not confused with it: in the first local run the seed lost the session's activation in a race with the engine (ECONNREFUSED …:4000), the dump came out without any session_event and the proof failed because of it, as it should; with three events written through the internal route the proof's own message indicates, it passed. In CI the seed activated the session on the first try.
documents.s: The measurement of criterion 2

documents.t: The image is born with mini, which adds WebDAV, an Admin UI and an Iceberg catalog. server -s3 brings up master, volume, filer and S3 gateway — the minimum that answers S3. The rest would be surface and memory without a consumer.
documents.s: Why server -s3 and not mini

documents.t: The NetworkPolicy matches the POD's port, not the Service's. With -s3.port=9000 the gateway listens where MinIO listened, and the two policies and the BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT only change NAME. Master (9333), volume (8080) and filer (8888) listen inside the pod and remain denied by the baseline.
documents.s: Why port 9000

documents.t: Calling a Service that runs SeaweedFS minio would save three bootstrap lines and would teach wrongly whoever opened the cluster. What the backup consumes is the PROTOCOL; naming it after the product behind it is what would make the next swap repeat this one.
documents.s: Why the name is neutral

documents.t: The bootstrap gets past S3 again, and the property proofs run again (run 36362479629, all six green). The client did not change. No line of docker/backup/ was touched, and what the proofs measure (test-restore, test-restore-mutacao) is the same. Declared price: readOnlyRootFilesystem remains false, as it was with MinIO — weed writes the filer's socket to /tmp. A local test component, with no equivalent in production. Declared price: SeaweedFS is not MinIO. S3 compatibility is a per-operation contract, not a seal. The eight the product uses were measured; a NEW operation in lib.sh (lifecycle, versioning, object lock) needs to be measured against it before it enters, because it is here that it would be exercised first. Production keeps talking to the real bucket, which does not change. The pin by digest does not protect against the publisher disappearing — not even this one. The signal, if it happens again, is the same: the bootstrap dies at the S3 rollout status with ImagePullBackOff. The lesson went to cadeia-de-suprimentos-do-ci.md. The count of third-party images pinned by digest does not change (one leaves, one enters): 39. No RN is born: it is local validation infrastructure, with no business rule.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. The maintainer's decision on 2026-09-27 (AT-173): "both" — its own name for dev AND a guard. It references ADR 0150 (the installation compose, which was born saying it had a name different from dev's) and ADR 0152 (the volumes that matter). It edits neither.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured on 2026-09-19: docker/docker-compose.yml (dev) and docker/docker-compose.install.yml both declared name: brabo. The installation compose's comment asserted the opposite — "name diferente do compose de dev de propósito: os dois podem coexistir na mesma máquina" — and it was not true. For Docker, a machine with an installation AND a checkout had ONE project: the containers (brabo-api-1, brabo-postgres-1…), the network (brabo_default) and the same-name volumes (brabo_pgdata, brabo_neo4j_data, brabo_git_local_repos, brabo_project_workspaces…) were the same. Three consequences, the first measured: bringing up one compose over the other RECREATES the other's containers and connects them to its database — an installation's database received a migration from dev; scripts/dev/reset-total.sh does DROP SCHEMA … CASCADE on the Postgres of the brabo project — that is, it would delete the installation's database; docker compose down of one brings down the other. The PRODUCTION compose (docker-compose.prod.yml) was already brabo-prod, and is not part of this.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: 1. The dev compose is now called brabo-dev. Containers brabo-dev-<serviço>-1, network brabo-dev_default, volumes brabo-dev_<chave>. The observability overlay (docker-compose.observability.yml) repeats the name, because the name: of the LAST -f wins and a different value there would move the whole stack to another project; its Alloy filters by com.docker.compose.project=brabo-dev. The installation one STAYS brabo. It is the name already-made installations have, and changing it would disconnect each of them from their own volumes on the next update — the cost would fall on whoever never read this repository. Whoever changes is the developer side, which reads the CHANGELOG and has the runbook. 2. A guard, in preflight.mjs and in reset-total.sh. Both REFUSE, naming the containers found and the down (without -v) of each file, when there is on the machine a container — in any state, docker ps -a — whose com.docker.compose.project.config_files label points to the INSTALLATION compose (docker-compose.install.yml, or the asset name brabo-install-compose.yml). And they refuse when the dev compose, as the script calls it, would resolve to the brabo project (a COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=brabo in the .env or in the environment). In the reset, the guard is the FIRST step, even before the preflight, and the refusal comes out as RESET NÃO COMEÇOU. The criterion is the label's FILE, not the project name: an installation is recognized under any -p, and that is what makes the guard useful against what the name does not solve — the dev compose brought up with -p brabo by hand, the COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, and an old checkout with name: brabo (which does not have this guard, but whose accident the NEW checkout refuses to continue). The rule exists in TWO places, JS (scripts/dev/instalacao-na-maquina.mjs) and bash (recusar_se_ha_instalacao in scripts/dev/reset-total-lib.sh), because the reset's spec runs with a fake node in the PATH and needs to prove that the script itself refuses. Both are exercised by the specs next to them. Docker that does not answer does NOT refuse: the preflight says the guard did not run and continues (the up brings up nothing without Docker), and in the reset the build, still before the first effect, would fail the same way. 3. Migration for whoever already develops: a warning, never a refusal, never deleting. The next pnpm dev creates EMPTY brabo-dev_* volumes; the data stays in the brabo_* ones. The preflight WARNS when it finds a brabo_* volume with a key that ONLY the dev compose declares (*_node_modules, engine_build/deps/mix/hex) — the list is DERIVED from the two compose files, never copied — and separates, without asserting whose they are, those with a key common to both (pgdata, neo4j_data, git_local_repos, project_workspaces…), which may belong to an installation. The procedure to copy (volume by volume, cp -a, with Postgres stopped) or start over is in the runbook, "Moving a dev environment to brabo-dev". No script removes a volume.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Whoever develops acts once (that is why the branch is breaking/): brings down the old stack WITHOUT -v (docker compose -p brabo -f docker/docker-compose.yml down) and chooses to copy the data or start over. Until they do, the old compose holds the ports, and the preflight says exactly that instead of port is already allocated. Developing on a machine that has an installation now requires bringing the installation down first (down without -v: volumes and data stay, up -d brings it back). It is the declared price of the guard by PRESENCE, and it was chosen by the maintainer: the separate names already make coexistence safe in the common case, but the guard exists precisely for the uncommon case — and a guard that only looked at name collision would let through the old checkout and the manual -p with the installation stopped. Running both AT THE SAME TIME remains impossible either way: they publish the same ports. An orphan brabo_* volume with a common key is not distinguishable, on its own, between old dev and installation — the warning says so instead of asserting. The runbook teaches how to ask (config_files of the containers, exclusive keys, whether there was an installation on the machine). Documentation and commands that cited brabo-api-1, brabo-postgres-1, brabo-ollama-1, brabo_pgdata… in the DEV context now cite brabo-dev-*. Those that talk about the INSTALLATION (the brabo_project_workspaces volume install.sh measures, the broker root in the installation) stay as they are, because they remain true. Historical narrative (old CHANGELOG, accepted RNs and ADRs) is not rewritten. The local Prometheus pod labels become brabo-dev-api-1/ brabo-dev-engine-1, the container's real name; no dashboard filters by pod value, it only groups.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. Decided by the maintainer on 2026-09-27 (AT-179): scan and fail. It references ADR 0119 (the images published by digest), ADR 0149 (the keyless cosign signature by digest) and ADR 0162 (the fifth image). It edits none of them.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Trivy only existed in the images job of ci.yml, which scans a LOCAL build of the PR (brabo-api:prod in the runner's daemon). release.yml builds again, pushes to GHCR, records the digests in .release/images.json and signs — without any scan. The investigation of AT-110 measured why that is not the same artifact: the type=gha cache a PR writes is not readable from a tag (of the repository's 663 buildkit caches, all were in refs/pull/N/merge), so the tag builds COLD, and the final stage's apk upgrade runs again and can bring another set of packages. AT-110 closed the PR side (no-cache-filter = ["runtime"] in the bake), but the image the installer downloads remained the only one nobody scanned.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Where. In the release job of release.yml, after Registrar as imagens publicadas and before Instalar o cosign/Assinar as imagens publicadas. The order is the mechanism: a failed image receives no signature, and without a signature install.sh does not install it. On what. On the DIGEST of each image recorded in .release/images.json (repositorio@sha256:…), read from the registry (--image-src remote) — never by tag, for the same reason as the signature: the tag is a moving pointer and the digest is what was published. The list comes from scripts/ci/trivy-do-release.ts referencias, which fails an empty manifest or a malformed digest. The rule fails. HIGH or CRITICAL with a fix available fails the job. The flags are those of ci.yml, byte for byte: --scanners vuln --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed --ignorefile .trivyignore.yaml --skip-db-update --exit-code 1. Whoever decides is Trivy's exit code, never a second rule in TypeScript — it would diverge from Trivy's at the first new Status. All images are scanned before failing, so the log names WHICH ones failed. What has no fix is reported. A second scan per image, without --ignore-unfixed and with --exit-code 0, generates JSON; scripts/ci/trivy-do-release.ts resumo builds the markdown (the two numbers per image and the list of what has no fix), which goes to the job summary and is attached to the Release as trivy-sem-correcao.md. That step runs BEFORE the gate, so the summary also exists when the gate fails. No new allowlist. The only exceptions file is the .trivyignore.yaml ci.yml already uses — curated, with the three conditions at the top and expired_at on every entry. Not using it would make the release apply a HARSHER rule than the PR's, over the same exceptions the maintainer already accepted: measured, the engine of v6.1.0 would have 56 fixable findings, all in the third-party scanner binaries that file documents. The spec fails a second --ignorefile, --skip-files, --skip-dirs, --vex, --ignore-policy or --ignore-status. Same version, declared twice, guarded. TRIVY_VERSION and TRIVY_SHA256 enter the env: of release.yml with ci.yml's value. A single place did not fit: a workflow's env: cannot be imported from another file, and a composite action for two variables would be a third place to maintain. The binary is downloaded with curl and goes through sha256sum -c before extracting, as in ci.yml. No new action (no uses: entered). The proof. release.yml only runs on a final tag, so no PR executes it — the situation of install-e2e.yml. scripts/ci/trivy-do-release.spec.ts guards, on every PR: the gate after the registration and before cosign; no continue-on-error/always() on the path; the rule's flags equal to ci.yml's; the report without --ignore-unfixed and with --exit-code 0; version and hash equal; curl → sha256sum -c → tar; the asset in the gh release create. Proven by mutation: removing --ignore-unfixed from the gate or moving cosign-installer before it turns the spec red.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Failing leaves a published image without a signature. The push happens before the scan (it is what creates the digest), so a failed tag leaves :X.Y.Z and :<sha> on GHCR, without a signature, without a Release and without an attached images.json. It is the right state — the installer refuses an image without a signature —, but it is a public residue. Redoing it means fixing the base and cutting a new tag; republishing the same tag through workflow_dispatch rebuilds and rescans. The next tag can be born red because of a CVE published after the PR. The tag's scan uses the vulnerability database of the tag's day, not the PR's. That is the point: what reaches the installer is judged with what is known on the day it arrives. Measured on 2026-09-27 against the v6.1.0 digests: api and web would fail today because of CVE-2026-45447 (HIGH, libcrypto3/libssl3 3.3.7-r0 → 3.3.7-r1), a CVE later than that tag; engine and backup pass; nothing HIGH/CRITICAL without a fix. A new tag builds cold and runs apk upgrade, so it should bring 3.3.7-r1 — which was not proven here, because it would require cutting a tag. Time cost. Measured locally over the four v6.1.0 digests: 13 s to download the database and ~17 s for the eight scans (gate and report), over the network. On the runner the real number only exists at the first tag; the job keeps timeout-minutes: 30, against 4–11 min of the last three releases. .trivyignore.yaml now also applies to what is published. An entry that expires (expired_at: 2026-10-31 in the current ones) fails the PR AND the next tag. The discipline of reviewing the list does not change; what changes is that forgetting it now blocks publication, not only the merge. Declared duplication. Version, hash and flags exist in two workflows. The spec fails the divergence; whoever upgrades Trivy upgrades it in both in the same PR.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. It is the FOURTH in the line opened by ADR 0127 and continued by ADR 0156 and ADR 0157. It opens the door that 0157 refused to open in passing — "A route for removing a workspace member (…) Separate decision, if someone asks for it" — by decision of the maintainer (2026-09-27, AT-115/HS-006): the route is born, protected by a CLAUSE. An accepted ADR is not edited: 0157 still says the route does not exist, and this one is what says it now exists.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Offboarding a workspace member was a direct write to the database: WorkspacesController had no member @Delete — measured during BRB-002 and used by 0157 as part of its argument. 0157 left three questions for whoever opened this door, and HS-006 showed they are the same conversation: the last owner. Today the "never zero owners" invariant comes from a clause — removing the last one would require them to do it themselves, and ceiling 2 prevents that. HS-006 feared a removal route would reopen that path and that the guarantee would have to come from a count, which is what 0127 refused ("stated as a clause, it has no number to go stale"); ceiling 1 in the workspace. It was left out (0157, point 3) because, combined with the absence of a removal route, it would make owner an absorbing state; ceiling 2 on removal: does it inherit the delegation of project removal (remocaoEhAutoRebaixamento) or need its own statement, since here the "after" is always none?
documents.s: Context

documents.t: 1. DELETE /workspaces/:workspaceId/members/:userId is born, owner, 204. The same minimum as the upsert: whoever changes the member list is whoever maintains it. Idempotent like project removal — a target without a row is not an error. 2. Ceiling 2 is INHERITED, with no new rule. RemoveWorkspaceMemberUseCase calls remocaoEhAutoRebaixamento passing the actor's WORKSPACE role as today's effective role (in the workspace there is no composition: the effective role is the row) and null as the role AFTER. That branch already existed — it is the one for a project without a workspace row, "the maximum demotion" — and it answers question 3: the "after" here is always none, and the function already knew how to state none. Removing oneself from the workspace is always 403, with its own sentence (MENSAGEM_TETO_AUTO_REMOCAO_DO_WORKSPACE): whoever clicked "remove" did not ask for a role change, the same reason project removal got its own in 0156. The parameter names stayed the project ones: renaming them would change the other doors for the sake of a reading, and the function's docblock states the reading. 3. The last owner is protected by the SAME clause, without counting owners. The proof, in the mould of the one 0157 made for the upsert: the route requires owner (@RequireRole('owner')), so whoever removes is always an owner of the workspace; nobody removes themselves (point 2); therefore every successful removal leaves at least one owner standing: the caller themselves. Removing the last one would require them to remove themselves — the refused move. HS-006's premise ("the route would reopen the path") was not confirmed: the route OPENS the removal of others, but removing the last one is precisely self-removal, and that remains closed by the clause that already closed self-demotion. Counting stays refused for the reasons in 0157, point 2. The proof is in a test: "with two owners, any sequence of removals leaves at least one: whoever removes stays", and the route's owner minimum is asserted in the controller test, because it is HALF of the proof — if the minimum drops, the proof drops with it. 4. Removing ANOTHER owner remains possible. It is the way to revoke ownership entirely, and it is the natural extension of 0157's point 3, which kept demoting another owner. Ceiling 1 still has no counterpart in this scope (question 2): the premise HS-006 saw falling — "there being no way out of owner over HTTP" — was 0157's COST argument, and the PRINCIPLE one still stands: ceiling 1 is a rule about hierarchy inversion, and @RequireRole('owner') makes inversion impossible. The new route only reinforces the cost: with it and a mirrored ceiling 1, removing another owner would also be refused, and owner would become absorbing again. 5. The cascade, in one transaction. Removing the workspace_members row alone would be cosmetic: the projectRole ?? workspaceRole overlay (RN-471) would keep the removed person inside every project where they had their own row. So, together: the workspace_members row; the removed person's project_members rows in this workspace's projects (those of other workspaces are not touched); their credentials tied to those projects: the PROJECT device keys (by the same column that RN-519 lists) and the PATs — every PAT belongs to a project (project_id NOT NULL) —, revoked with the reason workspace_member_removed. Without this, being re-added one day would silently reactivate a pairing the removal should have ended. 6. After the commit, the live connection drops via the RN-520 path. One disconnectRunnerOfUser(projectId, userId) per project of the workspace — ALL, not only those in runner mode, because the runner also connects in container/mounted (the mirror, RN-516); one extra project costs a sem_runner, one missing leaves standing what the removal exists to bring down. In a try/catch that only logs: a side effect never brings down the main effect, the rule of RN-520. 7. The HOLDER does not leave; holdership is transferred (maintainer decision, 2026-09-27, RN-616). workspaces.created_by does not decide authorization (the role does, ADR 0127), but it is what resolves the LLM credential the agents spend and the git credential of agent actions (RN-058, ResolveCredentialOwnerUseCase) and the owner of the spending report (RN-060). Removing the creator through point 4 would leave the agents spending the credential of someone no longer in the workspace. So, under the name holder: DELETE .../members/:userId targeting the holder is a named 409, criador_do_workspace, saying that a transfer is needed first and why. The point-2 ceiling comes first: the holder trying to remove themselves gets the usual 403. Point 3 still holds — the holder is an owner, and the caller is still the owner who stays. PUT /workspaces/:workspaceId/owner-of-record is born, owner, body { userId }. The target must ALREADY be an owner of the workspace — being holder means paying — otherwise 409 titular_precisa_ser_owner. It writes created_by, in a transaction with the role read; transferring to the current holder is idempotent. Any owner can call it, including transferring to ANOTHER owner who did not ask: it is the same authority that already removes and demotes owners, and the target's consent would be an invitation flow the product does not have. Spending, from the commit on: ResolveCredentialOwnerUseCase starts returning the NEW holder; the agent turn looks for THEIR credential for the model's provider, and git actions, their git credential. If they do not have one, the product does what it already did with any holder without a credential: the turn ends with "Nenhuma credencial cadastrada para <provider>" (RunLlmTurnUseCase/StreamLlmTurnUseCase) and the git remote read fails naming whose credential is missing. The transfer does NOT check this beforehand — it would be one read per provider without knowing which ones the projects use, and refusing because of it would lock precisely the exit of the holder who is leaving. ollama uses no credential and stays the same. Spending already recorded stays where it was: token_usage does not store the holder, and the report is now read by the new holder in full, history included. There is no domain event for member or holdership changes (the upsert and the removal do not emit one either); the transfer leaves a log line with from/to/who. An audit event for all three is a separate front.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: MACHINE keys (project_id null) stay: they belong to the ACCOUNT and serve the person's other workspaces. Here they no longer reach anything — the PatAuthGuard resolves the role against the requested project, and it is none. Open sessions stay open: they belong to the project, not the person, and the event log is append-only. A session socket ALREADY connected by the removed person stays until it drops; the new ticket (RN-108) requires viewer and is refused. Dropping the session channel per user would require a new command in the engine — a separate front. The :web terminal of the removed person is not a target of the disconnection (RN-520 only drops :runner); same gap, same reason. Screen. There is no workspace members section in apps/web (measured: the only trace of /workspaces/:id/members is the generated type in api-types.generated.ts, and there is not even a GET of workspace members). None is created here; the route is an API route, like the upsert.
documents.s: What is declared and NOT done

documents.t: Offboarding stops being a database write. An owner removes any other person, including another owner (the holder after transferring), and the removal is real: they leave the workspace and all its projects, and their runner drops. The ceiling line has five doors and two ceilings. No new ceiling was born: ceiling 2 gained one more door, through the same function, and ceiling 1 stays only in the project. docs/security-surface.md gets the note about the fifth route. Two old sentences become false, and this ADR is what replaces them. The one in 0157 ("WorkspacesController has no member @Delete") and the 403 message for self-demotion in the workspace, which said "there is no route that removes a member" and no longer does — an error sentence cannot assert what is not true. One more query before writing (the actor's role), and N HTTP calls to the engine afterwards, one per project of the workspace, on the least frequent administration route in the product.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. Decided by the maintainer on 2026-09-27 (AT-065, HS-035). References ADR 0112 (the standalone binary via bun build --compile, born with five targets), ADR 0106 (the npm package, which becomes the Intel Mac path) and ADR 0149 (the signed checksums.txt that covers the binaries). It edits none of the three.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: ADR 0112 promised five targets — linux-x64, linux-arm64, darwin-x64, darwin-arm64, win32-x64 —, each built on its native runner. darwin-x64 never published, and the cause is measured in two layers: There is no usable Intel runner. The macos-13 label points to an image GitHub retired (changelog of 2025-09-19, end in Dec/2025). On the three tags that exist (v4.0.0, v4.0.1, v5.0.0) the job sat 24h00m01s in the queue and was cancelled by the Actions ceiling — the SAME number on all three, i.e. it was never scheduled. In a workflow_dispatch rehearsal (2026-09-13, run 34769280227) it sat 30 min in the queue, again with no runner. The replacement schedules, builds and fails. The Intel label GitHub offers instead, macos-15-intel, schedules in 3–22 s (five runs) and BUILDS the binary, but fails --self-test-pty: under Bun, node-pty's onData never delivers the child process output — an open runtime bug, oven-sh/bun#25822, with no fixed release. The SAME proof passes under Node on the same runner (run 34770476634). The second measurement changed the nature of the pending item: the blocker stopped being the runner (paying for an Intel runner would not solve it) and became Bun. Two ways out remained — wait for Bun to fix it and then switch the label, or drop the platform —, and CLAUDE.md recorded it as an owner's decision. Meanwhile, the five-target promise cost in four places: the matrix queued a job that never ran; ALVOS_ESPERADOS made every checksums.txt announce, forever, the absence of a target already known not to come (RN-565); the GET /runner-releases/binary proxy accepted darwin-x64 only to answer 502 plataforma_nao_publicada; and install.sh asked GitHub for an asset that returns 404 — with the same "the Release does not publish" output, indistinguishable from an incomplete Release.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The platform goes. The standalone binary now promises FOUR targets, and Intel Mac gets the npm path — npm install -g @brabo/runner, which runs under Node, where the node-pty proof passes. build-runner-binaries.yml removes darwin-x64 from the matrix and from ALVOS_ESPERADOS. checksums.txt now declares absence only of what is a real failure. The GET /runner-releases/binary proxy accepts the four, and refuses darwin-x64 with its own 400 — not with the generic "invalid platform" — naming this ADR and the npm command, without calling GitHub. install.sh, on darwin-amd64, does not try to download: it says in text that Intel Mac has no binary, that the rest of the installation is up and what the npm command is, and leaves RUNNER_BIN empty — the same signal by which the wrap-up (RN-547) already reported the pending key and service. The installation itself remains supported on Intel Mac (the cosign pinned for darwin-amd64 stays), only the local agent binary goes. The browser keeps detecting darwin-x64 — detecting Intel Mac is true, and it is what allows stating the right path —, but the binary step does not request the download: it fails upfront, and falls into the same best-effort (falhaDoBinario → npm command) of RN-473. scripts/ci/alvos-do-runner.spec.ts ties together the four places that enumerate targets, in three languages: the matrix, the api list, the installer's case and the browser's. Removing (or restoring) a target in one and forgetting another fails.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Wait for Bun and switch the label to macos-15-intel. Keeps the promise with no deadline, and switching the label alone does not make the target publish — it only trades 24 h of queue for a red job on every tag. It remains the way back (below), not today's decision. Build darwin-x64 by cross-compiling from darwin-arm64. ADR 0112 refused cross-compiling a native addon, and self-test-pty would not run on the target architecture — it would publish a binary nobody proved. Pay for an Intel runner. The measurement showed the blocker is the runtime, not the machine: the same hosted macos-15-intel builds and fails.
documents.s: Alternatives considered

documents.t: The standalone binary promise is four targets, and the Release keeps receiving two (linux-x64, linux-arm64) until a tag exercises the win32-x64 and darwin-arm64 fixes already on dev. This decision does not touch that. Intel Mac users need Node installed to have the local agent. install.sh and the browser panel say so in text; neither installs Node on its own. Not measured, and declared: the Bun issue was opened on darwin ARM64. It is likely that darwin-arm64 will hit the same defect after the spawn-helper fix. If it happens, this ADR is the precedent, not the automatic answer — deciding darwin-arm64 is another decision. Way back: when Bun fixes node-pty's onData in a release, re-enabling the target is a new ADR that switches the label to macos-15-intel, runs the workflow_dispatch rehearsal with an empty tag, and returns darwin-x64 to the four places the spec ties together.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-09-27 (AT-141). Maintainer decision: yes — the Infra Lead starts conversing through the composer and becomes the SEVENTH conversational agent. References ADR 0163 (the click responds on accept), which this document does NOT edit: what it decided for the six conversational agents now applies to the seventh, by the SAME mechanism. Also references ADR 0038 (the agent hierarchy, lead and subagent) and ADR 0086 (the Dev Lead suspension, which the Infra Lead does not have). Rule: RN-617. Closes the open decision that RN-584 left in writing.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: RN-584 (AT-098) removed the default recipient of the chat message and gave infra a NAMED refusal (422 agente_sem_conversa), leaving the product question declared: does the Infra Lead converse through the composer? And it declared the price of answering "yes" without preparation: the user_message/2 that InfraLeadServer exported ran the ENTIRE turn inside handle_call, with a 180 s ceiling on the GenServer.call. Measured in the code before the change, the Infra Lead was outside ALL the pieces that ADR 0163 and the following RNs gave the other six: Piece The six The Infra Lead Immediate accept, working recorded first (RN-578) TurnoAssincrono.iniciar/3 the whole turn in handle_call/handle_cast Named refusal 409 turno_em_andamento yes the second message waited in the process queue "Stop" (RN-122) via_for/2 of cancel/2 via_for/2 did not know it, nor was there a Task to kill Orphan turn on restart (RN-586) TurnoOrfao "left out — declared in RN-586" Stop on session close (RN-581) terminate/2 abandons the Task killed after 5 s of waiting Narrated iteration ceiling (RN-166) toolloop.limit_reached the loop ended silently at step 14 Also the kickoff: being a cast, it held no click, but it occupied the process for the entire turn — measured on the AT-089 installation, 8.4 min. A message arriving in the meantime would wait the 8.4 min in the queue and exit with :timeout in the controller (500), and "Stop" would only be served afterwards. And the ceiling: the propose_action of container actions that the api runs auto-approved waits up to 225 s (RN-605), more than the 180 s of user_message/2. A message leading the model to propose container_start could blow the GenServer.call with the proposal still standing.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: First the turn, then the clause. The Infra Lead's THREE turns — kickoff, gate correction ({:correct, _}) and message — go up through Engine.Agents.TurnoAssincrono, the SAME module as the six. The kickoff stays a cast, fired only on the FRESH start of the accepted handoff; what changes is where it runs (in a Task). The old user_message/2, which ran inline, ceased to exist: the name stayed, and now it is the accept — there are not two paths. Consolidation with Workflows runs INSIDE the Task. The end of the turn (concluir/1: HALT of propose_infra_pr → WorkflowsAgent → single PR) is part of the turn function and returns the state; the end signals (agent.done, agent.status: idle) come only from TurnoAssincrono, in the server process (RN-585). "Stop" also kills the Workflows in progress. The gate correction is not discarded. TurnoAssincrono.iniciar/3 without from ignores the request when a turn is in progress (the defensive kickoff case). For the correction that would lose the gate's request, so it enters a QUEUE (correcoes_pendentes) and goes up at the turn's close — success, failure, crash or "Stop" —, in arrival order. It is the mould of the Arquiteto's handoff_dev_pendente. The Infra Lead enters the engine's lists: @agentes_de_conversa and the own clause of message/2 (the RN-584 refusal goes), via_for("infra") in "Stop", and TurnoOrfao (@agentes). Engine.Agents.Conversacionais already listed it. The iteration ceiling is its own, 14, the same as Arquiteto, Dev Lead, UX Designer and Staff — and step 14 now emits toolloop.limit_reached. The screen offers it by the usual rule. infra enters AGENTES_DE_CHAT (apps/web/src/lib/session-readiness.ts): it is the recipient when it is the most recent agent.activated, with no default recipient (RN-584). The acceptance of ITS handoff stays in the own card of RN-499, and the thread card excludes it by NAME — otherwise the invitation would appear twice and, being the oldest, would again hide the Dev Lead's (RN-136). Conversing does not open external effects. The tools are the same four; the infra PR and the two container start-ups still are born as proposed_action, with the local refusals of RN-566/RN-577/RN-610 intact.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The 180 s ceiling stops mattering for the turn. The GenServer.call of user_message/2 only waits for the accept (milliseconds); the 225 s of the container propose_action run inside the Task, with nobody waiting synchronously. The number 180 000 stayed, equal to the other six, as the ACCEPT ceiling. A message during the kickoff is refused by name. Before it waited; now it is 409 turno_em_andamento, with the durable agent.error — the same rule as the other six. The generated list does not change. SOLO_CONVERSATIONAL_AGENTS (generated by pnpm --filter api gerar:areas) is the list of agents WITHOUT an area that a manual handoff addresses; the Infra Lead is an area lead and stays out of it. AGENTES_DE_CHAT is not generated: it is the list the scripts/ci/destinos-do-composer.spec.ts guard checks against the clauses. The screen narrates its tools. The four got a sentence in the activity strip (toolNarration.json), instead of the fallback. Declared and not closed: the Infra Lead has no ask_structured_questions nor backlog reading — conversing with it is conversing with what the kickoff gave it and with the usual tools, and widening that is a separate front. The message does not rerun the kickoff: an Infra Lead brought back up by a message (engine restarted) rehydrates the history and responds, without regenerating artifacts.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-09-28 (AT-138, BRB-015). Maintainer decision (2026-09-27): yes, and lock afterwards — decompose apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx to below 1,000 lines in mechanical PRs, and only then turn the ceiling into a CI lock. References, without editing, ADR 0122 (the five mechanical PRs that took the file from 3,807 to 2,661 lines and decided that the extracted siblings import SessionPage.module.css directly), ADR 0124 (the turn channel cluster in useTurnoDoAgente, which this program does NOT touch) and ADR 0125 (the same rule of "importers change nothing", applied to ProjectSettingsTab.tsx).
documents.s: Status

documents.t: The SessionPage.tsx debt line closed on 2026-08-30, through ADRs 0122 and 0124, at 2,479 lines. It closed on a NUMBER, and nothing measured the number afterwards: on 2026-09-13 the file had 2,559 lines (architecture.md started declaring this, AT-031), and on today's origin/dev (018b8cd24c, measured with wc -l) it has 2,637 lines and 122,379 bytes. Nobody did anything wrong — each addition was a legitimate feature (the fit-models filter, the Infra handoff card, the closed-session refusal, the Infra Lead in the composer) — and that is exactly why the regression happened: without a lock, debt comes back as a sum of right decisions. What the file was, measured before this program: A ~2,400-line component. The body of SessionPage went from line 237 to 2,637. Outside it there were only the imports, the re-export of the timeline functions and agruparNarracoesDoTurno. The biggest block was a 762-line useMemo, the timeline assembly: one JSX node per event type, the batch of stories awaiting promotion (RN-126/RN-148) and the approval cards (RN-155). The returned JSX had ~625 lines in three independent strips: the top bar, the scrolling thread content, and the bottom strip (Infra card, manual handoff, composer). The handlers were ~500 lines, in three families: the TURN ones (handleSend, handleCancel, handleReadiness, handleArchitectureReadiness — the door of the ADR 0124 cluster), the story PROMOTION ones and the HANDOFF/EXECUTION ones that are not turns. 28 SessionPage.*.test.tsx files, 173 tests, all with MODULE vi.mock (../lib/api-client, ../lib/hooks, ../lib/session-channel…). A module mock applies to any file that imports the module, so code moved to a sibling file stays mocked — that is what makes moving without editing tests viable.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Ten PRs, stacked in order (each on top of the previous, --base the previous one's branch), each MECHANICAL: move code without changing behaviour — no refactoring logic, renaming the component's public API or "improving in passing". The acceptance rule is ADR 0122's, word for word: the 28 existing test files pass WITHOUT EDITS. A PR that needs to edit one of them is not mechanical and stops. SessionPage.tsx goes from 2,637 to 834 lines (−1,803): PR What leaves Where to SessionPage.tsx after — ADR 0176 (this document) docs/adr/ 2,637 1 agruparNarracoesDoTurno, FIO_RECENTES_ABERTAS, the body of the useMemos timelineAgrupada (collapse by agent, RN-138) and fio (cut by origin, RN-177) routes/session-fio.tsx (agruparTimelinePorAgente, dividirFio) 2,445 (−192) 2 the body of the timeline useMemo (762 lines) routes/session-timeline-montagem.tsx (montarTimeline) 1,718 (−727) 3 the top bar routes/SessionTopbar.tsx 1,561 (−157) 4 the thread content (invitation, history, recent, optimistic, streaming bubble) routes/SessionFio.tsx 1,390 (−171) 5 the bottom strip (Infra card, manual handoff, composer) routes/SessionComposer.tsx 1,225 (−165) 6 activeFor, offeredHandoff, handoffDaInfraOferecido and the three "already declared" lib/session-handoffs.ts (derivarHandoffsDaSessao) 1,163 (−62) 7 the four refs and the four scroll effects, and rolarParaOFim lib/session-rolagem.ts (useRolagemDoFio) 1,094 (−69) 8 the five states and three story-promotion handlers, and the return modal lib/session-promocao.ts (usePromocaoDeHistorias) + routes/DevolverHistoriaModal.tsx 982 (−112) 9 the four states and five handoff/execution handlers that are not turns (RN-406, RN-440, RN-161, RN-137, RN-153) lib/session-acoes-de-handoff.ts (useAcoesDeHandoff) 834 (−148) 10 the lock routes/SessionPage.teto.test.ts 834 The order goes from least to most risky, as in ADR 0122: first what is a pure or nearly pure function (PRs 1–2), then stateless JSX (PRs 3–5), then pure derivation (PR 6), and lastly the HOOKS (PRs 7–9), which are the only ones that touch the component's hook order. What "mechanical" means for each kind of cut, decided once here so it is not relitigated in ten reviews: A useMemo body becomes a function called FROM INSIDE the same useMemo, with the SAME dependency list, byte for byte — including the ones it does not list. The timeline assembly closes over handlers (handlePromoteStory, handleAcceptHandoff…), t and semRepositorio that were never in the dependencies; completing the list would change WHEN the timeline is rebuilt, and that is behaviour. oxlint keeps warning (exhaustive-deps is warn) about what it already warned about. A JSX block becomes a component whose props have the SAME names the block read from SessionPage's scope. The component calls its own useTranslation('sessionPage'). A block with several siblings becomes a fragment. The modal's {recusandoStory && …} went along, inside the component. Pure derivation becomes a pure function that returns the same names, computed on every render as before. State + handlers become a hook called at the SAME point where the effects were (PR 7), or right after useTurnoDoAgente when the handlers depend on it (PRs 8–9). The position of the useStates in the hook order changes, and that is not observable: React only requires the same order between one render and the next. The handlers remain functions recreated on every render, as the component's async functions were. Without JSX goes to lib/*.ts; with JSX stays in routes/*.tsx and imports SessionPage.module.css directly — ADR 0122's answer to the CSS question, reused without reopening. lib/ stays without code .tsx. Comments go along with the code, including the ones saying "here" or "just below" — the new file says at the top where they came from. Rewriting a comment in passing is the "improving in passing" the program forbids. SessionPage.tsx re-exports what the tests import from it: agruparNarracoesDoTurno moved to session-fio.tsx and is still re-exported, for the same reason as the four timeline functions of ADR 0122. The lock is born in the LAST PR, and not before. It is a web test (SessionPage.teto.test.ts) that fails SessionPage.tsx at 1,000 lines or more, counting like wc -l, and that proves its own count at both edges (999 passes, 1,000 fails) — also measured by mutation, adding 166 lines to the real file. It lives in web, and not in scripts/ci/, because it runs in the suite that every PR touching the file already runs.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The TURN handlers (handleSend, handleCancel, handleReadiness, handleArchitectureReadiness, avisarSessaoEncerrada) and the session lifecycle ones (handleActivate, handleClose, handleRename, handleStartIdeation) stay in SessionPage. The turn ones are the entry door of the cluster that ADR 0124 moved to useTurnoDoAgente and left called FROM HERE; removing them would mean deciding again where the turn lives, and that is not mechanical. The ceiling was reached without them. useTurnoDoAgente, useSessionReadiness, ContextAside, StructuredQuestionCard, StorySlide — already extracted, they do not change. No dependency list is "fixed", no handler becomes a useCallback, no prop or function name changes. Each of those would be a change of behaviour or API, and each, if worthwhile, is its own PR that does not present itself as mechanical.
documents.s: Out of scope, on purpose

documents.t: The file goes from 2,637 to 834 lines, with 166 of slack until the lock. The slack is on purpose: the ceiling cannot be the next feature to fall into it. Whoever needs to pass 999 takes out a cut — there are candidates declared above —, never raises the number. Raising the ceiling is a new ADR that references this one. The total number of lines GROWS: the ten new files have 2,574 lines against the 1,803 that left, because each gained its own imports, a props or context block, and a header saying where it came from. It is the price of explicit boundaries, and it is the same that ADR 0125 accepted. The largest new file has 861 lines (session-timeline-montagem.tsx, almost all of the original useMemo). It does NOT get a lock here: the declared debt is SessionPage.tsx's, and locking a file that was just born would be the mistake AT-031 named. If it grows, the next natural cut is one file per event family. The file:line references to SessionPage.tsx in docs/business-rules.md and docs/business-rules/autenticacao.md moved — many were already stale before this program. They are updated in PR 10, once, when the lines stop moving; in PRs 1–9 verificarRefsComSimbolo (in warn) warns. BRB-015 stops reproducing in PR 10, and the architecture.md line that declared the regression closes with it, pointing to the lock. The stacked PRs merge in order. A feature PR touching SessionPage.tsx between two of them rebases onto the cut — the cost ADR 0122 had already accepted by not freezing the file.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Lock before decomposing, with the ceiling at today's number, going down with each PR. Refused by the maintainer: a ceiling that follows the descent is a number to edit in every PR of the program, and a fixed ceiling above the file prevents nothing. The lock only has value as the NO to "it grew again", and that only exists after getting there. A single PR. Refused for the same reason as ADR 0122: 1,800 lines moved in one diff cannot be reviewed, and the file keeps receiving features. Take the turn handlers along to get further. Refused: it is the cluster ADR 0124 decided, and the ceiling did not need it. One file per event type already in PR 2. Refused for this program: breaking the useMemo into functions per event requires deciding each one's signature (the promotion batch and the loop's continue cross types), and that stops being moving. Moving the whole body first is what allows that cut, if it comes, to be reviewed on its own.
documents.s: Discarded alternatives

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-09-28 (AT-162, epic EP-028). Maintainer decisions of 2026-09-28, written in the notes of AT-168 and AT-169: preference per ACCOUNT with an override per SESSION; an OPEN list of languages (any BCP-47); new accounts in automatico; the detected one only counts when CONFIRMED; shared artifacts and turns without an author in the PROJECT's language. References, without editing, ADR 0121 (a new table goes into its aggregate's file) and ADR 0006 (the system prompt belongs to the AGENT, not to the turn's author — that is why the language does not go into it, but into a per-turn guidance, which is AT-164's).
documents.s: Status

documents.t: An agent's response language, until now, was decided only by the model, from a system prompt written in pt-BR and from the messages. The report that opened the epic was a conversation in Portuguese answered in Spanish, with DeepSeek via OpenRouter. users.locale (RN-432) exists, but it is the INTERFACE language: closed to pt-BR/en because each value needs a translation file, and the engine does not read it anywhere. The maintainer's decisions call for four sources that did not exist and one that did, with a precedence among them, and three different scopes: the explicit choice belongs to the PERSON and applies in every project and session; the person can pin ANOTHER language in one session, only for themselves — two users in the same session do not affect each other; the one detected from messages belongs to the PERSON, global, and only counts after they confirm; what belongs to everyone (shared artifact, turn without an author) follows the PROJECT.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: No enum. The three places store text with a CANONICAL BCP-47 code, validated in the api by normalizarIdiomaBcp47 (apps/api/src/domain/iam/idioma-de-resposta.ts): form via Intl.getCanonicalLocales, a language subtag known to the process's ICU (Intl.DisplayNames with fallback: 'none'), never und nor private use, at most 35 characters. Opening the RESPONSE language does not depend on any resource file; an enum would require a migration per language, which is the cost the "open list" decision refused. Account: two columns in users, and locale untouched. users.response_language — NULL is AUTOMATIC, and that is how every account is born (no sentinel value inside a language column). And the pair users.detected_language + users.detected_language_confirmed_at, with a CHECK requiring both together: the detected one only exists CONFIRMED. Who writes the pair is AT-163 (detection and the confirmation question); the column is born here because it is a step of the precedence. Session: table session_language_overrides, in the sessions aggregate, keyed by {session_id, user_id}. Configuration and not an event: pinning again is an upsert, releasing is a DELETE, and a deleted session takes its rows with it. The key is the PAIR because the override is the person's; there is no "whole session" read. Project: column projects.language (implemented in AT-243, with the default and minimum role decided there, in RN-619). It is the language of whatever has no human author. The precedence for those with an author (RN-618), resolved per PERSON and never per session: session override > account choice > confirmed detected > users.locale. Since users.locale is NOT NULL, the chain always ends in a language. The "one-off request" inside a message is not a step: the model honours it, through the wording of the guidance. One resolution point. ResolverIdiomaDaRespostaUseCase returns the winner, the ORIGIN and the whole chain; it is what the screen shows (the Account, the session bar) and what AT-164 calls to send the language to the engine.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: users.locale stays closed and stays interface-only: neither the response choice nor detection write to it. The Account page shows both side by side, and the PATCH /users/me/preferences route accepts both fields as OPTIONAL and independent. The list of accepted languages is that of the ICU of the Node running the api. A rare ISO 639-3 code that ICU does not name is refused, declared — no plausible response language is in that case. There is no consumer in the engine yet: no turn changes behaviour with this ADR. The transport (the ephemeral per-turn guidance) is AT-164; detection and confirmation, AT-163. Until then, choosing a language in the Account is stored and shown, and does not yet reach the model — the screen does not claim otherwise. The per-session override is allowed in a closed session: it does not trigger a turn nor write to the event log.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-09-29 (AT-139, story HS-024, epic EP-016). On top of ADR 0159, which remains valid in everything that is not the reference's FORM: index digest, the three trees, what the check does not cover and why. Maintainer decision of 2026-09-27, written in the AT-139 note, which called it "ADR 0171" — a number that was reserved and never written; this ADR is that one, and 0171 remains vacant. The decision had two halves. This ADR records the one that went in — the form and the lint — and declares why the other, enabling Dependabot for images, did not go in (see What this ADR does NOT do).
documents.s: Status

documents.t: ADR 0159 pinned the 39 third-party image references by digest, with the tag in a comment beside it (neo4j@sha256:… # 5.26-community; in a Dockerfile, on the line above), mirroring the form of actions (uses: x@<sha> # v4). And it declared the price: a digest freezes, and "enabling Dependabot's docker ecosystem is a separate decision". The decision came on 2026-09-27 — Dependabot docker — with a condition: first measure whether its PRs pass the pin lint. The measurement (round 15 lane, which stopped at the gate, with no PR) knocked down ADR 0159's form: Dependabot does not read the tag in a comment, in any format. The comment its github-actions reads is a convention of THAT ecosystem; docker has no equivalent. A digest-only pin is updated to the latest digest (update_checker.rb). pgvector, neo4j and node would go to another major, with the comment still asserting the old tag and the lint GREEN — the check verified the comment's presence, not its truth. The compose × workflow duplicates (pgvector and ollama in the services: of ci.yml/golden-set-*.yml) would make every bot PR be born red by ADR 0159's own "same tag, two digests" rule: no ecosystem reads workflow services:. CloudNativePG's imageName also stays outside any ecosystem. And there was a reference in the repository that already had the other form, for another reason: CNPG's imageName is postgresql:16.10@sha256:… because the operator's webhook REFUSES a digest-only reference — it reads the Postgres version from the tag. That is, the imagem:tag@sha256: form was already proven in the repository by Kubernetes, by kubeconform and by the k3d bootstrap.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: 1. The third-party image reference becomes imagem:tag@sha256:<índice>. image: neo4j:5.26-community@sha256:22ec5cd0… FROM node:24.11.1-alpine3.21@sha256:b8f7c905… AS deps With both present, Docker pulls by the digest: the tag is information for the reader, and the digest decides the bytes — ADR 0159's immutability stays intact. What changes is that the tag is now read through the SAME syntax by whoever executes (Docker), whoever updates (Dependabot) and whoever reviews. The digest is still the INDEX one, never a platform's. The 39 references of the three trees migrated without changing any digest — 29 in docker/ (16 in compose, 13 FROM), 4 in deploy/k8s/ and 6 in .github/workflows/. The tag comments went away: the reference is the source, and an equal comment would be a second copy to go stale. 2. The lint derives the tag from the reference and fails what contradicts it. scripts/ci/imagens-pinadas.ts fails, besides the mutable reference: digest without an inline tag — including ADR 0159's form, with the tag only in the comment, because it is the one the bot would update to latest; a comment asserting another tag — a comment that is ONE token with a digit (# 5.26-community, # pg16) and diverges from the inline tag. A comment is still allowed (the decision says "comment out or equal"); what fails is the leftover of a version bump. Prose and a loose word without a digit do not assert a version and are not judged; a comment at the end of the FROM line — still failed, now with its own reason: Docker's parser does not accept it (ADR 0159); the same tag with two digests — the key becomes nome:tag read from the reference. Each rule is proven by mutation in imagens-pinadas.spec.ts: turning off any of the five breaks at least one test.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: ADR 0159's form now fails. Whoever copies an old example (from ADR 0159, from an old PR) gets the message telling them to put the tag inline, with the reason. The runbook (Bumping a third-party image), the supply chain page and CLAUDE.md now show only the new form. The comment stops being mandatory, and that is the inversion of ADR 0159's argument, not a loosening: there it was mandatory because it was the ONLY place for the tag; here the tag is in the reference, and what the check requires is that it exists and that nothing beside it contradicts it. No version changes. Every digest is the same as before; docker build --check passes on the nine Dockerfiles, a real build (docker/backup/Dockerfile.prod) completes, docker compose config passes on the touched composes and kubectl kustomize + kubeconform on the overlays.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: It does not enable Dependabot for images, and the reason is a blocker the 27/09 decision did not cover. The decision called for "a step that aligns the workflows' services: in the bot's PR", in the mould of dependabot-justifica-pin.ts. That step would have to PUSH a commit changing .github/workflows/*.yml to the bot's branch, and GITHUB_TOKEN cannot do that: it does not have, nor can it receive through permissions:, the workflows permission, and GitHub refuses the push ("refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow … without workflows permission"). Documented by the GitHub community and not measured here by execution. There is a second cost, already known in the repository: a push made by GITHUB_TOKEN does not trigger workflows, so the alignment commit would stay without checks until a human re-triggered it. Enabling docker/docker-compose without the step would make every bot PR touching pgvector or ollama be born red. The existing paths — which are the maintainer's decision, not this ADR's — are in the AT-139 report: a credential with workflows (GitHub App or token) only for that step; removing the literal from the workflows (the image: of a services: accepts the needs context, and a previous job would read it from the compose — a duplicate that does not exist does not diverge); the step only DIAGNOSING and a human applying it; or a bot ignore for the two duplicated images. Until then, bumping a digest is the runbook procedure. It does not extend dependabot-justifica-pin.ts to image pins. A bot PR touching docker/** would hit the drift (config-e-inferencia, block), and AT-094's decision limited the bot-written line to ACTION pin swaps. Widening that class is a separate decision. It does not cover what was already out: the product's own images, interpolated references, multi-stage stages and Helm's otel-collector-values.yaml (ADR 0159). And two images stay in the MANUAL procedure, with or without Dependabot, because they live outside the three trees or in a key no ecosystem reads: CNPG's imageName and the image of the QA golden-set cases (IMAGEM_DO_GOLDEN_SET_QA, a TypeScript constant — already in inline form). It does not create an RN. The rule is a sibling of the actions one and lives, like it, in CLAUDE.md and in docs/explanation/cadeia-de-suprimentos-do-ci.md.
documents.s: What this ADR does NOT do

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-09-29 (AT-238, story HS-063, epic EP-029). Implements the AT-235 specification with the sixteen maintainer decisions of AT-236 (2026-09-28) and the 2026-09-29 decision on the adoption criterion, below. It replaces no ADR: it adds a piece outside the provider contract of ADR 0041 and the model catalog of ADR 0042, and reuses metering, the budget (ADR 0110) and the holder's credential (RN-058) without changing them.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Today whoever chooses the tool for each step of an agent is the user's chat model, looking at a catalog of 7 to 19 definitions on every call. The measurements of 2026-09-27 to 29 (docs/explanation/medicao-do-jev.md) put Jev — the typesafe/jev-1.13 model of OpenRouter's Decisions API, which answers a multiple-choice question with probabilities — against 328 real steps already recorded: Jev top-1: 73% (66–79%), below the 90% AT-237 required for Jev to CHOOSE alone. Choosing and forcing does not work. menu coverage of policy P3: 91% (85.1–94%) — the fraction of steps in which the tool the agent actually called is INSIDE the menu {Jev's choice, previous tool of the same run}. Jev's top-2 covers 90%. Coverage is the CEILING of end-to-end accuracy (that of the chat model, now over 1.6 tools instead of 7.4), not the accuracy. P3 offers ONE single tool in 98 of the 160 validation steps, and the definitions the model reads per call drop from 746 to 138 tokens. Jev, therefore, serves to restrict the menu, not to decide for it — and that is what AT-236 had already decided (answer 12: Jev only restricts).
documents.s: Context

documents.t: AT-237's adoption criterion was a confidence interval lower bound of 90%. No policy reached it (P3: 85.1%). On 2026-09-29 the maintainer lowered the criterion to 80%, with the numbers above in front of him, and ordered P3 to be implemented. This is the owner's decision, not a finding: P3's lower bound (85.1%) exceeds 80%, and no other text in this repository should say adoption "passed the 90%". What the measurement does NOT prove remains declared: coverage is a ceiling, and the end-to-end accuracy measured in replay was between 62% and 91% depending on the hypothesis about the chat model; the Wilson interval treats 160 steps as independent and they are 10 runs — the honest interval is wider; the real validation is AT-239, live, comparing the turn's steps, latency and cost with and without Jev. This ADR delivers the mechanism, on by default as AT-236 ordered, with the per-workspace switch at hand.
documents.s: The maintainer's decision on the criterion (2026-09-29)

documents.t: 1. The router lives in the api, inside llm-turn, behind its own port. ToolRouter (apps/api/src/application/ports/tool-router.port.ts) is not an LLMProvider and is not in the LLMProviderRegistry: Jev decides, it does not converse, does not go through the provider contract suite and does not enter the models catalog. The adapter (JevToolRouter) talks to POST https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions, with the format MEASURED in scripts/jev/jev.ts — questions is an object keyed by the question id (the AT-235 note wrote a list, and the API answered 400). A single use case, DecidirFerramentaDoPassoUseCase, is called by BOTH turn use cases (RunLlmTurnUseCase and StreamLlmTurnUseCase) after the resolved provider and the budget gate pass and before provider.chat. Seven conversational agents, the ToolLoop of dev agents and gates, and the Infra Lead all go through them (AT-236 answer 2); only the Anamnese (paused) and the compaction summarizer stay out. 2. When it is consulted — all conditions, and only then is there a call: the turn model's provider is openrouter (AT-236 answer 1, reading (a)); the request carries two or more tools; there is an agent in the turn; the engine did not ask for the whole catalog; the workspace did not turn it off. Jev's key is the SAME one already decrypted for chat — the workspace holder's (RN-058) — and no new credential read is born. With provider ≠ openrouter no call goes out, not even the workspace read. 3. The policy is P3, and it only restricts. The step's menu is {tool chosen by Jev, previous tool of the same run}, in catalog order. If Jev answers responder_sem_ferramenta, or there is no previous tool in the step's catalog, the menu is the whole catalog (AT-236 answer 12: "whole catalog, only record"). There is no tool_choice: only the menu is restricted, the model can still answer in text (answer 7).
