There is no confidence threshold in v1 — the measured P3 does not use one, AT-236 answer 4 ordered it out of the measurement and P3's measurement does not produce one. Confidence is RECORDED on every step, and it is AT-239's job to propose a threshold (per agent, if the curves differ). 4. The state is what the product really has before the step — the fields of the escopo variant, the second round's winner, cut inside the api from the messages the engine already sends, with no database read: agente (the agentId), contexto (the beginning of the first system message, 1,500 characters), pedido (the last user message) and passos_recentes (the last 6 tool calls AFTER that message, argument and result cut at 500). Ceiling of 8 thousand tokens per request, a quarter of Jev's window; exceeded, fallback estado_grande. Two differences from what was measured, declared: contexto is the beginning of the real system, and not "actor identity + instruction" as in the replay; and in a dev agent under correction the pedido is the correction message, the last user, not the kickoff. 5. The turn NEVER fails because of Jev. HTTP error (includes the 404/410 of an alpha endpoint that changed), timeout (ceiling of 2,000 ms, TOOL_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_MS; 0 of 328 requests exceeded it in the measurement), network error, unexpected JSON, choice outside the options, large state, name collision with the reserved option: the provider receives the whole catalog and the reason goes to the event with RN-059's origin (infra for the first three, modelo for the two shape ones, codigo for ours). The adapter never throws, and the use case still protects itself with a last-resort try/catch. 6. Policy does not change. Jev does not approve, does not deny and does not choose a model. The tool remaining in the menu still becomes a Proposed Action and goes through decide() and the absolute ceilings as always; the router does not even import those modules, and an engine test asserts that its module does not know them. If the model calls a tool that was NOT on the step's menu (remembered from history), the engine dispatches it as today and the event only records foraDoCardapio (AT-236 answer 13: Jev narrows, does not forbid). The iteration ceiling stays intact: the Jev call is INSIDE the same llm-turn, and the loop only increments after dispatch. 7. Per-step record, for AT-239 to measure. The engine records tool_router.decided in the EngineApiClient facade (a single place, for the seven servers and the ToolLoop) with the menu before and after, choice, confidence, second option, previous tool, aplicado, motivoDaQueda, origemDaQueda, latency, cost and foraDoCardapio. Metrics come from a script over the log and over token_usage, never annotated. The api returns the step in the new optional field toolRouting of llm-turn and of the stream's final frame; an old engine ignores it. 8. Jev's spending is real spending. One token_usage row through the same RecordLlmUsageUseCase (the only metering path, with project, session and AREA budget): actor is the agent itself (answer 10 — with its own actor the spending would escape ADR 0110's area budget), provider = openrouter, modelId = null, modelName = typesafe/jev-1.13 (that is how the Spending tab separates Jev from chat, answer 8), estimated = false and costMicros = the RESPONSE's usage.cost, in micro-USD. The price per million is implicit (cost ÷ tokens of the response itself, answer 11) and the row says so in the new column price_implicit, keeping tokens × price = cost (RN-044) without pretending a catalog price exists. The budget gate is not re-checked between Jev and chat (answer 15). Jev's cost returns to the engine in toolRouting.custoMicros, and the ToolLoop adds it to its local budget without touching usage. Brabo's metering for CHAT records less than OpenRouter charges (catalog price, no cache nor reasoning); Jev's does not suffer from that, because it uses the cost the response returns. 9. The switch belongs to the WORKSPACE (answer 3), column workspaces.tool_router_enabled, default on, migration 0066, changed through PUT workspaces/:workspaceId/tool-router (owner, the owner of the key that pays). The api reads the flag from its own database in the turn path; the engine reads nothing and makes no extra HTTP. Off, no Jev call goes out and no event is born. The installation variable TOOL_ROUTER=jev|off that AT-235 proposed was NOT born: the maintainer's decision was per workspace. Only TOOL_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_MS was born. 10. The path for the agent to ask for the full catalog — AT-281 showed that 61% of steps would have a ONE-tool menu, and a wrong menu cannot become a dead end. The mechanism is the simplest one that does not open a new containment door: if the menu was restricted (aplicado) and the model answered without calling a tool (not even in text recoverable via ADR 0020) and without a provider error, the facade repeats the step once with catalogoCompleto: true, which makes the api skip Jev. The repetition asks for MORE tools, never one the agent did not have; the api trusts nothing from the engine beyond "don't restrict me"; the menu was never a security boundary. In the conversational agents' stream it only repeats if NOTHING was written to the person (a delivered delta cannot be undone). The repetition's cost is the two chat calls, both metered; the first one's toolRouting stays marked repetidoComCatalogoInteiro. Discarded: a request_full_toolset as a new tool (it is new tool surface in every agent, and the model with a one-tool menu has no reason to call it) and report_blocked as a signal (it ends the loop).
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Each eligible step gains a serial call (Jev, then chat): +~0.2–0.4 s of latency (the measurement's recorded rows) and ~US$ 0.00005 per step. The gain — fewer definitions per call, and maybe fewer steps — is a hypothesis, and AT-239 measures it. When Jev is wrong and the menu leaves the model without the right tool, the cost is one more round (item 10). The rate of that repetition is in the event (repetidoComCatalogoInteiro) and it is the metric that the menu is bad. The endpoint is ALPHA. If it changes, the manual smoke (jev-tool-router.smoke.spec.ts, ceiling US$ 0.05, skipped without OPENROUTER_TEST_KEY) fails and, in production, every step falls back to the whole catalog with erro_http or resposta_invalida in the event — the per-workspace switch exists for the case of the fallback being too noisy. A timeout on Brabo's side may have been charged by OpenRouter without us seeing the usage.cost: that spending does not enter token_usage. Declared, not measured. The key is one per workspace installation, not per agent nor per project.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: It does not measure the gain (AT-239) nor calibrate a threshold; there is no threshold in v1. It shows nothing on screen. AT-236 (answer 3) wants the screen to show that the step was routed by Jev, with the confidence, and (answer 16) the strip to narrate "choosing tool". The data exists (the event and the stream's tool_routing_started frame, which the engine ignores as an unknown type); the screen and the strip are apps/web work, outside this lane. It does not change the agent servers beyond what the facade already covers, does not route the Anamnese and does not put Jev in the model catalog. It does not decide on raising the 2,000 ms ceiling nor on the Dependabot ecosystem for the typesafe/jev-1.13 pin (bump by PR, answer 5).
documents.s: What this ADR does NOT do

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-09-29 (AT-247, story HS-071, epic EP-030, round 27). On top of ADR 0130 (the broker, the five-layer containment and the COMPUTED specification) and ADR 0144 (the broker serves mounted). It does not edit them: it adds a field to the specification and says why it opens no door.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured in real use on 2026-09-29: docker inspect of a project's container showed an empty User= (root) and CapDrop=[ALL]. The project folder, mounted at /work, is 755 owned by the operator's uid (1000). Root without CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE does not write into another uid's folder, and --cap-drop ALL is exactly what removes that capability. Result: npm install gave EACCES in every dev agent and in QA-automation; only write_file worked, because it writes through the engine process on the HOST, outside the container. Reproduced on real Docker (node:22-bookworm-slim, --cap-drop ALL, folder 755 of uid 1000): as root touch gives Permission denied; with --user 1000:1000 it writes. With a uid without an /etc/passwd entry HOME becomes / and npm dies at //.npm. DockerPort has five operations, the bind is ONE folder of a marked type and the type has no privileged/cap_add/free -v (ADR 0130). Any fix has to fit in that.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: EspecificacaoDeContainer gains usuario?: { uid, gid }. The CLI adapter translates it into --user <uid>:<gid> and --env HOME=/tmp (constant: a uid without passwd gets HOME=/). Without usuario, run comes out byte for byte as before. The api is who measures, since it reaches the folder (the base mounted by identity, or the managed root): GET /internal/projects/:id/container-spec now returns usuarioDaPasta (stat of the folder; null if it cannot measure, if the project is runner or if the owner is root). The broker composes usuario FROM THAT context — never from a request body: start has no body and pedidoDeExecValidado ignores any extra field. The broker revalidates (usuarioValidado): integers in 1..2^31-1, 0 refused naming the field. Root is the ABSENT one; an explicit --user 0 would be a loosening nobody decided. exec gets no field: docker exec inherits the container's user. It applies to container and mounted (the api measures the folder each one mounts); runner mode does not go through the broker and does not change.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: It opens no containment door. The process now has LESS power over the host than before (non-root instead of root), --cap-drop ALL stays, and there is no field where a caller writes user, capability, mount or network. The second option considered, giving back DAC_OVERRIDE/CHOWN/FOWNER, was refused: it loosens the containment ADR 0130 fixed and keeps root. A third, the broker doing stat itself, would require mounting the projects' folders in the broker (today it only has the socket) — more surface in a root-equivalent process. The api already reaches them. It is not BREAKING for the operator: an unreadable or root-owned folder falls into "as always". An ALREADY created container does not change until recreated (--user belongs to run); the next container_start already comes up right. Folder owner ≠ who the dev agent should be is not a distinction the product makes: the goal is to write where the operator already writes. Not measured: Docker Desktop (macOS/Windows), where the bind-mount uid mapping is different; rootless Docker; a folder on NFS with root_squash.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-09-30 (AT-283 and AT-284, story HS-073, epic EP-031, round 29). On top of ADR 0074 (the reachable theme, measurement in both themes, the eight syntax roles) and ADR 0036 (the rule "the handoff establishes the intent, measurement establishes the number"). It does not edit them: 0074's MECHANISM stays whole — boot by file, both themes measured, derived parity, the eight --syntax-* —; what changes is the NUMBER of almost every color token, and with it three things 0074 asserted about the dark theme.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: The dark theme was saturated petrol blue (--surface-0 #061b24, hue 198°, saturation ~71%) with cream text and a vivid terracotta accent (#d6633a). Owner decision on 2026-09-30: the product gets the market's neutral black dark, calm, with a soft terracotta accent (identity lives in the accent, not in the surface), and the light becomes the neutral of the same family in place of the sand paper. Three measured facts weighed before the switch: The dark theme carried contrast debt since PHASE 16. Five pairs in use were below 4.5:1 — --text-muted on --surface-1 (3.89) and --surface-2 (3.10), --accent and --danger on --surface-1 (3.88), and --success on --surface-2 (4.41). 0074 locked them by number, and four screens changed token to work around them (.hint, .link, the environment state block, the Shell's error navigation). The primary button had a "known exception". --on-accent (cream) on --accent gave 3.20:1 in dark; ADR 0036 refused to fix it because it "changes the brand across the whole UI". The same cream on --success in Button gave 2.07:1. Color outside the tokens. Three spots that paint with a runtime library (Mermaid, xterm, the minimap canvas) had 27 hand-written fallback hexes, in the former petrol, and the C4 "person" used the RAW palette --teal-400/600. Three agent colors were loose hexes in lib/agents.ts, calibrated only against dark. The Modal overlay was petrol in rgba. And two tokens in use did not exist: --surface-3 and --radius-pill.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: 1. The semantic values change; the names do not. No module needs to change references: --surface-*, --text-*, --accent*, --on-accent, states, --violet, borders, --code-bg, --diff-* and the eight --syntax-* keep the same names. A raw scale --neutro-* enters (000…950, hueless zinc) that both themes' surfaces, secondary text and borders reference; the four old raw matrices stay (nobody uses them in the UI, and removing them would buy nothing). 2. The number comes from measurement, not from the draft. The owner's draft was the starting point; where it failed, the number was adjusted until the floor passed: token (dark) draft final why --text-muted #71717a #86868f the draft repeated the debt (3.80 / 3.51 on card and header); the final measures 5.38 / 5.10 / 4.70 and stays below --text-secondary --on-accent (light) --neutro-900 white on #c8744f would give 3.46 and 2.68 on hover; neutral black measures 5.61 / 7.25, and 7.65 on --success, 5.24 on --danger token (light) draft final why --text-muted #71717a #696972 the draft gave 4.40 on --surface-2, and light closes text at 4.5 since 0074 The rest of the draft passed as it came: surfaces #0d0d0f/#141417/#1c1c21, borders #2a2a30/#3a3a42, text #ececef/#a1a1aa, accent #c8744f, states #3fb68b/#d4a13a/#e5534b, --code-bg #0a0a0c; in light #ffffff/#fafafa/ #f4f4f5, text #18181b/#52525b and the darkened terracotta #a4502c (5.08 against --code-bg, 5.58 with the button's white). The eight --syntax-* were recomputed against the two new --code-bg and pass 4.5:1 in both themes (the lowest is light's --syntax-type, 4.85). The accent stays terracotta: the hue stays at ~18° in both themes, and that is enforced by a test. 3. The dark debt ends, and what was a locked number becomes a FLOOR. The five debt pairs pass 4.5:1 in both themes, and the test now enforces the floor instead of "still at 3.89". The two INVERTED assertions of design-contraste.test.ts ("muted fails on card", "accent fails on card") were rewritten as floors, and the consumers revised: .link (AuthLayout) goes back to the --accent the mock always asked for; .hint (Input) stays on --text-secondary, now for hierarchy and not for contrast. The primary button exception ceases to exist, and the fix did not change the brand — it changed the TEXT on it. 4. Color outside the tokens enters the tokens (AT-284). apps/web/src/lib/tokens-padrao.ts keeps ONE copy of the primary theme's values for Mermaid, xterm and minimap, and tokens-padrao.test.ts fails when it diverges from :root. The C4 "person" moves to --accent on --surface-1. --agent-leve, --agent-frontend and --agent-secops are born with a value per theme and are measured at 3:1 on the three surfaces; lib/agents.ts now has only var(--token), and a test fails hexes. --overlay is the Modal veil, per theme. --surface-3 and --radius-pill are NOT born: the two uses fall to what they already rendered (--surface-1/--surface-2 and --r-pill), and design-tokens-existentes.test.ts fails the next var(--x) without a declaration in CSS nor a runtime write.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The CLAUDE.md gap "dark theme contrast debt locked by number (ADR 0074)" closes. The rule of never loosening a floor stays, now with no recorded exception. The modules' 111 color-mix() (AT-285) were NOT revised here: they mix tokens and remain valid, but each one's visual result changes with the new base, and the review belongs to its own lane. Several CSS module comments cite the old debt numbers (Shell.module.css, SinaisDoAmbiente.module.css, ProjectCard.module.css, ProjectRail.module.css, TurnActivityStrip.module.css, Input.module.css on the placeholder). The choices they justify remain valid; the cited number is historical. Updating them belongs to the modules review. The documentation site (website/src/css/custom.css) has its own palette and was not touched. The .design-sync previews that depend on contrast are invalid until the next visual validation (its own NOTES.md says so).
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-09-30 (AT-291 and AT-292, story HS-075, round 29; the vault's AT-273 merges into AT-292 by owner decision). On top of ADR 0038 (an external handoff addresses only an area lead or an agent without an area, validated in CreateHandoffUseCase) and ADR 0090 (AppSec delivers the threat model to three destinations). It does not edit them: it adds a state and an invariant to the handoffs table.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured in the dev code on 2026-09-30: HandoffStatus declared offered | accepted | completed | rejected, but only offered and accepted were written. There was no expiration, supersession nor dedupe. CreateHandoffUseCase inserted a new row on every call. Any repetition became a new offer: the agent repeating offer_handoff, the Criativo reconfirming readiness, the Staff returning another RFC. OfferInfraHandoffUseCase was not idempotent. A double click on "architecture ready", or two tabs, recorded the milestone twice and asked the engine for two Arquiteto closing turns and two offers to the Dev Lead — 2× Infra and 2× Dev Lead on screen. AppSec (criar_handoffs_appsec/3) creates three offers per story with run_design, to the same three destinations (arquiteto, dev-lead, infra). With N stories, 3N pending offers piled up. An offer to an agent that was already active stayed offered forever, and the screen showed it as actionable: accepting would activate again someone who was already up.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: New status superseded (migration 0064, only ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE). The offer that stopped being the current one changes status in the ROW, as acceptance already did, and gains a handoff.superseded event with handoffId, toAgent, motivo (agente_ativado | nova_oferta) and substitutaId. Never an UPDATE on an event: the handoff.offered that announced the offer stays as it was. The event lands in the OLD offer's session, with the system actor handoff-lifecycle, and goes in even in a closed session (it is not conversation, RN-581). At most ONE offered offer per (project, destination). The decision is pure (decidirOferta, domain/sessions/ciclo-de-vida-do-handoff.ts): no pending one, create; pending in the SAME session and the new offer brings no new artifact (null or equal) → return the existing one (desfecho: ja_oferecido), with no row nor event. It is the double click, the two tabs, the agent repeating the tool; any other case (NEW artifact, or pending in another session) → create the new one and SUPERSEDE the pending one (desfecho: substituiu_oferta). Why supersede, and not always return the existing one. The card asked for both options and preferred not to lose the new artifact. Returning the old one when the artifact changed would leave the rewritten brief (or the Staff's new RFC) without an offer carrying it. Returning a pending one from ANOTHER session would leave the requester with nothing to accept in the conversation they are in — and, if the other session already closed, with nothing acceptable anywhere (RN-581 refuses acceptance in a closed session). Returning only holds where nothing is lost: same session, same artifact. Concurrency via a TRANSACTION advisory lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('handoff:<projeto>:<destino>'))), not via a partial unique index. The index would require cleaning the duplicates that already exist BEFORE creating it, in the same migration — and the new enum value cannot be used in the transaction that creates it. Cleaning by marking rejected would lie; cleaning without an event would violate the rule itself. With the lock, the earlier duplicates converge on the next offer or activation for that destination, WITH an event. The lock is per destination, not per project: offers to different destinations do not wait on each other. An offer to an agent already ACTIVE in the project is refused, 409 agente_ja_ativo, with no row nor event. Active = agent.activated for it in a project session that is NOT terminal — the screen's reading (session-handoffs.ts) extended from session to project; a closed session stops its conversational agents. The message is the text the model reads (RN-163): the offer_handoff tool passes it on literally, and FalhaDeTurno.origem/1 classifies it as politica, not codigo. Activating an agent supersedes the pending offers to it, in ANY session of the project, through the three paths that activate: acceptance (which goes through ActivateAgentUseCase; the accepted one is already accepted and is not touched), direct activation and execution activation (by dev-<modulo>). OfferInfraHandoffUseCase idempotent. Each destination (infra, dev-lead) with a pending offer or already active is not triggered again; with both like that, nothing is written nor asked of the engine (desfecho: ja_oferecido, jaAtendidos saying why). Only what is missing is triggered: Infra active and Dev Lead without an offer asks only for the Dev Lead's, with no Arquiteto turn. AppSec only offers to whoever has not yet received one nor is active (RN-636). The engine asks the api in seAusente mode (create_handoff_if_absent/5), instead of checking beforehand: asking from here would race with another offer, and the api answers under the destination's lock. "Already offered" and "already active" do not become agent.error; a real failure is still narrated per target (RN-116).
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The screen gets one more status. GET .../handoffs returns superseded, and the creation routes return desfecho. The web types are regenerated here; what the screen DOES with the new status (not offering it as actionable, reading "active" from the project) belongs to the handoff-web lane (AT-293..295). The race of two clicks at the SAME instant on "architecture ready" still records the architecture.readiness_confirmed milestone twice. No offer is duplicated (the lock), and the Arquiteto's second turn is refused by the engine with 409 turno_em_andamento (ADR 0163). Also closing the event would require holding the lock during the engine call, which is network inside a transaction — refused. A new offer to an active agent ceases to exist, and with it "reactivating through the offer". Whoever rewrites the brief with the PO already active gets the named refusal; the artifact stays in the log and the conversation goes on with the active agent. Whoever needs a new round closes the session in which it is active. The threat model offer of a second story is not born while the first one's is pending (RN-636). The artifact stays in the log; the destination, when activated, reads the project's threat models. The pending offer does not point to the most recent one — that is the price of not superseding the offer that still awaits acceptance. Execution activation supersedes offers to dev-<modulo>, which today are not born (a subagent does not receive an external handoff, ADR 0038). The call exists so the rule holds the day the hierarchy changes, and costs one read per module. The earlier duplicates are not cleaned by the migration. They converge on the next offer or activation to the same destination. A destination that never again receives an offer nor an activation keeps its offered ones, as today.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-09-30 (AT-071, story HS-048, epic EP-027, round 30). Revises part of RN-001 — "terminal states have no exit" — and coexists with ADR 0061 (the session has an immutable kind, and the execution state is the execution.activated event). It edits neither: it adds a transition to the state machine and declares what it does not change. Three decisions of this ADR are a PROVISIONAL, CONSERVATIVE DEFAULT, AWAITING THE OWNER — the minimum role, the absence of a deadline and the refusal for a session with execution. They are marked as such below, and changing any of them does not require a new ADR: it is swapping the indicated line and the RN that cites it.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured on origin/dev (79e6b1209f), from the AT-071 survey (2026-09-13, b61bc49cd): session-state-machine.ts declared closed: [] and closed_abnormally: [], with the comment "Estados terminais: nenhuma transição sai deles", and the test fixed that. There was no session reopen/reabrir/retomar in api, engine, web, ADRs nor RNs. The real case (exp001, session fe57b393…): closed by heartbeat_timeout, 92 events, eleven artifact.business_rule, five pairs of structured questions. The whole conversation survives in the event log (RN-002) and the artifacts are events, but the session had no way to go back to accepting conversation — since RN-581 the api refuses, with 409 sessao_encerrada, every conversation event in a terminal session. "Opening a new session" is no substitute: activating an agent requires an accepted handoff in the session itself (agent-activation.ts) and the PO's kickoff reads the brief and rules of the session. Copying into a new session would duplicate artifacts and break the Criativo → PO chain. Both dependencies are closed: AT-072 (RN-581 — the heartbeat recognizes an ongoing conversation, with an 8h ceiling) and AT-073 (RN-580 — rehydration reads the whole conversation). A conversational agent stopped at closing comes back through the idempotent start_agent on the first message and rebuilds the history from the log. session.closed is not a session_events row: it is outbox. The only durable record of WHEN and WHY the session closed is the closed_at and termination_reason columns of the sessions row.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: One new transition, only from the terminal states, only to active. canReopen/assertReopen in session-state-machine.ts, SEPARATE from canTransition: ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS keeps closed: [] and closed_abnormally: [], so the generic route POST .../sessions/:id/transition keeps answering 409 to closed → active. closing → active stays forbidden by any path — the adoption in the shutdown drain depends on it (shutdown.ex). And a created/active session does not "reopen". Its own route, POST projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId/reopen, 200, use case ReopenSessionUseCase. Same design as TransitionSessionUseCase.activate: the engine is called (startSession) BEFORE the transaction, and its failure leaves the session closed as it was; under the lock everything is revalidated. What changes is state, and the previous closing becomes a NEW event. The sessions row goes to active with closed_at and termination_reason cleared. On the SAME seq counter (RN-002), through the usual funnel (AppendSessionEventUseCase), session.reopened goes in, actor user (who reopened), payload {from, to, closedAt, terminationReason} — the copy of what the column loses. Nothing is edited, deleted or renumbered; the kind is not touched (RN-097). PROVISIONAL DEFAULT — minimum role maintainer. One step above the generic transition (developer): reopening turns token spending back on in a session someone deemed finished. Lowering to developer is swapping the route's @RequireRole and the screen's roleAtLeast. PROVISIONAL DEFAULT — no deadline. Every closed session is reopenable forever. A deadline (e.g. 30 days) is a comparison with closed_at in the use case. PROVISIONAL DEFAULT — a session with execution.activated does NOT reopen. 409 sessao_com_execucao. findActiveExecutionSession picks the most recent active carrying execution.activated (RN-139): reopening an old execution session would return it to that search, and the next reactivation could divert the dev agents to it. The declared path to "execute again" remains opening a new session and activating execution in it (the "new execution" card). Engine: the closing that the reopening already undid stops nothing. SessionLifecycleWorker reads the session's status (ProjectSession.status/1, a direct read of the api's table, as the Anamnese already did) and, if it is no longer terminal, ignores the job with a log — a late or retried job would bring down the process and the conversational agents of the reopened session. With no row, closing goes on as always. Web. On the closed-session strip, "Reopen session" with a sentence about what comes back; inert below maintainer (roleAtLeast on the WORKSPACE role, the RN-471 gap already declared on screen), with the reason in TEXT. The api's refusal (execution, 403) becomes a toast with its sentence.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: RN-001 stops being literally true ("terminal states have no exit"): there is ONE exit, through its own route. RN-649 is the address of the new rule; RN-001 is not edited, and is pointed to by it. Second Psicólogo analysis: BLOCKED until the owner decides, with no new code. A second closing publishes session.closed again, and the PsychologistWorker short-circuits on the automatic path when a current analysis of the session already exists (alreadyAnalyzed). The post-reopening conversation gets NO automatic analysis; manual reprocessing (triggeredBy: "manual") remains available and supersedes the previous one. If the owner decides the second analysis is legitimate (the conversation grew), the change is in the worker. Today the Psicólogo is paused (PSYCHOLOGIST_ENABLED=false). A second graph consolidation is legitimate and idempotent: the Interacao is keyed by sessionId and the seq window extends monotonically (RecordInteractionUseCase). Per-session budget and measurement now have more than one active interval. A duration metric computing closed_at - created_at lies for a reopened session; the previous interval is in the session.reopened payload. Not measured here; no current script was changed. Heartbeat after reopening: the screen that reopens is open and connects the heartbeat; with no tab, the heartbeat would close it again (RN-064/RN-581, an ongoing conversation holds up to 8h). It is the usual behaviour of an active session. Known race window: if the transaction fails AFTER the engine brings up the SessionServer (concurrent reopening, which revalidation under the lock refuses), a process is left for a session still closed — the same price TransitionSessionUseCase.activate already pays. The heartbeat with no client ends it, and the report lands in a terminal session. offered handoffs stuck in the closed session become acceptable again on reopening (RN-581 refused acceptance only by state). The lifecycle of ADR 0182 still holds: if the destination was activated in another session while this one was closed, the offer is already superseded. Not touched, on purpose: the "Close" button in closed_abnormally (AT-155).
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-09-30 (AT-337, round 32). On top of ADR 0183, which is NOT edited: it marked three decisions as a provisional, conservative default, awaiting the owner, and this ADR records the owner's answer to all three.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: ADR 0183 opened an exit from the session's terminal states — reopening, through its own route (POST projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId/reopen) — and left three choices open, declared as provisional: the minimum role, set at maintainer, one step above the generic transition (developer) that closes the session; the absence of a deadline — every closed session reopenable forever; the refusal, with 409 sessao_com_execucao, of a session carrying execution.activated, so that findActiveExecutionSession (RN-139) is not diverted to an old execution session. The owner decided all three on 2026-09-30.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Minimum role developer. The same role that closes via the generic transition: whoever can deem the session finished can bring it back. 0183's argument for going one step up (turning token spending back on) does not hold given that the same developer can already open a new session and converse in it, spending the same tokens. viewer stays refused (403). The change is the one 0183 foresaw: the route's @RequireRole and the Session screen's roleAtLeast. No deadline — CONFIRMED. No comparison with closed_at. A session with execution.activated stays refused — CONFIRMED. 409 sessao_com_execucao; the path to execute again remains opening a new session and activating execution in it. Nothing else in 0183 changes: the dedicated transition (canReopen), the session.reopened event, the engine called before the transaction and the SessionLifecycleWorker that ignores the already-undone closing.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The three decisions stop being provisional. RN-650 now says developer, and RN-649 cites this ADR in the two confirmed decisions. docs/security-surface.md lists the route as role:developer; the route-surface.spec.ts test compares the table with the real annotation. The screen changes the text reason from "requires maintainer" to "requires developer" (key ativacao.reabrirExigeDeveloper, in both languages). Still open, and not decided here: the Psicólogo's second automatic analysis after reopening (Consequences of 0183).
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-09-30 (AT-311 and AT-312, story HS-079, epic EP-031, round 32). Owner decision, with the two questions of the AT-309 survey answered YES: "Can a single click 'I'm ready — the need is validated' close both gates, even with the product_brief produced after the click?" "Can the PO's acceptance be implicit in 'I'm ready'?" Revises the design of ADR 0095 (the necessidade-validada gate closes with a SEPARATE click) and RN-406. It does not edit 0095: it records what changes and what of it still holds.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured on origin/dev (94e5dc721d), from the AT-309 survey: "Validate need" locked nothing. The button was enabled only with artifact.product_brief in the session (hasProductBrief, session-readiness.ts), came AFTER "I'm ready to produce", recorded only necessity.validated (ValidateNecessityUseCase), and the gate is warn in docs/gates.yml — RN-406 itself says nothing in the product CHECKS the passage. Accepting the PO was one more click right after "I'm ready". The Criativo→PO handoff is born inside the turn that "I'm ready" triggers (CriativoServer.executar_confirm_readiness/1 → EngineApiClient.create_handoff → POST /internal/sessions/:id/handoffs), and the acceptance card called AcceptHandoffUseCase, which records the transition to accepted, handoff.accepted (actor the person), agent.activated (actor the person) and, by RN-635, the handoff.superseded of the other offers to the PO in the project. Three clicks — ready, validate, accept — to express one intent: "what the Criativo gathered is right, go ahead". 0095 explicitly refused merging the validation into confirm_readiness, with an argument that is still right: confirm_readiness alone is the structural FLOOR ("≥1 captured rule", RN-142), not a judgment of MERIT, and merging the two "would keep the shallow floor disguised as a new gate". What answers that objection here is the LABEL: the click stops being "I'm ready to produce" and becomes "I'm ready — the need is validated". The person declares both things with the words of both; the structural floor is still checked by the engine, and merit is still declared by a human.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: POST .../sessions/:id/readiness (ConfirmReadinessUseCase) records readiness.confirmed, calls the engine and, only if the engine accepted the turn, records necessity.validated with the same person as actor, productBriefId: null, via: 'readiness.confirmed' and the readinessEventId. A null productBriefId is the answer to the second half of the owner's question: the brief is born from the turn the click triggers, and the event points to the CLICK, not to a brief that does not exist yet. The engine's refusal (409 turn in progress, 422 no rule) surfaces before the second event: without an accepted turn there is no brief on the way, and the need is not validated. readiness.confirmed is still recorded BEFORE the command, as always (ADR 0163). The gate stays warn. Nothing started checking it, and promoting it remains a product decision with its own ADR, as 0095 said.
documents.s: 1. One POST, two events (RN-657)

documents.t: The readiness.confirmed of the new click carries the mark { necessidadeValidada: true, aceiteImplicitoDoPo: true }. When the engine creates the Criativo→PO offer through the internal route, the api asks (decidirAceiteImplicitoDoPo, a pure rule) whether it is the offer that click asked for — criativo → po, offered, from this session, carrying the product_brief born AFTER the most recent marked readiness.confirmed — and, if so, accepts it through AcceptHandoffUseCase, the SAME use case as the card, on behalf of whoever clicked. The auditable trail is the card's, with no new event: handoff.accepted and agent.activated with the person as actor, and the mark implicito: { via: 'readiness.confirmed', readinessEventId } in the payload of both. Of the two options the owner left (a new event, or the same ones with a human actor and a mark), the second was chosen because every reader today — canActivateAgent, the handoff list, the graph projection, the screen — already understands handoff.accepted; a new event would require teaching each one, and a forgotten one would read the PO as never accepted. No event is edited. Acceptance happens on the internal route and not on the click's POST because the offer does not exist at the moment of the click. The acceptance failure does not surface to the engine (the Criativo would narrate "I couldn't offer the handoff", false): it becomes a durable agent.error, actor system/aceite-implicito, with origin. The 400 "is not offered" is not a failure — another tab decided the offer in the interval, and that is already in the log.
documents.s: 2. The PO's acceptance is implicit, with the SAME events (RN-658)

documents.t: Measured: the Criativo expects nothing from the acceptance (the internal route's response is only matched with {:ok, _}), and the PO is activated by the same usual startAgent, whose kickoff is a GenServer.cast. The only difference is the MOMENT: the PO comes up inside the offer creation call, still in the Criativo's turn, and not after a human click.
documents.s: 3. The engine does not change

documents.t: The button is called "Estou pronto — a necessidade está validada" (en: "I'm ready — the need is validated"), the enabled title says what the click closes and that the PO comes in on its own, and the success notice repeats that. The "Confirm validated need" button went away, with handleValidateNecessity and the client's validateNecessity. The click also makes the PO the composer's recipient — it is the gesture of calling it, the same as accepting through the card (RN-631).
documents.s: 4. The screen

documents.t: For From three clicks to one, without touching any ceiling: accepting the PO does not provision a repository (only Arquiteto and Dev Lead, RN-582), does not merge nor push. Validation is still done by a PERSON, never by the Criativo — the anti-pattern 0095 existed to avoid is still avoided. The acceptance trail is the same as the card's, readable by every existing consumer, and the mark says which click it came from. Against, declared necessity.validated stops pointing to the brief it validated: the link is through readinessEventId, and the brief is the artifact.product_brief following that click. Whoever needs the exact pair reads the log in order. The validation is declared BEFORE the person reads the summary. That is what the owner decided; the gate is warn and measures the declaration, not the reading. POST .../agents/criativo/validate-necessity stays in the api, with no consumer on screen: it is the path for a session whose "I'm ready" predates this ADR (there the acceptance card also stays, because the old event does not have the mark). Removing it is an API contract break and is left for when no old session uses it. The PO comes up without a human click at the moment it comes up. The human decided earlier, at the click, and is the recorded actor.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: A new event (handoff.accepted_implicitly). Refused: see point 2 — every reader of handoff.accepted would have to learn the second type. Accepting on the click's POST, pre-creating the offer. Refused: the offer carries the product_brief as artifact and is born from the Criativo's turn; creating it earlier would require changing the engine and offering a handoff without the artifact that justifies it. Letting the engine call the human acceptance route. Refused: the human route requires an authenticated user, and an agent activating an agent is exactly what the internal route's description refuses. Here the api decides, through the mark the PERSON recorded.
documents.s: Alternatives considered

documents.t: ADR 0095 — the design this revises ADR 0163 — the click responds on accept ADR 0182 — superseded, preserved RN-406, RN-657, RN-658, RN-633, RN-635 apps/api/src/domain/sessions/estou-pronto.ts apps/api/src/application/use-cases/agents/confirm-readiness.use-case.ts apps/api/src/application/use-cases/agents/aceite-implicito-do-po.use-case.ts
documents.s: References

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-09-30 (AT-314, story HS-079, round 32; owner decision on 30/09: "Can a handoff offered by the PO (LLM) provision the local repository without a click?" — yes). On top of ADR 0165, which placed the repository's birth in the acceptance of the handoff to the Arquiteto and had, as an implicit premise, that this acceptance is always a person's click. It does not edit it: it adds a second author of the same acceptance, with closed conditions, and leaves the place of provisioning exactly where 0165 put it.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured in the dev code on 2026-09-30 (AT-309 survey): The PO finishes the backlog and calls offer_handoff(to_agent: "arquiteto") (po_server.ex, kickoff: "Cubra TODAS as regras com ao menos uma história. Quando o backlog estiver pronto, ofereça um handoff ao arquiteto"). The offer is born offered and waits for the "Accept handoff and start Arquiteto" click. That click is what provisions the repository (AcceptHandoffUseCase, RN-582). For the local repository — the only one the acceptance creates, because it is the only provider without a credential — the click chooses nothing: there is no hosting to decide nor secret to resolve. It is a confirmation step on a path without alternatives. Backlog coverage already has ONE computation in the product, computeCoverage (domain/backlog/coverage.ts), used by the Backlog tab (GetCoverageUseCase) and by the PO's read tool (ListBusinessRulesUseCase, RN-164): a rule is covered when at least one story cites it in businessRuleIds. The survey's table counted ~11 decision clicks (+N promotions) from the brief to execution; this is one of those that protect only themselves.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: When. The po → arquiteto offer is accepted by the system, in the SAME request in which the engine creates it (POST /internal/sessions/:id/handoffs), after the offer's transaction and never inside it, if and only if: the offer is offered; the backlog is covered — an objective definition, measured over what the PO records: the project has at least one business rule (artifact.business_rule) and no rule without a story citing it in businessRuleIds, through the SAME computeCoverage as the Backlog tab. Zero rules is not covered: "nothing to cover" does not prove the PO worked; the repository the acceptance touches is local and without a credential: the project has no repository (the acceptance will provision local) or the one it has is local, and the project has no git connection (OAuth) registered in project_git_connections; whoever opened the session still has, in the project, the role the human acceptance route requires (developer, effective role of RN-471). The decision is the pure predicate decidirAceiteAutomatico (domain/sessions/aceite-automatico-do-handoff.ts); each "no" has a named reason, and that is what the response to the engine returns. Whoever accepts is still AcceptHandoffUseCase. The new use case (AceitarHandoffAutomaticamenteUseCase) only READS and DECIDES; with "yes" it calls the usual acceptance, which provisions the repository BEFORE activateAgent (RN-582, ADR 0165). There is no second provisioning path. Auditable. The automatic acceptance's handoff.accepted is recorded with the SYSTEM actor {kind: 'system', id: 'handoff-auto-accept'} and payload automatico: true, emNomeDe (whoever opened the session — the repository is provisioned on their behalf, provisionedBy) and criterio (regras, cobertas, repositorio). The following agent.activated carries the SAME actor. Human acceptance does not change: actor user, without those fields. Failure does not surface. The offer is already committed when the automatic acceptance runs, and the engine waits for its response; an exception there would become "failed to offer handoff" on an offer that exists. So the failure becomes the NEW event handoff.auto_accept_failed (system actor, origem: 'infra', error) and the response says falhou. The offer card stays there when the acceptance did not get to mark accepted. The model is told. The internal route's response gains aceiteAutomatico: {aceito, criterio?, motivo?} and, with aceito: true, status: 'accepted'; the engine's offer_handoff tells the PO that the Arquiteto was already activated and that it should not offer again (re-offering would give 409 agente_ja_ativo, ADR 0182).
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The common path (new project, local repository, a PO that covers the rules) loses one click; the thread shows the acceptance with the criterion ("the backlog covers the N business rules and the repository is local"). A remote or credentialed repository still asks for the click, as the owner asked. A manual handoff (ADR 0109) too: it does not go through the internal route. A handoff offered by an LLM now produces a git effect (the local provider's git init --bare and the Gitflow bootstrap) without a human click. That is the declared price, and it is what the owner approved; the absolute ceilings (push, PR, deploy, merge into a protected branch — RN-418) do not move, because none of that happens in local provisioning. Offers to other destinations, and the offer to the Arquiteto by another agent, do NOT get automatic acceptance. Extending to another pair is a new ADR. The response to the engine takes as long as local provisioning and startAgent take, within Req's default receive_timeout. Not measured on a real installation in this session. Not measured: the engine was not compiled nor tested in this session (no Elixir in the environment); the new offer_handoff clause and its ExUnit test were written and are left for CI.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. Decided by the maintainer on 2026-09-30 and confirmed on 2026-10-01 (AT-343). Follows the mould of ADR 0174, which removed Intel Mac by the same path, and references ADR 0112 (the binary via bun build --compile), ADR 0106 (the npm package, which becomes the Windows path) and ADR 0150 (the install.sh, which already refused Windows entirely). It edits none of them.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Since ADR 0174 the matrix promised four targets, and the Release only received the two Linux ones. win32-x64 had a build fix on dev never exercised, and the workflow_dispatch rehearsal with an empty tag (the mode that attaches nothing) exercised it. The layers fell one by one, and the last one is not the runner's: Run 36775746724 — the binary BUILDS, and exits with code 1 on usage without arguments: ENOENT in realpathSync. The runner only recognized the compiled binary's virtual path for Linux/macOS (/$bunfs/root/); the Windows one is B:/~BUN/root/. Fixed (AT-343, apps/runner/src/binario-compilado.ts). Run 36779817686 — usage passes, and --self-test-pty fails with Cannot find package 'node-pty': the loader received the form WITHOUT the colon (B/~BUN/root/) and fell into the plain import('node-pty'). Fixed. In this same run darwin-arm64 and the two Linux ones PASSED with AT-342's own PTY reader (RN-688). Run 36780804339 — node-pty loads, and from cmd.exe only the ConPTY's initial sequences arrive (ESC[?9001h ESC[?1004h), not even the prompt. The self-test gained a PROBE that does not depend on input, to separate input from reading. Run 36781729045 — the probe decides: cmd.exe /c echo in a second PTY delivers 1 chunk (the same two sequences), the read stream gives end,close, and the child exits with -1073741510 — 0xC000013A (STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT). Under Bun, the net.Socket over the ConPTY's output named pipe ends after the first chunk; node-pty treats the end of the pipe as the end of the terminal, closes the pseudoconsole, and Windows kills the child. No input is involved — even a command that only writes dies. It is the same family as oven-sh/bun#25822 that removed Intel Mac: Bun's stream layer under node-pty. On Unix it had a workaround (the master's fd is a regular fd, and AT-342 reads it with fs.read, waiting on EAGAIN); on Windows the read side is a named pipe opened by node-pty itself as a net.Socket, and there is no fd the runner can read from outside without rewriting the Windows half of node-pty. Under Node, the same node-pty is what VS Code uses on Windows.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The platform goes. The standalone binary now promises THREE targets (linux-x64, linux-arm64, darwin-arm64), and Windows gets the npm path — npm install -g @brabo/runner, under Node. The same four places of ADR 0174 change together: build-runner-binaries.yml removes win32-x64 from the matrix and from ALVOS_ESPERADOS. checksums.txt declares absence only of what is a failure. The GET /runner-releases/binary proxy accepts the three, and refuses win32-x64 with its own 400 — naming this ADR and the npm command, without calling GitHub —, in the SAME table as the darwin-x64 refusal (SEM_BINARIO_POR_DECISAO, readable name and ADR per platform). install.sh already refused Windows entirely before any download (ADR 0150), and continues to: the refusal now also SAYS that the local agent there is the npm package, naming this ADR. The case of instalar_o_runner never had win32-x64 and does not gain it. The browser keeps detecting win32-x64 and does not request the download: it goes into SEM_BINARIO_PUBLICADO, which fails upfront and falls into the usual best-effort (falhaDoBinario → npm command, RN-473). scripts/ci/alvos-do-runner.spec.ts ties the four places together and now fails windows-latest in the matrix. The Windows fixes the rehearsal produced (the virtual path in the three forms, the node-pty loader, cmd.exe in the self-test and the probe) STAY: they are the starting point of the way back, and cost nothing to the other targets.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Keep the target and publish the binary that fails the terminal. Usage without arguments passes, but the Code tab's interactive terminal would die on the first output chunk, with the child killed by Ctrl+C. Publishing a binary known to be broken in the function that justifies it is worse than not publishing. Read the ConPTY pipe outside node-pty, as AT-342 did on Unix. It would require reimplementing the Windows half of node-pty (the pipe is opened and connected inside it), and a workaround of that size against an open runtime bug is debt without a deadline. Switch the binary's runtime (Node SEA) only for Windows. It would change ADR 0112's distribution mechanism for one target, with a second build and proof path. It is a bigger decision than this one, and fits in its own ADR if Bun does not fix it.
documents.s: Alternatives considered

documents.t: The standalone binary promise is three targets, and all three are PROVEN in rehearsal (runs 36779817686 and 36805241339, the latter already with the three-target matrix). The Release keeps receiving two until the next final tag exercises darwin-arm64. Windows users need Node installed to have the local agent, and the user service stays out (ADR 0147 point 5). The browser panel says so in text; install.sh too. Way back: when Bun fixes the named pipe stream in a release, re-enabling the target is a new ADR that returns win32-x64/windows-latest to the matrix and to the four places the spec ties together, the names with .exe in the proxy, and runs the workflow_dispatch rehearsal with an empty tag — the --self-test-pty probe says straight away whether reading came back.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-09-30 (AT-270 and AT-272, story HS-070, epic EP-030, round 34; owner decision on 30/09: "the real cost becomes the number" — when the provider returns what it charged, that is the value recorded and shown, with estimated = false; the catalog price stays only where there is no real cost). Complements ADR 0042 (frozen, auditable price) and ADR 0076 (the provider as a spending dimension) without editing them: the frozen price still exists and is still the number of every call whose response does not state the cost; what changes is which of the two sources wins when both exist. Extends to CHAT the design that ADR 0179 set for the cost of Jev's tool decision — the SAME price_implicit column and the SAME precoImplicitoPorMilhao function —, instead of a second way of saying "this cost is the real one".
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured in the dev code on 2026-09-30, before changing: The cost recorded in token_usage.cost_micros came from ONE place, repeated in three use cases — RunLlmTurnUseCase (276 of the 305 rows of the 29/09 real use), StreamLlmTurnUseCase (28) and SendChatMessageUseCase (1): calculateCostMicros(tokens, preço de models). No other path records metering (RecordLlmUsageUseCase is the only one, and it just passes the number on). OpenAICompatibleProvider.chat read, from the usage frame, only prompt_tokens and completion_tokens. It discarded usage.cost (the cost OpenRouter charged, in USD), model (the model that SERVED — the alias ~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest resolves to a dated version) and id (gen-…, the identifier GET /api/v1/generation?id= accepts). The finding of the real-use analysis (openai-compatible-provider.ts:237-245) reproduces byte for byte on dev. The gap is measured, not assumed: the 29/09 real use added up to US$ 0.314259 at the frozen price (20,000 / 600,000 micros per million), and the test key recorded US$ 0.5807 that day (1.85×). Repriced by the UNDERLYING provider that upstream_provider already recorded, the no-cache ceiling gives ≈ US$ 0.917. A hub's catalog price is that of ONE route; the hub charges for the route it used. usage.cost was already the spending source of all paid measurements done against OpenRouter (docs/explanation/medicao-do-idioma.md, medicao-do-jev.md, scripts/idioma/validar.ts): the field exists in the real /chat/completions response and it is through it that their spending was summed, never through the /key counter.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Precedence. When the usage chunk carries costMicros, it IS the row's cost_micros, the number the engine adds to the loop's local budget (the turn's usage.costMicros), what increments the project, session and area budgets, and what the Spending tab sums. Without it, the catalog's frozen price (ADR 0042) produces the number, as always. One domain function decides both things — custoDaChamada (domain/llm/custo-da-chamada.ts) —, and the three use cases go through it; there is no second rule. The price of a row with real cost is IMPLICIT. cost ÷ tokens, the same value in both price columns (the provider returns ONE cost; splitting it between input and output would be inventing the proportion), and price_implicit = true says so. That is what keeps tokens × price = cost (RN-044) reproducible, up to the rounding of the integer price, without pretending a list price produced the number. It is the SAME formula (precoImplicitoPorMilhao) and the SAME column as ADR 0179. What the catalog would have charged goes alongside, in catalog_cost_micros, only on rows whose number is the real one (null on the others). It is what the card asked for ("record the real cost alongside the estimate") and it is what allows measuring, row by row, the gap the 29/09 analysis measured in aggregate. estimated does not change meaning. It still says whether the TOKENS were counted by the provider or estimated locally (RN-041). A row with real cost has estimated = false because the cost only arrives together with the provider's usage; the mark that the COST is real is price_implicit. Reusing estimated for both questions would erase the distinction "the provider said 0 tokens" × "the provider said nothing". The resolved model and the generation id are recorded — resolved_model_name and generation_id, read from the frame's model and id by EVERY provider of the dialect (they are fields of the /chat/completions dialect itself, not a hub quirk). model_name stays the CATALOG name: it is the reports' dimension (RN-101/RN-186) and the link to model_id; swapping it for the resolved one would split the same binding into N report rows with every new dated version of the alias. Whoever reads the cost is a config hook, not the base. extrairCustoReal in OpenAICompatibleConfig, configured ONLY on OpenRouter (extrairCustoRealOpenRouter). A provider without the hook ignores a usage.cost even when present — the field's unit and meaning belong to the hub, and the Phase 9 rule is that a provider particularity becomes a hook/flag, never an if. No new capability is born in LLMProviderCapabilities: the cost is observed PER RESPONSE, and its absence degrades on its own to the catalog, row by row. BYOK is not real cost. With usage.is_byok === true, cost is the hub's fee and inference is charged by the provider separately; recording only the fee would be recording LESS than what was charged — the defect this ADR closes —, so the row falls back to the catalog. A cost that is not a finite, non-negative number is also "did not say", never zero; real zero (a free model) is real cost. The parts of input and output are recorded (AT-272, RN-666): cached_input_tokens (usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens) and reasoning_tokens (usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens), read by the base for every provider of the dialect, because they are OpenAI's own fields. They are PARTS of input_tokens/output_tokens, never added to them, and do not recompute cost: with real cost, the cache discount is already in the number; without it, the catalog has no cache price to apply, and inventing one would be another estimate. null is "did not say", distinct from 0. The measurement (medir-execucao.ts) now states, per agent, how much of the input was cache read — only over the calls that reported it, and in how many — and in how many the cost is the real one. The range the 29/09 analysis left as a hypothesis (between US$ 0.58 and 0.92, depending on cache) becomes measurable in new calls; the 305 old ones remain without the information.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The number of the Spending tab, of the budgets and of the loop's local budget becomes what OpenRouter charges, on the calls it measures. The same report sums real rows and estimated rows; price_implicit distinguishes the two per row. A budget may "jump". A budget calibrated on the catalog price sees, from here on, spending up to ~1.85× higher for the same calls (the 29/09 measure): the 70/90/100% thresholds arrive earlier. It is the requested behaviour — the budget becomes about money, not the estimate —, and it stays declared for whoever calibrated a ceiling before. The screen still says "estimated". The subtitle of the member's Spending tab (RN-101) states that the cost is estimated. How the screen distinguishes real from estimated — a label per row, a proportion, or just changing the sentence — is a product decision pending with the owner; no screen was touched here, and the api does not expose price_implicit on any route yet. Proof without a key. There is no OpenRouter credential on this machine: the proof is the RECORDED RESPONSE in the contract suite (openrouter-provider.contract.spec.ts, with the usage shape the paid measurements read) and the manual smoke (openrouter-provider.smoke.spec.ts) now requires price_implicit and the gen-… with a credential. The meaning of cost in BYOK is a READING of the documentation, not a measurement. One column, two authors. price_implicit was born in migration 0066 (Jev); this decision only adds a second writer of it, and migration 0067 creates only the three new columns. A row with price_implicit = true is either Jev (model_name = typesafe/jev-1.13, null model_id) or a chat call with real cost (model_id filled, non-null catalog_cost_micros); Jev does not record catalog_cost_micros, because it has no catalog price. Anthropic stays out of the parts. It reports cache in its own protocol (cache_read_input_tokens), which its adapter does not read; its rows record null in both columns. No other provider changes. What the resolved model and the id unlock — checking a row's charge with GET /generation?id=, repricing by dated version — remains to be built; here it is only recorded.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-259, AT-255, AT-258 and AT-257 — this one closes AT-170 —, story HS-066, epic EP-030, round 35; owner decision of 01/10, written in the activities). References ADR 0167 (automatic mode releases the path scope) and ADR 0055 (the terminal policy's path scope) without editing them: 0167 is not revoked — automatic mode still releases any command, including outside the folder —, and 0055 is still the ceiling, now compared against the folder where the command RUNS.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: The real use of 2026-09-29 measured three defects of one policy (analise-uso-real.md, items 9 and 11): "Always allow" turned automatic mode off. The seven dev agents received the *: auto_approve wildcard at 06:48:28–34 and, seconds later, got the terminal: auto_approve row recorded by the dev agent's "Always allow" (RN-509). The repository returned the SPECIFIC rule before the wildcard, with origin especifica, and decide() only recognizes automatic mode with origin curinga (RN-603). Result: 97 requests "compound command with at least one segment not covered by allow" and 37 "scope" with automatic mode lit on screen. The scope compared against the folder where the command does NOT run. The 37 "scope" ones were all /work/... or /tmp, compared against the HOST root (/home/<usuario>/projetos-brabo/<projeto>). With a running container, the engine executes the command INSIDE it (RN-492/RN-502), in /work, and translates the host cwd to /work only afterwards, in terminal_executor.ex. Automatic mode did not say, on screen, what it releases. The batch card of RN-661 said what it does NOT release; the agent card toggle and the ApprovalCard had different sentences, and none said that git commit and a local branch pass. Activity AT-259 proposed revoking the part of RN-603 that releases the scope. The owner decided the opposite on 01/10: "RN-603 is NOT revoked — since the command runs in the container, automatic mode keeps releasing any command, including outside the folder, as long as it is kept so that no problem occurs with the code Brabo is running". Measured on dev before changing (tests that failed on today's code): decide.spec.ts (5 cases of the root in the container), agent-autonomy.repository.spec.ts (the specific shadowing the wildcard) and approve-always-action.use-case.spec.ts (the measured scenario, end to end). Did not reproduce: the autopilot already approved git commit, git checkout -b/switch -c/branch and the git_commit/git_branch_create types with the wildcard on, and already held push/PR/merge/deploy, sudo/doas, container_remove, instruction_patch and parallelism — AT-259 closes only through AT-255 and the screen.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The *: auto_approve wildcard approves EVERYTHING, including the compound synthesized from permissions.json and a path outside the folder (RN-603, kept), and git commit and LOCAL branch creation. Still out, never auto-approvable: git push/PR/merge/deploy through the terminal (RN-418), sudo/doas, merge into a protected branch, container_remove, instruction_patch and parallelize/raise_max_parallel. An explicit deny still wins, and an ask WRITTEN in the file still asks — it is the user's rule, as it already was in RN-603.
documents.s: 1. Automatic mode is the AUTOPILOT

documents.t: The specific auto_approve under the auto_approve wildcard resolves as the WILDCARD, in the SAME repository that already resolved precedence (DrizzleAgentAutonomyRepository.resolve). Of the two forms AT-255 offered — not recording the specific when there is a wildcard, or the wildcard applying to the exemptions with the specific auto_approve —, it was the second, for three reasons: it fixes the rows ALREADY recorded in real use (the first would only avoid the next ones); the click still records the specific, which stays in effect if the toggle goes back to manual (with the scope, as always); and no new path is born — decide() does not change its rule, it just receives the right origin. A specific saying SOMETHING ELSE (require_approval, deny) still wins over the wildcard. AutonomiaResolvida gains especifica (the mode of the specific row, when it exists), and it is through it, and not the resolved mode, that "Always allow" decides whether the agent's pattern is already recorded.
documents.s: 2. "Always allow" does not turn the autopilot off (the simplest form)

documents.t: With a registered running container in a container or mounted project, the scope ceiling's root is /work (the mount point — the project's folder and .worktrees) plus the container's /tmp. The host cwd is translated to /work by the SAME rule as the engine (cwd_para_container/2): the root becomes /work, what is under it becomes /work/..., what is outside stays as it came. In mounted the translation is bijective (the bind-mount is the folder's identity). Without a container, the root is the project folder on the host, and the host's /tmp stays OUT — it belongs to the whole machine, including Brabo. This applies to whoever is NOT on autopilot — the specific terminal rule —, because the autopilot does not go through the scope. projectScopeRoot does not change and does NOT merge with permissionsFilePath (RN-478): the host root is still the input, and the root in the container is DERIVED from it in path-scope.ts. The container auto-approval FLOOR (RN-493) is still only for container mode; the new DecideContext field (execucaoNoContainer) is WHERE the command runs, and it is a different thing. runner stays out, on purpose: the host-vs-container choice is internal to the runner (ADR 0137), and a restarted runner with the container up routes to the HOST (RN-558) — the api does not know which of the two will happen, and releasing /tmp for someone who may be on the host would be releasing the /tmp of the user's machine.
documents.s: 3. The scope compares against the REAL execution folder

documents.t: ONE list (OQueOPilotoLibera), in the THREE places where automatic mode is turned on: the Executors batch card (open), the ApprovalCard and the agent card toggle (collapsed, under the sentence that already existed). The "does not release" half is the text RN-661 already had, reused; the "releases" half is born here.
documents.s: 4. The screen says what the autopilot releases and what it does not

documents.t: The decision's condition — no problem with the code Brabo is running — is not policy, it is the container's containment, and it is proven end to end in apps/broker/src/contencao-do-brabo.spec.ts: the project container mounts ONE folder, always at /work, STRICTLY below the broker's root (managed or base), with no Docker socket, no --privileged, no host network, and an empty/absolute/traversing segment is refused before any Docker call. Added to the guards preventing the root from containing the checkout (baseSobrepoeOCheckout in preflight.mjs, tested in scripts/dev/base-de-projetos.spec.ts) and to the refusal to execute without a container (RN-502/RN-507), the autopilot's command does not reach Brabo's checkout.
documents.s: 5. The owner's guarantee: containment, proven

documents.t: Owner decision of 01/10 (AT-257, which closes AT-170 — point 6 of ADR 0055, left open there): the click stops recording the whole command, byte for byte, and records ONE pattern per SEGMENT of the command, in the VERB + SUBCOMMAND unit (npm test, git status); an argument that is not a word generalizes to the verb (cat src/x.ts → cat); verb + flag stays EXACT (it is the form, where findings Z/AD say verb and invocation diverge); and a unit that is a prefix of an RN-418 ceiling (git remote, gh pr) stays exact, or disappears if even the exact one is. AT-170's four sub-questions are answered: the unit is this one; it does NOT inherit the verb allowlist (no verb list is born, and doubt between argument and subcommand falls on the narrow side); whoever records is the same role as today; and precedence with the wildcard is point 2's. Detail in RN-675.
documents.s: 6. The unit of "Always allow": verb + subcommand, per segment

documents.t: The scenario measured on 29/09 stops asking for approval: wildcard + "Always allow" stays on autopilot (non-regression test in approve-always-action.use-case.spec.ts). The specific rule terminal: auto_approve stops asking for approval for /work/... and /tmp with the container up, and starts asking for a HOST path in a command (which does not exist inside the container — the engine translates only the cwd, never the arguments). What the containment proof does NOT cover — declared, not fixed here (the owner's decision was to describe, not patch policy): In the PRODUCTION compose (docker/docker-compose.prod.yml) nothing on the host checks that BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE does not contain the folder the compose runs from (the checkout, or the .env folder). preflight.mjs only runs in pnpm dev, and caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido compares against the api's OWN cwd (/app), which is never the host path. With such a base, a mounted project whose folder is the checkout mounts the checkout at /work — with or without autopilot. In the INSTALLATION, install.sh refuses a base overlapping the installation folder only at consent (consentir_base), without its own test; an .env edited afterwards is not checked again. In runner mode, nothing compares the project folder (or the local agent's base) with a Brabo checkout or with the installation folder on the user's machine — the api compares against its own cwd, and the runner's guard.ts only restricts to $HOME on Linux. segmentoDeProjetoValidado (packages/docker-port) accepts . as a segment: <raiz>/. passes raizDeProjetoValidada as the root itself and would mount ALL projects of that root. The api never produces . (the mounted segment comes out normalized, and the managed one is [A-Za-z0-9_-]), so it is not reachable today; but the broker exists so as not to depend on the caller being correct. It does not reach the checkout (the root does not contain it), it reaches the OTHER projects. The egress network is bridge: the container reaches the ports the machine publishes, including those of the api and the engine. Files no; services, yes — behind authentication. "Always allow" on a compound now releases the NEXT compounds with the same verbs and subcommands — including, for a verb without a subcommand (cat, rm, cd), the verb with ANY argument. It is the expansion AT-170 asked to be decided and not deduced; outside the autopilot the path scope still limits where, and the ceilings still run after the file. TYPED git_push and pr_open are not a ceiling in decide(): activation seeds auto_approve for them per dev-<modulo> (ADR 0053) and the wildcard also approves them; what holds them is "Always allow" refusing to record them (AT-320) and the ceiling on merging into a protected branch. Not changed here.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-260, story HS-065, epic EP-030, round 35; owner decision on 01/10: "container_start is born seeded auto_approve on acceptance of the Infra handoff, and the server triggers the start-up on its own when there is module_routing, without depending on the model"). Revises the sentence "never seeded for auto-approval" of ADR 0133 (RN-491) and relies on the containers page of ADR 0136 without editing either: the election path, the ceilings and the refusals they set remain; what changes is WHO triggers the first start-up and whether it waits for a click. In the same round, and by the same 01/10 decision (AT-262, RN-672): "the Dev Lead is offered by Infra, only with the container running; the Arquiteto's double handoff goes away". That changes the relationship between roles that ADR 0053 set (the Dev Lead is born from the Arquiteto) and that ADR 0085 recorded in docs/fluxo.yml, without editing them — decision 7 below.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured in the dev code on 2026-10-01, before changing: In the real use of 29/09 (session be70) Infra wrote that it would bring up the container "in parallel" with the infra PR (seq 282) and did not call propose_container_start; the only attempt was container_start_via_runner (seq 280), refused by mode (mounted). The container only came up at 06:47:53, by a human on /containers. The start-up depended entirely on the model: the Infra Lead's kickoff (build_kickoff) asked for the election in step 4, and nothing in the code did it if the model did not. AT-264 (RN-668) had already closed both halves of the SILENCE — the whole batch of the response is dispatched before the PR's HALT, and the turn's close says, with a server sentence, when the start-up was NOT proposed —, but it left declared that the start-up as a server step was this activity. What RN-668 promises ("was not proposed") was true, but it was the common outcome. The card text said the kickoff made the start-up optional ("before, after, or never", infra_lead_server.ex:955-961). It no longer reproduces: RN-668 rewrote step 4 ("it only happens if it is called BEFORE it or in the SAME response"). The rest reproduces. Acceptance of the Infra handoff seeded TWO autonomies (INFRA_AUTONOMY_SEEDS in accept-handoff.use-case.ts): open_infra_pr: auto_approve and terminal: deny. container_start stayed require_approval by default — maintainer in decide.ts, OUTSIDE the absolute ceilings block and PROVEN able to reach auto_approve through agent_autonomy (decide.spec.ts, "agent_autonomy auto_approve CONSEGUE chegar a auto_approve") —, and ProposeActionUseCase already executes the start-up on the auto_approved path (the branch existed for whoever configured permissions.json). That is: the whole mechanism already existed, the seed and the trigger were missing. /containers (ADR 0136, RN-521) proposes as a HUMAN (actor.kind: 'user'), and agent_autonomy is only read when the actor is an agent. Seeding for Infra changes nothing on that page.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The seed. Acceptance of the handoff addressed to infra seeds a THIRD autonomy: container_start: auto_approve, alongside the usual two. Only it: container_start_via_runner and container_stop remain configurable and never seeded, and container_remove remains in the absolute ceiling of decide.ts (RN-495), which no autonomy crosses. The trigger is a SERVER step, not a new tool. In the Infra Lead's kickoff — the turn born from the accepted handoff —, BEFORE the first trip to the model, the server reads the infra context (one read, the same as the kickoff text) and, if there is CURRENT routing (artifact.module_routing with status: roteado and at least one candidate) and the project comes up through the broker (container/mounted), proposes container_start by the SAME path as the tool (propor_container_start/2): the local refusals by mode and state (RN-566, RN-610) first, then propose_action, where the api refuses without a broker (RN-591), resolves autonomy and — auto_approved — executes ExecuteContainerStartUseCase, which elects the image through DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase with decidedBy: 'infra-lead' (RN-491). No parallel election path is born. The server's election is deterministic. The candidate of the LARGEST number of modules in the routing; on a tie, the one that appears first. Network none and default resources — the same defaults as the tool. The rationale says it was the server and why ("the Arquiteto's candidate for N of M modules"). It is always one of the candidates, and the api refuses any other. The trail is a tool's, without lying about who called. The step records durable tool.call (with origem: "servidor") and tool.result, and does NOT put a role: "tool" message in the model's history: there was no call from it, and a tool response without the call is refused by providers. The model learns about the start-up through the kickoff TEXT, which now says what ALREADY happened (proposal and the returned status, or the refusal and the reason) instead of asking for the election. runner stays as it is. The container_start_via_runner path (brings up the already decided image, on the user's machine) gets no server step nor seed: the owner's decision did not touch it. The kickoff of a runner project keeps the usual steps, and the start-up stays proposed by the model and decided by a human. RN-668 remains coherent. The server step marks the turn through the SAME registrar_subida/3 as the tool: a start-up proposed by the server does not get the "was not proposed" sentence at the close; a server start-up REFUSED (and not corrected by the model) gets the refusal sentence, which is true. The close still speaks in the cases where the start-up was not the server's (no routing, runner) and the model did not propose it. The Dev Lead is offered by Infra, with the container running (RN-672). "Confirm architecture ready" now offers only to Infra: the offerDevHandoff, the engine's offer-dev-handoff route and the Arquiteto's :offer_dev_handoff/handoff_dev_pendente go away. The Infra Lead's server offers infra → dev-lead (if_absent mode, ADR 0182) when the project's container is REGISTERED running, asking at the end of each of its turns and when the outbox's container.running arrives — the second consumer of that event, alongside the dev agents' wake (RN-502). The repository's second door on acceptance to the Dev Lead (RN-582) remains: the acceptance is the same, only who offers changed.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The promise becomes true by construction in the common case. A container/mounted project with routing has the start-up proposed — and, with the seed, executed — before the model says anything. "Never seeded" stops being true, and it is the ONLY rule that changes.
