The minimum role remains maintainer, read as the EFFECTIVE role of whoever opened the session (resolveEffectiveRole.forProject(session.createdBy)): a session opened by a developer gets deny, as before, and the kickoff states the refusal. A deny in permissions.json still wins over autonomy. Turning it off means touching the SPECIFIC rule. The agent card's manual/auto toggle writes the wildcard (*, RN-153), and a specific rule wins over the wildcard: putting Infra on "manual" does NOT turn this seed off — the same situation that already held for open_infra_pr since Phase 4a. Whoever wants the start-up with a click needs to change Infra's container_start rule. Declared, not resolved here. Re-accepting Infra re-seeds. Acceptance does an upsert, as it already did with the two previous seeds: a new handoff to Infra in a new session puts auto_approve back. Same behaviour as the existing seeds. The kickoff may wait for the start-up. The auto-approved container propose_action answers after the broker's start (225 s ceiling in the engine, RN-605), and the step runs before the first trip to the model: the kickoff turn stays working for that time, in a Task, with "Stop" served as always. A large image that blows the pull ceiling (RN-605) arrives as failed, and the kickoff tells the model. An infra context that fails brings up nothing. Without the context read there is no routing to elect; the kickoff degrades as before and the start-up goes back to depending on the model in that turn. The server's start-up also only happens at the kickoff: gate correction and composer messages do not repeat it. The Dev Lead stops being acceptable without a container. The chain becomes Arquiteto → Infra → (container running) → Dev Lead → execution, and docs/fluxo.yml says so: the Arquiteto's handoff-duplo exit becomes a single handoff, to Infra, and Infra gains two exits to the Dev Lead (the container and the handoff). A project whose container never comes up does not reach the Dev Lead by this path; the manual handoff to an agent of choice (ADR 0109) still exists. The outbox notice is at-most-once, like Engine.Dev.Wake: with no Infra Lead up when container.running arrives (session closed, engine restarting), the offer waits for the end of Infra's next turn. A runner project depends on that notice, because its start-up never happens inside an Infra turn. The decide.ts comment saying "não está semeado em INFRA_AUTONOMY_SEEDS" becomes outdated with this change, because the file belongs to another front in progress in the same round; the rule itself (container_start outside the ceilings, able to reach auto_approve) does not change.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-267, owner decision of 01/10). Revises, only for the user's MESSAGE, the synchronous turno_em_andamento refusal of ADR 0163. ADR 0163 is not edited: the immediate acceptance it decided still holds, and the named refusal still holds for commands that are not speech (the PO's story review, the Criativo's readiness, the Arquiteto's handoff offer). Rule: RN-673.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Since ADR 0163 a message arriving at a conversational agent in the middle of a turn was refused with 409 turno_em_andamento and a durable agent.error. That closed the silence — before, the 409 was a silent 202 —, but not the defect: the api records the chat.message BEFORE talking to the engine (SendAgentMessageUseCase), so the message stayed in the thread looking said and never reached the model. The screen asked "send it again when it finishes". The real use of 2026-09-29 (session be70) measured three of these on the same day, one per agent: seq 100 (PO, 06:28), seq 268 (Infra Lead, 06:39 — "infra ainda está executando") and seq 312 (Dev Lead, 06:46 — "ok"). All three are recorded as chat.message and none was read. Reproduced in this tree's code: TurnoAssincrono.iniciar/3 answered {:error, :turno_em_andamento} with from and a turn in progress, and AgentCommandController.responder_ao_aceite/2 converted it into 409 — the agent_command_controller_test.exs test ("turno já em curso: 409 nomeado") pinned exactly that outcome. The only queue precedent was the Infra Lead's (correcoes_pendentes, RN-617): IN MEMORY, for gate correction, never for user speech — and lost on an engine restart. The owner's decision (01/10), which is the requirement: a message arriving during a turn enters a persisted queue that survives restart; N messages = 1 turn: at the end of the turn in progress, the pending ones are read together, in order, in a single turn; each one can be cancelled while pending, by whoever sent it, with the minimum role the message route already requires; ceiling of 10 pending per agent and session, and above that a named refusal; it applies to the SEVEN conversational agents through the same path (TurnoAssincrono), never per server.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The queue lives in TurnoAssincrono, and its state lives in the event log. TurnoAssincrono.receber_mensagem/4 replaces the direct iniciar/3 in the seven handle_call({:user_message, …}). With no turn and no queue, it starts the turn as always (:ok, 202). With a turn in progress and the queue below 10, it enqueues, records chat.message_queued and answers {:ok, :enfileirada, posicao} — 202 too, with the body {entrega: "enfileirada", posicao}. With the queue at the ceiling, {:error, :fila_de_mensagens_cheia}: named 409 and durable agent.error (the message is recorded and will NOT be read — the same honesty ADR 0163 required of the old refusal). The server only says how speech becomes a turn. Each of the seven now has turno_de_mensagem/2 (the same assembly the handle_call did inline) and the guard in the state (:montar_turno_de_mensagem). TurnoAssincrono decides WHEN; the server, HOW. No server got its own queue. At the end of the turn — finalizar/1, never suspender/1 — the queue becomes ONE turn. Delivery is a message to itself (:entregar_fila_de_mensagens), not a call inside the close, because the server still has its own close in the same handle_info (the Infra Lead drains the gate correction, the Arquiteto the handoff to the Dev Lead) and must not find a queue turn already up. The pending ones become a single text (FilaDeMensagens.texto_do_turno/1: one is itself; several, numbered in order, with a line saying they are several), and chat.message_delivered lists the ids. The turn's language is that of the author of the MOST RECENT message (RN-622). The queue that matters is the CURRENT state's, never the Task result's, which captured the state at the start of the turn. A message arriving between the end of the turn and delivery goes to the END of the queue, and the whole queue is delivered at once — the newest never jumps ahead of those waiting. Three immutable events, all with the chat.message id. chat.message_queued (agent; mensagemId, texto, idioma, posicao — the text goes along because it is what the queue needs to reread after a restart), chat.message_delivered (agent; mensagemIds) and chat.message_cancelled (actor user, who cancelled; mensagemId, agente). Pending is enqueued and neither delivered nor cancelled — the same derivation in the engine (FilaDeMensagens.pendentes/2) and on screen (estadosNaFila). No table. Restart. The seven's init/1 rebuilds the queue from the log (TurnoAssincrono.fila_ao_subir/3) and schedules delivery; Reidratacao removes from history the cancelled one (it was never said) and this agent's pending one (it will arrive via the queue turn — otherwise it would come in twice). At boot, after closing the orphan turn (RN-586), the Rehydrator wakes the agent that has a pending queue (FilaDeMensagens.acordar_pendentes/2): without this the queue of whoever was mid-turn when the engine went down would wait for someone to write again. The interrupted turn is still NEVER redone — what is read is the message no turn read. Cancelling. POST …/agents/:agent/messages/:messageId/cancel (developer, the same as the message route). The api checks that the message is a chat.message of this session, that its actor is the caller (403 mensagem_de_outra_pessoa otherwise) and that the session accepts conversation (RN-581). Whoever decides whether it is still in the queue is the agent's process, which serializes the race with delivery: 409 mensagem_fora_da_fila when it was already read or cancelled. With the agent down there is no in-memory queue — the queue is the log — and the engine records the cancellation directly. A turn suspended on approval (Dev Lead, RN-284) keeps refusing, with aguardando_aprovacao. Using the same queue was considered and refused: the suspended turn has no foreseeable end (it depends on a human deciding in Approvals), and enqueueing would promise reading "at the end of the turn" with no end in sight. A message already in the queue when the turn suspended waits for the RESUMPTION to finish — delivery skips the suspended state. The screen. The composer stops locking during the turn when the message goes to an agent: the button becomes "Queue", the message does not arm a new turn (the one in progress stays the one followed) and appears in the thread with the badge "in 's queue" and, for whoever sent it, the cancel button. A cancelled one is struck through. Chat without an agent (SSE) keeps locking: there is no queue there.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The turno_em_andamento refusal did not go away. It remains for story review, readiness and handoff offer, which call iniciar/3 with from. Whoever reads ADR 0163 alone will think the message is still refused; RN-578 points here. The message text is in the log twice when it enters the queue (in the chat.message and in the chat.message_queued). Accepted cost: without it, a queue whose chat.message left the 200-event window could not be rebuilt. Reading the queue in init/1 is one more query per agent start-up (by type, with ADR 0060's ceiling of 200). More than 200 queue events in a session would make the rebuild see only the most recent ones — declared, not measured; the ceiling of 10 pending makes it unlikely, not impossible. Waking at boot spends tokens without anyone clicking — on behalf of messages the user sent and no turn read. It is the deliberate difference from RN-586, which does not redo the turn: the interrupted turn may have had an effect; the pending message, none. Cancelling with the agent down has a window: the agent may be starting (reading the queue from the log) at the same instant the cancellation is recorded. There is no lock; the message may be read. Declared. Messages to another agent with a turn in progress on screen. The screen follows one turn at a time; sending to an IDLE agent while another works starts its turn (entrega: lida) and the screen starts following it through the log. The recipient selector stays locked during the turn, as before. Closed session. The agents stop (RN-581) and the queue dies with them; the message that was pending stays "in the queue" in the log forever, and the screen does not offer cancelling in an inactive session. If the session is reopened (ADR 0183) and the agent starts again, its init/1 delivers the queue — an accepted consequence, not designed separately. Only CI proves the engine. In this tree repo.hex.pm answers 403 and the ExUnit suite does not run locally; the new tests (fila_de_mensagens_test.exs) and the adjusted ones were written against the existing fakes and verified only by parser and formatter.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-269, story HS-069, epic EP-030, round 35; owner decision on 01/10: "QA only after the dev's delivery" — the activity's exit (b), chosen knowing it contradicts ADR 0090). Revises part of ADR 0090 without editing it: QA-strategy is still the qa-lead at a second MOMENT, without a new agent, but the moment moves — it leaves design (PRE-DEV) and goes to the start of the delivery review cycle. Appsec, the other half of 0090, does NOT change.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Real use of 29/09 (analysis analise-uso-real.md, item A23): two rounds of toolloop.limit_reached 8/8 followed by agent.error origin modelo, "limite de iterações atingido sem emit_plano_de_teste" (session be70, seq 373/374 and 463/464). The loop spent the eight iterations reading docs, an empty RAG and folders (seq 375–463), and seq 454 states the reason in text: "O código ainda não existe". The Dev Lead never got an assessment.
documents.s: The symptom

documents.t: Who opens the gate. implementavel (docs/gates.yml) belongs to dev-lead, fluxo: pre-dev, severidade: warn, aprovacao_humana: true, evidence in the event log (proposed_action.* filtered by actionType: assess_implementability). It is opened by the assess_implementability tool (Engine.Agents.DevLeadTools.run_assessment/2), which the Dev Lead's kickoff presents as OPTIONAL ("use judgment"). What it judged. run_assessment/2 read the session tail; without the story's artifact.plano_de_teste, it called Dispatcher.run_qa_estrategia/3 → QaLeadServer.run_design/3 → QaEstrategiaAgent.run/4 and returned {:error, "chame de novo em instantes"}; with a plan, it proposed the assessment (implementavel/ inviavel + justification) with planoDeTeste and criteriosExecutaveis embedded in the payload. The input was the plan; the JUDGMENT was already the Dev Lead's. QA-strategy's context. QaEstrategiaContext.fetch/3 gave story + module_map, no worktree; ReadFile/SearchWorkspace fell into the project's shared checkout. EmitPlanoDeTeste only accepts after a read — so, with no code to read, the model searches until the ceiling. The ceiling. "qa-estrategia" falls into the :conversacional default (8) of Engine.Harness.Iteracoes, on purpose (ADR 0090: without token_budget_micros underneath, raising the ceiling would multiply the worst case). Who depends on the verdict. Nobody in the code. No api use case nor engine module reads the assess_implementability decision: execution activation does not check it, no other gate has it as entrada, and the only consumer is the screen (the sentence in apps/web/src/lib/aprovacoes.ts). The gate is warn: passing is evidence, not a lock. The later gate. qa-verificada (block, owner area-qa) runs in QaLeadServer.run/2 over the dev's worktree: ContextBuilder.fetch/3, delegations (Automation always, Performance/Security per NFR) and ONE consolidated qa_verdict. Automation builds the coverageMatrix from the story's rules (FR + NFR) and only approves with a green suite and every rule covered.
documents.s: What the code did (measured on dev, 2026-10-01)

documents.t: The test plan is the first step of the qa-verificada cycle. QaLeadServer.run_area/3, after ContextBuilder.fetch/3 and before the delegations, gets the DELIVERY's plan: it finds again in the session tail (rehydration ceiling, RN-580) the artifact.plano_de_teste of the SAME taskId — the correction round (RN-015) does not pay another loop; if there is none, it runs QaEstrategiaAgent.run/6 synchronously, in its own process (the agent never suspends), with the dev_state/dev_context the subspecialties receive: workspace_root = the dev's worktree, the business rule units, and the list of files the delivery touched (Engine.Gates.Diff, git diff dev...HEAD, up to 40 names) in the first message. A diff that fails becomes text ("couldn't list: reason"), never an empty list. The plan enters the dev_context as :plano_de_teste, and Automation receives it AT THE END of its message, as input to step 2 ("which test covers each rule"). The verdict's rule does not change: one coverageMatrix row per story rule, approved only with a green suite and every rule covered. The external contract is still ONE qa_verdict per cycle. A plan that fails does not hold the review. QA-strategy already records agent.error with origin (RN-059); the Lead goes on without a plan, and Automation's message is the previous one, byte for byte. Making the plan's failure block the task would be a new lock in a block gate because of a new input — that was not decided, and the owner's decision is about WHEN the plan is born, not about it failing deliveries. implementavel judges itself on the story and the module_map. assess_implementability neither reads nor triggers a plan: the input becomes what the Dev Lead ALREADY has in the turn's context — its kickoff lists the modules of the current module_map and the backlog stories (FR, NFR, DoD) —, and the judgment goes in the justificativa. The assessment comes out on the FIRST call; the payload loses planoDeTeste/criteriosExecutaveis. The gate still exists, with the same owner, severity, human approval and evidence — only the entrada changes ([story-ready, module_map]). No new gate. What goes away. QaLeadServer.run_design/3, Dispatcher.run_qa_estrategia/3 (and the callback) and QaEstrategiaContext — without a caller after item 3, they would remain triggerable for a moment the owner's decision retired. The artifact changes shape. artifact.plano_de_teste now requires taskId (Engine.Harness.ArtifactSchemas): it is the plan of ONE delivery, and it is through it that the Lead finds it again. The ceiling STAYS 8. "qa-estrategia" gets no clause in Iteracoes.tipo/1. What was missing was input, not slack: with the code existing and the delivery's files in the message, two or three reads suffice. What changed on the spending side is that there is a task now, and the agent runs under the task_budget_micros the subspecialties share (RN-036) — RN-085's criterion would even allow the gate ceiling with that budget underneath, and the decision is NOT to use that door for the plan to pass. docs/gates.yml and docs/fluxo.yml change because who delivers what to whom changed: qa-verificada gains plano-de-teste in its entrada; implementavel swaps plano-de-teste for module_map; in fluxo.yml, qa-estrategia now receives the delivery from dev and delivers to area-qa, with gate_saida qa-verificada (input, not its own verdict), and dev-lead stops receiving the test plan.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: For The real-use symptom loses its cause: the plan is no longer asked of an agent at a moment when what it needs to read does not exist. The Dev Lead has the assessment on the first call, without the asynchronous callback-less window ADR 0090 declared as its price (it depended on the MODEL deciding to call again). The plan is now written over the real code, with worktree and diff, and is consumed by whoever verifies — qa-verificada —, in the same process and the same cycle. Zero routes, zero tables, zero new GenServers; three fewer pieces. The plan now has a budget underneath (the task's). Against implementavel becomes shallower. Before there was a second look (QA) at the story before spending tokens writing code; now the assessment is only the Dev Lead's, on the story and the module_map. It is the direct price of the owner's decision, and the gate was warn and optional — but the QA "shift-left" ADR 0090 bought ceases to exist for QA (appsec stays in design). One more LLM loop per DELIVERY, on the review's critical path: Automation only starts after the plan. Per task, not per round (reuse by taskId); in a long session the plan may have left the 200-event window and is written again — cost, never wrong data. The plan competes for the same task budget the review uses: an expensive delivery may reach Automation with less slack. The plan is input, not a rule. Whether the plan's executable criteria should become mandatory coverageMatrix rows (and therefore fail deliveries) is a product decision this ADR does NOT take. Ceiling 8 can still blow on a large delivery; then the outcome is the narrated agent.error and the review goes on without a plan. Measuring this in the next real use is what would say whether 8 is enough. The translated pt-BR of docs/fluxo.yml (website/i18n/…) was already behind the original before this change, and stays behind (AT-209).
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Exit (a): keep the plan in design, from story, rules and module_map, without exploring code, with emit_plano_de_teste required early. It did not contradict 0090 and was the cheapest fix of the symptom. Refused by the owner (01/10) in favour of (b). Raise the qa-estrategia ceiling to 60. Refused by the activity and by this ADR: it would make the plan pass by spending more, at a moment when there is nothing to read. A new gate for the plan (plano-de-teste-pronto) after delivery. Refused: a new gate is a product decision with its own ADR, it would change the external contract (one more verdict per PR) and the plan has nothing to veto alone — the coverage verdict already belongs to qa-verificada. Trigger QA-strategy asynchronously on delivery (cast from DevAgentServer), in parallel with the review. Refused: Automation would start before the plan existed, which is the race this design exists to avoid; and the result would again depend on an event nobody waits for. Retire implementavel. Refused: nobody asked; the gate still has something to judge (the story and the module_map) and is still the measurable record that someone thought about the story before the code.
documents.s: Alternatives considered

documents.t: ADR 0090 — the second moment of qa-lead and secops; this ADR changes the first one's moment ADR 0054 — the gates' external contract ADR 0085 — docs/fluxo.yml RN-674 (docs/business-rules.md), RN-340/341 (revised by it), RN-085, RN-036, RN-163, RN-580 apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/qa_lead_server.ex, qa_estrategia_agent.ex, qa_automacao_agent.ex, dispatcher.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/dev_lead_tools.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/artifact_schemas.ex
documents.s: References

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-116, story HS-037, epic EP-010, round 36; owner decision on 01/10: "credentialed git operations on the HOST, code in the container"). Closes the half that RN-558 left declared as open and references, without editing them, ADR 0130 (the Docker port without a free -e), ADR 0145 (RunnerReadiness and the three preconditions of runner mode) and ADR 0056 (the git credential only in the child process's ENVIRONMENT). The proof is AT-111.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured on dev on 2026-10-01, before changing: The ONLY engine exec carrying env is the authenticated git fetch of Engine.Actions.Workspace.RunnerGit.fetch!/3 (GitAuth.env_de_auth/1, converted into a map; nil for a provider without a token). TerminalExecutor calls RunnerRouter.exec/4 and never passes env. There is no credentialed push nor clone via exec in runner mode: the folder creation clone travels in workspace_create (RN-532), which already runs on the HOST (criarPastaDoProjeto). RunnerReadiness (ADR 0145) requires a REGISTERED running container before any RunnerGit operation, and in a runner project that record only exists because the SAME runner brought up the container — which sets estado.containerAtivo. With it set, tratarExec (apps/runner/src/index.ts) routed EVERY command to docker exec, which has no env field (ADR 0130). Since RN-558 that pair (env present, container active) was REFUSED with the mark credencial-nao-atravessa-o-container: the COMMON path of the authenticated fetch ended in a named refusal, never in success. The folder is the SAME on both sides: tratarContainerStart mounts estado.dir (the root confirmed by the runner) at /work (DockerViaCli.start, ${raizDoProjeto}:/work:rw, PONTO_DE_MONTAGEM in packages/docker-port/src/docker-port.ts), and every exec's cwd is validated inside estado.dir (validarCwdDentroDaRaiz) and translated to /work/... only when it goes to the container. The .git a fetch updates on the host is the one the container sees. The two vetoed exits stay vetoed: a free -e on DockerPort (ADR 0130 refused it) and a "skip container" flag in RunnerReadiness (it would knock down ADR 0145's third precondition for the whole exec).
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The credentialed git operation runs on the runner's HOST, even with an active container. The dev agent's command still goes to docker exec. The credential reaches the child process by the path that always worked: apps/runner/src/exec.ts merges env over process.env. The discriminator is an EXPLICIT MARK set by the engine, not the env. The exec payload gains gitCredenciado: true, optional, and whoever sets it is RunnerRouter.exec_git_credenciado/5, called from ONE point (RunnerGit.despachar/5, from fetch!/3, only when there is a credential). The function requires a non-empty env by a clause guard. The runner runs on the host ONLY with the CONJUNCTION (literal true mark and non-empty env). Why not the env alone, which already existed: with it, any exec arriving with an env would escape the container — the env would become the exit door from the containment ADR 0145 set for code. With the mark, the exit is a NAMED decision of a single engine caller, and an env without the mark does not get the host. The mark is not enough on its own either: without a credential there is nothing to protect, and the command follows the usual routing. No ADR 0130 port changes. DockerPort.exec still has no env field; the image, the network, the mount and the broker are not touched. RunnerReadiness stays byte for byte: the mark changes WHERE the runner executes, never WHETHER the engine dispatches — the registered running container precondition still holds for the fetch too. RN-558's refusal still exists, and shrinks to one case. The pair (env present, container active) WITHOUT the mark is still refused with the same protocol mark and origin politica. No engine caller produces that pair today; in practice it appears through a version MISMATCH — a brabo-runner older than this ADR does not read the mark, routes the fetch to the container and refuses as before. That is why the message of Engine.Runners.CredencialDeGit.mensagem/2 now states the fix (update the runner, or stop the container), instead of "the missing half does not exist". The runner's refusal text also changes (it says "WITHOUT the credentialed git mark"), and the fixture apps/runner/fixtures/exec-result-recusa-de-credencial.json changes along. The log invariant holds. Neither the refusal nor the host path's log cite the name or value of an env variable — the refusal gives the COUNT, and the host log adds only [git credenciado, no host]. The command text is still logged as always (it carries ADR 0056's helper, which references the variables by name, but never the value — that does not change here).
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: AUTHENTICATED fetch/clone of a remote repository in runner mode now works with the container up, which is the common path. RN-558 stops firing on it. Old runner + new engine: the runner ignores the mark and refuses with the RN-558 mark; the engine says "update the runner". New runner + old engine: the engine does not send the mark, and the runner refuses as before. No combination goes back to silent discard. Credentialed git runs with the HOST's user and git, not the container's. The files the fetch writes in .git are born owned by the runner process's owner — who is the mounted folder's owner. Not measured: a runner project container whose --user is not that owner would see the updated .git with another owner; today the spec the api sends to the runner (EspecificacaoDeContainerParaRunner) has no usuario, so the container runs with the image's user, and the effect was not exercised against real Docker. RN-558 listed this option as the one that "would break the invariant that work happens inside the container". The owner's decision accepts it with that price written down: what leaves the container is git's CONVERSATION with the remote (the credentialed fetch), never the project's code — the dev agent's npm install, tests and build remain in docker exec. What the fetch brings is git objects, and they only become working files in a checkout/worktree add that carries no credential and follows the usual routing. The host needs git installed. It already did: workspace_create (RN-532) and the path without a container always ran git on the host. The mark is a second protocol constant in the exec pair, alongside env. It only travels when it is true (the ordinary terminal payload stays byte for byte as before), and the runner accepts only the boolean true — any other value is absence. Left out: credentialed push through the runner's exec does not exist today; if it is born, it enters through the same function (exec_git_credenciado/5), never through a second mark path. The proof (AT-111) swaps refusal for success on both sides: apps/runner/src/index-handlers.spec.ts (with an active container and the mark, the real git helper receives the credential and a real git fetch origin succeeds on the host, without docker.exec; env without the mark stays refused) and apps/engine/test/engine_web/channels/credencial_no_runner_test.exs (through the real TerminalChannel, the fetch goes marked and the chain ends in {:ok, _}). The ExUnit tests did not run in this delivery's environment (repo.hex.pm answered 403); CI is what proves them.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-263 and AT-274, epic EP-030, round 36; owner decisions on 01/10: "execution activation becomes the APPROVAL of the Dev Lead's plan; accepting the Dev Lead's handoff only brings it in to plan" and "whoever assigns the task's module is the Dev Lead, when assembling the execution plan; only that module's dev picks it up"). Revises, without editing them, ADR 0069 (the conditional merge of acceptance with activation, RN-161) and the part of ADR 0086 that said propose_execution_plan has no execution pipeline. Preserves ADR 0165 (the repository is born on acceptance to the Arquiteto, the Dev Lead's is the second door, and execution/activate without a repository is 409) and ADR 0061 (execution.activated in a consultative session is 409).
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured on dev (d89f777) before changing: Whoever emits execution.activated is only ActivateExecutionUseCase, and it is only called by the POST .../execution/activate route. The acceptance backend (AcceptHandoffUseCase) never activated anything: it provisions the repository when the destination is arquiteto or dev-lead and activates the AGENT. The "activation on acceptance" was the WEB's — handleAcceptHandoff chained activateExecution when the destination was dev-lead and the workspace role was maintainer/owner (RN-161). The plan had no consumer. propose_execution_plan is a proposed_action since ADR 0086 and the Dev Lead suspends waiting for the decision, but once approved it stayed approved forever: ApproveActionUseCase had no branch for the type, and the Dev Lead read "plan approved and recorded". In the real use of 29/09 execution came up at 06:45:01, on acceptance; the plan arrived at 06:47:47 and stayed pending. The task had no module. claimNext takes the next todo task of a ready story whose module_ids (jsonb, several) contains the dev's module. With a two-module story, dev-input-keyboard took "piece automatic drop loop" and dev-board-engine took "map keys" (session d7e9, seq 185/187). The Dev Lead saw no task_id: the kickoff listed only modules and stories, taken from its own session's log.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The Dev Lead's acceptance does not activate execution, for any role. handleAcceptHandoff only accepts; AcceptHandoffUseCase does not change (it keeps provisioning as the second door). The card's explicit "Activate execution" button (RN-137) and the Overview's STAY: they are a gesture of their own for whoever decides to skip the plan, and the execution/activate route keeps all its refusals. Approving propose_execution_plan executes the plan, in a new executor in the api — ExecuteExecutionPlanUseCase, in the execution module, next to ExecuteParallelizationUseCase —, called by manual approval and by auto-approval (the type stays OUTSIDE the absolute ceilings of decide.ts, as ADR 0086 decided). It: rereads the plan against the current module_map; records the tasks' module; and calls the SAME ActivateExecutionUseCase as the button, with whoever approved (or, auto-approved, whoever opened the session) as the activator. Without originSessionId: the Dev Lead's session is where it resumes and narrates. The outcome is executed (sessaoDeExecucao, modulos, tarefasAtribuidas) or failed (motivo), with execution.plan_applied/execution.plan_failed on the timeline, and it is what the Dev Lead reads on resuming. The task gains a module column (tasks.module text NULL, migration 0068_modulo_da_tarefa). The plan carries tarefas: [{ taskId, modulo }], validated by a PURE function (lerPlanoDeExecucao) against the current module_map and the project's tasks, TWICE: on proposal (400 plano_de_execucao_invalido, without creating the action — the sentence goes back to the Dev Lead as a tool error) and on approval (the map may have changed; refusal becomes failed without recording anything). The Dev Lead's kickoff lists the pending tasks of the PROJECT's backlog (list_backlog), with task_id and the story's modules. Only the module's dev picks up the task. claimNext and countClaimableByModule now use a single predicate: t.module = $modulo, OR a task without a module whose story has exactly ONE module and it is $modulo.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Activation now costs the approval of a valid plan, and a plan is only valid with EVERY cited task assigned to a module_map module. A Dev Lead that cannot assemble tarefas (empty backlog, tasks in another project) activates nothing through the new path; the explicit button remains the way out, and is declared as such. The bridge for a task without a module is deliberate and narrow. Without it, whoever activates from the Overview without a plan would have no claimable task at all; with it restricted to a ONE-module story, the rule "only that module's dev" stays true, because there is no other there. A task without a module from a multi-module story stays parked until the next plan — and the PO does not assign modules, so a task created AFTER the approved plan falls into that case. Closing that (the PO assigning, or automatic replanning) is a separate decision. The task.became_claimable notice is still routed by the STORY's modules. Waking a dev that will pick up nothing costs one query and no model spending; routing by the task's module would require touching the notice's emitters, out of scope. agentes per module stays informative. Activation brings up one dev per module_map module, as before; more than one per module still goes through parallelize (RN-083), with its ceiling. The engine's propose_action call stays at Req's default of 15 s for this type. Auto-approved, the api activates execution within the same request (seeds instructions and autonomy, calls the engine); a case exceeding 15 s was not measured, and if it does the outcome arrives through the timeline even with the tool result saying transport error. The screen does not navigate to the execution session after approving the plan (RN-634 did that on the button): the approval is the ApprovalCard's, from another front. The Dev Lead says in which session execution came up.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-277, story HS-072, epic EP-030, round 36; owner decision on 01/10: "turn the Anamnese back on with fixes" — an eligible subject guard, and the ACCEPTED hypothesis becomes a profile fact in the graph and enters the context of the agents that converse with the person; the refused one is only recorded). Ends the 2026-08-10 pause only for the Anamnese — the Psicólogo stays paused (PSYCHOLOGIST_ENABLED=false). Uses the graph of ADR 0099 as it was designed (memory DERIVED from the event log) and the language's ephemeral guidance path (RN-622) without editing either.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured in the dev code and in the report of the real use of 2026-09-29, before changing: Six rounds, six anamnese.run_skipped written by the MODEL with the same reason, "no eligible member" (sessions be70, 67f3, d7e9 ×2, 5d66 ×2), for 8,933 micros in 6 calls. anamnese_runs = 0, proficiency_profiles = 0. Where the subject came from: GetAnamneseContextUseCase read ProjectRepository.listMembers, which is ONLY project_members. Creating a project writes no row there (CreateProjectUseCase), and authorization treats the workspace owner as a project member through projectRole ?? workspaceRole (RN-471). In a one-person project, the list always came back empty. The worker did not look at the list: AnamneseWorker.maybe_analyze/3 only asked the triage (window volume, hypothesis queue), and a hypothesis in the queue FORCED the round. The prompt said "(no eligible member)" and the model was paid to conclude that. The accepted hypothesis had no real consumer: AcceptHypothesisUseCase enqueued in anamnese_queue (3 rows in real use), and the only consumption was a round's propose_instruction_patch — which, in 5d66 seq 17, answered "there is no agent instruction file available in the context". The graph did not project psychologist.hypothesis_accepted. The graph's read path had no consumer: QueryUserContextUseCase existed (hypotheses, profiles, handoffs per user and project) and no code called it. ANAMNESE_ENABLED had a false default in runtime.exs and in the three composes since RN-540; the report records the real-use engine with the flag true via environment.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The round does not run without an eligible subject. Engine.Anamnese.Elegibilidade decides BEFORE the triage, without exception (not even the hypothesis queue crosses it): a subject is the project's EFFECTIVE member, outside the opt-out, with their OWN interaction in what the prompt shows — an actor_kind: "user" event of theirs in the window, or a decision of theirs. Without a subject: no LLM call, no RAG search, a named reason in the engine log (sem_sujeito_elegivel, with nenhum_membro or nenhuma_interacao_propria and the numbers) and, only in the round requested by hand (origem: "manual"), a durable anamnese.run_skipped. The prompt now lists only the subjects. A project member is the EFFECTIVE member. ProjectRepository gains listEffectiveMembers (membrosEfetivos, RN-471's rule: the project row overrides the workspace one in both directions), used by the Anamnese's three use cases. listMembers is still only project_members, which is what the Members screen edits. The accepted hypothesis becomes a profile FACT, derived from the event log. psychologist.hypothesis_accepted now carries projectId, sujeito (the author of the analyzed session), hipotese, sugestao and fatoDoPerfil. The GraphEventTranslator — the SAME one as the projector and grafo:reprojetar — translates it into (:FatoDoPerfil {hypothesisId})-[:SOBRE]->(:Usuario) and -[:NO_PROJETO]->(:Projeto) (RecordProfileFactUseCase, MERGE by the hypothesis, a new unique constraint). The event is self-sufficient: reprojecting does not read psychologist_hypotheses. The fact is only born from the subject's own click. fatoDoPerfil is true when whoever accepted IS the session's author. A third party's acceptance still holds for everything else (status, Anamnese queue) and says in the payload why it did not become a fact (motivoSemFato). The refused one does not change: it is only recorded. The fact enters the context of the agents that converse with the person. SendAgentMessageUseCase reads the facts of the message's AUTHOR through QueryUserContextUseCase — scoped to the project, the 5 most recent, with the total beside — and sends them to the engine as perfilDoAutor, text built by textoDoPerfilDoAutor (2,000 characters at most, cut stated). The engine puts them into the turn by the SAME path as the language: the controller joins both in a map, IdiomaDaResposta.com_idioma_do_autor/2 recognizes it, and the EngineApiClient facade appends the text as an EPHEMERAL system message before the language guidance (Engine.Harness.PerfilDoAutor). No agent server changes. Graph down becomes a log, and the turn goes on without the facts. Turning back on. The ANAMNESE_ENABLED default goes back to true in runtime.exs and in the three composes (the flags-do-engine-no-compose.spec.ts rule still holds: compose repeats the code). START_ANAMNESE does not change anywhere: true in code, in dev and in the installation; false in the production compose, a divergence already declared. PSYCHOLOGIST_ENABLED does not change.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The 29/09 real use stops spending: a project without a subject does not reach the LLM. And the workspace owner in a project without their own row now IS a subject — the Anamnese turned back on now does something in the most common case, instead of nothing. Declared price: the Anamnese now profiles whoever is a member only through the workspace. A workspace member who never interacted in the project is not profiled (not a subject), and the opt-out still holds. Declared price: each message to a conversational agent makes one more read in the graph (four QueryUserContextUseCase queries). Without Neo4j configured, it is an immediate GraphUnavailableError and a log. Declared price: the facts reach EVERY turn of the author, including the agent that was not the hypothesis's target — the label says whom it addressed, and filtering by agent is an open decision. Out, declared: the three acceptances of the real use were recorded before this change, without the fact fields, and do NOT become facts on reprojection. They remain in the Anamnese queue, which reads them in the next round WITH a subject. A turn without an author (kickoff, dev agents, gates) gets no facts. The Staff still has no automatic trigger: the Anamnese never fired it in code. A tick round without a subject does not become an event (it would be a notice every 15 minutes per project); only the one requested by hand narrates.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-246, story HS-024, epic EP-016, round 36; owner decision on 01/10: "remove the literal from the workflows" — the image: of the services: now comes from a previous job that reads the compose, a single source of digests, and Dependabot docker/docker-compose is turned on). On top of ADR 0159 (third-party image by index digest) and ADR 0178 (the tag inside the reference), without editing them: both remain valid in everything; this one closes the half 0178 declared NOT done in "What this ADR does NOT do".
documents.s: Status

documents.t: ADR 0178 put the tag inside the reference — the form Dependabot reads — and left image Dependabot off because of ONE blocker: pgvector and ollama lived twice, in the compose and as a literal in the workflows' services:. No ecosystem reads workflow services:, so every bot PR bumping one of the two in the compose would be born red by the "same tag, two digests" rule of scripts/ci/imagens-pinadas.ts; and the step that would align the workflow in the bot's PR would have to push a commit into .github/workflows/, which GITHUB_TOKEN cannot, not even through permissions:. The ADR listed four exits; the owner chose the second. Measured on origin/dev (d89f77714e) before changing — every third-party image: in .github/workflows/, and where each should read from: workflow job → service image reads from ci.yml test-api-shard → postgres pgvector/pgvector:pg16@sha256:ccc6e83d… postgres service of docker/docker-compose.yml ci.yml test-engine → postgres same same golden-set-rag.yml golden-set-rag → postgres same same golden-set-rag.yml golden-set-rag → ollama ollama/ollama:0.33.1@sha256:075246f7… ollama service of docker/docker-compose.yml golden-set-qa.yml golden-set-qa → postgres pgvector, same postgres service golden-set-qa.yml golden-set-qa → ollama ollama, same ollama service Six literals, two images, all with the same digest as the DEV compose. No job container: and no other image: in the workflows. The dev compose, and not the production or installation one, is the right source for the two reasons that already existed: it is against it that the api and engine suites run in dev, and it is it that golden-set-rag.yml promised to follow (the golden-set floor is keyed by MODEL, not by environment). The three composes carry the same digest today, and the lint guarantees they keep doing so. And the lint had a blind spot the new form would open if nobody looked: the image: pattern was (\S+), and a line with an expression (${{ … }}, which has a space) did NOT match — it vanished from the check instead of being judged. Worse: what matched with $ was treated as interpolation and skipped. image: ${{ 'postgres:16' }} would pass green.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: 1. The workflows' services: read the image from the compose. A new reusable workflow, .github/workflows/imagens-do-compose.yml (only workflow_call), runs scripts/ci/imagens-do-compose.ts, which reads the direct child image: of each service listed in IMAGENS_DOS_WORKFLOWS and returns it as an output. The caller does: jobs: imagens: uses: ./.github/workflows/imagens-do-compose.yml test-engine: needs: imagens if: ${{ !cancelled() }} services: postgres: image: ${{ needs.imagens.outputs.pgvector }} The script REFUSES a nonexistent service or one without image: (renaming in the compose breaks CI on the spot, instead of delivering an empty string) and a reference outside the imagem:tag@sha256:<índice> form — a second door, because the reading job cannot depend on lint having run before. No pnpm install: the script only uses node:fs, with a sparse checkout of docker/ and scripts/ci/. Reusable and not a job copied into each file: there are three callers, and three copies of the same checkout + setup would be the duplicate this ADR exists to remove, one level up. 2. The lint understands the new form and closes the door it opens. In a .github/workflows/ file, imagens-pinadas.ts now reads image: and the short form container: <imagem> with a pattern that accepts spaces, and fails: literal no workflow — any literal third-party reference, EVEN pinned by digest: it is the duplicate no ecosystem reads; expressão de imagem fora da forma — anything that is not EXACTLY ${{ needs.<job>.outputs.<imagem> }}: a literal inside the expression, || with a default value (before or after the output), env., vars., format(), a suffix after }}, an unclosed expression; imagem do workflow fora do compose — needs.<job> whose job does not call ./.github/workflows/imagens-do-compose.yml, or an output it does not declare. The product's own image (brabo-*) stays out, as in the other trees. Each rule is proven by MUTATION in imagens-pinadas.spec.ts: turning off the literal, loosening the expression form, not checking the job, not checking the output, ignoring the rest after }} or reverting the pattern to \S+ — each mutation breaks at least one test (measured: 4, 1, 2, 1, 1 and 12). And imagens-do-compose.spec.ts ties the reusable to the table: the declared outputs are EXACTLY the keys of IMAGENS_DOS_WORKFLOWS, each bound to the step that runs the script — an output in between with a literal fails. 3. Image Dependabot is turned on in .github/dependabot.yml, with target-branch: dev like the others: docker-compose in /docker — the five composes live there, so a bump updates dev, production and installation in the SAME PR; docker in /docker/* (the FROMs, one folder per image) and /deploy/k8s/** (the manifests). NEVER /docker without the /*: the docker ecosystem also reads YAML with image: (that is how it covers Kubernetes — the YAML_REGEXP of dependabot-core's shared_file_fetcher.rb, read on 01/10), and would read the composes, opening a second PR for the same image; each ecosystem with ONE group (patterns: ['*']): node:24-alpine lives in three dev Dockerfiles and node:24.21.0-alpine3.23 in three production ones, each in a folder, and without a group they would be three PRs with the same tag and different digests — red by the rule; ignore for brabo-* (and ghcr.io/*/brabo-*): the images this repository builds have no third-party registry to look in. 4. The golden-set-rag.yml promise becomes construction. It said, in a comment, that it ran "a MESMA versão pinada de docker/docker-compose.yml". Since ADR 0159 the lint VERIFIED that through the "same tag, two digests" rule; now there is nothing to verify, because there is no second copy: the golden-set's Ollama is, by construction, the reference of the dev compose's ollama service. The same holds for golden-set-qa.yml and for the Postgres of the ci.yml suites.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The bot's PR only touches the compose, and that PR's CI already runs against the new image — the services: reads the compose from the PR itself. There is no alignment step, no credential with workflows, no GITHUB_TOKEN push without checks. Two required jobs gain a dependency, and cannot become skipped. Testes do engine (ExUnit) (required check) and the api shards wait for the imagens job. GitHub's default would SKIP the job if imagens failed, and skipped counts as green for a required check — the same trap the api aggregator already avoids with if: always(). That is why both carry if: ${{ !cancelled() }}: with imagens red, the job runs, receives an empty image and fails. The new job (imagens / Ler as imagens do compose) does NOT enter a ruleset. Cost measured in time: none measured yet — it is a sparse checkout and a setup-node without cache, running in parallel with lint; TODO(humano) on the first run. A new workflow service has a single path: image in the compose, a line in IMAGENS_DOS_WORKFLOWS, an output in the reusable (the spec fails if they diverge), needs: imagens in the workflow. The runbook (Bumping a third-party image) says so. The lint's count drops from 39 to 33 literal references: the six in the workflows ceased to exist, and the sentence in cadeia-de-suprimentos-do-ci.md that contagens-do-codigo.mjs checks follows.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: It does not resolve the duplicate BETWEEN ecosystems. neo4j:5.26-community and ollama/ollama:0.33.1 also live in deploy/k8s/base/ (neo4j/statefulset.yaml, ollama/job-model-loader.yaml), which belongs to the docker ecosystem, while the composes belong to docker-compose — and Dependabot does not group across ecosystems. Two consequences, declared: when the bot bumps the TAG (the common case), two green PRs come out, each in one place; until both go in, compose and cluster run different versions — and the lint does not fail different tags, only the same tag with different digests; when the registry RE-PUBLISHES the same tag with another digest (5.26-community is a moving tag), both PRs are born red by the "same tag, two digests" rule, and the reviewer merges the two bumps into a single PR (the runbook procedure). The same fate awaits a re-published digest of node:24-alpine if it one day lives in a compose AND a Dockerfile. It was not resolved here because every exit is a product decision, not this ADR's: deriving the manifest from the compose (a kustomize transformer still holds a literal), taking the compose from docker-compose and giving it to docker (which also reads YAML, not measured for compose) or relaxing the rule between trees (what the rule protects — dev and cluster running the same bytes under the same tag — is real). It does not measure Dependabot running. No image bot PR exists yet. Not measured by execution: docker-compose accepting the five file names (docker-compose.<sufixo>.yml) and ignoring interpolated references (${BRABO_API_IMAGE:?…}); grouping by directories producing ONE PR across folders. The bot's first PR is the proof, and what it contradicts comes back here in a new ADR. It does not extend dependabot-justifica-pin.ts to image pins. The bot's PR touches docker/**, and the drift (config-e-inferencia, block) will ask a human for docs-not-needed: — AT-094's decision limited the bot-written line to ACTION pin swaps, and ADR 0178 already declared that. It does not cover what was already out. They stay in the runbook's MANUAL procedure, with Dependabot or without: CloudNativePG's imageName (a key no ecosystem reads) and IMAGEM_DO_GOLDEN_SET_QA (a TypeScript constant read by golden-set-qa.yml via sed). The product's images, interpolated references and multi-stage stages stay out of the lint (ADR 0159). It does not create an RN. The image rule has no RN, for the same reason as the actions: it lives in CLAUDE.md and in docs/explanation/cadeia-de-suprimentos-do-ci.md.
documents.s: What this ADR does NOT do

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-171, story HS-047, epic EP-026, round 36; owner decision on 01/10: "embedding with a threshold, only warns" — it compares at emission against the project's existing stories and rules and WARNS above the threshold, never blocks; the embedding spending of this check enters metering as its own row). Opens ONE exception to the metering cut of ADR 0075 without editing it: the cut still holds for RAG indexing and search (ADR 0080); only this check now records token_usage. Closes the half that RN-080 and RN-081 declared out of reach, without changing either: the EXACT duplicate is still refused.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured in the dev code on 2026-10-01, before changing: Where emission happens. Story: the PO's create_story (apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/create_story.ex) calls POST /internal/sessions/:id/stories, and whoever creates is CreateStoryUseCase in the api — an equal title refuses, a contained justification warns (RN-081). Business rule: emit_artifact (the Criativo and five other conversational agents) records the artifact.business_rule event through the api (append_event), after ArtifactDedupe refuses an equal title (RN-080). There is no rules table: the rule IS the event. Neither server (po_server.ex, criativo_server.ex) needed to change — emission lives in the two tools. How the RAG calls embed. Through a single point, RagEmbeddingService, with a FIXED provider and model (ollama/nomic-embed-text, 768 dimensions — RN-222/233): the only provider declaring capabilities.embeddings (RN-191). Failure becomes available: false with a reason, never an exception. The service discarded the inputTokens the contract returns — the 0075 cut. Whether vectors are stored. They are not. chunks indexes chat.message, agent.response, docs/ and ADRs; no artifact.*, no story. The check has to vectorize on the spot. Why the 0075 cut does not reach this check. Its reason was structural: token_usage.session_id is NOT NULL, and indexing a repository does not happen in a session. Emitting a story or rule ALWAYS happens inside an agent's session — the session_id exists.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: What it compares. The new TITLE against the titles of the existing ones of the SAME type in the PROJECT (story with story, rule with rule), by cosine between vectors from the RAG model, called through the SAME RagEmbeddingService — never a second path to embed. Title, and not title+description: finding R's pair is of titles, and the description changes size and tone between the model's turns (cost and noise with no case asking for it). The exact duplicate (equal normalized title) is not this ADR's subject — it is refused earlier, by RN-080/081, and for that reason also leaves the comparison. It only WARNS. The check runs AFTER recording: the story and the rule exist with or without a warning. The warning goes back to the agent as part of the tool result (create_story, emit_artifact) and stays in the log as backlog.semantic_duplicate_warned, naming the similar item and the number. The threshold is 0.80, an uncalibrated STARTING POINT — like the four numbers of 0080's hybrid search. "From": equal warns. See "What was not measured". Erring low costs one more warning, which blocks nothing; that is why a provisional number fits here and would not fit in a refusal. Without an embedding provider, the check is SKIPPED and STATED. Missing capability, daemon down, model not pulled, or the time ceiling — all become status: skipped with the reason, narrated as backlog.semantic_duplicate_check_skipped and in the sentence to the agent. It never fails the emission, it is never silent: without this, "no warning" would read as "not a duplicate". The spending enters metering as ITS OWN ROW. Through the only path, RecordLlmUsageUseCase, with actor system/duplicata-semantica (outside the per-agent sums, RN-038, and area spending, ADR 0110), the RAG's provider/model, output_tokens = 0, input_tokens and estimated from what the provider said, catalog price when the model is in it (otherwise 0, with a null model_id). RagEmbeddingService now RETURNS the summed usage (uso); indexing and search ignore it, and that is what keeps 0075's cut for them. Ceilings. The 100 MOST RECENT existing ones, at most (TETO_DE_COMPARACOES_DE_DUPLICATA), in a single batch; when it cuts, the result says how many of how many (RN-180). And 10 s of wall clock for the whole check (TETO_DE_TEMPO_DA_CHECAGEM_MS), below the 15 s of the engine's Req that calls it: Ollama's timeout reaches 300 s in the installation, and the check is on the path of an agent tool. No migration. Nothing is stored: no vector, no new column. The own row in token_usage is distinguished by the actor, which already exists.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The cost of emitting now grows with the project. Each emission vectorizes min(N, 100) + 1 titles, N = existing ones of the same type. A story or rule title has 5 to 15 words; with the nomic-embed-text tokenizer that is ESTIMATED at 10–30 tokens per title, i.e. up to ~3,000 input tokens per emission at the ceiling — with local Ollama, catalog price 0 and cost 0 micros; what grows is LATENCY, not measured here. The real number comes from metering, which is what the row exists for. Storing each item's vector (a column in stories, a table for the rule-events) would reduce it to one call per emission, and is a migration — left for when the measured cost asks for it. Finding R's pair stops going unnoticed — if the threshold is right. And that "if" is this decision's gap (below). The warning sentence has ONE source, fraseParaOAgente in the api; the engine only passes it on. The same check serves both types. What still passes. A duplicate whose meaning is in the DESCRIPTION and not the title ("Saudação com nome" × "Quem chama pode se identificar", RN-080's example) is not compared. A warning lost to timeout is stated, but the check is not redone. And the budget with policy = 'block' (RN-019) is not checked BEFORE this call: the row adds to spending and may cross the thresholds, but the check is not refused for an exceeded budget — it blocks nothing, and with local Ollama the recorded cost is 0. If a paid embedding provider comes in, that choice is back on the table. What this ADR does NOT change: the refusal of the exact duplicate (RN-080/081), the metering cut of indexing and search (ADR 0075), the RAG's fixed model and provider (ADR 0080), and no conversational server.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: The owner's decision asked to calibrate the threshold with finding R's pair and with pairs that are NOT duplicates, proving it by a test with recorded vectors. The environment where this change was born could not reach the Ollama registry (registry.ollama.ai: 403 at the proxy) nor Hugging Face (403), and had no daemon — measured on 2026-10-01. A hand-written vector would prove the hand, not the model. What exists, then: apps/api/test/fixtures/duplicata-semantica/pares.json — the calibration pairs: finding R's and two paraphrases that MUST warn; five neighbouring-topic pairs that MUST NOT. apps/api/scripts/gravar-vetores-de-duplicata.ts — records vetores.json against real Ollama, with the model the daemon said it used, and prints each pair's cosine against the current threshold. apps/api/test/domain/backlog/limiar-de-duplicata.calibracao.spec.ts — runs on its own when vetores.json exists: every duplicata pair warns, every distinta passes. Without the file, it SKIPS with a named notice (the rule of Ollama's embedding smoke), never passes silently. Until someone records the vectors, 0.80 is general knowledge about sentence embedding models, not measurement. If the recording shows that no number separates the two sides, the answer is to revise the pairs or the compared text — never to loosen the test.
documents.s: What was not measured

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-261, story HS-065, epic EP-030, round 36; owner decision on 01/10: "the minimum resource is derived from the module_map — what the Arquiteto declares per module —, not a fixed preset per stack"). Changes the schema of the artifact.module_map artifact (Phase 3b) and what the container_start execution does with an omitted resources, referencing without editing them ADR 0065 (resources with a ceiling in the image artifact), ADR 0130 (pidsLimit in the broker's spec), ADR 0131 (the Arquiteto's routing), ADR 0133 (Infra elects) and ADR 0190 (the server's start-up on acceptance, which used "default resources").
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured on dev on 2026-10-01, before changing: RECURSOS_PADRAO = {cpus 2, memoryMb 4096, pidsLimit 512} and the ceiling RECURSOS_MAXIMOS = {8, 16384, 4096} in apps/api/src/domain/containers/project-container.ts. An omitted resources field became the default in validarDecisaoDeImagem; above the ceiling, refusal. There was no notion of a MINIMUM. The server's start-up on acceptance (subir_no_aceite/2, ADR 0190) always sends resources: %{}, so every container started by it got the default. The real container of the 29/09 use had Mem=4 GiB, NanoCpus=2e9, Pids=512 — the default. The module_map had {name, stack, responsibility, dependsOn} per module (ModuleNode in domain/architecture/module-graph.ts, the JSONB column module_maps.modules, the engine's create_module_map tool) and no resource field. The routing (artifact.module_routing) and the image neither. "Compatible minimum" was not derivable from the existing data. A project has ONE container: project_id UNIQUE in project_containers.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The module_map gains resources per module. Optional in the artifact (old maps do not have it; no migration — it is a JSON field), with the THREE numbers of the broker's spec: cpus, memoryMb, pidsLimit. It means what THAT module needs on its own inside the container. The create_module_map tool now asks for it (required in the item schema, with the three fields mandatory inside). The api validates on map creation: all three or none (a half declaration is 400 — completing the missing field with the default would be inventing the number), each positive and within the container's ceiling. The minimum is the SUM across modules, not the maximum. All modules live in the same container at the same time: each one's dev agent works there, in parallel when the area parallelizes, and one's dev server does not shut down for the other's to run. The maximum would only be true if there were never two up, and its failure mode is an OOM-kill mid-command, not a readable refusal. A sum exceeding the ceiling is refused ALREADY at map creation (400 to the Arquiteto, who is the one who can fix it), and again, as a defence, at start-up. A module without a declaration counts with today's default as a FLOOR. A number is never invented for it: the only one that exists is what it gets today, the container default. So, with a module lacking a declaration, the minimum is the GREATER of the sum of the declared ones and RECURSOS_PADRAO, field by field; only with all declared does the minimum go below the default. A map with no declaration at all — every map predating this ADR — gives exactly the default, and its behaviour does not change. The floor per CONTAINER, and not "default per module summed", is on purpose: adding 2 cpus per undeclared module would make an old five-module map exceed the ceiling and stop starting. The api is who derives, in the container_start execution. ExecuteContainerStartUseCase reads the current module_map (the same the routing nominated), derives the minimum and resolves resources field by field: OMITTED becomes the minimum; BELOW the minimum is a named failed (without recording a decision nor starting); above holds up to the ceiling, checked as always by validarDecisaoDeImagem. Without a current module_map, the minimum is the default. The engine does NOT derive: the server's start-up keeps sending empty resources, and its rationale says the resources are the derived minimum — a single rule, in TypeScript, never a second copy of the sum in Elixir. The artifact's rationale says where each number came from. The decision DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase records (artifact.project_image, decidedBy: 'infra-lead') gains the sentence "Recursos mínimos (RN-683): …", with the summed modules, those that did NOT declare (named) and the map version. Whoever audits the container reads why it has those numbers.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The server's start-up (ADR 0190) now starts with the SMALLEST eligible resource: a fully declared project may stay below the default of 2 cpus/4 GiB/512 pids, which was the waste AT-261 measured. The Arquiteto now declares resources per module, and a model can get the number wrong. Erring HIGH costs machine and is auditable in the rationale; erring above the ceiling is a 400 with a reason; erring LOW is the remaining risk, and it is of the same calibre as what the Arquiteto already decided when choosing the image. The number is DECLARED, not measured — measuring the container's real consumption is another front, not taken here. The Infra Lead asks ABOVE the minimum when it wants (up to the ceiling), never below. The below-minimum refusal happens at EXECUTION: a pending proposal with resources below the minimum only fails when approved, with the reason in executionResult. Refusing already at proposal would require reading the map in ProposeActionUseCase, and was not done here. choose_project_image (the Arquiteto deciding the image from scratch, RN-105) does NOT change: there the Arquiteto chooses its own resources, and the owner's request was about Infra's choice. The start-up through the runner (container_start_via_runner) does not either: it starts the already decided image, with the resources recorded in it. The ceiling stays the same, and no other moves. The sum of CPU fractions is rounded to three decimals, so the artifact does not record 0.30000000000000004.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-276, story HS-071, epic EP-030, round 36; owner decision on 01/10: "the contract between modules becomes a versioned Arquiteto artifact (in the mould of module_map/c4_diagram), read by the devs through the read tool; changing a contract is a new Arquiteto version"). Extends the table-less artifact design of ADR 0065, ADR 0068 and ADR 0131; applies the rule "an agent that writes must be able to read" (RN-164/165) to the dev agents, under the contained reading of ADR 0060.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Real use of 2026-09-29 (analysis analise-uso-real.md, item A30, 6(e)): dev-board-engine, seq 1157/1230/1268/1344/1486 — five turns reading interfaces in other modules' worktrees. Against the AT-237 measurement (medicao-do-jev.md), this agent had 24 steps with a tool in the whole round: 5 of 24, ~21% of its steps, went into discovering someone else's interface. The project had seven dev modules (piece-catalog, retro-renderer, input-keyboard, game-session, scoring, persistence, board-engine). What could NOT be measured here: the token cost of those five steps. The 29/09 event log lives in the maintainer's local instance (compose brabo-dev) and is not in this environment; the number above comes from the analysis and from the agents table of the Jev measurement, not from a redone query. The cost gain is measurable later, by the same rule as AT-239 (token_usage per actor).
documents.s: The symptom

documents.t: The module_map (domain/architecture/module-graph.ts) is {name, stack, responsibility, dependsOn[]}. It says WHO depends on whom and nothing about WHAT a module offers. None of the Arquiteto's artifacts (module_map, project_image, module_routing, c4_diagram) carries an interface. The dev's context (Engine.Dev.ContextBuilder) brings story, task, business rules and ADRs filtered by module — no neighbour interface. The dev's tools (Engine.Dev.Tools) were read_file, search_workspace, write_file, terminal, rag_search/rag_feedback and the termination ones: no project artifact reading. The only way to see the neighbour's interface was the terminal reading the other dev's worktree — code IN PROGRESS on a branch that has not yet reached dev, and that may change after the read.
documents.s: What the product gave the dev (measured on dev, 2026-10-01)

documents.t: The contract is the artifact.module_contracts artifact, the Arquiteto's. No table: the event is the record, versioned by version in the payload, and the current one is the highest version with a tie broken by seq — the same reduction as GetC4DiagramUseCase/GetModuleRoutingUseCase. Each declaration carries the WHOLE list and REPLACES the previous one; changing a contract is a new version emitted by the Arquiteto, and the previous ones remain in the log. The format is the smallest that solves it: per module, only what it EXPOSES. {modulo, expoe: [{tipo, assinatura, descricao}]}, with tipo in funcao | rota | evento | dado, mandatory assinatura (up to 300 characters), optional descricao, and from 1 to 40 items per module. What it CONSUMES is not written in the contract. It is derived, at read time, from the current module_map's dependsOn — the same argument as the C4 Container level (ADR 0068): the map already validated those edges as acyclic, and a second hand-written list would diverge from it at the first revised map. The granularity "which items of X module Y uses" was left out: the Arquiteto does not know it before implementation, and whoever consumes X reads the whole list of what X exposes. tipo is an enum and assinatura is free text. The type is what changes how the item is USED; the signature does not fit a single schema because each module's stack is free (an Elixir function and a Go route). The ceilings exist because the contract goes into every dev's context. A contract that becomes the whole API documentation would cost on every step what the worktree read cost on one. An artifact SEPARATE from the module_map, never one more field in it. The map is a table, is read by the whole execution (task claim, routing, C4) and revising it reopens cycle validation. The contract changes at another pace — the interface is discovered while the devs work —, and revising one cannot re-emit the other nor fight over its schema with another front (the round-36 resources lane adds a field to the module_map). The Arquiteto gains declare_module_contracts (:direct, like route_modules_to_infra: an architecture declaration, with no external effect, never a proposed_action). The api validates and refuses with the whole reason, which goes back to the model (RN-061): a module outside the current map (listing the valid ones), no module_map, a repeated module, empty expoe or above the ceiling, unknown tipo, empty or too long assinatura. Its kickoff gains step 5; the tool enters Engine.Harness.IdiomaDaResposta.ferramentas_de_artefato/0 (RN-623). The dev agent gains listar_contratos_de_modulos (:direct, in the Engine.Dev.Tools registry, outside the global one). CONTAINED reading: scope closed to the project by the route's path (GET internal/projects/:projectId/module-contracts), NO parameter, and the dev's module comes from the loop context (ctx.module, set by DevAgentServer), never from the model. With the module known, it shows in full only its own and those it consumes; those that consume it and the rest appear by name. A ceiling of 120 items in the text, with what was left out stated. A contract of a module that left the map is STATED, never attributed. The dev's kickoff says the contract exists and where to read it, and that another module's interface is not read in its worktree. Without a contract for the module it needs, the tool says what to do: implement from what the story and task say and, if the task depends on an interface that does not exist, report_blocked naming the module and what is missing — for the Arquiteto to declare. It does not tell it to reread the worktree.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The step the dev spent discovering interfaces becomes a constant-cost read, and what it reads is the version the Arquiteto fixed, not another dev's in-progress code. The interface now has an owner and a version. Whoever changes it is the Arquiteto, in a new version; the dev that needs a change does not make it in the neighbour's code, it blocks naming what is missing. It is not a lock. Nothing prevents the terminal from reading another worktree: the tool and the kickoff change the path the dev knows, they do not forbid the other. Closing the reading of someone else's worktree would be path containment (ADR 0055), another front. The Arquiteto gains a step in the kickoff, under the SAME ceiling of 14 iterations. Not measured whether it fits together with the other seven in a large architecture; exhausting the ceiling is still narrated (toolloop.limit_reached, RN-166). Projects without a contract keep working: the read returns the map with expoe: null on each module and the notice. No migration, no table. The artifacts' docs/ folder (ADR 0148) gains the type as versioned: the current one overwrites the same file, like the other four. Out of here, declared: its own screen (the contract appears on the timeline and in the docs/ folder, not on the Architecture tab); the effect on Jev's gain (AT-239 measures tool per step; this one changes the dev's menu, and scripts/jev/catalogo.json is the 29/09 snapshot, not regenerated here); the ExUnit tests ran outside mix (repo.hex.pm gives 403 in this environment) — CI proves them.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-013, story HS-008, epic EP-003, round 36; owner decision on 01/10: "yes, revocation by KEY, with an ADR — key column in the socket ticket and a new auth contract; revoking drops only the connections opened with that key. It touches the engine, on purpose."). Revises RN-520 — born in ADR 0147 point 6 — and references, without editing them, ADR 0154 (the MACHINE key, which put "Revocation by key" among what it did NOT do) and ADR 0155 (the machine key born in the terminal and registered by the installation). New rule: RN-685.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Since RN-520, revoking a device key drops the runner's LIVE connection, and not only the next ticket. The target of that drop was {project, user}, and RN-520 said why: the identity of the credential that requested the ticket — the key's kid (which is the record id, RN-475) or the PAT — died in the PatAuthGuard. runner_socket_tickets stored project_id, user_id and kind, and nothing else; the channel only knew how to compare the user. Measured in the code before changing (origin/dev, ec0fbea52d): How the ticket is born. POST /projects/:projectId/runner-ticket goes through PatAuthGuard, which authenticates by PAT (validarEUsar returns {id, userId, projectId}) or by device key (the JWT header's kid finds the public key in runner_device_keys; chave.id is that kid). The guard set only request.user. RequestRunnerTicketUseCase asked the engine POST /internal/projects/:projectId/runner-tickets with {userId, kind}, and Engine.Runners.SocketTicket.emitir/3 recorded the row. How the engine consumes. EngineWeb.RunnerSocket.connect/3 validates the ticket and puts project_id/user_id/kind in assigns; the socket's id/1 was runner_socket:<kind>:<projectId>:<userId>; the channel's join/3 consumes and registers the presence in Engine.Runners.Registry (:global, at most ONE runner per project in the cluster). Where revocation dropped. RevokeRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase records the revocation and calls disconnectRunnerOfUser(projectId, userId) — POST /internal/projects/:projectId/runner/disconnect —, the engine finds the pid through the Registry, the channel compares user_id and broadcasts disconnect to its OWN id. For the MACHINE key (null project) PR #534 made the target PLURAL: the same pair, once per runner-mode project the owner reaches (listRunnerModeReachableBy). What drops today that should not. The same user's runner connected with a PAT, or with another key, in that project. With the machine key, the cost multiplies: revoking the laptop's key drops the desktop's agent in every project where both cross. What does NOT drop today and should. (1) The machine key's connection in a project the api's list does not have — an owner's role that dropped, a project converted in mode with the runner up. (2) The ticket requested seconds BEFORE the revocation and used AFTER: connect/3 and join/3 do not ask about the credential. (3) Revoking a PAT dropped nothing — it only prevented a new ticket. AT-013 was blocked for two stacked reasons: it was outside the PHASE 30 cut, and changing the target is changing what "revoke" means. The owner decided.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The ticket records WHICH credential requested it. Two NULLABLE columns in engine.runner_socket_tickets — credential_kind ("device_key" | "pat") and credential_id (the kid, or the PAT id) —, Ecto migration 20261001120000_add_credential_to_runner_socket_tickets.exs, additive, no backfill (tickets live 30 s). The table is the ENGINE's (schema engine), so the migration is its own; the Drizzle journal does not change (stays at 0068). Null is a legitimate state: the terminal ticket is the web tab's, authenticated by session, and a runner one issued by an api predating this ADR arrives without it during the rollout. The auth contract now carries the credential up to the engine. PatAuthGuard fills request.credencialDeDispositivo ({tipo: 'pat', id} or {tipo: 'device_key', id: chave.id}) after authorizing; the controller passes it on; RequestRunnerTicketUseCase sends it only with kind: "runner" (the terminal one never carries it, even if someone passes one); the internal request gains credentialKind/credentialId, which only travel together. The engine normalizes the pair (SocketTicket.credencial/2): an unknown kind or empty id become nil, never an invented credential — and the ticket still works. The engine keeps the credential in the socket. connect/3 sets assigns.credencial, and id/1 gains two segments when it exists — runner_socket:<kind>:<projectId>:<userId>:<espécie>:<id> —, so the disconnect the channel broadcasts to its OWN id reaches only that credential's connections. Without a credential, the id is the previous one. Revoking ONE credential has its own route and its own target. POST /internal/runner/disconnect-credential (no :projectId: the machine key does not have one), Engine.Runners.Revogacao.derrubar_credencial/4: voids the credential's PENDING tickets (consumed_at filled — the same "already used" state that validar/1 and consumir/2 refuse, no new state), closing the window between issuing and using; asks EVERY runner registered in the cluster (Registry.todos/0) whether it was born from this credential — only the channel knows, because the credential lives in assigns. Whoever was born from it drops (transport + {:stop, …} releasing the presence); whoever was not answers :intocado and stays up; answers 200 with a TALLY (derrubados, legados, intocados, semResposta, ticketsAnulados), with a 5 s ceiling for the WHOLE set. 400 only for a malformed credential — so "I targeted nothing" never passes for "there was nothing". The MACHINE key stops being the pair applied N times: it is ONE request, and it drops in every project where it opened a connection, including one the api would not list. Key and PAT revocation use that target.
