RevokeRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase (and, by delegation, the Account door, RN-611) asks for the drop by {tipo: 'device_key', id}; both PAT revocations (the owner's, RN-426, and the maintainer's, RN-427) now drop by {tipo: 'pat', id} — before they dropped nothing. The order does not change: revoke FIRST, drop afterwards, and dropping is a side effect that only LOGS. Not failing to drop what already dropped (AT-013's prohibition). Two TRANSITION pieces, and neither is the target: The LEGACY connection (ticket without a credential) of the same owner, in one of the projects the api sends as reach (the row's, or the machine's candidates), drops by the pair as before (:derrubado_legado). Only for a device key: the PAT dropped nothing before, so it gains no legacy reach — it would gain a drop it never had, on someone who has nothing to do with it. PLAN B: if the engine does not serve the by-key request (an engine predating this route answers 404), key revocation falls back to the old target, disconnectRunnerOfUser per project. Dropping too much is reversible; failing to drop would reopen RN-519. {project, user} still exists, with ANOTHER owner. POST /internal/projects/:projectId/runner/disconnect and Revogacao.derrubar/3 stay byte for byte (with the finer socket id): it is the target of MEMBER REMOVAL (RN-615), which removes the PERSON from the project and needs to drop any connection of theirs, with whatever credential — besides plan B above. The screen changes the text, not the behaviour. The revoke confirmation — in the device keys section of Settings and in the machine keys section of Account — swaps the "collateral" ("another runner of yours in the same project also drops") for PRECISION ("only what connected with THIS key drops"), because RN-561 requires the screen to state the right reach and the old sentence would assert a drop that does not happen. It is the answer to AT-013's TODO(humano) ("does the screen change behaviour or only label?"): only label — the click, the route and the invalidation are the same. The runner does not change. It already sent the kid in the JWT header, and that is all the path needs. Not one line of apps/runner/.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: It does not change what AUTHORIZES. No new ceiling, none loosened: PatAuthGuard decides as always, and the credential is only ANNOTATED after authorizing. This ADR moves the drop's target, never the authority. It does not drop the web's Terminal tab. The kind: "terminal" socket has no device credential, does not occupy the Registry and is never asked — as before. It does not close a ticket issued and not yet CONNECTED with an old api's credential. A ticket without a credential (issued by an earlier api) is not voided on revocation: there is nothing to compare. The window is 30 s and only exists during the rollout. It does not give the maintainer view revocation of another user's key. It stays out by RN-519's decision.
documents.s: What this ADR does NOT do

documents.t: The same user's other runner stays up. The cost RN-520 declared goes away: revoking the laptop's key does not drop the desktop connected with another key, nor the runner connected with a PAT. Revoking the machine key is ONE request, and more complete than the plural. It reaches projects the api's list does not have. The price is asking EVERY runner in the cluster — linear in connected runners, only when someone revokes, and with a 5 s ceiling for the set. Revoking a PAT now drops. It is an observable behaviour change: the runner connected with a revoked token drops immediately, instead of going on until it reconnects. For the maintainer's revocation (incident response, RN-427) it is what was missing for it to contain anything. The tally replaces the single outcome in the key revocation log. The four outcomes of derrubar/3 still exist for member removal. Rollout without operator action. The migration is additive and runs in the usual migration job (Engine.Release.migrate/0). New api with old engine: the ticket request's new fields are ignored and revocation falls into plan B. Old api with new engine: tickets without a credential, which drop by the pair (legacy), and the old revocation keeps calling the pair route, which did not change. That is why the branch is feature/ and not breaking/. The runner socket's id changes shape. Nothing outside reads it — it is Phoenix's internal disconnect topic —, and a socket opened before the deploy dies with the old pod. Engine proof only in CI. The ExUnit (real channel with a credential, a PAT that stays up, a machine in two projects without a list, legacy by the pair, a pending ticket voided, controller 200/400) was written without running locally (repo.hex.pm gives 403 in this environment); syntax and formatting checked.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-137, story HS-014, epic EP-011, finding BRB-026, round 36; owner decision on 01/10: "yes, reorganize by theme, with the theme OUTSIDE the ADR" — a mapping file ADR → theme next to the index, checked by docs:check, and no accepted ADR edited). The taxonomy — the list of 15 themes and the theme of each of the 191 ADRs — is a PROPOSAL of this lane, and the owner reviews it in the PR: changing an ADR's theme or merging two themes is a change to docs/adr/temas.yml, not to this text.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: docs/adr/index.md was grouped by PHASE. That helped while phases were the way the project moved; it stopped helping when phases ended and work started being born from the kanban: measured on 2026-10-01, of the index's 191 rows, 148 lived under a single heading, ## Phase 12 — Post-dogfooding operability, from 0044 to 0197 — the section that was "the rest" became the index. Whoever looks for "what was decided about the broker" or "why the machine key is like this" has nowhere to start except reading 148 lines. AT-027 did the counting half of BRB-026 (the index said 134 with 156 written) and separated this half in writing, with the question that blocked it: the theme would be a tema: metadata in each ADR's frontmatter — and adding frontmatter to an accepted ADR is editing it, which the index convention forbids without exception. The owner's decision solves the question from the other side: the theme lives OUTSIDE the ADR. What already existed and remains: verificarIndiceAdr (scripts/docs/generate.mjs) fails an ADR without a link in the index, and verificarContagensEmProsa checks the count in the index's description and "the next one is NNNN". Neither knows anything about grouping.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: 1. The theme lives in docs/adr/temas.yml, next to the index. Two keys: temas: — the CLOSED list, in order, each with id (kebab-case, the anchor {#tema-<id>} and the map's value), titulo (the section heading in the index, in English like the index) and descricao — and adrs:, the map "NNNN": <id>. Each ADR has ONE theme, the main one: when two fit, the one where someone would look first wins. No accepted ADR is touched. 2. The index is CHECKED, not generated. Each index row is a curated sentence about the ADR, and no script writes it (the reason verificarIndiceAdr already recorded). Generating the index would require moving the 191 sentences into the YAML — trading readable Markdown for a long YAML string, to gain an ordering the check already guarantees. The index now has one section ## <titulo> {#tema-<id>} per theme, in list order, with the one-line sentence of the descricao and the usual table, in numeric order. 3. scripts/docs/temas-de-adr.mjs checks, and docs:check fails (verificarTemasDeAdr, sibling of verificarIndiceAdr, called right after it): an ADR in docs/adr/ without a theme; a theme in the map not in the list; a map entry for an ADR that does not exist; a list theme with no ADR; a list with a repeated id or title; in the index, a theme section missing, repeated, with a title different from the list's, out of list order or of a nonexistent theme; and an ADR row under another theme's section, outside any theme section, repeated or out of numeric order. Unreadable YAML, an empty list or map, or an index with no theme section is CEGO and fails. Each rule is proven by mutation in scripts/docs/temas-de-adr.spec.ts, like the other checkers. 4. The proposed taxonomy has 15 themes. It comes from the product's FRONTS — the same that organize CLAUDE.md and the agent-areas.ts catalog —, not from phases nor code folders: id theme ADRs git Git, repository and branch policy 11 agentes Agent harness, turns and sessions 11 time The agent team — roles, areas and handoffs 26 gates Gates, QA and security review 12 execucao Execution, terminal policy and approvals 13 modos Where the code lives — execution modes 9 container Project container and broker 15 runner The local runner 11 iam Auth, access and secrets 13 llm LLM providers, models and spend 16 conhecimento RAG, knowledge graph and artifacts 11 web Web UI and design system 12 operacao Operation, deploy and installation 15 engenharia CI, release and supply chain 10 docs Documentation 7 Why THIS list, and the boundaries that are not obvious: agentes × time. agentes is HOW an agent runs (context, tool loop, turn, session, message queue, response language); time is WHICH agents exist and what they deliver to whom (roles, areas, delegation, handoff, the Psicólogo and the Anamnese). Together they would make 37 ADRs — a smaller "Phase 12". The conversational Infra Lead (0175) falls in agentes because it decides its turn; the Dev Lead (0053) in time because it decides the role. modos × container × runner. Three fronts that touch each other in every ADR since 0104, and therefore separated by the QUESTION: where the folder lives (modos), who brings up the container and with what containment (container), the CLI on the user's machine (runner). The runner bringing up the container (0137) is container; credentialed git on the runner's host (0193) is runner. execucao × gates. execucao is the policy that holds the agent that ACTS (proposed_action, path scope, automatic mode, absolute ceilings); gates is the verdict on what was done. operacao joins deploy and installation. Both answer "how the product runs on a machine that is not its developer's" and share backup and the installation compose; separated, installation would have 7 ADRs and be the 16th theme. engenharia takes what belongs to the REPOSITORY and not the product: the pipeline, published images, signing, Trivy, pin by digest, the test layers and the schema split by aggregate (0121) — the api's only structural refactoring, which would not be looked for in any other theme. The splits of SessionPage.tsx/ProjectSettingsTab.tsx stay in web, where whoever touches those files looks. Language is not a theme (only 0177 decides on it, and it is in agentes); security is not a theme — it crosses iam (CSP, CORS, envelope), execucao (ceilings), container (broker containment) and engenharia (supply chain), and a "security" theme would empty four to fill one. Ten to fifteen was the requested range: fewer than ten would join modos/container/runner or agentes/time, which is where the by-phase index failed; more than fifteen would make the theme become the folder. 5. Who decides a new ADR's theme: whoever writes it, in the same PR — one line in adrs: and the index row in the theme's section, in numeric order. Whoever reviews the PR confirms. A NEW theme is a change to the list in temas.yml, justified in the PR that creates it; going beyond 15 requires an ADR revising this one.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The index stops having a section per phase, and with it go the opening sentences of each phase. The per-phase narrative stays where it was always complete, docs/explanation/historico-de-fases.md; the open acceptance criterion notice of ADRs 0020/0021 goes with them to gates. A new ADR costs one more line (temas.yml), and forgetting it FAILS docs:check — the same price and the same reason as verificarIndiceAdr. The theme is a CLASSIFICATION and several ADRs serve two. The index shows each one once, in the main one; whoever looks under the other theme does not find it there. It is the price of "one theme per ADR", and the alternative (a secondary theme) was considered and did not go in: it would duplicate the curated row or leave it in two places that age separately. Parallel ADRs: the mapping covers the ADRs that existed on origin/dev on 2026-10-01 (from 0001 to 0197, plus this one). Whoever integrates an ADR born on another branch adds its line — docs:check points out which is missing. The pt-BR translation of the index (website/i18n/pt-BR/.../adr/index.md) stays by PHASE and was already behind (103 of 191 rows); it is not reorganized here. The docmap's traducao-pt-br rule warns, in warn, as always.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: It edits no ADR, not even to fix a title. It does not generate the index: the sentences stay hand-curated. It creates no RN: the rule is about documentation, like the runbook procedures one.
documents.s: What this ADR does NOT do

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-01 (AT-014, BRB-031, round 36; owner decision on 01/10: "retire ADR 0118's browser flow — generating the key, downloading the binary and writing config through the browser; the path is install.sh"). Revises, without editing it, ADR 0118 (automatic runner configuration through the browser, RN-464..466) and closes BRB-031. Preserves ADR 0154 (the two key kinds), ADR 0155 (the machine key is born in the terminal and the installer registers it, RN-547/551/552) and ADR 0150 (the one-line installer and the verification of its own origin).
documents.s: Status

documents.t: ADR 0118 made the browser generate the Ed25519 pair (Web Crypto), register the public key (POST /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys), download the binary (GET /runner-releases/binary) and write three files into a folder through the File System Access API — or, outside Chromium, trigger two downloads. It accepted a limitation in writing: "the browser does not preserve the execute bit; chmod +x on Linux/macOS stays manual". It was the last manual step of any installation path, and it is BRB-031. PHASE 29 created a second path without that step: install.sh downloads the binary, checks it against the signed checksums.txt and installs it with install -m 0755 (RN-531). PHASE 30 completed pairing on the machine side: brabo-runner device-key create generates the pair ON THE MACHINE (RN-551), the installer registers the public key through the internal MACHINE route with the service token (RN-552) and chains both things at the end of the installation (RN-547). Since then the browser flow was the second path, collapsed in a <details> of RunnerOnboardingPanel (RN-548), and retiring it was declared as a maintainer decision, not a consequence of that delivery. Measured on dev (ec0fbea52d) before changing — who uses what the flow uses: apps/web/src/lib/runner-bootstrap.ts (generate pair, export JWK, download binary, write folder, manual kit) had one production consumer, RunnerOnboardingPanel. Outside it, only its own test and scripts/ci/alvos-do-runner.spec.ts, which read the browser's platform list as the fourth place enumerating targets. registerRunnerDeviceKey (apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts) was only called by runner-bootstrap.ts. POST /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys was only called by runner-bootstrap.ts and by e2e/testes/chave-de-dispositivo.spec.ts, which existed to prove EXACTLY the key generated in a Chromium. No script, no runner, no workflow, no install.sh calls it — the installer uses POST /internal/machine-device-keys. GET and DELETE of the same route have OTHER consumers: the keys section of Settings (RN-561), the panel's recognition (RN-548) and revocation. PatAuthGuard accepts a PROJECT key by kid, and there are project keys registered on real installations through the browser flow. GET /runner-releases/binary (the download proxy) had only the browser as a production consumer.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: RunnerOnboardingPanel sends to install.sh. The panel's foreground becomes the installer command (curl -fsSLO …/install.sh && bash install.sh, the SAME sentence as the runbook and install.sh itself, RN-526), copyable, with what it does stated in text — downloads the binary, checks it against the signed manifest, installs it already executable and pairs the machine — and the EsperaDoRunner (RN-474) below. The command is a TS copy of the installer's sentence, and scripts/dev/install-invocacao.spec.ts fails a diverging copy. What STAYS in the panel: recognition of an already paired key (RN-548 and that of the PROJECT key, AT-107), with the same caveats — and, once a key serving the project is recognized, the installer block LEAVES. The manual command with a PAT (--token) stays in the <details>, renamed for the case it solves: "Another machine, or run manually". What GOES from web: all of runner-bootstrap.ts and its test (key generation through Web Crypto, binary download through the browser, writing via File System Access and the two-download kit), registerRunnerDeviceKey and the RunnerDeviceKeySummary type, the i18n keys of the flow's buttons and states, and the platform selector. What GOES from the api: POST /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys, with RegisterRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase and the two DTOs only it used. It was left without a caller. The internal MACHINE route (POST /internal/machine-device-keys) STAYS, and the JWK shape rule (exigirJwkPublicaEd25519, in the domain) stays with it. An ALREADY registered project key remains valid, and is revocable. Nothing in the database changes: a filled runner_device_keys.project_id is still a valid kind, PatAuthGuard still accepts the JWT signed by it, GET still lists and DELETE still revokes. A runner configured through the browser before this ADR does not break: the folder with brabo-runner.config.json and brabo-runner-device-key.jwk.json is still read by the CLI (RN-466 in full), and the PROJECT unit it may have installed stays up. What ceases to exist is creating a NEW project key. The e2e of the browser-generated key goes too. What it proved — that the kid written by the BROWSER is accepted by the server — has no producer anymore. The chain kid → JWT → PatAuthGuard with a real key remains covered in apps/api/test/interfaces/pat-auth.guard.spec.ts and the pair generated on the machine in apps/runner/src/criar-chave-de-dispositivo.spec.ts. The runner's target list now lives in THREE places, not four: the browser's went with the module, and scripts/ci/alvos-do-runner.spec.ts locks it from silently coming back. The branch is breaking/: removing a public route documented in OpenAPI is a contract change for whoever calls it, and the version policy (scripts/ci/version.ts) says the FUNCTION decides — a patch would say "update without thinking".
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Good. The installation path no longer has a manual chmod step anywhere in the product: the only one that had it is gone. BRB-031 closes. A NEW device key is born in one place only — the machine's terminal — and is registered by one registrar only — the installer. The api loses a write route authenticated by a session JWT. Web loses ~530 lines of crypto, download and disk-writing code that jsdom could not exercise without a double. Bad, declared. An installation with a team loses the PAT-less path. The route that creates a MACHINE key only serves a ONE-person installation (409 with two or more, RN-552), and install.sh installs the whole of Brabo on a machine — it does not serve to pair a SECOND machine with an existing installation. For those people the path becomes the manual command with a PAT (--token), which the panel keeps offering and names as the other machine's. The browser flow was the only way to pair without a PAT in that case, and the owner's decision retires it anyway. GET /runner-releases/binary is left without a production consumer. The proxy was NOT removed here: the decision named the key registration route, and the proxy carries RN-525's integrity check and the open provenance half of BRB-005. Removing or keeping it is the owner's decision, separately. Whoever had the flow's tab open at deploy time gets a 404 on the POST when clicking — the old bundle still calls the route. Reloading the page fixes it. RNs 464..466 and 473/475 describe the flow as it was; they get a revision note, never deletion.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-02 (AT-385; owner decision on 02/10: "yes, allow auto-promotion of any and every agent if the agent is in auto mode", confirmed as applying also to the dev agents' git push and PR opening). Revises, without editing them, ADR 0102 (the absolute ceiling on external effects, RN-418) and RN-689 (the same ceiling through the typed door), only in the push and PR half. Preserves ADR 0167 and ADR 0189.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Since RN-418, git push, PR opening, deploy and sudo/doas were unconditional require_approval in decide(), even with automatic mode on; RN-689 extended the ceiling to the typed actions git_push and pr_open. With the autopilot (ADR 0189) the dev agent already runs free inside the container, and the only point where the execution flow still stopped for a human decision in automatic mode was each task's push and PR.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: With the agent's AUTOMATIC MODE — the agent_autonomy wildcard actionType: "*" resolved to auto_approve (origin curinga) —, typed git_push and pr_open, and the same effect through the terminal command (git push, git remote add/set-url, gh pr create, glab mr create), come out auto_approve, with the reason modo automático (RN-713) in proposed_action.created (RN-567). ONLY the wildcard releases. A specific auto_approve rule without the wildcard, "Always allow" (still refused at the source for push/PR) and allow in permissions.json still fall into the ceiling. Activation still seeds only git_commit (RN-689). Still an absolute ceiling, even in automatic mode: merge (into a protected branch, through the typed action; and git merge/gh pr merge through the terminal), deploy, sudo/doas, container_remove, instruction_patch and parallelism. open_adr_pr/open_infra_pr already followed automatic mode and still do. Switching the toggle back to manual restores approval for push and PR.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The dev agent in automatic mode pushes and opens PRs without stopping; the merge into dev stays manual, so code only reaches a permanent branch through a human click. The guarantee becomes the explicit consent of automatic mode, per agent, and no longer the ceiling. The price is declared: a PR opened by mistake does not ask for confirmation before existing in the provider.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-02 (AT-356 part 2, owner decision on 02/10: "Yes, a product signal"). Complements ADR 0196 without editing it: the Anamnese still maintains the PERSON's profile; what this ADR adds is a second record, about the AGENTS.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: In the 02/10 test store (AT-376) the Anamnese read as a user trait what was an agent failure: "Não vi o handoff aparecer. Pode passar ao Arquiteto?" became a "continuity driver" — it was the person covering for the PO's failure. The same holds for an agent in a loop and for a turn cancelled by the user. That signal has value, but for whoever improves the PRODUCT, and not for the profile of whoever produced it. Measured on dev before changing: the Anamnese only had verbs about the person (emit_proficiency, skip_proficiency) and about instructions/ceiling (propose_instruction_patch, propose_max_parallel, which become proposed_action). There was nowhere to say "agent X deviated" without attributing it to someone.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Its own durable event, anamnese.agent_deviation, recorded in the event log of the round's session by the new tool report_agent_deviation (:direct, does not end the round, actor agent/anamnese). No personal data, by construction. The payload is assembled in the engine by an ALLOW list: agente, tipo (closed vocabulary: laco, cancelamento_pelo_usuario, reparo_pelo_usuario) and evidenceEventIds (deduplicated, ceiling of 20). There is no free-text field — it is in one that the model would write a name or trait. Session and project come from the event's envelope. An extra field the model invents is discarded. Outside the user's graph. GraphEventTranslator does NOT translate the type: the graph is the PERSON's memory (profile, accepted facts), and the signal is not theirs. A test pins its absence in EVENTOS_DO_LOG_PROJETAVEIS. Reading by event, no new screen. Whoever improves the product reads by querying the event log (session_events with type = 'anamnese.agent_deviation'). The Insights tab gains no reading now: it is per project and for whoever decides, and this signal's reader is the product's maintainer.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The user's profile stops absorbing agent failure: the kickoff tells it to record the repair as a deviation (RN-716/RN-717). Declared gaps: the api does not check that the evidenceEventIds exist (the internal append does not validate this type's payload); there is no aggregation nor screen; and recognizing the deviation is the model's — the code only guarantees the shape and the absence of personal data. Changing the tipo vocabulary is a change of this contract, with an RN.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-02 (AT-359; owner decision on 02/10). Revises, without editing it, ADR 0033 in its PUBLISHING half: the spec still comes from the code (docs/reference/openapi.json, DTOs by type, table test) and web's openapi:types:check does not change.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: ADR 0033 published the reference with docusaurus-plugin-openapi-docs and docusaurus-theme-openapi-docs (5.1.2): 235 generated .mdx in docs/reference/api/, locked by a hash manifest. Both drag in postman-collection@5.3.1, which pins @faker-js/faker@5.5.3 EXACTLY — High alert #43, GHSA-qxc2-j82w-r537. Measured on 02/10: no parent in the chain has a version that leaves faker 5.5.3, and the override to 10.x fails docs:build (v5 API removed). There was no way to close the alert while keeping the plugin.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Swap the pair of packages for Redocusaurus (redocusaurus 2.5.x): ONE Redoc page, with SSR, at /reference/api/, read from the same docs/reference/openapi.json. Why it: it is a Docusaurus 3 preset, renders on the server (the page comes out in the build's HTML, checkable without a browser), follows the site's theme and does not pull postman-collection nor faker. pnpm docs:generate stops generating .mdx and the .openapi-manifest.json manifest; docs/reference/api/ leaves the repository. The sidebar gains a LINK to /reference/api/ in place of the per-tag category. scripts/docs/api-render-check.mjs remains the post-build guard (0033's lesson: a green build is not a page that renders), now asserting in the HTML of both languages the spec's title and one section per operation.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Closes alert #43: @faker-js/faker and postman-collection leave the website/ tree. Two overrides were left without a consumer and went (js-yaml@>=5.0.0 <5.2.2 and undici@>=6.0.0 <6.28.1, which only arrived through the plugin), along with the allowBuilds of postman-code-generators. LOSSES accepted by the owner: the 235 per-operation pages, the per-tag sidebar, the per-operation URLs (external links to them break), the playground and the cURL snippets. The guard does not open a browser: a Redoc hydration failure is not caught; a missing, empty or operation-less page is.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-02 (AT-391, owner decision on 02/10). Revises ADR 0067 without editing it: automatic rescue continues, with an age ceiling.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: ADR 0067 made the GateRescuer resume on its own every in_progress cycle stalled for more than 15 min, at boot and on every tick. The real use of 02/10 showed three problems: (1) it restarted a cycle whose session had a proposed_action pending from a qa-* actor — the cycle was waiting for a person, the area was paid again and the action would be orphaned; (2) the "live process" test was per PROJECT and the row is per TASK, so a lost cycle went 8 h without rescue because the project's QA Lead was alive and idle; (3) there is no ceiling: a cycle nobody looked at for hours is restarted entirely over a context that may have changed.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Alive is per task. The rescue asks the lead ({:em_voo?, task_id}); a lead too busy to answer counts as alive. A pending human decision holds the rescue. A pending action from a gate actor (qa*, secops*, appsec) in the cycle's session: log only. A 2 h ceiling, by last activity. Age counts from updated_at, the same column as the staleness threshold, and not from inserted_at: upsert! touches updated_at on every subagent, so a cycle that advances is not old; counting from creation would park long, live cycles. Above the ceiling, the row gets parked_at, the session log gets gate.rescue_parked (task, gate, age, reason) and the sweep stops seeing it — boot and tick. Resuming requires a human gesture, through GateRescuer.retomar_estacionado/3. A new in-flight entry of the same cycle clears the mark.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: There was no human path to resume a gate cycle; the minimum delivered is the engine function, called by the operator. An internal route and a button on the event remain proposed, not done. The pending item is read by SESSION, not by task: proposed_actions has no task_id. Two tasks in the same session with a pending QA action hold each other — an accepted price, the worst case is not rescuing, never paying twice. Rule: RN-722, which revises RN-140.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-02 (AT-392; owner decision on 02/10, "direct egress"). Revises, without editing them, point 3 of ADR 0190 (the server's start-up with a literal network: "none") and departs from §4 of ADR 0065, which asked for the user's authorization for egress.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured on 02/10 (project loja-teste-2): the Arquiteto decided artifact.project_image v1 with network: "egress" ("Egress needed for npm install…"). On acceptance of the Infra handoff, the server's automatic start-up (subir_no_aceite/2, infra_lead_server.ex) proposed container_start with none, and ExecuteContainerStartUseCase recorded v2 (infra-lead) with none, overwriting the Arquiteto's decision. The Node container came up without network, and npm install does not run.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Infra's election INHERITS the network of the most recent artifact.project_image emitted by the Arquiteto (actor_id: "arquiteto"), in any session of the project — read locally by the engine (Event.rede_do_arquiteto/1, the same Postgres, no HTTP in the loop). It applies to the server's start-up on acceptance and to the propose_container_start tool when the model does not pass network. Without an Arquiteto decision (or with a value outside none/egress), it stays none, as before. The start-up still happens on its own: ADR 0190's container_start: auto_approve seed does not change, so egress comes up without a click.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The price is DECLARED, not paid: the egress network reaches the machine's published ports (ADR 0189, edge 5), and the reasoning of external-effect.ts that "without a network, curl | sh reaches nothing" stops holding for every project where the Arquiteto declared egress. The user consent ADR 0065 §4 asked for leaves the path by owner decision. The version recorded by Infra now repeats the Arquiteto's network instead of downgrading it; the artifact's history stays coherent. Rule: RN-723.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-02 (AT-398; owner decision on 02/10, "move the engine up to OTP 29.1.x"). Changes the runtime pinned in ADR 0024 (decision 10: the same Elixir version in the Dockerfiles and in CI), without editing it — the SINGLE version rule still holds, what changes is the version.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Since AT-361 the engine's Dockerfile.prod runs on Alpine 3.24.2 with OTP 27.3.4.18 (hexpm does not publish 27.1.2 on 3.24), while dev and CI stayed on Elixir 1.17.3 / OTP 27.1.2 / Alpine 3.20.3. The engine build in CI started aborting in about 10% of runs (0/57 before #821, 5/49 after) with: sys_signal_stack.c:101:sys_sigaltstack(): Internal error Measured cause: Alpine 3.24's musl 1.2.6 refuses the fixed-size alternate signal stack (SIGSTKSZ = 8192) that ERTS 27 requests, on hosts with AMX (erlang/otp#11349). The fix — sizing by sysconf(_SC_MINSIGSTKSZ) (commits 3a94587176/fc35c2496c) — exists ONLY from OTP 29.1 on. The same defect would make the PRODUCTION engine die at boot on a server with AMX: the CI flakiness is the machine lottery. Moving Alpine back to 3.22 would fix the symptom and freeze the image on a line that stops receiving security fixes; it was not chosen.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The engine runs Elixir 1.20.4 / OTP 29.1.1 in dev, production and CI. The image is hexpm/elixir:1.20.4-erlang-29.1.1-alpine-3.24.2, pinned by the INDEX digest (sha256:ad851f40…, ADR 0159/0178), the SAME in the Dockerfile.prod builder and in the dev Dockerfile. The production runtime stays alpine:3.24.2 (the builder's musl matches the runtime's). Elixir 1.20 is the only line with an hexpm image and build for OTP 29.1. ELIXIR_VERSION/OTP_VERSION go up together in the three workflows that declare them (ci.yml, golden-set-rag.yml, golden-set-qa.yml), and mix.exs now requires ~> 1.20. The "Build, scan e smoke" job prints whether the host has AMX (grep -c amx_tile /proc/cpuinfo): green on a host with AMX is the proof that the defect did not come back, and not luck of the draw. No mix.lock dependency changed: mix deps.get + mix compile --warnings-as-errors pass on the new version. Elixir 1.20's type checker pointed out a dead clause in Engine.Agents.FilaDeMensagens.acordar/3 — the failure to start the agent RAISES, it does not come back as a value — and it was fixed by containing the error per agent, not silenced.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Dev price: the engine's _build/deps volumes were compiled with OTP 27. Mix recompiles on its own what was built with another Elixir version, so docker compose up -d --build engine is enough; if the volume insists on old artifacts, docker volume rm of the engine's two volumes. Being automatic recompilation, the change is NOT breaking for operators. Whoever runs the engine outside Docker needs Elixir 1.20.4 / OTP 29.1.1 (mix format --check-formatted depends on the version, ADR 0024 decision 10). Dependabot docker: with OTP 29.1 + Alpine 3.24 there is no broken pair anymore, and no ignore was added. It may propose a newer OTP 29.1.x hexpm/elixir tag — all contain the fix. A proposal that GOES DOWN to OTP < 29.1 with Alpine ≥ 3.24 reintroduces the defect and must be refused in review. A Kubernetes rollout mixes, for moments, OTP 27 and 29 nodes: Erlang distribution accepts pairs up to two major versions apart.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-03 (AT-401; owner decision on 03/10: use AI Elements' Shimmer on every "in progress" text, with the motion lib).
documents.s: Status

documents.t: The text saying "the agent is working" ("Thinking…", "Gathering information…", the "working" status) was static or came with three pulsing dots. The owner chose AI Elements' Shimmer (https://elements.ai-sdk.dev/components/shimmer). The original uses motion/react, Tailwind and shadcn's cn; Brabo's web has no Tailwind, shadcn nor clsx — it is CSS Modules over design/tokens.css.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: motion enters apps/web and lives behind ONE component, apps/web/src/components/ui/Shimmer.tsx; no other file imports it. LazyMotion + domAnimation + m.create(tag) (cached per tag in the module), to load only the DOM animation subset. Its OWN vendor group, vendor-motion, in the allow list of codeSplitting.groups (AT-300). The chunk does not enter the initial load: only the screens that use the Shimmer (session, Overview, Executors) pull it. The gradient uses tokens: base --text-secondary, shine --text-primary. The worst point (the base) is measured in design-contraste.test.ts over --surface-0/1/2, in both themes. This PR applies it to the agent's turn; the loading texts and the other in-progress states come in their own PRs.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Measured weight (pnpm --filter web build): initial index chunk 52.81 → 52.89 kB (16.73 → 16.75 kB gzip); new vendor-motion, 76.23 kB (26.53 kB gzip), outside index.html. Reduced motion: useReducedMotion() returns the static text in the base color, and the CSS Module has @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce). The thread's three .typing/.typingDot dots went away; the bpulse keyframe stays, because other components use it.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-03 (AT-404; owner decision on 03/10: "The expandable navigation bar on the left becomes the ONLY one; remove the other navigation bar, but include in this one all items of the removed bar"). Revises ADR 0126 — which stays accepted and is not edited — and RN-201.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Since ADR 0126 the project tabs existed in TWO places: the 180px vertical rail (ProjectRail.tsx, mounted in ProjectPage.tsx) and the sidebar's per-project list (LinhaDeAba, RN-196). CLAUDE.md declared this as a gap ("reconciling is a separate product decision"), along with the frame's price: 492px on the Code tab (264 of the sidebar + 180 of the rail + 48 of the CodeShell). Measured before changing, what only the rail had: the three GROUPS with a heading; the ACTIVE tab marked (aria-selected); the five counters (Insights, PRs, Approvals, Backlog, Architecture), each on its tab and never summed — the sidebar showed only Approvals, from the dashboard summary; the keyboard (ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End with wrap-around, crossing groups); the active one scrolled into view; the vertical role="tablist"; and, on the phone (RN-643), the scrollable horizontal bar above the panel. The sidebar had, and the rail did not: the project collapsed in the 62px rail, the phone drawer and the link to another browser window.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The sidebar is the project's only navigation. ProjectRail.tsx, its CSS and its mounting in ProjectPage.tsx go. The project list in the sidebar becomes AbasDoProjeto (apps/web/src/routes/AbasDoProjeto.tsx), with everything the rail had: groups from GRUPOS_DO_PROJETO, active tab, per-tab counters, keyboard, a vertical tablist named by the project, roving tabindex and the active one scrolled into view. Each tab is a link to /projects/<id>?tab=<chave>. The five counters have the SAME source, with no new request. The five queues are now read by a single hook, useContagensDoProjeto (apps/web/src/lib/contagens-do-projeto.ts), which the frame uses for the "needs you" panel (RN-467) and the sidebar uses for the numbers. Same queryKeys, deduplicated. The sidebar only turns it on while the project frame is MOUNTED — that was the only place the rail existed; on another project screen (the Session, for example) and on closed projects the Approvals number from the summary stays, as before. The *.orcamento.test.tsx budgets pass without changing any ceiling. The active tab comes from the frame. ProjectPage publishes the tab it shows (publicarAbaAtiva) — the URL is not enough, because the "needs you" panel switches tabs without going through the router. The sidebar ASKS the frame for the clicked tab (pedirAba, an event and not state, so two frames never pull each other) and navigates with ?tab=. The project link without ?tab= goes back to the default tab. Collapsed, a flyout. In the 62px rail, the OPEN project's square opens a flyout with the same tabs (closes on Esc, on choosing and on the second click), without expanding the sidebar. The other projects still expand. On the phone, the drawer. RN-643's horizontal bar goes; the tabs live in the drawer, which closes when one is chosen. The CodeShell's 48px rail stays: it is the editor's activity, not project navigation.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The Code tab's frame drops from 492px to 312px with the sidebar expanded (264 + 48) and to 110px collapsed (62 + 48). The gap "the tabs exist in two places" closes. Switching tabs requires the expanded sidebar, the flyout or the drawer. Whoever collapsed the sidebar and navigated through the rail now uses the flyout. The sidebar list loses the router's <Link> per tab: it is an <a> with the click intercepted, calling navigate. Middle button/Ctrl still open in another window. rail.ariaLabel leaves both languages; the list is named by sidebar.projects.tabsAriaLabel ("Abas de {{name}}").
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-03 (AT-406; owner decision on 03/10: "PO and user" — the PO and the Backlog tab edit and archive a draft story with no task in execution). Rule in RN-727.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: In the 03/10 TP-01 the PO created two duplicate stories and had no way to remove them: its tools were create_epic, create_story, create_task and complete_story, and the Backlog tab was read-only. The duplicates got tasks, entered the Dev Lead's plan and confused the Arquiteto. The decision was to allow ARCHIVING (and fixing the title), without deleting anything from the log. Three ways of representing "archived" were weighed: A new story_status value. Rejected: status = 'ready' is the claimability gate (claimNext), and the state machine (story-state-machine.ts) is about the story's progress. Archiving only happens from draft, has no way back in this delivery and is not a progress step — putting it in the enum would force every transition to know about it. Deleting the row. Rejected by the owner's decision and by the product's convention: what was done stays, and the tasks and events citing the story would keep pointing to something that vanished. An archived_at (and archived_reason) column in stories. Chosen.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: stories gains archived_at timestamptz NULL and archived_reason text NULL (migration 0069), in the backlog aggregate's file (ADR 0121). NULL is the story in play. Every read that DECIDES filters archived_at IS NULL: the backlog and coverage (findByProject), the promotion queue (listProposedReady), the Dev Lead's plan (findInProjectByIds) and the claim and claimable count (claimNext, countClaimableByModule). TASKS leave play through the story — no new column in tasks. findById still finds the archived one, for the named refusal and auditing. Archiving turns off proposed_ready in the SAME write (the story never stays "awaiting you" after being archived). The fact goes to the log in NEW, immutable events: backlog.story_archived (storyId, title, reason, taskIds) and backlog.story_updated (storyId, previousTitle, title, descriptionChanged). The backlog. prefix follows the aggregate's existing events (backlog.story_created, backlog.story_promotion_returned). A single rule (recusaDeCorrecaoDeHistoria) for both doors — the PO's tool and the user's route —, with a named 409.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Unarchiving does not exist in this delivery: the column allows it, but it is a separate product decision, not taken here. The archived story disappears from listar_backlog (the PO does not see it so as not to complete it again); whoever needs to know about it reads the event in the session log. The user's minimum role is developer, the same as promoting and returning (RN-048) — no new role.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-11 (AT-517; owner decisions of 11/10: "through Infra's compose", no published port on the broker). Rules in RN-851..855. References, without editing, ADR 0130, ADR 0190 and ADR 0199.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: At the end of an execution the user had merged code and no declared way to see it running. What was measured: The docker-compose.yml Infra opened in the PR was "for development": it brought up the environment, not the APP, and the Infra Lead's prompt said the project container does not come up through it. The image decided in artifact.project_image did not reach Infra when it wrote the compose, so the module Dockerfile's FROM was a guess. The app's default port (3000) collides with Brabo's on the same machine. The project container has no Docker (ADR 0130 containment), so nothing inside Brabo can run docker compose up to prove the compose. The deliverable's routes are already documented in the README by the dev (RN-850), and QA already brings up processes in the background and ends the group (RN-817), but nothing tied a URL to what the user opens.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The path is Infra's compose, run by the user in the delivered repository. The broker does NOT publish a port: ADR 0130's containment stays intact. The compose brings up the APP (RN-851): build of the module's Dockerfile with FROM equal to the artifact.project_image image, host port ${APP_PORT:-8080}:<porta interna> (8080 is free next to Brabo's ports: 3000, 4000, 5173, 5432, 7474, 7687, 8088, 11434), a volume for persistent data and env_file with a committed .env.example — never .env. Infra writes the README's "Run on your machine" section, in its PR. The dev keeps "HTTP routes" (RN-850) and adds the Swagger or page URL when it creates it. propose_infra_pr gains the MANDATORY run field, validated in the engine and the api: command: non-empty string, up to 300 characters (e.g. cp .env.example .env && docker compose up --build); urls: 1 to 5 items { label, url, kind }, label up to 60 characters, kind ∈ api_docs | web, url starting with http://localhost: or http://127.0.0.1:; envExample: boolean — when true, the .env.example is among the PR's files. The api emits artifact.run_instructions (RN-852) when executing open_infra_pr successfully: versioned, no table, the current one replaces — the design of artifact.project_image —, payload { command, urls, envExample, prUrl }, read by GET /projects/:projectId/infra-artifacts (or a dedicated GET if that one does not serve). The dev exposes what is opened (RN-853), without tying a stack: an HTTP module serves /openapi.json (OpenAPI 3) and /docs (Swagger UI); with network none or without the package, /docs is an HTML page loading swagger-ui from a CDN — whoever downloads it is the user's browser, not the container. A web module serves the home page. The clause only enters when the task touches the entrypoint or routes. QA proves INSIDE the container (RN-854): it brings up the app with the README's command in the background, hits localhost:<porta interna>/openapi.json and /docs (curl, wget or node -e fetch) and ends the process group (RN-817). The real docker compose up is an OBSERVATION ("proven only on the user's machine"), never a plan item. The Overview gains the "Run on your machine" card (RN-855): the command with a copy button and the clickable URLs, with the text "declared by Infra, not verified on your machine" (RN-468) — never green.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Token cost: the run payload, the README section and the dev and QA clause are more text in turns that already existed; no new turn. Declared gap: the real docker compose up never runs inside Brabo. What QA proves is the app answering inside the container; host port, volume and build through the compose are only proven on the user's machine, and the screen says so. What does NOT change: the containment of ADR 0130 and the broker (no published port, no socket in the container, internal network), the automatic start-up of ADR 0190 and the resources derived from the module_map of ADR 0199. The evidence that the entrypoint comes up (RN-813) and the HTTP route in the README (RN-846) still hold; this ADR adds the URL that is opened, it does not replace the proof.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: A port published by the broker for the user to open the app from the project container. Refused by owner decision: it would open the project container's first port to the host and change ADR 0130's containment. The screen reads the repository's README or compose to build the card. Refused: it would be parsing prose and YAML on the client, without a contract; the validated run payload and the versioned artifact give the same data with a fixed shape.
documents.s: Alternatives considered

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-11 (AT-521; owner decisions on 11/10). Extends ADR 0207 (gate cycle parking) and REVISES part of ADR 0212 (story correction). Rules in RN-858, RN-859, RN-860 and RN-861. Theme: gates. The mechanism that really changes behaviour is QA's new verdict, which does not consume a cycle and parks through ADR 0207's mechanism; the record and the queue exist so that verdict has someone to ask.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured in TP-01 (14th round): The Criativo left four questions to the user only in the response TEXT. None became a record; nothing on screen listed them after the thread scrolled. QA failed GET /:codigo for "not confirmed by the user" until it EXHAUSTED the correction cycle (RN-762) — twice. The second came AFTER the owner answered in the chat: the story was already ready, ADR 0212 only allows correcting a draft story, and QA read the story's DoR, which still said "not confirmed". The dev had nothing to fix: the decision was the user's, and changes_requested spent a cycle on every round. Three things were missing: a RECORD of the question with state, a VERDICT that says "this depends on the user" without punishing the dev, and a path for the ANSWER to reach whoever works (the dev's context, QA's cut, the story itself).
documents.s: Context

documents.t: artifact.open_question (append-only, in the log of the session where it is born): { questionId, pergunta (≤ 500), sugestao (≤ 300, optional), afeta: { regras, historias, tarefas }, autor, sessionId }. It closes with open_question.answered { questionId, resposta, aceitouSugestao, decisionEventId, respondidaPor }. The STATUS comes from the log (open = no answered), never from a table. The answer records a decision_record (actor: the user) with context = the question, choice = the answer, consequences = what it affects, and the questionId. It is the same generic artifact as RN-505.
documents.s: 1. The record

documents.t: declare_open_question (Criativo, PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead), with ONE CENTRAL instruction sentence, not repeated per server: "Every doubt you leave for the user becomes declare_open_question, with your suggestion and what it affects; do not end the turn with a question only in the text."
documents.s: 2. The origin is only the tool

documents.t: Only the AUTHOR of the session where the question was born. For QA's question, the author of the execution session (whoever activated execution). Other members see the question with the control inert and the reason in text (ADR 0064).
documents.s: 3. Who answers

documents.t: GET /projects/:projectId/open-questions?status=open|answered|all — viewer, limit 50 with the total (RN-180). POST /projects/:projectId/open-questions/:questionId/answer — body { resposta } or { aceitarSugestao: true }; 403 so_o_autor_da_sessao, 409 pergunta_ja_respondida, 404 for a question of another project.
documents.s: 4. The routes

documents.t: "I'm ready" (Criativo) and "Confirm architecture ready" show "N questions are still open — answer", with a shortcut to the queue. They do not block.
documents.s: 5. Readiness warns and moves on

documents.t: emit_qa_verdict gains needs_user_decision with { pergunta, sugestao } (or an existing openQuestionId). The api does NOT increment the correction counter (RN-762), records the open_question (author qa-agent, affecting the task) and the cycle stays PARKED through ADR 0207's mechanism (gate.rescue_parked). The task appears as "waiting for you". Answering the question turns the gate back on through GateRescuer.retomar_estacionado/3 (RN-724's path), and QA judges with the decision in context. In the QA Lead's consolidation, a subspecialty's needs_user_decision wins over approved. QA's cut rule: a requirement marked "not confirmed by the user" (or contradicted by a current decision) → needs_user_decision, never changes_requested. This EXTENDS ADR 0207: there the cycle parked due to idle time; here it also parks due to a pending user decision. The resume gesture is the same mechanism, triggered by the answer.
documents.s: 6. The needs_user_decision verdict

documents.t: GET .../dev-context returns decisoes — those linked to the story/task through afeta, ceiling 10 and 1,500 characters. The dev's kickoff and QA's cut show "User decisions — they win over FR/DoR when they conflict".
documents.s: 7. The decision reaches whoever works

documents.t: What CHANGES in ADR 0212: recusaDeCorrecaoDeHistoria now accepts a ready story when the correction request cites an ANSWERED questionId; the PO receives the answer and fixes FR/DoR. What does NOT change: the refusal with an in_review (and in_progress) task stays; archiving stays only for draft; correcting ready without an answered questionId stays refused; editing by the user in the Backlog tab follows 0212's rule.
documents.s: 8. The PO corrects a ready story by the user's answer (revises ADR 0212)

documents.t: An "Open questions" queue in the chat's pending block, with its own title and count (never summed with the other queues, RN-467): the question, who asked, what it affects, the suggestion with "Accept suggestion" and a short field with "Answer" — both only for the session's author. The "N open questions" notice sits next to "I'm ready" and "Confirm architecture ready".
documents.s: 9. The screen

documents.t: Token cost: ~60 tokens per conversational turn (the central sentence and the tool description) and up to ~400 in QA's cut / the dev's kickoff when there are linked decisions (ceiling of 10 and 1,500 characters). The correction cycle stops being spent on what the dev cannot solve. The question has an owner: the session's author. A member who is not the author does not unlock — declared price (see Alternatives). What does NOT change: the absolute ceilings (RN-418), the manual merge into a protected branch, the correction cycle ceiling (it only stops counting this verdict), ADR 0212's archiving rule, and ADR 0207's time-based parking.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Blocking readiness with an open question. Refused: the question may be a detail that does not prevent the PO from moving on; blocking would trade forgetting for a lockup. Warning with a shortcut solves the forgetting. Detecting questions in the agent's text. Refused: a heuristic over prose errs both ways and creates pending items nobody declared. The origin is the tool, and the central instruction is what makes the agent use it. QA going ahead with the agent's suggestion. Refused: approving on a guess hides the user's decision and is exactly the "not confirmed" requirement QA exists not to let through. Any developer member answering. Refused by owner decision: the question is about the intent of whoever conducted the session; another member answering would swap the owner's decision without them knowing.
documents.s: Alternatives considered

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-14 (AT-526; owner decisions on 14/10). REVISES part of ADR 0214: the dev context rule "a decision without an afeta touching the task does not go in". Rules in RN-870, RN-871 and RN-872. Theme: gates. The effect that matters is the QA gate's: it stops repeating a question the user already answered.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured in TP-01 (15th round, viralabs-app-2026-10-11b): The user answered "does a nonexistent or deleted code respond 404?" at 15:45. The "list and delete links" task belonged to ANOTHER story, and its QA stated that the question was still unanswered, gave needs_user_decision and the gate parked with no open question in the project — the thread had nothing to answer. The afeta.regras the Criativo records are rule TITLES, and ADR 0214's filter (afetaAlgum) compares with IDS: no Criativo decision ever matched. Even with ids, the cited rules were not those of the task's story. The verdict accepted an openQuestionId of a nonexistent or already answered question, and would park forever.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The verdict's openQuestionId is checked (RN-870): it must exist in the project and be OPEN, before any write. Nonexistent (or of another project) is 404 pergunta_nao_encontrada; already answered is 409 pergunta_ja_respondida with the decision text in the body (decisao), without a write and without pr.gate_changed — QA reads the decision instead of waiting. afeta.regras accepts the exact title (RN-871): in the event funnel, the exact title of a project artifact.business_rule becomes the id (the most recent, if the title repeats); what is neither an id nor an exact title is a named 400. The dev context read also matches by the TITLE of the story's rules, for decisions recorded before this rule. The project's other decisions arrive too (RN-872, the owner's option (a)): GET /internal/sessions/:sessionId/dev-context returns, besides decisoes (those touching the task), decisoesDoProjeto — the project's other decision_records, in a SEPARATE list, within the SAME ceiling of 10: the task's come first and consume the ceiling before. That is what revises ADR 0214, whose sentence "a decision without afeta does not go in" stops holding for the project list (it still holds for decisoes).
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The new field is additive: the engine ignores it until the engine lane prints the "Other project decisions" section in the dev's kickoff and QA's cut (context_builder.ex reads the context by Map.get with a named key). The ceiling of 10 is SHARED. In a project with many decisions, the old ones not touching the task are left out — the price of not widening the context. decisoesDoProjeto includes every project decision_record, not only those born from a question answered by the user (the Criativo's about technical constraints too, RN-711). A title repeated across rule versions resolves to the most recent; there is no refusal for ambiguity.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-15 (AT-545, epic EP-032; owner decisions of 15/10). The owner asked for the documentation (site and README) and the interface in four languages — Brazilian Portuguese (DEFAULT), English, Russian and Mandarin (Simplified Chinese) —, in PHASES, and answered this ADR's four open questions (see the Decision, items 4, 9 and 10). Model for the README and for measured localization: the storytold/photocraft repository (README.md, docs/localization.md, docs/localization-parity.md). Theme: docs. Reverts English as the interface default, which came from the i18n foundation (RN-432) without an ADR, and the site's defaultLocale: 'en'. No accepted ADR is edited: RN-432 gets a revision through a new RN in the interface PR.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Measured on origin/dev (f0a355fe5a): The site declares defaultLocale: 'en' and locales: ['en', 'pt-BR'] (website/docusaurus.config.ts:109-116), and docs/ is the default locale's tree. But, of the 261 files in docs/ (5.7 M characters), 92 are in pt-BR in the body — the RNs (business-rules.md, 1.58 M, and business-rules/autenticacao.md), the ADRs since 0127 and the phase history —, about 2.7 M characters. The "en" site serves that text in Portuguese. The site's shell (sidebar, navbar, footer) is also in pt-BR, with no translation file at all. The translations in website/i18n/pt-BR/ cover 135 of the 261 pages, and 97 of them have the source changed after the translation's last commit. Nothing tells the reader nor the PR author: the docmap's traducao-pt-br rule is warn and measures nothing. Of the 100 ADRs with a pt-BR copy, 66 are, byte for byte, the text of the commit that created the ADR: ADRs 0001–~0103 were written in Portuguese, and what is in docs/adr/ is the English translation. The interface has en as default only in web (apps/web/src/lib/idioma.ts:38, i18n.ts:52); the api already records pt-BR as the users.locale default (apps/api/src/db/schema/iam.ts:87). There are 2,310 strings in 27 namespaces, about 90 thousand characters per language. The language of the agents' RESPONSES is already an open BCP-47 list (ADR 0177, RN-618/622) and does not depend on the interface language. The Docusaurus theme ships translations for pt-BR, ru and zh-Hans (@docusaurus/theme-translations@3.10.2); zh-CN does not exist there. The local search (@easyops-cn/docusaurus-search-local) segments Chinese with jieba and indexes Russian through lunr-languages.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: pt-BR is the SOURCE and the default, in both products. On the site, docs/ becomes the pt-BR tree (defaultLocale: 'pt-BR'), and en, ru and zh-Hans live in website/i18n/<locale>/. The alternative — keeping English as the source and only opening the site in pt-BR through localeConfigs.<locale>.baseUrl — is possible in Docusaurus 3.10 and was refused: every new text would be born in English, and the 2.7 M characters in Portuguese would keep being served under the English label. In the interface, pt-BR is web's default and the fallbackLng, and it is the reference of the parity tests. The codes are pt-BR, en, ru and zh-Hans, the same in Docusaurus, in i18next, in <html lang> and in users.locale. The local search uses its own codes (pt, en, ru, zh). Locale resolution in the interface: the choice recorded in the account always wins and is never overwritten by detection. Without a choice, the browser suggests: pt* → pt-BR; zh, zh-CN, zh-SG and zh-Hans* → zh-Hans; ru* → ru; en* → en. A language without a catalog falls back to pt-BR (owner decision): German, Traditional Chinese and any other open in the default, not in English. Text missing in a locale falls back to the pt-BR source — and is not missing in the interface, because parity fails it. The site's switch is a single PR, through git mv: the current English goes to website/i18n/en/; the UP-TO-DATE pt-BR translations replace the source; the outdated and nonexistent ones leave the page in the language it is in until its batch, with a notice; and website/i18n/pt-BR/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs leaves in the SAME PR, otherwise the default locale's folder would override docs/ and the 97 outdated copies would go live. A page not translated, or whose source changed after the translation, SAYS so, in the reader's language: a DocItem/Content wrapper tells source from translation through metadata.source, and each translated page carries in its frontmatter traducao_de: <commit da fonte>. Parity is MEASURED and the report is GENERATED by pnpm docs:generate (docs/reference/paridade-de-traducao.md, generated: true; --check fails an out-of-date file): per locale, pages and characters translated over the source, outdated pages, review date, native review and what stays untranslated by decision; in the interface, keys per namespace against pt-BR and the plural forms of Intl.PluralRules (pt-BR: one/many/other; en: one/other; ru: one/few/many/other; zh-Hans: other). The written rules live in docs/explanation/localizacao.md, with a terminology note per language — what is never translated: Brabo, the glossary's agent and role names, user data, commands and RN/ADR numbers. The README is a showcase, in the photocraft model, with pt-BR as the source and README.en.md, README.ru.md and README.zh-Hans.md. The translations carry neither version nor derived counts: they link the pt-BR, which is the checked one. ADRs 0001–~0103 go back to the original pt-BR text in docs/adr/ (owner decision), and the English goes to website/i18n/en/. It is not editing an accepted decision: it is restoring the text that was accepted, which today is in the pt-BR copy. It only applies to a copy that is byte for byte the text of the creation commit; one that diverges stays as it is and is stated in the parity report. Until the English batches arrive, the English site shows the RNs and recent ADRs in Portuguese, with the banner warning (owner decision). And old links /brabo/<ambiente>/pt-BR/… are rewritten by the root 404 to /brabo/<ambiente>/…, like ADR 0073's /main/ → /prd/; English leaves the root for /brabo/<ambiente>/en/… (owner decision). Phases. Phase 1: the site switch, the entry pages (intro, getting-started, glossary and the zero-to-deliverable tutorial) in the four languages, the four READMEs, the full interface in ru and zh-Hans, and measured parity. Phase 2 onwards: batches per sidebar category × locale, one PR each — first the pt-BR of the 97 outdated pages and of the 26 English-only ones, then the English of the pt-BR pages, then ru and zh-Hans.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The docmap swaps the traducao-pt-br rule for traducao, warn and NEVER block: requiring translation in every doc PR would cost four translations per change. What holds the lag is the generated report and the page banner. A sentence anchored in code (verificarFrasesAncoradasNoCodigo, counts) on a page that becomes pt-BR fails as CEGO until the pattern follows, in the batch's PR — on purpose. There are 19 sentences today. The same holds for the heading procedimentos-do-runbook.mjs looks for and for the titles of docs/adr/temas.yml when the index switches. ancoras-de-rn.mjs now checks the RNs of the three translated locales, and links-do-locale.mjs now knows en, ru and zh-Hans as prefixed locales. users.locale gains ru and zh-Hans (Postgres enum, DTOs, generated types). The response language does not change mechanism — an account in ru already gets the generic BCP-47 guidance —, and native guidance texts and the detection of Cyrillic and Han remain a measured improvement, not a prerequisite. Declared costs: the site build compiles four locales (about double today, not measured); the search index grows (not measured); translating everything is about 2.9 M characters to English and 5.3 M for each of Russian and Chinese; every PR changing a translated source needs to run pnpm docs:generate; English leaves the environment root for /en/. Without native review, Russian and Chinese come out as machine translation reviewed by an agent, and the report says "native review: no" until a human reviews.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: docs/reference/** (generated) stays out of translation, and the generator keeps writing in English. Languages beyond the four, Traditional Chinese and right-to-left scripts. Translating the content users and agents produce (artifacts, messages): that is the PROJECT's and the responses' language (ADR 0177), not the interface's.
documents.s: Out of scope

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-15 (AT-555, owner decision of 15/10): "To gain agility, an auto-merge rule into qa whenever there is a merge into dev, and a notice that, while it is in a test phase, qa will not yet be considered." Theme: git. Revises, without editing, ADR 0030's promotion flow (the promotion merge as a manual act) and its approval ladder, only for the dev → qa pair and only with the variable on. ADR 0073 (the published path names the environment) does not change: what changes is how much /brabo/qa/ publishes.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: The dev → qa promotion was always manual: promote.yml (workflow_dispatch) computes the version and opens the PR through BRABO_BOT_TOKEN, and the owner approves and merges. With qa not yet used as a validated environment, that step cost one human gesture per cycle without protecting anything anyone consumed. The repository has no required checks: gh pr merge --auto would merge at once, without waiting for CI. Automating the merge requires the WAIT to be the automation's.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Workflow promote-auto-qa.yml, on push to dev, only with the repository variable QA_FASE_DE_TESTE == 'true'. It runs the SAME version computation (scripts/ci/promote.ts) and the SAME opening step (scripts/ci/abrir-pr-de-promocao.sh, extracted from promote.yml) to open or update the dev → qa PR through BRABO_BOT_TOKEN. Wait and merge through scripts/ci/promocao-automatica.ts: it reads the head's check runs until ALL have finished; it merges with a merge commit (and --match-head-commit) only if none ended failure, cancelled, timed_out, action_required, startup_failure or stale. Zero checks means waiting, never merging. Any failure stops the promotion and writes in the job summary which check and the link. A 50-minute wait ceiling. Concurrency promote-auto-qa, no cancellation. An empty cycle is not a failure in automatic promotion (cicloVazioEhFalha): a push to dev with no new work — a promotion merge, a backmerge, dev already equal to qa — exits 0 with ::notice:: and "nothing to promote: the cycle is empty" in the summary, without opening a PR. Recurring red would teach people to ignore red. In the manual promote.yml it is still a failure. Without BRABO_BOT_TOKEN, a visible failure: the job exits red saying so. The default token would open the PR with checks in action_required and its merge would trigger neither tag-release nor docs-deploy. The ladder (scripts/ci/approval-ladder.ts, ehPromocaoAutomaticaDaFaseDeTeste) waives approval ONLY when the pair is dev → qa, the variable is on and the PR's author is the BRABO_BOT_TOKEN user — resolved in the workflow through gh api user with the secret itself, never by a fixed name. The reason appears in the check's summary. qa → main and any other pair still require approval, in both modes. The notice: the site published at /brabo/qa/ gains a fixed announcementBar, and the automatic PR's body opens with the same text — "Fase de teste: a QA é promovida automaticamente a cada merge na dev e ainda não é considerada ambiente validado."
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Each merge into dev with green CI becomes a -qa.N tag (tag-release runs on the push to qa), and N now counts merges, not validation rounds. /brabo/qa/ is republished on every merge into dev. The variable turns on and off without touching code: deleting it or changing the value goes back to the manual promote.yml, and the ladder again requires the owner. qa → main stays intact: manual, with approval, and the final tag is only born on the commit of the last -qa.N. If the BRABO_BOT_TOKEN user is the owner themselves, the ladder already passed by authorship (solo mode); the new waiver only changes the written reason. Declared price: qa stops being a validated candidate while the variable is on — which is exactly what the notice says.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-15 (AT-559, owner decision of 15/10): standardize ADR naming in the title only. Theme: docs. Complements, without editing, the index convention (0202).
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Of the 213 ADRs in docs/adr/, 82 opened with # ADR NNNN — … and 131 with # NNNN — …. Both forms coexisted without a rule, and whoever wrote a new ADR copied the neighbor's. The title is what shows in the browser tab, the site's local search and the sidebar; the number alone does not say the page is an ADR.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The title (H1) of every ADR is ADR NNNN — <title>: the ADR prefix, the 4-digit number and the em dash —. The file name stays NNNN-<slug>.md, and existing slugs stay as they are, in any language: the file name is the published URL, and renaming it would break outside links. Replacing # NNNN — with # ADR NNNN — in accepted ADRs is a mechanical normalization of the LABEL, not an edit of the decision. The rule "an accepted ADR is never edited" still holds for the content: Context, Decision, Consequences and the title text stay intact. Translations under website/i18n/<locale>/ get the same prefix; the translated title text stays. docs:check (scripts/docs/temas-de-adr.mjs) fails an ADR whose H1 does not start with # ADR NNNN — , with the number equal to the file's.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: One form only, checked: the next ADR no longer picks between two. The change touches 131 source files and the translated copies in the same commit; the traducao_de: of the copies that were up to date is bumped in the next commit, so parity does not report staleness that does not exist. Slugs keep mixing languages (short-title in English in the old ones, pt-BR in the new ones). That is accepted: the URL is worth more than uniformity.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-15 (AT-564, owner's decisions of 10/15). Theme: docs. Revises, without editing it, the point of 0216 that kept docs/reference/** out of translation.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: ADR 0216 made pt-BR the source of the documentation, with en, ru and zh-Hans as measured translations, but left docs/reference/** out on the grounds that "it is generated". That holds only in part: of the ten reference/ pages, six are hand-written (artifacts, brb, git-providers, internal-api, permissions, rulesets) and were in English, and the four generated ones (configuration, events, llm-providers, scripts) carry hand-written prose around the generated block. Readers of the pt-BR site landed on whole pages in English, and parity did not count them.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: docs/reference/** ENTERS translation and parity, except reference/paridade-de-traducao.md (the report itself) and reference/openapi.json. The source of the six hand-written pages becomes pt-BR in docs/, and the current English becomes the en copy. In the generated pages, the generated BLOCK is translated too: the generator writes the pt-BR source and writes the block into each locale's copy, from a table of fixed texts. The lag that appears with every new variable or event is accepted as a warning of the parity report and of the page banner, not as a failure. A heading that is a link target gets an explicit {#current-slug} anchor before being translated, so outside links do not break. The translation banner declares the page's real language through idioma_original in the frontmatter. The API page (Redoc) will also be translated; that is AT-565, and this ADR only records the decision. The docmap traducao rule starts watching the docs/reference/ pages, except the parity one.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Parity starts counting reference/, and the numbers drop in the first report: untranslated pages show as missing or outdated until translation rounds reach them. The docmap has no glob negation, so the traducao rule lists the reference/ pages one by one; a new reference page enters it in the same PR. The generator gains one output per locale (item 3), work for its own round; until then the generated block of the copies stays in the source language.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: 0216 — four languages, pt-BR as source. 0206 — the Redoc API page.
documents.s: References

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-16 (AT-565, owner's decisions of 10/16). Theme: docs. Fulfills item 7 of 0219 and opens a declared exception to the pt-BR source of 0216.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: The API reference is a Redoc page generated from openapi.json (0206), and its text comes from the api decorators: almost all in English, with a few dozen texts in pt-BR. The site has four locales, but the page came out the same in all of them. The plugin only accepts a file path as spec, and Docusaurus loads the config once per locale with DOCUSAURUS_CURRENT_LOCALE set.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The source of the descriptions remains the decorator text; the api is not touched. This is an EXCEPTION to the pt-BR source of ADR 0216: pt-BR, ru and zh-Hans translate every text, and en only those in pt-BR (heuristic: a Portuguese diacritic or a function word such as "não", "para", "que"). The translation lives in a CATALOG per locale, website/i18n/<locale>/openapi-textos.json, keyed by the sha1 (12 hex) of the source text, with fonte and traducao. It covers summary/ description at any level of the spec and the tag label (x-displayName); the tag NAME does not change, so the #tag/<name> anchor stays. The locale spec is DERIVED at build time by docusaurus.config.ts (scripts/docs/openapi-por-locale.mjs) and written to website/.openapi/, ignored by git. Nothing derived is committed. An ORPHAN key (a hash the spec no longer has) and an INVALID entry (source that does not match the hash, or a different number of `…` spans between source and translation) fail docs:check; a missing entry only warns and falls back to the source text, as in D3 of 0219. The 18 labels of Redoc 2.4.0's LabelsConfig are translated via theme.options.labels. The texts it hard-codes with no option ("Request Body schema", "Response Schema", "Authorizations", "Search...", "Expand all", "Copy", "required", "API docs by Redocly" and the like) stay in English. Translation parity gains its own "API (Redoc)" section, in distinct texts per locale, not added to the page characters.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: New text in the api shows up as missing in every catalog until the next translation round; changed text leaves the old entry orphaned, and docs:check requires removing it in the same PR (pnpm docs:openapi-textos <locale> adds the new keys with traducao: ""). The catalogs start empty; translating the texts is a round of its own. The pt-BR page mixes Redoc labels in English with the translated rest, a Redoc limitation, not a content choice.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: 0206 — the API Redoc page. 0216 — four languages, pt-BR as source. 0219 — the reference enters translation.
documents.s: References

documents.t: Accepted. 2026-10-21 (AT-580). Tema: llm. Estende o 0166 (que só mandava provider.sort; seu docblock dizia que os outros campos do objeto provider são decisão de produto própria) sem editá-lo, e segue o 0041 e o 0042: a capability só vira true com prova contra a API real.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: No TP-01 da 18ª rodada, o mesmo modelo foi servido por 17 upstreams diferentes e o acerto de cache dos dev agents caiu. O OpenRouter já tem a memória pedida (provider sticky routing): prende a conversa no upstream que a atendeu e só cai para o próximo se ele falhar, por 10 minutos de inatividade. Sem session_id, a "conversa" é o hash da primeira mensagem system mais a primeira não-system, e o grude só liga depois de um acerto de cache; cada tarefa do dev abre com outra primeira mensagem, então cada uma sorteava um upstream novo. Com session_id no corpo (até 256 caracteres), o grude liga na primeira resposta com sucesso.
documents.s: Contexto

documents.t: O Brabo manda session_id = brabo:<sessionId>:<agentId> (sem agente, brabo:<sessionId>) nas chamadas ao OpenRouter, montado em StreamLlmTurnUseCase e RunLlmTurnUseCase (chaveDeSessao) e levado em ChatOptions.sessionKey. Por agente + sessão, nunca por projeto: cada agente tem prefixo próprio (instruções + ferramentas) e misturar dois num grude não ganha cache. Capability nova stickySession em LLMProviderCapabilities, obrigatória nos nove providers, false em oito; no OpenRouter é true depois do smoke openrouter-provider.sessao.smoke.spec.ts (6 de 6 chamadas no mesmo upstream com a chave, 4 upstreams em 6 sem ela). Declará-la sem o hook campoDeSessao falha na construção. Fora: provider.order, only e allow_fallbacks — order desliga o sticky routing, pede o slug (e gravamos o nome do frame) e escolher o "melhor" exigiria ler token_usage por chamada (teto do ADR 0060). Só entra como evolução se a medição pós-entrega mostrar o upstream grudado ruim. Sem tabela, sem engine: a chave é derivável de token_usage (session_id + actor_id) e o hub guarda a memória. O Jev (ADR 0179) não recebe a chave.
documents.s: Decisão
