documents.t: The dashboard sidebar shows a health dot per project, derived from three independent signals: budget (the same 70%/90% thresholds as RN-018), blocked task (tasks.blocked), and recent activity (7 days). Colors: green = healthy and active; amber = budget ≥70%; red = budget ≥90% or blocked task; gray = no activity in the last 7 days. When a risk signal (amber/red) and the inactivity signal (gray) apply at the same time, the risk one wins — an overrun, stalled project is still something to look at, not something to hide behind "no activity". Where: apps/web/src/lib/project-status.ts (deriveProjectStatus) Test: apps/web/src/lib/project-status.test.ts Origin: fidelity of the projects dashboard to the approved design
documents.s: RN-039 — Project status dot: risk always beats inactivity

documents.t: Every screen that loads data from the api distinguishes three states, never two: loading (skeleton), error (the message the api sent, with the trace_id and a try-again button), and empty (the empty-list text). if (!dado) return null collapses the three, and the observed outcome was the worst possible: with the api rate-limiting with 429, the main area of /projects/:id was completely blank — no message, no error, no skeleton — and the reason existed only in the console. On the dashboard it was worse than blank: !projects was also true on error, so the screen invited you to create the first project of a workspace that could have twenty. It's RN-059 on the other end of the wire: failure never becomes an empty response. Whoever fails, says so. The sentence is the api's, extracted by mensagemDaApi — the same function the mutation path already used in toasts. A generic text of ours doesn't know the difference between "rate limit exceeded, try again shortly" (wait) and "access denied" (waiting won't help). The other side of the same rule is not answering the limit with more traffic. 4xx is not retried: 429 is literally the server telling you to stop, and 401 has already been renewed once inside request(). And polling stops when the query errors — it comes back on window focus, on remount, or on the button. Before, there were three retries per failure added to ~25 polls of 3 to 5 seconds that didn't know how to stop: a real session accumulated 1128 429 errors against a limit of 300 requests per minute per user (RateLimitGuard), and the loop kept the sliding window from recovering. 5xx and network failure keep the three attempts, where repeating is the right reaction. Where: apps/web/src/lib/query-policy.ts (deveRetentar, pollQueParaNoErro), apps/web/src/components/ErroDeCarregamento.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectPage.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/Dashboard.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/Shell.tsx, apps/web/src/main.tsx Test: apps/web/src/lib/query-policy.test.ts; apps/web/src/routes/ProjectPage.test.tsx (429 becomes a message with the api's sentence; 403 shows the 403's reason; loading is not an error); apps/web/src/routes/Dashboard.test.tsx (error on the list doesn't become "no project yet"); apps/web/src/routes/Shell.test.tsx (the sidebar says so instead of staying empty) Origin: real navigation on /projects/:id with 1128 429 errors in the console
documents.s: RN-088 — Load failure is said on screen; 429 is not retried

documents.t: Project name is not unique — nothing in the domain prevents it. When two or more projects in the list have the same name, each of them shows in the sidebar the abbreviated id and the creation date (#a1b2c3d4 · 07/08 14:32), both already present in the project payload. Projects with a unique name show nothing: the caption on every row would be noise in the place with the least space on screen. Concrete origin: a validation run created twenty projects called validacao-real, and the twenty sidebar rows were visually identical. Where: apps/web/src/lib/project-label.ts (nomesRepetidos, desempateDoProjeto), apps/web/src/routes/Shell.tsx Test: apps/web/src/routes/Shell.test.tsx (repeated name gets a tiebreaker, unique name doesn't) Origin: real navigation with the sidebar full of validation projects
documents.s: RN-089 — A repeated project name is disambiguated in the sidebar

documents.t: The card grid and the sidebar dots are fed by one request per cycle — GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/projects-summary —, and the number of requests doesn't grow with the number of projects. The card shows git provider, provisioning status, budget, agent chips, and last activity; the sidebar shows the status dot and the unread counter. All of that came from seven POLLED queries per project, which made 23 projects cost 3,824 requests per minute against a limit of 300 (RateLimitGuard) — the screen knocked itself down with 429 before finishing loading. RN-088 made the app stop insisting when that happens; this one reduces the request. Two boundaries the rule fixes, which are not implementation detail: The api answers facts, not a roster. roster brings what happened in the event log (execution activated, modules, gate already opened, delegated subagents, infra accepted). Who is area lead, which icon each agent has, and how members become a chip remain the web's — and the PRESENCE rule is a single one (rosterFromFacts), shared with the team panel, so that a new agent doesn't appear in one place and go missing in the other. The bell drawer only fetches when open. It was, until RN-091, the only read that was still one request per project — the "where I stopped reading" cutoff is a seq kept in the browser (read-state), which the server doesn't know. Today the browser sends that cutoff, and the drawer is also a single request. Accepted and desired side effect: gatesEverOpened and delegatedSubagents now cover the ENTIRE session. The client derived from the last 200 events and lost chips in long sessions (see ADR 0021) — the text of deriveAgentRoster always said "has opened at some point". Where: apps/api/src/application/ports/projects-summary-repository.port.ts, apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/workspaces.controller.ts (getProjectsSummary), apps/web/src/lib/hooks.ts (useProjectsSummary), apps/web/src/lib/agent-status.ts (rosterFromFacts), apps/web/src/routes/Dashboard.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/Shell.tsx Test: apps/web/src/routes/Dashboard.fanout.test.tsx (30 projects cost the same as 3; no per-project endpoint is called); apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.spec.ts (the number of database queries doesn't grow with N); apps/web/src/lib/agent-status.test.ts (the api's facts produce the same chips as the event log) Origin: dashboard of 23 projects measured in the browser — 3,824 req/min before, 12 after
documents.s: RN-090 — The dashboard reads the workspace, not one project at a time

documents.t: With the notifications drawer open, its content comes from one request per cycle — POST /workspaces/:workspaceId/unread-events — and the number of requests doesn't grow with the number of projects. It's the missing half of RN-090. That one brought the dashboard down from 3,824 to 12 req/min, but the bell kept fetching one project at a time: 23 projects with the drawer open measured 286 req/min against the limit of 300 (RateLimitGuard). It passed, and vanished with one more project. The obstacle, and why this is the way out. There's no "mark as read" on the server, on purpose: the cutoff is a per-project seq kept in each browser's localStorage (read-state). There were two ways out, and the difference between them is PRODUCT: stop repolling while the drawer is open changes how current what the user sees is — refused, nobody asked for that trade; the browser sending the project → afterSeq map returns exactly the same data at the same cadence. It's pure batching: nothing changes for whoever looks at the screen, neither freshness nor content. It's a POST that mutates nothing, and the api answers 200 (never 201) to say so. The verb was chosen for being the only one with a BODY: there are dozens of pairs, and in a query string that becomes a long URL — which proxies truncate — besides putting the user's project id in access logs, against the rule of not passing personal data through query strings. Three semantic guarantees the route fixes, because batching reads with different cutoffs is where the easy mistake lives: an empty map returns empty, without touching the database. "I asked nothing" is not "give me everything"; each project respects ITS cutoff — seq strictly greater than its own; the 50-event ceiling is per project, the same one GET .../events applies without limit. A limit on the whole response would let the noisy project eat the quiet ones' quota. A cursor pointing to a project of another workspace is ignored, not refused: it comes from the caller's local storage and may be a leftover from an old workspace. Where: apps/api/src/application/ports/projects-summary-repository.port.ts (unreadEventsForWorkspace), apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/workspaces.controller.ts (getUnreadEvents), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/dto/unread-events.dto.ts, apps/web/src/lib/notifications.ts (useNotificationGroups), apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts (getUnreadEvents) Test: apps/web/src/routes/Dashboard.fanout.test.tsx (with the drawer OPEN: one request, and 30 projects cost the same as 3); apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.spec.ts (the number of database queries doesn't grow with N; empty map, per-project cutoff, per-project ceiling, and workspace isolation) Origin: measured residual of RN-090 — 286 req/min with the drawer open on a 23-project workspace
documents.s: RN-091 — The browser sends where it stopped reading; the bell is one request

documents.t: The Overview's Activity column shows a window of 100 events anchored at the session's tail, and goes down into the past page by page. Each page uses the afterSeq/nextCursor that GET /projects/:p/sessions/:s/events already returns: no new route, no new parameter. Two questions, two queries. useSessionEvents answers "how is it now" — the last 200 under polling — and feeds the team panel, the tree timeline, the execution section, and the Approvals tab. None of them paginates. Activity's answers "what happened", and it was the only one asking that question with the other one's answer: 200 items at once, with no beginning or end, and still not reaching the start of a long session. The anchor is the tail, not the start of the session. The endpoint paginates FORWARD, and there's no beforeSeq — inventing one would be a new contract. But opening the feed at event #1 of a session with thousands delivers the wrong screen: whoever opens Activity wants what just happened. So the first page is the same latest read the screen already does, with the same queryKey (React Query serves both with ONE fetch), and each click goes down a fixed window with afterSeq. What pagination can't cost. One request per poll cycle — the same as before, and the savings of RN-090/RN-091 don't regress. Three pieces guarantee that: the tail is the query the screen already had, shared by queryKey; the first click does not become a request: the latest read brings 200 and the window shows 100, so revealing what was already paid for comes before asking again; an old page is a closed seq window over immutable events (there's never an UPDATE on an event table): staleTime: Infinity and no refetchInterval. A poll there would be paying N requests to receive N identical responses. The count is honest about what it knows. The filters by agent and by type run over the loaded page, not over the session — so the UI says N of M loaded, not "N results". Taking the filter to the server would give the true total and touch the event repository; it's not for this phase, and saying the wrong total would be worse than saying less. The three states of RN-088 apply here: error before empty — the column said "no activity" when the api had refused. Where: apps/web/src/lib/hooks.ts (useSessionEventHistory, EVENTOS_POR_PAGINA), apps/web/src/components/ActivityFeed.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectOverviewTab.tsx, apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/session-event.repository.ts (listPaginated, already existing) Test: apps/web/src/lib/session-history.test.tsx (opens at the tail; the first click costs no request; the next paginates with contiguous afterSeq; the loop ends at the start of the session; mounted together with the current state, the tail is ONE fetch; an old page doesn't repoll); apps/web/src/components/ActivityFeed.test.tsx (the "N of M loaded" follows the filter; without the pagination props nothing changes) Origin: user request on the first real navigation — "Activity in the Overview tab must be paginated, so it isn't infinite"
documents.s: RN-099 — Activity paginates the past without repolling what doesn't change

documents.t: The notifications drawer shows events from most recent to oldest, and when a project has more unread than the 50 ceiling the ones that appear are the NEWEST. The ordering is the database's out of necessity, not taste. The query cuts at 50 per project with a window function (row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY session_id ORDER BY seq DESC)), and it's what decides which 50 events survive — not just in what order they come out. With ASC, the 50 oldest survived, and a .sort() on the client would sort by recency precisely the window the query had already chosen wrongly: in a project with 300 unread, the 251st event would appear as "the most recent". That's why there's no sorting at all in the front-end path, and the comment in the component says there can't be. The consequence, and why the read cutoff didn't change. The cutoff is a per-project seq in localStorage, and there's no mark-as-read endpoint, by decision recorded in RN-091. A seq cutoff marks a prefix; the drawer now shows a suffix. Marking as read "the 50 displayed" is inexpressible without a set of reads per event — a new table, out of scope. The only two expressible cutoffs remain "nothing" and "everything up to now". The way out wasn't changing the semantics (it keeps advancing to the last seq, exactly as before), it was to stop hiding what that advance swallows: each project shows the total unread, not the window size, and declares how many were left out (+ N older); the button now says what it does — mark the N as read — when there's something outside the window; the missing number comes from subtraction, not a request: latestSeq minus the cutoff already comes in the workspace summary (RN-090). Since the cutoff's semantics didn't change, there's no ADR for this rule: what changed was which window the query chooses and what the drawer declares about it. Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.ts (unreadEventsForWorkspace), apps/api/src/application/ports/projects-summary-repository.port.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/dto/iam.response.dto.ts (ProjectUnreadEventsResponseDto), apps/web/src/lib/notifications.ts (useNotificationGroups), apps/web/src/components/NotificationBell.tsx Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.spec.ts ("with more unread than the ceiling, the MOST RECENT come back, from new to old" — asserts the SET before the order); apps/web/src/components/NotificationBell.test.tsx (renders in the order received, without reordering; the counter is the total; the button says how many it marks); apps/web/src/lib/notifications.test.tsx (what was left out of the window comes out by subtraction, without a second request); apps/web/src/routes/Dashboard.fanout.test.tsx (the drawer is still ONE request) Origin: user request on the first real navigation — "Bell and notifications must always sort by last modified date descending to the oldest"
documents.s: RN-100 — The bell's order is SQL's, not the front end's

documents.t: AgentTimelineTree/timeline-tree.ts (PHASE 14b) already grouped the event log by agent, but with three gaps: the criterion for opening a branch was only active/stopped (unrelated to how many agents existed), the header counter was the TOTAL of milestones (never "what's new"), and tool.call/ tool.result/agent.response became a milestone showing only the tool name — args, result, and iteration, which the event log already records, never reached the screen. Default opening becomes "the 5 agents with the most recent activity (highest seq of the last milestone)", with active keeping priority over recency — they don't add up: since montarArvore already sorts actives first and, within each group, from most recent to oldest, the two criteria collapse into a single slice (ramosAbertosPorPadrao, the first max(number of actives, 5) branches). More than 5 actives: all open, with no cutoff. The novelty counter per agent uses the SAME mechanism as the bell (read-state.ts, localStorage), granular by projectId:agentId instead of only projectId — there was no "last seen" at that granularity before. A collapsed branch with a milestone seq greater than that agent's last seen shows the NOVELTY count in place of the total; opening the branch (automatically or manually) marks as seen up to the most recent seq. Expandable detail is per MILESTONE, not per branch — only tool.call, tool.result, and agent.response (EVENTOS_EXPANSIVEIS) become an individual button, because only they carry a payload worth expanding. The visual grouping by ITERATION uses iteration from the agent.response payload when it exists (ToolLoop — tool.call/tool.result inherit the iteration of the response that dispatched them, because in the ToolLoop they are emitted AFTER it); agents outside the ToolLoop (PO, Criativo, with no iteration in the payload) get their OWN counter per agent, incremented on each response — inference by seq proximity, not a new field in the event log. Where: apps/web/src/lib/timeline-tree.ts (Marco.iteracao, Marco.eventType, Marco.payload, ramosAbertosPorPadrao, marcoExpansivel), apps/web/src/components/AgentTimelineTree.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/read-state.ts (getAgentLastSeenSeq/ setAgentLastSeenSeq) Test: apps/web/src/lib/timeline-tree.test.ts (grouping by real and inferred iteration, ramosAbertosPorPadrao with active/recency/no cutoff), apps/web/src/components/AgentTimelineTree.test.tsx (default opening, novelty counter appearing/disappearing, milestone expanding with args/result/iteration) Origin: user request — gaps confirmed by investigation of the existing PHASE 14b component; no ADR, same "unseen" semantics as the bell, only a new granularity
documents.s: RN-118 — The team tree exposes execution detail per milestone, and opens the "last 5"

documents.t: Every proposed_action type has a sentence in Portuguese describing the effect of approving, and it is the first visible thing on the card — before any detail, on the three screens where a decision is asked for (the Approvals queue, the card inside the session chat, and the Insights tab). The raw payload remains accessible, inside a collapse that is born closed, and is never dumped on the screen. What existed was a dump. Every type without its own visual body fell into an Object.entries(payload).map(([k, v]) => k + ': ' + JSON.stringify(v)), always open. Whoever opened the queue read worktree: /workspaces/dev-api, coAuthor: Brabo User <user@brabo.dev>, and proposto: 4 — and had to deduce what would happen if they clicked Approve. Approval that requires deduction is approval given on autopilot, and the whole product rests on the user being the final authority. The sentence degrades, and that's what makes it reliable. None of them assumes that a payload key exists: with an empty payload the sentence is still a true sentence, just less specific ("Records a commit in the project's repository."). The payload comes from the engine and from ten different use cases, and none of them promises a format — a sentence that only works with the right fixture is a sentence that breaks on the first real approval. A type the web doesn't know yet is not a theoretical case. The web's ActionType union has already fallen behind twice: first with the three Gitflow bootstrap types, and again with parallelize/raise_max_parallel, which came in during PHASE 14d. The compiler doesn't catch it: the canonical list is in apps/api, which the web doesn't import. Hence two things at once — the card degrades (neutral verb "see details", with the payload collapsed, instead of the undefined in the icon map that took down the whole React tree), and the test reads the backend's decide.ts and fails when a type comes in without a sentence. The open/closed default is derived, not configured. The rule is a single one — it opens what is still waiting for a decision from whoever is looking: in the chat, a pending action; in the queue, never (there are N cards, and N open details are the same wall of text); in Insights, a proposed hypothesis. And the RAW payload doesn't open in any variant. The project consequence is that ApprovalCard gained no new mandatory prop: the default comes from variant and status, which already existed. Verb and sentence come from a single module, consumed by the three screens. The Psicólogo's hypothesis literally uses the instruction_patch verb instead of a parallel vocabulary — and its sentence says what accept really does (queues it for the Anamnese, which may propose the adjustment, which still comes for approval), never "the instruction will be changed". write_file had a sentence, but no body. It was born outside COM_CORPO_PROPRIO: the sentence showed only the path, and the detail fell into the same collapsed raw-JSON dump this RN exists to avoid — so a write that genuinely asked for approval (outside the dev- prefix, or a path outside the agent's scope) required one more click to see the content. It entered COM_CORPO_PROPRIO with its own body: path and a preview of the content (up to 25 lines/4,000 characters, with a truncation notice — never the entire file, same rule as the raw payload), open by default in the chat while pending, like terminal. An empty payload is not an absent payload. command (terminal) or path/content (write_file) arriving as an empty string — a malformed tool call from the model, not a rendering bug — degraded into a $ prompt or a blank preview, which the user read as a screen defect. The two bodies now distinguish the two cases and show "the model did not produce a valid X for this action" instead of a blank. Where: apps/web/src/lib/aprovacoes.ts (VERBO_DA_ACAO, fraseDaAcao, descreverAcao, descreverHipotese), consumed by apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.tsx (Approvals + session chat, COM_CORPO_PROPRIO, previewConteudo for the write_file content) and apps/web/src/components/HypothesisCard.tsx (Insights); collapse via the Disclosure of apps/web/src/components/ui/Disclosure.tsx Test: apps/web/src/lib/aprovacoes.test.ts (reads ACTION_TYPES from apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts and requires verb + sentence for each type, with an empty payload); apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.test.tsx (frase e colapso — payload collapsed in both variants, readable JSON on opening, an unknown type doesn't take the screen down, write_file with its own body open by default and preview truncation, empty command/path/content showing the fallback message); apps/web/src/components/HypothesisCard.test.tsx (frase e colapso) Origin: PHASE 19 of program 16–26, from the request "today reading is very hard" on the first real navigation after the database reset
documents.s: RN-096 — Every decision says in plain language what happens; the raw payload is born collapsed

documents.t: The Overview's "Agent team" grid and "Team timeline" mixed Criativo/PO/Arquiteto/Infra with dev-<module> and QA (lead + qa-automacao/qa-performance-seguranca) — seven, eight agents in the same grid, without distinguishing who CREATES/DECIDES from who IMPLEMENTS/VERIFIES. The Executors tab isolates the last two, with the SAME rendering as the Overview (AgentCard, the area grid — extracted to AgentTeamGrid.tsx — and AgentTimelineTree), never a reinvented card. The separation rule is a single function, isExecutorGroup/ isExecutorAgentId (lib/agent-status.ts): dev-lead/dev-<any module> and the entire qa area (lead + sub-specialties) are executors; the rest isn't. BOTH screens filter the SAME groupRosterByArea with that function — the Overview with !isExecutorGroup, Executors with isExecutorGroup — so an agent can't appear in both nor vanish from both: it's always exactly one side. The tree doesn't duplicate: each tab filters the EVENTS before passing them to AgentTimelineTree (by whether actor.id belongs to the set of executors), so a dev agent's branch appears only in Executors, never also in the Overview. The Activity column (ActivityFeed, RN-099/100) was NOT filtered — it answers "what happened" in the whole session, dev/QA included, and the component's own per-agent filter already lists everyone who spoke; only the grid and the "who is doing what" tree change place. Where: apps/web/src/lib/agent-status.ts (isExecutorGroup, isExecutorAgentId, autonomyActionTypeFor — moved from ProjectOverviewTab.tsx), apps/web/src/components/AgentTeamGrid.tsx (extracted from the grid that already existed), apps/web/src/routes/ ProjectExecutorsTab.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectOverviewTab.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/project-tabs.ts (key: 'executores', ordem: 12 — right after the Overview, before Criativo/Chat/Code) Test: apps/web/src/lib/agent-status.test.ts (isExecutorAgentId/ isExecutorGroup — dev-<module>, dev-lead, the entire qa area are executors; criativo/po/arquiteto/infra/secops are not); apps/web/src/routes/ProjectExecutorsTab.test.tsx (shows only dev/QA, empty state without both, header count); apps/web/src/routes/ProjectOverviewTab.test.tsx (dev-backend/QA disappear from the grid, the rest of the team remains); apps/web/src/routes/ project-tabs.test.tsx (the new tab enters the registry's generic sweep — ruler, panel, deep-link, unique order) Edge case: SecOps is NOT an executor — it enters the roster through the SAME pr.gate_changed that brings QA (Phase 4a, rosterFactsFromEvents), but stays in the Overview. dev-lead is in the executor list for completeness (RN-087 describes it as conversational), although today no path instantiates it in the session roster (the Dev Lead → dev-<module> delegation remains out of scope, ADR 0053 item 5). Origin: user request — its own "Executors" for dev agent and QA, outside the Overview's mixed grid.
documents.s: RN-121 — Dev agent and QA are "executors": their own tab, outside the "Agent team"

documents.t: The "X passed the baton to Y" divider that already existed in the timeline (handoff.offered) becomes an actionable card — with the accept button embedded — whenever it represents the current pending offer (the same one offeredHandoff already resolved for the topbar button). The topbar button was removed: with acceptance living inside the thread, at the exact place where the handover happened, keeping both would pull two buttons with IDENTICAL text visible at the same time — the same problem ApprovalCard already avoids by never duplicating the action outside the thread (RN-096). Which event becomes the card is decided by PAIR, not by id. The handoff.offered payload carries only toAgent; the fromAgent is the event's actor (RN-054 already used that reading for the divider text). Without the handoff id in the event, "this is the current offer" is answered by finding the most RECENT handoff.offered (highest seq) with the SAME fromAgent/toAgent pair as offeredHandoff — which prevents reopening an accept invite that an older offer for the same pair has already resolved (accepted, declined, or superseded by a new offer). The card for the Dev Lead gets a second link, "Follow the execution in Executors", to the tab that already exists (RN-121) — it's the start of EXECUTION, and whoever accepts needs to know where to look afterwards. The other offers (PO, Arquiteto…) don't get the link: their session remains the place to follow along itself, there's no "elsewhere to look". Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (timeline — the handoff.offered block, offeredHandoffEventSeq; isActive moved to before the useMemo), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.module.css (.handoffCard, .timelineLink) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.handoff-inline-e-links.test.tsx (actionable card only on the current offer, an old offer of the same pair stays silent, an already-accepted handoff shows no button, Executors link only on dev-lead); apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.pista-e-status.test.tsx updated for the inline button (no longer in the topbar) Verified by real execution: accepting a handoff to the PO in a creative session against an isolated build (its own Docker stack, real project/session) — the card becomes a silent divider and the event log advances as soon as the click returns from the api; the CTA for the Dev Lead navigates to ?tab=executores for real. Origin: user request — handoff acceptance also inline in the thread, not only in the topbar.
documents.s: RN-125 — Handoff acceptance is INLINE in the thread, with a CTA for the Dev Lead pointing to Executors

documents.t: backlog.epic_created/backlog.story_created — which the PO already recorded in the event log (CreateEpicUseCase/CreateStoryUseCase) — had no handling at all in the session timeline: creating a story left NO trace in the thread, only in the Backlog tab, for those who already knew to go look there. The two types get an entry in the timeline, in the SAME visual body as the agent's other messages (.message/.bubble) — no new class for the chip itself, only the link. The link ("See in Backlog") reuses the tab's generic deep-link (?tab=backlog, the same mechanism as the dashboard card's "Set budget" CTA) — it doesn't try to highlight the newly created story inside the tab, which is out of scope. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (timeline — the backlog.epic_created/backlog.story_created block) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.handoff-inline-e-links.test.tsx (item 2) Verified by real execution: epic and story inserted into the event log of a real session appear as "Epic created"/"Story created" with the title, and the link navigates to ?tab=backlog for real. Origin: user request — link from the PO to the created stories, straight to the Backlog.
documents.s: RN-124 — The PO narrates epic/story created in the thread, with a direct link to the Backlog

documents.t: backlog.story_promotion_proposed (RN-048) gets the same treatment that RN-125 gave to the handoff: the event becomes an actionable card in the session timeline, with the "Promote" and "Return" buttons calling the SAME promoteStories/returnStory that PromotionQueue (ProjectBacklogTab.tsx) already uses — no new endpoint, no second source of truth. The decision still happens in ONE place (the backend), only the trigger gained a second path. Resolution by later event, not by separately derived status. The card disappears on its own (becomes a silent divider, without buttons) as soon as an event with a GREATER seq decides the fate of the SAME story — backlog.story_transitioned{storyId} (promoted, emitted by PromoteStoriesUseCase via TransitionStoryUseCase) or backlog.story_promotion_returned{storyId} (returned). Without that check, promoting or returning would leave the same two buttons planted in the thread, offering again a decision already made. backlog.story_promotion_returned gets symmetric narration in the thread (reason included), reusing the same sentence that apps/web/src/lib/activity.ts already used only in the sidebar's collapsed log. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (timeline — the backlog.story_promotion_proposed/backlog.story_promotion_returned blocks, handlePromoteStory/handleReturnStory, reason modal reusing Modal/Textarea) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.promocao-inline-e-volta.test.tsx (card with the buttons, promoting calls promoteStories with the payload's storyId, returning requires a reason and calls returnStory, a story resolved by a later story_transitioned becomes a silent divider, story_promotion_returned narrates with the reason) Origin: user request — inline story promotion in the thread, a cheap option reusing RN-048 instead of gating story creation.
documents.s: RN-126 — Story promotion is decidable INLINE in the thread, with the same mechanism as the Backlog tab

documents.t: Three defects found by actually navigating SessionPage.tsx in Chrome, not by test — and all three were race conditions or an incomplete criterion disguised as a product decision. 1. conversaComecou became "ANY event exists", not "a chat.message/agent.response exists". The previous criterion (finding G) was born so as not to confuse the git bootstrap cards with conversation, but had the opposite effect: a session created by git-bootstrap (commit/branch actions already approved, zero chat.message) showed the invite on top of them, and the same happened — much more seriously — in the session that execution activation uses, with dozens of real events (tool.call, tool.result, task events) and no chat.message/agent.response: the invite covered the entire execution history. A new session is the only one with no event at all — that's the right question. 2. conviteVisivel waits for useSessionEvents to finish loading. With a cold cache (page reload), session could arrive while events was still [] — the default of data?.items, indistinguishable from "truly empty session" until the first fetch resolved. Without the !eventsQuery.isPending gate, the invite flickered over sessions with a large history. 3. The "thinking" indicator (bubble with the 3 dots) only turns on after 5s with no text arriving. Before, it turned on the instant streaming/statusAgent became truthy — visual noise on most turns, which answer in under a second. A useEffect arms a setTimeout(…, 5000) when the turn starts with no text yet, and disarms it (via cleanup) as soon as the first delta arrives or the turn ends before the deadline. Real text (streamingText) still appears immediately, never waits for the timer — only the empty indicator gained patience. 4. handleReadiness got the same safety net that handleSend already had. confirmReadiness is, like sendAgentMessage, a synchronous GenServer.call in the engine (up to 120s) — and the Phoenix channel may not have finished connecting (ticket + join, RN-108) when the turn ends, losing the agent.done broadcast forever. handleSend already called finalizarTurnoDoAgente() as soon as the synchronous call resolved, regardless of whether the channel had delivered the event; handleReadiness had been left out of that fix, and without it the agent's bubble stayed stuck empty (streaming: true, no text) until the page reloaded. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (conversaComecou, conviteVisivel, the pensandoVisivel useEffect right below agenteExibido, and the success block of handleReadiness) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.convite-so-em-sessao-vazia.test.tsx (an empty session shows the invite; a session with git-bootstrap events or with dozens of tool.call/tool.result hides it; eventsQuery.isPending holds the invite until the first fetch resolves), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.pista-e-status.test.tsx (finding B — the indicator doesn't appear before 5s, appears after, disappears on the first delta, and never appears when the turn ends before the deadline), and apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.readiness-turno-preso.test.tsx (confirmReadiness resolving without onAgentDone reconciles the state the same way SessionPage.turno-preso.test.tsx already proves for handleSend) Origin: LIVE investigation of the product in Chrome — all three reproduced manually before the fix.
documents.s: RN-131 — Three races confirmed LIVE in the session thread: invite over the history, anxious indicator, and a turn stuck in handleReadiness

documents.t: Since ADR 0185 (RN-658) the Criativo→PO handoff that "I'm ready" requested is born and accepted in the same call, on behalf of whoever clicked — its accept card only appears when that acceptance doesn't fit (a session predating the ADR, a brief that didn't come from the click) or failed. The filter below doesn't change. OfferInfraHandoffUseCase offers the handoff to Infra and, in the SAME confirmation, offers it to the Dev Lead right after (PHASE 14d) — two separate calls, the Infra one first. handoffs (what SessionPage.tsx reads from useHandoffs) comes sorted by createdAt ASC (DrizzleHandoffRepository#findBySession), and the offeredHandoff that decides which card becomes "actionable" resolved with a plain .find() — always the oldest offered. Since the Infra Lead isn't conversational (it isn't in AGENTES_DE_CHAT, and is never accepted by this screen), the Dev Lead's card would only become actionable after someone accepted the Infra one in a place this screen doesn't show — in practice, never: the user only saw "accept handoff from Infra" and the invite for the Dev Lead stayed invisible behind it. The filter restricts offeredHandoff to handoffs addressed to an agent of AGENTES_DE_CHAT. The handoff to Infra is still narrated in the thread — its handoff.offered becomes a silent divider, like any offer that isn't "the current one" — only the card with a button now ignores it: Infra never had (nor needs to have) a way to be accepted from here. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (offeredHandoff) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.handoff-devlead-e-colapso.test.tsx, describe "problema 1" — older Infra + newer Dev Lead resolves to the Dev Lead's card, never to Infra's; only Infra offered shows no card at all Origin: code investigation + live test in Chrome — the handoff to the Dev Lead never became actionable after PHASE 14d
documents.s: RN-136 — The actionable handoff card in the chat only considers those who CONVERSE on this screen

documents.t: The accept card of the handoff to the Dev Lead gained an "Activate execution" button next to the "Follow the execution in Executors" link — a shortcut for those who already know what they want, without going through the conversation. It calls the SAME activateExecution that the Overview uses, now with sessionId (the open chat session) as originSessionId — without this the session that brought the Dev Lead stayed active forever, even with execution (in a SEPARATE session) having already taken off through this shortcut (RN-135). The route still requires maintainer — DELIBERATELY not aligned with the developer that already suffices to accept the handoff on the same card. Whoever activates becomes the session.createdBy of the execution session, and that's the role that ProposeActionUseCase resolves (ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject) as the EFFECTIVE one of every git_commit/git_push/pr_open the dev agents propose from then on — it's the same reason that already justified the maintainer of the Overview button (ExecutionController#activate). Lowering the requirement here would silently invert that resolution: every PR the execution opened would go from auto_approve to require_approval whenever whoever clicked was developer, without anyone having decided that. Whoever isn't maintainer receives the api's real sentence ("Papel insuficiente para esta ação", via mensagemDaApi) instead of a generic error. No client-side module_map gate: when this card exists, the Arquiteto has already defined it — it's the artifact that precedes the handoff offer to the Dev Lead —, so replicating the Overview's disabled={!hasModuleMap} would lock the button for nothing. The rare case (inconsistent session) falls into the same catch that handles 403/other errors. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (handleActivateExecution), apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts (activateExecution gained originSessionId) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.handoff-devlead-e-colapso.test.tsx, describe "problema 2" — the click calls activateExecution with sessionId; 403 shows the api's real sentence; the button coexists with the accept-handoff one and with the Executors link Origin: code investigation + live test in Chrome — shortcut request, with the role divergence confirmed and kept by decision (not fixed by automatic alignment)
documents.s: RN-137 — "Activate execution" has an inline shortcut on the Dev Lead card, without lowering the role requirement

documents.t: The chat timeline showed everything always expanded, without grouping by author — in a long session with Criativo, PO, and Arquiteto taking turns, the history of those who already left the scene competed for space with whoever is speaking now. Each timeline entry gained an agentId (the actor.id of whoever generated it, when it's an agent — agent.response, agent.error, epic/story created by the PO, approval card); user entries and those that mark a TRANSITION (handoff, story promotion) are left without agentId on purpose, because they're cut points by nature. A CONSECUTIVE sequence of the same agentId becomes a collapsible header (the design system's Disclosure, closed by default — agent name + count, reopens with one click) when both conditions hold: the agent has already passed the baton — there's a handoff from it (fromAgent) with status: 'accepted' (the same truth the event log's handoff.accepted records, without needing to rebuild by joining events); and none of its actions is pending — the check is by actor.id across ALL the session's actions, not only those in the current sequence: an open approval race can't stay hidden behind a click at ANY point of the thread. A sequence of 1 entry never collapses — "So-and-so · 1 message" in place of the message itself gains nothing. Any entry without agentId, or from a different agent, breaks the current sequence exactly as a change of agent does — it only groups what is really consecutive. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (TimelineEntry.agentId, timelineAgrupada), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.module.css (.agentGroup*) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.handoff-devlead-e-colapso.test.tsx, describe "problema 3" — collapses with the baton passed and no pending action; doesn't collapse without an accepted handoff; doesn't collapse with a pending action from the same agent; a message from another author in the middle breaks the grouping Origin: code investigation + live test in Chrome — collapse request, with AgentTimelineTree/timeline-tree.ts as the reference of FORM (group by agent, name + count, open/closed), adapted to the chat's heterogeneous interleaved timeline
documents.s: RN-138 — An agent's messages collapse after it passes the baton

documents.t: The evidenceEventIds must point to events that exist and belong to the analyzed session. Validation is atomic per batch: one invalid id fails the entire batch. Where: apps/api/src/domain/psychologist/hypothesis-evidence.ts Test: test/domain/psychologist/hypothesis-evidence.spec.ts Origin: ADR 0015 §3
documents.s: RN-021 — A hypothesis without valid evidence is not recorded

documents.s: RN-022 — The hypothesis lifecycle is compare-and-swap

documents.t: It comes from the recorded reason, never from the LLM's judgment and never by elimination. Every failure records its origin: infra | modelo | código | política. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/psychologist/termination_classifier.ex Origin: ADR 0022 §5 and ADR 0020 §6
documents.s: RN-023 — The termination cause is a deterministic classification

documents.t: Process competencies are six, closed: git, agile, arquitetura, testes, seguranca, infra. Plus the technical stacks derived from the module_map. Anything else — "anxiety", "mental health" — has no write path: it's a domain error, not a prompt instruction. Where: apps/api/src/domain/anamnese/competency-catalog.ts:16 Test: test/domain/anamnese/competency-catalog.spec.ts Origin: ADR 0016 §1 Why: the Anamnese profiles technical competence, not the person. The limit is structural because a prompt instruction is not a guarantee.
documents.s: RN-024 — The Anamnese only profiles competencies from the catalog — a structural guardrail

documents.t: Where: apps/api/src/domain/anamnese/proficiency-profile.entity.ts + table anamnese_opt_outs Origin: ADR 0016 §2

There's no dedup table — the source is the proposed_action history itself with actionType = instruction_patch and status = denied. Where: apps/api/src/domain/instructions/patch-dedup.ts:22 Test: test/domain/instructions/patch-dedup.spec.ts

documents.s: RN-027 — Instruction rollback is a forward operation

documents.t: An unsupported operation (branch protection on the local provider) is declared in capabilities and rejected with GitNotSupportedError — never a silent failure. There are four capabilities: protectBranch and pullRequests since Phase 2, and listTree and pullRequestDiff since PHASE 26 (Code tab, read-only). The rule didn't change with them — its reach did. And the criterion for declaring is still proof: a capability is only true when the suite exercises it on that provider; without proof, it's declared false and degrades (same criterion as ADRs 0041/0042). Where: packages/shared/src/index.ts (GitProviderCapabilities); the ceilings of the two read operations in apps/api/src/domain/git/git-read-limits.ts, outside shared because it's 100% types Test: single contract suite, test/contract/git-provider.contract.ts, run against the three providers Origin: ADR 0001
documents.s: RN-028 — Capability decides, not the provider's name

documents.t: Five steps; each one checks before acting and can be resumed from the point where it failed. skip is success, not error. There used to be six. The sixth created the rc branch, a rung that ADR 0030 removed from the policy — the bootstrap kept creating, protecting, and documenting in the user's repository a ladder the product had already abandoned (finding #3 of the first dogfooding). The value create_rc_branch remains in the bootstrap_step enum: old rows reference it, and a step that really happened isn't erased from history. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/git/bootstrap-steps.ts + domain/git/repo-bootstrap.entity.ts (RETIRED_BOOTSTRAP_STEPS) Test: test/domain/git/repo-bootstrap-status.spec.ts Origin: ADR 0005
documents.s: RN-029 — The Gitflow bootstrap is idempotent and resumable

documents.t: The user's LLM key and git token live in the same table (user_credentials), under the same envelope encryption. This section applies to both.
documents.s: Credentials

documents.t: Registration doesn't judge the credential: it encrypts and saves, even if the provider would refuse it. Verifying is an explicit action on the already saved credential — the api decrypts, calls the provider, and returns only the verdict. The plain text never comes back in any response, not in pieces, not in the refusal reason. It used to be the opposite: registration tested before persisting and refused to save (ADR 0004, extended to LLM keys in Phase 11a). The real failure mode was the opposite of what was predicted — since the field is write-only and the screen never redisplays what was typed, a refusal left the user with no credential and without the text to fix it. The verdict has three values, and the third is mandatory: when ok the provider accepted recusado the provider rejected — carries its reason nao_suportado there's no verified test endpoint (ollama, anthropic, openai) Without nao_suportado, a provider whose tester is a NO-OP would come back ok and the screen would assert a verification that never happened. It's the capability rule of ADR 0041 applied here: only what was proven is declared. That's why the port declares supports() — the silence of test() alone is ambiguous. A bad key is not an HTTP exception: the use case catches LLMCredentialConnectionTestFailedError/GitCredentialConnectionTestFailedError and returns a result, with 200. The only exception is when there's no credential for (user, provider) — 404, because then there's nothing to test. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/credentials/test-stored-credential.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/llm/upsert-user-credential.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/git/register-git-credential.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/ports/llm-credential-connection-tester.port.ts (supports) Test: test/application/use-cases/credentials/test-stored-credential.use-case.spec.ts (the three results, the git×LLM dispatch, the 404, and the absence of the secret in the response); test/application/use-cases/llm/upsert-user-credential.use-case.spec.ts and test/application/use-cases/git/register-git-credential.use-case.spec.ts (the unconditional save, which is the inversion) Origin: ADR 0050
documents.s: RN-055 — A credential is always encrypted and saved; verifying is a separate action, with three answers

documents.t: The first-party auth RNs live in Business rules — Authentication. They left here because of SIZE, not subject: together with Cost they were half of a 640 KB page. The content didn't change, and the #rn-NNN anchors are the same — what changed was the file that hosts them.
documents.s: Authentication

documents.t: The Wave 3 port (RN-226) only covered basic write/read. Wave 4 added deleteByScope/deleteBySession (for idempotent reindexing by full rebuild — delete and recreate, never UPDATE) and searchByVector/searchByLexicalQuery (the two halves of hybrid search, each an independent query, taking advantage of the index built for it — HNSW or GIN). deleteByScope is typed Exclude<ChunkScope, 'session'>: deleting session for a whole project would delete sessions that aren't being reindexed now, so a session is only deleted by deleteBySession. Where: apps/api/src/application/ports/chunk-repository.port.ts (lines 105-146), apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/chunk.repository.ts Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/chunk.repository.spec.ts — describes "Onda 4 (G2)" (delete by scope/session, search by vector/lexical, happy and empty case of each) ADR: 0080
documents.s: RN-231 — ChunkRepository gains DELETE and both halves of hybrid search

documents.t: docs/adr are indexed via ReadProjectCodeUseCase — the same surface as the Code tab, with the same owner credential, the same container gate (RN-105), and the same path check (RN-095) — never Brabo's documentation as a product. session indexes only two event types (chat.message, agent.response); the rest of the event log (tool.call, agent.status, agent.error...) is mechanism/failure, not citable knowledge. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/rag/index-project-docs.use-case.ts (lines 16-17, 64), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/rag/index-session.use-case.ts (line 29, 45) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/rag/index-project-docs.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/rag/index-session.use-case.spec.ts (happy cases + "project without docs/" + "event without payload.text is ignored") ADR: 0080
documents.s: RN-232 — Source of the indexed text: docs/adr from the project's OWN repository, session only from chat.message/agent.response

documents.t: When ollama/nomic-embed-text doesn't respond, RagEmbeddingService.embedMany doesn't throw — it returns available: false and null per requested entry. The pipeline saves the chunks anyway (embedding: null; search_vector is GENERATED ALWAYS AS and doesn't depend on any provider), and the indexing report declares the gap (embedding: { available, embedded, skipped, reason }). The same degradation applies to search: HybridSearchUseCase runs with only the lexical signal and vectorAvailable: false warns. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/rag/rag-embedding.service.ts (lines 53-58) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/rag/rag-embedding.service.spec.ts — "CASO DE FALHA: provider sem a capability..." and "CASO DE FALHA: provider que lança no meio do lote..."; index-project-docs.use-case.spec.ts/ index-session.use-case.spec.ts — "CASO DE FALHA: provider de embedding indisponível grava os chunks SEM vetor..."; hybrid-search.use-case.spec.ts — "quando o embedding está indisponível, degrada para busca só léxica" ADR: 0080
documents.s: RN-233 — Embedding provider unavailable: saves without a vector and declares the gap, never pretends complete indexing

documents.t: searchByVector/searchByLexicalQuery are SEPARATE queries (never a JOIN), fused in HybridSearchUseCase by weighted sum (RAG_SEARCH_WEIGHT_VECTOR = 0.6, RAG_SEARCH_WEIGHT_LEXICAL = 0.4 — the scales of cosine and normalized ts_rank aren't comparable by nature) and cut at RAG_SEARCH_SCORE_THRESHOLD = 0.2. None of the four numbers comes from calibration with real data — they're a documented starting point. The citation (HybridSearchHit) exposes chunkId/content/separate scores (null, not zero, when the signal didn't find the chunk)/origin as a union discriminated by kind (file with sourcePath/headingPath, session with sessionId/eventId). Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/rag/hybrid-search.use-case.ts (lines 44-113), apps/api/src/domain/rag/rag-search-limits.ts (lines 60-93), apps/api/src/domain/rag/rag-citation.ts (lines 12-71) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/rag/hybrid-search.use-case.spec.ts (fusion/ordering/threshold, out-of-range query, lexical-only degradation, session origin) and apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/chunk.repository.spec.ts (the actual SQL queries, against real pgvector/tsvector) ADR: 0080
documents.s: RN-234 — Hybrid search: two independent queries, weighted fusion (0.6/0.4), threshold 0.2, and the citation contract

documents.t: CHUNK_TARGET_CHARS = 1200 (~300 tokens in Portuguese), CHUNK_OVERLAP_CHARS = 150 (12.5%), with the cut preferring a paragraph break, then a word break, within a 200-character window. Markdown (docs/adr) is split by HEADING before being cut by size, preserving headingPath. Numbers documented as an adjustable starting point, not calibrated against real retrieval-quality data (there isn't, yet, a body of real questions run against this index). Where: apps/api/src/domain/rag/chunking.ts (lines 30-31, 53 onward) Test: apps/api/test/domain/rag/chunking.spec.ts (text that fits/doesn't fit, empty text, real overlap, pathological text with no space, nested headings, markdown without heading) ADR: 0080
documents.s: RN-235 — Chunking: 1200 characters, 150 of overlap, by paragraph/heading

documents.t: There's no watcher on push nor on session close. ReindexProjectUseCase runs docs/adr once and one IndexSessionUseCase per project session, each indexing deleting the scope/session before recreating — running twice in a row doesn't duplicate. Triggered by POST /projects/:projectId/rag/reindex, role:maintainer. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/rag/reindex-project.use-case.ts (line 36) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/rag/reindex-project.use-case.spec.ts (aggregates docs+sessions, embeddingAvailable false when any run fails, nonexistent project) ADR: 0080
documents.s: RN-236 — Reindexing is always MANUAL, an idempotent full rebuild

documents.t: GetRagCoverageUseCase counts real .md files in the project's repository against how many have a chunk, and the project's sessions against how many have a chunk. There's no per-scope indexing timestamp column, and the response includes no "reindexed Xmin ago" — a guessed number would lie (same ruler as ADR 0042 for a model's grade). Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/rag/get-rag-coverage.use-case.ts (line 47) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/rag/get-rag-coverage.use-case.spec.ts ADR: 0080
documents.s: RN-237 — Index coverage is a REAL count, never an invented "N minutes ago"

documents.t: POST .../rag/search and GET .../rag/coverage are role:viewer (pure read); POST .../rag/reindex is role:maintainer, because it triggers N calls to the project's repository and to the embedding provider — the same "changes what the product spends without asking" ruler as the area parallelism ceiling (RN-083). Where: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/rag/rag.controller.ts (lines 50, 57, 81, 98), docs/security-surface.md Test: apps/api/test/interfaces/route-surface.spec.ts (role classification, closed tags, OpenAPI metadata of the three routes) ADR: 0080
documents.s: RN-238 — The three RAG HTTP routes split role by who CHANGES what the product spends

documents.t: CodeEditor.tsx renders only the lines within the visible window (plus OVERSCAN = 20 of margin) as [data-line-row]; the rest becomes two spacers that reserve the height without existing as a node. The decision NOT to use react-window/react-virtual: line height is FIXED (ALTURA_LINHA = 21, monospace), which reduces "which line is visible" to an integer division over scrollTop — the problem those libs really solve is VARIABLE height per item, which isn't the case for the Code tab. Where: apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeEditor.tsx (lines 38-96, 45, 48) Test: apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeEditor.test.tsx — describe "CodeEditor — virtualização", "caminho feliz: arquivo de 5.000 linhas renderiza uma janela pequena de nós, não o arquivo inteiro" (< 150 [data-line-row] nodes) and "rolar para o meio do arquivo troca a janela — linha 1 some, linhas do meio aparecem"
documents.s: RN-239 — Line virtualization: only the visible window becomes a DOM node

documents.t: When containerHeight hasn't been measured yet (1st render, or jsdom without ResizeObserver in tests), the window falls to LINHAS_SEM_MEDICAO = 40 — generous enough not to truncate the small files the tests use, small enough never to become "render everything" on a truly large file. Where: apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeEditor.tsx (line 57) Test: apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeEditor.test.tsx — "falha/borda: sem medição de altura (jsdom sem ResizeObserver, clientHeight 0), degrada para uma janela padrão em vez de não renderizar nada"
documents.s: RN-240 — Without a height measurement, it degrades to a generous default window, never renders everything

documents.t: minimap.ts tokenizes nothing: it summarizes the output highlight.ts already produced (HighlightToken[][] from highlightFile, called only once) — the SAME one virtualization uses to color the visible lines. Tokenizing again just for the minimap would pay the cost of reading the file a second time, and that's why the minimap only comes in after virtualization is in place, never before. Where: apps/web/src/routes/code/minimap.ts (lines 1-18, 39) Test: apps/web/src/routes/code/minimap.test.ts
documents.s: RN-241 — The minimap reuses the SAME tokenization as virtualization — zero second pass over the file

documents.t: The drawing is on <canvas> (desenharMinimapa), not one element per line: a minimap with one node per line would double again the count that virtualization (RN-239) just cut. With no 2D canvas context available (jsdom without the canvas package), the clickable overlay keeps working — only the drawing is skipped, never the interaction. Where: apps/web/src/routes/code/minimap.ts (lines 14-16, 91) Test: apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeEditor.test.tsx — describe "CodeEditor — minimapa", "caminho feliz: clicar no minimapa rola o editor e troca a janela renderizada" and "falha: sem contexto de canvas 2D (jsdom sem o pacote canvas), o overlay continua clicável e nada quebra"
documents.s: RN-242 — The minimap is a CANVAS, a single DOM node, never one <div> per line

documents.t: project_containers (migration 0046) records the mutable STATE of a project's container — distinct from artifact.project_image in the event log (ADR 0065), which is the Arquiteto's immutable DECISION. Neither RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase nor ObterCicloDeVidaDoContainerUseCase calls a Docker daemon: no product service mounts /var/run/docker.sock nor runs privileged today, and granting that is a security decision outside the scope of this rule. A real orchestrator, when it exists, CONSUMES this table after really acting — never the other way around. Where: apps/api/src/domain/containers/container-lifecycle.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/containers/registrar-transicao-de-container.use-case.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/containers/ciclo-de-vida-do-container.use-case.spec.ts ADR: 0081
documents.s: RN-243 — The container lifecycle is a TABLE, and none of its rows calls Docker

documents.t: provisioning → running ⇄ stopped, with failed reachable from provisioning/running/stopped, and removed → provisioning as the ONLY exit from removed — no state is truly terminal, because a project can reprovision with an image revised by the Arquiteto. A transition outside the table throws InvalidContainerTransitionError, which the use case translates to 409 — same format as session-state-machine.ts and pr-gate-state-machine.ts. Where: apps/api/src/domain/containers/container-lifecycle.ts (ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS) Test: apps/api/test/domain/containers/container-lifecycle.spec.ts ADR: 0081
documents.s: RN-244 — The container state machine: only removed exits by reprovisioning

documents.t: There's no row until the first call with to: 'provisioning', and it's only accepted if the Arquiteto has already decided the project's image (RN-105) — the same gate that already protects the Code tab, applied at the source instead of duplicated. The version of artifact.project_image and the resources declared at that instant are FROZEN in the new row (image_version, cpus, memory_mb, pids_limit): a later revision of the artifact doesn't retroactively change what an already provisioned instance promises. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/containers/registrar-transicao-de-container.use-case.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/containers/ciclo-de-vida-do-container.use-case.spec.ts — "a primeira transição (provisioning) cria a linha…" and "sem decisão de imagem do Arquiteto, não há o que provisionar" ADR: 0081
documents.s: RN-245 — The first transition requires the image already decided, and FREEZES version and resources

documents.t: A project with workspace_mode: 'local' (ADR 0072, RN-169) runs in the usual AGENT container — it doesn't bring up its own container. Requesting any transition for a local project is refused with 400 BEFORE touching the table, at the source, not filtered later in the UI. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/containers/registrar-transicao-de-container.use-case.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/containers/ciclo-de-vida-do-container.use-case.spec.ts — "projeto em modo local não tem ciclo de vida de container (ADR 0072)" ADR: 0081
documents.s: RN-246 — A project in local mode has no container lifecycle

documents.t: There's only ONE current container per project at a time — the same design as dev_agent_states in the engine (ADR 0045). The unique constraint lives in the DATABASE (project_containers_project_id_unique), not only in the use case: create called twice for the same project fails on write, never producing a silent second row. Where: apps/api/src/db/migrations/0046_chilly_forgotten_one.sql Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/container.repository.spec.ts — "só uma linha por projeto — create duplicado viola a constraint única" ADR: 0081
documents.s: RN-247 — One row per project: project_id is unique

documents.t: cpus/memory_mb/pids_limit record what the Arquiteto's artifact promised at provisioning time, but no process today makes the kernel respect that ceiling — there's no orchestrator calling docker run --cpus … --memory … --pids-limit …. The field is born anyway because postponing the column until the orchestrator exists would force a corrective migration on the day it arrived; declaring without enforcing is honest as long as the table doesn't lie about ENFORCING (no screen or API response today asserts "the container is limited to X" — only "the recorded intent was X"). Where: apps/api/src/db/schema/containers.ts (projectContainers) Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/container.repository.spec.ts — "create nasce em provisioning, com a versão e os recursos passados" ADR: 0081
documents.s: RN-248 — Resource ceiling DECLARED, not enforced — the field exists for when there is an orchestrator

documents.t: The milestone WITH detail in AgentTimelineTree had min-height: 20px on the clickable header — below WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8 (Target Size, minimum 24px), which a previous comment already promised without delivering. The migration to the shared Disclosure fixes that for free: the generic component is already born at 24px, and there's no need to remember to set the ruler in each new consumer. Where: apps/web/src/components/AgentTimelineTree.module.css (lines 135-155, .marcoLinha) Test: apps/web/src/components/AgentTimelineTree.test.tsx ADR: none — a one-off a11y fix, same pattern as ADR 0036
documents.s: RN-249 — The click target of a milestone with detail goes from 20px up to Disclosure's 24px floor

documents.t: The diff file strip in ApprovalCard rotates the chevron via transform: rotate(90deg) with its own transition (.chevron.open/ApprovalCard.module.css); the generic Disclosure SWAPS the icon (right arrow → down arrow) with no animation at all. Forcing the migration would erase the micro-interaction with no gain — exclusivity (only one file open at a time) already comes from outside (expandedFile), the same thing the controlled Disclosure would do. What was missing, and wasn't a peculiarity — it's the same defect Disclosure exists to close —, was aria-controls pointing to a named region: fixed directly, without changing component. Where: apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.tsx (lines 511-539) Test: apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.test.tsx
documents.s: RN-250 — The diff file strip in ApprovalCard does NOT migrate to Disclosure — its own animation is the reason

documents.t: ModelCatalogSection (the original reference that generated the component in PHASE 16), AgentTimelineTree (branch + milestone), code/CodeExplorer.tsx (tree folder), and code/CodeShell.tsx (bottom panel) now use the shared Disclosure — none of the six ad-hoc implementations that survived PHASE 16 is left out, except the declared exception of RN-250. testId is the only new prop a consumer needed (data- testid on the header, so existing tests keep selecting the right button without rewriting the whole suite). The controlled region exists in the DOM even when closed — only hidden and without the children mounted —, because aria-controls pointing to an id that doesn't resolve is worse than not having the attribute (a screen reader would announce control of something nonexistent); it's that same property that allows collapsing expensive lists (the OpenRouter catalog has 338 models) without mounting what nobody is looking at. Where: apps/web/src/components/ui/Disclosure.tsx (lines 33-71), apps/web/src/components/ModelCatalogSection.tsx, apps/web/src/components/AgentTimelineTree.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeExplorer.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeShell.tsx Test: apps/web/src/components/ui/Disclosure.test.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeExplorer.test.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeShell.test.tsx
documents.s: RN-251 — Five call sites migrate to the shared Disclosure; the component gains testId as its only new hook

documents.t: HybridSearchUseCase already returns vectorAvailable: false when the embedding provider didn't respond (RN-233) and GetRagCoverageUseCase already never includes an indexing timestamp (RN-237) — but an honest contract in the backend doesn't guarantee an honest screen if it decides not to read both fields. ProjectRagTab shows a warning above the results when vectorAvailable is false (with vectorUnavailableReason, when it exists), and RagCoveragePanel only renders a REAL count (filesIndexed/ filesInRepo, sessionsIndexed/sessionsInProject) — no text of the kind "reindexed Xmin ago" is born on this screen, because the response doesn't carry that data and inventing it would lie (same ruler as ADR 0042 for a model's grade). Where: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectRagTab.tsx (lines 27-31, 176-182), apps/web/src/components/rag/RagCoveragePanel.tsx (lines 27-34) Test: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectRagTab.test.tsx — "CASO DE FALHA (degradação honesta): vectorAvailable false avisa..."; apps/web/src/components/rag/RagCoveragePanel.test.tsx — "CASO DE FALHA (degradação honesta): nunca escreve..." ADR: 0082
documents.s: RN-252 — The Chat RAG screen shows the two honest degradations the backend already declares, never hides them

documents.t: RagCitationCard doesn't invent a second navigation path: origin { kind: 'session', sessionId, eventId } calls useNavigate to /projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId with search: { highlightEvent: eventId } — the SAME route and the SAME parameter that the Psicólogo's evidence chips already use (HypothesisCard.tsx, Phase 4b) to scroll the thread to the event and highlight it. Origin { kind: 'file' } shows path and headingPath as text, without a link: the Code tab today has no deep-link by path, and building that navigation is outside the scope of this front. Where: apps/web/src/components/rag/RagCitationCard.tsx (lines 32-38, 49-56) Test: apps/web/src/components/rag/RagCitationCard.test.tsx — "caminho feliz: origem de sessão navega até o evento exato ao clicar" ADR: 0082
documents.s: RN-253 — A citation with session origin navigates to the exact EVENT, reusing the Psicólogo's mechanism

documents.t: POST .../rag/reindex already requires role:maintainer (RN-238) — the api guarantees it. ProjectRagTab mirrors the ruler on the CLIENT with the same pattern that ProjectSettingsTab/ProjectApprovalsTab already use for other maintainer gates (useCurrentWorkspaceWithRole, since there's no PROJECT role on the client today, only the workspace one the listing returns): the "Reindex now" button doesn't even appear for whoever isn't owner/maintainer, instead of appearing disabled — reindexing triggers N calls to the project's repository and to the embedding provider (same "changes what the product spends without asking" ruler as the parallelism ceiling, RN-083), and a visible but always-refused button would only teach people to ignore the 403. Where: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectRagTab.tsx (lines 43-44, 109) Test: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectRagTab.test.tsx — "botão de reindexar só aparece para maintainer/owner..."; "maintainer vê e pode disparar a reindexação" ADR: 0082
documents.s: RN-254 — The reindex button is maintainer/owner on the SCREEN, mirroring the route's ruler

documents.t: ADR 0081 created ObterCicloDeVidaDoContainerUseCase without a route, on purpose ("exposing one would be guessing a contract" before a real consumer existed). Wave 5/F2 is that consumer (RN-268), and the route is born as a faithful mirror of the use case: null when the project has never been provisioned — the result expected today, because no real orchestrator transitions project_containers in production (RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase has no caller at all outside tests) — or the recorded state (status/imageVersion/resources/failureReason/statusChangedAt), NEVER confirmed against a Docker daemon, because there's no Docker client in the product (RN-243). Same permission as the sibling route (GET /projects/:projectId/container): viewer, GET, no @Post — whoever would transition the lifecycle is an orchestrator that doesn't exist yet. Where: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/containers/containers.controller.ts (cicloDeVida), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/containers/dto/containers.response.dto.ts (CicloDeVidaDoContainerResponseDto) Test: apps/api/test/interfaces/http/containers/containers.controller.spec.ts Edge case: id/projectId/containerId of the internal row do NOT leak into the response — the HTTP contract isn't the same shape as the database row. ADR: 0083 (revises 0081)
documents.s: RN-267 — GET /projects/:projectId/container/lifecycle is the first HTTP exposure of the container lifecycle

documents.t: The original plan for this front was the full interactive terminal, but the investigation confirmed that PHASE 25b remains cut: no service mounts /var/run/docker.sock, and even after ADR 0081 (Wave 4) nothing transitions project_containers in production. Implementing a terminal that pretends to execute commands — or that runs in the same container as Brabo's monorepo, the debt ADR 0055 already describes as policy and not isolation — would be inventing capability, the same mistake ADRs 0041/0042 already refuse for LLM provider and catalog model. What the tab GAINS is honest: under the explanatory text that already existed (PHASE 26b), CodeBottomPanel fetches GET .../container/lifecycle (RN-267) only while the Terminal tab is open (enabled: aba === 'terminal' — no background polling, the same traffic discipline as RN-107) and shows the status with a Badge (provisioning/running/stopped/failed/ removed, in pt-BR), how long ago, and the failureReason when the state is failed. A project never provisioned — the common case today — shows the sentence "not provisioned yet", never an invented badge. Where: apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeBottomPanel.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeBottomPanel.module.css, apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts (getContainerLifecycle), apps/web/src/lib/api-types.ts (CicloDeVidaDoContainer) Test: apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeBottomPanel.test.tsx (describe "Terminal — o estado REAL do ciclo de vida do container") Edge case: the interactive terminal itself is NOT born here — it's PHASE 25b, which remains cut and depends on the container's physical wall (the agent's worktree living inside it), not on this read route. ADR: 0083
documents.s: RN-268 — The Terminal tab shows the REAL state of the container, never pretends a terminal that doesn't exist

documents.t: SocialLoginCallbackUseCase resolves the provider's identity in three steps, in this order, and never out of it: (provider, providerUserId) already linked → direct login; no link but the e-mail matches an existing account → decides by RN-274/RN-275; neither of the two → provisions a new account (RN-278). The lookup key of the first step is always providerUserId, never e-mail — it prevents changing the e-mail at the provider from "losing" the link. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.spec.ts — the seven cases of SocialLoginCallbackUseCase ADR: 0084
documents.s: RN-272 — The social login callback decides in ORDER: known identity, then link by e-mail, then new account

documents.t: domain/auth/social-oauth-state.ts signs with GIT_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET — the SAME HMAC key as the state of "connect git to project X" (domain/git/oauth-state.ts) — but the payload carries purpose: 'social_login', checked BEFORE any other field. A state from the git connection flow, even with a valid signature, is refused here: without the discriminator, accepting it would amount to logging in as the userId of whoever started that connection — privilege escalation. Where: apps/api/src/domain/auth/social-oauth-state.ts Test: apps/api/test/domain/auth/social-oauth-state.spec.ts — "RN-273: rejeita um state do fluxo de CONEXÃO de git, mesma chave" ADR: 0084
documents.s: RN-273 — The social login state has its OWN purpose, even though signed with the same key as the git connection flow

documents.t: When the e-mail returned by the provider matches an already registered account, the link only happens if the provider marks that e-mail as verified (emailVerified: true) — GitHub via GET /user/emails, GitLab via confirmed_at. A typed but unverified e-mail is not proof of identity: anyone can register someone else's e-mail at an OAuth provider. Accepting the link without that check would open account takeover — whoever already has alguem@empresa.com on Brabo didn't ask for someone else's GitHub, with that address only TYPED, to inherit the account. The refusal is 403, and no link is saved. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.ts (vincularAContaExistente) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.spec.ts — "RECUSA vincular quando o e-mail bate mas NÃO está verificado pelo provider" ADR: 0084
documents.s: RN-274 — Linking a social identity to an existing account requires an e-mail VERIFIED by the provider

documents.t: RN-274's e-mail verification protects an account that already exists; when there's no matching account, there's nothing to protect, only a new account to be born. Requiring a verified e-mail in that case would make the common path more expensive (most GitHub users have a verified e-mail, but not all, and refusing the login for that would be friction with no corresponding security gain) without reducing any risk — the worst case is a new account with an unproven e-mail, the same risk that password registration already implicitly accepts until the click on the verification link. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.ts (provisionarContaNova) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.spec.ts — "provisiona conta nova mesmo com e-mail NÃO verificado" ADR: 0084
documents.s: RN-275 — Provisioning a NEW account doesn't require a verified e-mail — only linking to an existing one does

documents.t: social_identities has a unique index on (provider, provider_user_id) — the provider's stable NUMERIC id. E-mail and login (username) can change owner or value at the provider without notice; using them as a key would make an e-mail change on GitHub "lose" the link of whoever already had an account, or worse, silently inherit the link of another person who reused that address later. Where: apps/api/src/db/migrations/0047_complete_hannibal_king.sql, apps/api/src/application/ports/social-identity-repository.port.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.spec.ts — "identidade já conhecida: login direto, sem criar segunda linha" ADR: 0084
documents.s: RN-276 — providerUserId, never e-mail or login, is the social identity key

documents.t: buildLoginAuthorizeUrl asks for read:user user:email (GitHub) and read_user (GitLab) — never the repo/api that the git CONNECTION flow asks for. Entering the account shouldn't grant access to any repository; the two flows reuse the SAME OAuth app (RN-281) but ask for different authorizations, decided at authorization time, not in the app's configuration. Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/git/github-oauth-client.ts, apps/api/src/infrastructure/git/gitlab-oauth-client.ts (buildLoginAuthorizeUrl) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.spec.ts — "StartSocialLoginUseCase › caminho feliz" ADR: 0084
documents.s: RN-277 — Social login asks for MINIMAL scope, never the repository connection one

documents.t: Provisioning by social login writes one row in users and NONE in auth_credentials — the same pair the Keycloak migration already left for "account without a password yet" (see RN-032 and migracao-keycloak.spec.ts). LoginUseCase and ResetPasswordUseCase already handle that state; no second "pending password" mechanism was needed for social login. Where: apps/api/src/application/ports/auth-credential-repository.port.ts (criarUsuarioSemCredencial), apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/auth-credential.repository.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.spec.ts — "caminho feliz: provisiona um usuário NOVO, sem senha (RN-278)" ADR: 0084
documents.s: RN-278 — An account provisioned by social login is born WITHOUT a password — the same "pending" state as the Keycloak migration

documents.t: When an account registered by password (and never verified) is linked to a social identity whose e-mail the provider marks as verified, the account gets emailVerifiedAt filled in as a side effect.
