The provider has just proven, through an independent path, exactly what clicking the verification link would prove — it makes no sense for the account to remain blocked from password login (RN-032) after proving possession of the e-mail through another equally strong path. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.ts (vincularAContaExistente) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.spec.ts — "vincula a conta existente (…) e marca o e-mail dela como verificado (RN-274/279)" ADR: 0084
documents.s: RN-279 — Linking by verified e-mail also verifies the existing account's e-mail

documents.t: A social identity linked to an account with auth_credentials.disabled_at filled in is refused with 403, both on direct login (already known identity) and on the attempt to link. Disabling an account can't be bypassed by switching the sign-in method. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.ts (entrarComIdentidadeConhecida, vincularAContaExistente) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.spec.ts — "recusa login de identidade vinculada a conta DESABILITADA" ADR: 0084
documents.s: RN-280 — Social login refuses a DISABLED account, same ruler as password login

documents.t: GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/_SECRET and GITLAB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/_SECRET remain the only registered client id/secret. What changes per flow is the redirect_uri (/auth/oauth/<provider>/callback versus /git/oauth/<provider>/callback) and the scope (RN-277) — both decided at request time. OPERATOR action is still needed (registering the second callback URL in each provider's app), documented in .env.example — it's that requirement, not a new env var, that justifies the branch being born breaking/. Where: .env.example, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/start-social-login.use-case.ts Test: manual (registration in the OAuth app) — there's no way to automatically test a configuration external to the product ADR: 0084
documents.s: RN-281 — Social login reuses the SAME OAuth app as the git connection — no new environment variable

documents.t: GET /auth/oauth/:provider/callback writes the session cookies (definirCookiesDeSessao, the SAME function as password login) and redirects to WEB_ORIGIN/. The web boot (restaurarSessao(), called on every page load) exchanges the freshly written refresh for an access token — no new client-side code besides the buttons and the error route alias. Where: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/auth.controller.ts (oauthCallback) Test: apps/api/test/interfaces/route-surface.spec.ts — covers the public classification and the route's OpenAPI metadata; the complete cookie→boot flow is E2E, outside the scope of unit testing ADR: 0084
documents.s: RN-282 — The social login access token never travels in the URL nor in the callback body

documents.t: Any failure (invalid state, code rejected by the provider, disabled account, unverified e-mail) redirects to WEB_ORIGIN/login?oauth_error=1 — a single generic signal, never the real reason. Same pattern as the git connection callback (WEB_ORIGIN/git-error). Where: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/auth.controller.ts (oauthCallback, catch block) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.spec.ts — covers the failure outcomes the controller maps to the same generic redirect ADR: 0084
documents.s: RN-283 — A social login callback failure doesn't leak the reason in the URL

documents.t: It's not a planned phase: it's the fix for a divergence that the docs/fluxo.yml × code audit found (docs/explanation/auditoria-fluxo-vs-codigo.md, finding A2) — the flow already declared the dev-lead's plano-de-paralelismo output as via: proposed_action, and the code was never adjusted to match.
documents.s: fluxo.yml × code audit — the Dev Lead's plan becomes a real approval (RN-284, ADR 0086)

documents.t: Revised by RN-677 (ADR 0194): propose_execution_plan gained an execution pipeline — approving the plan records the tasks' module (RN-678) and ACTIVATES execution; the action ends executed or failed, and that outcome is what the Dev Lead reads when resuming. Item 1 below ("has no execute-* pipeline") no longer holds for this type. Revised by RN-578 (ADR 0163): EVERY conversational agent's turn stopped holding the GenServer.call — the from is answered on acceptance, and the suspension described here changed only the turn's CLOSING (awaiting_approval instead of agent.done), no longer the moment of the response. A user_message refused during suspension now becomes 409 on the click. The first time a conversational agent (Criativo, PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead — all run a synchronous turn via a GenServer.call of up to 180s, mediated by Engine.Agents.TurnoAssincrono) suspends waiting for a human decision. The pattern already existed for the dev agent (RN-073, ADR 0052) and the QA/Infra gates (ADR 0057), but both are triggered by cast and never waited for a synchronous response — that's exactly the point this mechanism solves, and the parallelism ceiling that made the Dev Lead exist (RN-083) is the reason the first suspended approval is its. The mechanism, in four pieces: Engine.Agents.DevLeadTools.run/2 (apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/dev_lead_tools.ex:81-107) calls EngineApiClient.propose_action/5 instead of append_event/3, and returns {:ok, texto} (status executed/auto_approved/approved — all three count as success, because propose_execution_plan has no execute-* pipeline of its own and manual approval stays at "approved" forever), {:pending, action_id}, or {:error, texto}. Engine.Agents.DevLeadServer.run_turn/2 (apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/dev_lead_server.ex, tool_calls dispatch block) uses Enum.reduce_while to STOP at the first :pending, without processing the following calls nor recursing — and returns the state with the key :aguardando_aprovacao set (%{action_id:, tool_call_id:, tool_name:, remaining:}, the remaining already discounting the suspended iteration against the ceiling). The role: "tool" message does NOT enter state.messages at that moment — writing "pending" there would lie to the model that the command had already answered that (same reasoning as the dev agent, Engine.Harness.Hooks.ActionPipeline). Engine.Agents.TurnoAssincrono.tratar_resultado/2 (apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/turno_assincrono.ex) answers the from the same way and at the same time as always — that's what breaks the synchronous block at the right moment —, but instead of finalizar/1 (which emits agent.done and agent.status: idle) it calls suspender/1: only agent.status: awaiting_approval, no agent.done, because the turn hasn't ended. The check is by the key's VALUE (Map.get/2, truthy), never by its presence — the Dev Lead carries aguardando_aprovacao: nil since init/1, so the key itself is always present. Engine.Sessions.LiveBroadcast.agent_status/4 (apps/engine/lib/engine/sessions/live_broadcast.ex:38-39) widened the guard from ["working", "idle"] to include "awaiting_approval" — without this, the agent.status from step 3 wouldn't even be persisted. The resumption. Engine.Agents.DevLeadServer subscribes Engine.Dev.Wake.subscribe(project_id, "dev-lead") in init/1 — the SAME module that Engine.Gates.QaLeadServer already reuses for the QA subagents, despite the name being "dev": delivery of {:action_settled, ...} is per AGENT, routed by the payload's agentId (apps/engine/lib/engine/workers/dev_agent_wake_worker.ex), not by agent type. When the decision arrives, a handle_info builds the role: "tool" message with the REAL result (texto_do_desfecho/1, same vocabulary as the dev agent and QaLeadServer), clears aguardando_aprovacao, and resumes with TurnoAssincrono.iniciar(state, nil, fn -> run_turn(state, pendente.remaining) end). While suspended, a second user_message doesn't start a new turn — a guard on handle_call({:user_message, _text}, _from, %{aguardando_aprovacao: %{}}), tested BEFORE the generic clause, emits agent.error (origin politica) explaining that there's a pending decision in Approvals, without starting any task. Accepted gap, declared — restart during the wait. Unlike the dev agent (which rehydrates laco_pendente via handle_continue in init/1, ADR 0052), the Dev Lead does NOT rehydrate aguardando_aprovacao — it's in memory only. If the engine restarts while it's suspended, the decision remains recorded and visible in Approvals (it's durable in the api), but the Dev Lead doesn't narrate the outcome automatically: the process that subscribed to Wake died, and the next restart brings up a new Dev Lead, with no subscription for that action. Closing this would require the same mechanism as ADR 0052 — outside the scope of this change, which only makes the behavior match what docs/fluxo.yml already declared. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/dev_lead_tools.ex, dev_lead_server.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/turno_assincrono.ex (shared by the four conversational agents); apps/engine/lib/engine/sessions/live_broadcast.ex; apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts (propose_execution_plan) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/dev_lead_tools_test.exs, dev_lead_server_test.exs (describe "suspensão em aprovação"), turno_assincrono_test.exs (describe "resultado com :aguardando_aprovacao"), live_broadcast_test.exs, wake_do_outbox_ao_dev_lead_test.exs (the ENTIRE chain — outbox → drain → worker → Engine.Dev.Wake → the Dev Lead's process, same pattern as Engine.Dev.WakeDoOutboxAoAgenteTest), apps/api/test/domain/actions/decide.spec.ts (describe "plano de execução do Dev Lead") ADR: 0086 (revises part of ADR 0053; direct precedent: ADR 0052 and ADR 0057)
documents.s: RN-284 — A conversational agent's turn can SUSPEND waiting for human approval

documents.t: It's not a triggered separation trigger (docs/fluxo.yml always declared "when the MANAGED project has its own interface to design" as the criterion) — it's a conscious decision by the product owner to bring the role forward. teste-de- usabilidade (requires a real human user) stays out of reach; metricas-de- uso remains a gap, because it depends on the analytics role, which is still proposto.
documents.s: UX Designer — the fifth conversational agent (RN-285..287, ADR 0087)

documents.t: Engine.Agents.UxDesignerServer (apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/ux_designer_server.ex:40) mirrors Engine.Agents.ArquitetoServer/DevLeadServer: a GenServer per session, its own bounded tool-use loop with a ceiling of 14 (same caliber as Arquiteto/Dev Lead — a reasoning agent, not light conversation like Criativo/PO). Activated by an accepted handoff addressed to "ux-designer" — an already existing GENERIC mechanism (ActivateAgentUseCase/canActivateAgent in the api gained no line at all: any agent with an accepted handoff is already activatable). The kickoff (build_kickoff/1, ux_designer_server.ex:222) reads the session's most recent artifact.product_brief — the SAME "business need" the Criativo produces, with no new artifact. The design system (design/tokens.css, design/COMPONENTS.md) is DESCRIBED in the identity (Engine.Harness.Agents, entry "ux-designer"), static text, because the conversational agents have no tool for reading files from the repo — it's the only prompt layer present in EVERY turn, not only in the kickoff. No area, no subagents: docs/fluxo.yml already classified the role as camada_produto, alongside Criativo and PO, neither of which has an area.
documents.s: RN-285 — The UX Designer is a SOLO conversational agent, with no area

documents.t: artifact.prototipo_navegavel follows the table-less design of artifact.project_image/artifact.c4_diagram (RN-149) — the event log is the record —, but through a DIFFERENT path from the one those two use. choose_project_image/create_c4_diagram need a use case IN THE API (DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase/CreateC4DiagramUseCase) because they have content DERIVED from another artifact (the Container level comes from the current module_map) or a domain refusal shared by more than one consumer (the image's resource ceiling). propose_prototype (Engine.Agents.UxDesignerTools.run/2, apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/ux_designer_tools.ex:122) has neither of the two reasons — it's SELF-CONTAINED content that only the UX Designer itself writes and only it reads back —, so FORM validation lives in the engine (Engine.Harness.ArtifactSchemas, type "prototipo_navegavel", artifact_schemas.ex:49/135 — non-empty personas and journeys, at least one screen) and recording uses the GENERIC path the api already exposes for any event type (EngineApiClient.append_event_returning/3), the same mechanism as the Criativo's artifact.product_brief. No new route in the api. After recording, gravar_e_ofertar_handoffs/2 (ux_designer_tools.ex:149) offers TWO handoffs over the SAME artifact — create_handoff to "po" and to "dev-lead", both with the prototype's artifactId. Never a second artifact for "spec-visual" (docs/fluxo.yml): the PO reads resumo/prototipo to design the backlog, the Dev Lead reads the SAME telas/anotacoes as a visual implementation reference — duplicating the content would risk the two copies diverging on the next revision, the same argument behind the C4 not retyping the module_map. Failing to offer ONE of the two handoffs doesn't undo the already recorded artifact nor the other handoff (RN-116) — the reason comes back as tool-result text, an input to the loop and not the end of the line (RN-163): the model reads it and can report to the user in the next response. A SUCCESSFUL propose_prototype ends the turn (ux_designer_server.ex:120, same guard as propose_execution_plan in the Dev Lead) — without it the loop would go back to the model, which could propose again and produce two prototypes with the same total. There's only ONE tool here (there's no second tool call to chain as in the Arquiteto), so "stops at the first success" loses nothing.
documents.s: RN-286 — propose_prototype records an artifact with no table and no dedicated use case, and offers TWO handoffs over the SAME artifact

documents.t: Same criterion as infraActive: an accepted handoff addressed to "ux-designer" in the session. apps/web/src/lib/agent-status.ts (rosterFactsFromEvents/rosterFromFacts) gained the fact and pushes it conditionally into the roster as a SOLO agent — with no corresponding pushAreaMembers, because it isn't an area. RN-090 requires BOTH sources in sync (team panel via event log; the dashboard card via ProjectCardSummary.roster, computed in the api) so that a new agent doesn't appear in one place and go missing in the other. The fact went into both: apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.ts widens the SAME infraActive query (an inArray(handoffs.toAgent, ['infra', 'ux-designer']) in place of the single eq, split into two Sets by toAgent) — no new query, the count of twelve constant queries that projects-summary.repository.spec.ts proves doesn't grow. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/ux_designer_server.ex, ux_designer_tools.ex, ux_designer_supervisor.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/agents.ex (identity), artifact_schemas.ex (type prototipo_navegavel); apps/engine/lib/engine/application.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine_web/controllers/agent_command_controller.ex; apps/web/src/lib/agents.ts, agent-status.ts; apps/api/src/application/ports/projects-summary-repository.port.ts, apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.ts Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/ux_designer_server_test.exs, ux_designer_tools_test.exs; apps/web/src/lib/agent-status.test.ts; apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.spec.ts (describe with both toAgents in the same session) ADR: 0087
documents.s: RN-287 — uxDesignerActive in the roster, in BOTH sources (RN-090)

documents.t: It's not a planned phase: docs/fluxo.yml declares the Staff/Principal Engineer as status: planned since ADR 0085 ("contract ready, activation decided, awaiting trigger"). The product owner decided to bring the CODE forward even knowing that the automatic trigger (the Anamnese noticing a RECURRING systemic problem) won't fire — the Anamnese is paused (ANAMNESE_ENABLED=false, product decision of 2026-08-10). See the pending item already documented in RN-086: the same signal that would make the Anamnese propose raising the parallelism ceiling is what would make it propose a handoff to the Staff, and neither fires while it is paused.
documents.s: Staff: code ready, dormant for automatic triggering (RN-305/RN-306, ADR 0088)

documents.t: USER_STARTED_AGENTS (apps/api/src/domain/sessions/agent-activation.ts) is the Criativo's exception (starts WITHOUT a handoff, by user command) — the Staff does NOT enter it. Investigation confirmed that canActivateAgent already activates any agent with an accepted handoff addressed to it, the same path that already applies to dev-lead/arquiteto/infra; and assertHandoffTargetAllowed (apps/api/src/domain/agents/agent-areas.ts) only refuses a handoff addressed to an area SUBAGENT — the Staff has no area, so no domain change in the api was necessary. "Manually triggerable" means the domain MECHANICS allow it (any agent can call EngineApiClient.create_handoff(..., "staff", ...), and a human accepts through the already existing route), not that there's a dedicated screen today to choose "address handoff to the Staff" — the generic UI for handoff to an agent of choice remains in the backlog (docs/explanation/backlog.md), as it already was before this change. Engine.Agents.StaffServer (apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/staff_server.ex) is the fifth solo conversational agent (along with Criativo, PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead), mirroring the Arquiteto — a GenServer per session, rehydration from the event log, bounded tool-use loop with a ceiling of 14 (staff_server.ex:49) — but without kickoff/1: the other leads synthesize an opening instruction from a previous artifact in the session's event log (product_brief, module_map, backlog); the Staff has no such source, because the systemic problem is born outside the session. StaffSupervisor.start_agent/2 brings up the process (rehydrates the history) and it stays idle until the first user_message (staff_server.ex:60) — which is how whoever addressed the handoff explains the problem. apps/engine/lib/engine_web/controllers/agent_command_controller.ex:60 (the start/2 clause for "staff") never calls kickoff (the function doesn't even exist), unlike po/arquiteto/dev-lead/infra. Where: apps/api/src/domain/sessions/agent-activation.ts (canActivateAgent, USER_STARTED_AGENTS — untouched), apps/api/src/domain/agents/agent-areas.ts (assertHandoffTargetAllowed — untouched), apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/staff_server.ex, staff_supervisor.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine_web/controllers/agent_command_controller.ex (the start/2/message/2/via_for/2 clauses for "staff"), apps/engine/lib/engine/application.ex (Engine.Agents.StaffSupervisor in the supervision tree) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/staff_server_test.exs (rehydration, absence of automatic kickoff — the turn only runs via user_message) ADR: 0088
documents.s: RN-305 — The Staff activates through the GENERIC handoff path, without USER_STARTED_AGENTS, and without kickoff/1

documents.t: Engine.Agents.StaffTools.propose_rfc (apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/staff_tools.ex:41) is the Staff's only tool: problem, options with trade-offs, recommendation, and the scope of a DISPOSABLE PoC (descartavel: true is FIXED — never written by the model). run/2 (staff_tools.ex:89) records artifact.rfc_staff via EngineApiClient.append_event_returning/3 — the same pattern WITHOUT a table and WITHOUT a dedicated use case as Engine.Harness.Tools.EmitInsight (the Arquiteto's emit_insight), and not that of artifact.c4_diagram (ADR 0068), which has its own use case in the api because it DERIVES the Container level from the current module_map — the RFC derives nothing from that side, the whole payload comes from the tool call. After recording, the SAME run/2 calls EngineApiClient.create_handoff(..., "staff", "arquiteto", artifact_id) — with no human confirmation in between, same pattern as CriativoServer.executar_confirm_readiness/1 emitting the product_brief and offering the handoff to the PO in the same response. propose_rfc is NOT a proposed_action: recording an architecture document isn't an external effect (it isn't git, terminal, nor agent spend) — the real decision (adopt, adapt, refuse the recommendation) is the Arquiteto's, in the handoff the tool already returns. Failing to create the handoff does NOT take down the process nor lose the already recorded RFC (RN-116) — the reason goes into the tool-result, and the model knows it needs to retry only the handoff, not rewrite the RFC. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/staff_tools.ex Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/staff_server_test.exs ("propõe o RFC, grava o artefato e devolve o handoff ao arquiteto"; "propose_rfc com opções vazias vira tool-result de erro"; "falha ao devolver o handoff ao arquiteto NÃO derruba o processo") ADR: 0088 Declared, not hidden: the team panel's roster (apps/web/src/lib/agent-status.ts, staffActive) and the dashboard card (ProjectCardSummary.roster, apps/api/.../projects-summary.repository.ts) show the Staff when active, same criterion as infraActive — avoiding the divergence the RosterFacts comment already warned about. SessionPage.tsx was NOT touched: staff stays out of AGENTES_DE_CHAT, the same pattern already accepted for infra (a REAL and ACTIVE lead also outside that list — the handoff to it "is never accepted HERE", as the file's own comment says). Today's end-to-end usage path is the internal route (POST .../agent/message, agent: "staff"), not the Session screen.
documents.s: RN-306 — propose_rfc records the artifact DIRECTLY and returns the handoff in the SAME tool call, without proposed_action

documents.t: docs/gates.yml declared the implementavel gate (owner dev-lead) since PHASE 14d with status: planned — never activated. ADR 0090 activates it: the Dev Lead's assess_implementability tool proposes the implementability opinion of a story (implementavel/inviavel + justification) as a proposed_action, the SAME pattern as propose_execution_plan (RN-284) — three outcomes ({:ok, texto} | {:pending, action_id} | {:error, texto}), minimum role maintainer in decide.ts, and DELIBERATELY outside the block of absolute ceilings (it's an initial decision, not exceeding a ceiling). The opinion depends on the test plan, which is a PREREQUISITE, not an argument. run_assessment/2 reads the story's most recent artifact.plano_de_teste in the HISTORY of the Dev Lead's own session (emitted by the QA-strategy, RN-341): No plan yet — triggers Engine.Gates.Dispatcher.run_qa_estrategia/3 (the same test-swappable indirection that run_qa/2/run_secops/2 already use) and returns {:error, texto} asking to try again shortly. A tool error is an INPUT to the loop, not the end of the line (RN-163): the Dev Lead has a ceiling of 14 iterations to try again. The wait window is accepted and declared — QA-strategy runs in a separate process (qa-lead), and a synchronous run/2 can't block waiting for the result without coupling the two processes. With a plan — builds the opinion with the test plan EMBEDDED in the payload (synthesis and executable criteria), so the user can decide without needing to open two events, and proposes the action. Since RN-674 (ADR 0192) the two steps above NO LONGER hold. The test plan is born AFTER the dev's delivery and feeds qa-verificada; run_assessment/2 neither reads nor triggers a plan, proposes the opinion on the FIRST call, over the story and the module_map the Dev Lead already has in context, and the payload lost planoDeTeste/criteriosExecutaveis. Dispatcher.run_qa_estrategia/3 was removed. The rest of this rule (proposal, three outcomes, minimum role, outside the absolute ceilings) remains the same. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/dev_lead_tools.ex (run_assessment/2, spec_assess_implementability/0), dev_lead_server.ex (run_tool/3); apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts (assess_implementability); docs/gates.yml (implementavel, status: active) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/dev_lead_tools_test.exs (describe "assess_implementability"), dev_lead_server_test.exs (describe "suspensão em aprovação" — the two new tests), apps/api/test/domain/actions/decide.spec.ts (describe "parecer de implementabilidade do Dev Lead") Origin: ADR 0090
documents.s: RN-340 — The implementavel gate decides the story BEFORE the dev agent writes code

documents.t: docs/fluxo.yml declared the qa-estrategia role as proposto, with the separation criterion written in the registry itself: "it can be the qa-lead itself in a second MOMENT, not necessarily a new agent — the separation is by deliverable". ADR 0090 builds exactly that: Engine.Gates.QaEstrategiaAgent is a STATELESS module (not a GenServer), triggered by Engine.Gates.QaLeadServer.run_design/3 — a NEW and ADDITIVE entry point in the SAME qa-lead process, without touching run/2 (the usual path, PR review, tied to DevAgentState.find_by_task_id). The context is LIGHT, and that's where the deliverable separation shows up. Engine.Gates.QaEstrategiaContext.fetch/3 fetches ONLY the story (from EngineApiClient.list_backlog/1, the tree the PO already reads — RN-164) and the current module_map (from EngineApiClient.get_infra_context/2, the SAME GetInfraContextUseCase the Infra Lead consumes, here only through the moduleMap field) — NO dev_state, NO worktree_path: the implementavel gate runs PRE-DEV, before a dev agent, worktree, or task_id exists. No new route in the api — both functions already existed. It never suspends. The tool registry (ReadFile, SearchWorkspace, EmitPlanoDeTeste) includes neither terminal nor write_file — the ONLY TWO tools that Engine.Harness.Hooks.ActionPipeline intercepts to create a proposed_action. With no call at all going through the actions pipeline, this agent's ToolLoop never produces :pending, and run_design/3 runs SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the handle_cast itself — with no suspension/resumption mechanism, unlike the rest of the QA area. The iteration ceiling stays at 8 (conversational), not 60 (gate) — on purpose, not a gap. This agent runs WITHOUT token_budget_micros — there's no task nor task budget yet. The criterion of RN-085 isn't "who works a lot": it's "what holds spend beyond the iteration ceiling". With no budget underneath, raising the ceiling would multiply the worst case with nothing to contain it — the SAME reason why infra-workflows stays at 8 even though it uses a tool. "qa-estrategia" did NOT get its own clause in Engine.Harness.Iteracoes.tipo/1: falling into the default is the right decision. The deliverable — emit_plano_de_teste (synthesis, verifiable executable criteria, a GENERIC automation strategy with no framework — a scope decision of this front, in the spec/0 the model reads, not a validation in code) — becomes the artifact.plano_de_teste artifact (ArtifactEmitter.emit/5, validated schema, criteriosExecutaveis can't be empty), in the event log of the SAME session that called run_design/3 — that's where assess_implementability (RN-340) reads it afterwards. Failure (iteration limit, budget, a model that stops without emitting) is NEVER silent: a durable agent.error with origin, same ruler as RN-059. Since RN-674 (ADR 0192) the MOMENT changed. The second moment still belongs to the qa-lead, with no new agent, and still never suspends; but it runs AFTER the delivery, at the start of the run/2 cycle, with the dev's worktree and the diff's files — run_design/3 and QaEstrategiaContext were removed, and the artifact gained taskId. The ceiling is still 8, now WITH the task's budget underneath. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/qa_estrategia_agent.ex, qa_lead_server.ex (run_area/3, since RN-674), tools/emit_plano_de_teste.ex, hooks/termination_plano_de_teste.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/artifact_schemas.ex (plano_de_teste); apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/iteracoes.ex (NO new clause, see above); docs/fluxo.yml (qa-estrategia, status: active) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/gates/qa_estrategia_agent_test.exs, qa_lead_server_test.exs (describe "plano de teste da entrega (ADR 0192)"), apps/engine/test/engine/harness/artifact_schemas_test.exs (describe "plano_de_teste"), iteracoes_test.exs ("qa-estrategia é conversacional DE PROPÓSITO") Origin: ADR 0090
documents.s: RN-341 — QA-strategy is the qa-lead's second MOMENT, and never suspends

documents.t: docs/fluxo.yml already declared id: appsec as proposto, with the separation criterion written in advance: "same pattern as QA: two MOMENTS, not two agents for now". This change builds that second moment — a DESIGN threat model, BEFORE code/PR exists — a conscious decision by the product owner to bring the activation forward, without waiting for the implementavel gate the registry itself cited as the trigger.
documents.s: appsec gains secops's second moment (RN-360/361, ADR 0090)

documents.t: Whoever runs appsec is the SAME Engine.Gates.SecOpsAgentServer that already exists for the deterministic PR verdict — not a new process. run_design/2 (apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/secops_agent_server.ex:76) is a GenServer.cast to the same Registry key ({project_id, "secops"}) that run/2 already uses; the handle_cast({:run_design, story_id}, state) (secops_agent_server.ex:93) fetches the context via Engine.Gates.AppSecContextBuilder.fetch/2 (apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/appsec_context_builder.ex:31) — the story in the project's backlog (EngineApiClient.list_backlog/1, the SAME read that RN-164 gave the PO) and the current module_map of the session that created the story (EngineApiClient.get_infra_context/2, the SAME read without task/story that the Infra area already does) — and then calls Engine.Gates.AppSecAgent.run/3 (apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/appsec_agent.ex:47). AppSecAgent is a STATELESS module (not a GenServer, same shape as QaPerformanceSegurancaAgent), with a tool registry WITHOUT Terminal — [ReadFile, SearchWorkspace, EmitThreatModel] — running a STRIDE-lite checklist (Spoofing/Tampering/Repudiation/Information disclosure/Denial of service/Elevation of privilege) via Engine.Harness.ToolLoop.run/1. The structural difference of the "second moment without Terminal, without task_id" from the earlier gate pattern: no dev_state/worktree_path enters the ctx — ReadFile/SearchWorkspace degrade to the fallback of Engine.Actions.Workspace.workspace_dir/1 (the project's SHARED checkout, not an agent worktree), and session_id comes from story["sessionId"], never from a dev_state. EmitThreatModel (apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/tools/emit_threat_model.ex) has no approved/changes_requested verdict — appsec always ENDS by recording the threat model, never approving/failing anything —, and that's why it doesn't reuse Engine.Gates.Hooks.Termination (the extracted shape is different): it has its OWN hook, Engine.Gates.Hooks.AppSecTermination. Finished successfully, run_appsec_design/3 (secops_agent_server.ex:234) emits artifact.threat_model (storyId/threatModel/requisitosDeSeguranca/riscos, schema in apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/artifact_schemas.ex:71 — riscos stays out of the required keys because an empty list is a valid answer). Failure (iteration ceiling, budget, or the model stopping without calling emit_threat_model) becomes a durable agent.error with origin (modelo/politica/infra), same ruler as RN-059 — never an empty response nor silence only in broadcast. The automatic trigger exists since RN-539. This delivery was kept self-contained on purpose (no file of another front touched: decide.ts, docs/gates.yml, and dev_lead_tools.ex untouched), and declared the gap: run_design/2 was TRIGGERABLE and nothing triggered it on its own. The trigger point it named — the Dev Lead's assess_implementability, front qa-estrategia, gate implementavel, same ADR 0090 — became the real caller, in parallel and only once per story. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/secops_agent_server.ex (run_design/2, handle_cast/2, run_appsec_design/3, emit_threat_model/3, emit_bloqueio_appsec/3); apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/appsec_agent.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/appsec_context_builder.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/tools/emit_threat_model.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/hooks/appsec_termination.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/artifact_schemas.ex (schema threat_model) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/gates/appsec_agent_test.exs, apps/engine/test/engine/gates/appsec_context_builder_test.exs, apps/engine/test/engine/gates/secops_agent_server_test.exs (the three run_design tests) Origin: ADR 0090
documents.s: RN-360 — The DESIGN threat model runs over story + module_map, without worktree/task_id, in the SAME secops process

documents.t: criar_handoffs_appsec/3 (secops_agent_server.ex:326) creates one handoff per target declared in docs/fluxo.yml (saidas of appsec): arquiteto, dev-lead, and infra — same pattern as OfferInfraHandoffUseCase/ArquitetoServer.executar_offer_infra_handoff/1 (SEPARATE calls, one per target, so that one handoff failure doesn't undo the other two already created). The flow id is area-infra, but the addressable AGENT is "infra" (apps/api/src/domain/agents/agent-areas.ts — lead: 'infra'), never area-infra: an external handoff addresses only the area's LEAD (ADR 0038), and CreateHandoffUseCase.assertHandoffTargetAllowed would refuse a toAgent that doesn't resolve to a lead/agent-with-no-area. Failure of ONE target becomes an agent.error narrated per target (RN-116) — the other two handoffs already created are not undone. Since RN-636 the three are ASKED, no longer always created: a destination that already has a pending offer or is already active in the project doesn't get another one, and that isn't a failure. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/secops_agent_server.ex:55 (@appsec_handoff_targets), :362 (criar_handoffs_appsec/3) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/gates/secops_agent_server_test.exs ("run_design: threat model concluído emite artifact.threat_model e cria os TRÊS handoffs") Origin: ADR 0090
documents.s: RN-361 — The completed threat model creates THREE handoffs, always addressing the LEAD

documents.t: A conscious decision by the product owner to BRING FORWARD the construction of the analytics and delivery-metricas roles (docs/fluxo.yml, status: proposto) without waiting for the organic trigger each one already declared. Both become a single SCRIPT — apps/api/scripts/analise-funil.ts — in the same format as medir-execucao.ts (Phase 13b): NestFactory.createApplicationContext, mandatory --projeto <uuid>, pure read via Drizzle, no writes at all. The shape is the one the flow itself already prescribed: analytics is "absorbed by medicao" and delivery-metricas "never becomes an agent" — no GenServer, no LLM agent.
documents.s: Analytics and delivery-metricas: both roles become a REPORT (RN-320..322, ADR 0089)

documents.t: The command is pnpm --filter api analise:funil -- --projeto <uuid> [--json]. It only reads proposed_actions (filtered by actionType IN (git_commit, pr_open, git_merge)) and projects, never writes. The guard if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith('analise-funil.ts')) void main(); at the end of the file is the same as medir-execucao.ts: without it, importing the module in the test would bring up all of Nest and take down the process at the argument parser's process.exit. Where: apps/api/scripts/analise-funil.ts:64-73 (lerOpcoes), :256-319 (main), :390 (execution guard) Test: apps/api/test/scripts/analise-funil.spec.ts (only the pure functions — the part that talks to the database is exercised by real execution, same pattern as medir-execucao.spec.ts) ADR: 0089
documents.s: RN-320 — analise-funil.ts is a script, never an agent — same skeleton as medir-execucao.ts

documents.t: calcularFunil counts how many sessions produced at least one git_commit, pr_open, and git_merge with status: 'executed' — a session with three commits enters only once in each stage it reached, never three times. A stage's conversion rate is sessions-of-the-stage / sessions-of-the-previous-stage, and is null (not 0, not Infinity) when the denominator is zero — there's no "conversion from" anything to measure. calcularLeadTimes uses the updated_at of the proposed_actions row, not created_at: it's the instant when ExecuteGitActionUseCase#record actually wrote the execution_result (updateExecutionResult bumps updatedAt), not when the action was PROPOSED — the same distinction that token_usage/frozen price already make in another context (RN-042). A merge whose updated_at precedes the commit's (two batches in the same session, or incoherent data) is discarded, never becoming a negative lead time. Where: apps/api/scripts/analise-funil.ts:115-160 (calcularFunil), :170-193 (calcularLeadTimes) Test: apps/api/test/scripts/analise-funil.spec.ts (describe "calcularFunil", "calcularLeadTimes") ADR: 0089
documents.s: RN-321 — The funnel counts SESSIONS per stage, only executed actions, and lead time uses the execution's updated_at

documents.t: deploymentFrequencyPorDia only counts executed git_merges whose executionResult.targetBranch is in PROTECTED_BRANCHES (apps/api/src/domain/actions/protected-branches.ts) — a merge into a feature branch isn't a deploy. It crosses by REFERENCE with the backmerge gate (docs/gates.yml): its evidence is CI, in .release/gate.json, out of reach of a script that only reads the database, so there's no data join, only the same branch slice the gate observes. Three metrics leave the report with a "Not measured, on purpose" section instead of an approximate number: Complete product funnel (ideation → commit). sessions has no storyId — RN-230 already declares the gap in the Criativo tab. Closing it requires a new schema, outside the scope of this front (no migration). Evidence of adoption per feature. It isn't data that's missing to collect: Brabo doesn't instrument the projects it BUILDS, and there's no path at all for that telemetry to exist today. MTTR and change failure rate. They require a real production INCIDENT signal — the same dependency docs/fluxo.yml already records for secops-runtime/platform (status: proposto/planned, activation synchronized with DEPLOY_ENABLED). Where: apps/api/scripts/analise-funil.ts:220-247 (deploymentFrequencyPorDia), :372-386 (printed "Not measured" section) Test: apps/api/test/scripts/analise-funil.spec.ts (describe "deploymentFrequencyPorDia") ADR: 0089
documents.s: RN-322 — Real deployment frequency filters merges into a PROTECTED branch; three metrics stay DECLARED absent, never approximated

documents.t: A conscious decision by the product owner to bring forward the secops-runtime role (docs/fluxo.yml, camada_seguranca), which was born proposto with the separation criterion "production with real traffic (after DEPLOY_ENABLED + platform active)". That trigger didn't fire — there's no production traffic. What exists today is rate_limit_hits (RateLimitGuard, ADR 0027): one row per counted request, written even under dev/CI traffic. secops-runtime comes in as a SCRIPT (pnpm --filter api relatorio:seguranca-runtime), not an LLM agent nor a GenServer — there's no decision to make, only data to aggregate.
documents.s: secops-runtime — abuse report over rate_limit_hits (RN-375..377, ADR 0091)

documents.t: DomainGaugesCollector.pruneRateLimit (apps/api/src/infrastructure/observability/domain-gauges.collector.ts:177-186) deletes hits older than 2 × RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS (240s with the default of 60s), every METRICS_GAUGE_INTERVAL_MS (15s by default) — the table never keeps more than a few minutes. relatorio-seguranca-runtime.ts prints TWO windows, never just one: the CONFIGURED one (the pruning's theoretical ceiling) and the OBSERVED one (what the data actually covers, from the first to the last occurred_at read). When the two coincide, the report says explicitly that it's a sign of pruning — older hits may have existed and have already been deleted — never "there were no more hits than that".
documents.s: RN-375 — The report declares the window, never pretends a longer history

documents.t: RateLimitGuard.registrarEContar (apps/api/src/interfaces/http/shared/rate-limit.guard.ts:150-170) records only bucket_key (user:<uuid> or ip:<endereço>) and occurred_at — there's NO route, HTTP method, nor block reason. rankingDeBaldes and interpretarBalde (apps/api/scripts/relatorio-seguranca-runtime.ts) classify by these two fields and only them; a bucket_key outside the user:/ip: format falls into desconhecido instead of blowing up, so the script doesn't break if a future RateLimitGuard writes another format. Asking for an "IP ranking by route" would be inventing a dimension the table never kept.
documents.s: RN-376 — The ranking works only with what bucket_key keeps: bucket and when

documents.t: montarRelatorio always includes naoMedido: automatic incident detection, incident response, and security postmortem. All three depend on the same trigger docs/fluxo.yml already declared for secops-runtime — real production traffic — and none of them is simulated with a sample incident or invented number (same principle as ADRs 0041/0042/0077: without the real data, the gap stays visible instead of faked). The section only leaves the list when the product has real traffic to measure against it — it isn't a TODO to delete in the next cleanup. Where: apps/api/scripts/relatorio-seguranca-runtime.ts, apps/api/package.json (relatorio:seguranca-runtime) Test: apps/api/test/scripts/relatorio-seguranca-runtime.spec.ts ADR: 0091
documents.s: RN-377 — The "not measured" section is permanent, and names the three gaps

documents.t: docs/fluxo.yml describes platform (camada_plataforma) as "SRE / Platform — owner of the feedback loop", status: planned, with activation synchronized with DEPLOY_ENABLED — which doesn't exist. The product owner decided to bring forward the half that already has real data behind it: pnpm --filter api relatorio:telemetria [--projeto <uuid>] [--json] reads, on demand, the SAME questions that DomainGaugesCollector already answers every METRICS_GAUGE_INTERVAL_MS for the Prometheus scrape — active/closing sessions per project, blocked tasks per project, state of the last backup (age, status, size, always GLOBAL, never per project, because the product has a single backup). It isn't an LLM agent nor a GenServer: it's a standalone, stateless read that ends after printing. The SQL queries are REPLICATED, not imported from the collector — its methods (collectSessions/collectBlockedTasks/collectBackup) are private and end by writing into a Prometheus gauge (this.metrics.*.set(...)); there's no pure "query only" half to reuse without coupling a standalone script to the lifecycle of a NestJS @Injectable. The script is also NOT a second collector: it registers no metric, doesn't run on setInterval. The output always brings "where to see more" (the three versioned dashboards in deploy/k8s/observability/dashboards/*.json, the alerts in deploy/k8s/observability/alerts/brabo-alerts.yaml, docs/runbook.md #observabilidade, and pnpm dev:obs for local observability) — the script LINKS to what already exists, never duplicates. Where: apps/api/scripts/relatorio-telemetria.ts; mirrors apps/api/src/infrastructure/observability/domain-gauges.collector.ts Test: apps/api/test/scripts/relatorio-telemetria.spec.ts (pure functions — parseArgs, formatarIdade, formatarBytes — same slice as medir-execucao.spec.ts: the part that talks to the database is exercised by running the script against a real database) ADR: 0092
documents.s: RN-385 — The platform role is born as a one-off read SCRIPT, over the same sources as DomainGaugesCollector

documents.t: The real trigger of the platform role (DEPLOY_ENABLED) doesn't exist: there's no production environment with real traffic, no numeric SLO defined anywhere in the product, and no postmortem possible without a real incident. relatorio-telemetria.ts says so in its OWN output, in a "not measured" section, instead of pretending coverage it doesn't have — the same discipline as ADR 0042 for a model's grade and ADR 0077 for code quality: without the real data, the product DECLARES the gap, never invents the number. Three gaps, all explicit: formal numeric SLO (none is defined); postmortem (depends on a real incident that hasn't happened); and telemetry back into the product in a closed loop (the script is a one-off on-demand read — observing, deciding, and acting on its own is what would make platform active in docs/fluxo.yml, and that's why the role's gate_saida: { id: operavel, status: planned } remains planned, untouched by this change). Where: apps/api/scripts/relatorio-telemetria.ts (function imprimir, "Não medido" section); docs/fluxo.yml (camada_plataforma › platform › saidas_alvo, artifact telemetria-consolidada, field nota) Test: indirect coverage — the section is fixed text verified by reading the file; there's no conditional truth to test here (nothing to get wrong between "measured" and "not measured" beyond the text itself) ADR: 0092
documents.s: RN-386 — The telemetry report declares, without inventing, what it does NOT measure

documents.t: lintarConteudo (the pure core of lint-migracao.ts) scans each .sql of apps/api/src/db/migrations/ line by line, without depending on --projeto or a database — the risk it finds is SCHEMA risk, not load risk, and that's why it doesn't depend on any real data volume (the separation criterion that docs/fluxo.yml already declared for the role). Five patterns, each with the reason attached to the finding: DROP TABLE/TRUNCATE (total loss, irreversible), DROP COLUMN (loss of the column, irreversible), ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE/SET DATA TYPE (can rewrite the whole table), and ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL without DEFAULT (fails against a non-empty table — the pattern 0042_tough_captain_midlands.sql consciously avoided, with nullable-first-then-backfill-then-SET NOT NULL). A line starting with -- (comment) is ignored on purpose: this repository explains in prose, in the SQL itself, why a pattern was AVOIDED — analyzing the comment's text would find the pattern exactly in the sentence describing why it wasn't used. Where: apps/api/scripts/lint-migracao.ts (REGRAS, line 75; lintarConteudo, line 126) Test: apps/api/test/scripts/lint-migracao.spec.ts — each pattern individually, a combination of several in the same migration, and "ignora o padrão de risco quando ele aparece só em COMENTÁRIO" ADR: 0093
documents.s: RN-400 — The migration opinion is STATIC SQL analysis, and ignores the risk pattern when it appears only in a comment

documents.t: Running pnpm --filter api lint:migracao against the repository's real migrations FINDS three occurrences in migrations already merged and accepted (0006_whole_princess_powerful.sql:22 and 0034_quick_saracen.sql:33 — DROP COLUMN; 0007_groovy_bullseye.sql:2 — ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE). That's not a defect to fix in passing (same CLAUDE.md rule that protects findings Z/AD/AE): they're already accepted migrations, and deleting them would erase the evidence of why the decision was made. It's also why the script exits != 0 but is not wired into .github/workflows/ci.yml — a gate that fails the whole repository would fail every PR forever, for a finding that isn't its own. Becoming a real blocking gate requires scoping to the DIFF against the PR's base (the same technique as scripts/ci/pr-police.ts), left for when dbre needs to BLOCK a merge — today it's a manual opinion, not an automatic verdict. Where: apps/api/scripts/lint-migracao.ts (principal, exit code at the end of the file); decision documented in the file's header and in the ADR Test: not applicable to CI (there's no step); the manual run against the real repository is recorded in ADR 0093, Consequences section ADR: 0093
documents.s: RN-401 — The linter is not a CI gate: it scans the whole repository, not the PR's diff

documents.t: relatorio-backup.ts isn't a new Prometheus gauge — it's the SAME read of backup_runs that DomainGaugesCollector.collectBackup() already does (last SUCCESS, for age and size; the LAST run, to catch the case of failing for days with an older good backup), on demand. avaliarBackup is pure — it receives the two rows and the current instant, returns status (ok|atrasado|nunca_houve|falha_recente_com_sucesso_antigo). The "late" threshold (26h = BACKUP_AGE_ATRASADO_SEGUNDOS) is the SAME as the brabo-backup-atrasado alert (deploy/k8s/observability/alerts/brabo-alerts.yaml), duplicated (not imported — the Grafana YAML isn't read by the Node process) and subject to diverging if one side changes without the other. Where: apps/api/scripts/relatorio-backup.ts (avaliarBackup, line 82; BACKUP_AGE_ATRASADO_SEGUNDOS, line 54) Test: apps/api/test/scripts/relatorio-backup.spec.ts — there was never a backup, backup ok, late, exactly at the threshold (doesn't count as late), recent failure with an old success, late takes priority over recent failure, age never negative ADR: 0093
documents.s: RN-402 — The backup report rereads exactly the logic of collectBackup(), never a second way of computing

documents.t: The procedure for actually restoring (make test-restore / deploy/k8s/test-restore.sh) has already been executed and is documented in docs/runbook.md#restore, with real RTO (~40s against a ~108 KB database) recorded in that document's "Last verified run" section. relatorio-backup.ts answers a narrower and more frequent question — "is the backup that this restore would use healthy now?" — and cites the runbook for whoever really needs to restore, instead of duplicating the procedure or rerunning it. Where: apps/api/scripts/relatorio-backup.ts (final message of imprimir, citing docs/runbook.md#restore) Test: not applicable (it's static text pointing to the runbook, not logic); the existence of the tested procedure is an RN of docs/runbook.md#restore itself ADR: 0093
documents.s: RN-403 — The backup report does NOT rerun the restore; it points to the already tested procedure

documents.t: Closes the audit's last two findings (section D, docs/explanation/auditoria-fluxo-vs-codigo.md): B6 (RN-160 guaranteed only on the client) and B1 (the Dev Lead → dev-<modulo> delegation declared by ADR 0053 item 5 and never implemented).
documents.s: fluxo.yml × code audit — Wave 2: RN-160 in the backend and Dev Lead → dev delegation (RN-404/405, ADR 0094)

documents.t: RN-160 guaranteed the rule ("at least 1 promoted story before the double Arquiteto→Dev Lead/Infra handoff") only by disabling the button in SessionPage.tsx — a direct HTTP call to POST /agents/arquiteto/handoff-infra, without going through the UI, ignored the rule entirely. OfferInfraHandoffUseCase.execute now queries StoryRepository.findByProject(projectId) and refuses with BadRequestException when NO story of the project has status !== 'draft' — the check comes BEFORE recording architecture.readiness_confirmed and BEFORE any call to the engine (offerInfraHandoff; offerDevHandoff was removed in RN-672): a refusal can't leave a trace of a half-offered handoff in the event log, which is immutable. StoryRepository was chosen (and not ListBacklogUseCase) for being lighter — it doesn't need to build the epic→story→task tree to answer "is there any non-draft?". Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/agents/offer-infra-handoff.use-case.ts (lines 27-34, the check; injection of StoryRepository in the constructor) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/agents/offer-infra-handoff.use-case.spec.ts — zero promoted stories refuses with ZERO calls to the engine and ZERO events recorded; with at least one ready/in_progress/done, it follows the normal flow ADR: 0094
documents.s: RN-404 — "Confirm architecture ready" (RN-160) is revalidated in the BACKEND, not only disabled in the UI

documents.t: ADR 0053 (PHASE 14d) already foresaw the Dev Lead → dev-<modulo> delegation as "the same path as QA and Infra" (delegations, area = 'dev'), but declared it out of scope. dev_lead_server.ex never wrote to the table — only QA (qa_lead_server.ex) and Infra (infra_lead_server.ex) did, both on the ENGINE side, because that's where the subagent produces an OPINION (a single-round verdict) that justifies parecerArtifactId. The Dev Lead doesn't have that pattern: activating a dev-<modulo> happens on the API side, in AcceptParallelizationUseCase.execute — called both by the direct path (RequestParallelizationUseCase, below the session ceiling of RN-083) and by the approved one (ExecuteParallelizationUseCase, after the user approves the parallelize-type proposed_action). The recording went INSIDE that method — it covers both paths for free, because both already converge there —, with status: 'completed' REDEFINED for this area: it means "the delegation was CARRIED OUT" (the agent came up), not "the subagent finished and emitted an opinion" as in QA/Infra (decision recorded in ADR 0094). parecerArtifactId points to the id of the project's most recent and current artifact.module_map event — obtained from SessionEventRepository.listByTypeForProject(projectId, 'artifact.module_map') (an already existing generic method, used by computeCoverage for artifact.business_rule; no new query was written, just one more call to it — the last item of the list is the most recent, because the function sorts by createdAt ASC) — the artifact that justified the decision to delegate. area: 'dev', leadAgent: 'dev-lead', subagent is the exact id of the activated agent (extraDevAgentId(module), the SAME function that builds the id in all the rest of the use case — no new format). With no artifact.module_map in the project (it shouldn't happen — it's a mandatory input of the Dev Lead in docs/fluxo.yml), the delegation is NOT recorded with an invented id: it only logs the unexpected state, by the same lesson as RN-059 (never a silent failure, but also never pretending a justification that doesn't exist). And a failure of RecordDelegationUseCase.execute (e.g. database down) is caught and logged, never propagated — the dev agent's activation is already a success when the attempt to record the delegation happens, and can't be taken down by an auxiliary write. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/execution/accept-parallelization.use-case.ts (recordDevDelegation, called at the end of execute) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/execution/accept-parallelization.use-case.spec.ts, describe "delegação Dev Lead → dev (área dev, ADR 0094)" — records with area: 'dev' pointing to the most recent module_map; without a module_map it doesn't record (and doesn't throw); RecordDelegationUseCase failing doesn't take down the activation ADR: 0094
documents.s: RN-405 — The Dev Lead → dev delegation becomes data in delegations, with parecerArtifactId redefined as "what justified the decision"

documents.t: Closes the last finding of the audit plan (section D, docs/explanation/auditoria-fluxo-vs-codigo.md) — B2. The other five waves had already closed (3, 4, and 5 brought forward out of order by ADRs 0089/0090; 1 and 2 in the previous PRs). docs/fluxo.yml (role criativo) declared gate_saida: { id: necessidade-validada, status: proposto } since ADR 0085 with no mechanism at all behind it — and modelo-de-time.md already recorded why: the Criativo (the model) deciding on its own that the need it produced itself is validated would be self-validation, not a real gate.
documents.s: fluxo.yml × code audit — Wave 6 (last): the necessidade-validada gate (RN-406, ADR 0095)

documents.t: Revised by ADR 0185 (RN-657), by the owner's decision on 09/30. The click is no longer SEPARATE: "I'm ready — the need is validated" records readiness.confirmed and necessity.validated in the same POST, with the product_brief produced AFTER the click (productBriefId: null). The "Confirm validated need" button left the screen. What still holds from this rule: whoever validates is always a PERSON, never the Criativo; the gate stays warn. POST .../agents/criativo/validate-necessity remains in the api, with no consumer on screen — it's the path for a session whose "I'm ready" predates ADR 0185. The text below is the design of ADR 0095, kept as history. SessionPage.tsx gains a third confirmation button, in the SAME interaction pattern as "I'm ready to produce" (RN-142) and "Confirm architecture ready" (RN-160): "Confirm validated need" (handleValidateNecessity) calls POST .../agents/criativo/validate-necessity, which records necessity.validated with payload.productBriefId pointing to the session's most recent artifact.product_brief. The button only enables AFTER confirm_readiness has already consolidated the product_brief (hasProductBrief, events.some(e => e.type === 'artifact.product_brief')) — it makes no sense to "validate" an executive summary that hasn't been produced yet, and that's the most consistent reading with docs/fluxo.yml: necessidade-validada is the Criativo's EXIT gate, the moment when its work has already delivered a concrete artifact. ValidateNecessityUseCase revalidates the same precondition in the BACKEND (SessionEventRepository.listByTypeInSession(sessionId, 'artifact.product_brief'), takes the last by seq) — the disabled UI alone wouldn't suffice, same lesson as RN-404. Unlike OfferInfraHandoffUseCase (RN-160), this confirmation does NOT signal the engine: the Criativo→PO handoff has already happened inside confirm_readiness itself (CriativoServer.executar_confirm_readiness/1), so there's no agent waiting for this event — it's only the record that a human validated the MERIT of what was already delivered. ValidateNecessityUseCase doesn't receive ApiToEngineClient in the constructor. docs/gates.yml gains the necessidade-validada gate: status: active, aprovacao_humana: true (it's literally a human click), verificacao: script, but severidade: warn — nothing in the product today CHECKS the passage of this gate before letting the PO proceed (unlike story-promovida/plano-de-adocao, which are block because a real code lock prevents them from being skipped). docs/fluxo.yml (role criativo) goes status: proposto → status: ativo. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/agents/validate-necessity.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/interfaces/http/agents/agents.controller.ts (validateNecessityHandoff); apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (hasProductBrief, necessidadeJaValidada, handleValidateNecessity) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/agents/validate-necessity.use-case.spec.ts — without product_brief, refuses BEFORE recording any event; with one or more, records referencing the MOST RECENT; apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.validar-necessidade.test.tsx — button disabled without product_brief, enabled with it, disappears after necessity.validated ADR: 0095
documents.s: RN-406 — The necessidade-validada gate closes with a SEPARATE click from the user, never with the Criativo validating itself

documents.t: The PO gained a THIRD read tool — listar_metricas_de_produto (:direct, with no parameter at all) — served by GET /internal/projects/:projectId/product-metrics, the same design as the two siblings of RN-164: scope closed on the project, no search term, no pagination. docs/fluxo.yml (role po, input metricas-de-produto) declared status: lacuna since ADR 0089, which had already delivered the DATA — the script pnpm --filter api analise:funil measures the real session → commit → PR → merge funnel, the real lead time, and the real deployment frequency from proposed_actions. What was missing was only the MECHANISM: the PO never had a way to reread that report within the turn. It closes item B4 of the fluxo.yml × code audit (docs/explanation/auditoria-fluxo-vs-codigo.md) — the LAST pending item of the "Team model backlog" table (docs/explanation/backlog.md), which is empty after this one. The CALCULATION is the SAME as the script's, never duplicated: the pure functions (calcularFunil/calcularLeadTimes/leadTimeMedioMs/ deploymentFrequencyPorDia) and the query that builds AcaoGit[] (buscarAcoesGitDoFunil) were extracted from apps/api/scripts/analise-funil.ts to apps/api/src/application/services/funil-metrics.ts — a use case in src/ can't import from scripts/, and the script now REEXPORTS from there instead of defining locally, without changing signature or behavior (the script's regression test stays green without being touched). The JSON body the route returns has no field at all for the three permanent absences the script already declared in text ("Not measured, on purpose": complete product funnel ideation → commit, evidence of adoption per feature, MTTR/change failure rate) — the report's shape never reserved space for them. The PO's tool names all three in the TEXT it returns to the model, always, and not only when the number is zero: without that section the PO would read only the funnel numbers and conclude by omission that there's no gap at all. Where: apps/api/src/application/services/funil-metrics.ts; apps/api/scripts/analise-funil.ts (reexports); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/backlog/list-product-metrics.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/internal-projects.controller.ts; apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/dto/product-metrics.response.dto.ts; apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/listar_metricas_de_produto.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/po_server.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/sessions/engine_api_client.ex Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/backlog/list-product-metrics.use-case.spec.ts; apps/api/test/scripts/analise-funil.spec.ts (regression — still imports from scripts/analise-funil.ts, unchanged); apps/engine/test/engine/harness/tools/listar_metricas_de_produto_test.exs; apps/engine/test/engine/agents/po_server_test.exs Origin: same pattern as RN-164 (agent read scoped to the project, no external effect, no proposed_action); the data is from ADR 0089 — this RN only closes the read mechanism that was missing.

documents.t: Closes the backlog item "Real SMTP in MailSender" (ADR 0096). resolverConfigSmtp() validates SMTP_HOST/SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASSWORD/ SMTP_FROM in the SAME format as RN-114 — in production (NODE_ENV === 'production'), each one takes down the boot if missing, whitespace only, or (in the case of SMTP_HOST) equal to the example literal published (commented out) in .env.example. SMTP_FROM has one more check: it must match "Nome <email@dominio>" or just email@dominio. An invalid SMTP_PORT (non-numeric or outside 1–65535) also takes down the boot in production. The difference from the original RN-114 is structural, not of rigor: the four secrets of RN-114 (AUTH_JWT_SECRET and company) HAVE a public development default, and it's the existence of that default that makes "not empty" an insufficient check. Here there's no default at all — SMTP_HOST stays blank if nobody sets it —, so the whole ruler is only applied when NODE_ENV=production AND MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp. Outside production, or with the transport at log (the default, including in production), none of the five variables is required: sending real e-mail is opt-in by the operator, and without that explicit opt-in the behavior stays the usual log-only one — including in production, so that whoever already runs the product today doesn't break on updating. The validation runs inside the constructor of SmtpMailSender, exercised by the useFactory of AuthUseCasesModule when assembling Nest's provider graph (NestFactory.create()) — not by an eager call in main.ts, like the four secrets of the original RN-114. The difference is deliberate: those four protect a path that ANY request can exercise at any moment, so failing before coming up matters. SmtpMailSender is only instantiated when the operator opted for smtp, and AuthUseCasesModule is imported unconditionally (via AuthHttpModule), so validation still happens at boot — the same design CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY already uses (validated in the constructor of EnvelopeEncryptionService, exercised by the same graph assembly). Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/mail/smtp-config.ts (resolverConfigSmtp, resolverModoDeTransporte), apps/api/src/infrastructure/mail/smtp-mail-sender.ts (SmtpMailSender, calls resolverConfigSmtp() in the constructor), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/auth-use-cases.module.ts (useFactory of the MailSender) Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/mail/smtp-config.spec.ts (same pattern as auth-key-material.spec.ts/service-token.spec.ts), apps/api/test/infrastructure/mail/smtp-mail-sender.spec.ts Origin: ADR 0096, extending the pattern of RN-114 (which in turn extends ADR 0059)
documents.s: RN-408 — MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp gates boot by the RN-114 pattern, without the public default

documents.t: An item from the previous backlog. Prior investigation (docs/explanation/backlog.md) confirmed that there was no liveness aggregate at all — neither per project, nor per workspace: what existed was only HISTORICAL presence (RosterFacts — "has appeared in the session at some point") and REAL live status only on the client, derived from the event log, and only when a project is OPEN (deriveAgentRoster). The dashboard card today forced () => 'ocioso' because it drew no status at all — that's the hardcode this RN replaces.
documents.s: "N agents online" on the dashboard — LIVE status, never historical presence (RN-409, ADR 0097)

documents.t: ProjectCardSummary.onlineAgentCount (GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/ projects-summary) is the count of agents ONLINE now — working or with a pending item waiting for a decision —, never team size. Calling "online" a number that is really "has appeared at some point" would be misleading (same principle as ADR 0041/ 0042/ 0077 against faked data). Two SOURCES, one ruler: Dev agents — engine.dev_agent_states.status, aggregated in batch by project_id (status NOT IN ('idle', 'idle_tripped')). working, awaiting_gate, and awaiting_approval count (RN-047/ADR 0052 — the five states of the dev's machine); idle/idle_tripped don't. dev-<modulo> and dev-<modulo>-2 are DISTINCT keys (agent_id in the table), so they count separately with no effort at all — it's the primary key itself that already separates them. Conversational agents (criativo/po/arquiteto/dev-lead/ux-designer/ staff/infra) — the last agent.status event of each actor_id, in the project's MOST RECENT session (the same session scope the rest of RosterFacts uses, RN-090). agent.status has only three possible values (Engine.Sessions.LiveBroadcast.agent_status/4 refuses any other): working/awaiting_approval count, idle doesn't. QA/SecOps NEVER count — it isn't a filter, it's an ABSENCE of data: neither of the two emits agent.status (they run a single verdict per invocation, with no notion of "idle" between calls — their status comes from pr.gate_changed/ infra.gate_changed, a separate mechanism that deriveAgentRoster already handles separately). No explicit exclusion was needed: the query only sums what has the right event type. The ruler is the SAME that deriveAgentRoster would already apply if the project were open ('trabalhando'/'aguardando' on the client ≅ working/ awaiting_gate/awaiting_approval on the backend) — BOTH paths compute "online" from the same eventual state (event log/persisted state table), only by different MECHANISMS (SQL aggregation on the backend, a fold over already fetched events on the client), in the same spirit as infraActive/uxDesignerActive/staffActive (RN-090/RN-287: two sources, one ruler). There's no shared function between apps/api and apps/web for this — the two already diverge in language/runtime for the rest of RosterFacts too, and introducing a shared package just for one count would be a heavier weight than the problem. A new query against a schema the api doesn't migrate. engine.dev_agent_states is an ENGINE table (Ecto, Postgres schema "engine"), same physical database, same connection — not a second data source, a second NAMESPACE in the same Postgres. The precedent already existed: apps/api/scripts/medir-execucao.ts already reads engine.oban_peers the same way (raw SQL via Drizzle), only as a manual SCRIPT, never tested. This RN raises the pattern to tested PRODUCTION code — see ADR 0097 for the decision NOT to expose this as an internal HTTP route in the engine. Cost measured, not pretended free. The two new queries take the read model's total from TWELVE to FOURTEEN (RN-090 still holds — fourteen is CONSTANT, proven by projects-summary.repository.spec.ts counting trips to the database with 2 and with 20 projects). Neither has a time WHERE — the agent.status one scans the same session_events of the most recent sessions that lastEvents/marcos already scan next to it, so the marginal cost is that of one more type filter over a query plan that was going to happen anyway, not a new table being scanned from scratch. DECLARED gap: there's no recent real execution (dogfooding) with production volume to measure real ms against the Phase 22 ruler (525 thousand rows, EXPLAIN ANALYZE) — the two new queries remain without a measured number, only the structural argument above. Where: apps/api/src/application/ports/projects-summary-repository.port.ts, apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/dto/iam.response.dto.ts, apps/web/src/lib/api-types.ts, apps/web/src/components/ProjectCard.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/Dashboard.tsx Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.spec.ts (describe('onlineAgentCount (RN-409)') — dev agent working/idle/ idle_tripped, awaiting_gate/awaiting_approval, two instances of the same base agent, conversational agent working/idle/awaiting_approval, only the LAST agent.status counts, QA/SecOps never count, sum between the two sources, isolation between projects); apps/api/test/support/global-setup.ts (ensureEngineFixture — the engine's table created as a MINIMAL and declared fixture, only so the test above can exist); apps/web/src/components/ProjectCard.test.tsx (the "N online" badge disappears with 0/undefined, appears with onlineAgentCount > 0) Origin: docs/explanation/backlog.md (item inherited from PHASE 13c/ the dogfooding harvest); product decision that the number had to be real liveness, not historical presence, recorded in the prompt that commissioned this fix
documents.s: RN-409 — "N online" adds two mechanisms by the SAME ruler: not idle, not tripped

documents.t: Found by real USE, not by test: in an execution session, five dev agents came up, became idle_tripped (the circuit breaker of RN-047, stuck waiting for the user to unblock a task manually), and the 30-second heartbeat (Engine.Sessions.SessionServer.handle_info(:heartbeat_timeout, state)) closed the session from underneath while the work — and the wait for a human decision — continued. GetSessionPendingWorkUseCase already had a third signal (RN-064) for the same problem: an agent activated, with no later idle, holds the session. But that signal only reads agent.status, the vocabulary of CONVERSATIONAL agents (Criativo/PO/Arquiteto/Dev Lead/UX Designer/Staff/Infra). Engine.Dev.DevAgentServer (via Engine.Dev.AgentIo) never emits agent.status — it uses its OWN vocabulary in the session's event log: dev.started, dev.working, dev.awaiting_gate, dev.awaiting_approval, dev.idle, dev.idle_tripped, dev.blocked, dev.blocked_by_container, dev.error. An execution session with a dev agent working OR stuck always returned pending: false by the third signal, because no agent.status exists for it. The FOURTH signal fetches the LAST dev.* event of each actor.id (dev-<modulo>/dev-<modulo>-2, the same key as RN-195) that has already appeared in the session — like the third signal, but over multiple event types instead of just one, because the dev agent's state isn't ONE type with a variable payload.status, it's distinct event TYPES per transition. The ruler: pending: true when the last one is dev.working, dev.blocked, or dev.idle_tripped — all three mean "there's work running or a human needs to act", and stuck waiting for unblocking IS pending work (it's literally what the user was doing when the session closed in the real execution). Only dev.idle (no task at all to pick up, truly drained) doesn't count. dev.awaiting_gate and dev.awaiting_approval, as the last event, did NOT originally trigger this signal — they were left out of the ruler as decided at the time. awaiting_gate was a KNOWN residual gap; RN-412 closed it, together with awaiting_approval (by a new argument, not the original — see RN-412). dev.blocked_by_container came in LATER, by the same argument and through an equally real finding. The type was born with RN-502/ADR 0143 — the dev agent doesn't claim a task before the project has a registered running container — and the use case's DEV_EVENT_TYPES list didn't keep up. Since it's the list the use case QUERIES, the event became invisible: the api didn't see it even to ignore it. In the real exp004 execution (session f782257e) five dev agents emitted dev.started and dev.blocked_by_container at 22:41:38, the engine closed by heartbeat_timeout at 22:42:07 — exactly 30 seconds —, and events from that session kept arriving 13 and 32 minutes later. The last VISIBLE event per agent was dev.started, which is deliberately outside the ruler. The five were waiting for a HUMAN to bring up the container, which is the definition of pending work the other signals already use. The claim that the list was "the complete vocabulary, confirmed by direct reading of the engine's code" was true when it was written — and it's what silently aged. What keeps it true now is MECHANISM: scripts/ci/vocabulario-de-eventos-dev.spec.ts extracts the dev.* types from apps/engine/lib/**/*.ex and fails when they diverge from the use case's two lists, naming the missing type. It COMPARES instead of GENERATING (the agent-areas.ts precedent) because only half of the pair is derivable: DEV_EVENT_TYPES is mechanical, DEV_PENDING_TYPES is judgment — which states mean "a human needs to act". The SAME drift had a third instance, in the WEB, and the mechanism now covers it. DEV_STATUS_EVENTS (apps/web/src/lib/agent-status.ts), which the team panel queries to tell each dev agent's state, also didn't know dev.blocked_by_container nor dev.awaiting_approval — and there the consequence wasn't invisibility, it was a LIE: both fell into the switch's default: return 'trabalhando', so in exp004 the panel said that five dev agents stopped for HOURS, waiting for a human to bring up the container, were working. Both map to aguardando, the same state dev.awaiting_gate already used (the agent doesn't proceed until something OUTSIDE it happens), with no new state in AgentStatus; dev.error, which wasn't in any list and therefore made the panel go back to the previous dev.working, maps to falhou. The list stopped being a list: it became a type -> AgentStatus MAP, which erases the default and makes it impossible to add a type without answering what it means. And the cross test gained the engine × web pair, with a requirement the api doesn't have — an explicit DECISION per type, mapped OR declared in DEV_STATUS_EVENTS_FORA (type -> reason, empty today) —, because in the panel a dev.* type MAY legitimately not matter; what it can't do is be left out by forgetfulness. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/sessions/get-session-pending-work.use-case.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/sessions/get-session-pending-work.use-case.spec.ts (dev agent dev.working/dev.blocked/dev.idle_tripped/dev.blocked_by_container as the last event → pending: true, including the five agents of the exp004 scenario and with dev.blocked_by_container beating an earlier dev.idle; dev.idle → pending: false; a session without a dev.* event keeps the previous behavior; only each agent's LAST event matters; dev-<modulo>-2 also holds; isolation between sessions), scripts/ci/vocabulario-de-eventos-dev.spec.ts (the engine's dev.* vocabulary × the api's two lists AND × the panel's map, plus the three fabricated cases that prove the DEV_STATUS_EVENTS_FORA valve, which no real data exercises today), and apps/web/src/lib/agent-status.test.ts (dev.blocked_by_container and dev.awaiting_approval → aguardando, dev.error → falhou, never trabalhando; and the most recent event still prevailing) Origin: found by real use — a real execution session with five dev agents in idle_tripped closed by the heartbeat while the user was still unblocking tasks manually; and, later, five dev agents in blocked_by_container in exp004, by the same mechanism
documents.s: RN-411 — The fourth pending-work signal: dev agents speak dev.*, not agent.status

documents.t: Found by real USE ("on PRs it's always blowing up with entity too large"), with two defects that chain together. The QA/SecOps gate died with 413 request entity too large → the dev agent waiting for the verdict stayed stuck in dev.awaiting_gate indefinitely → that state was NOT one of the three RN-411 held → the 30s heartbeat closed the session from underneath → the Executors tab required an active session (findActiveExecutionSession) and erased the entire roster, even with real work hanging. The cause of the 413 was Brabo's own api, never the LLM provider — see ADR 0098. Two fixes, both necessary (one without the other only postpones the overflow): apps/api/src/main.ts never configured Express's body limit — the 100 KB default applied, the narrowest bottleneck in the engine→api direction (Phoenix accepts up to 8 MB). POST /internal/sessions/:sessionId/llm-turn resends the conversation's ENTIRE history on each ToolLoop iteration, and 3-4 tool results of 32 KiB (RN-150's individual ceiling) already added up to more than 100 KB. API_JSON_BODY_LIMIT (default 10mb) closes that end. Engine.Harness.ContextManager.Default had two defects that made compaction unreachable before the body overflowed: estimate/1 counted only content, so assistant messages with heavy toolCalls cost ~zero tokens in the estimate; and the compaction window used only context_window (128,000 tokens in the gate agents — qa_automacao_agent.ex, qa_performance_seguranca_agent.ex, qa_estrategia_agent.ex, appsec_agent.ex, dev_agent_server.ex), giving ~350 KB before compacting (threshold 0.7 × window). The EFFECTIVE window is now min(context_window, transport_ceiling) (transport_max_body_bytes, a single config, default 8 MiB), and the cut always happens at an ITERATION BOUNDARY of the ToolLoop (group_by_iteration/1) — never separating an assistant message with toolCalls from the role: "tool" that answer it, which would break the provider's tool-use protocol. The pending-work ruler (DEV_PENDING_TYPES, get-session-pending-work.use-case.ts) gained two types: dev.awaiting_gate (the original argument — the gate now shouldn't die anymore, but locking the session because of it was never correct, it's defense in depth) and dev.awaiting_approval, by an argument DIFFERENT from what RN-411 had discarded: the approval/denial decision writes proposed_actions.status SYNCHRONOUSLY in the ApproveActionUseCase transaction (the second signal no longer sees pending there), but the dev agent's resumption is ASYNCHRONOUS — only after avisarQuemEsperava() writes task.action_settled/task.pr_settled to the outbox does Engine.Outbox.Drain enqueue the Oban job that wakes DevAgentServer. In that window, nothing held the session: the same defect as RN-411, one level deeper. The Executors/Overview tabs had the sibling defect on the web side: executionActivated was derived from events.some((e) => e.type === 'execution.activated') over the window of only 200 events of useSessionEvents ({ limit: 200, latest: true }) — execution.activated is among the FIRST events of an execution session and left the window in any real session.
