The correct value already existed, aggregated over ALL events (bool_or(...), RN-090), in the workspace summary (ProjectCardSummary.roster.executionActivated) — ProjectExecutorsTab.tsx and ProjectOverviewTab.tsx now consume it instead of deriving from the window. gatesEverOpened suffers from the SAME class of defect and was DECLARED as a known limitation, not fixed here — fixing it would require changing the signature of deriveAgentRoster/rosterFactsFromEvents, outside the scope of this fix. Where: apps/api/src/main.ts, apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/context_manager.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tokenizer.ex, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/sessions/get-session-pending-work.use-case.ts, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectExecutorsTab.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectOverviewTab.tsx Test: apps/api/test/main.spec.ts (1 MB body accepted; above the limit → 413); apps/engine/test/engine/harness/context_manager_test.exs (heavy toolCalls trigger compaction; :pinned survives; the transport ceiling forces compaction even with a large model window); get-session-pending-work.use-case.spec.ts (last event dev.awaiting_gate/dev.awaiting_approval → pending: true); ProjectExecutorsTab.test.tsx/ProjectOverviewTab.test.tsx (a session with >200 events still shows the roster via the aggregated summary) Origin: found by real use — "on PRs it's always blowing up with entity too large", investigated together with the product owner
documents.s: RN-412 — dev.awaiting_gate/dev.awaiting_approval hold the session; the effective compaction window is consistent with the transport

documents.t: Every agent prompt was an inline Elixir heredoc until this delivery — identities (Engine.Harness.Agents), the kickoffs of PO/Arquiteto/Dev Lead/UX/Infra, the ContextManager summarization prompt. A prompt template can now live as (:PromptTemplate {name})-[:HAS_VERSION]-> (:PromptVersion {version, body, hash, active}) in Neo4j, written via POST /internal/graph/prompt-templates and read via GET /internal/graph/prompt-templates/:name. Upsert is idempotent by hash — writing the SAME content twice doesn't create a new version, only the already existing version with an equal hash is returned. First batch extracted to prompts/*.md (front-matter name/version, placeholders documented in a "Variáveis" section for passages that in the original .ex were interpolation): ux-designer-identity, psychologist-kickoff, anamnese-kickoff, context-manager-summarize. scripts/dev/seed-prompts.ts reads prompts/*.md, computes the sha256 hash of the body, and sends it to the endpoint above. No .ex was edited in this delivery — the four GenServers keep the inline text; consuming the templates from the graph (the :graph source of InstructionFiles, precedence db > graph > dir > root) is the next Wave, declared out of scope here. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/graph/upsert-prompt-template.use-case.ts, get-prompt-template.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/internal-graph.controller.ts; prompts/*.md, prompts/README.md; scripts/dev/seed-prompts.ts (SECAO_DE_DOCUMENTACAO, corpoSemDocumentacao, parseFrontMatter) Test: use cases with a mocked GraphStore (upsert with the same hash doesn't duplicate) + integration test against real Neo4j, skipping gracefully when unavailable; scripts/dev/seed-prompts.spec.ts (front-matter parsing, deterministic hash, malformed template fails with a clear message; and, since AT-244, the sweep of EVERY prompts/*.md: the seeded body doesn't have the documentation section and each placeholder appears in it only once, and the summarizer receives the turns only once through the same engine render) Since AT-244 the "## Variáveis" section of each file is NOT seeded: the template's body ends at the ## Variáveis line, and the seeder discards from it onward. Before, the body carried the whole section — documentation that cites the same {{placeholders}} as the body —, and since each consumer replaces ALL occurrences (String.replace/3), with graph_templates_enabled? on the model received the documentation and the data TWICE: the ContextManager summarizer the turns doubled, the kickoffs of the Psicólogo and the Anamnese the event log doubled, and the UX identity (behind graph_instruction_templates_enabled?) the documentation in every turn. The four files had the shape; the cut lives in the SEEDER, and not in the render, because there's one render per consumer and the question "what is body" is about the file, which only the seeder reads. The versions went up (anamnese-kickoff and ux-designer-identity to "2", psychologist-kickoff and context-manager-summarize to "3") with the SAME prompt text. It doesn't close on its own in an installation that has already seeded: the ACTIVE version in the graph stays the old one, with the documentation, until scripts/dev/seed-prompts.ts runs again — the body's hash changed, so the seeder creates the new version and deactivates the previous one. With the flags off (the default) the defect never existed: the inline text applies, which never had the section. Origin: product owner's decision, inspired by the repository ErickWendel/neo4j-ai-experiments (see ADR 0099)
documents.s: RN-413 — Prompt templates live outside the code, versioned in the graph

documents.t: grep -rn "rag" apps/engine/lib gave ZERO occurrences before this delivery — the complete RAG (pgvector, hybrid search) was only consumed by the "Chat RAG" web tab. The new tool rag_search (apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/rag_search.ex, category :direct, reading isn't an external effect) calls POST /internal/rag/search — a new route that REUSES HybridSearchUseCase without duplicating the search logic — and returns hits formatted with citation (path + excerpt), always with degraded: true visible at the START of the text when embedding wasn't available (never hidden by the ceiling cut). Its own ceilings, in the spirit of RN-150: top_k clamped to 10 within the tool itself (it doesn't trust what the api would accept), a 16 KiB ceiling on the formatted text (smaller than the 32 KiB of search_workspace/read_file — each RAG hit is already a whole chunk+excerpt). A network failure becomes an error readable by the model, never a ToolLoop crash (RN-163). Registered in Engine.Harness.Tools (PO/Arquiteto/conversational) and Engine.Dev.Tools (dev agent); also extended to the read gates that already cite indexed ADRs/conventions (QA-automation, QA-strategy, AppSec, QA-performance/security) — not to Infra.WorkflowsAgent nor Psicólogo/Anamnese, which reason over the event log, not over the project's docs/code. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/rag_search.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/sessions/engine_api_client.ex (rag_search/4); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/internal-rag.controller.ts Test: rag_search_test.exs (hits formatted with citation; visible degradation; network failure without crash; byte ceiling truncating with a clear mark; top_k clamp); engine_api_client_rag_test.exs Origin: see ADR 0100
documents.s: RN-414 — rag_search: agents get the tool the product had never exposed

documents.t: nomic-embed-text (RAG_EMBEDDING_MODEL) was never pulled automatically — a real bug, not only of this feature: the ollama service's entrypoint only pulled llama3.2:1b, and RAG degraded to lexical-only SILENTLY in any clean environment, with no sign that this was happening. A new service ollama-model-loader (one-shot, dev and prod docker-compose.yml), reading OLLAMA_REQUIRED_MODELS (default gemma3:1b,yi-coder:1.5b,nomic-embed-text), additive to the existing ollama service — its entrypoint stays untouched. The degradation is no longer silent: rag_search (RN-414) and the api's hybrid search already returned degraded: true when embedding failed — what was missing was a CONSUMER that made that flag visible. Now that the tool exists, the model itself sees the warning in the formatted text, and the model-loader reduces the chance of degradation happening in the first place. Where: docker/docker-compose.yml, docker/docker-compose.prod.yml, docker/ollama/pull-models.sh; deploy/k8s/base/neo4j/, deploy/k8s/base/ollama/job-model-loader.yaml (template, NOT wired into any kustomization — deploy/k8s/ doesn't yet have an ollama Service to point to, wiring it today would cause CrashLoopBackOff in every real deploy) Test: scripts/dev/verificar-modelos-ollama.sh, executed end to end with a real small model (all-minilm) so as not to pay the cost of several GB of the production list on a shared machine Origin: found during the foundation of the knowledge graph — see ADR 0100
documents.s: RN-415 — Ollama models guaranteed at boot, RAG degradation declared

documents.t: The alternative of the engine writing to Neo4j directly was REFUSED — it would open a second write path besides the event log, breaking the guarantee of a single source of truth. GraphProjector (api) drains a SECOND outbox row, the usual same transaction, aggregateType: 'graph_projection' — a value the engine-side Engine.Outbox.Drain never matches (its filter is aggregate_type IN ('session', 'task')), avoiding the race that would exist if it reused 'session' (the engine already drains and marks that type in ~2s). Same pattern as deny-action.use-case.ts, which already writes in two aggregateTypes in the same transaction. Instrumented at two points: AppendSessionEventUseCase (for handoff.offered, psychologist.hypothesis_proposed, anamnese.profile_updated — payload only {eventId}, the projector REREADS the complete envelope from the event log at projection time, never trusting a potentially stale copy) and TransitionSessionUseCase (for session.closed/session.closed_abnormally, which don't go through session_events). GraphProjector is a poller (~2s, same shape as DomainGaugesCollector) that calls the write use cases already existing from the previous foundation — idempotency lives IN THEM (natural key per type: Hipotese.id, Handoff(sessionId,seq), PerfilAnamnese(userId,dimensao), Interacao.sessionId with range extension). A GraphUnavailableError in the middle of a batch STOPS the whole cycle (the rest would fail for the same reason) — the row stays unprocessed and retries on its own in the next cycle, with no intervention. Where: apps/api/src/application/graph-projection/graph-projector.ts; apps/api/src/domain/graph/graph-projection-events.ts; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/sessions/append-session-event.use-case.ts, transition-session.use-case.ts Test: graph-projector.spec.ts (happy path of the four types; evidence→seq resolution of a hypothesis; GraphUnavailableError leaves the row unmarked and stops the cycle; the following cycle reprocesses successfully; reprocessing the SAME row twice doesn't duplicate in the graph); new tests in append-session-event.use-case.spec.ts/ transition-session.use-case.spec.ts (a projectable type writes the second row; a non-projectable type writes nothing extra) Origin: see ADR 0101
documents.s: RN-416 — The graph is DERIVED memory, rebuildable by projection from the outbox

documents.t: Psychologist.ContextBuilder/Anamnese.ContextBuilder keep reading what they always read (recent events / time window), and gain a SECOND source, EngineApiClient.rag_search/4, with a query derived from the analysis's TRIGGER — the already classified termination cause, in the Psicólogo; catalog competencies still without current_profile, in the Anamnese (NEVER free text of a hypothesis/rationale, by the already established prohibition on the Anamnese ever inferring health/personality/age/gender — the query only contains competency/member/project names). The hits enter the EXISTING Triage budget (max_prompt_events/max_payload_chars) — they take slots from the recents window, never adding outside it. The RAG call is strictly ADDITIVE: with no hit (RAG unavailable, error, or simply no result), the behavior is IDENTICAL to before this RN — no pre-existing test needed to change. degraded: true (RAG fell back to lexical-only for lack of embedding) appears EXPLICITLY in the final context, in both agents — never hidden by the ceiling cut. The kickoffs of the Psicólogo (psychologist-kickoff) and the Anamnese (anamnese-kickoff) now resolve as a graph TEMPLATE (EngineApiClient.get_prompt_template/2) when graph_templates_enabled? is on (GRAPH_TEMPLATES_ENABLED, default false) — with a mandatory fallback to the inline text on any failure (api down, template not seeded, flag off). :pinned => true stays the same on both paths. The THIRD consumer of the same flag is the ContextManager's summarization prompt (context-manager-summarize, the fourth and last template of the RN-413 batch — it was the only one still without a consumer, a gap that ADR 0101 declared open and that closes here). Same ruler, byte for byte: flag on tries the template and replaces {{turnos}} with the SAME <role>: <content> body the inline path already built; any outcome that isn't {"body" => corpo} with a non-empty binary body falls to the inline — WITHOUT an error and WITHOUT an error log, because flag off, template not yet seeded, and the graph api down are the SAME degradation path. With the flag off (the default) the api isn't even called. The render is its OWN private function, not a shared helper: the set of placeholders belongs to the template, not to the mechanism — each of the three consumers has its own. And the deterministic fallback for when the MODEL fails ("(N turnos anteriores omitidos)") is something else and does NOT go through any template: it's code behavior, not prompt text, and the template's own .md declares so. Since RN-621 the summary prompt, on both paths, asks that each turn keep its original language and that quotation and code not be translated; the versioned template went up to version "2". Consumption of the rest of the graph (query_user_context — hypotheses with evidence and profiles read DIRECTLY from Neo4j) stays DECLARED out of this delivery: still with no exposed HTTP route on the api side; Psicólogo/Anamnese today only query RAG (pgvector) via rag_search, not the relations graph itself. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/psychologist/context_builder.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine/workers/psychologist_worker.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/anamnese/context_builder.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine/workers/anamnese_worker.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/context_manager.ex (prompt/1, render_template/2, prompt_inline/1) Test: context_builder_test.exs of both agents (hits present; RAG failure degrades without error; degraded: true visible; top_k clamp; query derived from the trigger); psychologist_worker_test.exs/ anamnese_worker_test.exs (template with success and with fallback; :pinned identical on both paths; flag off never calls the api); context_manager_test.exs (template with {{turnos}} replaced; {:error, :not_found} falls to the inline and compaction ends normally; flag off never calls get_prompt_template) Origin: see ADR 0101
documents.s: RN-417 — Psicólogo and Anamnese query by relevance, with declared degradation to recency

documents.t: Revised by RN-713 (AT-385, 10/02): with automatic mode (the wildcard on auto_approve), push and PR are auto-approved. Revised by RN-689 (AT-347, owner's decision of 10/01): the ceiling below also applies to the TYPED actions git_push and pr_open, which until then only had the minimum role and were born auto_approved by the wildcard, by a specific rule, or by permissions.json. The rest of this entry still holds. Revises RN-106 by a GLOBAL and explicit decision of the product owner: git push, PR opening, deploy (the same prefix detection RN-106 already had), and sudo/doas (new — matched by VERB in comandoPrivilegiadoNoComando, scanning all segments of the command) stop being an unconditional deny and become an ABSOLUTE CEILING — unconditional require_approval, in the SAME final block and SAME code pattern as the other ceilings (protected merge, instruction_patch, parallelize/raise_max_parallel, path scope): current.policy === 'auto_approve' → overridden. Never auto-approvable by agent_autonomy (including automatic mode's "*" wildcard) nor by permissions.json. The condition that makes this safe — without which the ceiling would be decorative — is the half that closes "always allow" AT THE SOURCE: ApproveAlwaysActionUseCase/patternsForAction refuse to write a pattern into allow for a terminal action with a git external effect or a privileged command. The specific instance can still be approved through the normal flow (ApproveActionUseCase); only the click that would write a pattern forever is refused, with a clear message. It's the same argument the original RN-106 used to justify deny — resolved at the source, no longer blocking the symptom. An automatic security warning flagged this change during implementation (rewriting a rule the product documented as an absolute deny deserves scrutiny) — the product owner confirmed explicitly, after reviewing, that this was the decision. Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts (absolute ceilings block), apps/api/src/domain/actions/external-effect.ts (comandoPrivilegiadoNoComando, mensagemDeComandoPrivilegiado), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/approve-always-action.use-case.ts Test: decide.spec.ts (git push with auto mode "*" AND with allow matching in permissions.json resolve to require_approval; sudo likewise; the previous ceilings stay intact — complete regression); approve-always-action.use-case.spec.ts ("always allow" over git with external effect/sudo doesn't write a pattern; a common command keeps writing normally — regression); external-effect.spec.ts Origin: see ADR 0102
documents.s: RN-418 — Git external effect and privileged command (sudo/doas) become an absolute ceiling, never deny

documents.t: REVISED by RN-421 (ADR 0104): the ticket's refusal condition cited below (workspaceMode !== 'local') became executionMode !== 'runner' — same ruler, new name. The rest of this entry still holds as is. The terminal:<projectId> channel (new Phoenix socket, /runner) receives two distinct roles — :runner (the CLI on the user's machine, at most ONE per project, exclusivity guaranteed by :global.register_name/3) and :web (the Terminal tab, multiple simultaneous) — and both come in authenticated by a SINGLE-USE TICKET, the same security pattern as RN-108 (session socket ticket), with an ownership inversion: the ticket is ISSUED BY THE ENGINE (runner_socket_tickets, schema "engine", its own Ecto migration — not an extension of the session ticket table, which belongs to the api), and the API requests it via a new internal HTTP route (POST /internal/projects/:projectId/runner-tickets) — the inverse of the session ticket flow, where the api writes directly into its own table. POST /projects/:projectId/runner-ticket (role developer+, refuses if workspaceMode !== 'local') and POST /projects/:projectId/terminal-ticket (role viewer+, any mode) are the two public routes that issue the ticket to the right client — the runner asks for the first, the web asks for the second. The ticket is consumed (validation + single-use conditional UPDATE) at the channel's join; a ticket from ANOTHER project or reused never opens the topic. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/socket_ticket.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/registry.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/{runner_socket,terminal_channel}.ex; apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/runner-tickets.controller.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/runner/request-runner-ticket.use-case.ts Test: runner_socket_test.exs/terminal_channel_test.exs (join with a valid ticket succeeds; reused ticket refuses; a ticket from another project doesn't open the wrong topic; a second :runner on the same project is refused; a second runner manages to connect after the first drops); request-runner-ticket.use-case.spec.ts/ runner-tickets.controller.spec.ts (refuses for a non-local project on the runner ticket; the terminal ticket works for any mode) Origin: see ADR 0103
documents.s: RN-419 — The local runner authenticates with a single-use ticket, scoped to project and role

documents.t: REVISED by RN-423 (ADR 0104): the condition to route is no longer binary. workspace_mode == "local" became execution_mode == "runner" AND non-null workspace_verified_at AND runner connected — missing any of the THREE, the command is explicitly REFUSED, never falling into the System.cmd/bind-mount of mounted (which doesn't exist for a runner project, with no bind-mount at all). The rest of this entry — the usual approval pipeline, PTY as a user action — still holds as is. Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor decides to route a command to the runner (instead of the usual System.cmd, inside the container) AFTER the normal pipeline (decide()/proposed_action) has already approved — routing is only a choice of DESTINATION for the same already authorized command, never a second execution path escaping the policy (which keeps the absolute ceilings of RN-418 applying the same, sudo/git included). Condition to route (history, see revision above): workspace_mode == "local" AND runner connected (Engine.Runners.Registry.connected?/1) — without either of the two, the usual behavior continues (System.cmd in the container via bind-mount, ADR 0072 becomes the FALLBACK, never removed). Interactive PTY is DIFFERENT: it's an action of the authenticated USER typing in the terminal of their own machine, not the agent's — that's why it does NOT go through proposed_action. But it needs to leave a trace: pty_open/pty_close coming from the web emit terminal.session.started/terminal.session.ended in the event log (addressed to the project's most recent session, ProjectSession.latest_id/1, the same mechanism the Anamnese already uses to narrate something project-scoped). A real finding during consolidation: with no runner connected, the web needs an EXPLICIT pty_error back — discarding the request with only a log on the server would leave the tab stuck in "loading" forever, never reaching the "no runner" state the screen already knew how to show. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/actions/terminal_executor.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/runner_router.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel.ex Test: terminal_executor_test.exs (routes to the runner with local mode + runner connected; cwd is passed along; falls to the current path without a connected runner; never routes in container mode); terminal_channel_test.exs (pty_open without a connected runner returns pty_error to the web, never stays without an answer) Origin: see ADR 0103
documents.s: RN-420 — An agent command routed to the runner goes through the SAME approval pipeline; PTY is a user action, audited

documents.t: Found while navigating the product after a database reset: the dashboard's "New project"/"+" button did NOTHING, with no error at all. The root cause was in two layers. The visible one: Dashboard.tsx only opens the NewProjectWizard when useCurrentWorkspace() finds a workspace (list[0]?.workspace from GET /workspaces); with none, the click has nowhere to go. The deep one: RegisterUseCase created user and credential but NEVER a workspace, and the same held for SocialLoginCallbackUseCase in the branch that provisions a new account — EVERY new sign-up, by password or by social login, hit that wall. It just hadn't shown up before because db/seed.ts always creates a workspace along with the demo data, and no product screen calls createWorkspace (the route, the use case, and the HTTP client exist — they just have no caller at all in the UI).
documents.s: Automatic personal workspace on sign-up (RN-410)

documents.t: RegisterUseCase (e-mail/password registration) and SocialLoginCallbackUseCase (provisioning a new account via social login) create the workspace and add the user as owner — the same create/addMember pair that CreateWorkspaceUseCase already uses — inside the SAME transaction that already creates user and credential. It isn't a second call to the use case: that one opens its OWN transaction, and the point is that a user without a workspace never exists if something fails midway. Name and slug come from ONE pure function, nomeESlugDoWorkspacePessoal(nome, email, userId) (apps/api/src/domain/auth/personal-workspace.ts), reused by both creation points — so the rule doesn't diverge in two files, the same reason behind normalizarEmail/exigirSenhaValida living in the domain. The name uses the given nome (social login uses the provider's login), with the e-mail's local-part as a fallback when there's no name — it never invents either. The slug is kebab-case of the same text, ALWAYS suffixed with userId.slice(0, 8) (same pattern as extraDevAgentId/workspaceDirName/session label): workspaces.slug is UNIQUE in the database and nothing in the product does retry-on-conflict, so two sign-ups with an equal name or local-part would collide without the suffix. A name or e-mail with NO alphanumeric character degrades to the literal workspace-<8 chars>, never to an empty string. Where: apps/api/src/domain/auth/personal-workspace.ts (nomeESlugDoWorkspacePessoal), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/register.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/social-login-callback.use-case.ts (method provisionarContaNova) Test: apps/api/test/domain/auth/personal-workspace.spec.ts (name with/without nome, fallback to the e-mail's local-part, accent/uppercase becoming ASCII kebab-case, workspace-<id> fallback with no alphanumeric character at all, slug always unique thanks to the suffix); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/register.use-case.spec.ts (a new account gets a workspace with the user as owner, a duplicate e-mail doesn't create a second); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/ social-login-callback.use-case.spec.ts (same proof in the branch that provisions a new account via social login) ADR: none — the fix of a path that should have done this from the start, not a new structural decision Origin: found by real use, navigating the product — not a planned backlog item
documents.s: RN-410 — Every NEW account is born with a personal workspace, in the SAME transaction as the account

documents.t: ADR 0072 (RN-169/RN-170) and ADR 0103 (RN-419/RN-420) never talked to each other: the runner reused the same workspace_mode == 'local' flag without any bind-mount, so really using the runner still required going through the MOUNTED FOLDER validation. ADR 0104 reconciles the two. Migration 0048 recreates the enum (project_workspace_mode → project_execution_mode, local → mounted) in a single transaction — ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE can't be referenced in the same transaction where it was added — and adds workspace_verified_at (nullable).
documents.s: Wave 1 of ADR 0104 — execution_mode in three values, workspace verified by the runner

documents.t: projects.workspace_mode (two values) became projects.execution_mode (three): container (DEFAULT, unchanged), mounted (the old local, RENAMED — same behavior, same disk validation on creation), and runner (NEW: a user folder without bind-mount, confirmed by the brabo-runner CLI). The database CHECK became (execution_mode <> 'container') = (workspace_path IS NOT NULL) — it covers both non- container modes with the SAME condition, with no explicit OR per value. projectScopeRoot/Project.workspace_dir_name (api and engine) derive the root by the SAME rule in both non-container modes: the user's path is the root, distinguished from the managed folder name by the leading slash. What changes between mounted and runner isn't WHERE the root is — it's WHEN/WHO confirms that it really exists (RN-422/RN-423). Where: apps/api/src/db/migrations/0048_quiet_iron_fist.sql, apps/api/src/db/schema/iam.ts (projectExecutionModeEnum), apps/api/src/domain/iam/project.entity.ts (PROJECT_EXECUTION_MODES), apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts (projectScopeRoot), apps/engine/lib/engine/projects/project.ex Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.spec.ts (describe "projectScopeRoot nos modos mounted/runner"), apps/engine/test/engine/projects/project_test.exs Architectural decision: ADR 0104 Origin: reconciliation requested by the product owner, between ADRs 0072 and 0103
documents.s: RN-421 — execution_mode has THREE values: container/mounted/runner

documents.t: CreateProjectUseCase.caminhoValidado gained a third branch. mounted remains exactly as local was (RN-170, history): it refuses with 400 a path that doesn't exist, isn't a folder, or isn't writable inside the container, with the mounting instruction. runner validates only the LEXICON — the same list of prohibitions (absolute, no .., outside root/system folder, no overlap with Brabo's checkout) — without touching disk: only the runner, running on the real HOST, has the authority to confirm that the folder exists. The project is born with workspace_verified_at: null. caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido (the lexical predicate) was EXPORTED from project-workspaces-root.ts to be reused on both sides that need it without touching disk: the creation of a runner project and the runner's confirmation (RN-423) — the same function, never two copies that one day diverge. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/create-project.use-case.ts (caminhoValidado), apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts (caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido, exported), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/dto/create-project.dto.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/create-project-modo-de-workspace.spec.ts (runner block), apps/api/test/interfaces/http/iam/project-dto-modo-de-workspace.spec.ts, apps/web/src/lib/wizard.test.ts (canAdvanceFromWorkspace for runner) Architectural decision: ADR 0104 Origin: reconciliation of ADR 0104
documents.s: RN-422 — Creation validation DIVERGES by mode: mounted touches disk, runner only the lexicon

documents.t: The runner is the source of truth for a runner project's path, not what was typed in the wizard. Right after the Phoenix channel connects (terminal:<projectId>, :runner role), apps/runner/src/index.ts pushes workspace_confirm with the --dir it received on the command line. The engine passes it on (Engine.Sessions.EngineApiClient.confirm_workspace/4) to POST /internal/projects/:projectId/workspace-verification (ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase), which: Refuses with 400 if the project isn't in runner mode; Revalidates the path with the SAME lexical predicate as creation (RN-422) — even coming from the runner, system root and overlap with Brabo remain forbidden; OVERWRITES workspacePath with the normalized path and writes workspaceVerifiedAt = now() — without requiring equality with what was typed at creation: the runner rules; Is IDEMPOTENT — reconnecting reporting the SAME path rewrites nothing (changed: false); a DIFFERENT path rewrites, because the runner remains the source of truth at each reconnection; With no session in the project yet (ProjectSession.latest_id/1 returns nil): the UPDATE happens all the same, only the project.workspace_verified event (and the evidence for the workspace-verificado gate) is absent — the SAME degradation that pty_open/pty_close already accept (RN-108/RN-420). An accepted and declared gap, not a silent one. Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor.decisao_de_execucao/1 gained FOUR outputs, not two: runner with workspace_verified_at: nil refuses (:recusar_nao_verificado); verified runner without a connected runner refuses (:recusar_runner_desconectado); verified and connected runner routes (:rotear_runner); any other mode follows the usual path (:caminho_de_sempre). The two refusals NEVER fall into System.cmd — a runner project has no bind-mount, and "falling to the usual path" would be executing blindly in a folder the engine's process doesn't see. The same refusal applies in the race (Registry said connected at the start of run/3, but the runner dropped before the dispatch answered). Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/confirm-project-workspace.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/internal-projects.controller.ts (POST :projectId/workspace-verification), apps/engine/lib/engine/actions/terminal_executor.ex (decisao_de_execucao/1), apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel.ex (handle_in("workspace_confirm", ...)), apps/engine/lib/engine/sessions/engine_api_client.ex (confirm_workspace/4), apps/runner/src/channel.ts (enviarWorkspaceConfirm), apps/runner/src/index.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/confirm-project-workspace.use-case.spec.ts, apps/engine/test/engine/actions/terminal_executor_test.exs (describe "roteamento pro runner local"), apps/engine/test/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel_test.exs (describe "workspace_confirm"), apps/runner/src/channel.spec.ts (enviarWorkspaceConfirm after the join) Edge case: docs/gates.yml registers workspace-verificado as severidade: warn — what really locks is the engine's explicit refusal, the gate is only the record/evidence. Architectural decision: ADR 0104 Origin: reconciliation of ADR 0104, decision confirmed with the product owner (the runner is the source of truth; with no session, the UPDATE happens anyway; command explicitly refused without verification/connection)
documents.s: RN-423 — The runner CONFIRMS the path; without confirmation, the command is refused — it never falls into the container

documents.t: A Personal Access Token (brb_…) never authorizes any route other than POST /projects/:projectId/runner-ticket. The guarantee isn't an if that a new route could forget to check: it's structural. @RequirePatAuth() marks the handler with IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY; JwtAuthGuard (the global APP_GUARD) checks that metadata BEFORE trying JWT verify() and returns true without validating anything — the same bypass shape that IS_PUBLIC_KEY and IS_SERVICE_ROUTE_KEY already use. PatAuthGuard, applied only to that handler via @UseGuards(), is what actually authenticates: it extracts the bearer, refuses (401) any value not starting with brb_ without querying the repository — it never tries to validate as JWT on that route, and no other route accepts brb_… as a bearer. After PatAuthGuard populates request.user, RolesGuard/ ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase keep running, unchanged — belt and suspenders: if the PAT's owner loses sufficient role in the project through the normal path (ProjectMember/workspace), the token stops authorizing even without having been explicitly revoked. The alternative considered and refused: the global JwtAuthGuard recognizing the brb_ prefix and populating request.user directly, for ANY route. That would authorize the PAT for everything the user's role allows in the rest of the api — the "only asks for a runner ticket" scope would become decorative. Where: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/pat-route.decorator.ts (IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY/@RequirePatAuth()), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/jwt-auth.guard.ts (the third early-out), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/pat-auth.guard.ts (PatAuthGuard), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/runner-tickets.controller.ts (runnerTicket, the only marked handler) Test: apps/api/test/interfaces/pat-auth.guard.spec.ts, apps/api/test/interfaces/jwt-auth.guard.spec.ts (@RequirePatAuth() passes without trying verify()), apps/api/test/interfaces/http/runner/runner-tickets.controller.spec.ts (runnerTicket has the decorator, terminalTicket doesn't) Architectural decision: ADR 0105
documents.s: RN-424 — A PAT authenticates ONLY runner-ticket, by construction — never dual-auth with JWT on that route

documents.t: PersonalAccessTokenRepository.validarEUsar(hash) is ONE query: UPDATE personal_access_tokens SET last_used_at = now() WHERE token_hash = $1 AND revoked_at IS NULL AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now()) RETURNING id, user_id, project_id. Zero rows returns null, and the guard answers 401 for "doesn't exist", "revoked", and "expired" with the SAME message — whoever presents a stolen or expired token doesn't find out which of the three is the reason (same pattern as AccountTokenRepository.consumir()). Incorrect project scope is a DIFFERENT category: if the project_id returned by the query doesn't match the route's :projectId, it's 403, not 401 — the token really authenticated, it just has no right to THIS project. last_used_at is updated UNCONDITIONALLY, in the SAME validation query — never with a throttle (e.g. "only if last_used_at is NULL or older than 5 minutes") in the same WHERE. A throttle there is a real bug: a PAT presented twice in under 5 minutes would fall out of the WHERE the second time (because last_used_at would be "too fresh"), and the query would return zero rows for a valid token — rejecting a legitimate reconnection with 401. The runner's retry loop reconnects in seconds, not minutes. The cost of not throttling is a one-row UPDATE by unique index per call — irrelevant in the real worst case (up to 10 attempts in a row, the runner's ceiling). Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/personal-access-token.repository.ts (validarEUsar), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/pat-auth.guard.ts Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/personal-access-token.repository.spec.ts (nonexistent/revoked/expired → null; "toca last_used_at sempre que válido, sem throttle" — regression of the bug above), apps/api/test/interfaces/pat-auth.guard.spec.ts (wrong scope → 403, not 401) Architectural decision: ADR 0105
documents.s: RN-425 — PAT validation collapses nonexistent/revoked/expired into a single answer; wrong scope is 403; last_used_at is never throttled

documents.t: ListPersonalAccessTokensUseCase/RevokePersonalAccessTokenUseCase filter by userId inside the SQL query (WHERE user_id = $1 AND ...), never fetching everything and filtering afterwards in memory. Each user only sees and only revokes their OWN tokens — including within a project where they're maintainer. revogar(id, userId, motivo) is IDEMPOTENT: if the UPDATE (with the same WHERE user_id = $1) finds no row because it was already revoked, a second tie-breaking query returns the row (revoking again isn't an error); if it finds none because the token doesn't exist OR doesn't belong to the calling user, it returns null — the SAME answer (404 in the controller) for both cases, so as not to leak the existence of someone else's token through the status code. Closed by RN-427: a maintainer revoking another user's PAT — the incident response case (a dismissed dev with a leaking token) — which this section declared out of scope left the backlog and is implemented. This ruler (self-revocation, scope by userId) didn't change at all. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/list-personal-access-tokens.use-case.ts (ListPersonalAccessTokensUseCase), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/revoke-personal-access-token.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/personal-access-token.repository.ts (listarDoUsuarioNoProjeto, revogar) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/list-personal-access-tokens.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/revoke-personal-access-token.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/personal-access-token.repository.spec.ts (revoking another user's token → null) Architectural decision: ADR 0105
documents.s: RN-426 — Listing/revoking a PAT is scoped to the user's OWN tokens, in the query's WHERE — no cross-user admin in this wave

documents.t: An extension of RN-426's model, not a new architecture decision: the same pattern already used to close RN-407 (PO reading product metrics) over an already decided model, with no ADR of its own. It closes the cut that ADR 0105 declared "outside this wave" — real incident response (a dismissed dev with a leaking token), where waiting for the user themselves to revoke isn't an option. ListPersonalAccessTokensAsMaintainerUseCase/ RevokePersonalAccessTokenAsMaintainerUseCase are NEW use cases, on SEPARATE routes (GET .../personal-access-tokens/all, DELETE .../personal-access-tokens/:tokenId/admin, both @RequireRole('maintainer')) — never an if inside the self-service handlers, the same principle already used in the rest of the product for authorization by level (OfferInfraHandoffUseCase). The self-revocation route (RN-426) doesn't change at all. listarDoProjeto brings ALL of the project's tokens — with no userId filter — with an innerJoin on users for the owner's e-mail, the same pattern the project members listing already uses: without the e-mail, a maintainer seeing "revoke whose token?" would only have a raw UUID, and the item's very reason (incident response) asks to know WHO the owner is. revogarComoMaintainer(id, projectId, motivo) is the same idempotent design as revogar() — a conditional UPDATE followed by a tie-breaking SELECT when the UPDATE finds no row —, but the WHERE compares project_id, never user_id: a maintainer revokes any owner WITHIN their project, never a token of another project. With no row at all (the token doesn't exist OR belongs to another project), it returns null — the SAME answer (404) for both cases, the same discipline of not leaking existence that RN-426 already applied. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/list-personal-access-tokens-as-maintainer.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/revoke-personal-access-token-as-maintainer.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/personal-access-token.repository.ts (listarDoProjeto, revogarComoMaintainer), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/personal-access-tokens.controller.ts (listAllPats, revokePatAsMaintainer), apps/web/src/routes/settings/PersonalAccessTokensSection.tsx (sub-list visible only to owner/maintainer) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/list-personal-access-tokens-as-maintainer.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/revoke-personal-access-token-as-maintainer.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/personal-access-token.repository.spec.ts (listarDoProjeto/revogarComoMaintainer), apps/api/test/interfaces/http/runner/personal-access-tokens.controller.spec.ts, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSettingsTab.test.tsx Architectural decision: ADR 0105 (extension of the existing model, no new ADR)
documents.s: RN-427 — A maintainer revokes the PAT of ANY user of the project, scoped by project_id — incident response

documents.t: promocoesPendentes/the PO's promotion carousel (RN-148) no longer depends on a scan over the window of the last 200 events of useSessionEvents. The source of content/count is useBacklog (Story.proposedReady, per session, complete and without a window) — in a long session, backlog.story_promotion_proposed leaves the window while the story is still really pending, and before this the carousel shrank (or vanished) silently. The same class of bug that RN-180 already fixed for ContextAside. When the story isn't in the loaded backlog (query hasn't answered yet), it degrades story by story to the usual window scan. The anchoring in the timeline still comes from the event within the window when it exists; if the event that opened the batch has already left the window, the carousel anchors at the TOP of the visible stretch instead of vanishing — never hiding a real state because of a read cutoff. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (useMemo timeline) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.carrossel-janela-estourada.test.tsx ADR: none — a bug fix, the same class already fixed by RN-180 Origin: found by real use ("the chat failed to show the PO's carousel")
documents.s: RN-428 — The story promotion carousel survives the event window

documents.t: The terminal:<projectId> channel gains two events, in the SAME relay design as the PTY: fs_list_dir/fs_home_dir (:web asks, the engine relays DIRECTLY to the registered runner's pid, immediate error when there's no connected runner — it never waits for a response that won't come) and fs_list_dir_reply/fs_home_dir_reply (:runner answers, a broadcast filtered only to :web, correlated by a client-generated ref). The api does NOT gain any new route — it still doesn't enumerate the filesystem, the argument ADR 0072 had already fixed against a folder picker still stands. apps/runner/src/guard.ts (which restricts the cwd of an already approved command to the project root) on purpose does NOT apply to navigation — listing a directory is a free read on the user's machine, with the privileges they already have, and an entry without permission is skipped, it doesn't abort the whole listing. Declared gap: the channel's ticket is issued PER already existing PROJECT — on the project creation screen (NewProjectWizard.tsx), the project is only born on confirmation, so FolderBrowserModal receives projectId: null there and shows the declared state instead of trying an impossible connection; the free text field remains the manual path, as before. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel.ex; apps/runner/src/fs-browser.ts, apps/runner/src/channel.ts, apps/runner/src/index.ts; apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser-channel.ts, apps/web/src/components/FolderBrowserModal.tsx, apps/web/src/components/RunnerOnboardingPanel.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/code/TerminalPanel.tsx Test: terminal_channel_test.exs (pure web↔runner relay, immediate error without runner, wrong role ignored); fs-browser.spec.ts (ordering, empty/nonexistent folder/file, permission per entry); FolderBrowserModal.test.tsx (null projectId, navigation, selection, no runner); NewProjectWizard.test.tsx ("Browse folder..." button) ADR: 0107, revises 0072 without editing it Origin: product owner's request — "I couldn't link to a user folder"
documents.s: RN-429 — Local folder navigation is a pure relay through the Runner, never the api enumerating the container

documents.t: The prs tab resolves the defect of ProjectApprovalsTab.tsx, which scoped the "PRs in review" section to usePendingActions(projectId, latestSession?.id) — a pending review from a previous session disappeared as soon as a new session was born. The listing comes straight from the provider (GET /projects/:id/code/pull-requests, already project-wide by design); the crossing with the corresponding proposed_action (e.g. git_merge) uses ProposedActionRepository.findPendingByProject(projectId, actionType?), new, next to the already existing one scoped by session. The decision (approve/deny/always allow) uses the sessionId the ProposedAction itself carries, never latestSession — the action may have been born in a session different from the current one. The PRs tab is the first real producer of git_merge through the UI (actor.kind: 'user'); the protected branch lock in decide.ts (RN-154) remains absolute regardless of who proposes. git_merge gained its own body in the approval card instead of the raw JSON dump (the same defect that RN-096 already fixed for other types). Where: apps/api/src/application/ports/proposed-action-repository.port.ts, apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/proposed-action.repository.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/list-project-pending-actions.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/actions/project-actions.controller.ts (GET /projects/:projectId/actions?status=pending&actionType=), apps/web/src/routes/ProjectPrsTab.tsx, apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.tsx Test: list-project-pending-actions.use-case.spec.ts (a pending action from an old session found project-wide; filter by actionType; never returns a decided action); propose-action.use-case.spec.ts (git_merge with a real payload from the PRs tab stays pending even with GitMerge() in allow, and with the agent_autonomy wildcard on); ProjectPrsTab.test.tsx (PRs from multiple sessions appear together; the decision uses the action's sessionId, not the most recent session's); ApprovalCard.test.tsx (git_merge's own body) ADR: none — extension of an already existing read path, without changing the decision pipeline Origin: product owner's request — "there are no ways to manage PRs"
documents.s: RN-430 — PRs are project-wide; the decision uses the action's own sessionId, never the most recent one

documents.t: contagens.arquiteturaPendente (tab ruler) comes from architecture.pendencies.length (story↔module cross-validation divergence), not from c4Diagram.status === 'sem_diagrama'. The other three counts of the ruler (promocoesPendentes, aprovacoesPendentes, hipotesesPendentes) all mean "something is waiting for YOUR decision" — generating the diagram is the Arquiteto's work, not the user's decision queue, and badging for it would be noise. Where: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectPage.tsx Test: ProjectPage.test.tsx ADR: none Origin: design decision made when extracting the Architecture tab from the Overview
documents.s: RN-431 — The Architecture tab badge counts pending validation items, never "diagram not generated"

documents.t: Revised by RN-891: the column also accepts ru and zh-Hans, and the web's default went from en to pt-BR (ADR 0216). Foundation of the interface's i18n (Wave 6a of a larger program — the mass extraction of the rest of the app's strings is a separate stage, in parallel). A locale column in users ('pt-BR' | 'en', default 'pt-BR' — never silently flips whoever already has an account). EmitirSessaoUseCase is the ONLY point that issues a session (login, refresh, social login) — locale embedded in the body of /auth/login//auth/refresh from it, with no additional round-trip. GET/PATCH /users/me/preferences exists as a REDUNDANT path, for AccountPage to reassert the value without waiting for the next refresh. en is the app's DEFAULT language from now on (react-i18next, a new dependency — the same "a new dependency needs a justification" ruler that mermaid/@xterm/xterm already followed); pt-BR remains available. apps/web/src/lib/idioma.ts (same design as tema.ts): the SERVER is the source of truth, localStorage['brabo.locale'] is only a cache to avoid a flash of the wrong language on the first paint. A user without an account yet uses navigator.language only as a DISPLAY suggestion, never persisting anything before an account exists. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/emitir-sessao.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/user-preferences.controller.ts, apps/web/src/lib/idioma.ts, apps/web/src/lib/i18n.ts, apps/web/src/routes/AccountPage.tsx Test: apps/web/src/lib/idioma.test.ts, apps/web/src/routes/AccountPage.test.tsx, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/*.spec.ts, apps/api/test/interfaces/route-surface.spec.ts ADR: none — an additive extension of an already existing choke point, without changing the session format for anyone who doesn't use the new field Origin: product owner's request — interface and docs in English by default, with Portuguese preserved
documents.s: RN-432 — The language preference comes in the login/refresh payload, never in an extra call

documents.t: Found testing a new project in runner mode (ADR 0103/0104) and opening Code → Dev → Terminal: the screen never left the loading skeleton, and the console showed socket do terminal com erro/socket do terminal fechado in a loop, with growing backoff until stabilizing at ~5-6s — the pattern of the phoenix.js DEFAULT backoff.
documents.s: Local runner terminal stuck at "Opening terminal..." forever (RN-433)

documents.t: Three stacked defects. The first two were found investigating the symptom; the THIRD only showed up after fixing the first two — without them, the browser never reached the engine to reveal the path bug underneath. Fixing only one leaves the others standing: ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL (RN-419) never had any default in docker/docker-compose.yml — only ENGINE_URL (http://engine:4000, a hostname that ONLY resolves inside the Compose network). The code's fallback (process.env.ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL ?? process.env.ENGINE_URL ?? …, request-runner-ticket.use-case.ts) silently fell to the wrong value, and the browser tried to open a WebSocket against a hostname it never resolves. docker/docker-compose.yml gained ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL: ${ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL:-http://localhost:4000} in the api service — the SAME default VITE_ENGINE_URL already uses in the web service, for the same reason. Even with the right URL, a transport that NEVER opens (engine down, firewall, a wrong future reconfiguration) had no ceiling at all: apps/web/src/lib/terminal-channel.ts never passed reconnectAfterMs to the Socket, so phoenix.js fell into its DEFAULT backoff and kept trying to reconnect on its own forever — the module's own docblock already declared the intent of "no automatic reconnection" (same ruler as session-channel.ts/RN-108), but it was never fulfilled in practice. Without onError/onClose calling handlers.onErro, TerminalPanel stayed stuck in 'carregando' (RN-088 — every screen distinguishes loading/error/ empty — silently violated). Fixed with reconnectAfterMs returning a value that practically never fires (24h, same pattern as session-channel.ts) and an OWN 8s timeout (TIMEOUT_CONEXAO_MS): if onOpen doesn't fire before that, the module calls handlers.onErro with an actionable message and disconnects. The defect that actually prevented the connection, masked by the two above: terminal-channel.ts concatenated '/runner/websocket' to an engineWsUrl the api already returns READY — ws://host:porta/runner (engineWsUrlPublico()) —, and phoenix.js's OWN Socket also appends /websocket by itself in the constructor (this.endPoint = ${endPoint}/websocket). The result hit the engine as GET /runner/runner/websocket/websocket, which Phoenix.Router.NoRouteError refuses — confirmed in the engine's log (docker logs brabo-engine-1) during the end-to-end verification of this fix. apps/runner/src/channel.ts (the CLI side) already did it right — it passes engineWsUrl straight to the Socket, without touching it — and the terminal-channel.ts test never caught it because the mock of getTerminalTicket used an engineWsUrl (http://engine.local, without /runner) that doesn't reflect the api's real contract; fixed along with it. Fix: terminal-channel.ts now uses engineWsUrl (only with the defensive .replace(/^http/, 'ws')) directly, without concatenating any path. Verified END TO END against exp001 (runner mode, without a real brabo-runner connected): before the fix, the tab spun forever; after, the engine's log shows CONNECTED TO EngineWeb.RunnerSocket → JOINED terminal:<projectId> → pty_resize descartado — sem runner conectado, and the screen shows RunnerOnboardingPanel with the brabo-runner command in under 1s — never item 2's 8s timeout, which remains as a safety net for the case of the engine being genuinely down. Where: docker/docker-compose.yml, .env.example, apps/web/src/lib/terminal-channel.ts Test: apps/web/src/lib/terminal-channel.test.ts (a socket that never opens calls onErro within the timeout, without phoenix's automatic reconnection; the mock's engineWsUrl fixed to reflect the real contract — already with /runner, without /websocket — and the happy path assertion now requires the URL used in the Socket EQUAL to the ticket's engineWsUrl, with no concatenation) ADR: none — a bug fix restoring the behavior that ADR 0103/0104 and the module's own docblock already declared as intent Origin: found manually testing a new project in runner mode; item 3 only showed up when verifying the fix of items 1/2 end to end in the browser against the real engine
documents.s: RN-433 — The terminal socket gives up after a timeout, the ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL default is reachable BY THE BROWSER, and the endpoint doesn't duplicate the path

documents.t: The brabo-runner CLI (runner mode, ADR 0103/0104) only validated that --dir exists and is a folder — with no restriction at all on WHERE that folder could be in the file system. lerArgumentos() (apps/runner/src/index.ts) now calls validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux(dir, process.platform, homedir()) (apps/runner/src/guard.ts) right after the existence check: on Linux (process.platform === 'linux'), --dir is only accepted inside os.homedir() — the $HOME itself or any subfolder of it; a path outside that tree (/etc, /root, /, or even another account in /home) is refused with process.exit(2) and a message explaining the reason and showing the expected home. Outside Linux (macOS, Windows) the behavior doesn't change — the restriction is Linux-only. The check reuses dentroDoEscopo/semBarraFinal, the same path comparison primitives that validarCwdDentroDaRaiz already uses in the same module, but is deliberately simpler than it: no realpath nor TOCTOU/symlink protection, because it doesn't protect against a malicious SERVER (that's the role of validarCwdDentroDaRaiz, exercised on each exec) — it's a STARTUP check of the local CLI itself, guiding the user who typed a wrong path when bringing up the runner. Where: apps/runner/src/guard.ts (DirForaDoHomeError/validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux), apps/runner/src/index.ts (lerArgumentos) Test: apps/runner/src/guard.spec.ts (describe('validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux', …) — accepts the home itself and a subfolder of it on Linux, refuses a path outside home and another account inside /home on Linux, and confirms the restriction does NOT apply outside Linux) ADR: 0104 (additive extension — the runner was already declared "source of truth of the path"; this rule only narrows what it accepts as --dir on Linux) Origin: explicit request from the product owner, during a real project creation test (an attempt to point --dir at a path outside home, /home/dev/exp001, which didn't exist on the machine — it led to the decision to lock paths outside $HOME on Linux)
documents.s: RN-434 — On Linux, the local runner's --dir is only accepted inside the user's $HOME

documents.t: The brabo-runner CLI (runner mode, ADR 0103/0104) refused with process.exit(2) any --dir that didn't yet exist on disk — the project folder had to be created manually before bringing up the CLI. garantirDiretorio() (apps/runner/src/guard.ts) now creates the folder automatically (mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })) when it doesn't exist, and lerArgumentos() (apps/runner/src/index.ts) calls that function RIGHT AFTER validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux (RN-434) — the ORDER is the rule: the $HOME check works on a path that doesn't exist yet (only resolve(), without touching disk), so it runs first and keeps refusing --dir outside home on Linux even when it doesn't exist yet, BEFORE any creation attempt — creating first would reopen the hole that RN-434 had just closed. --dir pointing to an already existing FILE remains a real error (DirNaoEUmaPastaError, process.exit(2), without trying to create anything) — this CLI never overwrites a file silently. A failure in the creation itself (permission denied, disk full, etc.) also refuses (NaoConsegiuCriarDiretorioError), with the original error's message embedded. Where: apps/runner/src/guard.ts (garantirDiretorio/DirNaoEUmaPastaError/NaoConsegiuCriarDiretorioError), apps/runner/src/index.ts (lerArgumentos) Test: apps/runner/src/guard.spec.ts (describe('garantirDiretorio', …) — does nothing when the folder already exists, creates recursively when it doesn't, refuses without creating when the path already exists and is a file, and wraps a mkdir failure in NaoConsegiuCriarDiretorioError; and one more case in describe('validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux', …) proving that a --dir outside home and NOT YET EXISTING stays refused, confirming that the order of the two checks opens no hole) ADR: 0104 (additive extension — it doesn't change the design of the runner as source of truth of the path, it only reduces the friction of bringing up a new project) Origin: product owner's request, upon noticing that the folder of a new project in runner mode didn't exist on the machine and needed to be created manually before running the CLI — the same scenario that motivated RN-434 (nonexistent /home/dev/exp001), now solved by creating the folder instead of just refusing
documents.s: RN-435 — A nonexistent local runner --dir is created, not refused

documents.t: resolve(dirBruto) in lerArgumentos() resolved a relative --dir against process.cwd() — correct when the CLI runs directly (standalone binary, npm install -g @brabo/runner), but WRONG in the only invocation path that exists today without a real npm publication (a real finding, ADR 0106/backlog): pnpm --filter runner start REBASES process.cwd() to the PACKAGE's folder (apps/runner), not the folder from which the user typed the command. pnpm --filter runner start -- --dir ../exp001, run from ~/dev/brabo, created ~/dev/brabo/apps/exp001 instead of ~/dev/exp001 — silently, with no error, because RN-435 already makes a nonexistent --dir get created instead of refused. resolverDir() (apps/runner/src/guard.ts) resolves against INIT_CWD when present — the variable that npm/pnpm ALWAYS defines with the original invocation folder, existing only when the process is born from a package.json script — and falls back to process.cwd() when absent (direct binary, where it's already the right folder). Node's resolve() already ignores the base when dirBruto is absolute, so an absolute path (the case documented in the README) doesn't change behavior. Where: apps/runner/src/guard.ts (resolverDir), apps/runner/src/index.ts (lerArgumentos) Test: apps/runner/src/guard.spec.ts (describe('resolverDir', …) — relative against INIT_CWD when present, falls back to the process's cwd when absent, absolute ignores both bases) ADR: 0104 (additive extension, same category as RN-435 — it reduces invocation friction, it doesn't change the runner as source of truth of the path) Origin: found in real use, running pnpm --filter runner start -- dir ../exp001 from inside the monorepo checkout — the only invocation path available today, because @brabo/runner hasn't really been published on npm yet (NPM_TOKEN pending, see ADR 0106's backlog)
documents.s: RN-453 — A relative local runner --dir resolves against INIT_CWD, not against pnpm's rebased cwd

documents.t: Two changes requested by the product owner after testing the creation of a real project: (1) the existing folder browser (FolderBrowserModal) was a simple list with a breadcrumb, when the visual reference he sent (a GNOME Files/GTK-style picker, with three columns) already existed as a ready design handoff to adapt; (2) "Browse folder..." didn't work on the project's CREATION SCREEN — only after it was created — because the Runner channel's ticket (ADR 0107) is anchored to a projectId that, until this fix, was only born on confirmation.
documents.s: The Runner's folder explorer becomes three columns, and creating a runner project no longer waits for the final step (RN-436/436)

documents.t: The single-list layout became three columns inside the Modal size="full": shortcuts (Home folder, which calls diretorioInicial(); Root, /), the central list with breadcrumb, and a details panel on the right. The protocol (FsEntrada, in apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser-channel.ts) only has { nome, isDir } — no size nor modification date — and wasn't extended (it would touch apps/engine/apps/runner, outside the scope of this delivery); the details panel only shows what can be derived client-side: name, type, and the item count when the displayed item is the ALREADY OPEN folder (never of a merely selected folder, which would require an extra call to the runner). The TWO gestures that were previously fused into a single click (which already navigated into the folder) were separated: one click now only SELECTS (highlights the item and updates the details panel) and a double click ENTERS. The final button ("Use this folder", renamed from "Select this folder" — the folderBrowserModal.select key of pt-BR/en changed along with it) uses the selected item when there is one (selected.kind === 'dir' ? join(path, selected.name) : path) or the currently open folder when there's none. The list stopped filtering files — the whole listing appears now, with files rendered as <div aria-disabled> instead of <button>: visually dimmed and with no gesture at all, because only folders remain navigable/selectable. Where: apps/web/src/components/FolderBrowserModal.tsx, FolderBrowserModal.module.css, apps/web/src/locales/{pt-BR,en}/terminal.json Test: apps/web/src/components/FolderBrowserModal.test.tsx — a single click selects without calling listarDiretorio again; a double click navigates; a file appears in the list but isn't reachable by getByRole('button'); "Home folder"/"Root" shortcuts; and "Use this folder" uses the selected one when there is one, otherwise the open folder ADR: none — a UI redesign over a component that already existed, with no protocol change nor data boundary change (ADR 0107 still describes the mechanism behind it) Origin: product owner's request, after testing the creation of a real project and finding the folder browser not much like a real file explorer — a visual reference sent by him (three-column picker, GNOME Files/GTK style)
documents.s: RN-436 — FolderBrowserModal becomes a three-column explorer: shortcuts, a list where one click selects/double click enters, and a details panel

documents.t: ADR 0107 had already declared this gap in its own Consequences section: with no project yet, the channel's ticket (RN-429) has nothing to anchor to, and "Browse folder..." always fell into the "available after the project exists" state — even in runner mode, where creation does NOT depend on validating disk (ADR 0104, item 2). Closed by ADR 0108: NewProjectWizard.tsx (handleProcurarPasta) calls createProject when clicking "Browse folder..." when modoDeWorkspace === 'runner' — using the already typed path, or a lexically valid and clearly provisional placeholder (/workspace-a-confirmar) when the field is still empty, never blocking the click. mounted mode doesn't change: it keeps projectId={null} until confirmation, because there disk validation runs on creation and creating early with an empty path would return RN-422's refusal at a moment when the user hasn't even thought about a path yet. An identity SNAPSHOT ({ name, externalId, adotando } — never caminhoLocal, whose refinement is the PURPOSE of browsing) decides when to reuse: clicking "Browse folder..." again with the identity intact reopens the modal with the SAME project, without creating another; changing the name (or going back and swapping the repository to adopt) invalidates the snapshot, and the next browse creates a new project. handleConfirm applies the same ruler — it reuses the project already created when browsing when the snapshot still matches, and only calls createProject when there's nothing to reuse. montarPayloadDeCriacao, a pure function extracted from what used to live only inside handleConfirm, is reused by both paths. The button's prerequisite is stated BEFORE the click (AT-214): in this mode the list comes from the local agent, so without a brabo-runner running and connected to the newly created project the modal can only show the wait and the onboarding. The screen now says so in TEXT below the field (aviso-procurar-runner, ADR 0064 — never a tooltip), with the command brabo-runner --project <id> --dir <pasta> and the alternative that depends on nothing: typing the path in the field, which the runner confirms on connecting. The mechanism (the early creation, the transport through the local agent) didn't change. Where: apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.tsx (handleProcurarPasta, handleConfirm, montarPayloadDeCriacao, snapshotDeIdentidade/mesmaIdentidade) Test: apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.test.tsx, describe navegação de pasta antecipada no modo Runner — creates the project and opens the modal with the real id; uses the placeholder when the field is empty; clicking again without changing anything doesn't create another; changing the name invalidates the snapshot and creates a different project; handleConfirm reuses instead of duplicating. The preexisting test "'Procurar pasta...' mostra o estado declarado" (mounted mode) stays green, unchanged — it proves the scope didn't leak ADR: 0108 — a structural change (WHEN a project comes to exist in the creation flow), with the accepted side effect of an orphan "not provisioned" project when the wizard is closed without finishing (the SAME state that any interrupted creation already produces today, not a new regression) Origin: product owner's request, after testing the creation of a real project in Runner mode and not being able to browse folders before confirming — the gap ADR 0107 had already declared and postponed
documents.s: RN-437 — In runner mode, "Browse folder..." creates the project IN ADVANCE, and the final confirmation reuses it by identity SNAPSHOT

documents.t: Found while verifying RN-437 end to end in Chrome, against the real engine: the modal opened with the right projectId, but the connection dropped immediately with "The connection to the runner dropped — close and reopen to try again." instead of showing RunnerOnboardingPanel. apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser-channel.ts concatenated '/runner/websocket' to an engineWsUrl the api already returns READY (ws://host:porta/runner, from engineWsUrlPublico()) — the same phoenix.js Socket also appends /websocket on its own in the constructor, and the result hit the engine as GET /runner/runner/websocket/websocket, which Phoenix.Router.NoRouteError refuses. It's EXACTLY item 3 of RN-433, only in the SIBLING module — the fix there had never been replicated here, and no suite caught it because this module had no test at all until now (its own docblock said, incorrectly, that terminal-channel.test.ts covered it "indirectly"). Fix: the same line as RN-433 — engineWsUrl.replace(/^http/, 'ws'), without concatenating any path. Verified END TO END against a real runner project (owner logged in, teste-navegacao, created by RN-437): before the fix, the modal fell straight into the connection error; after, it shows RunnerOnboardingPanel with the command brabo-runner --project <id-real> --dir <pasta> in under 2s — the expected result without a real runner connected. Where: apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser-channel.ts Test: apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser-channel.test.ts (new — the module had no test of its own at all until this fix). The happy path confirms socket.url === engineWsUrl without concatenation; plus diretorioInicial/listarDiretorio roundtrip, failure fetching the ticket, and idempotent fechar() ADR: none — it restores the behavior that ADR 0103/0107 and RN-433 already declared as intent, only in a module the previous fix didn't reach Origin: found manually testing RN-437 (early creation of a runner project) against Chrome and the real engine — the first time FolderBrowserModal was exercised end to end against a real connection, because before this delivery "Browse folder..." never reached a real project before confirmation
documents.s: RN-438 — fs-browser-channel.ts had the SAME duplicated-path bug that RN-433 had already fixed in its sibling terminal-channel.ts

documents.t: POST /projects/:projectId/runner-ticket answered 403 "Não autenticado" for EVERY PAT, even a valid one, freshly issued, scoped to the right project — found in a LIVE verification of brabo-runner connecting to a real project, never by an automated test. Root cause: JwtAuthGuard and RolesGuard are the two APP_GUARDs — GLOBAL — and a global guard ALWAYS runs BEFORE a route's LOCAL guard (@UseGuards), regardless of the order of the decorators in the controller. JwtAuthGuard already knew how to abstain on this route (the IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY bypass already existed, without populating request.user, counting on PatAuthGuard to authenticate afterwards); RolesGuard didn't, and refused every call with request.user still empty — PatAuthGuard never got to run. The controller's comment described the order backwards ("RolesGuard runs AFTER PatAuthGuard"), and it never was so. The fix followed the SAME pattern JwtAuthGuard already used for this problem: RolesGuard gained the twin bypass (IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY → returns true without checking request.user), delegating the entire authorization to whoever becomes the ONLY guard running after request.user is populated on this route — PatAuthGuard itself, which now also reads @RequireRole (via Reflector) and resolves the effective role (ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject), refusing with the SAME message RolesGuard would use ("Papel insuficiente para esta ação"). The logic is duplicated between the two guards ON PURPOSE — RolesGuard lives in iam, PatAuthGuard lives in auth, and a cross dependency just to reuse ~10 lines wouldn't be worth it. A SECOND defect was hidden behind the first, and only showed up when the integration test started exercising the two guards TOGETHER: PatAuthGuard compared the RAW token directly against personal_access_tokens.token_hash in validarEUsar — which always expects the HASH (hashDeToken, HMAC-SHA256+ pepper, the same one TokenFactory/IssuePersonalAccessTokenUseCase use to write). Fixed to this.tokens.validarEUsar(hashDeToken(token)). While RolesGuard refused everything before, this second bug never got to manifest — fixing only the first would have swapped an always-403 for an always-401, and the runner would still never really connect. Where: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/roles.guard.ts (the IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY bypass); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/pat-auth.guard.ts (authorization by role + token hash); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/runner-http.module.ts (IamUseCasesModule imported, for the ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase that PatAuthGuard now needs); comment fixed in apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/runner-tickets.controller.ts Test: apps/api/test/interfaces/pat-auth.guard.spec.ts (authorization by role in isolation + token hash); apps/api/test/interfaces/roles.guard.spec.ts (IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY bypass); apps/api/test/interfaces/http/runner/runner-tickets.guards.integration.spec.ts (NEW — brings up JwtAuthGuard+RolesGuard+PatAuthGuard in a real Nest, with supertest, in the SAME relative order as AppModule: it's the test that was missing, because each guard was only exercised in isolation before this). Also verified LIVE: brabo-runner really connected to a real runner project with a PAT issued after the fix ADR: 0105 — a bug fix in the implementation of the decision already made there (PAT authenticates this route), not a new decision Origin: found running brabo-runner for real against a real project and isolating with curl directly — never by an automated test, because no suite exercised RolesGuard and PatAuthGuard in the same request
documents.s: RN-439 — POST .../runner-ticket authenticates AND authorizes in the SAME guard; RolesGuard (global) abstains on an @RequirePatAuth() route

documents.t: Closes the "budget per area" item of ADR 0038's cut, open since PHASE 8. agent_areas gains budget_micros (nullable — null is NO CEILING, the default) and spent_micros (NOT NULL DEFAULT 0), mirroring exactly max_parallel: same row, same decision owner, same AgentAreaRepository. It's not the model binding cascade of ADR 0064 (session > agent > area > project > workspace, "the most specific wins") — the two mechanisms use the word "area" and have nothing else in common. The area budget is a THIRD independent ceiling alongside the project and session ones that already existed: CheckBudgetGateUseCase.execute now resolves the agentId's area (via areaDo, a pure function, without touching the database unless it finds a match) and checks all three in parallel — any one blocked already refuses the call, with no hierarchy among them. RecordLlmUsageUseCase increments the actor's area spent_micros WHENEVER it belongs to one (lead or member — areaDo returns an area for both), with or without a configured budget_micros: the area's real spend becomes visible even before anyone configures a ceiling. An actor without an area (user in the chat, agent outside any area) records nothing — it isn't a silent omission, it's the correct behavior when there's nothing to increment. SetAreaBudgetUseCase requires maintainer (same ruler as SetAreaMaxParallelUseCase — changing how much the product can spend without asking), converts dollar→micro-USD in the controller (same convention as BudgetsController) and emits no domain event (project config, with no session to record into — the same reasoning already recorded in SetAreaMaxParallelUseCase). null CLEARS the ceiling — a required field that accepts null as a valid value (ValidateIf, not IsOptional), the same pattern as RenameSessionDto. Where: apps/api/src/db/schema/agents.ts (agentAreas, columns budgetMicros/spentMicros and the two CHECKs); apps/api/src/domain/llm/area-budget.ts (isAreaBudgetExceeded); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/llm/check-budget-gate.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/llm/record-llm-usage.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/execution/set-area-budget.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/agent-area.repository.ts (setBudget/incrementSpent); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/execution/execution.controller.ts (PUT agent-areas/:key/budget); apps/web/src/routes/settings/BudgetSection.tsx Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/llm/check-budget-gate.use-case.spec.ts (describe budget de área — aditivo, não cascata: an exceeded area blocks with project/session OK and vice versa, no ceiling never blocks, an agent without an area isn't affected); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/llm/record-llm-usage.use-case.spec.ts (describe gasto por área: increments for the member and the lead, does nothing harmful without an area, adds up with no ceiling configured); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/execution/set-area-budget.use-case.spec.ts (writes, clears with null, refuses negative/NaN/Infinity, zero is valid); apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/agent-area.repository.spec.ts (setBudget/incrementSpent, atomicity under concurrency) ADR: 0110 Origin: backlog item approved by the product owner in an explicit planning session — docs/explanation/backlog.md, "Older backlog" table
documents.s: RN-443 — Area budget is ADDITIVE to the project/session ones, never a cascade; only maintainer changes the ceiling

documents.t: Manual handoff to an agent of choice (backlog, ADR 0109): assertHandoffTargetAllowed (ADR 0038) only refuses an area SUBAGENT — an agent citing "abc" as a target would pass through it without error, because an AGENT only cites targets it already knows from its own instruction. That stops being true when whoever chooses is a HUMAN, in a <select> fed by a client that may diverge from the backend. addressableAgents() (apps/api/src/domain/agents/agent-areas.ts) is the CLOSED catalog — area leads (AGENT_AREAS.map(a => a.lead)) ∪ SOLO_CONVERSATIONAL_AGENTS (criativo, po, arquiteto, ux-designer, staff) — and RequestManualHandoffUseCase refuses with 400 any toAgent outside it, BEFORE calling CreateHandoffUseCase. SOLO_CONVERSATIONAL_AGENTS is its OWN list, not derived from the apps/web/src/lib/agents.ts roster (which also lists gate agents and the Psicólogo/Anamnese, none addressable by handoff). The direction of the derivation is from the api to the web: since AT-046 the web's copy is no longer a MANUAL mirror and comes out of the SAME generator as the areas (pnpm --filter api gerar:areas, Phase 18), in apps/web/src/lib/agent-areas.generated.ts, which agents.ts only reexports. agent-areas.spec.ts fails when the disk diverges from what the generator produces, and the generated list comes out as const satisfies readonly AgentKey[] — a name the web's roster doesn't know breaks the web's build. The engine does NOT receive the list (there's no consumer there). Even with both copies locked, what decides what's accepted is still RequestManualHandoffUseCase.
