Where: apps/api/src/domain/agents/agent-areas.ts (addressableAgents, SOLO_CONVERSATIONAL_AGENTS); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/agents/request-manual-handoff.use-case.ts; apps/api/scripts/gerar-areas.ts (renderWeb, which writes the list into the web); apps/web/src/lib/agent-areas.generated.ts (GENERATED copy, reexported by apps/web/src/lib/agents.ts) Test: apps/api/test/domain/agents/agent-areas.spec.ts (describe('addressableAgents (ADR 0109)') and describe('a lista solo sai do gerador para o web (AT-046)'), plus the freshness check of the web's file); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/agents/request-manual-handoff.use-case.spec.ts (refuses a subagent AND refuses an unknown agent); apps/web/src/lib/agents.test.ts ADR: 0109 Origin: team model backlog — an item open since PHASE 13c, closed by the real case of the Staff (ADR 0088) and of the UX Designer (ADR 0087), both with engine plumbing ready and no human path to them
documents.s: RN-440 — addressableAgents() is the CLOSED catalog of the manual handoff, stricter than assertHandoffTargetAllowed

documents.t: The only path to write toAgent is still CreateHandoffUseCase (ADR 0038) — not a second mechanism. RequestManualHandoffUseCase resolves fromAgent on its own (the session's most RECENT agent.activated, via SessionEventRepository.listByTypeInSession — the same criterion as activeAgent in SessionPage.tsx, finding 9-fix; a session with no agent activated yet falls to the "usuario" sentinel, never a guessed name) and calls CreateHandoffUseCase.execute passing actor: {kind: 'user', id: userId} — CreateHandoffInput gained the optional field actor?: Actor for that, with default {kind:'agent', id: fromAgent} preserving the usual behavior for the internal caller (the engine). The handoff is born offered, the SAME way as an automatic one, and the already existing accept card (offeredHandoff/handleAcceptHandoff in SessionPage.tsx) picks it up on its own on the next useHandoffs poll — with NO change to the accept path. (It didn't pick it up, and nobody saw it until AT-253: the card matched the offer by ACTOR, and the manual one's actor is the person. Fixed in RN-631, which matches by handoffId.) The route (POST projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId/handoffs) requires the developer role, the same as handoffs/:handoffId/accept (RN-136: those who CONVERSE on this screen). ux-designer and staff entered AGENTES_DE_CHAT (SessionPage.tsx) in the same change — the two message/2 clauses already existed in agent_command_controller.ex (ADR 0087/0088), verified by reading BEFORE writing any web line, and neither of them had a human path to itself. Where: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/agents/agents.controller.ts (requestManual); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/agents/dto/request-manual-handoff.dto.ts; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/agents/create-handoff.use-case.ts (actor?: Actor); apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (AGENTES_DE_CHAT, .manualHandoffRow, handleRequestManualHandoff); apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts (requestManualHandoff) Test: apps/api/test/interfaces/http/agents/agents.controller.spec.ts (required role); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/agents/request-manual-handoff.use-case.spec.ts (derived fromAgent, "usuario" sentinel, actor: user); docs/security-surface.md + apps/api/test/interfaces/route-surface.spec.ts (role:developer classification at runtime) ADR: 0109 Origin: team model backlog (see RN-440)
documents.s: RN-441 — POST .../sessions/:sessionId/handoffs requires developer; a manual handoff is born offered, with no new state

documents.t: ConvertProjectExecutionModeUseCase (PUT .../execution-mode, role maintainer) reads engine.dev_agent_states DIRECTLY (cross-schema, same physical database — the same path as RN-409) by project_id, across ALL of the project's sessions, not only the most recent one. Any status other than idle (working/blocked/idle_tripped/awaiting_gate/ awaiting_approval) refuses the conversion: Engine.Dev.DevAgentServer does NOT re-resolve the worktree on its own — workspace_root is captured ONCE, at the worktree's creation, and swapping the column underneath it would leave the agent writing in a scope that permissions.json and the terminal policy (ADR 0055) have already abandoned. The decision is to REFUSE and explain (same "refuse and teach" pattern as RN-088/RN-422) — never to drain or force the migration of a live agent. idle_tripped counts as ACTIVE here, unlike RN-409 (which excludes it from onlineAgentCount): the two questions are different — "is someone watching this agent work now" (RN-409) versus "is there a scope pointer that would become stale" (here). An agent with the circuit breaker tripped still has workspace_root captured, waiting for human unblocking — it isn't "idle" for conversion purposes, even though it isn't "online" for counting purposes. The same (mode, path) as today is a NO-OP: the dev agent check doesn't even run — resubmitting the form without changing anything shouldn't cost a sweep of active agents. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/application/ports/dev-agent-activity.port.ts; apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/dev-agent-activity.repository.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.spec.ts (refuses with an active dev agent, writing nothing; a no-op doesn't check); apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/dev-agent-activity.repository.spec.ts (idle doesn't count, everything else counts, isolation between projects) ADR: 0111 Origin: a fix recorded in docs/explanation/backlog.md during the implementation of Wave 1 of the runner (ADR 0104), closed in this Wave 2
documents.s: RN-447 — Converting the execution_mode of an EXISTING project refuses (409) while any of the project's dev agents is not idle

documents.t: PermissionsFileStore.move(from, to) reads the file at the OLD location (projectScopeRoot(localAntiga)), writes the SAME content at the NEW location, and deletes the old one (best-effort — if it no longer exists, there's nothing to delete). The content (allow/deny/ask patterns) carries neither path nor mode inside it, so there's nothing to REWRITE, only to move. from === to (no effective root changed) is a no-op. Confirmed by reading projectScopeRoot (project-workspaces-root.ts): for mounted/runner the root IS the workspacePath, treated as a path INSIDE THE API'S CONTAINER — in runner, that was already true BEFORE this delivery (with no bind-mount, the file lives in a folder that only coincides in STRING with the user's real folder, disconnected from it). The conversion doesn't change that existing property, it only relocates it consistently — with no special case for runner besides using move() like any other pair. Where: apps/api/src/application/ports/permissions-file-store.port.ts (move); apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/fs-permissions-file-store.ts Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/fs-permissions-file-store.spec.ts (content survives and is deleted from the origin; an origin without a file writes empty without throwing; from === to is a no-op) ADR: 0111
documents.s: RN-448 — permissions.json is RELOCATED on conversion — the content never changes, only the path

documents.t: ConvertProjectExecutionModeUseCase calls RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase (ADR 0081) to take the project_containers row to removed — via stopped first when it's running (container-lifecycle.ts has no direct running -> removed edge) — BEFORE writing the new execution_mode. The order is mandatory: RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase refuses (400) any transition in a project that isn't in execution_mode = 'container' AT THE MOMENT of the call, so calling it after swapping the column would always fail. With no container row (a project that never provisioned), no transition is triggered. Entering container from mounted/runner does NOT auto-provision anything — the Arquiteto's image gate (RN-105) and the normal lifecycle apply from then on, as for any container project — never a shortcut that skips the gate because the project "already had code somewhere". Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.ts (removerContainerSeExistir) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.spec.ts (running goes through stopped; provisioning goes directly; with no row, no transition; entering container never triggers a transition) ADR: 0111
documents.s: RN-449 — Leaving container, the container lifecycle is ended (removed) BEFORE the column changes

documents.t: It only makes sense in execution_mode: 'runner' (RN-423): a timestamp proving that a CONNECTED runner confirmed the path on the real host. Any conversion that actually changes the (mode, path) pair — including one that lands in runner again with a seemingly equal path — resets the field, forcing a NEW confirmation: the old timestamp attests a verification that happened under a DIFFERENT pair, and carrying it forward would assert a confirmation that never happened for the new state. The no-op (RN-447) is the only exception — nothing changes, so nothing resets. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.spec.ts (runner -> container resets; no-op preserves) ADR: 0111
documents.s: RN-450 — workspaceVerifiedAt resets on EVERY real conversion, even going back to runner with the "same" path

documents.t: The same discipline pattern that smoke-dist.mjs (ADR 0106) already applies to the dist/index.cjs published to npm now also applies to dist-bin/brabo-runner-<platform>-<arch>[.exe] (ADR 0112): no suite proves that a PACKAGED artifact works by reading its source code — only by executing the real artifact, as a subprocess, and observing real output. scripts/smoke-bin.mjs runs the COMPILED binary (never node src/index.ts nor any non-compiled form) with --self-test-pty — an internal flag, not documented in uso() — which resolves node-pty exactly as production does and spawns a real PTY via GerenciadorDePty, writing to and reading from it. Only the line node-pty carregado com sucesso + SELF_TEST_PTY_OK: in the real process's stdout counts as proof; no mock of node-pty nor of child_process is acceptable for this specific test, because what it exists to prove is precisely that the embedded native .node (with { type: 'file' }, native-pty-embed.generated.ts) loads and works INSIDE the binary — mocking any piece of the path would erase the only thing the test needs to prove. Where: apps/runner/scripts/smoke-bin.mjs; apps/runner/src/index.ts (rodarAutoTestePty, the implementation of --self-test-pty) Test: smoke-bin.mjs itself — there's no unit test that replaces it, on purpose (it's the same design as smoke-dist.mjs, which also has no unit counterpart) ADR: 0112 Origin: explicit requirement from the product owner for this backlog item ("no mocking")
documents.s: RN-451 — The standalone binary smoke runs the real SUBPROCESS, never a mock

documents.t: pty.ts stopped doing a static import * as nodePty from 'node-pty' at the top of the module — it now receives the already resolved module by injection in the constructor of GerenciadorDePty, resolved once in main() (src/index.ts) via native-pty-loader.ts#carregarNodePty(). The change exists for the standalone binary (ADR 0112): the compiled path needs to extract the embedded files to a real directory BEFORE resolving node-pty, which requires an asynchronous call — incompatible with a hoisted static import. Outside the compiled binary, the behavior is identical to before (await import('node-pty'), resolved from the node_modules of whoever installed the package). The gap the change opened, closed in the SAME commit: ADR 0106 already recorded that the static import of node-pty, being hoisted before any argument parsing, made smoke-dist.mjs prove that the native binding loaded just by IMPORTING dist/index.cjs — even on the uso() path (zero arguments), which never reaches main(). Moving the resolution into main() silently broke that guarantee, because smoke-dist.mjs only exercised the uso() path. smoke-dist.mjs gained a third check — it runs the CLI with valid arguments (but without real api/engine on the other side) and waits for the line node-pty carregado com sucesso on stdout before killing the process — closing the gap the change itself opened, instead of leaving it as a silent loss of coverage. Where: apps/runner/src/pty.ts (GerenciadorDePty, injection of NodePtyModule); apps/runner/src/native-pty-loader.ts (carregarNodePty); apps/runner/src/index.ts (main, resolves once); apps/runner/scripts/smoke-dist.mjs (third check, verificarNodePtyCarrega) Test: apps/runner/scripts/smoke-dist.mjs (npm/tsup path) and apps/runner/scripts/smoke-bin.mjs (binary path, RN-451) — the only two places that exercise the really packaged artifact, no unit test replaces them ADR: 0112 Origin: a technical need of the standalone binary; the gap in the npm smoke was found by an audit of the change itself, not by a real run reporting failure
documents.s: RN-452 — node-pty resolved by injection, not static import — and the gap this opened in the npm smoke was closed in the same commit

documents.t: Found by USE: the Insights tab, with zero hypotheses, showed "No hypotheses yet — the Psicólogo analyzes each closed session" even with PSYCHOLOGIST_ENABLED=false — the same sentence that appears when the Psicólogo is ACTIVE and just hasn't run yet. The two situations are indistinguishable by the text, which is the same class of defect RN-088/RN-107 already closed for other screens: a state that exists and that the product knows, but doesn't show. RN-117 already covered discovering the pause, but only on the CLICK of "Reanalyze" (503 → PsychologistDisabledError) — and that button only exists in the analyses strip, which only appears when runs.length > 0. A session with no hypothesis at all never gets near it, so the pause was invisible precisely on the empty screen. GET /internal/psychologist/status (engine, PsychologistCommandController.status/2) is a pure read of PsychologistWorker.enabled?/0 — WITH NO side effect, unlike /reanalyze, which creates a job when enabled. The api exposes GET /projects/:projectId/psychologist/status (GetPsychologistStatusUseCase, role:viewer) on top of that — the project in the URL only for consistency with the sibling routes (hypotheses, psychologist/analyses); the flag itself is GLOBAL, as RN-117 already records. ProjectInsightsTab.tsx consumes that read (usePsychologistStatus) and chooses the empty state's sentence by it: paused shows "The Psicólogo is paused — no session is analyzed until it's reactivated" (insights.projectInsightsTab.emptyPaused); otherwise, it keeps the original sentence, which IS honest when the feature is indeed active. The persistent warning (pausedNotice) and the "Reanalyze" buttons also now reflect that proactive read, and not only the useState discovered by the 503 — which still exists, as reinforcement, for the rare case of the flag changing IN FLIGHT between the status read and the click. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine_web/controllers/psychologist_command_controller.ex (status/2), apps/engine/lib/engine_web/router.ex (GET /internal/psychologist/status), apps/api/src/application/ports/api-to-engine-client.port.ts (getPsychologistStatus), apps/api/src/infrastructure/http-clients/api-to-engine-client.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/execution/get-psychologist-status.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/psychologist/psychologist.controller.ts (status), apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts (getPsychologistStatus), apps/web/src/lib/hooks.ts (usePsychologistStatus), apps/web/src/routes/ProjectInsightsTab.tsx Test: apps/engine/test/engine_web/controllers/psychologist_command_controller_test.exs (status/2, enabled: true/false), apps/api/test/infrastructure/http-clients/api-to-engine-client.spec.ts (getPsychologistStatus), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/execution/get-psychologist-status.use-case.spec.ts, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectInsightsTab.test.tsx Edge case: the flag remains GLOBAL (see RN-117) — the api route accepts projectId in the URL only to match the pattern of the controller's sibling routes, and not because the response varies per project. Origin: found by real USE navigating the Insights tab with PSYCHOLOGIST_ENABLED=false, not a script. No ADR — a one-off extension of the already existing read mechanism of RN-117, the same pattern as RN-088/ RN-107 for the rest of the product.
documents.s: RN-454 — The Insights tab knows the Psicólogo is paused BEFORE the user runs into the 503

documents.t: The product owner's request: attach a folder from the user's OWN machine to a project as a read reference for the agents — without requiring the brabo-runner CLI (ADR 0103), unlike execution_mode: runner (ADR 0104), which needs a real HOST path because it routes commands there. The browser reads the files' CONTENT (File.text()) and the RELATIVE path inside the chosen folder (File.webkitRelativePath) — never an absolute machine path, because the browser's File API doesn't expose one, for any site. What crosses the network is text the browser already had the right to read, the same trust model as any ordinary file upload.
documents.s: An attached local folder becomes the fourth scope of the RAG index, read by the BROWSER (RN-455..457, ADR 0113)

documents.t: ChunkScope goes from 'docs' | 'adr' | 'session' to include 'local' (migration 0052, ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE) — additive, with no data migration, no new CHECK: the two CHECKs of chunks (migration 0045) are already written as "is session or isn't", so local falls on the same side as docs/adr (has source_path, doesn't have session_id) with no change at all besides the enum value. origemDoChunk (domain/rag/rag-citation.ts) needed no new branch: a local chunk carries sourcePath exactly like docs/adr, so it falls into the kind: 'file' the citation already knew how to render. Where: apps/api/src/db/schema/rag.ts (chunkScopeEnum), apps/api/src/db/migrations/0052_chunks_local_scope.sql, apps/api/src/application/ports/chunk-repository.port.ts (ChunkScope), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/rag/index-local-folder.use-case.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/rag/index-local-folder.use-case.spec.ts (happy path and full rebuild), apps/api/test/interfaces/http/rag/rag.controller.spec.ts ADR: 0113 Origin: product owner's request
documents.s: RN-455 — chunks.scope gains 'local', reusing the entire RAG pipeline

documents.t: Unlike docs/adr (a background sweep, with nobody watching), attaching a folder is a SINGLE gesture with a folder picker on the screen. IndexLocalFolderUseCase refuses (400) the whole batch when the number of files (RAG_LOCAL_FILE_COUNT_LIMIT, 500) or the summed bytes (RAG_LOCAL_TOTAL_BYTES_LIMIT, 8 MiB) overflow — it never truncates silently, because whoever clicked "Attach" can choose a smaller folder. An individual file that's too large (RAG_LOCAL_FILE_BYTES_LIMIT, 512 KiB) or with an unrecognized extension (RAG_LOCAL_ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS, allowlist) is only SKIPPED (filesSkipped), it never takes down the batch — the same distinction that IndexProjectDocsUseCase already makes implicitly by filtering only .md. A path with .. or a leading slash is REFUSED (400), never accepted silently, the same discipline of never trusting a path coming from the client (RN-092/095) even when it "shouldn't" contain that. apps/web/src/lib/rag-local-limits.ts mirrors the same numbers on the client, only as a UX convenience (summary before sending) — what really guarantees it is the server. Where: apps/api/src/domain/rag/rag-search-limits.ts (RAG_LOCAL_*), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/rag/index-local-folder.use-case.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/rag/index-local-folder.use-case.spec.ts (count and summed-bytes ceilings reject; a large/binary file is skipped; a path with ../leading slash is refused) ADR: 0113 Origin: product owner's request
documents.s: RN-456 — The aggregate ceiling REJECTS (400) the whole upload; a large/binary individual file is only SKIPPED

documents.t: POST .../rag/local requires maintainer, the same ruler as POST .../rag/reindex (RN-238): both call the embedding provider and replace what the project had already indexed. ReindexProjectUseCase was NOT extended to cover local — it reindexes by reading from a source the SERVER can revisit (the project's repository, the event log), and local has no source at all to revisit: the text only exists in the browser of whoever attached it, and the server never kept any host path (there isn't one). Calling deleteByScope(projectId, 'local') on the generic button would delete the attached reference with no way to recreate it — reattaching the folder (a new upload) IS the resync mechanism, and it's a deliberately separate button. Both use cases carry a cross comment explaining why, so that a future "fix" doesn't rewire the two and silently delete the user's material. Where: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/rag/rag.controller.ts (anexarPastaLocal, @RequireRole('maintainer')), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/rag/reindex-project.use-case.ts (comment "Por que local NÃO entra aqui") Test: apps/api/test/interfaces/http/rag/rag.controller.spec.ts ADR: 0113 Origin: product owner's request

documents.t: Found during the investigation of the turn activity strip (RN-460): arquiteto_server.ex, dev_lead_server.ex, ux_designer_server.ex, and staff_server.ex ended SILENTLY when the iteration ceiling overflowed (defp run_turn(state, remaining) when remaining <= 0, do: state, with no event at all) — contradicting the permanent rule that an agent loop doesn't end silently. Only the PO already emitted toolloop.limit_reached (RN-166); the Criativo deliberately diverges with agent.error (reason: "limite_de_iteracoes", a decision documented in the code itself — reusing the ToolLoop's name would lie about who produced the event) and wasn't touched. The four fixed ones now emit toolloop.limit_reached (the same event as the PO, the same iteration/max_iterations payload) before returning — no change in the structure of each one's dispatch_tool. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/arquiteto_server.ex:195, dev_lead_server.ex:244, ux_designer_server.ex:121, staff_server.ex:113 Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/{arquiteto,dev_lead, ux_designer,staff}_server_test.exs ("teto de iterações emite toolloop.limit_reached") Origin: found by a complete reading of the six servers, during the implementation of RN-460; scope extended by the product owner's decision
documents.s: RN-459 — The iteration ceiling no longer ends silently in four of the six conversational agents

documents.t: The Session screen shows, ABOVE the composer, a strip that narrates in human language what a conversational agent (Criativo, PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead, UX Designer, Staff) is doing DURING the turn — visual reference: Claude Code's status line. The thread only receives the response bubble AFTER the turn ends; the rule belongs to the CHAT (Phoenix channel) and applies only to the six conversational agents — the consultative chat without an active agent (SSE, streamChatMessage) keeps the usual streaming bubble, untouched. (Since RN-682 the screen no longer calls that SSE: a consultative session with no agent asks for an agent before sending.) Mechanism (engine): the six servers already emit a DURABLE tool.call in the event log; they now also do broadcast(state, "tool.call", %{tool: name, agent: @agent}) — EPHEMERAL, without args (never a raw payload, the same ruler as RN-096/RN-412) — right after, for the session:<id> channel to deliver in real time. There's no shared behaviour/macro among the six dispatch_tools (four distinct structural shapes confirmed by a complete reading): the change is six edits adapted to each one's local shape. Mechanism (web): a PURE reducer (reduzirAtividadeDoTurno/lib/atividade-do-turno.ts) accumulates the agent.delta text as "current"; when a tool.call arrives from the channel, it archives the non-empty current as a NARRATION line, resets, and ALWAYS adds a TOOL line with fraseDaFerramenta(tool) (a dictionary of the 19 tools of the six agents, lib/narracao-de-ferramentas.ts, with no RN of its own — it only exists to serve this rule) — two consecutive calls with no delta between them become two separate lines, never one. End of turn resets (finalizarTurnoDoAgente, the ONLY reset point). turnoViaCanal is an OWN flag (never derived from statusAgent/streamingAgent, which go through legitimately null windows in the middle of a turn) that decides whether the strip appears OR the old bubble — never both. Presentation rule (history): agruparNarracoesDoTurno, a new pure pass that runs AFTER afundarDesfechos (RN-172) in the same useMemo — within the same turno+autor, consecutive agent.responses become a compact Disclosure ("Turn steps · N"), leaving only the last one intact and outside it. turno === 0 (the sentinel prologue of turnoDoSeq) is left OUT of the grouping, on purpose — it isn't a real turn, and old fixtures stack agent.response without a turn boundary to test another mechanism (RN-138/RN-177). An agent-agnostic function (it only reads turno/autor), afundarDesfechos itself doesn't change. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/{po,criativo,arquiteto, dev_lead,ux_designer,staff}_server.ex (tool.call broadcast); apps/web/src/lib/atividade-do-turno.ts (reducer); apps/web/src/components/TurnActivityStrip.tsx (component); apps/web/src/lib/session-channel.ts:54 (onToolCall); apps/web/src/routes/session-fio.tsx:48 (agruparNarracoesDoTurno), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx:197 (turnoViaCanal) Test: apps/web/src/lib/atividade-do-turno.test.ts, apps/web/src/components/TurnActivityStrip.test.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/session-channel.test.ts, apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.ordenacao-e-avisos.test.tsx (agruparNarracoesDoTurno), suite of apps/engine/test/engine/agents/ *_server_test.exs (tool.call broadcast without raw args) Origin: product owner's request
documents.s: RN-460 — The turn activity strip narrates in real time, and the thread only receives the response at the end

documents.t: scripts/dev/preflight.mjs detects a native Ollama already listening on OLLAMA_PORT (the same default, 11434, as a native installation) confirming by HTTP (GET /api/tags) that it really is an Ollama, not any process on the port. Confirmed, it ASKS only once whether to use that instance — default "Yes" when there's no TTY (bootstrap.sh runs the command with stdin from /dev/null on purpose, so as not to steal the user's arrow keys) — and writes the answer to .env (OLLAMA_MODE=host|container). From then on the detection doesn't even run again: with OLLAMA_MODE already present, the function returns early. ollama/ollama-model-loader enter profiles: ["local-llm"] in the compose so they don't come up when the mode is host. The ONLY way to reopen the question is the dedicated menu item "Docker › Reconfigure Ollama", which deletes the written keys — never a spontaneous question again while they exist. Where: scripts/dev/env-file.mjs:41 (escreverEnv), scripts/dev/preflight.mjs:157 (ehOllama), scripts/dev/preflight.mjs:202 (perguntarUsoDoOllama), scripts/dev/preflight.mjs:238 (detectarOllamaNativo), scripts/dev/reconfigurar-ollama.sh, scripts/dev/perfil-ollama.sh, docker/docker-compose.yml:82,119 (profiles: ["local-llm"]) Test: scripts/dev/bootstrap.spec.ts (covers the menu wiring — the conditional profile in Deploy › All/Create and the dedicated item "Reconfigurar Ollama"). The detection/persistence logic itself (detectarOllamaNativo/escreverEnv) was validated end to end manually against a fake HTTP server and against this machine's real Ollama (see ADR 0114) — declared gap: there's no dedicated automated suite for preflight.mjs today. ADR: 0114 Origin: product owner's request, a real finding during execution (port collision with a native Ollama)
documents.s: RN-461 — Native Ollama: asks once, the answer persists in .env, never asks again

documents.t: POST .../huggingface/pull-requests only CREATES the request, in pending_confirmation — no download starts. Only a SEPARATE call, POST .../pull-requests/:id/confirm, moves the request to confirmed → pulling and actually calls OllamaProvider.pullModel. ConfirmModelPullUseCase REFUSES (409) to confirm a request that is no longer in pending_confirmation — the state transition IS the second confirmation, not a separate flag, and that's why it isn't re-executable. An Ollama failure during the pull marks the request failed with a failedReason prefixed by the origin (infra/modelo/código, ADR 0020's vocabulary) — never a silent failure, and nothing is activated in the catalog when it fails. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/llm/huggingface/request-model-pull.use-case.ts:23 (RequestModelPullUseCase), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/llm/huggingface/confirm-model-pull.use-case.ts:45 (ConfirmModelPullUseCase), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/llm/huggingface-models.controller.ts:109-165 (the two routes, role:maintainer) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/llm/huggingface/request-model-pull.use-case.spec.ts (creates in pending_confirmation, nothing more), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/llm/huggingface/confirm-model-pull.use-case.spec.ts (the happy path activates in the catalog; an Ollama failure marks failed with the right origin — modelo/infra; refuses to reconfirm a request that has already left pending_confirmation; 404 for a request nonexistent in the workspace) ADR: 0115 Origin: product owner's request
documents.s: RN-462 — A Hugging Face model pull requires explicit two-step confirmation; it never runs on its own

documents.t: Search on the Hugging Face Hub filters to OFFICIAL publishers by default — HUGGINGFACE_OFFICIAL_PUBLISHERS, a CLOSED vocabulary curated by hand (meta-llama, google, mistralai, microsoft, Qwen, deepseek-ai, openai, nvidia), compared by EXACT case equality — a lowercase reupload (qwen/...) doesn't inherit the official org's seal (Qwen/...). includeCommunity=true brings all the rest, each result marked official: true|false, never hiding the distinction. On screen, the community toggle is born OFF and, while on, shows a security warning (Alert tone="danger") — the opt-in and the warning are the same gesture, never a preference the user turns on once and forgets is on. documents.t: Revised by RN-687 (ADR 0203, 10/01): the browser flow was RETIRED, and POST .../runner-device-keys left with it — together with RegisterRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase and its test, cited below as they were. GET/DELETE and the self-service revocation remain; the new key is born in the terminal (RN-551) and whoever registers it is the installer (RN-552). The project keys already registered remain valid and revocable. runner_device_keys keeps only the PUBLIC Ed25519 key of a runner device — generated in the browser, never the private one. POST/DELETE .../runner-device-keys require the minimum role developer and are authenticated by the normal SESSION JWT (unlike runner-ticket: whoever calls here is the already logged-in browser registering its own device, not the runner running without a session). RegisterRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase validates only the minimal SHAPE of the JWK (kty:"OKP", crv:"Ed25519", x present) — the deep validation (whether it's really a valid Ed25519 point) is left to jose.importJWK at the moment of use, in RN-465. RevokeRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase is IDEMPOTENT and scoped to the calling userId — the same design as revogar() of RN-426 — and returns 404 both for a nonexistent key and for another user's key, the same discipline of not leaking existence. Declared asymmetry with the PAT: unlike RN-427 (a maintainer revokes the PAT of ANY user of the project, incident response), the device key does NOT have an equivalent maintainer route today — only self-revocation. The docblock of RunnerDeviceKeysController declares this explicitly as a cut of this round, not forgetfulness: extending the same pattern of RN-427 to device keys is direct future work, if it comes to be requested. Where: apps/api/src/db/schema/auth.ts:338 (runnerDeviceKeys), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/register-runner-device-key.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/revoke-runner-device-key.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/runner-device-keys.controller.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/register-runner-device-key.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/revoke-runner-device-key.use-case.spec.ts ADR: 0118 Origin: product owner's request
documents.s: RN-464 — The runner's device key: self-service registration/revocation; NO maintainer view in this round (declared cut)

documents.t: Revised by RN-687 (ADR 0203, 10/01): nothing of this RN changed in the guard — PatAuthGuard still accepts the JWT of a PROJECT key, and that's why a runner configured through the browser before ADR 0203 doesn't break. What no longer exists is creating a NEW project key: the browser no longer generates the pair. PatAuthGuard gained a second path, next to the unchanged PAT (brb_...): a bearer in compact JWT format (three segments) is treated as a device key. The guard reads the header's kid (without verifying the signature yet), fetches the corresponding ACTIVE public key in runner_device_keys, and only then verifies the EdDSA signature with jose.importJWK/jwtVerify. Short and MANDATORY TTL: exp - iat can't exceed 60s — checked against the token's SIGNED life, not against "now", closing the replay window of a leaked JWT from the moment it was signed. The userId/projectId used to authorize always come from the record saved in the database, never from a JWT claim — the token only needs to prove possession of the private key, never to state who the owner is. projectId is checked TWICE (the JWT's claim against the route, and the key's registered project against the route) — the same 401 vs 403 discipline the PAT path already uses: a token/key valid for the WRONG project is a different category from an invalid token/key. The runner signs that JWT in assinarTicketComChaveDeDispositivo (apps/runner/src/auth.ts), with the private JWK already LOADED in memory — never reading a file there, preserving the "no file I/O" guarantee of auth.ts (whoever reads the file is RN-466's separate module). This does NOT reopen RN-439: RN-439 closed the guarantee that runner-ticket never accepts the LOGIN JWT as a credential — it still stands. The device key is a DIFFERENT JWT, self-signed by the runner itself with a key whose private part the api never saw, with no user sub at all — only a second way of proving "I am the device of such user in this project", as scoped as the PAT it complements. Accepting the session JWT here would make RolesGuard/@RequireRole authorize that user for everything their role allows in the rest of the api, blowing past the runner:project:<id> scope — exactly what RN-439 prevented. Where: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/pat-auth.guard.ts:104-216 (autenticarChaveDeDispositivo), apps/runner/src/auth.ts:143-188 (assinarTicketComChaveDeDispositivo, obterTicketDoRunnerComCredencial) Test: apps/api/test/interfaces/pat-auth.guard.spec.ts (describe "chave de dispositivo (JWT EdDSA autoassinado, ao lado do PAT)" — happy path, invalid signature, revoked key, the claim's projectId doesn't match the route, a key registered in another project, TTL too long, a kid with no corresponding key), apps/runner/src/auth.spec.ts (describe "assinarTicketComChaveDeDispositivo"/"obterTicketDoRunnerComCredencial") ADR: 0118 Origin: product owner's request
documents.s: RN-465 — POST .../runner-ticket accepts a PAT OR a device key (Ed25519, TTL ≤60s) — a second form of DEVICE credential, never dual-auth with the session JWT (RN-439's distinction)

documents.t: Revised by RN-687 (ADR 0203, 10/01): the browser no longer writes these files — the flow was retired. The READ remains intact: a folder configured before ADR 0203 keeps working, and it's also through --dir pointing to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/brabo/ that the machine unit finds the key created in the terminal (RN-551). apps/runner/src/device-key.ts (a NEW module, separate on purpose from auth.ts) reads — never writes — brabo-runner.config.json ({projectId, apiUrl}) and brabo-runner-device-key.jwk.json from the current cwd(); the absence of either of the two returns null, never throws, because that absence is the NORMAL case of whoever still uses explicit flags. In lerArgumentos (apps/runner/src/index.ts), the rule is the SAME three times — an explicit flag always beats the local file: --project beats configLocal.projectId; an absent --dir falls to . (the very folder where the command runs) when there was a local config, instead of the usage error from before; --token/BRABO_ACCOUNT_TOKEN beats the local device key when both exist. With NO credential at all (neither token nor local key), the CLI keeps refusing with the usage message — nothing here makes authentication optional, only which of the two forms is used. Where: apps/runner/src/device-key.ts (lerConfigLocal, lerChaveDeDispositivo), apps/runner/src/index.ts:95-206 (lerArgumentos) Test: apps/runner/src/device-key.spec.ts (happy path of each read; null without throwing for a missing file/invalid JSON/missing field; respects the received cwd; the module doesn't import writeFileSync/mkdirSync) ADR: 0118 Origin: product owner's request
documents.s: RN-466 — brabo-runner runs without --project/--dir/--token when the folder has a local config written by the browser

documents.t: The "Needs you" chip, at the top of the project, opens a panel with the project's FIVE decision queues — action approvals, PR merges, story promotions, architecture pending items, and Psicólogo hypotheses. Two guarantees define it, and neither of them is aesthetic: It never sums. Each queue has its OWN header and count, and there's no project total anywhere: neither in the panel, nor in the chip that opens it — the chip announces PRESENCE (a dot, temAlgoEsperando, boolean by signature) and never quantity. It's the same product decision that already keeps the five rail counters separate (ADR 0126): summing erases WHICH queue is asking for attention, which is precisely the question of whoever opens the panel. montarFilas returns the five in the declared order of urgency (ORDEM_DAS_FILAS) and doesn't export a total function — the absence is the mechanism, not an oversight. The only dedupe that exists is by IDENTITY, never between queues: the SAME git_merge proposed_action arrives through both hooks (usePendingActions is the session's and doesn't filter by type; useProjectPendingActions is project-wide) and would appear twice in the same list, under two titles. It stays in the most specific group (prs). It never executes. The two actionable queues in the panel (aprovacoes, prs) render the SAME ApprovalCard as the Approvals tab (a single variant since AT-322, with the detail collapsed), and the buttons call the same decision endpoints — the panel is a SHORTCUT to the decision, never a substitute for it. That matters especially for git_merge: a merge into a protected branch is downgraded to require_approval UNCONDITIONALLY (apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts), a ceiling that neither agent_autonomy nor permissions.json lift, and nothing in the panel touches that path. onActivateAutoMode is OMITTED on both cards on purpose: turning on "auto mode" (RN-153) is changing the agent's POLICY, not deciding the action that's in front of you — whoever wants that decides in the Approvals tab, where the workspace role is already checked. The other three queues have no decision card outside their context and therefore LEAD to the tab where the decision lives. The architecture pending item has no date of its own — none, in any field (ArchitecturePendency): it's a view DERIVED from crossing story and module_map, recomputed on every read and never recorded. The panel BORROWS the related story's date and SAYS it borrowed it ("story updated 18 min ago", dataEmprestada); without the story in the loaded backlog, it shows "no date" and sorts the item at the END of the queue. In no case an invented instant: rendering "now" would make the most urgent line of the screen the one least known about, with nothing exposing the lie. Adding a column and a migration in the api would solve it for real and is a separate decision, outside this one's scope. Where: apps/web/src/lib/precisa-de-voce.ts:108 (ORDEM_DAS_FILAS), :117 (FILAS_ACIONAVEIS), :139 (montarFilas — the dedupe by identity and the date borrowing), :245 (temAlgoEsperando); apps/web/src/components/PainelPrecisaDeVoce.tsx:246-248 (role="dialog", aria-modal, label) and :279-284 (group per queue, with its count); apps/web/src/routes/ProjectPage.tsx:120 (builds the queues from the five hooks the rail counters already use) Test: apps/web/src/lib/precisa-de-voce.test.ts (the five queues separated with each one's items; nothing summed and no total function; the duplicated git_merge appears once, in the PRs queue; order by longest wait; borrowed date marked, absent becomes null and goes to the end), apps/web/src/components/PainelPrecisaDeVoce.test.tsx (five headers with each queue's count; the total appears nowhere; the empty state's own sentence; ApprovalCard decides by the action's OWN session; "Automatic mode" isn't offered; an architecture line without a date renders without breaking; Esc, click-outside, focus, and aria-expanded) Origin: design review by the product owner (item #3 of the UI improvements canvas)
documents.s: RN-467 — The panel of the five decision queues NEVER sums and NEVER executes: it separates by queue and forwards to the decision

documents.t: The product shows environment state in two places, and the slice of each is the rule: the login screen shows only what's true WITHOUT identity, and the project Overview shows what's only true WITH it. Pre-login, the slice is imposed by the data's scope, not by aesthetic choice. What remains are the two /health endpoints — public in both services on purpose (@Public() in the api; "Sem auth de propósito" in router.ex), the same ones StatusPage already consumes without a session. Runner presence is keyed by {user_id, project_id} (runner_device_keys) and the model list is projects/:projectId/models with role viewer: before login neither subject exists, so the screen declares the absence ("Runner and local models depend on your account and a project") instead of omitting it — omitting it would make the platform look like it doesn't have what it has. The two /health keep the THREE states separate (RN-088 applied to an environment signal): checking… is not no response, and neither of them is responding. The probe has a CEILING (6s): an api that accepts the connection and never answers would leave the line at "checking…" forever, which is honest for half a second and a lie by omission after ten. And the form never waits for the probe. The state is local to the block, which is a SIBLING of the card — an api that's down changes a text and doesn't delay or hide a pixel of the login. That matters exactly at the moment the api goes down, which is when someone most needs the screen to at least OPEN. Post-login, the rule is about what the data does NOT assert. The runner signal comes from projects.workspace_verified_at — the stamp ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase writes when a runner connects and confirms the folder (RN-423), and the SAME field the engine uses as a gate (TerminalExecutor refuses a command in a runner project with the field null). It is not a heartbeat, for two independent reasons: there's no process being observed, and reconnecting reporting the same path doesn't rewrite the stamp (an explicit decision of the use case), so that not even the date is "the last time the runner showed up". The screen says "folder confirmed on <date>" with the caveat of what that isn't, and never "up", "online", nor a green dot — the tone is neutro, and green there would read as a liveness guarantee the data doesn't support. What knows about NOW is the terminal's socket, in the Code tab (TerminalPanel/RunnerOnboardingPanel), and the caveat points there. The same discipline RN-467 used when borrowing the story's updatedAt. The runner line only exists in a project in runner mode: in the other two the field is null by definition (the mode conversion resets it, RN-450) and a "never confirmed" line there would be an invented absence. Where: apps/web/src/components/SinaisDoAmbiente.tsx:72 (useSaude — the probe with a ceiling and the .catch of the connection rejection), :133 (SinaisDoAmbiente, the pre-login block); apps/web/src/components/AmbienteDoProjeto.tsx:92 (AmbienteDoProjeto), :102 (runner line, only in runner mode, with neutro tone and caveat); apps/web/src/routes/AuthLayout.tsx:46 (colunaDeIdentidade — nothing focusable there, or the first Tab stop stops being the e-mail field); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/confirm-project-workspace.use-case.ts:93 (the stamp is NOT rewritten when the path doesn't change — the reason the date isn't recency) Test: apps/web/src/components/SinaisDoAmbiente.test.tsx (the three distinct states; a connection rejection becomes "no response" and not silence; a non-OK response likewise; ceiling of a hanging probe; no focusable element; the absence of runner/models is declared), apps/web/src/components/AmbienteDoProjeto.test.tsx (no runner line outside runner mode; confirmed requires the caveat and the block doesn't contain de pé|online|conectado agora; never confirmed teaches the path; count of local models in singular, plural, and zero; query keys reused), apps/web/src/routes/LoginPage.ambiente.test.tsx (the form renders and submits with the probe rejecting AND with the probe hanging; a single <h1>; the version still has one source) Origin: design review by the product owner (item #6 of the UI improvements canvas)
documents.s: RN-468 — An environment signal says what it KNOWS: workspaceVerifiedAt is a record of confirmation, never a guarantee that the runner is alive

documents.t: In the Settings sections whose rows are a SCALAR setting per key (Parallelism per area and Spend ceiling per area, both per agent_areas), the save button is ONE, the section's, and not one per row. Saving triggers one call per dirty row — PUT .../areas/:key/max-parallel and .../budget are per-AREA endpoints, there's no transactional endpoint for "write these N ceilings", and this product didn't invent one. The consequence is that the outcome of a click can be partial, and the rule is about what the screen can say then. The calls are in SERIES, in the screen's order, and one failure doesn't interrupt the following ones. In series because the failure report names rows and needs to come out in the order the person sees them. Without interrupting because whoever clicked asked for the N: aborting on the first refusal would leave rows with no attempt at all, and the screen wouldn't be able to distinguish "the api refused" from "it didn't even try". The outcome is per ROW, and that's what the UI shows. Only the draft the api CONFIRMED is discarded; what failed stays in the field, with what the person typed, and the section stays marked as unsaved by exactly those rows — clicking Save again tries only them. The three outcomes are distinct and none disguises itself as another: all passed → success; none passed → the message the API gave, never a count; some passed → a warning saying how many out of how many and naming the ones left. "Saved" and "not saved" would both be a lie in the third case, and it's the one this RN exists to protect. The section declares HOW MANY rows are pending before the click. One button per section says "Save" the same with one dirty row and with five; the count ("2 unsaved changes in this section") is the counterpart of having swapped N buttons for one. Dirty is a comparison by interpreted value, not by text: 20 and 20.0 are the same ceiling, and comparing strings would send a call the api treats as a no-op. An invalid draft counts as dirty and replaces the count with the message explaining the block — two numbers about the same set would be noise, and whoever has an invalid value needs what locks the button. Where the rule does NOT apply, and why. A section whose control is a choice of a NAMED value (Story promotion, Models per agent, Model per area, role in Members) saves on onChange, with no button, and stays that way: the confirmation exists for a TYPED field, where saving on each key press would send 1 on the way to 12. What that sentence measures is whose value it is: it applies to the control that writes its OWN value, and doesn't reach a selector whose value is the ARGUMENT of an action over other rows — see RN-476, which is the exception and says why. And Credentials keeps a button per row despite also having drafts per key: the credential is write-only (ADR 0050) and never comes back from the server, so there's no value to compare against to decide "dirty"; the row's button alternates between "Save" and "Replace" depending on whether that provider already has a key; and it shares the card with "Test" and "Remove", which are irreducibly the row's. Where: apps/web/src/routes/settings/secao-salvavel.tsx:105 (useSecaoSalvavel — the serial loop, the per-row outcome, and the three toasts), :130 (dirty by interpreted value), :241 (MarcaDeNaoSalvo — the count, and the invalid one replacing it), apps/web/src/routes/settings/ParallelismSection.tsx:31, apps/web/src/routes/settings/BudgetSection.tsx:37 (the two consumers), apps/web/src/routes/settings/CredentialsSection.tsx:57 (why this section was left out) Test: apps/web/src/routes/settings/secao-salvavel.test.tsx (the count of dirty rows; going back to the server's value clears the mark; invalid replaces the count and locks the button; one click persists all the dirty rows; a number and null in the same batch; a partial failure says how many out of how many and names the one left; the section stays marked by those that failed; the second click tries only them; one failure doesn't interrupt the following ones; none passing shows the API's message and not the count) Origin: design review by the product owner (item #7 of the UI improvements canvas — "save per section instead of per row")
