documents.t: Closes the gap that the comment on ContainerBrokerPort (ADR 0130) and the CLAUDE.md declared since PR 1.5: stop/remove had a ready HTTP CLIENT (HttpContainerBrokerClient.stop/.remove) and ZERO callers — the global containers page (/containers, RN-496) is the first. The two are NEVER an agent action: only a human clicking "Stop"/"Remove" on a row of the screen proposes them. container_stop follows container_start's EXACT caliber (RN-491): maintainer, require_approval by default, CAN be configured auto_approve (never seeded) — ExecuteContainerStopUseCase asks the broker to stop and, only when the registered state still said running, registers the running -> stopped transition (container-lifecycle.ts). Already registered stopped/provisioning/failed: the broker is called anyway (it's idempotent — stopping what's no longer running is a no-op on the Docker side), but NO transition is written — inventing one the state machine didn't really describe would be the same defect RN-486 already named for the observed state. container_remove is the MOST destructive of the three — it discards the container and requires reprovisioning from scratch (container-lifecycle.ts: removed only exits by provisioning again, never "coming back to life") — and that's why it enters the SAME absolute ceiling of decide.ts as git push/privileged command (RN-418): never auto-approvable, neither by agent_autonomy nor by permissions.json, even with "automatic mode" on. The "always allow" gap is closed AT THE SOURCE, by the same mechanism as RN-418: ApproveAlwaysActionUseCase refuses (400) to write the pattern for container_remove — the whole click is refused, and whoever wants to remove approves the instance through the normal flow (POST .../approve). On the web, ApprovalCard.podeSemprePermitir hides the "always allow" button for container_remove, the same ruler that already applies to instruction_patch. ContainerBrokerPort.remove is docker rm --force — it removes even a running container, in a single call. The state machine has NO direct running -> removed (only running -> stopped/failed, and only FROM THERE to removed): ExecuteContainerRemoveUseCase registers BOTH hops when the registered state still said running (stopped, then removed), reflecting what really happened on the Docker side without widening the state machine with a shortcut that would only exist here. Neither of the two decides an image — unlike container_start, which reuses DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase to emit a new version of artifact.project_image. stop/remove only ask the broker to act on the container that already exists. Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts (ACTION_TYPES, MIN_ROLE_FOR_ACTION_TYPE, the absolute ceiling of container_remove), apps/api/src/domain/actions/command-matcher.ts (ACTION_TYPE_LABELS), apps/api/src/domain/containers/container-stop-remove-execution-result.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-stop.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-remove.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/approve-action.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/propose-action.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/approve-always-action.use-case.ts, apps/web/src/lib/aprovacoes.ts, apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.tsx (podeSemprePermitir) Test: apps/api/test/domain/actions/decide.spec.ts ("container_stop, a página global de containers" — CAN auto_approve; "teto de container_remove" — NEVER can), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-stop.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-remove.use-case.spec.ts (both hops from running; a single hop from stopped/ failed; idempotency; BrokerRecusouError/BrokerIndisponivelError never propagate), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/approve-always-action.use-case.spec.ts, apps/web/src/lib/aprovacoes.test.ts, apps/web/src/routes/ContainersPage.test.tsx Architectural decision: ADR 0136 Origin: the product owner's plan, Part 1 / PR 1.8
documents.s: RN-495 — container_stop/container_remove are born as proposed_action, and only container_remove enters the absolute ceiling

documents.t: The same family as RN-486/RN-468, applied to a NEW screen: GET workspaces/:workspaceId/containers (/containers, cross-project) returns one row per workspace project that already has project_containers (ContainersOverviewRepository, THREE batch queries, never one per project — the same spirit as ProjectsSummaryRepository), but asking the broker for the OBSERVED state is a NETWORK call per project, and it doesn't fit in a SQL query. The ceiling (ADR 0060) is by TWO rulers, not one. First, only provisioning/running rows are ELIGIBLE — a stopped/failed/ removed container doesn't need the daemon's confirmation for the screen to make sense (nobody expects it to be up). Second, among the eligible ones, at most TETO_DE_VERIFICACOES_POR_CARGA (20, revisable) are asked of the broker PER LOAD — in parallel, never in series. What's left out of either ruler carries naoVerificado (fora_do_escopo_da_verificacao | teto_de_verificacoes_atingido), the screen's OWN field — never confused with naoObservado (broker-nao-configurado/broker-sem-resposta/broker-recusou), which is about the broker HAVING BEEN asked and not having answered. A row outside the ceiling has observado/naoObservado/detalheDaObservacao all null: the screen never invents an answer the broker didn't give. The image read is the FROZEN one, not the current one. imageVersion in project_containers points to the version of artifact.project_image that was current when the row was born — the Arquiteto may have revised the decision AFTERWARDS. The screen resolves the image text by fetching the artifact.project_image event whose version matches imageVersion (decisaoNaVersao, domain/containers/project-container.ts), never the most recent decision — showing the most recent would lie about which image the container that really came up uses. null when that version's event isn't found (never invented). The pending container proposed_action (if any) travels in the SAME batch read, matched by projectId IN (...) like the other two — it's what lets the screen swap the three action buttons for the inline ApprovalCard without a fourth query per project. Where: apps/api/src/application/ports/containers-overview-repository.port.ts, apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/containers-overview.repository.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/containers/obter-visao-geral-de-containers.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/domain/containers/project-container.ts (decisaoNaVersao, versaoDoPayload), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/containers/containers-overview.controller.ts, apps/web/src/routes/ContainersPage.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/hooks.ts (useContainersOverview) Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/containers-overview.repository.spec.ts (only projects with project_containers enter; FROZEN image, not the current one; cross-session acaoPendente; the number of queries doesn't grow with the number of projects), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/containers/obter-visao-geral-de-containers.use-case.spec.ts (eligibility by status; ceiling per load; naoObservado never confused with naoVerificado), apps/api/test/interfaces/http/containers/containers-overview.controller.spec.ts, apps/web/src/routes/ContainersPage.test.tsx Architectural decision: ADR 0136 Origin: the product owner's plan, Part 1 / PR 1.8

documents.t: Closes the half that RN-494 (ADR 0135) left declared: mounted/runner came to REQUIRE a decided image (RN-105's gate applies in the three modes), but still brought up NO container — only execution_mode: container had someone (the broker, apps/broker) capable of really calling Docker. container_start/container_stop/container_remove (RN-491/495) now have a SECOND execution path, branched by the project's executionMode inside ExecuteContainerStartUseCase/ExecuteContainerStopUseCase/ ExecuteContainerRemoveUseCase — never in the action's PROPOSAL nor APPROVAL, which remain mode-agnostic (decide.ts doesn't change). container goes through the broker, with no change at all. mounted/runner ask the ENGINE (ApiToEngineClient.startContainerViaRunner/ stopContainerViaRunner/removeContainerViaRunner, synchronous like executeTerminalAction) to pass on to the connected RUNNER — the CLI that already keeps the terminal:<projectId> channel (ADR 0103/0104) gains THREE new event pairs, container_start/_result, container_stop/_result, container_remove/_result (apps/runner/src/channel.ts), in the SAME mold as exec/exec_result: Engine.Runners.RunnerRouter dispatches to the channel correlated by ref and stays blocked on receive, the runner calls DockerViaCli.start/stop/remove (@brabo/docker-port, ADR 0128) with the USER'S DOCKER — not the server's — and answers. EngineWeb. ContainerCommandController (routes POST internal/projects/:projectId/ containers/{start,stop,remove}) is the only caller; no other path reaches those three operations on the engine side. The image that comes up isn't ELECTED again — unlike the container path, which reuses DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase to write a new version of artifact.project_image. The mounted/runner path only READS the CURRENT decision (ObterSpecDeContainerUseCase, the SAME use case that already composes GET .../container-spec for the broker — called directly, without HTTP, because both run in the api's process) and sends it to the runner; without a decided image (RN-105), it fails BEFORE asking the engine. "No runner connected" is a NORMAL FAILURE, never a generic exception — the same discipline as BrokerIndisponivelError/BrokerRecusouError on the container path. RunnerNaoConectadoError (no runner, or timeout) and RunnerRecusouContainerError (the runner answered and REFUSED — Docker unavailable on the user's machine, invalid specification) are the two classes HttpApiToEngineClient throws; the three use cases catch them and write failed with the reason, never letting them propagate. On the engine side, the response is ALWAYS 200 — sucesso: false in the body, with motivoCodigo ("not_connected"/"timeout") only when the engine DIDN'T EVEN GET to ask the runner (RunnerRouter returned {:error, _}), never an HTTP error status for what is a normal failure of the command. Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor did NOT gain a new output. The decision "run the command on the host or inside the container this runner brought up" is INTERNAL to the runner — decisao_de_execucao/1 already routes UNCONDITIONALLY every command of a connected runner project to RunnerRouter.exec/4 (RN-423). What changes is only apps/runner/src/index.ts: EstadoDoRunner gains containerAtivo (the NAME of the container THIS runner brought up, or null), and tratarExec now routes to DockerViaCli.exec (via docker exec) when there's an active container, or to the usual path (executarComando directly on the host) when there isn't — the cwd, already validated by validarCwdDentroDaRaiz against the project root, is translated into /work by PREFIX swap (cwdParaContainer, guard.ts), the same reasoning as cwd_para_container/2 on the engine side (RN-492). guard.ts (containment in $HOME on Linux, RN-434) now also covers the mounted path, with NO new validation. The container's bind-mount IS estado.dir — the same root validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux already validated at the CLI's startup, before any container came up. There's no second check of "valid mount path" because there doesn't need to be: the mount IS the confirmed root, period. Where: apps/runner/src/channel.ts, apps/runner/src/index.ts (EstadoDoRunner.containerAtivo, tratarContainerStart/Stop/Remove, tratarExec), apps/runner/src/guard.ts (cwdParaContainer), apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/runner_router.ex (start_container/stop_container/remove_container), apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine_web/controllers/container_command_controller.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine_web/router.ex, apps/api/src/application/ports/api-to-engine-client.port.ts (RunnerNaoConectadoError, RunnerRecusouContainerError), apps/api/src/infrastructure/http-clients/api-to-engine-client.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-start.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-stop.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-remove.use-case.ts Test: apps/runner/src/channel.spec.ts (roundtrip of the three new pairs), apps/runner/src/index-handlers.spec.ts (tratarExec routes host vs. container; tratarContainerStart/Stop/Remove never throw), apps/runner/src/guard.spec.ts (cwdParaContainer), apps/engine/test/engine/runners/runner_router_test.exs, apps/engine/test/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel_test.exs, apps/api/test/infrastructure/http-clients/api-to-engine-client.spec.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-start.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-stop.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-remove.use-case.spec.ts (the three with describe "mounted/runner (ADR 0137)") Architectural decision: ADR 0137 Origin: the product owner's plan, Part 1 / PR 1.3

documents.t: RN-490 recorded the RAG golden-set (ADR 0132) being born as a manual mix golden_set.rag, "never in CI", for the same reason as the QA golden-set (ADR 0123): without an API LLM secret or new infra, there was no way to run a real Ollama on a CI runner. This RN closes that half — only for RAG, never for QA — with a dedicated workflow (.github/workflows/golden-set-rag.yml, schedule + workflow_dispatch) that pulls nomic-embed-text into a real Ollama service (the same pinned version as the rest of the product, today 0.34.4) and really runs mix golden_set.rag. The difference that makes this tractable for RAG and not for QA: the RAG golden-set only calls the EMBEDDING model — CPU, deterministic, no sampling — never a CHAT model making a judgment, which is what the QA golden-set requires (expensive, it measures something non-deterministic by nature, as ADR 0123 itself records with real rounds varying from 1 to 5 hits out of 6). ubuntu-latest, with no GPU at all, suffices here — it wouldn't suffice for QA. The QA golden-set doesn't change at all with this RN: it remains entirely manual, a TODO(humano) in CLAUDE.md. severidade: warn (docs/gates.yml) STAYS warn, and the reason changed. It's no longer "there's no CI with an LLM" — it becomes cadence: the workflow is SCHEDULED (nightly + manual trigger), it never runs on pull_request. block would promise a merge lock that doesn't exist — the same reasoning that already held in Stage 2, now applied to the right reason. A regression in search accuracy becomes a trend signal visible within 24h (or immediately, via workflow_dispatch), never a gate that blocks a PR — a trade-off accepted explicitly by the product owner, given the cost of pulling the model and running 17 searches (a few minutes) in every window. No secret needs to be generated in the workflow. seed-golden-set-rag.ts never defines NODE_ENV, and the four secrets the api would refuse with an example literal in production (RN-114) are only checked when NODE_ENV === 'production' — the script falls into the development branch and uses the dev literals without complaint, unlike docker/smoke.sh, which comes up with NODE_ENV=production on purpose and therefore generates its own with openssl rand. The permanent exclusion of the :golden_set_rag tag in test_helper.exs (RN-490) doesn't change. It protects the regular mix test — including on the machine of any developer with Ollama up — never the new workflow, which invokes mix golden_set.rag explicitly, just as it was always necessary to run it manually. Fixed after measuring: the workflow above never ran green once. Five consecutive scheduled runs (09/05 to 09/09/2026) failed, and there were three stacked defects, each hiding the next: mix golden_set.rag is an alias that calls test, and Mix refuses that outside the :test environment — ** (Mix) "mix test" is running in the "dev" environment —, before running anything. def cli in apps/engine/mix.exs now declares preferred_envs for BOTH golden-set tasks: that's what makes the short command, the only one documented everywhere, work without an environment prefix. Requiring MIX_ENV=test from whoever calls would transfer the fix to all the prose that teaches the command — and to whoever forgot, again. The job never brought up the api, and the test SKIPS when API_URL doesn't respond (an environment precondition declared in ADR 0132). With item 1 fixed, the job would be green without measuring anything. It now brings up the real api (build, node dist/main.js, waiting for /health) — satisfying the precondition, and never loosening the test, which would be changing the judgment to fit the CI. What does the work is still seed-golden-set-rag.ts, which brings up its own Nest context; the instance exists to answer /health. The seed died with 409 at the image gate. It created the project as runner precisely to ESCAPE the gate (RN-105), relying on the exemption that RN-169/RN-421 gave to mounted/runner — an exemption revoked by RN-494 (ADR 0135), with the script's comment still citing it. Now the seed CROSSES the gate through the real path: it decides the image via DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase, the same use case as the Arquiteto's choose_project_image, in a consultiva session it opens (the decision event requires session_id, which is NOT NULL) — never a hand-written artifact INSERT, which would make the golden-set measure against a state production doesn't know how to produce. And the job now requires the golden-set to have MEASURED. The guard is the result line (N/N casos acertaram), which is only printed after the 17 cases run; without it the step fails naming the reason. It's necessary because the {:skip, motivo} the test returns from the BODY is inert — there's no runtime skip in ExUnit, and what you see is Result: 1 passed. That was exactly what happened when measuring: with the seed dying with 409, the test passed. excluded does NOT work as a signal here, unlike what the sibling guard in ci.yml checks: the legitimate output carries over a thousand excluded, which are all the other engine tests, out by the tag. Measured after the three fixes, on this machine, through the path the job now follows: 17/17 in the top-5, the same as the two manual rounds that recorded the floor. Where: .github/workflows/golden-set-rag.yml, docs/gates.yml (rag-acertivo), apps/engine/mix.exs, apps/api/scripts/seed-golden-set-rag.ts ADR: 0138 Origin: the product owner's plan, Part 2 / Stage 3

documents.t: OfferInfraHandoffUseCase offers the handoff to the Infra Lead (offer-infra-handoff.use-case.ts:43), and until now no screen could accept it. offeredHandoff (SessionPage.tsx) restricts the thread's card to AGENTES_DE_CHAT (RN-136), which doesn't include infra, and acceptHandoff (api-client.ts) had a single consumer — that card, behind that filter. The code's own comment recorded the consequence as accepted: "since Infra is never accepted HERE … in practice, never". The effect wasn't cosmetic: the handoff stayed offered forever, the Infra Lead was never activated, propose_container_start was never called (RN-491) and no project of any mode ever got to have a container up. The chain "Infra accepts → proposes container_start → approved → running" was unreachable through any screen path. The filter was NOT widened, and that's the rule. AGENTES_DE_CHAT is right to exclude infra: the engine's agent_command_controller.ex has no message clause for the Infra Lead, and the last clause (unguarded) would treat "infra" as if it were the Criativo — putting infra on the list would make the screen offer a conversation thread that doesn't exist and the composer send a message to the wrong agent. (Since RN-584 the engine refuses by name instead of delivering to the Criativo; the filter remains right for the same reason.) Accepting the Infra is a propositional action, not a conversational one. The actionable card lives, then, outside the thread: in the fixed strip between the scrolling area and the composer, the same one that hosts the manual handoff (RN-440) and already declares itself the place of handoff actions that "aren't conversation, they're redirection". Three consequences the choice buys: the Infra's handoff.offered stays narrated in the thread as a silent divider (nothing changes in the timeline); no conversational handoff changes shape; and the button doesn't disappear when the offer leaves the 200-event window in a long session — the thread's card would depend on the event being visible, this one doesn't. The card states the click's consequence, because it isn't obvious: accepting activates the Infra Lead, which takes over provisioning and will propose bringing up the container; the proposal still goes through the usual approval pipeline (container_start, maintainer, never auto-approvable by seed — RN-491). Accepting brings up no container at all. Closing: the same activeFor(h.toAgent) as the thread's card — a handoff already accepted, or Infra already active in this session by any other path, doesn't reopen the invite. And the click calls the same handleAcceptHandoff, with no second accept path. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (handoffDaInfraOferecido, and the styles.infraHandoffRow block above the manualHandoffRow) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.handoff-da-infra.test.tsx — the card appears and accepts with the right ids; disappears with Infra already active; disappears in a non-active session; the thread's silent divider stays there with no thread button; and the non-regression of RN-136: Infra (older) + Dev Lead (newer) pending show BOTH cards, each accepting its own handoff Origin: exploration of the plan "Name and location on the same screen, and container before the dev agents" (D0) — the blocker that made the requirement "dev agent only after the container is up" equivalent to "dev agent never starts"
documents.s: RN-499 — The Infra's handoff has its OWN actionable card, outside the thread — without widening AGENTES_DE_CHAT

documents.t: Two halves of the same rule: without an execution environment, the dev agent doesn't start, and without an execution environment, the command doesn't run anywhere. The claim guard. Engine.Dev.AgentIo.try_claim/2 — the SINGLE claim point — queries Engine.Containers.ProjectContainerLifecycle.running?/1 BEFORE calling claim_task/1. Without a REGISTERED running row in project_containers (RN-243/ADR 0081), the agent falls into :idle, persists, emits dev.blocked_by_container, and doesn't call the api. The guard comes before the claim on purpose: claiming only to give it back right after would leave the task marked and with no live owner, which is the state block_task/4 exists to never produce. :idle, and not a new status. It's the only state from which a wake still rescues — the guards of handle_info/2 all match it ({:wake, :became_claimable} requires :idle, :rearm requires :idle_tripped, gate_resolved requires a matching task_id, RN-047). An invented :blocked_by_container would be a state from which nothing rescues. In the ENGINE and not only in the api's activate-execution, because the claim has a path no route covers: REHYDRATION. Engine.Dev.DevRehydrator doesn't cast :work; whoever claims after a restart is DevAgentServer.init/1 → finish_restart_recovery/1 → try_claim/2. A gate only at the HTTP boundary would let every rehydrated agent go back to work without a container. The wake. A read doesn't notify anyone: an already stopped agent would stay stopped until an unrelated event passed nearby. So arriving at running PUBLISHES — RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase writes the row and the event in the SAME transaction, aggregateType: 'container' (the third aggregate that Engine.Outbox.Drain now drains, alongside session and task), aggregateId = the PROJECT. Engine.Workers.DevAgentWakeWorker delivers {:wake, :became_claimable} to ALL agents of the project (DevAgentState.list_by_project/1 — the container belongs to the project, not to a module). It's the SAME message that already existed, not a new one: its semantics are already "there may be work now", and an own message would require a new handle_info/2 clause in both servers with a guard identical to the one that already exists. Only running publishes; provisioning/stopped/failed/removed release nobody. The second half: the terminal. Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor degraded silently — container without a running container fell into :caminho_de_sempre, that is, System.cmd INSIDE the engine's process, the same one that talks to the database, the api, and all the other projects. ADR 0134 (RN-492) had closed isolation only on the happy path. Now it refuses (:recusar_container_ausente), mirroring the :recusar_nao_verificado/:recusar_runner_desconectado that runner mode already had (RN-423), and as a normal failed_result — never a crash. mounted enters the SAME branch: with a running container it goes through to the broker like container; without it, it refuses. The :caminho_de_sempre catch-all shrinks to what it should always have been on its own — nonexistent project or malformed project_id. No execution mode falls into it. Declared consequence: a project without a container up stops working, and says why. It's deliberate — it's what the rule exists to do — and that's why it can only come in AFTER the changes that give a container to mounted mode. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/dev/agent_io.ex (try_claim/2), apps/engine/lib/engine/actions/terminal_executor.ex (decisao_de_execucao/1), apps/engine/lib/engine/outbox/drain.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine/workers/dev_agent_wake_worker.ex, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/containers/registrar-transicao-de-container.use-case.ts Test: apps/engine/test/engine/dev/claim_com_container_test.exs — an initial :work without a container falls into :idle, persists, emits, and does not call the api; the Noop goes through the same guard; a REHYDRATED agent stops at :idle without claiming; container.running in the outbox goes through drain → worker → wake → agent and it re-claims; and the usual path stays intact with a running container. apps/engine/test/engine/actions/terminal_executor_test.exs — refusal for container (no row and with stopped) and for mounted; mounted with running goes through to the broker; only a nonexistent project falls into :caminho_de_sempre. apps/api/test/application/use-cases/containers/ciclo-de-vida-do-container.use-case.spec.ts — running publishes container.running on the container aggregate; the other destinations and the row's creation publish nothing ADR: 0143 Origin: the plan "Name and location on the same screen, and container before the dev agents" (PR 7) — ten tasks of exp001 locked up at once because nothing ordered the container before the dev agent
documents.s: RN-502 — A dev agent only claims a task with a running container, and the terminal no longer falls outside it

documents.t: BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE is the only folder of the operator's computer that Brabo's containers see. It's mounted by identity ($X:$X) in the api and engine services, which means the path is the SAME on the host and inside both containers. The identity isn't a style preference. The projects.workspace_path string is typed by the user and shown back to them; with host ≠ container the product would have to choose which of the two to keep, and any choice makes the screen lie to someone. And it's what makes projectScopeRoot (api) and Engine.Actions.Workspace.workspace_dir/2 (engine) remain correct without a single new line of code — the leading-slash discriminator still holds, and the terminal scope of ADR 0055 keeps authorizing exactly the folder the user sees. Absent is a NORMAL state, not an error. baseDeProjetos() returns null when the variable isn't defined or is empty, and NEVER throws. null travels to the client through GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/projects-base (maintainer, the same minimum as POST .../projects, because it's to decide what that route offers that the value exists) and that's how project creation learns not to offer the Mounted folder mode. Offering a mode the installation doesn't honor produces a project that locks up later, at the first tool of the first agent, far from the screen where the decision was made — it's the same lesson as RN-170. dentroDaBaseDeProjetos reuses dentroDoEscopo, the same function as the terminal scope, and not a prefix comparison written again: the trap is exactly the one it already solves — /home/voce/brabo2 is not inside /home/voce/brabo, although the string starts the same. The base itself counts as inside; with a null base, nothing is inside. The base is its OWN variable, never PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR. The three reasons are in the ADR, and the first has data consequences: a managed workspace is named by workspace_dir_name (UNIQUE) and a mounted project is named by the user, so <base>/loja and a container project with workspace_dir_name = loja would land in the SAME physical folder, with init_from_bare! doing git init inside the other's project. The checkout guard lives in the preflight, and it's the only place where it's possible. pnpm dev refuses to come up when the base overlaps Brabo's checkout, in both directions. The api can't do that check: it compares against process.cwd(), which inside its container is /workspace, and never sees the real path on disk. Without that guard, whoever clones Brabo into $HOME/brabo and points the base there passes all the existing validation and makes the dev agents execute inside the product's own tree — ADR 0055's failure coming in through a door it doesn't watch. What this RN does NOT do: it doesn't require a mounted project to be inside the base. caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido and projectScopeRoot stay intact — that predicate runs on every READ, and a legacy mounted project outside the base would start blowing up when read. The base is a CREATION and CONVERSION rule, and comes in the next RN. Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts:67 (baseDeProjetos) and :92 (dentroDaBaseDeProjetos); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/workspaces.controller.ts:197 (GET :workspaceId/projects-base); scripts/dev/base-de-projetos.mjs and the call in scripts/dev/preflight.mjs; docker/docker-compose.yml and docker/docker-compose.prod.yml (services api, engine, broker) Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.spec.ts (describe('baseDeProjetos / dentroDaBaseDeProjetos')) and scripts/dev/base-de-projetos.spec.ts ADR: 0141 Origin: the product owner's plan, PR 1
documents.s: RN-500 — There's ONE base for mounted projects, it's mounted by identity, and absent means "don't offer the mode"

documents.t: RN-500 built the base and said what to do when it's missing — projectsBase: null, and the "Mounted folder" mode isn't offered. What was missing was someone asking for it to be configured: nothing in the product did, and the result is that a ready mode became unreachable for whoever installs. The consent step lives in pnpm bootstrap (Docker › Projects base), proposes $HOME/projetos-brabo, and accepts another typed path. The name isn't a preference: .env.example already uses ~/brabo-projetos as an example of PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR, the root the PRODUCT manages, and proposing the same name for both variables would be walking into the collision that ADR 0141 refused — <base>/loja would land in the same physical folder as a container project whose workspace_dir_name was also loja, and the bootstrap would do git init inside the other's project. The name is only the dodge; the protection is a mechanism. validarBase refuses any candidate that overlaps — in BOTH directions — Brabo's checkout (the guard RN-500 already had) or PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR (the new rule), besides refusing ~, a relative path, and the root. The refusal applies to the TYPED path, not only to the default; a well-chosen default only avoids the refusal being the first thing the user sees. Docker Desktop sharing is proven by MOUNTING, never read from settings.json. That file isn't documented, changes between versions and between macOS and Windows, and describes what the user CONFIGURED — not what the daemon will do. It's the same ruler of "a capability is only declared when proven by execution" of ADRs 0041/0042, applied to the host. The proof is a sentinel, and not a bare ls: an empty folder and a non-shared folder produce the same empty listing, so the script writes a file and asks whether the container sees it. Only on macOS and Windows (process.platform); on Linux there's no sharing list, and the check is existence and write. It's the product's SECOND platform guard, symmetric to the first (validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux, in the runner): each one restricts only where the restriction means something. The proof has three outcomes, and they don't collapse: proven; failed (the variable is not written, and the refusal names the path and where to add it); and couldn't prove — no local Docker image to mount —, which writes the variable and says out loud that the proof didn't run, with the command to run it later. "Couldn't look" becoming "everything's fine" is exactly how a non-shared base would reach the user in the form of a container that comes up with an empty folder, far from the screen where the choice was made. Without a TTY, the step REPORTS and does nothing. The bootstrap.sh menu item runs with stdin coming from /dev/null — on purpose, otherwise anything that reads stdin steals the user's arrow keys — so from there the script can only report, and the output says the command that asks. It's the same design as perguntarUsoDoOllama, which without a terminal applies the default and warns instead of hanging. A consent script that "consents" on its own in a CI pipe is the negation of the word. For the same reason preflight.mjs reports the base's state and never asks: the answer is a path on someone's disk, and there's no default that can be applied silently. mkdir -p only happens after acceptance and validation — creating a folder from a path that hasn't yet gone through the refusals is creating a folder in any place the process reaches. And an already present value is never overwritten without confirmation. Where: scripts/dev/consentir-base.mjs (the I/O: ask, prove, create, write); scripts/dev/base-de-projetos.mjs:143 (basePadrao), :177 (validarBase), and :208 (exigeProvaDeCompartilhamento) — the pure decision; scripts/dev/env-file.mjs (lerEnv/escreverEnv, extracted from preflight.mjs, which runs await main() at the top and therefore can't be imported); scripts/dev/bootstrap.sh (item 1.6); scripts/dev/preflight.mjs (relatarBaseDeProjetos) Test: scripts/dev/base-de-projetos.spec.ts (describe('basePadrao'), describe('validarBase') — happy path and the six refusals — and describe('exigeProvaDeCompartilhamento')); scripts/dev/bootstrap.spec.ts (the menu tree, 25 leaves) ADR: 0146 Origin: PHASE 28, session 2
documents.s: RN-511 — The base is CONSENTED once on the host, sharing is proven by MOUNTING, and without a terminal the step reports instead of consenting

documents.t: The broker was born under profiles: ["container-broker"] with a justification that ADR 0130 itself wrote: "giving access to the host's Docker to a process that nothing calls yet would be a posture change for every development machine, in exchange for nothing". Both halves died. "Nothing calls it" is false since ADRs 0133/0134/0136 — the broker has four real callers. And "in exchange for nothing" stopped describing the trade when ADR 0144 made mounted bring up a container THROUGH THE BROKER and ADR 0146 made mounted the local default: with the profile off, the default mode ends in BrokerIndisponivelError. So it leaves profiles in docker/docker-compose.yml — and only there. In docker/docker-compose.prod.yml the profile STAYS, and the two files start diverging on purpose. The asymmetry is what the socket means on each side. Whoever runs pnpm dev already has the Docker socket — they're running docker compose, against the host's own daemon —, so the broker receiving it grants nothing the operator doesn't already have. The marginal surface is the broker's own HTTP, which publishes no port, lives on an internal: true network only the api reaches, and compares BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN in constant time. In production the calculation is the opposite: the socket is a real privilege boundary, the operator isn't the developer, and nothing in this phase changes the default mode of a production installation. The five containment layers aren't touched. This changes when the broker runs, never what it accepts: it still receives projectId and one of the five operations, still goes to the api to read the Arquiteto's decision, and still has no parameter where one could write privileged, cap_add, network: host, or a free -v. The containment was never the profile. The environmental consequence, and why it got reported. DOCKER_GID stops mattering only to whoever turned the profile on on purpose — someone who was, by definition, paying attention to it — and starts applying to anyone who runs pnpm dev. The socket is root:docker on the host and the broker's process runs non-root; the compose's group_add is what gives it the group, and the default 999 is the most common and is wrong in several distributions. Getting it wrong doesn't break boot — the broker comes up normally —, it breaks USE: every operation dies with permission denied on the socket, and the symptom appears much later, when someone proposes container_start. That's why preflight.mjs now reports the state on every pnpm dev. The report has three outcomes, and they don't collapse: matches; diverges (with the origin of the effective value — configurado × default — because the two ask for different instructions); and doesn't apply, when the machine has no docker group. The third isn't an error nor "couldn't": on macOS and Windows Docker Desktop doesn't use a unix group, and in a rootless Docker the socket belongs to the user themselves. Treating the absence as a divergence would accuse half the machines of a defect they don't have — the same care as baseSobrepoeOCheckout, which returns false for an unknown checkout. And it reports, never blocks: pnpm dev comes up the same. Leaving profiles wasn't enough, and the defect only appeared on the first default startup. The development image prepared pnpm with corepack as root at build time and ran as uid 1000, which doesn't read that cache; without the cache corepack tries to download pnpm at start, and the broker's only network is internal: true — the attempt died with getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN registry.npmjs.org and the container exited with 1, five seconds after coming up. The service also had no healthcheck, so up --wait printed Healthy and the total reset announced "reset completo" with the process dead. While the service was under a profile this never showed up: whoever turned it on on purpose was already watching. The fix takes the registry out of the runtime path — the pnpm install moves to a BUILD step and COREPACK_HOME goes to a directory owned by the runtime uid — and doesn't open the network, which is the first of the five layers above. Since the three node_modules are named volumes mounted over what the image installed, and Docker only seeds an empty volume, docker/broker/entrypoint.sh reconciles the three against a copy kept outside /workspace, stamped with the sha256 of the build's pnpm-lock.yaml — the same stamp that, compared to the tree's lockfile, warns that the image is stale without refusing to come up. The PRODUCTION compose didn't suffer from this: Dockerfile.prod already installed in a build stage, removed corepack from the final image, and already had a HEALTHCHECK. Since AT-360 no image uses corepack (Node 25+ doesn't ship it): pnpm is installed from the registry tarball, checked against a sha512 recorded in the Dockerfile, in /usr/local/bin, and COREPACK_HOME left the dev broker — with the version equal to packageManager's there's no cache to read nor download to attempt at start (measured under --network none). Where: docker/docker-compose.yml (broker service, without profiles, with healthcheck) and docker/docker-compose.prod.yml (with profiles, and the note that prevents uniformizing the two); docker/broker/Dockerfile (pnpm pinned by sha512, the build-time pnpm install, and the copy in /opt/broker-deps); docker/broker/entrypoint.sh (the reconciliation of the three volumes and the lockfile warning); scripts/dev/docker-gid.mjs (avaliarDockerGid, mensagemDoDockerGid, GID_PADRAO_DO_COMPOSE — the pure decision); scripts/dev/preflight.mjs (relatarDockerGid, gidDoGrupoDocker) Test: scripts/dev/docker-gid.spec.ts — the happy path, the two divergences (absent default and wrong value), the "doesn't apply" without a docker group, and the default that happens to be RIGHT ADR: 0146, point 3 Origin: PHASE 28, session 4
documents.s: RN-512 — The broker leaves profiles in the LOCAL compose and only there, and DOCKER_GID now gets reported in the preflight

documents.t: Revised by RN-573 (ADR 0161): the preselection of mounted now ALSO requires the container broker confirmed. With a base and no broker (the installation from a Release), runner is preselected and container/mounted stay inert with the reason in text; with the broker unknown, container stays selected. The rest of this rule holds as is. Two halves of this rule were already rules and had never reached the client. "Don't offer the mode without a base" is RN-500; "suggest <base>/<slug>" is RN-501, and ADR 0142 postponed disk validation precisely so that the wizard could propose a folder that doesn't exist yet. Until now, GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/projects-base had no caller at all in the web, and the "Mounted folder" card was offered unconditionally — in an installation without BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, choosing the mode ended in a 400 refusal from the api after the person had chosen, typed the path, and reached the end of the wizard. What's new is the preselection: with a configured base, mounted is born selected. It revises the default of ADR 0072 (where container is "the normal one" and the local mode is an escape hatch) and revises it only for the local installation, where the base was consented by a human on the host (RN-511). The project_execution_mode enum doesn't change, no new mode is born, and mode conversion (ADR 0111) isn't touched. The query is born with the wizard, not with the step. The "Where the code will live" step is the fifth; a useQuery mounted only there would make the card appear flickering after the person was already looking at the screen. Unknown doesn't become an offer. While the answer hasn't arrived, and also when the query fails (403, network, api down), the card doesn't appear and container stays selected. A failure isn't permission to offer a mode whose precondition couldn't be confirmed: it's the same ruler as RN-088/RN-468 — the product doesn't collapse "don't know" with "doesn't have" — and that of ADRs 0041/0042, where a capability is only declared when proven. The preselection never overrides a human choice. The base arrives over the network, always AFTER the first render. The screen keeps the user's choice separate from the current mode (modoDeWorkspaceEscolhido × modoDeWorkspace), and the preselection only holds while nobody has touched the cards — swapping the mode under the hand of whoever already clicked is a defect, not a convenience. The suggestion never clobbers what was typed. <base>/<slug> comes in in two cases and only in them: an empty field with nothing suggested yet, or a field containing exactly this screen's previous suggestion (the name changed in the details step, and the suggestion follows). Anything else — including the empty field after the user deleted the suggestion — stays as it is. An empty slug (adoption, where the name comes from the provider) doesn't become an invented segment: the field stays empty, and canAdvanceFromWorkspace holds the step. The field is editable the whole time; the preselection didn't relax any advance ruler. And the mode's warning stopped lying. The previous text predated ADR 0141: it said the path was free and that it would only work if the user mounted it. Today there are two states, and they're the two the backend has — under the base, a neutral note (creation passes, and the folder doesn't even need to exist: the Infra creates it when bringing up the container, RN-501); outside the base, a warning saying that the api refuses creation (400, in resolverWorkspacePath) and naming the base, instead of telling you to go look for the variable. An empty field isn't "outside the base": there's no path for the api to refuse yet, and alarming before the person types would be the screen asserting about what it doesn't have. The comparison is by segment, never a raw startsWith — /base-outra isn't inside /base —, mirroring the api's dentroDoEscopo. Where: apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.tsx:220 (the query), :238 (podeOferecerMounted/baseDeProjetos), :283 (the current mode), :333 (caminhoForaDaBase), :360 (the suggestion); apps/web/src/lib/wizard.ts:143 (caminhoSugeridoNaBase) and :171 (caminhoDentroDaBase) — the pure functions; apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts:296 (getProjectsBase) Test: apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.test.tsx (describe('NewProjectWizard — a base de projetos decide o que é oferecido') — base present, null base, query refused with 403, the human choice before the base arrives, and the two states of the warning); apps/web/src/lib/wizard.test.ts (describe('caminhoSugeridoNaBase') and describe('caminhoDentroDaBase')) ADR: 0146, point 4 Origin: PHASE 28, session 3
documents.s: RN-513 — With a consented base, mounted is preselected with <base>/<slug> suggested; without a base, or without knowing, it isn't offered

documents.t: Creating a mounted project stopped touching disk. It requires two things, and both are lexical: the same predicate runner already used (caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido) — absolute, no .., outside the root and system folders, not overlapping Brabo's checkout (RN-422/RN-423); being inside BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE (RN-500), which is the only folder of the computer the api's and the engine's containers see. The project is born with workspaceVerifiedAt: null, exactly like a runner. Why postpone. The requirement is the product owner's and it's literal: "if it's a Mounted folder, the bind-mount must be created AFTER the architect's decision". Disk validation ran at CREATION, which is the first screen of the flow, and the Arquiteto's decision happens many sessions later — requiring the folder ready at creation is requiring it before any decision exists. And it's what prevented mounted from being a first-class choice: a path SUGGESTED by the wizard (<base>/<slug>) is, by construction, a path that doesn't exist yet. The difference between mounted and runner was never what counts as a valid path — it's when and who confirms the disk. In runner it's the CLI connecting; in mounted it's the materialization. Without a configured base, the MODE isn't available. The refusal says so, with the variable's name and what the operator needs to do — it never pretends the path was what was wrong. Outside the base, the refusal names the base and suggests <base>/<the name the person asked for>, never the bare base, which would teach putting the project at the root of all of them. Both messages come from ONE source (motivoDeForaDaBaseDeProjetos), because the two doors that apply the rule — creation/conversion and materialization — refuse for the same reason. The materialization (materializarWorkspaceMontado) is mkdir -p plus the usual three disk questions (does it exist? is it a folder? can it be written?), with the refusal for being outside the base before the mkdir — otherwise a path written outside the product would make the api create a folder anywhere it reaches. Two callers: ExecuteContainerStartUseCase — the normal one. When the Infra brings up the container, the folder is created, proven writable, and workspace_verified_at is stamped by the SAME path ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase uses. Failing is a NAMED failed, never a throw nor a 500 — the same discipline as BrokerIndisponivelError/RunnerNaoConectadoError —, and the lifecycle does not get marked provisioning: marking it and only then finding out that it can't write would leave project_containers asserting a state that never existed. The message names the variable, the path, the probable cause (the folder's owner on the host; the images run non-root, ADR 0024), and the next step ("approve container_start again"). ConvertProjectExecutionModeUseCase — the exception, declared. Conversion has no container step to hang the work on, and right after it MOVES permissions.json to permissionsFilePath(localNova), which in mounted is the user's folder. Moving a file into a nonexistent folder fails, so here mkdir-at-decision is right — before the transaction, so the refusal doesn't leave a transaction open, and becoming a 400. What this RN does NOT do, and it's the easiest regression to cause. The base rule does not go into caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido. That predicate runs on EVERY READ, through projectScopeRoot (terminal scope, permissions.json, Code tab), and a LEGACY mounted project — created when the bind-mount was one compose line per project, therefore outside the base — would start blowing up with LocalizacaoDeProjetoInvalidaError when simply read. The base is a creation and conversion rule; the lexicon is forever. No migration, and the database CHECK stays intact. mounted keeps writing a NON-null workspace_path, so (execution_mode <> 'container') = (workspace_path IS NOT NULL) remains satisfied. Postponing verification never touches the pairing invariant. Declared consequence: between creating the project and bringing up the container, workspace_path points to a folder that may not exist. Nothing breaks (projectScopeRoot is lexical; permissions.json degrades to EMPTY_PERMISSIONS_FILE, which is require_approval on everything), but the screen needs to SAY so — a screen that shows a path without saying it doesn't exist yet is a screen asserting what it doesn't know. Where: apps/api/src/application/services/workspace-location.ts:93 (lexicon) and :108 (base); apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts:575 (motivoDeForaDaBaseDeProjetos), :624 (validarWorkspaceMontadoEmDisco, the former validarCaminhoDeWorkspaceLocal), and :705 (materializarWorkspaceMontado); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.ts:139; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-start.use-case.ts:133 and :334 Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.spec.ts (describe('materializarWorkspaceMontado') and the non-regression "projeto mounted LEGADO, FORA da base, continua resolvendo sem lançar"); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/create-project-modo-de-workspace.spec.ts (describe('mounted valida só o léxico + a base na criação')); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.spec.ts; apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-start.use-case.spec.ts (describe "ExecuteContainerStartUseCase — materialização do mounted") ADR: 0142, which references 0141 Origin: the product owner's plan, PR 2
