documents.t: A project in Mounted folder mode couldn't get any container until now, and for two independent blocks: ExecuteContainerStartUseCase sent every mode other than container to the RUNNER (which requires a connected brabo-runner), and the broker refused at the source any mode that wasn't container, with ModoDeExecucaoNaoSuportadoError. Both existed for the same reason of GEOMETRY, not because of the mode's name: the folder of a mounted project was in an arbitrary place on the operator's disk, which the server's Docker daemon had no reason to see. ADR 0141 (RN-500) changed that geometry — every mounted project now lives under one base mounted by identity —, and that's what, and only what, this rule harvests. The branching is now by DESTINATION, not by mode. container and mounted go to the BROKER; only runner goes to the runner, because its folder remains on a machine this server doesn't reach (ADR 0137). The same holds for the three lifecycle actions — container_start, container_stop, and container_remove: they HAVE to change together, otherwise a mounted project's container comes up on the server and the request to stop goes looking for it on the user's machine, leaving up, with no way to stop it, what is up. ADR 0130's invariant doesn't move: no absolute path crosses the network. The broker is root-equivalent on the host and COMPOSES the -v from ITS roots; if the api sent /home/voce/brabo/loja, the bind-mount's containment would come to depend on the api being correct, which is exactly the dependency the broker exists not to have. What changes is that now there are TWO roots on the other side, so the spec needs to SAY against which of them the relative piece applies — and it says so, in a discriminated locator: localizacao.tipo segment broker root gerenciada workspace_dir_name (RN-109) PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT montada the RELATIVE path under the base BRABO_PROJECTS_HOST_BASE indisponivel — (there's a motivo) none Three states and not two, because the third really exists and has two different fixes: a runner project (the folder is on another machine — the fix is the runner, on the other side) and a LEGACY mounted project created outside the base (the fix is moving the folder). Collapsing them into a null would make the same absence send whoever operates to the wrong place. The folder that IS the base itself also falls here, and doesn't become an empty segment: <raiz>/ would mount the whole base — the folder of ALL mounted projects — inside the container of a single one. The lack of one root is never supplied by the other. Without BRABO_PROJECTS_HOST_BASE, a mounted project's start refuses naming the variable (BaseDeProjetosNaoConfiguradaError, origin infra, 503) and doesn't touch any container — the same mold as RaizDeWorkspacesNaoConfiguradaError. Falling to the other root by omission would be the worst possible outcome: the managed root is named by workspace_dir_name and the base is named by the user, so the same name points to different folders and the container would come up with ANOTHER project's folder, with nothing indicating why. For the same reason, the list of modes the broker serves is an ALLOWLIST: a new mode in the enum is born refused, with a message, instead of accepted by omission. The composition still goes through three barriers, not one. The api refuses what isn't under the base (segmentoSobABaseDeProjetos); the broker refuses a segment that isn't relative (segmentoDeProjetoValidado — .., absolute, empty, double slash, NUL); and the concatenation's result still goes through raizDeProjetoValidada before becoming a -v. Validating the segment and not validating the concatenation would be trusting string arithmetic. mounted ELECTS the image, like container — it doesn't read the current one like the runner. It isn't aesthetic symmetry: it's the only design that works. The broker composes from artifact.project_image, going to FETCH it from the api. An Infra election that wasn't recorded in that artifact would be inert — the container would come up with the image the Arquiteto decided, the payload the human approved would say another, and nothing in the record would expose the difference. The runner's path can read the current one precisely because there the api SENDS the spec's fields through the channel; there the artifact isn't the source the other side consults. What this rule does NOT do: it materializes no folder — whoever creates the folder of the mounted project is RN-501, in the SAME use case and before this branching, precisely because the server's daemon needs the folder to exist to mount it. It also doesn't touch the image gate (RN-105 already applies to the three modes since RN-494) and doesn't change who PROPOSES container_start — the Infra Lead can still propose for a project with no connected runner and no decided image, the gap declared since RN-494. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/containers/obter-spec-de-container.use-case.ts (LocalizacaoDoProjeto, localizacaoDoProjeto); apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts (segmentoSobABaseDeProjetos); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/dto/container-spec-internal.response.dto.ts; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-start.use-case.ts, …/execute-container-stop.use-case.ts, …/execute-container-remove.use-case.ts (the !== 'runner' branching); packages/docker-port/src/docker-port.ts (segmentoDeProjetoValidado); apps/broker/src/config.ts (baseDeProjetosNoHost) and apps/broker/src/operacoes.ts (raizDoProjetoNoHost, garantirModoSuportado, BaseDeProjetosNaoConfiguradaError, LocalizacaoIndisponivelError) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/containers/spec-e-observacao-de-container.use-case.spec.ts (describe('… o localizador discriminado (RN-503)')); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-{start,stop,remove}.use-case.spec.ts; packages/docker-port/src/docker-port.spec.ts (describe('segmentoDeProjetoValidado')); apps/broker/src/operacoes.spec.ts and apps/broker/src/config.spec.ts ADR: 0130, 0141 Origin: the product owner's plan, PR 3
documents.s: RN-503 — A mounted project brings up a container through the BROKER, and what crosses the network is a discriminated locator — never an absolute path

documents.t: GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/project-folders lists the subfolders of a path, and exists because the project creation wizard loses, at once, BOTH "browse folder" mechanisms it had: FolderBrowserModal navigated through the runner's websocket (fs_list_dir/fs_home_dir) and RunnerOnboardingPanel used showDirectoryPicker, which returns a browser handle and never an absolute path. Without a runner, the browser has no way to list any filesystem — and it's an absolute path that projects.workspace_path keeps. The containment is ONE, and it's hard. path is optional and omitted means the base (baseDeProjetos()); every provided path has to satisfy dentroDaBaseDeProjetos (RN-500), which reuses dentroDoEscopo — the same function as ADR 0055's terminal scope — and that's why it catches the prefix trap: /home/voce/brabo2 is not inside /home/voce/brabo, although the string starts the same. .. and . are refused instead of resolved, for the same reason as caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido: resolving would accept that the path read isn't the path requested. Leaving the base is 400, and not 403. 403 would say "you don't have permission to see this" and would suggest another role would see it — that's not the case. There's no role that navigates outside the base, because outside the base isn't a more privileged area, it's an area this route simply doesn't address. The request is MALFORMED. The ceilings are a contract, not an implementation detail: only directories in entries; at most 500, sorted before the cut (otherwise "the first 500" would be the order the filesystem returned, which changes between machines); no recursion; entries starting with . left out; and symlinks reported, never descended — readdirSync(withFileTypes) has lstat semantics, so a link pointing outside the base isn't an exit door. What's left out is COUNTED (arquivos, simbolicos, truncado): without that a folder full of code would come back as an empty list and the screen would say "empty folder", asserting about what it didn't read (RN-180). There's no POST. Creating a folder belongs to the mounted workspace's materialization, at the moment the container comes up — never to the picker. The minimum is maintainer, the same as POST .../projects and .../projects-base, and by the same reasoning one step further: projects-base reveals ONE path of the operator's machine, this route reveals the TOPOLOGY below it. Inheriting the viewer of the neighboring routes because they're neighbors is the defect RN-102 names — the minimum is the ENDPOINT's, never the section's. workspaceId doesn't enter the calculation: the base belongs to the INSTALLATION, and it's in the route because it's what gives scope to RolesGuard. On the client, the transport becomes one of the TWO implementations of the FsBrowser interface (apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser.ts): criarFsBrowserViaApi (new) and connectFsBrowserChannel (the runner's channel, retyped). FolderBrowserModal chooses by origem: { tipo: 'api'; workspaceId } | { tipo: 'runner'; projectId } — a discriminated union, and not two optional props, because "neither of the two" and "both" would be representable states the component would have to handle at runtime. The transport via runner is left with no caller in the web from here on, and stays in the repository by the product owner's declared decision (the runner leaves the interface, the binary keeps being refined); the protocol in apps/runner/src/channel.ts isn't touched in any way. Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-folders-browser.ts (listarPastasDeProjeto, TETO_DE_ENTRADAS, PastaForaDaBaseError, PastaNaoLegivelError); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/workspaces.controller.ts (listProjectFolders); apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser.ts; apps/web/src/components/FolderBrowserModal.tsx Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/project-folders-browser.spec.ts, apps/api/test/interfaces/http/iam/workspaces-project-folders.controller.spec.ts, apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser.test.ts, apps/web/src/components/FolderBrowserModal.test.tsx ADR: 0141 (the base this route scopes) Origin: the product owner's plan, PR 4
documents.s: RN-504 — The folder browser is scoped to the projects base and NEVER leaves it

documents.t: ApproveAlwaysActionUseCase always wrote to permissions.json/allow — WHOLE PROJECT scope, shared by any actor. That meant "always allowing" a command for dev-checkout released the SAME command for dev-auth, for dev-lead, and for any future agent of the project: the intent of whoever clicked ("I trust THIS agent with THIS") had no way to be expressed — only "I trust anyone with this" existed. The write now branches by ACTOR, inside the SAME use case (not a new one — duplicating the two absolute-ceiling guards for out-of-scope terminal/git_push/sudo and for container_remove in two places would be the same defect RN-418/RN-495 already exist to avoid): An agent actor whose id is dev-<modulo> (ADR 0053/PHASE 14d — the DYNAMIC dev area, one agent per module_map module): writes to agent_autonomy(projectId, agentId, actionType) = auto_approve, through the SAME AgentAutonomyRepository.upsert that activate-execution.use-case.ts already calls to seed the three git actions per module. permissions.json stays untouched. Any other actor — user, system, an agent agent that isn't a module dev, and dev-lead — keeps going to the usual permissions.json/allow, whole-project scope, exactly as before. dev-lead is the exception that needs its own name. ehDevDeModulo (agent-areas.ts) is PURE agentId.startsWith('dev-'), on purpose — and that classifies dev-lead as true. What excludes the lead from its own area is ehMembroDe, not ehDevDeModulo alone ("the lead isn't a member of its own area" holds for any area — duplicating the exclusion inside the predicate left both copies unreachable by tests, a finding recorded in the comment of agent-areas.ts itself). That's why the branch uses ehDevDeModulo(actor.id) && actor.id !== DEV_LEAD: without the second term, "always allow" clicked on a dev-lead action would write module autonomy under the LEAD's agentId by accident — an agent that isn't a member of dev, has no module, and that the area never looks at via agent_area_members. The two absolute ceilings of decide.ts keep running BEFORE the branch, without changing order. Terminal with a git external effect (git push, gh pr create) or privileged (sudo/doas) — RN-106/RN-418 — and container_remove — RN-495 — keep refusing the WHOLE click (400, the action not even approved), for ANY actor, before the project is even fetched. Scoping the write per agent isn't a second door to the same ceiling: the two refusal ifs stay where they were, and the new branch comes after. The permission.granted event carries one payload OR the other, never one pretending to be the other. { pattern } remains the format of the permissions.json path (the text pattern written to the file); the new path emits { agentId, actionType } — there's no "pattern" at all to show when the write is a table row keyed by agent. No data migration. Old "always allow" entries written for a module dev in permissions.json, from before this rule existed, stay there exactly as they were — they just no longer receive MORE entries of that kind from then on. A conscious decision by the product owner, not a forgotten gap. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/approve-always-action.use-case.ts (the ehAgenteDeModulo branch), apps/api/src/domain/agents/agent-areas.ts (ehDevDeModulo, DEV_LEAD — consumed, not altered), apps/api/src/application/ports/agent-autonomy-repository.port.ts (upsert, already existing, no new method) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/approve-always-action.use-case.spec.ts (describes escopo por Dev Agent de módulo (RN-509): happy path dev-checkout writes agent_autonomy and doesn't leak to dev-auth; BOTH absolute ceilings refusing the whole click for a module-dev actor; dev-lead and a user actor — including with an id starting with dev- — stay on the old path) Origin: the product owner's plan, Front 2
documents.s: RN-509 — A module Dev Agent's "Always allow" scopes to agent_autonomy, PER AGENT — no longer the whole project's permissions.json

documents.t: A conversational agent that makes a relevant decision in a conversation (why it chose X and not Y, what it considered, what it accepted to lose) records it with emit_artifact and type: decision_record — a payload with context, options (list), choice, and consequences, the four mandatory keys in Engine.Harness.ArtifactSchemas (artifact_schemas.ex:82), tool-emittable since it entered @tool_emittable (artifact_schemas.ex:98). No cross validation on purpose: choice doesn't need to match an item of options — free text is more robust, and the generic schema only validates key presence (the same ruler as note/business_rule). Why reuse the GENERIC pattern instead of the dedicated one. artifact.project_image and artifact.c4_diagram (neighboring RNs of this one) are VERSIONED artifacts — each emission replaces the previous one as "current", with its own HTTP read route and a dedicated TypeScript schema in the api. A decision isn't like that: it's an append-only record by nature, not a "current" that gets replaced — the same reasoning that already holds for note/business_rule. Paying the price of the dedicated pattern (TS schema, versioning, new route) for a log that only needs to exist and be searchable in the session's event log would cost structure the decision doesn't ask for. Declared distinction from open_adr_pr (only the Arquiteto has it). The two COEXIST, with different purposes: decision_record is for EVERY relevant decision of any of the six conversational agents, with no friction at all — it never commits a file, never opens a PR, never waits for human approval. open_adr_pr is for when the decision is big enough to become a real DOCUMENT in docs/adr/*.md, with a real PR and mandatory human approval. A project can have ten decision_record and zero ADR in one session — the second isn't the "serious" version of the first, it's another tool for another scale of decision. Wiring in the five conversational agents that didn't have emit_artifact yet — PO (po_server.ex:115), Arquiteto (arquiteto_server.ex:103), Dev Lead (dev_lead_server.ex:153), UX Designer (ux_designer_server.ex:94), and Staff (staff_server.ex:94); the Criativo already had the tool since Phase 3b, it only gained the new type (it's the shared known/0 that decides, with no change to CriativoServer). In each one, the common run_tool/3 gained the clause "emit_artifact" -> EmitArtifact.run/2 (e.g. po_server.ex:279) — with no special handling: unlike propose_execution_plan/ assess_implementability in the Dev Lead (which suspend the turn waiting for approval, ADR 0086), emit_artifact never returns {:pending, _}, so it enters the common dispatch without needing the reduce_while those two tools require. And the five gained the SAME sentence in system_prompt/1 (e.g. po_server.ex:463) explaining when to use type: decision_record — outside the identity text (Engine.Harness.Agents) because it isn't about WHO the agent is, it's an operational instruction about a tool. Out of scope, declared. Execution agents (QA, SecOps, module Dev Agent) run on ToolLoop, with no harness common to the six conversational ones — they're left out of this slice, with their own per-module investigation before extending. Tying it to Front 1 of the same plan (the Infra Lead's dispatch emitting a server-emitted decision_record when it proposes bringing up a container via runner) is also left out: it depends on a tool (propose_container_start_via_runner) another PR is creating in parallel — see the TODO in this change's PR. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/artifact_schemas.ex (schema + @tool_emittable); apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/po_server.ex, arquiteto_server.ex, dev_lead_server.ex, ux_designer_server.ex, staff_server.ex (alias + tool_specs + run_tool/3 + system_prompt/1) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/harness/artifact_schemas_test.exs (describe("decision_record …")); apps/engine/test/engine/agents/po_server_test.exs and arquiteto_server_test.exs (describe("Frente 3 do plano de decision_record — emit_artifact")) Origin: the product owner's plan, Front 3 ("Decision artifact")
documents.s: RN-505 — decision_record reuses the GENERIC pattern of emit_artifact, not the dedicated one

documents.t: Until now, Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor.decisao_de_execucao/1 checked only TWO preconditions to route the terminal to an execution_mode: runner project — workspace CONFIRMED and runner CONNECTED now — and routed unconditionally as soon as both matched, without checking whether there was a REGISTERED running container (Engine.Containers.ProjectContainerLifecycle.running?/1), the same predicate container/mounted had already required since RN-502 (ADR 0143). The runner on the other side decided on its own whether the command ran inside the container it brought up (ADR 0137) or fell to the bare HOST — and without Docker up on the user's machine, it always fell to the host, silently: the isolation ADR 0134 sought to create for container never applied to runner. The fix unifies the three modes under the SAME question. runner gains a THIRD precondition, in the same order as the other two: verified → connected → running container. The three named refusals (workspace not verified, runner disconnected, no container) live today in Engine.Runners.RunnerReadiness — extracted because a SECOND consumer was born in the same PR (Engine.Actions.Workspace.RunnerGit, below): "they aren't two derivations, it's this function with two consumers", the same reasoning as the moduledoc of ProjectContainerLifecycle. The dev agent's worktree materialization changes mechanism, not result. Engine.Actions.Workspace.ensure!/4 tried LOCAL File.mkdir_p!/ System.cmd("git", ...) against the HOST path, even in runner mode — the gap RN-478 recorded and left OPEN on purpose ("the dev agent's working tree has nowhere to be born", since the engine's process has no bind-mount at all for a folder that lives on the user's machine). The fix isn't "improve the error message" again: ensure!/4 now forks by execution_mode — LOCAL for container/mounted (unchanged: mounted already sees its folder via BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, a bind-mount by identity in the engine since ADR 0141), via Engine.Actions.Workspace. RunnerGit for runner. RunnerGit does git init/remote add/fetch/ checkout (and the equivalents of File.dir?/ls/rm_rf that Engine.Dev.WorktreeManager needs) as NORMAL shell commands, delivered through the SAME Phoenix channel that already executes approved terminal commands (Engine.Runners.RunnerRouter.exec/5) — never a new mechanism, and always after RunnerReadiness.verificar/1 confirms the three preconditions (it raises with a named message before attempting any I/O, never a blind exec). Engine.Dev.WorktreeManager (create/3, remove/2, list/1, cleanup_orphans/2) forks by the same criterion. The periodic cleanup job SKIPS silently, never fails. Engine.Dev.WorktreeCleanup.run/0 swept File.dir?(work_dir) to decide whether to prune — always false for runner (the path is the HOST's, the engine doesn't see it), so runner was never really pruned nor tested through that path. The gate becomes by MODE: File.dir? stays for container/mounted; for runner, RunnerReadiness.pronto?/1 decides — with no runner connected or no running container NOW, the project is skipped IN THIS round ("can't know now", never an error, never a worktree treated as an orphan by mistake), and Enum.each/2 continues to the following projects without any exception crossing it. The exec/exec_result protocol gains a NEW field: env (ADR 0056). The authenticated git fetch of RunnerGit needs the provider's credential — which can only travel in the child process's ENVIRONMENT (never argv, never .git/config, the same discipline as the local Engine.Actions.GitAuth). Since the child process is now born on the user's machine, the env field (optional, Record<string,string>) enters the payload that RunnerRouter.exec/5 dispatches — present only when there's a real credential (the local provider never carries it). On the runner's side: apps/runner/src/exec.ts MERGES (never replaces) opts.env on top of process.env before the spawn — an env defined without merge would discard PATH and break the resolution of the git/sh binary itself. apps/runner/src/index.ts passes msg.env only to the HOST path (executarComando) — the container (docker exec, via packages/docker-port) didn't gain env support (out of scope of this delivery: the port's exec operation still lacks that field, on purpose, ADR 0130). No runner log prints env anywhere — audited by grep, console.log/console.warn/console.error keep citing only ref/command/cwd/exitCode. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/actions/terminal_executor.ex (decisao_de_execucao/1); apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/ runner_readiness.ex (new); apps/engine/lib/engine/actions/workspace.ex (ensure!/4); apps/engine/lib/engine/actions/workspace/runner_git.ex (new); apps/engine/lib/engine/dev/worktree_manager.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/dev/worktree_cleanup.ex; apps/engine/lib/engine/projects/project.ex (all_workspace_dirs/0 gains execution_mode); apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/runner_router.ex (exec/5); apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel.ex; apps/runner/src/channel.ts (ExecMessage.env); apps/runner/src/exec.ts; apps/runner/src/index.ts Test: apps/engine/test/engine/actions/terminal_executor_test.exs, apps/engine/test/engine/actions/workspace_runner_test.exs, apps/engine/test/engine/dev/worktree_manager_test.exs, apps/engine/test/engine/dev/worktree_cleanup_test.exs, apps/runner/src/channel.spec.ts ADR: 0145 Origin: the product owner's decision — Docker becomes a real prerequisite of runner mode, with no fallback to the host
documents.s: RN-507 — Docker becomes a real prerequisite of runner mode: the THREE execution modes require the SAME predicate

documents.t: container_start (ADR 0130/0133) requires imagem/network/resources/ rationale — the Infra ELECTS a candidate from the Arquiteto's routing. Until this delivery, the same action type also served execution_mode: runner (ExecuteContainerStartUseCase.executeViaRunner), but the runner's path NEVER read any of those four fields: the image that comes up is the one already DECIDED (there's no routing to elect against, because the broker never reaches a runner project's folder). Asking for 4 fields the dispatch always discarded is the defect that motivates a separate ACTION being born instead of a "smart" container_start branching by mode. container_start_via_runner only has rationale (optional). The same caliber as container_start (maintainer, require_approval by default, never seeded in auto-approval, configurable in permissions.json like the other three container actions — it doesn't enter the absolute ceiling of container_remove). ExecuteContainerStartUseCase loses the whole runner branch (executeViaRunner, ApiToEngineClient/ObterSpecDeContainerUseCase leave the constructor) — it becomes exclusive to container/mounted, both through the BROKER (RN-503). The extracted code becomes ExecuteContainerStartViaRunnerUseCase, a sibling file. The lifecycle dance (provisioning -> running) the two paths shared by copy becomes SubirCicloDeVidaDoContainerUseCase (apps/api/.../containers/) — extracted so as not to duplicate the state machine's rationale in the two files. The Infra Lead queries LOCALLY, without HTTP, before proposing. The new tool (Engine.Infra.Tools.ProposeContainerStartViaRunner) is intercepted by Engine.Infra.InfraLeadServer.dispatch_calls/2, which reads Project.get/1 (execution_mode) and Engine.Runners.Registry.connected?/1 (runner connected) — BOTH reads are already local, in the same BEAM process — BEFORE calling propose_action. It refuses with a NAMED reason (never proposes blindly) when the project is in container (use propose_container_start), in mounted (likewise, since RN-503), or in runner with no runner connected now. This gap — "proposing without knowing whether it'll work" — is the SAME one propose_container_start has had since RN-494, declared and accepted for that tool (touching the Infra Lead's prompt/instruction would be outside the API/domain scope); the NEW tool is born without it, because it's born knowing how to refuse. The specification the api composes is the one the runner VALIDATES, and that is now proven. EspecificacaoDeContainerParaRunner is the fields of EntradaDeEspecificacao (packages/docker-port) minus raizDoProjeto, which only the runner knows — TEN, not nine. It was born with nine, without projectId, and the consequence was that this path NEVER brought up any container since it existed: the engine passes the map on opaquely, the runner hands it to especificacaoValidada, which requires projectId as non-empty text, and the action ended failed with "especificação de container recusada em projectId: esperava texto não vazio, recebi undefined" — and from there the CORRECT block of RN-507/RN-502 did the rest, with no dev agent claiming a task. The data always existed (SpecDeContainer.projectId, the same one the BROKER receives through GET .../container-spec, and that's why only runner mode broke); it just wasn't copied. Three green suites didn't catch it because each one built its own fixture: the use case's test asserted what it itself expected, the runner's built a fixture WITH projectId, and the engine doesn't look at the map. What is now guaranteed is the CHAIN — the payload ExecuteContainerStartViaRunnerUseCase composes, going through the real especificacaoValidada —, and the test also locks the set of fields: raizDoProjeto is the only one the api doesn't send, so a new field on one side without the other fails. Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts (container_start_via_runner); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/ execute-container-start-via-runner.use-case.ts (new); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/containers/ subir-ciclo-de-vida-do-container.use-case.ts (new); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/propose-action.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/approve-action.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/application/ports/api-to-engine-client.port.ts (EspecificacaoDeContainerParaRunner, the ten fields); apps/web/src/lib/aprovacoes.ts; apps/engine/lib/engine/infra/tools/propose_container_start_via_runner.ex (new); apps/engine/lib/engine/infra/infra_lead_server.ex Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/execute-container-start.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/ execute-container-start-via-runner.use-case.spec.ts (new), apps/api/test/contract/ especificacao-de-container-para-runner.contract.spec.ts (the CHAIN — the payload composed by the api against the real especificacaoValidada), apps/web/src/lib/aprovacoes.test.ts, apps/engine/test/engine/infra/tools/ propose_container_start_via_runner_test.exs (new), apps/engine/test/engine/infra/infra_lead_server_test.exs ADR: 0145 Origin: the product owner's decision — Docker becomes a real prerequisite of runner mode, with no fallback to the host
