documents.t: Until now the join of the terminal:<projectId> channel was mute on both sides: the runner sent socket.channel(\terminal:${projectId}`, {}) and the server literally ignored them (def join("terminal:" <> project_id, _params, socket)). The whole identity came from the ticket — the role (:runner/:web) comes from the kind` —, and the server had no way of knowing whether the binary on the other side was from a version that understands a new message. The defect this produces is the worst possible one, and it is what this rule closes: the message arrives, the handler does not exist on the other side, and nothing happens — no error, no log, nobody knowing that the function never ran. Three capabilities, and only what the runner can do is declared. The server's vocabulary is exec (approved command, ADR 0104), pty (interactive terminal, ADR 0103) and espelho (copying the work to a folder outside the mounted base). The runner declares exec and pty, and espelho is left out on purpose: declaring what is not implemented is exactly the defect the negotiation exists to prevent — the server would grant it, deliver the message, and it would vanish just the same. espelho is born only as a name in the vocabulary, with no behavior at all; whoever implements it is session 6 of PHASE 28. Absence of params is the LEGACY, and that is a fact — not benevolence. Every binary prior to this change sends empty params, and every binary prior to this change can do exec and pty: they are the two functions the runner was born with. Granting {exec, pty} to whoever declares nothing is reading correctly the only thing that binary could have said. The opposite would make every installed runner stop connecting, which is a change requiring operator action before deploy — breaking/ and MAJOR, by the repository's convention, and that is not what this delivery is. Absent params, absent capacidades, an empty list and a value that is not a list all fall into the legacy: they are the shapes that "this binary cannot declare anything" takes on the network path. Unknown is IGNORED, never a reason for refusal. The granted set is the intersection of what was declared with the vocabulary that this server knows — a runner NEWER than the engine has to be able to connect. Declaring only unknown names, however, is an empty declaration, not legacy: whoever can declare said what it can do. What each mode REQUIRES. runner requires exec — it is literally what makes the mode work, and without it the TerminalExecutor would route an approved command to a binary that does not execute it, with the failure showing up as a timeout instead of a refusal. container and mounted require nothing (the runner is not even their execution path). Nothing requires espelho yet — the refusal mechanism is born implemented and tested, and does not fire in practice today. That is the design, not a pending item. A mode that could not be read (nonexistent project, malformed id, failed query) requires nothing: refusing on an unconfirmed precondition would be collapsing "I don't know" with "it doesn't have" (RN-088). The granted set lives in socket.assigns, never in a table. A capability is a property of that connection — a table could claim that a runner knows something the process connected now does not. It is the same reasoning that makes the :global entry of Engine.Runners.Registry die together with the pid. Only the :runner role receives a set: the :web socket does not get :capacidades and no capability check applies to it — the tab executes nothing, it asks. A join refusal names the one missing. {:error, %{reason: ...}} saying which capability the project requires and that the binary needs to be updated. The refusal is fatal on the runner side, with no retry (JoinRecusadoError, behavior that already existed and did not change) — that is why it is the only chance to explain, and "refused" without the name of what is missing would force guessing. The check happens before Registry.register/2: registering and then refusing would leave the Registry asserting a runner that did not get in. And the half that delivers value today: a message without the granted capability is REFUSED with a named reply, never swallowed. exec to a runner without exec answers the caller in the same exec_result format that the runner would send (exitCode 126 — "found, but not executable" —, the cause in output), instead of leaving the RunnerRouter blocked until the receive ... after and the user seeing a timeout in place of the cause. pty_* to a runner without pty is not relayed, and the originating :web receives a named pty_error, through the same filtered broadcast the runner would use to report a PTY error — without it the tab would stay "loading" forever, the defect that the whereis of handle_in("pty_open", ...) had already closed for the "no runner" case. Since the legacy has both capabilities, nothing changes for anyone today. This is not a security boundary. A capability is a protocol negotiation; what authorizes is still the single-use ticket (RN-108) and the proposed_action pipeline. What the runner gains by declaring is that messages of that type are delivered to it, never permission for anything. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/capacidades.ex (new — the vocabulary, the legacy, what each mode requires and the two messages); apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel.ex:208 (join/3 now receives params), :215 (autorizar_por_papel/3), :251 (entrar_como_runner/3, the grant before the Registry), :305 (exigencias_do_projeto/1, which was modo_de_execucao/1 until RN-516 made the same query also answer the mirror destination), :595 (the exec gate in handle_info({:dispatch_exec, ...})) and :762 (the pty one in handle_info({:relay, "pty_" <> _, ...})); apps/runner/src/channel.ts (CAPACIDADES_DO_RUNNER and the params of socket.channel/2) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/runners/capacidades_test.exs (new — the pure vocabulary: legacy, empty list, unknown ignored, what each mode requires, and that nothing requires espelho); apps/engine/test/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel_test.exs (describe "capacidades declaradas no join (ADR 0147 ponto 1, RN-514)" — grant in assigns, join without params, unknown ignored, :web without a set, the refusal naming exec in a runner project, and the two refused messages with a reply instead of silence); apps/runner/src/channel.spec.ts (the CONTENT of the join params, espelho out of the list, and the refusal becoming JoinRecusadoError with the server's message readable) ADR: 0147, point 1 Origin: PHASE 28, session 5
documents.s: RN-514 — The runner DECLARES what it can do on join, the server GRANTS the intersection in socket.assigns, and a message without the capability is REFUSED instead of vanishing

documents.t: The espelho capability (RN-514, ADR 0147) copies the agents' work to a user folder outside the mounted base — which is the reason it exists, because a bind mount does not cross a network nor reach a path outside what was mounted. This rule decides where that destination lives and how the user declares it; it does not copy any file. PER PROJECT, never global. The destination is the projects.mirror_path column and the project's mirrorPath field, written by PUT /projects/:projectId/mirror-path (maintainer, the same minimum as execution-mode and projects-base: the route speaks of a path on the operator's computer). Never a global setting in the runner, never an environment variable: a global destination would make project B's artifact land in project A's folder, and the user would find that out through the content, not through an error (ADR 0147, point 4). null is the NORMAL state, not a pending item. The column is nullable and is born null; a project without a mirror is the majority, and the product never picks a destination on its own. Clearing is {"mirrorPath": null} — the key is mandatory, and omitting it is 400: a body that omits the field would be indistinguishable from "clear", and clearing silently is precisely the defect. Clearing always works, even in a container project, otherwise a converted row would be stuck in the state the rule forbids. Only the LEXICON, and the api SAYS it is only the lexicon. The api does not see the machine where the destination will exist — it is the situation of the runner mode (RN-423), not that of mounted, where the folder ends up inside the base the api actually reaches. It reuses caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido, the same predicate as creation and conversion (absolute, no ../., never the root nor a system folder, never overlapping the Brabo checkout), instead of a fourth copy of the same rule — and it does not require BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, because the mirror destination is by definition the folder the base does not cover. The refusal message declares that the disk was not verified and who verifies it. The two directions of the same loop. A destination inside the workspacePath and a destination that contains the workspacePath are the same refusal seen from two sides (ADR 0147, point 2): writing the mirror inside the source makes the mirror copy itself, and a source inside the destination nests the copy on every round. Refusing one and allowing the other would be closing the door and leaving the window open. The comparison is by SEGMENT (dentroDoEscopo), never raw startsWith: /base-outra is not inside /base, and refusing it would penalize a perfectly legitimate sibling folder. This is the LEXICAL half of the guard, and only it. The other is realpath, and it belongs to the RUNNER (espelho-guard.ts, ADR 0147 point 2), on the machine where both paths really exist. A symlink in any segment of the destination pointing back to the source passes through here unseen — the api has no disk on which to resolve it. The api did not guarantee the loop; it prevented the WRITTEN loop. container is refused, and the refusal is NAMED. The source of a container project is a managed volume on the server, and whoever would copy is a process on the user's machine, which does not see it. Accepting and never copying would be worse than refusing, because it would look configured. mounted and runner can. For the same reason, converting the mode ZEROES the destination (RN-447..450): in container it could not exist, and even between mounted and runner the conversion MOVES the source against which both directions of the loop were validated. The value comes back in every project read (ProjectResponseDto.mirrorPath), so the mirror implementation and the status screen do not need a new route. There is no dedicated read endpoint. And it is NOT a proposed_action. Writing the mirror is configuration the user declared, not an agent asking to act — ADR 0147 is explicit about it, and syncing via a terminal command would fall into the scope of ADR 0055 and become a queue of routine approvals. Where: apps/api/src/db/schema/iam.ts (mirror_path column, nullable, no CHECK — the container refusal lives in the use case because the mode is CONVERTIBLE); apps/api/src/db/migrations/0056_lovely_firelord.sql; apps/api/src/domain/iam/project.entity.ts (mirrorPath); apps/api/src/application/services/workspace-location.ts (validarDestinoDeEspelho — the reused lexicon, the container refusal and the two directions of the loop); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/set-project-mirror-path.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.ts (the conversion zeroing the destination); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/dto/set-mirror-path.dto.ts (@IsDefined @ValidateIf, never @IsOptional, which would collapse null and undefined); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/projects.controller.ts (PUT :projectId/mirror-path, maintainer); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/dto/iam.response.dto.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/set-project-mirror-path.use-case.spec.ts (writes, normalizes, clears, clears even in container, refuses non-absolute/../root/system folder/Brabo checkout, the two directions of the loop, /base-outra vs /base NOT being inside, container refused, 404); apps/api/test/interfaces/http/iam/projects-execution-mode.controller.spec.ts (describe "destino do espelho (RN-515)" — maintainer and the passing through of null); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/convert-project-execution-mode.use-case.spec.ts (the conversion zeroing the destination); apps/api/test/interfaces/route-surface.spec.ts (the route classified in docs/security-surface.md) ADR: 0147, point 4 Origin: PHASE 28, session 6 (half A — where the destination lives; the copy, the mirror_sync and the second realpath pass are half B, in the engine and in the runner)
documents.s: RN-515 — The mirror destination is declared PER PROJECT and is never global; null is the normal state; and the api validates ONLY the lexicon, saying it is only the lexicon

documents.t: Half B of session 6 of PHASE 28: the espelho capability (RN-514, ADR 0147) comes to EXIST. RN-515 decided where the destination lives and did not copy any file; this one decides how it reaches the local agent, what is copied and when. The destination travels in the join grant, never in runner configuration. The join reply of the terminal:<projectId> channel is no longer empty for the :runner role: when the project has a declared destination (projects.mirror_path) and the espelho capability was granted, it carries %{espelho: %{destino: "<caminho>"}}. The runner keeps this in estado.destinoDoEspelho, which dies with the connection, and refuses mirror_sync for a destination not granted to it on that connection (ADR 0147, point 4). Never an environment variable, never a local file: a global destination would make project B's artifact land in project A's folder, and the user would find that out through the content, not through an error. A declared consequence, and it is the price: changing the destination with the runner connected requires reconnecting it. The grant belongs to the join, and a new destination arriving through another door would be exactly the global configuration the rule refuses. A non-null mirror_path now REQUIRES the capability. It does not enter the map by execution_mode — what requires it is a project DATUM, not the mode (and mounted and runner can have a destination while container cannot). This is the first REAL case of the refusal mechanism RN-514 left implemented and never firing: a brabo-runner older than this version connected to a project with a destination stops connecting, with a named refusal (JoinRecusadoError, fatal and with no retry). It is opt-in — it only happens where someone configured a destination — and the cost is declared in ADR 0147 itself. The THREE refusals of the guard, and the realpath pass is not redundant. apps/runner/src/espelho-guard.ts is a sibling of guard.ts, not an extension of it: it reuses semBarraFinal/dentroDoEscopo/realpathMaisProximo and the double lexical-then-realpath pass of validarCwdDentroDaRaiz, and inherits in writing the same TOCTOU caveat — it is best-effort, not a security boundary. It refuses (1) a symlink escaping the destination, (2) a destination that contains the workspace and (3) a destination inside the workspace; (2) and (3) are the same loop in opposite directions, and with the identity bind of ADR 0141 writing the mirror inside the source makes the mirror copy itself. The api already refused the lexical half (RN-515) and says, in the code itself, that it is only the lexicon — it has no disk on which to resolve a symlink on the user's computer. destino/atalho -> /caminho/do/projeto passes through there unseen, and it is here that it is resolved. A difference in mechanism, found while implementing: realpathMaisProximo falls back to the first ancestor that exists, and the mirror destination almost never exists (it is the mkdir -p of this round that creates it). Collapsing both sides onto the ancestor would make /base-outra and /base both become /, and the guard would refuse every sibling folder. That is why the second pass resolves the ancestor and puts the suffix back — a symlink can only live in a segment that exists, so what remains never hides any link. Refusal (1) also has a second half, per file (caminhoNoDestino): a destino/sub that links to /etc would make the copy of sub/passwd write outside, with the destination itself perfectly valid. One direction, and it NEVER deletes. Workspace → destination. Never --delete, never unlink, never rm. A file deleted in the workspace remains in the destination, and that is a decision, not carelessness: the user's folder is not a replica, it is an accumulation — an agent that deletes a file in someone's personal folder because of a git clean on the other side is the surprise the product exists not to produce. Overwriting a file that changed is expected; removing never is. The price, declared in the ADR: the destination only grows, and no automatic mechanism cleans it. What is copied is the GIT LIST, and nothing else. The tracked files (git ls-files) plus the untracked ones that are not ignored (git ls-files --others --exclude-standard), with -z (git quotes and escapes a path with a space or accent without it). That is exactly "the work": it skips node_modules, dist, build output and .git itself without keeping any exclusion list, which would age with every new stack — the project's .gitignore is already the list, maintained by whoever maintains the project. The workspace is a git repository by construction (the product provisions Gitflow in it and materializes it with git init/fetch/checkout), so the precondition belongs to the PRODUCT, not an assumption about the machine. Git that fails or a folder that is not a repository fail with a named reason — never a cp -r of everything as a plan B, which is how an entire node_modules would end up in someone's personal folder. Two properties verified and declared, not hidden: a nested git repository comes back as ONE directory entry and is not descended into — the worktree of each dev agent (<workspace>/.worktrees/<agent_id>) is one of those, so the mirror shows the main checkout, never the work still isolated in a worktree; and a symlink at the source is skipped, because following the link would bring content from outside the project into the personal folder. What is left out is COUNTED (pulados/recusados), never swallowed. And there is no "did it change?" heuristic: always copying costs bytes that are already equal, while skipping by size+mtime would make the mirror silently not copy a file that changed. Its OWN predicate, and the mirror does not require Docker. Engine.Runners.RunnerReadiness stays byte for byte as it is (ADR 0147, point 3) — Engine.Runners.Espelho does not call it, does not extend it and receives nothing from it. The mirror has TWO preconditions, confirmed workspace and connected runner, and not the third that RN-507 added (container REGISTERED running). A RunnerReadiness with a "skip container" flag is precisely the mechanism by which that third one would fall by accident for exec in a future refactoring, and ADR 0145 exists so that it does not fall. And the mirror legitimately does not need it: the third exists because there were two possible executions and the wrong one was invisible; a file copy on the user's machine has no container to fall from. It also does not ask for the execution_mode — whoever already decided that was the api when writing the destination (RN-515 refuses container), and repeating the decision would be the second source of the same rule. Trigger by a NAMED MOMENT, never a watcher. The engine pushes mirror_sync from a point in the code that has a name — today the successful commit (EngineWeb.ActionCommandController, git_commit). Never fs.watch: a watcher is unbounded work triggered by anything — a dependency install, a build, and worse, by the mirror's own writes, which is a loop — and would run continuously on the user's machine without anyone having asked, which is the opposite of what "local agent" should mean. The push is fire-and-forget: no from, no pending_execs and no mirror_sync_result, because whoever triggered it is in the middle of something else and the sync telemetry is point 7 of the ADR, from another session. A mirror failure becomes a local log, never an exception that takes the runner down and never silence. It is NOT a proposed_action, and must not become one. Writing the mirror is configuration the user declared, not an agent asking to act — ADR 0147 is explicit about it, and syncing via a terminal command would fall into the scope of ADR 0055 and become a queue of routine approvals, eroding the ceiling that gives the click its meaning. Where: apps/runner/src/espelho-guard.ts (the three refusals, the double pass with the suffix preserved, the inherited TOCTOU caveat); apps/runner/src/espelho.ts (the git list, the one-direction copy, the mkdir -p only AFTER the guard); apps/runner/src/guard.ts (the three helpers are now exported — a single source of path comparison); apps/runner/src/channel.ts (CAPACIDADES_DO_RUNNER gains espelho, MirrorSyncMessage, EspelhoConcedido, espelhoConcedidoDaResposta); apps/runner/src/index.ts (EstadoDoRunner.destinoDoEspelho, tratarMirrorSync — the refusal of the non-granted destination); apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/capacidades.ex (exigidas/2/conceder/3 and destino?/1 — the destination, not the mode, is what requires); apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/espelho.ex (the own predicate, the destino/1 of the join and the fire-and-forget sincronizar/2); apps/engine/lib/engine/projects/project.ex (mirror_path in the read schema); apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel.ex (the grant in the join reply and the dispatch_mirror_sync); apps/engine/lib/engine_web/controllers/action_command_controller.ex (the commit trigger) Test: apps/runner/src/espelho-guard.spec.ts (destination inside, destination containing, real symlink in tmp escaping through the destination itself and through a middle segment, /base-outra vs /base, the per-file target, lstat vs stat); apps/runner/src/espelho.spec.ts (real git repository: tracked + untracked-not-ignored, ignored left out, file deleted at the source remains in the destination, nested repository skipped, source symlink skipped, destination symlink refused, guard before the mkdir, folder without git failing named); apps/runner/src/channel.spec.ts (the destination coming in the join reply, the three declared capabilities, mirror_sync reaching the handler); apps/runner/src/index-handlers.spec.ts (describe "tratarMirrorSync" — the non-granted destination refused, the connection without a grant, the failure that does not throw, and the channel with no push back at all); apps/engine/test/engine/runners/capacidades_test.exs (the destination requiring the capability, the legacy binary refused, destino?/1); apps/engine/test/engine/runners/espelho_test.exs (the TWO preconditions and the ABSENCE of the third — :pronto with no container registered at all); apps/engine/test/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel_test.exs (describe "o destino do espelho na concessão do join" — the grant, the two refusals and the mirror_sync push); apps/engine/test/engine_web/controllers/action_command_controller_test.exs (the trigger: a successful commit fires, a failing commit does not fire) ADR: 0147, points 2, 3, 4 and 8 Origin: PHASE 28, session 6 (half B). The second named moment of point 8, "end of agent turn", was declared and not wired: the engine has two disjoint things with that name and neither is an unambiguous hook — Engine.Agents.TurnoAssincrono.finalizar/1 closes the turn of the six conversational agents, which have no write tool in the workspace, and also fires on crash and on cancellation; Engine.Dev.AgentIo.finish_task/3 is not an idleness boundary (it claims the next task in the same call) and what the dev agent writes lives in the worktree, which the mirror deliberately does not descend into. Choosing one would be inventing product where the ADR named a moment without naming a function
documents.s: RN-516 — The mirror destination travels in the join GRANT, the mirror copies the git list in one direction only and never deletes, and the trigger is a named moment — never a watcher

documents.t: Session 8 of PHASE 28 and point 7 of ADR 0147. RN-516 made the mirror really copy and left mirror_sync fire-and-forget — with no mirror_sync_result in the protocol, on purpose, because the telemetry format was this delivery's decision. It is this one that closes the loop. The path is that of workspace_confirm, and no other. The runner pushes mirror_sync_result on the terminal:<projectId> channel after the round ends; the engine handles it in handle_in/3 and RELAYS it to the api over internal HTTP (POST /internal/projects/:projectId/mirror-sync-result), which writes through the use case. The engine does not write the table — a second write path would be the second source of the same truth, and the first thing to diverge. It is the only precedent of the runner telling something about itself, and that is why the ADR named it. Never an optimistic "ok". The reported outcome is the REAL one: the three counts that sincronizarEspelho returned (copied, skipped, refused — never recounted) or the named error. ALL THREE exits of tratarMirrorSync report, and with different messages: the refusal for a non-granted destination, the copy failure and the success. ok is NEVER deduced from there being a count or a message — neither in the runner, nor in the engine's translation, nor in the api's use case: deducing would make a round that copied 0 files (perfectly normal) indistinguishable from one that never even ran. A TABLE, and not the event log. project_mirror_states, one row per project (unique project_id, same design as project_containers). The reason is the same one that made rag_searches become a table (RN-479): session_events.session_id is NOT NULL and a mirror round has no session — the event log would lose the whole thing, not part of it. And it is not a proposed_action under any circumstances: writing the mirror is configuration the user declared, not an agent asking to act. The THREE states of RN-088, and they do not collapse. "Never synced" is the absent row. "Synced and copied nothing" is a present row with files_copied = 0 — an outcome, not an emptiness. "Failed" is last_error_at more recent than last_synced_at. They are three different answers, the person acts differently on each one, and a dash serving all three would be the screen refusing to name what it knows (RN-470). Success and error COEXIST in the same row. The two writes mention disjoint columns: the success one does not touch last_error/last_error_at, the failure one does not touch any success column, and neither erases the other. What decides which one is CURRENT is the comparison of the two timestamps (deriveMirrorSyncStatus, a pure domain function), and that is what lets the screen say "the last round failed — last good copy yesterday, with 412 files". A destructive write of one side over the other would throw away precisely the most useful information the screen has while the mirror is broken. Two smaller choices in the same direction: a failure WITHOUT a destination does not erase the destination of the last copy that worked, and an exact timestamp tie resolves to failed — between asserting that everything is fine and asserting that something failed, the safe assertion is the one that makes the person look. destination is FROZEN, like image_version in project_containers and the weights in rag_searches (RN-479): it is the REAL destination of that round, resolved by realpath on the user's machine after the mkdir -p. Reading projects.mirror_path at display time would state the destination of NOW over a copy from yesterday — and the two really diverge, because the grant travels in the join and only changes when the runner reconnects (RN-516). When they diverge, the screen SAYS so. Writing telemetry never takes down what it measures. The copy has already finished when the report goes out; the engine's handle_in only LOGS the api's refusal and returns {:noreply, socket} in both branches, and the runner's channel stays alive. Without a channel (the connection dropped between the request and the end of the copy) the runner does not report and does not throw — the round that happened is not undone because of that. And a project whose destination was CLEARED midway still records: the round happened, and its error is what usually explains what happened. On the screen, the row goes into AmbienteDoProjeto (the side column of the Overview, next to those of execution mode and runner) and only exists in a project that has mirrorPath — in a project without a mirror, "never synced" would be an invented absence, the same argument that already held for the runner row. An ABSOLUTE date with a caveat and never a green "it's up" dot, by the same precedent as workspaceVerifiedAt: the timestamp says a round happened, not that the folder is up to date with what changed afterwards (the trigger is a named moment, the commit — never a watcher). The status arrives RESOLVED from the api: the rule deciding which timestamp counts has a single source, and it is what decides which of the three sentences the person reads. viewer role to READ, maintainer to write the destination — the rule of RN-102 applied: the minimum belongs to the ENDPOINT, and this one only reads. The destination already travels in every project read (GET /projects/:projectId, viewer), so requiring maintainer here would lock information away from whoever already sees it in the same project, which is the worse of the two defects because it is invisible to whoever lost the capability. Where: apps/api/src/db/schema/iam.ts (project_mirror_states, in the iam aggregate because that is where the destination lives — there is no domain/runners); apps/api/src/db/migrations/0057_brave_silver_centurion.sql; apps/api/src/domain/iam/mirror-state.ts (deriveMirrorSyncStatus, the rule of the three states, pure); apps/api/src/application/ports/mirror-state-repository.port.ts (TWO write methods, not one upsert with everything optional — that is what makes the disjunction an invariant of the type, not a convention of the caller); apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/mirror-state.repository.ts; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/record-mirror-sync.use-case.ts and .../get-project-mirror-state.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/internal-projects.controller.ts (POST .../mirror-sync-result); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/projects.controller.ts (GET .../mirror-state, viewer); apps/engine/lib/engine/sessions/engine_api_client.ex (report_mirror_sync/2); apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel.ex (handle_in("mirror_sync_result", …) and the vocabulary translation); apps/runner/src/channel.ts (MirrorSyncResultMessage, enviarMirrorSyncResult); apps/runner/src/index.ts (tratarMirrorSync reports the three exits); apps/web/src/components/AmbienteDoProjeto.tsx Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/mirror-sync-telemetry.use-case.spec.ts (the three states in the pure function and in the read; error that does not erase the success; changed destination; count 0; message without text and long message; project without a destination that still records); apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/mirror-state.repository.spec.ts (the invariant of the disjoint columns against the real database — a fake would prove the fake); apps/engine/test/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel_test.exs (describe "mirror_sync_result" — the relay with translation, the filesCopied: 0 that does not vanish, an absent field that does NOT become nil, a missing sucesso that becomes ok: false, :web ignored, and the api that refuses without taking down the channel); apps/runner/src/index-handlers.spec.ts (describe "o desfecho é reportado em mirror_sync_result" — real count, empty repository as success, named failure, refusal without a destination, and the dropped connection that neither reports nor throws); apps/web/src/components/AmbienteDoProjeto.test.tsx (describe "linha do espelho" — without mirrorPath the row disappears and does not even query; the three states with three sentences; no liveness vocabulary; changed destination stated) ADR: 0147, point 7 Origin: PHASE 28, session 8. Declared and NOT done: no alarm, no notification and no automatic retry of a round that failed — the next round happens at the next named moment, as always, and the screen is the only place where the failure shows up today
documents.s: RN-517 — The outcome of each mirror round comes back through the channel and becomes TELEMETRY in its own table; "never synced", "synced and copied nothing" and "failed" are THREE answers, and success and error coexist

documents.t: Session 7 of PHASE 28 and point 5 of ADR 0147. Until now the local agent was foreground only: a process ended by SIGINT/SIGTERM, which dies with the terminal and does not come back with the user's session. There was no precedent at all — no mention of systemd, launchd or LaunchAgent in apps/runner/. User level, ALWAYS — and root is a REFUSAL, not a warning. systemd --user on Linux, LaunchAgent on macOS. This is not a packaging preference: the docblock of apps/runner/src/guard.ts:9-31 declares "the runner runs ON the user's machine, with HIS privileges" as the premise on which the product's three real boundaries rest (authentication, approval pipeline, consent) — and the cwd guard is best-effort in writing, precisely because it is not what holds anything. A system service running as root would break the invariant and leave the best-effort guard as the only thing between an approved command and the machine's disk. That is why install with uid 0 refuses naming the reason, without writing any file and without running any command: installing-and-warning would leave the wrong installation up, and the warning would be read only once. Windows is OUT OF SCOPE, and the refusal is named. The build matrix already produces the Windows binary (ADR 0112), but a user service there is a third mechanism (OS Services with a user account, or Task Scheduler at logon) — not a variation of the two. The three subcommands answer naming the platform, saying that the decision is declared, and pointing to the path that keeps working (running in the foreground). Never a mute failure, never an "installed" that installed nothing. Any other platform falls into the same refusal. One unit PER PROJECT, named by the projectId — brabo-runner-<id>.service / dev.brabo.runner.<id> — because the server already enforces one runner per project: a second join on the same terminal:<projectId> is refused by Engine.Runners.Registry. Naming by FOLDER would allow installing two units that can never be up at the same time, and the second would show up as a connection failure instead of an installation error. Installing again, from another folder, overwrites. uninstall and status reach exactly the same unit because they derive the name from the SAME projectId, resolved by the SAME two sources in the same order as the usual CLI (--project, otherwise brabo-runner.config.json), and the folder comes from resolverDir of guard.ts — never a second rule. On Linux the file goes where systemd looks, with its precedence: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user when the variable is set, ~/.config/systemd/user when not — choosing only the second would make the unit be born where the manager never looks, and the failure would show up as "unit file does not exist" on enable, visible but for the wrong reason. The projectId becomes a FILE NAME, so it is validated here. It comes from two sources that are not the server (a typed flag and a file in the folder), and a --project ../../etc/systemd would write outside the units directory. Only letters, digits, ., - and _, up to 64 characters — a UUID, the real format of every project of the product, passes whole. A runner path and a folder with a double quote or a line break are also a named refusal: a line break in a unit file is directive injection, not an edge case. A service authenticates with a DEVICE KEY, never with a token. install requires a valid brabo-runner-device-key.jwk.json in the folder and refuses without it, ignoring --token/BRABO_ACCOUNT_TOKEN on purpose: writing an account token inside a unit file would leave it on disk, readable by any process of the user and surviving the shell that exported it — and this CLI never wrote a credential to disk (the docblock of auth.ts has a test lock against exactly that). RN-434 runs the same, through the SAME function: a service pointing outside $HOME on Linux is refused, because doing via a unit what the CLI refuses to do via a flag would be getting around the rule through the back door. Restart=on-abnormal, and never on-failure (in the plist, KeepAlive with Crashed, and never SuccessfulExit). The runner exits with 1 when the join was REFUSED — invalid ticket, another runner on the project, a missing capability (RN-514) — or when it exhausted its own retry ceiling, and both things are "stop and call a human". on-failure would restart a fatal refusal in a loop, which is exactly what the CLI refuses to do on its own. Signal, OOM and watchdog — what on-abnormal covers — are the only failure that restarting fixes. The PATH goes frozen into the unit, with the cost declared in the file itself: both managers give the service a minimal PATH, and the runner calls git (the mirror, RN-516) and docker (ADR 0137); without it the service would come up perfectly and both functions would fail with "not found". It is a snapshot, and it only changes by reinstalling. The TWO halves of the unit file do NOT have the same syntax, and WorkingDirectory= goes WITHOUT quotes. ExecStart= is parsed with unquoting and word splitting — that is why each argument goes in quotes —, and WorkingDirectory= is not: systemd takes the whole rest of the line as the path. Treating the two as if they were the same cost an entire release: with quotes the value no longer starts with /, the unit is refused at load (Loaded: bad-setting, WorkingDirectory= path is not absolute) and never starts — in both kinds, in no installation at all. The suite was green the whole time, because each assertion asked back for exactly the wrong form: that is why the proof is now made against systemd-analyze --user verify, the real validator, and not against text. What REMAINS to escape is one character, and it is not the space (the line goes whole, so /home/eu/pasta com espaço works literally): it is %, because that directive goes through specifier expansion — /home/dan/50%off becomes /home/dan/50<id-do-os-release>ff with no error at all, and the service comes up in the wrong folder. %% is the way to say a literal %. Reading back accepts both forms, and that is a deliberate debt to whoever already has a broken unit on disk: status and uninstall need to keep reaching its folder. Whoever is in that state fixes it by reinstalling — install overwrites the whole file. And there is a THIRD syntax in the same file: Environment= (AT-095). It is a LIST of space-separated assignments, with unquoting and C-style escaping, and it also expands specifiers. Written raw — as the XDG_CONFIG_HOME of the MACHINE unit and the PATH of both kinds came out —, Environment=XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/home/dan/50%off com espaco reached the service as /home/dan/50popff: %o expanded and com/espaco discarded by the word splitting. The unit loads, verify approves, the service comes up — and the agent looks for the base and the key in a folder that does not exist, silently. That is why the WHOLE assignment goes in quotes (Environment="VAR=valor"), with \ and " escaped by backslash and % as %%; $ is not escaped there (Environment= does not expand variables). The --dir of ExecStart= had the same class and went along: each argument still goes in quotes, and now \ becomes \\, % becomes %% and $ becomes $$ (the variable substitution of ExecStart=). A line break in PATH/XDG_CONFIG_HOME is REFUSED before writing — in a unit file it is a new directive, not a value. None of this changes the READING back: it only reads the WorkingDirectory=, and neither of the two environment values is read from disk. The proof is the EFFECTIVE VALUE, not verify (which approves the broken form): the very systemd --test --user --unit=<u>, over a temporary units folder, dumps the resolved configuration, and the test compares what systemd UNDERSTOOD with what was written. An activation that fails does NOT delete the file, and does not say "installed". Writing the unit and activating it are two steps, and the manager may not be there (systemctl out of the PATH, launchd refusing). The file stays — it is what the person needs to finish by hand — and the answer is a third outcome, which names the pending command and the reason. Deleting the file would turn "I could not activate" into "nothing happened", which is false. uninstall removes the THREE, and the folder comes from the UNIT — never from the cwd. The ADR is explicit: the unit file, the brabo-runner.config.json and the brabo-runner-device-key.jwk.json. The last two live in the runner's folder, and the folder that matters is the one that was INSTALLED, not the one from which the person happened to type the command — that is why the WorkingDirectory is read back from the unit file itself, which is the record of what was installed. Without a unit there is no record: the two files are only removed with an explicit --dir, and the message says why. Guessing by the cwd would delete the key of a project that nobody asked to remove. A failing deactivation becomes a warning and the file is removed anyway — a unit the manager no longer recognizes is no reason to leave the file behind. And uninstall SAYS what it did not do: the key left the disk, not the server. The corresponding public key remains in runner_device_keys, and revoking it is something else (DELETE /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys/:deviceKeyId, ADR 0147 point 6). A "removed" that let the person think they had revoked would be worse than removing nothing. The LaunchAgent log is also not deleted: it is the user's record of what happened, and deleting it was not asked for. status answers FOUR states, and they do not collapse (RN-088): not installed, installed and running, installed and stopped, and installed and I could not ask. The first answer comes from the DISK — is there a unit file? —, and that is why it stays right on a machine where the manager does not exist; only afterwards is the manager asked. A spawn that failed (binary absent from the PATH) never becomes "the manager said no": they are different answers, separated at the source, and a word this CLI does not know how to interpret also falls into "could not ask" instead of becoming "stopped" by guesswork. Each state has its own sentence and its own exit code (0 / 3 / 4 / 5, with 1 and 2 left out because they already mean generic failure and usage error in this CLI): a single exit(1) for the three "not running" ones would collapse through the code exactly what the sentence separates. Nothing here is a proposed_action. It is the user running a command on their own machine, about their own service — not an agent asking to act. service is dispatched before lerArgumentos, because none of the three subcommands connects to anything and what matters most (status) needs to work in a folder whose configuration is broken, which is precisely when someone asks. Where: apps/runner/src/servico.ts (new — the vocabulary, the two platforms as answers to the SAME five questions, the refusals, the four states and CODIGO_POR_ESTADO); apps/runner/src/servico-sistema.ts (new — the real disk and systemctl/launchctl adapter, separated so that the guarantee "servico.ts does not touch node:fs/node:child_process" stays verifiable); apps/runner/src/index.ts (comandoDoRunnerParaServico, rodarSubcomandoDeServico, the dispatch of service in main() before lerArgumentos, and the new line in uso()) Test: apps/runner/src/servico.spec.ts (new — happy path on both platforms with the real content of the unit/plist; root refused without writing anything; Windows named; without a device key; a projectId that would become a path; absent systemctl leaving the file and saying it did not activate; the RN-434 passed through; uninstall reading the folder from the unit and not from the cwd, without a unit and without --dir touching no file at all, and the failing disable becoming a warning; the FOUR states of status plus the unknown word and the three outcomes of launchctl; and the four distinct exit codes); apps/runner/src/index.spec.ts (describe "brabo-runner service é despachado antes de exigir credencial" — a REAL process in a folder without any credential: status answers 4 instead of the usage block, and an unknown subcommand falls into the service usage); apps/runner/src/servico-systemd.spec.ts (the GENERATED unit asked of the real systemd-analyze --user verify, in both kinds, with a folder that has a space and a folder that has % — plus the OLD form, in quotes, being REJECTED by the same validator; without systemd on the machine the file SKIPS naming the reason, never passes silently nor fails because of the environment) — and, since AT-095, describe "o valor EFETIVO de Environment= é o valor gravado" and describe "o --dir do ExecStart= e o WorkingDirectory= também chegam intactos", which ask the dump of systemd --test --user for the RESOLVED value of XDG_CONFIG_HOME, PATH, WorkingDirectory and of the --dir with %, space, quotes, backslash and $, and pin the old form of Environment= as delivering ANOTHER value; servico.spec.ts gained the two line-break refusals and the project unit without XDG_CONFIG_HOME ADR: 0147, point 5 Origin: PHASE 28, session 7. Declared and NOT done: BRB-031 (the manual chmod +x of the flow of ADR 0118) does not die here — whoever runs brabo-runner service install already had to make the binary executable to get to the command, and ADR 0147 ties that side effect to the installation coming from the versioned bootstrap of ADR 0146, which this delivery does not touch. Also out: any start/stop/restart subcommand (what manages the lifecycle is the OS service manager, and duplicating it in the CLI would create a second source of truth about the state) and Windows, above
documents.s: RN-518 — brabo-runner service install|uninstall|status installs at USER level and never root; uninstall cleans the folder the UNIT records; status answers four states without collapsing any; Windows is a named refusal

documents.t: Session 7 of PHASE 28 and point 6 of ADR 0147. Revocation had existed since ADR 0118 (DELETE /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys/:deviceKeyId, developer, 204, idempotent) — and there was no way to see what one revokes. The real cut was bigger than the docblock said. It declared the absence as "without the maintainer view (list/revoke any user's) that the PAT has". But PersonalAccessTokensController has five routes — @Post(), @Get() and @Delete(':tokenId') for the user themself, plus @Get('all') and @Delete(':tokenId/admin') for maintainer (RN-427) — and the device key one had two. It was not only the maintainer view that was missing: the listing for the OWN owner was missing. An orphan key (tab closed in the middle of the flow of RN-473) was inert, invisible and permanent, with no screen at all on which to revoke it — the gap that CLAUDE.md already declared. @Get() comes in, developer, in the same format the PAT already has and scoped to the user themself in the repository's WHERE, never in a filter of the use case. The revoked one STAYS in the list. Same choice as listarDoUsuarioNoProjeto of the PAT: whoever revoked needs to see they revoked, and making the row disappear would make the screen claim the key never existed. revokedAt is what separates the two, and a null lastUsedAt is the sign of the ORPHAN — registered and never used by any runner. Never the public JWK. It is not a secret, but it serves no purpose here: the list exists to revoke, and for that id, name and the three dates suffice. The private half the api never saw. The maintainer view stays OUT — now by decision, not by omission. The PAT's two admin routes were born from incident response (RN-427): a dismissed dev with a SHARED secret circulating. A device key is not that animal — the private key never leaves the browser that generated it, so there is no secret in someone else's hands to contain. What the DELETE here gained in exchange was REACH (RN-520), not breadth. Where: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/runner-device-keys.controller.ts:99 (@Get(), listDeviceKeys, developer); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/list-runner-device-keys.use-case.ts:24; apps/api/src/application/ports/runner-device-key-repository.port.ts:90 (listarDoUsuarioNoProjeto); apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/runner-device-key.repository.ts:69; apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/dto/runner-device-key-list.response.dto.ts:19 (the TWO type locks, Wire/MesmasChaves, unlike the registration DTO) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/list-runner-device-keys.use-case.spec.ts (delegation with userId/projectId in the right order; the revoked one that stays in the list; the orphan with a null lastUsedAt; a repository that rejects and propagates); apps/api/test/interfaces/http/runner/runner-device-keys.controller.spec.ts (the THREE routes at developer; the delegation; the route that does not return an empty list by mistake) ADR: 0147, point 6 Origin: PHASE 28, session 7. Declared and NOT done: no screen at all. This delivery is the server-side half; the CLAUDE.md gap closes by half — the api can now list and revoke, and apps/web still has nowhere to do it The other half CLOSED in RN-561: the Settings tab gained the section that lists and revokes, marking the KIND of each key. What remains open from here is the maintainer view (above, by decision) and the {projeto, usuário} target of the disconnection (RN-520)
documents.s: RN-519 — Nobody revokes what they cannot see: the device key gains a listing for its OWN owner, and the maintainer view stays out by DECISION

documents.t: Revised by RN-685 (ADR 0201): the socket ticket now stores WHICH credential requested it, and revoking a key (and a PAT) takes down only the connections opened WITH IT — another runner of the same user, with another key or with a PAT, stays up. The "declared cost" below no longer holds. The {projeto, usuário} pair survives as the target of member removal (RN-615), as that of the LEGACY connection (ticket without a credential) during the rollout, and as plan B when the engine does not know the per-credential route. The other half of point 6 of ADR 0147. Revoking a device key prevented the NEXT ticket and nothing else: an already connected brabo-runner kept the terminal:<projectId> channel up — executing approved commands, serving PTY, starting containers — with the revoked key, until it dropped on its own. The one that sends the command is the api; the one that reaches the pid is the engine. The api calls POST /internal/projects/:projectId/runner/disconnect (the same internal HTTP with the usual service token, never a second mechanism), and the engine finds the channel via Engine.Runners.Registry.whereis/1 — the pid it already handed out. The engine does not query the keys table and the api does not talk to the channel; neither of the two does the other's work, the same division as EngineWeb.ContainerCommandController (RN-497). The precision that exists is {projeto, usuário}, and the one that does not exist is {chave} — by construction, not by taste. Engine.Runners.SocketTicket stores project_id, user_id and kind, and only that; the api requests the ticket with {userId, kind}. The identity of the CREDENTIAL that originated the ticket (the PAT, or the kid of the device key — RN-475) dies in PatAuthGuard and never reaches the socket. Carrying it there would require a new column in runner_socket_tickets, a new field in the internal request and a new assign in connect/3: an auth contract change, outside this delivery. A DECLARED cost, and named in the code, not only here: a runner of the SAME user connected with a PAT, or with another key of the same project, also drops. It reconnects on its own — the next round requests a new ticket, and the credential that is still valid gets one. Whoever was revoked does not, and that is where the revocation bites. A runner of ANOTHER user on the same project does not drop: the comparison is socket.assigns.user_id, inside the channel process, which is the only one that can read it — and the de_outro_dono outcome goes back to the requester instead of an :ok that does not describe what happened. It takes down the TRANSPORT, not just the channel process. Stopping only the channel would leave the socket alive and the Phoenix client re-entering the topic forever with an already consumed ticket — silent degradation, exactly the defect ADR 0147 exists not to repeat. EngineWeb.RunnerSocket.id/1 stops being nil and now names the connection (runner_socket:<kind>:<projectId>:<userId>), and the channel uses Phoenix's documented mechanism, Endpoint.broadcast(id, "disconnect", %{}). It is through it that the runner NOTICES the drop: onDisconnected resolves the round, the loop requests a new ticket and the api refuses. A side effect NEVER takes down the main effect. The DELETE stays 204 and idempotent: engine down, no runner connected or a timeout cannot make the revocation fail nor become 5xx. The call to the engine lives in a try/catch that only LOGS, inside the use case — the SAME rule as rag_searches (RN-479) and mirror_sync_result (RN-517). And the four outcomes are information, not error: sem_runner is the normal case of whoever revokes an orphan key (RN-519), and an UNKNOWN outcome coming from the engine becomes timeout and never derrubado — between asserting that the connection dropped and asserting that maybe not, the safe assertion is the one that does not promise what is not known. Revoke FIRST, take down afterwards, and the project comes from the revoked ROW, never from the URL: the route's projectId was already ignored in the DELETE, and reading it here would make a divergent projectId take down the runner of a project that has nothing to do with this key. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/revoke-runner-device-key.use-case.ts:63 (the order, the row's project and the try/catch that only logs); apps/api/src/application/ports/api-to-engine-client.port.ts:411 (disconnectRunnerOfUser, DesfechoDeDesconexaoDeRunner); apps/api/src/infrastructure/http-clients/api-to-engine-client.ts:477; apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/revogacao.ex:92 (derrubar/3); apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel.ex:697 (handle_info({:derrubar_por_revogacao, …})); apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/runner_socket.ex:79 (id/1, which stopped being nil); apps/engine/lib/engine_web/controllers/runner_connection_command_controller.ex:27; apps/engine/lib/engine_web/router.ex:86 Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/revoke-runner-device-key.use-case.spec.ts (describe "a revogação alcança a conexão viva" — the row's project; the revoke→take-down order; engine down not taking down the revocation; a 404 that takes down nobody); apps/api/test/infrastructure/http-clients/api-to-engine-client.spec.ts (the route and the body; unknown outcome becoming timeout; a 500 that THROWS, for the use case to handle); apps/engine/test/engine/runners/revogacao_test.exs (no runner; the owner; the other owner; the ceiling; a malformed argument that does not raise); apps/engine/test/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel_test.exs (describe "revogação alcança a conexão viva" — the REAL channel that stops and releases the presence in the Registry, the other owner's one that stays up, the :web that is never a target); apps/engine/test/engine_web/controllers/runner_connection_command_controller_test.exs (the 200s with an outcome, and the 400 of a malformed request) ADR: 0147, point 6 Origin: PHASE 28, session 7. Declared and NOT done: revocation does not reach a runner connected in ANOTHER project with the same key — that case does not exist, because runner_device_keys.project_id ties the key to a single project; and no screen triggers this yet (the web half of RN-519)
documents.s: RN-520 — Revoking stops only preventing a NEW ticket and now takes down the LIVE connection; the target is {projeto, usuário} and never {chave}, and taking down never takes down the revocation

documents.t: Extended by RN-574 (ADR 0161): a fourth local refusal reason, sem_broker_na_instalacao, for container/mounted in an installation without a container broker — after "already up" and before "no image decided". Extended by RN-590 (AT-105): the same reading holds in the mode conversion, in stop/remove and in the Infra Lead's proposal (409 refusal from the api when proposing). Starting a project's container had one path: the Infra Lead, inside a session, calling its tool. In a real execution of exp004 (runner mode) container_start_via_runner failed due to the defect that RN-508 closed — and there was no way to TRY AGAIN. Five dev agents spent hours emitting dev.blocked_by_container (RN-502), and the only way out was to open a new session and talk to an agent to re-execute a machine operation. The global containers page (ADR 0136, RN-495) was already the place where a HUMAN decides a container's lifecycle — but it did not even show the project: the rule was "one row per project that already has project_containers", and a start that fails BEFORE recording leaves no row at all. The screen hid exactly the project for which it needed to exist. The THIRD state has its own name, and it is not stopped. The read model becomes a LEFT JOIN (it was INNER) and registrado becomes null for those that never provisioned — it is not a new value of ContainerLifecycleStatus (stopped is a container that EXISTED and stopped), and it is not "not observed" (which is about the daemon having been asked). The screen prints "never provisioned" and the Observed column says sem_container_registrado, the third reason of naoVerificado — the three do not collapse (RN-088/RN-486). The list widened; the BUDGET did not. Asking the broker for the observed state is a network call per project, with a ceiling of 20 per load (TETO_DE_VERIFICACOES_POR_CARGA). A project without project_containers has nothing to observe, so it is never eligible and never takes up a slot: in a workspace with hundreds of empty projects, those with a real container stay verified exactly as before. And it remains THREE batch queries, however many projects there are — none inside a loop. The action branches by execution_mode, with the same rule as the backend (RN-497/RN-503): container and mounted propose container_start (broker, on the server) and runner proposes container_start_via_runner (local agent, on the user's machine). The TWO payloads are different on purpose and are not copied: container_start carries the image ELECTION (image, network, resources), read from the project's current decision at click time; container_start_via_runner has a schema with only rationale (RN-508), because it starts the ALREADY decided image and elects nothing. The screen does NOT propose what is already known to fail — and says the reason in place of the button. Three refusals, each with its own text, in the order "state of the WORLD before the capability of whoever is looking" (so a viewer still reads "the image remains to be decided", and not only "you cannot"): no image decided — the gate of RN-105, which holds in all THREE modes since RN-494; without artifact.project_image there is nothing to start; runner that never had a confirmed folder (null workspaceVerifiedAt, RN-423) — no local agent ever connected, so the action would fail for sure. The same honesty the Infra Lead's tool already practices when refusing LOCALLY before proposing (RN-508); role below maintainer — the minimum is that of the ENDPOINT (RN-102): both types require maintainer in decide.ts, and the comparison comes from roleAtLeast, never from a hand-written list of roles. What is taken away is the CONTROL, never the INFORMATION (ADR 0064): whoever cannot still sees state, image and resources, and the reason is said ONCE in TEXT — title on a disabled element does not open in Chromium. And what the screen does NOT know, it declares instead of promising. workspaceVerifiedAt is the record of ONE confirmation and never a heartbeat (RN-468): non-null does not prove a local agent connected NOW, and the api has no presence signal (what knows about now is the Phoenix channel, in the engine). So the runner row offers the button with a written caveat — "if it is not running now, the action fails when approved" — instead of a green dot that would lie. No ceiling moved. Every proposal on this screen is a proposed_action, always with a HUMAN clicking, never an agent; container_remove stays at the absolute ceiling (RN-418) and decide.ts stays byte for byte. The role read is the WORKSPACE one, and the gap is declared: the effective one is projectRole ?? workspaceRole (RN-471), and fetching project_members per row would be the network N+1 this page exists not to pay — whoever was DEMOTED in a project still sees the button and gets a 403, which is the repairable defect (it ends in a toast), not the invisible one. Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/containers-overview.repository.ts:96 (the LEFT JOIN, the ORDER BY and temImagemDecidida); apps/api/src/application/ports/containers-overview-repository.port.ts:20 (executionMode/null lifecycle/temImagemDecidida/workspaceVerifiedAt); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/containers/obter-visao-geral-de-containers.use-case.ts:33 (sem_container_registrado) and :101 (elegivelParaVerificacao, which is what keeps the budget intact); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/containers/containers-overview.controller.ts:60; apps/web/src/routes/containers-subida.ts:114 (decidirSubida, the whole rule, pure); apps/web/src/routes/ContainersPage.tsx:119 (the two payloads) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/containers/obter-visao-geral-de-containers.use-case.spec.ts (the third state with its own reason; 25 empty projects that do NOT push the 20 with a real container out of verification); apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/containers-overview.repository.spec.ts (a project without project_containers in the list; temImagemDecidida; pending container_start_via_runner; the THREE queries that do not grow); apps/api/test/interfaces/http/containers/containers-overview.controller.spec.ts (the nested registrado and the null that survives the conversion); apps/web/src/routes/containers-subida.test.ts (the branching by mode, the three refusals, the caveat, the role hierarchy); apps/web/src/routes/ContainersPage.test.tsx (the REAL scenario of exp004: a runner project, no row, image decided, folder confirmed → the action proposed is container_start_via_runner with a payload of only rationale, and GET .../container is not even called) ADR: 0136 (the page), 0145 (the action type), 0133 (the other one) Origin: real execution of exp004, decision of the product owner. Declared and NOT done: the screen does not know whether a local agent is connected NOW (there is no presence signal in the api), and the role read is the workspace one, not the project's effective one

documents.t: The appsec (Engine.Gates.SecOpsAgentServer.run_design/2, RN-360) was born implemented, tested and with no production caller at all: the only mention outside tests was a comment in artifact_schemas.ex. RN-360 itself declared the gap, and docs/fluxo.yml (role appsec, field acionamento) already NAMED the missing trigger — assess_implementability of the Dev Lead, gate implementavel, the same ADR 0090. That was it. run_assessment/2 now calls it via Engine.Gates.Dispatcher.run_appsec_design/2 — the sixth callback of the behaviour, a structural COPY of run_qa_estrategia/3 and swappable in tests for the same reason as its five neighbors (the caller is exercised by a light test, without an Ecto sandbox, and should not start a real GenServer just to prove it ASKED). In parallel, and the assessment does not wait. The trigger happens on BOTH exits of run_assessment/2 — with a test plan and without — and the outcome of each one stays byte for byte as it was. Making the assessment depend on the threat model would make the implementavel gate depend on TWO asynchronous productions instead of one, and would burn two Dev Lead turns where today one is burned: the :sem_plano branch already returns {:error, ...} asking the model to call again (RN-163), and a second wait stacked on it would multiply the window. The threat model reaches whoever needs it through the path that RN-361 already defined — handoff to arquiteto, dev-lead and infra —, never through this return; the :sem_plano message does not even mention the appsec, because promising the model something it will not receive there is the defect that RN-163 closes. Since RN-674 there is no more :sem_plano: the assessment comes out on the first call, the appsec trigger accompanies the proposal, and the read of the history serves only the guard below. The appsec stays in DESIGN — the owner's decision that took the test plan out of pre-dev was about QA. And only once per story. The model is INSTRUCTED to call assess_implementability again while the test plan does not exist: without a guard, each re-call would cost another appsec LLM round and three more handoffs about the SAME story. disparar_appsec_se_preciso/3 only triggers when there is no artifact.threat_model of that storyId in the history. The question here is DOES IT EXIST, not WHICH — the opposite of the test plan, where the most recent wins because a story can be reassessed. The event log read is one per call: the two questions ("is there already a test plan?", "is there already a threat model?") are answered over the same list. Two list_events/2 in the same invocation would be the traffic amplifier that ADR 0060 refuses, and this path is hot precisely because of the retry. An UNREADABLE history triggers nothing: absence of an answer is not proof of absence of the artifact, and triggering there would reopen the re-call through another door. The invalid args clause also does not trigger — it does not know which story it is. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/dev_lead_tools.ex:457 (run_assessment/2, the single history read) and :519 (disparar_appsec_se_preciso/3, the idempotency guard); apps/engine/lib/engine/gates/dispatcher.ex:29 (the callback) and :86 (Engine.Gates.Dispatcher.Live.run_appsec_design/2); apps/engine/test/support/fake_gate_dispatcher.ex:23 Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/dev_lead_tools_test.exs, describe "assess_implementability dispara o appsec (RN-539)" — a story without a threat model triggers, a story with a threat model does NOT trigger (the idempotency), a threat model of another story does not count, the outcome of :sem_plano does not change, the assessment is proposed normally alongside the trigger, invalid args and an unreadable history do not trigger ADR: 0090 (which declared the automatic trigger out of scope) Origin: docs/fluxo.yml, role appsec. Declared and NOT done: artifact.threat_model is emitted in the STORY's session (emit_threat_model/3 reads story["sessionId"]), while the guard reads the history of the DEV LEAD's session. On the common path they are the same session — the Dev Lead assesses stories that the execution session itself created. When not, the guard does not see the threat model and the appsec runs again: the cost of one repeated LLM round, never wrong data (the artifact is append-only and what consumes it is the handoff). Closing this would require the api to accept an artifact search by story ACROSS sessions, which does not exist today
