documents.t: A pause is only reversible if the path to turn it on exists. The pause of the Anamnese and that of the Psicólogo (RN-115, RN-117) were declared reversible in THREE places — the docblock of AnamneseSchedulerWorker.enabled?/0 ("Turning it back on is ANAMNESE_ENABLED=true and restarting the engine"), that of PsychologistWorker.enabled?/0 and the configuration table — and the path did not exist in any environment. Measured, not a hypothesis. With the dev compose up: $ docker compose … exec -T engine sh -lc \ 'echo "[$START_ANAMNESE] [$ANAMNESE_ENABLED] [$PSYCHOLOGIST_ENABLED]"' [true] [] [] The cause is the layer only Compose has: it does not pass the host environment through to the container. A variable reaches the process if, and only if, it is written in the environment: (or in an env_file) of that service. The engine mapped THIRTEEN Anamnese/Psicólogo variables — all of them cost CEILINGS (ANAMNESE_INTERVAL_SECONDS, ANAMNESE_BUDGET_MICROS, PSYCHOLOGIST_TRIAGE_THRESHOLD, …) — and neither of the two that decide whether the agents run. ANAMNESE_ENABLED=true in .env was inert: apps/engine/config/runtime.exs fell back to the default "false" and both stayed off silently, with no error. Probable origin of the defect: when the code's default became false (2026-08-10), nobody needed the variable to TURN OFF. Only whoever tries to TURN ON finds out the wire does not exist — and that person, by construction, shows up months later. The rule. Every BOOLEAN flag that runtime.exs reads — the form System.get_env("X", "true"|"false") == "true" — has to be mapped in the environment: of the engine service of both composes. The cut is that of the booleans and not that of the file's 58 variables because a flag exists precisely to be flipped, and the flip happens through the environment: a flag without a line in the compose is a switch without a wire. A numeric ceiling with a good default (READ_FILE_MAX_BYTES) and a release variable (SECRET_KEY_BASE, POOL_SIZE) are legitimately left out, and that is why the list is DERIVED from runtime.exs instead of maintained by hand. The default differs per file, and the difference is the decision: in docker/docker-compose.yml (dev) the line repeats the CODE's default. Dev is where the docblocks' promise is exercised, and a divergent default there would make the compose decide product underneath runtime.exs. in docker/docker-compose.prod.yml it is enough to be mapped. That file turns the background agents off on purpose (START_ANAMNESE:-false against the code's true), with the reason written alongside — demanding equality would reject a conscious decision. This does NOT change any product decision. Both flags remain false by default in both composes: the pause of 2026-08-10 still holds, byte for byte. What came to exist is the switch. And ANAMNESE_ENABLED=true alone is not enough. START_ANAMNESE (BOOT key, apps/engine/lib/engine/application.ex:82,106-108) decides whether the kickoff/0 that SCHEDULES the periodic tick is called; ANAMNESE_ENABLED (PRODUCT flag) decides whether a NEW round can happen. They are different questions, and the periodic Anamnese requires both at true. The Psicólogo has only the second — its automatic trigger is session closing, not a tick. deploy/k8s/ is left out, and by decision. The layer that breaks does not exist there: a Deployment/ConfigMap intercepts nothing, and the variable is written where every variable is written. brabo-config has FOUR literals (service addresses and the web's log level), with none of the 13 ceilings nor START_ANAMNESE — the engine runs with the code's defaults, coherently. There is no wireless switch to fix there. Where: docker/docker-compose.yml:406-425 (the four boot keys and the four product flags, in each agent's block); docker/docker-compose.prod.yml:308-315; apps/engine/config/runtime.exs:157,158,162,168,185,229,238,264 (the eight flags); .env.example (the two questions, side by side) Test: scripts/ci/flags-do-engine-no-compose.spec.ts — derives the flags from runtime.exs and fails naming the one missing in either of the two composes, and the one diverging from the code's default in the dev one. No warn: it really fails, in the test-packages job Origin: found by direct measurement in the engine container, 2026-09-08. Declared: the exception list FLAGS_FORA_DO_COMPOSE is born EMPTY — it exists so that "out by decision" has somewhere to be said, and does not become indistinguishable from "out by forgetfulness"
documents.s: RN-540 — A boolean flag read by runtime.exs is mapped in the environment: of the engine service of both composes, with the code's default

documents.t: The local agent had no notion of a base. The only root was --dir, resolved by resolverDir against INIT_CWD ?? process.cwd(); without the flag, the root was the cwd itself. estado.dir is one path, singular — that of the project of that connection —, and there was no constant, variable or field saying where the projects live on that machine. The word "base" only appeared in comments. The base is LOCAL, and never arrives over the network. It is the broker's design (ADR 0144) applied to the local agent: whoever has the root is whoever executes, and what crosses the network is the relative segment. There is no base field coming from the server, and resolverPastaDoProjetoNaBase refuses an ABSOLUTE segment lexically — never "accepts it and reinterprets". Two sources, and the flag wins. --base <caminho> on the command line, and $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/brabo/runner.json (otherwise ~/.config/brabo/runner.json), which is where the installer (ADR 0150) writes it. The file belongs to the USER and not to a project on purpose: the base is one for N projects, and storing it in brabo-runner.config.json — which is per project, lives INSIDE the project folder and is written by the BROWSER — would give N copies of the same value with N chances of diverging. An environment variable was refused for two reasons: BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE already exists and is the base of mounted projects on the SERVER side (RN-500), the namespace collision that ADR 0141 refused in writing; and under systemd --user/LaunchAgent (RN-518) the environment is the unit's, not that of the shell of whoever installed. The flag alone would not be enough either: the base would go into the ExecStart of each unit, and changing it would require rewriting them all. --dir keeps meaning exactly what it always meant, and the base does NOT enter its validation. This is the api's prohibition transposed: project-workspaces-root.ts forbids in writing that the base rule go down into caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido, because that predicate runs on every READ and a legacy project outside the base would blow up when read — "the base is a rule of CREATION and CONVERSION; the lexicon is forever" (RN-501). On this side it holds the same: --dir stays validated by validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux + garantirDiretorio (RN-434/RN-435), and being OUTSIDE the base does not invalidate it. Without this the base would be breaking/ with no gain, against the legacy binary of RN-514. The base decides only where a NEW project folder is born. The guard reuses the rule; a fourth copy is not born. base-guard.ts is the THIRD sibling of guard.ts, next to espelho-guard.ts: it imports semBarraFinal, dentroDoEscopo and realpathMaisProximo — the three helpers that stopped being private precisely for this (RN-516) —, repeats the lexical-then-realpath double pass of validarCwdDentroDaRaiz, and reuses validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux WHOLE to require the base inside $HOME on Linux (a base inside $HOME implies every subfolder inside it, so the two checks keep agreeing). From the loop refusal of espelho-guard.ts it reuses what is rule — dentroDoEscopo, comparison by SEGMENT and never raw startsWith, so /base-outra does not count as inside /base — and not the recusarLaco function, which throws DestinoDeEspelhoInvalidoError and would report a malformed base as a mirror problem. The same lesson as RN-515: one reuses the rule, not the message. The loop here is ASYMMETRIC, and that is the finding. In the mirror both directions are a defect. Here the project folder INSIDE the base is the NORMAL arrangement — it is literally what "each project is a subfolder of it" means. It is the opposite direction that is a loop: a base inside this project's root (or equal to it) would make every new project be born inside this one, with this one's git and mirror starting to sweep the others. Only that one is refused. A refusal has a different disposition per SOURCE, and none is silent. An absent base is the NORMAL state (null, the legacy intact). A base from the FLAG that does not pass the guard exits with code 2 — it is an explicit request typed just now and impossible to honor, the same disposition as a refused --dir. A base from the FILE that does not pass is stated on stderr, names what is lost ("it will have nowhere to create the folder of a new project") and the runner continues without a base: taking down a local agent serving a project because of a configuration it does not even use yet would be disproportionate. A file that exists and does not declare base is absence, not refusal — it is configuration WITHOUT a consented base, not broken configuration. And the startup line states the base in BOTH states, because omitting "none" would leave someone looking for why the folder did not appear. This is BEST-EFFORT, and the TOCTOU caveat is inherited in writing from guard.ts and espelho-guard.ts: a symlink created AFTER the check and BEFORE the mkdir is not covered, nor a link whose target does not exist yet. The security boundary is still authentication + approval pipeline + the consent of whoever ran the CLI. Nothing here CREATES a folder: the base validation does not require it to exist (what creates it is the installer, and it is the same reasoning as ADR 0142 — validating disk where only the lexicon is knowable would prevent consenting to a base before it exists). The only disk question is the one that is never ambiguous: a path that ALREADY exists and is not a folder will never become one. Where: apps/runner/src/base.ts:69 (caminhoDoArquivoDeBase, the XDG precedence of servico.ts), :106 (lerBaseConsentida, the four outcomes) and :181 (resolverBaseConsentida, the order of the sources and the origin of the refusal); apps/runner/src/base-guard.ts:128 (validarBaseDeProjetos), :209 (recusarLacoComARaiz, the asymmetric loop) and :296 (resolverPastaDoProjetoNaBase, the subfolder and the double pass); apps/runner/src/index.ts:321 (the resolution in lerArgumentos, AFTER garantirDiretorio and without touching the validation of --dir) and :452 (EstadoDoRunner.base) Test: apps/runner/src/base-guard.spec.ts (happy path with a base that does not exist yet; the sibling with a common prefix that is NOT confused; .., /, file, $HOME on Linux; the loop in both directions, including the one built by a REAL symlink; the absolute segment, with .., the one pointing to the base itself and the one escaping through a link in the middle); apps/runner/src/base.spec.ts (the XDG precedence, the four outcomes of the read, the flag beating the file, and the refusal carrying the ORIGIN) ADR: 0151 points 1 and 2 Origin: PHASE 29. The workspace_create/workspace_create_result pair and the workspace capability (points 3 to 6 of the ADR), declared here as not done, CLOSED in RN-532 — the base came to have a consumer. Still declared and NOT done: the install.sh, which is what will write the file
documents.s: RN-529 — brabo-runner is born with a local BASE, each project is a subfolder of it, and the base NEVER invalidates --dir

documents.t: RN-529 gave brabo-runner a BASE and validated it, and declared in writing that nothing consumed it. This is the consumer: the workspace_create/workspace_create_result pair, the workspace capability and an own predicate in the engine. The pair is REQUEST WITH REPLY, and could not be modeled on workspace_confirm. That one is UNIDIRECTIONAL: handle_in("workspace_confirm", …) answers {:noreply, socket} and pushes nothing back. Whoever requests the creation of a folder needs to know whether it appeared, and with what path — so the mold is that of exec/exec_result (despachar_pedido + pending_execs + responder_pedido_pendente/3), the same as the three container pairs. A record of precision, because the name circulated: workspace.verified does not exist in this repository — what exists is the project.workspace_verified event and the column workspace_verified_at. Only the SEGMENT crosses the network. The base is local and never comes from the server (RN-529); the engine sends projectId and the RELATIVE segment, and it is resolverPastaDoProjetoNaBase — on the runner side, which has the root — that joins them. It is the invariant of ADR 0130/ ADR 0144 applied to the local agent: whoever has the root is whoever executes. An ABSOLUTE segment is refused by LEXICON, never accepted and reinterpreted. The confirmation REUSES workspace_confirm, and that is what saves an entire front. Having created the folder, the runner pushes the workspace_confirm that has existed since RN-423 — and it is that which writes, through the path already built: channel → engine → internal HTTP → ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase, which revalidates the lexicon, is idempotent and stamps workspace_verified_at. No new write route is born, the engine still does not write the table, and the only path that stamps remains a single one. The ORDER is the mechanism, not aesthetics: the two pushes reach the SAME channel process, in order, and the workspace_confirm handler is synchronous — sending it BEFORE the result is what guarantees the stamp already exists when the requester unblocks from the receive. The workspace capability enters the vocabulary in the session in which the code enters, on both sides (ADR 0151 point 4). RN-514 had made the opposite bet with espelho — a name on the server without code on the other side — and it only paid off because someone called it in; repeating it would be repeating the silent defect the negotiation exists to prevent. It is the only one of the four whose declaration depends on the STATE of that execution, and not on the binary's version. The runner only declares it when it has a consented base (capacidadesDoRunner), and it is through that line — and no other — that the server KNOWS a base exists: the engine does not read the user's disk and has no table of bases. Nobody REQUIRES it at join, and that is a decision: requiring it in runner would make every binary without a base stop connecting, which is breaking/ and MAJOR, for a function that project may never use. It is opt-in from the other end — whoever has a base declares it, and only whoever declared receives the message. Its OWN predicate, and RunnerReadiness stays byte for byte. Engine.Runners.PastaDoProjeto has TWO preconditions — runner connected, base consented — and the ADR literally adopts the refusal that Engine.Runners.Espelho had already written: a shared function with a "skip container" flag is precisely the path by which the third precondition falls BY ACCIDENT for exec in a future refactoring (RN-507/ADR 0145 exists so that it does not fall). And here the third would be worse than unnecessary: it is circular — a runner project only comes to have a REGISTERED running container after the runner itself starts it, and the container starts over the folder this message exists to create. It also does NOT ask for workspace_verified_at (unlike the mirror: here it is the RESULT, and requiring it would make the message unreachable precisely in the case it was made for) nor the execution_mode (the second source of the same rule — whoever has a consented base is the local agent, and a local agent only exists where it exists). Where each precondition is answered, and why they are not both in the same place. "Runner connected" belongs to the Registry, and the module answers it on its own. "Base consented" is a property of that CONNECTION: it lives in socket.assigns and never in a table (the rule of ADR 0147), so what answers it is the dispatch — the channel refuses BEFORE pushing and returns motivo: "sem-base" through the SAME ref, in the format the module already expects, exactly as dispatch_exec does with the 126. Never a timeout, which is how the silent defect would show up. The two reasons, the two messages and the order in which they apply live in the module, and nowhere else. A NAMED error, and five reasons that do not collapse. sem-base, segmento, nao-e-pasta, mkdir and git travel as motivo alongside the erro text — separated on purpose: the text is for a human to read, the reason is for the other side to DECIDE, and collapsing them would force the engine to match a pt-BR substring. Only sem-base becomes its own atom in the engine (:sem_base), because only it has its own fix; the other four are :recusado with the runner's message. The failing init/clone is a named error and never a plan B: a folder without .git would break the dev agent's worktree, the mirror and the user's own versioning in a place far from the cause. Idempotent, and the three outcomes do not collapse. mkdir -p is already idempotent; what needed a decision was the repository — a folder that is ALREADY a repository comes back as SUCCESS, with the ja-era-repositorio mode, never an init on top (which would lie about what happened) nor a clone (which would fail due to a non-empty folder and turn "it was already ready" into an error). It is the same disposition as ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase, and for the same reason: the message can arrive twice. estado.dir does NOT change. The folder created is the project's from the SERVER's point of view — and it is workspace_confirm that records it there. The root guard.ts uses to contain an approved command remains that of this execution: changing it at runtime would move a containment boundary because of a network message, and this CLI never does that. This is NOT a proposed_action, and no ceiling gains an exception. Creating the folder of the project the user just asked for is CONSENTED configuration, not an agent asking to act — the same line the mirror already established (RN-516). Doing it through a terminal command would fall into the scope of ADR 0055 and become a queue of routine approvals, eroding the ceiling that gives the click its meaning. Where: apps/runner/src/pasta-do-projeto.ts:132 (criarPastaDoProjeto — the guard→disk→versioning order and the five reasons); apps/runner/src/channel.ts:173 (WorkspaceCreateMessage), :194 (WorkspaceCreateResultMessage), :476 (CAPACIDADE_DE_WORKSPACE and capacidadesDoRunner); apps/runner/src/index.ts:1027 (tratarWorkspaceCreate — the order workspace_confirm before the result); apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/pasta_do_projeto.ex:107 (verificar/1) and :134 (criar/3); apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/runner_router.ex:181 (create_workspace/3); apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/capacidades.ex:95 (workspace in the vocabulary, and out of the legacy); apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel.ex:666 (handle_info({:dispatch_workspace_create, …}), the named refusal) and :380 (handle_in("workspace_create_result", …)) Test: apps/runner/src/pasta-do-projeto.spec.ts (happy path with init and with clone; idempotency proven with the REAL versioning binary; the five reasons, with distinct texts, and the folder that is NOT born outside the base); apps/runner/src/index-handlers.spec.ts (the ORDER workspace_confirm → workspace_create_result; without a base, no confirm; a dropped connection pushes nothing); apps/runner/src/channel.spec.ts (workspace only declared with a base; payload without segmento/projectId discarded; malformed env becoming undefined); apps/engine/test/engine/runners/pasta_do_projeto_test.exs (the two preconditions WITHOUT a database — the assertion is the pure ExUnit.Case —, the exact payload, the four reasons and the success without a path that does not become success); apps/engine/test/engine/runners/runner_router_test.exs (the roundtrip and the timeout); apps/engine/test/engine/runners/capacidades_test.exs (workspace declarable, never in the legacy, never required); apps/engine/test/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel_test.exs (the refusal named through the same ref, and nothing pushed to the runner) ADR: 0151 points 3 to 6 Origin: PHASE 29, session 8. Declared and NOT done: what CALLS PastaDoProjeto.criar/3 — the web→api→engine path belongs to session 9 —, and the install.sh that writes the base file, which belongs to another front
documents.s: RN-532 — workspace_create creates the folder under the LOCAL base, and what WRITES is still the workspace_confirm that already existed

documents.t: The creation wizard had one folder browser for two modes that read different disks. RN-504 pointed both to the api — right for mounted, whose folder lives under BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, on the SERVER — and declared the price in writing: "for runner the list stops being the disk of the user's machine and becomes the base". That was accepted because "the runner mode leaves project creation in the next PR", which did not happen: the mode is still offered, and the direction of ADR 0151 (point 7) is the opposite. While it lasted, choosing runner and clicking "Browse folder…" browsed a disk that is not that project's — and nothing on the screen said so, so the error would only show up through the list's CONTENT. The MODE decides the transport, and they are two different questions. mounted stays byte for byte through the api (GET workspaces/:workspaceId/project-folders, hard-scoped to the base — RN-504 intact); runner goes back to fs_list_dir, which always existed on both sides and whose transport in the web never left the repository. It is not a leftover transport that gained a use: it is the question "what is on YOUR machine?", which the api has no way to answer, being asked again of whoever has a way. The anchor of the runner mode is the EARLY creation of RN-437. The channel ticket is scoped to a real projectId, so the click creates the project before opening the modal — the original purpose of that rule, which RN-504 had left without a consumer. And failing that creation does not open the modal in any transport: falling back to the api would show the SERVER's base under the label of "your machine", exactly the defect this rule closes. Without a connected local agent, the mode is still offered — and what declares it is the PICKER, not the mode step. RN-513 hides mounted when the base is unknown or absent, and it is right: there the api HAS a signal (GET .../projects-base), and without a base creation ends in a 400 at the end of the wizard, with no fix on the screen. Here neither of the two things holds. There is no runner presence signal in the api — RN-521 already declares that in writing —, so hiding the mode or graying out the button would be deciding "it doesn't have" from "I don't know", the collapse that RN-088/RN-468 forbid; and the mode is not broken without a runner, because the path is confirmed later, by the CLI (RN-423) — what is missing is only the NAVIGATION. So the declaration goes to the only place that actually asks: the picker, at the moment it asks. The reason is DISCRIMINATED, and the two outcomes do not collapse. MotivoDeFalhaDoAgente is sem-agente (the engine ASSERTS there is no runner connected — a server fact) or sem-resposta (request ceiling, dropped socket, refused ticket — ignorance, and stated as ignorance on the screen). Before this rule what decided was erro?.includes('Nenhum runner conectado') in the COMPONENT — a screen matching a substring of a pt-BR sentence that lives in an .ex of the engine, exactly what RN-532 refuses in writing on the other side ("the text is for a human to read, the reason is for the other side to DECIDE"). The matching remained in one place, the module that owns the channel protocol, and the degradation is named: a sentence rewritten in the engine falls into sem-resposta — the "I don't know" state —, never into "there is an agent". The api transport never fills in motivo, and that is a decision: an api refusal is an api refusal, it has its own message that TEACHES and there is no local agent to install to fix it. The wait is that of RN-474, REUSED and not rewritten. Both reasons lead to EsperaDoRunner — same three states (esperando/confirmado/ semResposta, which never collapse), same 3-minute CEILING, same wording, same signal (workspaceVerifiedAt CHANGING, never "existing"). It gained an optional callback because here the confirmation has a CONSEQUENCE: the listing that failed is redone on its own, instead of the person having to discover they need to click something. The callback fires ONCE per instance — without the ref, each round of the probe would re-fire it and the caller would enter a loop — and it does not assert "it is up now" (workspaceVerifiedAt never said that, RN-468): that is why whoever receives it REPEATS the request, and if the agent has already dropped again the screen goes back to the same state, honest both times. The wait is ONE per screen: RunnerOnboardingPanel gained mostrarEspera, false only where whoever mounts it already shows its own — two would be two probes, two ceilings and, in the worst case, two sentences disagreeing about the same stamp. And the picker says WHOSE disk it is, in BOTH origins. The only signal before that was the label of a shortcut ("Projects base" × "Personal folder"), which names a place and not a machine. The api's sentence is not symmetry decoration: without it the runner's would read as an exceptional warning, when it is information both owe. Where: apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser.ts:60 (MotivoDeFalhaDoAgente, and why only the runner transport fills it in); apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser-channel.ts:66 (FRASE_DO_ENGINE_SEM_RUNNER, the only substring match that remained) and :68 (motivoDaMensagem); apps/web/src/components/FolderBrowserModal.tsx:227 (agenteNaoRespondeu, the decision by reason) and the origin line in both origins; apps/web/src/components/EsperaDoRunner.tsx:91 (onConfirmado) and :136 (the ref that fires it once); apps/web/src/components/RunnerOnboardingPanel.tsx:131 (mostrarEspera); apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.tsx:304 (origemDoNavegador, the transport chosen by mode, undefined when there is no project to anchor) Test: apps/web/src/components/FolderBrowserModal.test.tsx (the list declaring the disk of the user's machine; sem-agente falling into the onboarding panel; the decision by REASON and not by text, with a wording that nobody promised to keep; sem-resposta with the caveat that this does not prove absence, ONLY ONE wait and the ceiling announced; the listing redone on its own when the stamp changes); apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.test.tsx (the mode deciding the transport in both directions; the early creation anchoring the channel; the creation that FAILS opening no browser at all) ADR: 0151 point 7 Origin: PHASE 29, session 9. Declared and NOT done: the picker does not trigger workspace_create — choosing a folder is choosing, and creating is something else. Engine.Runners.PastaDoProjeto.criar/3 (RN-532) still has no caller, and wiring it would require a new HTTP route in the api, outside the scope of this session. The definitive fix of the substring match — the engine sending a code alongside the text, as the runner already does with the five motivo of RN-532 — also belongs to the engine side, and is declared in the code

documents.t: The backup covered one database and ran in one place. Three consequences, and the third is the one that costs code: make test-restore requires kubectl, a cluster and the brabo-backup CronJob in the namespace, and docker-compose.prod.yml had no backup service at all — the image was built by the bake and used only in k8s. Migrating a compose installation had no proven path. Classify before copying. The easy move would be "back up all the volumes", and it is wrong: of the seven, neo4j_data and project_workspaces are DERIVED, ollama_data is re-obtainable and brabo_projects_base belongs to the user. Copying them gives an impression of coverage without adding recovery. Sources of truth are TWO: pgdata — which was already covered, as a logical dump and never as a copy of the data directory of a running Postgres — and git_local_repos, which no backup covered. A project with the local provider keeps the bare repository in there, and it is NOT rebuildable from Postgres: the event log keeps the narrative, not the git objects. The runbook prose said the opposite ("the real repositories live in GitHub/GitLab") and it is that sentence that explains how the volume went years without coverage — it holds for github/gitlab, and for local there is no upstream at all. The guarantee of the repos archive is declared, and it is smaller than "snapshot". Nothing is quiesced. What is guaranteed is consistency PER REFERENCE — git writes the objects before moving the ref, and swaps the ref by atomic rename, so a tar that crosses a git push gets the old value or the new one, never half of one. What is NOT guaranteed is a global instant (the tar walks the tree over a period) nor object connectivity (the image has no git, on purpose). And a concurrent gc deleting a packfile becomes a FAILURE and not a partial archive: the status of tar is captured in a file, because in POSIX sh the status of a pipe is that of the last command — without it the incomplete archive would announce itself as good, and a backup that lies is worse than a backup that fails, because only the second becomes an alert. *.lock is left out: restoring an orphan lock produces a repository in which every git refuses to operate. Disk destination, S3 optional. The five S3 variables stop being mandatory and become what they already were in practice — the configuration of ONE of the destinations. BACKUP_DIR set chooses disk; absent, S3, which is how the k8s CronJob keeps running without a single line of change. The inference (instead of a mandatory destination variable) is what keeps that path intact: an explicit destination would break the CronJob on deploy day, not on commit day. Four prefixes and not two (daily/, weekly/, git-daily/, git-weekly/) because retention is by COUNT: two kinds of archive under one prefix would make "keep 7" mean three and a half backups. The compose restore changes the wrapper, never the judgment. test-restore-compose.sh triggers a REAL backup through the same image and the same production command, and calls the SAME brabo-restore, with the SAME three validations (table list against the source, count of the critical ones in the backup window, dense continuity of the seq of session_events). deploy/k8s/test-restore.sh stays intact — unifying them would make the compose path depend on kubectl, which is the dependency it exists not to have. And restore.sh still does not touch the SOURCE database, a property that is not negotiated for migration convenience. The step only compose can demand is the third: verifying the repos archive, because in k8s that volume is not even mounted in the pod (skipping is correct) and under compose it is (skipping would be a false green). Restoring the repos is a SIBLING command, not a phase of the other — they are two artifacts with two judgments, and joining them would make a git failure fail the validation of the event log. It verifies by default and only writes with --restaurar; it refuses to extract over existing repos (the mix of two states raises no error and only shows up in a fetch with the wrong history); and — a finding of the real execution — it refuses BEFORE the tar when the volume does not accept writes, naming --user 0:0. git_local_repos is shared by three images with different uids and carries the owner of whoever mounted it first (measured: 1000:1000, mode 0755) while this image runs as uid 70. When the extraction runs as root, what comes out is handed back to the DIRECTORY's owner and never left as root: otherwise the volume would come back intact and useless, with api and engine unable to write to what was just restored. Neo4j gets reprojection, not backup. Restoring a possibly old projection next to a Postgres restored at another instant gives two derived states from different moments, with nothing reconciling them. The reprojection was not built here (it is BRB-018): until it exists, a migrated installation is born with an EMPTY graph — known and named degradation, not data loss, because the RAG lives in pgvector and comes in the dump. Since RN-569 it exists (grafo:reprojetar), and the empty graph now lasts until someone runs it. Where: docker/backup/lib.sh:28 (destino_tipo, the inference that keeps the CronJob intact), :65 (destino_esperar asking about WRITING and not about existence), :105 (destino_enviar, writing to .parcial and rename), :181 (the guarantee of the bare repos, written next to the code that produces it), :221 (git_arquivar, the tar status in a file), :259 (git_restaurar, handing back the owner) and :273 (git_raiz_gravavel); docker/backup/backup.sh:31 (destino_preparar — the five S3 variables ceasing to be mandatory), :149 (the three outcomes of the repos volume, without collapsing "not mounted" with "empty"), :170 (the check of the tar status) and :220 (the pruning of the four prefixes); docker/backup/restore.sh:28 (the same destination as the backup) and :120, :184, :215 (the three validations and the verdict, without a single line of change); docker/backup/restore-git.sh:43 (verifying as default), :109 (the refusal to extract over) and :123 (the refusal for writing, with the fix named); docker/backup/test-restore-compose.sh:60 (the --profile in config and not in run); docker/docker-compose.prod.yml:392 (the backup service, under profiles and restart: "no") and :550 (the volume that does NOT enter the classification of the seven); docker/backup/Dockerfile.prod:80 (the /backups created and chown-ed BEFORE the USER); Makefile:54 (test-restore-compose) Test: scripts/ci/backup-lib.spec.ts — the functions in a real sh, against a real directory: the five operations of the disk destination; the absent object measuring 0; the atomic write and the .parcial that the listing ignores; the sibling prefixes that do not mix; the destination that exists and does NOT accept writes (failure case); "not mounted" × "mounted and empty"; the repos archive with status 0 and content re-read; *.lock and objects/tmp_* out; the archive→restore cycle returning byte for byte; the refusal to restore where one cannot write; and the truncated tar that fails when READ, never by size ADR: 0152 Origin: PHASE 29, session 5. Exercised for real against the development compose with real data (55 tables, 422 events, the bare repos of exp001 and exp004), including the restore into a new volume checked with git fsck — the record is in docs/runbook.md, section "Last verified run — compose, disk destination". Declared and NOT done: the adapter's S3 path has no automated coverage (it would require an endpoint), and it is still the same aws command as before; the Neo4j reprojection is BRB-018; and nothing here schedules the backup in a compose — what triggers it is a human or the installer (session 6)
documents.s: RN-528 — git_local_repos enters the backup, the destination can be disk, and the compose restore reuses the SAME three validations
