documents.t: PHASE 28 refused in writing the one-line installer while the artifacts were not signed (BRB-005), and that is why PHASE 29 signs before installing. Session 2, ADR 0149.
documents.s: PHASE 29 — the one-line installation: signing what is published

documents.t: Every final tag signs what it publishes, and verifies what it signed before publishing the Release: the five images are signed by DIGEST (they were four when this rule was written; the fifth, the broker, came in with ADR 0162), read from .release/images.json — never by tag. A tag is a moving pointer: signing :5.0.0 would attest what that tag pointed to at the instant of signing, and not what it points to when someone downloads. The digest is what the manifest already records and what the production overlay already applies (ADR 0119); the runner binaries (five targets when this rule was born, four since ADR 0174, which removed darwin-x64) are covered by ONE signed checksums.txt, and not by one signature per binary — whoever verifies three and forgets the fourth has no way of knowing they forgot; the signature is keyless (GitHub Actions OIDC): the identity that signs is the workflow itself, and there is no private key in custody. An own key pair would mean one more CI secret, and this repository has already seen a PAT expire silently and fail two runs of tag-release (ADR 0139); a verification failure is a named refusal, never a warning. A warning one accepts by clicking is a verification that does not exist. The manifest declares what it covers. The matrix is fail-fast: false on purpose, so a target that did not build does not prevent the other four from having a manifest — but the job names in the log the targets that were left out, because a checksums.txt that lists four and keeps silent about the fifth is worse than none: whoever verifies the four concludes they verified the release. This half was written intention and a mechanism that did not fulfill it: with needs: build, a target that does not build did not prevent, it DELAYED by a day — see RN-565, which makes it true and measures the number. Where: .github/workflows/release.yml (steps "Instalar o cosign" and "Assinar as imagens publicadas", with id-token: write in the permissions block); .github/workflows/build-runner-binaries.yml (job checksums, without needs: since RN-565 — the wait is for the assets, with a ceiling). Test: scripts/ci/actions-pinadas.spec.ts covers the SHA pin of sigstore/cosign-installer (with the version comment alongside, which is what tells a human and Dependabot which version that hash is). The signature itself is only proven on a real tag — declared, like the rest of the release pipeline. Origin: PHASE 29, session 2. Closes BRB-005 for images and binaries. Does NOT cover the operating-system code-signing of the binaries (macOS notarization, Windows Authenticode), which requires a paid identity and stays in the backlog.
documents.s: RN-524 — A published artifact is signed by workflow identity, verified in the same run, and the verification refuses instead of warning

documents.t: install.sh (repository root, versioned and published as a Release asset) is the single installation door. Four guarantees, and each one exists against a concrete defect: The invocation preserves stdin and leaves a FILE. The documented form is curl -fsSLO …/install.sh && bash install.sh — download and run a file with bash —, and never curl … | sh: with the script arriving through the pipe, the process's stdin IS the download, and any read reads bytes of the script itself or hits EOF. An installer that cannot ask would choose on its own where to create folders on someone's computer — the opposite of the rule RN-511 already applies to the base consent. Until AT-083 the documented form was sh -c "$(curl -fsSL …)", and it never worked: the verification of its own origin (the next paragraph) computes the hash of $0, and in X -c "…" the $0 is the shell's name, not a file; with dash as sh the script died earlier, at set -o pipefail. The maintainer's decision (09/18) was to change the DOC and keep the verification by $0, without a skip door (ADR 0150). The wrong forms became named refusals, before the first download, that print the right form: running under a shell that is not bash (POSIX block at the top, before set -o pipefail) and running without a file (exigir_o_proprio_arquivo, which requires the top-level BASH_SOURCE and a readable $0 — /bin/bash -c leaves $0=/bin/bash, which exists, and without the first half its hash would go to the manifest and the person would read the tampering sentence). The form is ONE constant (COMO_RODAR), used by the refusals and by the report without a TTY. It verifies its own origin before acting, and the chain has two links: the signature of the Release's checksums.txt (RN-524), and the hash of this file inside the verified manifest. The cosign that performs the verification is itself pinned by version and checked by hash against the value written in the script — whoever trusts install.sh enough to execute it trusts the hash it carries, and the chain does not become more fragile than the link that starts it. A failure in any link is a named refusal, never a warning. Computing a hash has ONE function and TWO accepted tools — sha256sum or shasum -a 256 —, resolved before the first download and never in the middle of a verification: a machine that has nothing to check with should not get to have anything to check. Lacking both is its OWN refusal, which names the two tools, says where each one lives and asserts that nothing was downloaded — never the divergent-hash refusal, which is the incident one ("stop and investigate"). The distinction is not style: the script called sha256sum directly at the five verification points, macOS does not ship it, and the command not found reached whoever was installing as an accusation of tampering — blocking every installation on the platform the script itself supports (there is a pinned cosign darwin-* in it) and teaching people to ignore the sentence on the day it is true. --print-plan runs without either and declares which one the script accepts (conferir-hash). And there is a THIRD refusal, since AT-083: the tool exists but cannot read the file. Without it, hash_sha256 returned empty from inside the command substitution (errexit does not reach the subshell) and the next comparison failed with the caller's incident text — the tampering accusation of AT-091 by another path. Now it is falha_ao_calcular_hash, which names the file and says there was nothing to compare. Detection names what it found. Through the marker ($XDG_STATE_HOME/brabo/install-state.json) when it exists; through signals (compose project brabo*, units brabo-runner-*, binary in the PATH) when not — and the list is printed before any question. There is no path "I found something and decide on my own". Without a TTY the script reports and exits 0, as consentir-base.mjs already does. It never deletes a user folder. The projects base and the mirror folder are out of reach of any confirmation — the same rule as the mirror (RN-516): a user folder is accumulation, not product state. A named volume only goes with confirmation, and listed one by one before asking. The marker lives in $XDG_STATE_HOME and not in ~/.brabo/, which is where the runner keeps things per PROJECT: installation state and project configuration are different lives, and joining them would make removing one delete the other. Where: install.sh (root). Test: scripts/dev/install.spec.ts — the --print-state and --print-plan modes prove the DECISION without a TTY, without network and without effect, in the mold of bootstrap.spec.ts; and the block "o hash num PATH sem sha256sum" runs the hash functions in the real shell, with the PATH assembled tool by tool, checking the TWO refusals (absent tool × divergent hash) and that the first never uses the second's vocabulary; scripts/dev/install-invocacao.spec.ts runs the script through the wrong forms (bash -c, /bin/bash -c, pipe, dash -c, dash install.sh) and demands the named refusal with the right form before any download, the third hash refusal, and that runbook, bootstrap and header teach the SAME form. Origin: PHASE 29, session 3 (ADR 0150). In this session the script installs nothing — bringing up the compose, generating secrets and installing the runner are sessions 4 and 7, and it says so in the output instead of ending silently.
documents.s: RN-526 — The installer verifies its own origin, NAMES what it found before asking, and never deletes a user folder

documents.t: Revised by RN-575 (ADR 0162): the broker service came to exist in this compose, off under the container-broker profile and turned on by the installer only with consent; the mandatory images are FIVE. The rest of this rule holds as is. docker/docker-compose.install.yml is what runs on the machine of whoever installed, and it is not docker-compose.prod.yml. Three differences, each with a reason: the five images come from a mandatory variable (${BRABO_API_IMAGE:?…}), with no default. With a default, an absent variable would bring up half the stack with an image nobody chose, and the error would show up as strange behavior instead of refusal; there is no build: block anywhere: this file does not build, and that is its point; the broker service does not exist here, because its image is not published (docker-bake.hcl has four targets). Declared consequence: with --source=ghcr, a mounted project does not start a container (ADR 0150, decision 7). docker-compose.prod.yml stays intact — it declares itself a validation compose, it is what docker/smoke.sh uses building locally on purpose, and promoting it would break that use. The cost of the two files is declared, and the ceiling against divergence is mechanical: scripts/dev/composes-em-conformidade.spec.ts fails if the installation one gains a service, volume or port the validation one does not have, if any build: survives, or if a third-party image loosens to a different tag. The image source is a choice, and "official" is the result of verification. --source=ghcr (default) resolves by digest from the Release's images.json; --source=local runs docker buildx bake and requires a clean tree on a tag — an image built from a dirty tree is not the version it says it is, and the marker would record a lie. The secrets are born once and persist. The five of RN-114 plus NEO4J_PASSWORD, generated with openssl rand in the same mold as docker/smoke.sh:31-57 — including the detail of NEO4J_PASSWORD being -hex and not -base64, because a / breaks the parse of NEO4J_AUTH. The .env is created empty and with mode 600 BEFORE receiving content: creating with the user's umask and tightening afterwards would leave the secrets readable for a window, and it is precisely the file that cannot have that window. And the .env is a file COMPOSE parses, and it is proven against it (AT-083). The SECRET_KEY_BASE came from openssl rand -base64 64, which BREAKS the line at 64 characters: the secret's 88 went on two lines, and the second was left loose in the .env. Measured over 100 generations, Compose refused 49 ("unexpected character in variable name") and ACCEPTED 51 — with the secret cut at 64 characters, which is still Phoenix's minimum and that is why it came up without a warning. Every base64 now goes through segredo_base64 (| tr -d '\n'), and the file is written by escrever_env — a function, and not the body of main, so that the spec writes the SAME file the installation writes. There is no migrate step, and there must not be: the compose chains api → migrate-api with service_completed_successfully, and up --wait waits. A second place ordering a migration would be the second source of the same truth. And the installer asks before asserting. After up --wait — which already waits for the healthcheck — it hits the /health of the api and of the engine, and only then says it installed. It is the rule reset-total.sh learned the hard way: it announced "reset complete" with the api in Exited (1). Where: install.sh (root), docker/docker-compose.install.yml. Test: scripts/dev/install.spec.ts (the plan, without a TTY or effect) and scripts/dev/composes-em-conformidade.spec.ts (the divergence between the two composes); scripts/dev/install-env.spec.ts generates the secrets and the .env through the real functions, runs the file through docker compose config against the installation compose and demands that EACH secret reach the services WHOLE (skips naming the reason without docker compose), with the old generation pinned as rejected. Origin: PHASE 29, session 4 (ADR 0150). Installing the runner (session 7) and migrating a previous installation (session 6) remain out, and --print-plan declares them nao-nesta-versao.
documents.s: RN-527 — The installation comes up from its OWN compose, by chosen image, and checks health before saying it installed

documents.t: GET /runner-releases/binary is @Public(), without authentication, and it is step 4 of the browser setup flow (RN-473, ADR 0118). Until session 3 of PHASE 29 it validated the INPUT (platform against a closed allowlist) and streamed the bytes from GitHub straight to the client, without verifying anything — it is the consumer that ADR 0149 names and RN-524 left pending. Now it checks the sha256 of the bytes against the checksums.txt of the SAME release before answering anything, and the Content-Digest header (RFC 9530) repeats the checked hash, so whoever receives it can redo the math. What this verification does NOT do, and it is written where it is done. It does not verify the signature of the manifest (checksums.txt.bundle). This is integrity against the manifest, not provenance: whoever can rewrite the Release rewrites both files and passes. The two ways of closing this were MEASURED in this session, and both were refused: path measured why not cosign in the api image 155 MB (cosign-linux-amd64 v2.6.1) nearly doubles the runtime image (Alpine + Node), published by digest on GHCR (ADR 0119), to verify an optional download @sigstore/verify + @sigstore/tuf 2.5 MB, 12 packages size is not the cost. getTrustedRoot() refreshes TUF metadata against tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev (the package's seeds.json only seeds the root.json), so a public route that today depends on ONE third-party host would come to depend on two. And, by the rule of ADRs 0041/0042 — a capability is only declared when proven —, there is no way to prove the path today: no Release has checksums.txt.bundle, because the checksums job was born in session 2 and only runs on a final tag, a gap RN-524 itself already declares on the signer's side What verifies the SIGNATURE is install.sh (session 4/7), which has a real cosign and downloads it pinned with sha256sum -c (decision 4 of ADR 0149). BRB-005 remains open for the provenance half of this route, and the registry says so — it is not a footnote, it is the limit of what the route proves. A Release without checksums.txt is a REFUSAL, never "I serve with a warning". A warning that one accepts by clicking is a verification that does not exist (ADR 0149, decision 3) — and it would be the cheapest downgrade possible: deleting 400 bytes from the Release would turn off everyone's check. The cost is measured and small: in v5.0.0 there are two binaries (linux-x64, linux-arm64) and no manifest, and the binary step is best-effort in the browser flow (RN-473, step 4) — it falls back to npm install -g @brabo/runner, which depends on no release at all. Every release prior to the first tag after ADR 0149 falls into that path, by construction. The six 502 outcomes do not collapse. The status alone does not separate them and they ask different actions of whoever called, so the refusal carries a motivo in the body — plataforma_nao_publicada, release_sem_manifesto, manifesto_nao_cobre_a_plataforma, manifesto_ilegivel, download_falhou, hash_divergente. It is the rule of RN-470 in an api response: "this platform has not come out yet" says to wait for the next release, "release without a manifest" says to use npm, and "divergent hash" is an incident. In particular, "manifest not listed in the release" and "listed manifest that failed to download" are DIFFERENT outcomes — confusing them would send the person to install via npm because of a momentary network failure. Checking a hash requires reading all the bytes, and that goes through disk. Buffering the binary's ~79 MB in memory would be trivial exhaustion on a public route (the api pod has limits.memory: 512Mi), and caching the bytes would be worse — five platforms × 79 MB. The bytes come down in a stream to a temporary file in /tmp (an emptyDir mounted precisely because the api's rootfs is read-only), with the hash computed along the way, and the file is re-read in a stream to the client only after the hash matches: constant memory, and no unchecked byte reaches the client. A ceiling of 256 MiB aborts an absurd response before filling /tmp. The existing cache (URLs, 5 min) stays, and now also keeps the already parsed manifest — hundreds of bytes of TEXT, never binary bytes —, in the SAME entry and never in a cache of its own: in different windows, a release published in the middle would make the new hash be checked against the old binary, and the outcome would be a hash_divergente that would look like tampering. Where: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/runner-releases.controller.ts (the verification, the byte ceiling, the temporary file and the Content-Digest), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/checksums.ts (the pure reading of the manifest and the union of MotivoDaRecusa), apps/web/src/lib/runner-bootstrap.ts (baixarBinario now reads message and motivo from the body, and the sentence reaches falhaDoBinario) Test: apps/api/test/interfaces/runner-releases.controller.spec.ts (happy path with Content-Digest; divergent hash with NO byte or header in the body; release without a manifest refusing before downloading the binary; manifest that does not cover the platform; unreadable manifest; failed download; and the cache keeping release and manifest together) and the describe('parsearChecksums') of the same file; apps/web/src/lib/runner-bootstrap.test.ts (the api's sentence and the motivo reaching the caller, and a non-JSON body not becoming a second exception) Origin: PHASE 29, session 3. ADR 0149, the third consumer of the table of decision 3 — for the HALF the api can prove today, with the other half named instead of faked | BACKUP_DIR points to a directory that exists and does NOT accept writes | the backup refuses BEFORE the pg_dump, saying it is WRITING — a read-only destination would pass an existence test and fail later, with the diagnosis pointing to the wrong place (RN-528) | | A concurrent git gc deletes a packfile in the middle of the bare repos tar | the execution becomes failed in backup_runs, with the tar status named — never a partial archive announcing itself as good, because only a failure becomes an alert (RN-528) | | git_local_repos volume not mounted in the backup container (the k8s CronJob) | the step is SKIPPED and stated in the log — and "not mounted" is never collapsed with "mounted and empty", which is the normal state of an installation without a local project (RN-528) | | There are bare repos in the volume and NO archive in the git-daily/ prefix | brabo-restore-git fails saying this volume is without coverage — absent-and-empty is another outcome, and exits successfully (RN-528) | | Truncated bare repos archive | fails when READ (tar -tzf), never by size: a cut tar has bytes to spare. It is the pg_restore --list of the git side (RN-528) | | brabo-restore-git --restaurar on a volume that already has bare repos | refused: overlaying two repository states raises no error at all and only shows up in a fetch with the wrong history. RESTORE_GIT_FORCE=1 for whoever really wants it (RN-528) | | brabo-restore-git --restaurar without being able to write to the volume (uid 70 × api owner) | refuses BEFORE the tar, naming --user 0:0 — finding out in the middle of the extraction would leave the volume half done. And what is extracted as root goes back to the DIRECTORY's owner (RN-528) |
documents.s: RN-525 — The binary proxy checks the hash against the manifest of the same release, refuses when it cannot check, and SAYS that this is integrity and not provenance

documents.t: Installing over an existing installation is not offered: either one migrates, or one stops. An up over volumes of another version is the kind of damage that gives no warning. The migration has an order, and the middle step is what gives it meaning: backup → PROVE it restores → ask → delete → install → restore. The proof is not overzealousness. A backup nobody tried to restore is a file, and the time to find that out is not after the down -v — that is why the installer runs docker/backup/test-restore-compose.sh (the SAME three validations as restore.sh, ADR 0152) before any deletion. A backup that fails, or a proof that fails, interrupt the migration without deleting anything, and the message says where the backup was left. The backup destination is a HOST folder, and that is the detail that makes the difference between migrating and losing: the compose default is the named volume backup_local, which down -v would delete together with what one wants to preserve. What the migration deletes: the installation's named volumes (pgdata included), the containers and the network. What it never deletes: the projects base — when BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE points to a host folder, the compose line is a bind-mount, and down -v does not touch binds —, the mirror folder (RN-516) and the freshly proven backup. The Postgres dump is not restored automatically over the new database: brabo-restore validates against a test database and never overwrites the source (ADR 0152), and restoring over an already populated database is a destructive operation the installer does not take on its own. The local git repositories, yes — they are a source of truth that would be born empty. Where: install.sh, migrar_instalacao_anterior and restaurar_apos_migrar. Test: scripts/dev/install.spec.ts — the plan declares apagar-sem-backup-provado: nunca, and a test checks that the call to the proof comes before the deletion call in the code. Origin: PHASE 29, session 6 (ADR 0150, ADR 0152).
documents.s: RN-530 — Migrating requires a PROVEN backup: the installer only earns the right to delete after restoring

documents.t: One base, consented once. install.sh asks where the projects will live and writes the same path in BOTH places: BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE in .env (the server, ADR 0141) and the base field of runner.json (the local agent, RN-529). What differs between mounted and runner is who executes, not where the code lives — two different bases for the same folder would be the namespace collision ADR 0141 refused in writing. The base is refused when it is not absolute, when it is inside the Brabo checkout and when it contains the checkout — both directions, as preflight.mjs already does on the server side. The ~ is not expanded on purpose: the value goes into a configuration file, and a ~ written there is read literally. The local agent is installed already executable. The binary is downloaded, checked against the same signed checksums.txt the script already verified to check itself (RN-524) — downloading it twice would be two chances of getting different manifests, and the second would not be verified — and installed with install -m 0755, which sets the execute bit in the same act in which it copies. This closes BRB-031. The manual chmod +x survived PHASE 28 because installing as a service did not come from a versioned artifact: whoever got to run brabo-runner service install had already needed to make the binary executable to get to the command. Coming from the installer, the step disappears — the browser's File System Access API does not preserve the bit, a script does. A release without the platform's binary does not interrupt the installation: the rest is already up, and the message points to npm install -g @brabo/runner. It is the same disposition as the binary step in the browser setup (RN-473), and the reason is the same — the local agent is the last stage, not a prerequisite. Where: install.sh, consentir_base and instalar_o_runner. Test: scripts/dev/install.spec.ts — install -m 0755 present, the chmod instruction addressed to the user absent, and the check against the signed manifest named. Origin: PHASE 29, session 7 (ADR 0150, ADR 0151).
documents.s: RN-531 — The installer consents ONE base for both sides and installs the local agent already executable

documents.t: Two halves of the same guarantee. install.sh enters checksums.txt and the Release. Without that the verification it does of itself (RN-526) would be a dead letter: it checks its own hash against the signed manifest, and the manifest did not cover it. The file comes from the tag's checkout, not from a download — it is the same commit that produced everything else being signed in the same job. And it is exercised on a clean machine, which is what the ephemeral Actions runner is: a freshly created host, without Brabo, without .env, without a marker. The E2E proves, in this order: the plan did not stop promising what it never deletes; the state on a clean machine does not invent a marker or signals; without a TTY the installer reports, exits 0 and does not write; and, with a real TTY (not a pipe — the pipe is precisely what would kill consent), the full installation verifies the signature, checks its own hash, writes the marker and leaves the .env in mode 600. Correction (AT-083): the "TTY simulated by script -qec" this paragraph asserted was never a TTY for the installer. The step ran script -qec "… ./install.sh … < respostas", with the < INSIDE the script command: the installer's stdin was the file, [ -t 0 ] was always false, and the interactive flow was never exercised. Today what runs the installer is a PTY driver in Python (python3 -I, no new dependency), which puts it on the slave side of the pty and WAITS for each question before answering — and, for the two password ones, waits for the echo to be OFF, which proves the "no echo" of RN-547 and prevents the password from appearing in the output. The E2E also downloads and runs the installer through the SAME form the runbook prescribes (curl -fsSLO + bash install.sh, RN-526), and fails right away if the installer says "Sem terminal interativo". Since the workflow still does not run on PRs, the driver is extracted from it and exercised in scripts/dev/install-e2e.spec.ts against a fake installer (terminal seen, answers in order, password out of the output, and the two named stops), with the old form pinned as the one that did NOT give a terminal. It does not run on pull_request, and the reason is the same as for the signature: the signed manifest only exists after a final tag. Making the script run on a PR would require giving it a door to SKIP verification — the door ADR 0150 refuses, and which once opened would hold for anyone, not only for CI. It is the decision the RAG golden-set had already taken by the same reasoning (ADR 0138): what is not exercisable on a PR runs on its own cadence, and the workflow says why instead of faking coverage. Where: .github/workflows/install-e2e.yml; .github/workflows/build-runner-binaries.yml, job checksums. Test: the workflow itself — and scripts/dev/install.spec.ts keeps covering the decision without network; scripts/dev/install-e2e.spec.ts (block "o TTY do E2E é um TTY para o INSTALADOR") exercises the PTY driver on PRs. Origin: PHASE 29, session 10 (ADR 0149, ADR 0150). TODO(humano): the RNs above were extracted from code and tests. It remains to confirm whether there is a business rule not implemented that should be here — something agreed on and not yet coded does not show up in this sweep.
documents.s: RN-534 — The installer enters the signed manifest, and is exercised on a clean machine

documents.t: Creating a project and provisioning git were, in practice, the same gesture — and what joined them was a SCREEN. ProvisioningPage fires provisionRepository in the mount effect and is its only caller in the web; the wizard navigated there on confirm, so every project was born with a full repository and Gitflow, without anyone having asked. The product owner wants the opposite: what is generated for now goes without git, and the repository is only born when development really starts — the moment when the Arquiteto passes the handoff to the Dev Lead. The postponement mechanism is not navigating to that screen. On create, the wizard goes straight to the PROJECT page. Nothing else needed to be turned off: since the trigger lives in the useEffect of a route that is no longer visited, ceasing to visit it IS the postponement. The route still exists and is still reachable — the Dashboard leads to it when provisioning failed and needs to be resumed. Provider and credential leave creation, and stay in adoption. With no repository to create now, asking "where to host" would be collecting a decision the screen does not use, and the credential step would demand a PAT for a repository nobody will create. Adopting is the opposite by construction — it points to a repository that already exists, and without a provider there is nothing to point to. The wizard now has three steps when creating and four or five when adopting. The Confirm screen stops promising Gitflow. It announced "N Gitflow steps" when creating, counting BOOTSTRAP_STEPS; that would become a lie the moment the bootstrap stopped running there. It now says WHEN the repository is born, instead of asserting it is already being born. Declared consequence: between creation and the handoff, the project exists without a repository. Nothing breaks — GET .../repository answers null and not 404, the project page already has the "repository not provisioned" state and the Repository section in Settings simply does not appear —, but every path that needs a working tree fails NAMED until then (remoto_de_trabalho returns :not_found, and open_adr_pr refuses with "Projeto sem repositório provisionado"). That stops being an edge and becomes the normal state of the beginning of a project. The trigger is the next delivery, and without it a project created today would stay without a repository forever: accepting the Arquiteto → Dev Lead handoff now provisions local, the only provider that does not ask for a credential. Since RN-582, that trigger is accepting the handoff to the Arquiteto (the Dev Lead one stayed as a second door), and activating execution without a repository is refused. The warning "on GitHub's free plan, a private repository does not accept branch protection" left the screen along with it — not because it stopped being true, but because it became unreachable: the condition was provider === 'github', and when creating there is no longer a chosen provider. Where: apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.tsx:379 (stepKeys, now dependent on adotando), :540 (the provider guard restricted to adoption) and :590 (the navigation to /projects/$projectId) Test: apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.test.tsx, describe('NewProjectWizard — o git é adiado') — "criar não passa mais pela página de provisionamento — vai direto ao projeto", "criar tem TRÊS passos: provider e credencial saíram", "adotar mantém provider e credencial" e "a tela de Confirmar não promete mais o Gitflow agora" Origin: request of the product owner — "o que for gerado por hora segue sem git; git mesmo só será iniciado após iniciar desenvolvimento em projetos novos, neste momento que deve rodar o bootstrap"
documents.s: RN-541 — Creating a project does NOT create a git repository; the bootstrap is postponed until the Arquiteto's handoff

documents.t: Revised by RN-582 (ADR 0165): the TRIGGER became accepting the handoff to the Arquiteto. Accepting to the Dev Lead described below keeps provisioning, as an idempotent second door, and the rest of this rule (always local, failure as an event, adopted is not a failure) still holds. The text below is that of the original decision. RN-541 took provisioning out of creation and declared that the trigger would come next. This is the trigger — and without it a created project would stay without a repository forever, because ProvisioningPage was the only caller of provisionRepository in the web and creation stopped navigating there. The moment is accepting the handoff from the Arquiteto to the Dev Lead, and not execution activation. They are DISTINCT instants, in this order: accepting the handoff activates the Dev Lead; activating execution is when the dev agents start claiming tasks. It is at the first that "development has started" becomes true, and it is what the product owner asked for — "quando o arquiteto passar o handoff para o desenvolvedor iniciar o desenvolvimento". The branch lives in AcceptHandoffUseCase, next to the 'infra' branch that already existed and for the same ordering reason: the effect happens before activateAgent, so that the agent wakes up in a project that already has somewhere to work. Always local. It is the only provider that asks for no credential at all — the if (providerName !== 'local') of ProvisionRepositoryUseCase never gets to resolve a secret, and LocalGitProvider.createRepo does not even read the accessToken the signature accepts. That is what makes automatic provisioning possible: nobody chose hosting in the middle of the acceptance, so there is no credential to fetch nor question to ask. Publishing to a remote provider remains a separate path (adoption, or conversion in Settings) — declared, not forgotten. Accepted side effect: protectBranch: false in the local provider makes the last bootstrap step degrade (step_degraded), never fail. The failure becomes an EVENT, never an exception. This use case has no transaction: when provisioning runs, updateStatus('accepted') and the handoff.accepted event are already COMMITTED. A throw would return a 500 to the user about a handoff that, in the database, was accepted — and would also prevent the activateAgent right below, leaving the Dev Lead not waking up because of a git failure. So the outcome goes to the event log as repository.provision_failed, with origem and the real message, and the acceptance proceeds. It is the usual rule: a failure records the origin and never becomes an empty response. What is NOT a failure: a project that ADOPTED a repository. ProvisionRepository refuses that case with ConflictException on purpose — bootstrapping a third-party repository only runs by plan approval (RN-045) —, but the project HAS a repository, so there is nothing to provision and recording that as a failure would lie about its state. The branch queries findByProjectId and exits before. A created repository that already exists is not skipped: it falls into the normal use case, which is idempotent by design ("running again does not fail"), and that is how an interrupted bootstrap completes. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/agents/accept-handoff.use-case.ts — the dev-lead branch in execute and the private method provisionarRepositorio, with the try/catch and the early exit for the adopted repository; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/agents/agents-use-cases.module.ts (the import of GitUseCasesModule — the arrow is agents → git, and git does not import agents, so there is no cycle) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/agents/accept-handoff.use-case.spec.ts — happy path ("aceitar para o Dev Lead provisiona local com o slug do projeto"), the two failure cases ("provisionamento que falha NÃO derruba o aceite nem a ativação" and "a falha vira evento nomeado, com origem e a mensagem real"), and the limits ("aceitar para OUTRO agente não provisiona nada", "projeto que ADOTOU repositório não provisiona, e isso não é falha", "repositório já CRIADO cai no caso de uso, que é idempotente por desenho") Origin: request of the product owner — "o gatilho deve vir quando o arquiteto passar o handoff para o desenvolvedor iniciar o desenvolvimento"
documents.s: RN-522 — The repository is provisioned on ACCEPTING the Arquiteto → Dev Lead handoff, always local, and the failure never takes down the acceptance

documents.t: Every artifact the agents produce lives exclusively in the event log — apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/emit_artifact.ex:3-5 says literally that "there is no artifacts table". That stays right for the SOURCE, and this RN does not touch it. What it closes is another hole: that memory did not reach anywhere a person would open. Whoever opened the project folder in the editor found nothing of the reasoning that produced the code. (The postponed provisioning — creating a project no longer creating a repository, and git being born at the acceptance of the handoff to the Dev Lead — opens an entire interval in which the project does not even have a repository, and makes this folder even more necessary; it comes in its own PR, and this RN does not depend on it.) Each artifact.* event of an allowed type becomes a Markdown file in docs/<agente>/ inside the project's workspace. It is a derived projection, in the same strict sense ADR 0101 gave the Neo4j graph: the source is the event, the folder can be deleted entirely and rebuilt — since RN-590 via artefatos:reprojetar —, and nothing in the product reads from it to decide anything at all. The mechanism is that of GraphProjector, copied piece by piece — its own poller, public drainOnce(), a flag against overlapping cycles, batch of 50, and markProcessed only after success. The outbox row is a THIRD one, written in the same transaction as the event, under its OWN aggregate_type (artifact_projection): Engine.Outbox.Drain only drains session, task and container, and competing for the 'session' row would mean losing the race against it almost always. One deliberate difference from the graph: the aggregateId is the project, not the session — the folder belongs to the project, and writing it there spares the projector a query per artifact. The list is an ALLOWLIST. A new artifact type is born outside the projection and enters when someone decides it is a document, instead of showing up on its own in a folder the user reads. Left out are qa_verdict, secops_verdict, task_blocked and infra_delegation_files: they are OPERATIONAL outcomes, and a per-task gate verdict would fill docs/qa-lead/ with files nobody opens, costing the folder the property that makes it useful — fitting in one glance. Versioned overwrites; append-only carries the seq. The four types read by reduction to the highest version (module_map, module_routing, project_image, c4_diagram) always write the same file, and the folder shows the current one — the history stays whole in the event log. The others become their own file with the event's seq in the name, and without it two artifacts of the same type with the same title would generate the same file, with the second erasing the first: the only way for this projection to lose information the source has. Two barriers against the filesystem, and the second is not redundant. The name comes from the title the MODEL wrote. slugDeArquivo derives a name from a closed alphabet (no return path lets a separator survive; it returns null when nothing remains), and FsArtifactFileStore checks again with relative() before opening. The two answer different questions — "what name do I derive from this" and "what am I actually going to open" —, and trusting only the first would make the safety of the write depend on no future change of slug ever letting a separator through, which is the containment ADR 0130 refuses on principle. The projection never takes down the source. No throw escapes the cycle: each item fails in isolation, is logged and stays processed_at IS NULL for the next cycle. Unlike the graph, there is no error here that stops the whole batch — a write failure tends to belong to the ITEM, and stopping the batch would block all those behind it. An event that vanished from the event log is marked processed, not retried forever. In runner mode the folder diverts to the managed root, for the same physical reason as permissions.json (RN-478): what writes is the api, from inside its container, and the runner's channel only carries commands, with no primitive to write content. Declared cost: there docs/ does not sit next to the code. The write does NOT go through proposed_action, and it is not an omission: that pipeline is the origin of every external effect of an AGENT ASKING TO ACT, and here the artifact has already been emitted and is already in the event log. Passing the projection through the queue would fill approvals with routine decisions — one per artifact — and erode the ceiling that gives the click its meaning on the actions that are real external effects. Where: apps/api/src/domain/artifacts/artifact-projection-events.ts (the vocabulary and the naming rules, pure); apps/api/src/application/artifact-projection/artifact-projector.ts (the poller); apps/api/src/application/ports/artifact-file-store.port.ts and apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/fs-artifact-file-store.ts (the write, with the second barrier); apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts (pastaDeArtefatosDoProjeto, sibling of permissionsFilePath); apps/api/src/application/use-cases/sessions/append-session-event.use-case.ts (the third outbox row) Test: apps/api/test/domain/artifacts/artifact-projection-events.spec.ts (the naming rules, the traversal and the collision by seq) and apps/api/test/application/artifact-projection/artifact-projector.spec.ts (happy path, versioned overwriting, and the degradation: a failure leaves the row unprocessed, the next cycle retries, one failure does not block the batch, a vanished event is not retried forever, reprocessing is idempotent) ADR: 0148 Origin: request of the product owner — "criar apenas uma pasta por ora chamada docs, onde os artefatos estarão de cada um dos agentes"
documents.s: RN-523 — The docs/ folder is a PROJECTION of the event log: derived, per agent, and never a source of truth

documents.t: install.sh detected a previous installation since RN-530 and offered to migrate with a proven backup. What it did not know was which version was there: the marker ($XDG_STATE_HOME/brabo/install-state.json) recorded schemaVersion, instaladoEm, platform, source, digests and paths — and nothing that said 5.0.0. The question "migrate this installation?" was blind on both sides, and whoever answered had no way of knowing whether it went up, down or repeated. The information was always at hand and was ignored: the Release's images.json carries "versao" next to commit and publicadoEm, and resolver_imagens_do_ghcr read only repositorio and digest. From the other end, --source=local already requires a clean tree on a tag — so git describe is a reliable version there, through the two refusals that already happened before. The order is the decision. The images are now resolved before detection: knowing what comes in is a prerequisite for asking whether what exists goes out. The marker goes up to schemaVersion: 2 and records versao and commit — the two together, because a new marker without the field would pass for an old one. With both versions in hand, the offer stops being one question and becomes four, one per relation: relation offer default greater Atualizar 5.0.0 → 5.1.0? yes — it is what the person came to do, and the proven backup makes it reversible equal Já é a 5.0.0. Reinstalar do zero mesmo assim? no — there is no gain to offer lesser names a downgrade, warning that a database migration does not go backwards no — there may be no going back unknown a schema 1 marker has no version: says so, and does not guess no The maior branch is the only one with a default of yes, and it is the only one that can have it: the step is reversible through the backup that was just proven. The other three require a typed s. In any branch the installation is deleted and recreated from scratch, never brought up on top — a decision of the product owner, and the same reason as RN-530: an up over volumes of another version is damage that gives no warning, and half a migration is worse than none. The chain backup → PROVE → ask → delete → install → restore does not change in any of them. comparar_versoes is implemented by hand and not with sort -V: macOS's BSD sort gained -V late, and this script runs on other people's machines — the same discipline that already made sha_do_cosign refuse an associative array because of bash 3.2. It echoes the verdict instead of returning an exit code, because under set -e a legitimate return 1 would kill the script. In the pnpm bootstrap menu, Docker › Instalar (install.sh) reports the plan and does not install — mechanics, not preference: a menu item runs with stdin at /dev/null so the menu keeps reading keys from the same terminal, and this installer exists to ASK (that is the reason ADR 0150 refuses curl | sh). It is the same design as the Base de projetos item (RN-511), and the item's note carries the command that really installs. Code: install.sh (comparar_versoes, campo_do_marcador, resolver_imagens_do_ghcr, resolver_imagens_locais, main); scripts/dev/bootstrap.sh (item 1.7) Test: scripts/dev/install.spec.ts — "a comparação de versões" and "o marcador registra a versão"; the function is extracted from the script and run by bash, never reimplemented in TS (a copy keeps passing after the shell breaks) Found by running, not by reading: cut -d. on a string without a dot returns the whole line, not empty — so 5.0.0 vs 5 answered menor. Normalized with .0.0 at the end, with a regression test. ADR: 0150 Origin: request of the product owner — "o sh deve ser inteligente de entender que já há uma versão e verificar se será uma nova versão a ser executada ou não... caso seja uma nova ou escolhido isso pelo usuário deverá deletar a anterior e instalar do zero para evitar possíveis erros"
documents.s: RN-542 — The installer compares the installed version with the one it is going to install, and the offer is specific per relation

documents.t: The local agent's identity was per PROJECT. A machine with three projects in runner mode had three keys, three folders with brabo-runner-device-key.jwk.json and three service units — and the person went three times through the same browser flow (RN-464..466, RN-475) to describe one machine. It is item 4 of the five couplings ADR 0154 measured; items 1, 2 and 3 (topic, socket id, ticket) describe a connection and N connections satisfy them byte for byte, so nothing in the engine changes here. One table, two kinds. Filled project_id = the usual PROJECT key. NULL project_id = the MACHINE key. A sibling table was considered and refused in the ADR: PatAuthGuard finds the public key by kid and does not need to know the kind, and two tables would make two lookups — the second forgotten exactly once. NULL and not a sentinel: the FK is real, and project_id = '00000000-…' would require a fake row in projects. user_id stays NOT NULL — the ADR refuses a key that crosses users, because the credential describes who acts. The point that decides everything is a single one. PatAuthGuard.autorizarPapel refused when the credential's project differed from the route's project. That comparison was not deleted: it is what prevents project A's key from serving project B, and it disappears only for a null project_id, because then there is nothing to compare. The role is now resolved against the REQUESTED project, which is ADR 0154 point 2 to the letter — "authorization remains the usual one, resolved against the requested project". No new ceiling and none loosened: the machine key gives the runner nothing its OWNER did not already have, and an insufficient role in the requested project is still 403. The PAT branch does not change — personal_access_tokens.project_id stays NOT NULL. The agent ASKS which projects it serves. GET runner/projects returns the projects in execution_mode: 'runner' in which the credential's owner reaches at least developer — the SAME minimum as runner-ticket, because listing a project whose ticket would be refused is promising what the next route denies. It asks instead of sweeping the disk: the machine's base belongs to the user and may have a folder that is no project at all, and guessing by folder name is the class of error ADR 0141 refused. What travels is the SEGMENT (workspaceDirName, RN-109) and never an absolute path — the same invariant as the broker. It is the first @RequirePatAuth() route without :projectId in the path, and the two consequences are locked by tests: only a MACHINE credential gets in (a project one describes a single project and has nothing to discover — 403 with its OWN message, never the "wrong project" one, which would lie about the reason), and there is no @RequireRole, because there is no project to resolve it against. The minimum is applied per ROW, with the product's SINGLE rule (ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject, projectRole ?? workspaceRole — RN-471); the candidates query in SQL is alcança, never tem papel, and rewriting the ?? there would be a second rule. That is why route-surface.spec.ts classifies it as jwt — the classifier reads @RequireRole and does not see the mechanism — and docs/security-surface.md corrects the reading in prose, exactly as it already does for runner-ticket. The listing of RN-519 now states the KIND. A machine key serves every project of the owner, so it enters the listing of all of them — marked (especie: 'maquina', projectId: null). Both halves are mandatory: without entering the list it would be invisible and permanent on every screen, which is the defect RN-519 closed reborn in the new kind; without the mark, the same row would appear in N projects looking like N different keys. The kind is DERIVED from project_id in a single place — there is no column for it, and there must not be. And revocation now has a PLURAL target. RN-520 takes down the live connection of {projeto, usuário}, and a machine key names no project at all. Not taking it down would reopen exactly what RN-520 closed — the key dies for a NEW ticket and the live connections keep executing approved commands —, now in N connections instead of one. So revoking a machine key requests a disconnectRunnerOfUser per project in runner mode the owner reaches. It is the consequence the ADR declared in advance ("revoking will take down all of that machine's projects"), and it fits without touching the engine: the {projeto, usuário} signature stays byte for byte, it is just called N times. The list comes from the CANDIDATES, without a role filter, and that is deliberate — disconnecting is not an authorization decision, and missing a project would leave standing what the revocation exists to kill. Code: apps/api/src/db/schema/auth.ts (runnerDeviceKeys.projectId, without .notNull()); apps/api/src/db/migrations/0058_public_war_machine.sql; apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/pat-auth.guard.ts (autorizarPapel); apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/runner-projects.controller.ts; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/runner/list-runner-projects.use-case.ts; apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/project.repository.ts (listRunnerModeReachableBy); apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/runner-device-key.repository.ts; apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/revoke-runner-device-key.use-case.ts Test: apps/api/test/interfaces/pat-auth.guard.spec.ts — "chave de MÁQUINA", with BOTH directions locked (the machine one holds in any project; the PROJECT one stays refused in a different project) and the route without :projectId; apps/api/test/application/use-cases/runner/list-runner-projects.use-case.spec.ts (a role below developer is left out); apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/runner-device-key.repository.spec.ts and .../project-runner-mode.repository.spec.ts (against Postgres — what changed is a NOT NULL and a WHERE, and no fake proves either of the two); apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/revoke-runner-device-key.use-case.spec.ts ("o alvo da desconexão vira PLURAL"); apps/api/test/interfaces/http/runner/runner-projects.controller.spec.ts Gap DECLARED, and CLOSED by RN-552: when this RN closed, no api route created a machine key — the route would be born in the PR that had the first real caller, install.sh (ADR 0155 point 4), never before. That is what happened: POST /internal/machine-device-keys. The port's type is already the COLUMN's (projectId: string | null), so the future consumer has nothing to change there. And the web still has no screen on which to list or revoke a device key (the open half of RN-519): the new kind makes the gap bigger, and it stays declared, not closed here. CLOSED later by RN-561, which is the screen — and the kind mark created here is what it uses not to lie about the reach of revoking. ADR: 0154 Origin: PHASE 30, session 2 — the phase's scope
documents.s: RN-543 — A null runner_device_keys.project_id is the MACHINE key: it holds for the OWNER's projects, resolved against the requested project

documents.t: RN-543 opened GET runner/projects and was left without a caller. The brabo-runner still required --project: index.ts had if (!projectId) uso(), and there was no execution without a project. This RN is the consumer — and it is the half of ADR 0154 that proves its finding: "a single process that opens N connections — one per project it serves — satisfies items 1, 2 and 3 byte for byte". Nothing in the engine changes: the terminal:<projectId> topic, the socket id and the ticket describe a CONNECTION, and N connections remain N connections. The refusal of a second runner on the same project stays intact, and it is a real guarantee, not an accident. Two modes, and the old one stays byte for byte. --project/--dir with a project credential — including the browser flow (ADR 0118, RN-464) — is the usual path: ONE connection, and its outcome remains that of the process. The new mode requires BOTH things, and for different reasons: a MACHINE credential, because that is what the route accepts; and a consented base (RN-529), because without it there is nowhere to derive each project's folder from, and inventing one would be writing on the user's disk a path they did not consent to. Without a base, running without --project still falls into uso(), saying which of the two was missing. The runner does not know what kind its own key is, and that is a decision. On disk, machine key and project key are the SAME file: a private JWK with a kid (RN-475). What knows is the SERVER, which finds the public key by that kid. So the CLI asks, and the named 403 of PatAuthGuard becomes CredencialNaoEDeMaquinaError, with the api's words and the fix (--project) — never a generic "connection failure". A local guess would be a second source of truth about the same thing, and the local one would be the wrong one. The JWT of that call goes without the projectId claim, because the guard compares payload.projectId !== request.params.projectId and on a route without a project both need to be undefined. N connections require N states. Four fields of EstadoDoRunner are PER PROJECT — dir, canalAtual, containerAtivo, destinoDoEspelho — plus gerenciadorPty, which is born from dir. A shared state would make one project's docker exec run in ANOTHER's container, and one's PTY open in another's folder. docker and base belong to the MACHINE and go in as the SAME value in all of them, never copies that could diverge. The type did not change, and the handlers (tratarExec, tratarMirrorSync, tratarWorkspaceCreate…) did not change a line: the mirror (RN-516) and workspace_create (RN-532) were already per project and already traveled in the join grant of that connection, which is exactly what makes them correct with N. The ceiling and the refusal become the PROJECT's. They were the process's: a join refusal gave process.exit(1), and an exhausted TETO_DE_TENTATIVAS_SEGUIDAS too. With N connections, killing everything because of one would take down the agent for all the projects that are working. So each project has its own loop and counter; a project that refuses or exhausts ends on its own, NAMED, and the others continue — and only when NONE is left does the process exit with 1, with a summary stating the outcome of each one. Every loop log is prefixed by the project's name: with N interleaved loops, an ownerless "connection failure" is the form silence takes when there are N of something. In projeto mode the old disposition stays identical, and by the same reasoning inverted: with ONE connection, there is nothing left to serve. The list is queried ONCE, at start. Re-querying periodically was considered and refused: it costs a recurring call for a rare event, and the real price is not traffic — it is that a list that comes back SMALLER is ambiguous (project deleted, mode converted, role revoked, or a transient 500 disguising itself as the three), and taking down a LIVE connection because of that ambiguity would trade a right state for a guess. The process SAYS so when it starts, and the gesture to pick up a new project is reconnecting the agent — a single command, with the user service of RN-518. An EMPTY list is a NORMAL state, and the exit is 0. It is the state of every freshly installed machine: the installer brings up the agent before any project exists (ADR 0155). It is not an error, so it is not an error code — and Restart=on-abnormal (RN-518) does not bring it back up, which is right: there is nothing to bring back. Staying up with zero connections would be an "active" service that does nothing, and the unit's status would start to lie. Each project's folder is <base>/<workspaceDirName>, through the guards that already exist. resolverPastaDoProjetoNaBase (the SAME one workspace_create uses, and for the same reason: the name came over the network), plus validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux (RN-434) and garantirDiretorio (RN-435) — no fourth copy of the rule is born. Creating the folder is RN-435 applied to a DERIVED path instead of a typed one; what does NOT happen here is git init/clone, which remains workspace_create (RN-532). A project whose folder is refused leaves the plan named and does not take down the others. OpcoesDaBase.raizDoProjeto accepts null in machine mode: without --project there is no --dir, the loop refusal is left without a subject (every root is derived from the base, so "the base inside a project's root" has no way to be built), and passing the base itself there would be worse — dentroDoEscopo(base, base) is true and every base would be refused. Code: apps/runner/src/index.ts (the gate in lerArgumentos, lerArgumentosDeMaquina, manterConexaoDoProjeto, criarEstado, rodarComoAgenteDeMaquina); apps/runner/src/projetos.ts (listarProjetosDoRunner, planejarConexoes, CredencialNaoEDeMaquinaError); apps/runner/src/auth.ts (assinarDescobertaComChaveDeDispositivo — the JWT without the projectId claim); apps/runner/src/base-guard.ts (null OpcoesDaBase.raizDoProjeto) Test: apps/runner/src/projetos.spec.ts — happy path of the route and of the plan, the 403 becoming its OWN error, a response outside the contract, and the segment that escapes the base being refused WITHOUT taking down the neighbor (including by symlink, in the second pass); apps/runner/src/index.spec.ts — the GATE in the real process (without a base, uso() with the reason; with a base, the refusal comes from the credential); apps/runner/src/base-guard.spec.ts — a null raizDoProjeto does not loosen any other refusal Gap DECLARED, CLOSED later by RN-552: when this RN closed, nobody CREATED a machine key (it was install.sh, ADR 0155 point 4), so the new mode was only exercisable with a key registered by hand — the half RN-543 already declared. The apiUrl in machine mode comes from --api-url/BRABO_API_URL/default, and not from brabo-runner.config.json, which is per PROJECT: an installation on a different port or host needs the flag in ExecStart, and what writes it is the per-machine unit, which is session 4 of this phase. And the unit is still PER PROJECT — this PR changes the PROCESS, not the service ADR: 0154 Origin: PHASE 30, session 3 — the phase's scope
documents.s: RN-544 — The local agent opens N connections, one per project discovered by the route — and the retry ceiling and the join refusal stop belonging to the PROCESS

documents.t: About the number. The jump from RN-542 to 556 is deliberate: the range 543–555 is reserved for PHASE 30, which has already allocated it in branches in flight. Allocating here would produce the collision this repository has already observed three times at the same instant (ADR 0148 ×2, RN-522 ×2, RN-523 ×2), resolved afterwards by DATE. Nothing was skipped by mistake. ADR 0127 put the two ceilings of RN-472 only on the WRITE path and declared the third movement open, in writing and with the estimated cost: "RemoveProjectMemberUseCase did NOT gain a ceiling… The premise that 'removal is always benign' is false, and it stays written here so as not to be rediscovered". This RN closes that door — it is BRB-001, security P1. Removing does not erase a role, it SWAPS the effective role. ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject is projectRole ?? workspaceRole (RN-471), and the overlay holds in BOTH directions. Remove the project row, and the effective one starts resolving by the second term — which can be SMALLER. A maintainer whose authority came from the project row, viewer in the workspace, removed their own row and fell to viewer with no way back through the screen: restoring is POST :projectId/members, which requires the just-abandoned maintainer. Without any workspace role, the fall is to NO access. It is ceiling 2, not a new ceiling. ehAutoRebaixamento compares TODAY's effective role with the AFTER one, and never needed to know by which route the second arrived: in add the after-role comes from the body, in removal it comes from the workspace. remocaoEhAutoRebaixamento is that application, and it DELEGATES — it reimplements no comparison at all. It exists as its own function for ONE case the other's signature cannot state: an actor without a workspace role, where the after-role is "none", which is not a Role. That case is the maximum demotion and refuses. movement outcome removing one's own row, workspace with the SAME role passes — it is how someone leaves the list removing one's own row, workspace with a LOWER role 403 removing one's own row, WITHOUT a workspace role 403 — the fall is to no access removing ANOTHER person's row, even if they fall passes — the usual legitimate capability removing the row that restricted the WORKSPACE owner passes — it can only RAISE Ceiling 1 gains no counterpart, and the absence is a decision. owner is the top of ROLE_ORDER: removing the project row of someone who is owner in the workspace can only raise their effective role, or keep it. More than harmless, it is the ONLY way to undo a restriction ceiling 1 prevents from being created. A ceiling there would refuse only benign movements and make permanent the state ADR 0127 was born to eliminate. It is written next to the function and pinned in a test. Without a threshold, like ceiling 2 — and the price comes with it. The refusal is "oneself", not "below maintainer", for the same reason as RN-472: a threshold would copy a number from the controller's @RequireRole into the domain and would age silently if the route changed its minimum. The declared price is the self-removal of whoever has owner in the project and maintainer in the workspace: reversible, and refused too. It was the only benign movement that passed before and now refuses; it stays reachable by another maintainer. The message is its OWN. Whoever clicked "remove" did not ask to change any role, so MENSAGEM_TETO_AUTO_REBAIXAMENTO_POR_REMOCAO states the MECHANISM — without the project row the role falls to the workspace's, and coming back requires the abandoned role — instead of reusing the add sentence, which would talk about a movement the person did not make. The screen does not change, and the refusal shows up. MembersSection.handleRemove already shows mensagemDaApi(erro, …) in a toast (RN-471), so the api's sentence arrives without a line of web. Unlike ceiling 1, this gate IS computable on the client — but computing only it would produce the half-gate ADR 0127 refused. Code: apps/api/src/domain/iam/tetos-de-rebaixamento.ts (remocaoEhAutoRebaixamento and MENSAGEM_TETO_AUTO_REBAIXAMENTO_POR_REMOCAO, plus the comment saying why ceiling 1 has no counterpart), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/remove-project-member.use-case.ts (the signature with atorId and the two role reads), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/projects.controller.ts (@CurrentUser() on @Delete(':projectId/members/:userId'), the corrected description and the @ApiForbiddenResponse), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/resolve-effective-role.use-case.ts (UNTOUCHED — projectRole ?? workspaceRole stays as is) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/tetos-de-rebaixamento.use-case.spec.ts, block "Teto 2 pela outra porta — a remoção da própria linha" (the three refusals; the benign self-removal; removing another person; and the removal that returns the project to the workspace owner). The first of them is ADR 0127's gap test INVERTED, with the name keeping its origin ADR: 0156, which references 0127 and closes the gap it declared Origin: BRB-001, Security P1 of the maintainer's registry — the gap ADR 0127 wrote with the sentence "whoever closes it sees the test fail"
documents.s: RN-556 — Removing one's own project_members row is refused with 403 when the net effect is a demotion

documents.t: Extended by RN-615 (ADR 0173): the workspace member removal route said below not to exist came to exist, with the SAME ceiling (removing oneself is 403) — and it is that clause that holds the last owner, without counting. The reasoning below about ceiling 1 still holds. The third and last door of the line opened by RN-472 and continued by RN-556. ADR 0127 declared this one in writing — "POST workspaces/:workspaceId/members remains an upsert with no ceiling at all — same class of defect, scope above" — and ADR 0156 reaffirmed it as "different scope, separate decision". It is BRB-002, security P1. The defect, measured. AddWorkspaceMemberUseCase.execute received (workspaceId, userId, role) and called workspaces.addMember — it did not receive the actor —, and the controller (@Post(':workspaceId/members'), @RequireRole('owner')) called it with the bare body, without @CurrentUser(). There was nothing with which to apply any ceiling. Why it is more serious one scope above. Two things that exist in the project do not exist here: (a) there is no level above to catch the fall — in the project, demoting oneself drops the effective role to the workspace role, which often holds it; in the workspace the role is the role, and an owner who writes themselves viewer loses the entire workspace, with all the projects and the very capacity to invite whoever would restore them; (b) there is no member removal route — WorkspacesController has no member @Delete (measured, and ADR 0156 had already used that fact). Undoing is this same route, which requires the just abandoned owner. Self-PROMOTION was a loophole, and it closes. ADR 0127 recorded in the Consequences that it stayed: "A maintainer can write themselves as owner of the project (…) the ceilings are about going down". This RN revises that sentence. The two halves are the same movement — a person deciding alone what authority they have — and the upper one is the only one that escalates privilege: ADR 0127 could say its ceilings were not about escalation ("nobody gains a role they did not have"), and about promotion that is false. movement outcome changing one's own role in the PROJECT, downward 403 — RN-472, unchanged changing one's own role in the PROJECT, upward 403 — it was allowed, and this is what changes changing one's own role in the WORKSPACE, in any direction 403 — the new door rewriting one's own role with the SAME value passes — an idempotent upsert is not a movement an owner demoting ANOTHER owner in the workspace passes — it is the only way to revoke ownership associating/demoting ANOTHER person, in any scope passes — the usual legitimate capability self-promotion through REMOVAL of the project row passes — protected by ADR 0156, point 3 The ceiling does NOT count owners. Refusing only when the caller is the last owner was considered and refused by the literal criterion of ADR 0127: "it is stated in a clause, it has no number to age". A count adds a read that can get out of phase with the write, has to judge whether an inactive second owner counts, and makes the same call with the same body pass today and refuse tomorrow without anything the caller controls having changed. And the clause already produces the invariant the count would exist to guarantee: a workspace is never left without an owner, because removing the last one would require them to do it themselves. Ceiling 1 has no counterpart in this scope, and it was considered, not mirrored. Unlike removal (RN-556), here the movement EXISTS — an owner can demote another. The refusal comes from ceiling 1 being a rule about hierarchy inversion: in the project the row overlays the workspace one (RN-471) and a maintainer reaches whoever is ABOVE them; in the workspace @RequireRole('owner') already guarantees nobody reaches someone bigger than themselves — the precondition is absent. Putting the counterpart, added to the absence of a removal route, would make owner an absorbing state: nobody would leave it via HTTP, and offboarding, ownership rotation and correcting a wrong invite would come to require a direct write to the database — the class of state ADR 0127 was born to eliminate, with the sign flipped. The rule is not copied: the comparison becomes ONE classifier. autoMovimentoDoProprioPapel returns the DIRECTION ('rebaixamento' | 'promocao' | null) instead of a boolean, because whoever calls needs it to choose the message. ehAutoRebaixamento keeps existing as a READING of the classifier, and for a behavior reason and not a compatibility one: remocaoEhAutoRebaixamento delegates to it, and widening it would make REMOVAL also refuse self-promotion — removing one's own row that restricted someone is precisely how one undoes the restriction ceiling 1 prevents from creating, a movement ADR 0156 protected in writing. Four messages, one per DIRECTION and per SCOPE. Whoever tried to promote themselves does not receive the demotion sentence (it is not what they did), and whoever hits the workspace ceiling is not told to talk to a maintainer — there the role that undoes is owner. The same discipline as point 5 of RN-556 and of RN-470. The actor's role comes from the repository, not from ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase — the inverse of RN-556's choice, for the same reason it gave: in the project use cases the other one comes in so the actor's role does not become a second hand-written composition of projectRole ?? workspaceRole; in the workspace there is no composition to protect (forWorkspace IS workspaces.findMemberRole), and this use case already has the repository in hand. The PROMOTION half in the workspace is unreachable via HTTP, and is applied anyway. With @RequireRole('owner') the actor is already at the top and there is nowhere to go up. It goes in and is tested for the reason ceiling 2 always had for not having a threshold: the use case does not presume the guard, and it is what stays right on the day the route changes its minimum. The same design as the capability refusal of RN-514, implemented before it had any trigger. No web line changes, and it is not an omission: POST /workspaces/:workspaceId/members has no caller in apps/web — measured; the only occurrence is the generated type in api-types.generated.ts. There is no toast to adjust nor Select to close. Code: apps/api/src/domain/iam/tetos-de-rebaixamento.ts (autoMovimentoDoProprioPapel, the type SentidoDoAutoMovimento, the three new messages and the ehAutoRebaixamento that became a reading of the classifier), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/add-workspace-member.use-case.ts (the signature with atorId, the read of the actor's role and the two 403s), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/add-project-member.use-case.ts (the swap of ehAutoRebaixamento for the classifier, which is what closes the self-promotion there), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/workspaces.controller.ts (@CurrentUser(), the @ApiForbiddenResponse and the description), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/dto/add-member.dto.ts and apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/projects.controller.ts (the descriptions that promised "no ceiling at all" and "downgrading yourself"), apps/api/src/db/seed.ts (the owner.id as actor), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/resolve-effective-role.use-case.ts (UNTOUCHED, third ADR in a row) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/tetos-de-rebaixamento.use-case.spec.ts, block "Teto de auto-movimento no WORKSPACE — a quarta porta" (the refusal with another owner present, the refusal of the sole owner, the unreachable promotion, the message per scope, the idempotent upsert, the owner demoting another owner and the association of third parties), plus the three cases in the ceiling 2 block — the self-promotion test INVERTED, with the name keeping its origin, the assertion that each direction has its sentence, and the idempotent upsert in the project ADR: 0157, which references 0127 and 0156, and revises the first's sentence about self-promotion Origin: BRB-002, Security P1 of the maintainer's registry — the last movement the two previous ADRs left declared
