documents.t: A gap declared in writing when closing RN-507/RN-508 (ADR 0145) and measured again here, link by link, before any line was written. The chain, measured. Engine.Runners.RunnerReadiness.verificar/1 (runner_readiness.ex:52) requires a REGISTERED running container before ANY operation of Engine.Actions.Workspace.RunnerGit — including the initial authenticated git fetch, which comes out of fetch!/3 (runner_git.ex:226, via exec/4 at :288). The ONLY way for that record to exist in a runner project is the SAME runner having started its own container (ADR 0137), and it is that same success that marks estado.containerAtivo in it (apps/runner/src/index.ts:822, in tratarContainerStart). With containerAtivo set, tratarExec routes the command into the container (index.ts:728–730, and the new refusal at :693), and the exec operation of packages/docker-port has no env field — on purpose (ADR 0130: no free -e at all). The env field RN-507 added to the exec/exec_result pair (RunnerRouter.exec/5, runner_router.ex:50; ExecMessage.env, apps/runner/src/channel.ts:62) is only applied on the HOST path, where apps/runner/src/exec.ts:94 MERGES it over process.env. Result: the moment RN-507 lets the authenticated fetch run, the container is almost always already up on the SAME runner — and that is where the credential (ADR 0056, GitAuth.env_de_auth/1) was discarded, silently, with no error. git ran with the ephemeral helper installed by -c and the two variables EMPTY, and exited with an authentication failure — indistinguishable from an invalid token, wrong permission or network down. The person hunted the wrong thing, and the product said nothing. The fix is the NAMED outcome, not delivering the credential. The docker exec still has no env field — touching that is changing the containment door, and it is an ADR decision, not a cut (see the gap declared below). What changes is that the pair (env present, active container) stops being executed and starts being refused, with a mark, a message and an origin. What refuses is the RUNNER, and only it can. It is the only process that knows both halves at the same time: that the command carries a credential and that it goes inside the container. The engine does not know the second, and that was MEASURED: estado.containerAtivo is born null on each runner execution (index.ts:1449) and is only set by tratarContainerStart, so a running container REGISTERED in the database does not imply an active container in that process — a restarted runner with the container up routes to the HOST, and there the credential arrives normally. Moving the check up to RunnerReadiness or to RunnerGit would refuse a path that works. And RunnerReadiness stays BYTE FOR BYTE as it is: it gains no flag nor fourth precondition — it is the same rule RN-516 already stated about not hanging a "skip container" flag on it. The MARK is a PROTOCOL constant, not a message detail. MARCA_DE_CREDENCIAL_NAO_ENTREGUE (index.ts) and @marca (credencial_de_git.ex) carry the SAME token, and it is through it — not through the sentence — that the engine recognizes the refusal after it has crossed a rescue and become a loose string. Changing only one side breaks no compilation: the refusal keeps happening and only the CLASSIFICATION goes back to being wrong, which is the exact form of the defect this RN closes. Neither of the two suites reaches the other language (ExUnit does not read TypeScript, the runner's vitest does not read Elixir), so the guard lives in scripts/ci/, with the other tests that read the whole repository as text. The origin is politica, and the choice points to ACTION. The four of ADR 0020 do not assign blame, they say what to do. This is not a clause nobody wrote (codigo) nor a network that went down (infra): it is the containment of ADR 0130 working as designed, against a case it did not foresee. Whoever reads politica knows there is no bug to hunt — there is a pending product decision. Engine.Runners.CredencialDeGit.desfecho/1 adds ONE case and reclassifies no other: any other worktree failure keeps byte for byte {"falha ao preparar o worktree", "codigo"}, in BOTH dev agents (the real one and the Noop, which exists to exercise THIS path and not a copy of it). The CONTAINMENT refusal wins, and the order is a decision. It comes AFTER validarCwdDentroDaRaiz (guard.ts): a command pointed outside the root needs to hear that, because there a containment boundary is being refused, while here there is a missing capability. Collapsing the two would make an out-of-scope command look like a credential problem — the same diagnosis defect, with another sign. The env never appears in the refusal — only the COUNT. RN-507's invariant is that msg.env goes to no log at all, and this output goes to the product's event log: the refusal says "2 variável(is) de ambiente", never a name or a value. The number already says what needs to be known there. What is NOT affected, confirmed by reading: a local repository (provider without a token) — GitAuth.env_de_auth/1 returns [], fetch!/3 converts it to nil, the field does not even enter the payload, and the refusal does not fire; the container and mounted modes — they never go through RunnerGit (Workspace.ensure!/4 forks by execution_mode and only runner goes there), and their container comes up via the broker, on the other side of the network; and an ordinary terminal command, which never carried env. workspace_create also carries env, and is also not affected: it runs on the HOST (criarPastaDoProjeto), not in the container. Code: apps/runner/src/index.ts (MARCA_DE_CREDENCIAL_NAO_ENTREGUE and the refusal in tratarExec, after the cwd validation), apps/runner/src/channel.ts (the docblock of ExecMessage.env, which promised "runs only without the credential"), apps/engine/lib/engine/runners/credencial_de_git.ex (new — the mark, recusada?/1, mensagem/2 and desfecho/1), apps/engine/lib/engine/actions/workspace/runner_git.ex (the new clause in fetch!/3, before the generic one, and the moduledoc), apps/engine/lib/engine/dev/dev_agent_server.ex and apps/engine/lib/engine/dev/noop_dev_agent_server.ex (the outcome of {:error, reason} in the worktree creation) Test: apps/runner/src/index-handlers.spec.ts, block "a credencial não atravessa o docker exec (RN-558)" — the happy path (without a container, the env reaches the host and nothing is refused), the failure case (with a container, named refusal and docker.exec NOT called), the negative proof that the variables' name and value do not leak in the output, an empty env not becoming a refusal, and the containment refusal of guard.ts beating this one when the cwd is outside the root; apps/engine/test/engine/actions/workspace_runner_test.exs (the two RN-558 tests: the refusal that becomes a named message with origin politica, and the REAL fetch failure that keeps the usual message with origin codigo — the negative pair that proves the new clause did not hijack the old one); apps/engine/test/engine_web/channels/credencial_no_runner_test.exs (AT-111, the whole CHAIN through the real TerminalChannel: the env reaches the channel only on fetch, the runner's reply is the fixture apps/runner/fixtures/exec-result-recusa-de-credencial.json — which the runner's spec compares byte for byte with the real output of tratarExec —, RunnerGit returns the named message, and DevAgentServer records dev.blocked with origin politica; plus the branch without an active container, in which the fetch answers 0, and the real failure, which stays codigo. It does NOT prove the bridge between languages by execution: no node process starts in ExUnit, and the pair that closes it is the shared fixture. Verified by mutation: cutting the env in the channel, in RunnerGit, the recognition of the refusal, desfecho/1 or its use in the dev agent fails the test; turning off the refusal in tratarExec fails the runner's spec); scripts/ci/marca-de-credencial-do-runner.spec.ts (the identical mark on both sides). Verified by mutation: neutralizing the fetch!/3 clause fails the engine test with the old message in view Gap DECLARED, which is the HALF that remains open — CLOSED by RN-676 (ADR 0193, owner's decision of 10/01): the credentialed fetch goes MARKED by the engine and runs on the runner's HOST even with an active container; this refusal shrank to the env WITHOUT the mark (in practice, a runner older than ADR 0193). The text below is from when it closed the silence half: the credential still does not cross the docker exec. AUTHENTICATED clone/fetch of a remote repository in runner mode remains impossible with the container up — what changed is that now it fails SAYING so, instead of looking like a token error. Closing it requires deciding HOW a credentialed operation talks to a docker exec without an env field, and the known options all touch the containment door of ADR 0130 (giving the operation env; a credential file mounted and deleted; running the fetch on the host even with an active container, which would break the invariant that the work happens inside the container). It is an ADR, never a passing fix. The ADJACENCY this delivery also declared — the refusal happened AFTER init_from_bare!/5 had already done git init, and the git_dir?/2 of ensure!/5 marked the workspace ready on the next attempt because it found the .git, so the second attempt failed further on at worktree add instead of repeating the refusal — CLOSED in AT-112: the initialization that fails (any step, not only the credentialed fetch) UNDOES the .git it itself created (inicializar_ou_desfazer! in Engine.Actions.Workspace and in RunnerGit) and re-raises the original exception, so the next attempt repeats the SAME cause. The undo only runs on the branch where there was NO .git — that of the "workspace from before the mark" (which has a .git and is not re-initialized) stays intact, so it deletes nobody's work. On the runner side the rm -rf is best-effort (the runner may have dropped, one of the causes of the failure). Signals considered and refused: an "in progress" marker (a second file to maintain, and orphaned if the process dies between the two steps) and checking the expected ref (the empty repository, without origin/<branch>, is a LEGITIMATE state and would fall as a failure) ADR: none new — the delivery moves no boundary at all. It CONSUMES 0130 (the door without env), 0137 (the container on the user's machine), 0145 (the precondition and the env field) and 0020 (the four origins) Origin: AT-053 — the gap ADR 0145 left declared in writing

documents.t: Session 5 of PHASE 30, decided by ADR 0155. It is the api half of the step that closes the one-line installation; the install.sh that consumes this route is session 6, and it arrived in RN-547. The hole, measured. In a new installation nobody can get in. The .env the installer generates has no email variable at all, MAIL_TRANSPORT falls back to the default log (docker/docker-compose.install.yml), and normal registration requires verifying the email — which through a disabled channel does not close. The installation ends saying "Ready" and the only way out is fishing the link from docker compose logs api. The route. POST /internal/first-account, engine-service — authenticated by BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN, in the same header and with the same constant-time comparison as the other internal routes. Body { email, senha, nome? }, response { userId, email, workspaceId }, 201. Why internal, and never public. A public "create the first owner" route is a race between whoever installed and whoever scanned the port, and whoever loses the race loses the installation: owner of the first workspace is not a role one recovers via HTTP. The service token closes the race in the right place — it is generated by install.sh itself and written to .env with mode 600, so presenting it proves control of the machine, which is the credential this step really wants. The account is born VERIFIED, and that is the only thing this route loosens. What email verification proves is "this person controls this inbox"; whoever runs the installer has already proven something stronger — the machine, the .env with the five secrets and the Docker daemon. Demanding the weaker proof from them, through a channel the installation knows is off, is theater. Normal registration stays byte for byte: the ADR creates a path for a named case, it does not touch the other one. The refusal is about the INSTALLATION, not about the email. UserRepository.existeAlgumUsuario() (SELECT 1 … LIMIT 1, never count(*)), and 409 if there is any user. The question is about users and not about auth_credentials, because an account provisioned by social login (RN-278) is born without a credential and asking about the credential would say "there is nobody" in a populated installation. Inheriting the per-email idempotency of provisionarUsuario would turn the route into an account creator with a misleading name — it would be enough to vary the address. In a migration (RN-530) the users come in the restore and the step goes silent by the same criterion. Personal workspace in the SAME transaction (RN-410). This is the THIRD account creation point, and it gains no name/slug rule of its own: it calls the same nomeESlugDoWorkspacePessoal as the other two. Without it the installation would close with a login that goes through and a dashboard where "New project" has nowhere to create — the half of the hole this phase came to plug, not the other. The extraction, and why not BRABO_FORCE_SEED. provisionarUsuario refuses to run with NODE_ENV=production, and the installer runs exactly in production. What the refusal protects is written in its docblock: a known password created without human interaction. The route is another category — the password is chosen by a human in the TTY, read without echo and confirmed, behind the service token, and only when there is no user at all. So the core (the trio of writes that makes the account be born verified) became ProvisionarUsuarioUseCase, and the refusal stayed in the script, which is what it protects. Telling the installer to declare itself a "forced seed" would make it cross a rule that never spoke about it, and would loosen the refusal precisely where it holds. One password rule, not two. The domain's exigirSenhaValida, called by the SAME code registration calls — and that is why this route's DTO does not repeat a @MinLength: the call covers the policy's FIVE refusals, not only the length. The @MaxLength stays, because it is not policy: it is argon2id protection, which copies the input before deriving. PoliticaDeSenhaError is a domain Error and has no global filter, so the use case translates it to 400 — without that the installer would read "server error" where the right answer is "choose another password". Translating there does not touch normal registration. Its own kind in the auth trail. first_account_created, and not register_created: the account is born verified without any email having been sent, and whoever audits later needs to see that written, not deduce it from the absence of an email_verified alongside. A closed union in TypeScript, a text column in the database — a new kind costs no migration. No GET. "Is there any user?" is a question nobody needs to ask from outside: the POST answers 201 or 409, and the 409 is already the answer. A read route would publish the same fact with one more surface, and its answer would be exactly the signal a scanner wants. The new surface is declared, not hidden. A second user creation path that works in PRODUCTION comes to exist. It is narrow on three independent counts (first account, internal route, service token) and disappears as soon as the installation has people. It is in security-surface.md, in the ADR's Consequences and here. A declared window, not closed. The "is there any user" check runs INSIDE the transaction, but READ COMMITTED does not prevent two concurrent calls with different emails from passing together. Closing it would require an advisory lock on the absence of rows, and that is not where containment lives: whoever reaches the route already has the service token, that is, already controls the whole installation. What the condition prevents is the route BECOMING a permanent account creation surface, and that it prevents. What did NOT come in, by the ADR's decision: a public first-owner route; a password generated by the code or a default (the password is never written — neither in .env, nor in the marker, nor in a log); SMTP turned on by itself (MAIL_TRANSPORT=log stays the declared default); LLM credential (it belongs to whoever is going to spend, RN-058); and any change to normal registration. Code: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/criar-primeira-conta.use-case.ts (the refusal for a populated installation, the password rule, the personal workspace and the event), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/provisionar-usuario.use-case.ts (the extracted core, without the production refusal), apps/api/src/scripts/provisionar-usuario.ts (only the refusal, plus the delegation), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/internal-first-account.controller.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/dto/first-account-internal.dto.ts and …/first-account-internal.response.dto.ts, apps/api/src/application/ports/user-repository.port.ts and apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/user.repository.ts (existeAlgumUsuario), apps/api/src/domain/auth/auth-event.ts (first_account_created), apps/api/src/domain/auth/password-policy.ts (UNTOUCHED — it is the reused rule) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/criar-primeira-conta.use-case.spec.ts (happy path with a verified account and personal workspace, the own kind, the 409 with a populated installation, the 400 for length and the 400 for a reason that is NOT length, and the name fallback); apps/api/test/interfaces/http/internal/internal-first-account.controller.spec.ts (the pass-through to the use case, the absent nome becoming null, and the three guard refusals: absent header, wrong token, right token); apps/api/test/scripts/provisionar-usuario.spec.ts (the production refusal STAYED in the script, and the delegation); apps/api/test/interfaces/route-surface.spec.ts (the route classified) ADR: 0155, which depends on 0154
documents.s: RN-546 — An internal route creates the FIRST account, already verified, and refuses when any user exists

documents.t: Session 7 of PHASE 30, closing point 4 of ADR 0155 on the kind of key ADR 0154 created. It is the gap RN-543 declared in writing and left open on purpose, by the DEPLOY_ENABLED rule: "no api route creates a machine key yet; that is install.sh, and it is born with the first caller". The caller arrived — it is session 6's installer —, so the route is born. The route. POST /internal/machine-device-keys, engine-service. Body { name, publicKeyJwk }, response 201 with { id, userId, name, createdAt, replacedKeyIds }. No GET and no DELETE. The credential is the SERVICE TOKEN, and the alternative was refused for a written reason. It is the same installer, in the same minute, in the step following that of RN-546: the BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN was generated by install.sh itself and written to .env with mode 600, so presenting it proves control of the machine — which is exactly what this step wants to prove. The real candidate on the other side was the freshly created user's credential, and it contradicts ADR 0155 itself: the password is read in the TTY, "used and discarded", and point 5 declares that "the installer does not log in for anyone", which is why the first account's response does not return a session token. Requiring it here would force the installer to create, on the machine, the live session that ADR refused to create. What that choice costs, declared and not hidden. A leaked BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN can now manufacture a durable access credential for a user — not only talk to the internal routes. It is stated here, in security-surface.md and in the controller's docblock, next to the sibling declaration of the first account. What the key grants did not increase: it gives the local agent exactly the projects its owner already reaches at developer, resolved against the requested project (RN-543). The route does not know how to choose whose key it is. There is no userId in the body. The owner is the installation's SOLE user, resolved by UserRepository.usuarioUnicoDaInstalacao() (LIMIT 2, never LIMIT 1: with one row it would be impossible to distinguish "there is exactly one" from "there are many"); with zero or more than one, 409 and nothing is written. It is the exact analogue of the condition of RN-546 — about the INSTALLATION, never about the requested argument —, and it is what prevents whoever has the token from choosing the victim. Declared consequence: in an installation with two people the route no longer works, for anyone. It goes silent as the first account one goes silent, and for the same reason — it belongs to the MOMENT of installation, not to the product's life. Registering REPLACES, never accumulates. Every active MACHINE key of the owner is revoked in the SAME transaction, and the ids come back in replacedKeyIds. A reinstalled machine is a legitimate case and keeps passing; a thousand machine keys become impossible — and not by a number that ages, but because the set of live machine keys of a user never exceeds one. The revocation comes BEFORE the registration: revoking afterwards would leave a window with both alive, and failing in the middle would leave the installation with two machine credentials and no way of knowing which is the new one. Only the MACHINE ones fall (project_id IS NULL): the PROJECT ones came from the browser (ADR 0118), in a flow this route does not know, and taking them down would erase the pairing of whoever already uses the product — the error RN-545 named when refusing to convert someone else's installation silently. The response returns the id because it becomes the kid. It is the lesson of RN-475, the most expensive in this area: the record's id is written INSIDE the private JWK, in the kid, and the whole chain only PASSES IT ON — the local agent reads jwk.kid, the ticket JWT carries it in the header, PatAuthGuard finds the public key by it. Nobody derives that id from anything else, and it was for lacking it that the browser's automatic mode never authenticated. The userId also comes back, RESOLVED by the api: the caller does not send it, and returning it lets the installer check against the account it just created instead of assuming. The private key never travels, and one that arrives is REFUSED. The pair is generated on the machine and only the public half goes up — the same design as the browser, for the same reason, keeping true the sentence RN-519 uses. The shape validation became a SINGLE rule in the domain (exigirJwkPublicaEd25519), called by the TWO registrars: two copies would diverge on the first day one of them changed, as the password policy of RN-546 already resolves. And it gained a case neither of the two had: a JWK with d answers 400 saying what arrived. d is the private half of an OKP JWK (RFC 8037 §2) and only arrives by the mistake of whoever serialized the whole pair — before, it passed the check (it has kty, crv and x like any public one) and was written. Refusing is the answer; the message names what came, because a generic "invalid JWK" would make the person try again with the same file. Its own kind in the auth trail. machine_device_key_registered: this is the only durable credential of a user that is born without that user authenticating anything — what proves is control of the machine. Under suspicion of a service token leak, it is that row that says when and for whom it was created, and the metadata carries the ids it replaced, never the JWK nor the name. No GET and no DELETE, and what that costs. Listing through here would publish, to whoever only has the machine's token, the credentials inventory of a person; revoking already exists where there is a human owner (DELETE /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys/:deviceKeyId, which matches by {id, usuário} and never by project). The asymmetry has a price, and it is declared: in an installation that has no project yet, no screen reaches a machine key — and that is precisely why registering REPLACES instead of leaving orphans behind, which would be alive and unreachable. What did NOT come in: a public route (same race as RN-546); userId in the body; a machine key for an installation with a team (declared above as a gap, not as an accident); a new table (a machine key is still a row of runner_device_keys with project_id NULL, ADR 0154 point 1) — and no migration, because the column is already nullable since RN-543. Code: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/internal-machine-device-keys.controller.ts:87 (the route's @Post(), and the docblock with the credential choice), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/registrar-chave-de-maquina.use-case.ts:122 (the resolved owner), :124 (the 409), :136 (the replacement before the registration) and :146 (projectId: null, what makes it a machine key), apps/api/src/domain/auth/jwk-de-dispositivo.ts:33 (the single rule) and :59 (the refusal of the private key), apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/user.repository.ts:31 (usuarioUnicoDaInstalacao, LIMIT 2), apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/runner-device-key.repository.ts:148 (revogarChavesDeMaquina, the two IS NULL), apps/api/src/domain/auth/auth-event.ts (machine_device_key_registered), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/dto/machine-device-key-internal.dto.ts and …/machine-device-key-internal.response.dto.ts Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/auth/registrar-chave-de-maquina.use-case.spec.ts (happy path with a null projectId and resolved owner; the 409 without a sole user, without writing anything; the replacement BEFORE the registration; the private key refused before opening a transaction; the trail without the JWK); apps/api/test/domain/auth/jwk-de-dispositivo.spec.ts (the single rule, with the d and the curve's precedence); apps/api/test/interfaces/http/internal/internal-machine-device-keys.controller.spec.ts (the response contract, the body WITHOUT an owner, and the guard's three); apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/user.repository.spec.ts (one user returns; two return null, never "the first"); apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/runner-device-key.repository.spec.ts (the replacement against the real Postgres, and what it does NOT take down); apps/api/test/interfaces/route-surface.spec.ts (the route classified) ADR: 0155 point 4, on the kind created by 0154
documents.s: RN-552 — An internal route registers the MACHINE device key, for the installation's SOLE user, and registering REPLACES

documents.t: RN-544 made the machine agent exist as a PROCESS — N connections, one per project discovered by the route — and declared in writing what was missing: "the unit is still PER PROJECT; this PR changes the PROCESS, not the service". This RN is the other half, and it is the fifth and last of the five couplings ADR 0154 measured (apps/runner/src/servico.ts:264,391). The other four are already closed or declared untouchable: items 1, 2 and 3 describe a CONNECTION and N connections satisfy them byte for byte, and item 4 closed in RN-543. The machine unit's name cannot collide with any projectId, and it does not collide by construction. brabo-runner.service / dev.brabo.runner, without a suffix, against brabo-runner-<projectId>.service / dev.brabo.runner.<projectId>. PROJECT_ID_VALIDO requires at least one character, so the project name always has a - (or a separating ., in launchd) where the machine one ends — the two never produce the same string. It is locked by a test, and not by reading the regex. The platform layer is now keyed by KIND, not by projectId. Six of the eight members of PlataformaDeServico received projectId: string; they now receive AlvoDaUnidade, a discriminated type ({especie:'projeto', projectId} | {especie:'maquina'}) — and never projectId: string | null, because with the null each member would decide on its own what to do with it and the compiler would demand nothing. PlanoDeInstalacao becomes a union for the same reason: the three fields of the project plan lose meaning on the machine, where there is no project, there is no --dir (each root comes from the base) and the api cannot come from a file that is per project. caminhoDaUnidade went DOWN from a member to a function, because the two platforms answered the same thing — folder plus name — and keeping two identical implementations was the chance for them to diverge when the second kind arrived. The discriminator is the --machine flag, and NEVER the absence of --project. The ADR 0154 point 5 wrote "service install without --project installs the machine unit", and that was measured in this session and could not be implemented to the letter: resolverProjeto has TWO sources, and today's normal path is running install without any flag from inside the folder the browser configured — it is brabo-runner.config.json that answers. Treating "without --project" as "machine" would silently convert the installation of whoever already uses the product, which is exactly what point 5 of the same ADR promises not to do. So the new kind is explicit opt-in, the two project sources stay byte for byte, and --machine together with --project is a named refusal instead of an invented precedence. install --machine refuses more than the project half, and the two refusals of its own are measured. The first: the folder cannot have brabo-runner.config.json. lerArgumentos resolves the projectId from that file when --project is missing, and machine mode is precisely "without projectId" — a machine unit whose WorkingDirectory has that file would bring up the process in PROJECT mode, silently, serving ONE project and calling itself the machine's agent. The second: without a consented base (RN-529) the machine agent exits in uso() on the first boot (RN-544), and writing a service that never starts is the "wrong installation left up" this module refuses everywhere — the base comes in INJECTED (DependenciasDeInstalacao.resolverBase), like the other four dependencies, so that servico.ts keeps reading neither disk nor environment on its own. The unit freezes XDG_CONFIG_HOME, and never the base's VALUE. It is the same decision as the PATH of RN-518, with a bigger consequence: it is that variable that decides WHERE the base file lives (base.ts), and systemd --user does not pass on the environment of the installer's shell — without it, a user with the variable pointed outside ~/.config would have the service reading the wrong base, or none. The base's value is left out on purpose: changing it remains editing the file and restarting, never reinstalling, which is what the docblock of base.ts already defended when rejecting "only the --base flag". The machine unit's apiUrl reads BRABO_API_URL, and the project one does not. The precedence of the PROJECT plan stays byte for byte (--api-url › that folder's config › default), because there a file answers. In the machine one that file is per project and does not serve, so without the variable the only alternative to --api-url would be the localhost default — installing from a shell with BRABO_API_URL set would silently generate a unit pointing to the wrong place. It goes into ContextoDoServico (apiUrlDoAmbiente), never read directly from process.env. install REFUSES when the other kind is already installed, and nothing is removed. The machine agent serves EVERY project in runner mode of the key's owner; adding a per-project unit to it (or the opposite) puts two processes competing for the same terminal:<projectId>, and the server denies one of the two — probably the one the person just installed, which is the worst possible order to discover the problem. It is a refusal by the SAME criterion as the root refusal that already lives in that file: "installing and warning would leave the wrong installation up, and the message would be read only once". The unit that already exists stays intact, the message names the uninstall of each one, and there is no --force — a flag that knocks down a guard whose symptom is silent brings back the silent symptom. This does NOT contradict point 5 of the ADR: what it guarantees is that an already installed per-project unit keeps working, and it does, byte for byte; what is refused is creating the overlap NOW. status answers about the asked kind, and the four states do not become eight. The exit code is still that of the ASKED unit (RN-088) — summing the two would erase which one is asking for attention, in the same way summing the five decision queues would erase which queue is which. The coexistence shows up in TEXT, and it is an answer from the DISK: the units of the other kind are listed by name, without asking the manager the state of each one, and the output SAYS it did not ask. It is point 5 of ADR 0154 fulfilled — "letting six processes compete for three projects silently" is the defect that block exists to prevent. Without --machine and without a resolvable project, the main one is the machine unit (the only one whose name needs no argument) and the output names --project for whoever wanted the other; before this RN the same input answered "needs to know WHICH project", which is a question and not an answer for whoever has exactly the installation the installer produces. uninstall does NOT inherit that default, and the asymmetry is deliberate. Reading the wrong kind costs a wrong line; removing the wrong kind costs a service and a device key. Without --machine and without a resolvable project it REFUSES, listing what exists on disk with the exact command for each one — and never removes both, which would be removing more than was asked. Restart=on-abnormal stays byte for byte, in both kinds. Exit 1 is a fatal join refusal or an exhausted retry ceiling, and restarting would be the loop the CLI refuses to do on its own (RN-514). Moreover: RN-544 made an empty list exit with 0 precisely so that on-abnormal does not bring the service back up on a new installation, where there is nothing to serve — swapping for on-failure would undo both decisions at once. A folder with a PROJECT key installs the unit without error, and the refusal only shows up on the first boot, as CredencialNaoEDeMaquinaError. Verifying at install would require a network call in a subcommand that today makes none, and inventing a local guess would produce the second source of truth RN-544 refused. And, at the time of this RN, nobody CREATED a machine key: what registers it is install.sh (ADR 0155 point 4), in session 6 — this session delivers the subcommand it will call, and the route it calls arrived in RN-552 ADR: 0154 Origin: PHASE 30, session 4 —
documents.s: RN-545 — service install --machine installs ONE unit for the machine, and the two kinds do not overlap

documents.t: Session 7 of PHASE 30, decided by ADR 0154. It is the WEB half of the machine identity: RN-543 made the key listing mark the KIND (projeto | maquina) "so that a machine key would not stay invisible on every screen", and it was left without a consumer. This RN is the consumer. The defect, measured. RunnerOnboardingPanel is the panel the THREE onboarding points mount (TerminalPanel, FolderBrowserModal and the workspace step of NewProjectWizard), and it had a single question: "configure the folder". With ADR 0154's machine key, that question becomes wrong in the most common case — the machine has already been paired, what is missing is the agent running. Telling the person to repeat the pairing the machine already has is the panel answering the wrong question, with a flow that ends in their terminal. Seven states, and none becomes the other (RN-088/RN-470). semPapel (we did not ask), verificando (we asked and it did not come back), naoSei (the question failed), semChaveDeMaquina (it came back and there is none), revogada (there was and it was revoked), pareadaNuncaUsada (there is an active key that no agent used — the ORPHAN of RN-519 reborn in the new kind) and pareada. "I don't know" never becomes "it doesn't have", and the two empties have different texts because the gesture is different: one asks to pair, the other explains why the agent stopped connecting. The failure is derived from isError and not from there being a status — a network error has no status, and deriving it from the status would leave a refused fetch spinning in "verifying…" forever, which is a lie by omission after ten seconds. semChaveDeMaquina is the only one that renders NOTHING, and on purpose: the whole panel already IS the answer to "no machine paired". Recognizing is NOT saying the agent is up, and the rule is the usual one. workspaceVerifiedAt is the record of a confirmation and not a heartbeat (RN-468); a registered key is the same thing one step earlier — it proves the machine was paired one day, never that there is a live process now. A screen that confused the two would be WORSE than today's, because today's at least does not lie. That is why the alert's tone is accent and never success (green would read as "it's up" — the same arithmetic AmbienteDoProjeto does on the runner row), the caveat is stated in text alongside, and what answers for the NOW remains EsperaDoRunner (RN-474), REUSED and not rewritten: once the machine is recognized, what is missing is the agent CONNECTING, which is exactly its question. And there is a second limit, which the data imposes and no wording erases: the list belongs to the ACCOUNT, not to this browser. runner_device_keys does not know which machine the browser is talking about, so the strongest the screen can assert is "your account has a paired machine" — never "this machine is paired". That is why the browser flow (ADR 0118) is not removed: it changes PLACE, into a <details> whose label names the only case in which it is still the answer ("I am on another machine"). Retiring it is BRB-031, the maintainer's decision, and not a consequence of this delivery. The KIND shows up, and what shows up is its COST. The panel does not list keys nor offer revocation — that is the screen the web never got, the open half of RN-519, and it is its own front. What it says is what the kind means to whoever reads: a machine key serves ALL the owner's projects in runner mode, and revoking it takes down the local agent in all of them (RN-520, whose {projeto, usuário} reach does not change here). Without that sentence, RN-543's mark would be decoration. The role is the ENDPOINT's, and the api is the authority. The minimum comes from roleAtLeast (RN-102) against developer, which RunnerDeviceKeysController requires on the three routes — the screen stops asking what the api would deny, and says why ONCE in TEXT (title on a disabled element does not open in Chromium). This is not a security boundary: what refuses is the RolesGuard. The real 403 falls into the SAME state, and it is not redundancy — the role read is the WORKSPACE one and what authorizes is the project's EFFECTIVE one (RN-471), an OVERLAY in both directions: the proxy avoids the obviously lost question, the api corrects the proxy. Where it shows up, and why it is not the same in the three mounters. Recognition is per PROJECT, because the route is GET /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys — it exists in TerminalPanel and FolderBrowserModal, which always have a project, and in NewProjectWizard only AFTER the early creation (RN-437). Without a projectId there is no one to ask and the panel stays byte for byte as it was. The difference is not a design choice: it is the shape of the endpoint. The command the panel offers is brabo-runner service status --project <id>, the form that exists TODAY; the per-machine form arrives with session 4's unit — CLOSED later (AT-106): once the MACHINE key is recognized, the panel offers brabo-runner service status --machine (the machine unit of RN-545), and the PROJECT key block keeps offering --project <id>; both active kinds each show their own. The command is still for the person to ASK — the screen does not assert the answer (keys agenteDeMaquina.comandoDeServico and chaveDeProjeto.comandoDeServico, tests in RunnerOnboardingPanel.test.tsx in both branches and in the pair). An active PROJECT key does NOT change the panel: it is the sibling defect, one scope below, and closing it is a separate decision — CLOSED later (AT-107): the panel recognizes an active PROJECT key of THIS project (reconhecerChaveDeProjeto, lib/agente-de-maquina.ts, same listing and same queryKey, no new route), with the same vocabulary — accent tone, a registered key is not an agent up, the trigger is checking the service — and the cost of the KIND stated: revoking takes down the agent IN THIS project, not in all of them. Another project's key and a revoked one do not count, and the ADR 0118 <details> stays reachable. And the web still has no SCREEN on which to list or revoke a device key (the open half of RN-519) — this delivery consumes the listing and does not build it. CLOSED later by RN-561, which builds it: the Settings section reuses podeLerChavesDeDispositivo from here and the SAME queryKey, and that is why revoking from there invalidates the recognition of this panel ADR: 0154 Origin: PHASE 30, session 7 — the phase's scope
documents.s: RN-548 — With an active MACHINE key, the runner panel stops telling to pair and starts saying what is missing — without ever asserting that the agent is up

documents.t: Session 8 of PHASE 30. RN-544 made an empty list a NORMAL state and the process exit with 0, saying "create a project in Runner mode and bring the agent up again — the list is queried only at start". That contradicted, in writing, ADR 0155 point 5 — "it waits… when the person creates the first project on the web, the agent is already there" — and broke exactly the case the phase pursues: the new installation, which is the installation with ZERO projects. The installer brought up the agent, the agent found there was nothing and went away, and the person who created the first project minutes later would go back to the terminal without ever having been told about it. The rule is ASYMMETRIC, and the asymmetry is the design: conexões > 0 → a lista é consultada SÓ no start (a RN-544 fica byte a byte) conexões = 0 → reconsulta, com cadência declarada And it does NOT undo RN-544's decision. That session's argument remains whole: a list that comes back SMALLER is ambiguous — project deleted, converted mode, role revoked, or a transient 500 disguising itself as the three —, and taking down a LIVE connection because of that ambiguity would trade a right state for a guess. With zero connections there is nothing to take down and no ambiguity at all: any project that shows up is pure gain, and no decision is made about what disappeared. The re-query STOPS the moment the first non-empty list arrives, and from then on the behavior is byte for byte today's — the waiting module is not called again while the process lives. The exit 0 argument fell because its premise fell. RN-544 wrote that "staying up with zero connections would be an 'active' service that does nothing, and the unit's status would start to lie" — and that depended on the process doing nothing. It is that premise this RN removes: it re-queries, with a declared cadence, and SAYS it is doing so. active (running) becomes true, and what lied was the exit with 0, which left the new installation without an agent precisely in the minute the person was going to create the first project. The cadence escalates and STABILIZES: 15s, 30s, 60s, and the last one repeats forever. The two short steps exist because the case to serve is that of someone creating the first project NOW; a ceiling of minutes would make the agent show up after the person gave up looking. The 60s plateau is the steady-state price — ONE request per minute, from one installation, against a route that returns the list of the credential's own owner. Growing beyond that would save traffic nobody is paying for and worsen the only thing the wait delivers. There is a ceiling, and it is on FAILURES, never on waiting. Waiting has no limit — waiting is the normal state of a new installation, and can last days. What has a ceiling are CONSECUTIVE query failures: ten, and then the process exits with 1 NAMING the number, as the connection loop already does with TETO_DE_TENTATIVAS_SEGUIDAS and for the same reason (not hammering the api forever when the problem is not transient). A query that ANSWERS resets the counter — including when it answers EMPTY, which is success, because the empty list is the right answer. The constant is SEPARATE on purpose, with the same value: one counts failures to CONNECT and the other, failures to LIST, and tying them would make a change in connection cadence touch, without anyone asking, the time a new installation waits before giving up. CredencialNaoEDeMaquinaError (the 403 by key kind, RN-544) does not count toward the ceiling: it is fatal on the spot, because a project key does not become a machine key by waiting one more minute. Staying up silently would be worse than exiting. "Waiting" and "stuck" are the same picture to whoever reads journalctl, so the process states the cadence when entering the wait, says when the first project shows up, and beats a HEARTBEAT every 30 queries (half an hour, on the plateau) reporting how many queries there have been. Not every query becomes a line, also on purpose: one log per minute, forever, is the noise that buries the lines that matter. Restart=on-abnormal stays byte for byte, in BOTH unit kinds (RN-545), and nothing in them changes. Measured: on-abnormal restarts on SIGNAL, watchdog or timeout — never on exit code, neither 0 nor 1. The exit with 0 was never what prevented the service from being restarted; what prevented it is that on-abnormal looks at no code at all. The real effect of the change is the opposite of what was feared: the MACHINE unit, which is the one running this mode, now stays active (running) for real instead of ending in inactive (dead) seconds after starting — and service status --machine now answers rodando (0) where before it answered parado (3) on a new installation. The PROJECT unit is not affected in any line: it runs the projeto mode, which never gets here. One exception, declared: a NON-empty list whose projects are all refused still exits with 1. That is also zero connections, and even so it does not wait — because there each refusal names a concrete local defect (a segment escaping the base, a folder that is a file) with its own fix, and re-querying would repeat the same refusals indefinitely, burying in the log the line that says what to fix. The wait is for "no project exists yet", never for "it exists and I cannot serve it". documents.t: Session 8 of PHASE 30, the other half. Until now, only the browser generated a device key pair (apps/web/src/lib/runner-bootstrap.ts, ADR 0118, RN-464); the CLI only knew how to read what someone had put in the folder (device-key.ts). ADR 0155 point 4 asks for the other side: "the pair is generated on the machine; the private key never travels… keeps true the sentence RN-519 uses to refuse the maintainer view: 'the private key of a device key never leaves the browser' — becomes 'never leaves the machine'". Without it, RN-543, RN-544 and RN-545 all kept the same declared gap: nobody creates a machine key. There are TWO steps, and the reason is the kid. The kid written inside the private JWK IS the record's id on the server (RN-475) — the whole chain only PASSES IT ON (the runner reads jwk.kid, the JWT carries it in the header, PatAuthGuard finds the public key by it), and nobody derives it from anything else. It only exists after the public key is registered, and a private key written before that is born useless, which is literally the defect RN-475 cost a hunt to find. The browser solves it by keeping the pair in MEMORY between registration and writing; the CLI solves it with a PARTIAL file: PUB=$(brabo-runner device-key create) # gera aqui, imprime a PÚBLICA ID=$(… registra PUB na api … | jq -r .id) # quem registra é o instalador brabo-runner device-key finish --id "$ID" # carimba o kid e grava At no instant does a brabo-runner-device-key.jwk.json exist without kid. The create writes to …jwk.json.parcial, a name lerChaveDeDispositivo does not look for; the finish stamps and writes the real name. The file the runner READS is either complete or does not exist, and an interruption between the two steps leaves a .parcial the runner IGNORES and the next create NAMES — saying that the record of that attempt may have been ORPHANED, which is inert and shows up in the listing of RN-519. The CLI does NOT talk to the api, and the reason is a SECRET one, not a technical one. What registers the machine key is the installer, authenticated by the BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN it just generated (ADR 0155 point 1). Making brabo-runner call the route would require putting that token in its hands — an INSTALLATION secret, which opens internal routes, handed to a process that today only sees a device credential and that stays up forever on the user's machine. The cut is the opposite: each side keeps exactly one secret, and neither sees the other's. What crosses the boundary between them is the PUBLIC JWK and the id — nothing that needs protecting. The default destination is the machine's configuration folder, and the precedence is REUSED. $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/brabo/ (otherwise ~/.config/brabo/), next to the runner.json of RN-529 and for the same reason — it is MACHINE configuration, and a machine key has no project folder in which to live. pastaDeConfiguracaoDoBrabo was EXTRACTED from caminhoDoArquivoDeBase when it gained the second consumer, never copied. This does not reopen the door Wave 2 of ADR 0104 closed (a credential in a global and IMPLICIT path): device-key.ts still reads only from the cwd the caller passes, and what points to this folder is the --dir of the machine unit (RN-545), explicitly, written in the service. --dir exists and also serves a project folder — on disk the two kinds are the same file, and what knows the difference is the SERVER (RN-544): this command asserts no kind at all. The private key is written with mode 600, explicit, and never left to umask. The folder is born 700 when it is THIS command that creates it; a folder that already existed belongs to the user (it may be the one the browser configured) and is not re-tightened. The --dir goes through the SAME validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux of RN-434, reused whole: what is written is a user secret, and a folder outside their $HOME is not where their systemd --user will look. The stdout carries ONE value, on one line, and everything else is stderr. That is the contract install.sh depends on (PUB=$(…)): mixing the two would force the script to filter human output, which is how a contract breaks without anyone noticing. In create the stdout is the public JWK; in finish, the file's PATH — the value the next step (service install --machine --dir <pasta>) needs. Overwriting a complete key is REFUSED, and there is no --force. Swapping the key of an already paired machine would swap the identity of an agent that may be up NOW, silently: the public key would remain registered and the process would start signing with a key nobody knows. The refusal names the gesture (revoke, delete, recreate), and a flag that knocks down a guard whose symptom is silent would bring back the silent symptom. Code: apps/runner/src/criar-chave-de-dispositivo.ts:202 (criarChaveDeDispositivo), :275 (finalizarChaveDeDispositivo), :82 (SUFIXO_PARCIAL), :177 (resolverDestino); apps/runner/src/base.ts:85 (pastaDeConfiguracaoDoBrabo, extracted); apps/runner/src/index.ts:1280 (the dispatch before lerArgumentos, and the stdout/stderr separation) Test: apps/runner/src/criar-chave-de-dispositivo.spec.ts — the end-to-end happy path (the public key on stdout, the partial at 600, the finish stamping, and the resulting key read by lerChaveDeDispositivo and SIGNING a real ticket JWT), the --dir, and the refusals: finish without create, without --id, with --id pasted from the whole JSON, a complete key already in place (in both commands), a partial that is not the JWK, an unknown subcommand and the orphan warning; apps/runner/src/index.spec.ts — the JUNCTION in the real process: device-key create runs in a folder WITHOUT any credential, and the stdout contains only the public JWK Gap DECLARED, and CLOSED in both halves: what REGISTERS the public key did not exist in this repository when this RN closed — the route arrived in RN-552 and the install.sh that chains the two commands, in RN-547. The contract this command assumes is the one the PROJECT key route already has ({ name, publicKeyJwk }, with publicKeyJwk being the JSON of the Ed25519 public JWK — kty "OKP", crv "Ed25519", x — and a response with id), and that is what create's stdout produces: one line in that format. The command also does not choose the device's name, on purpose — it is a field of the record, and whoever names is whoever registers ADR: 0155 point 4 Origin: PHASE 30, session 8 — the phase's scope
documents.s: RN-551 — brabo-runner device-key create/finish: the Ed25519 pair is born ON THE MACHINE, the private key never travels, and the file the runner reads never exists without kid

documents.t: Session 6 of PHASE 30, decided by ADR 0155. The session would touch three workspaces at once and was split into three: the two pieces of the agent and of the api have already closed (RN-546, RN-551, RN-552, over the unit of RN-545), and what remained here is install.sh as an orchestrator and nothing more — no line of apps/ was touched, and no route was born. The hole it closes. A new installation ended saying "Ready" with a login that NOBODY got through: the generated .env has no email variable at all, MAIL_TRANSPORT falls back to the default log, and normal registration requires verifying the email. The only way out was fishing the link from docker compose logs api. And the local agent stayed installed without a credential, waiting for someone to go back to the browser to pair a folder. The chain, and every link already existed. POST /internal/first-account (RN-546) → brabo-runner device-key create (RN-551) → POST /internal/machine-device-keys (RN-552) → device-key finish --id <id> → brabo-runner service install --machine (RN-545). The id the api returns on registration is what becomes the private key's kid, and the whole chain only PASSES IT ON — nobody derives it from anything else (RN-475). The service's --dir comes from the PATH the finish printed, not from a second calculation by the script about where the configuration folder is. What happens when a middle link fails: nothing is undone, everything is REPORTED, and the script always exits 0. It is this delivery's decision, and the argument is that the links already fulfilled are useful on their own — with the account created the person gets in, with the key registered the machine is paired, and the service is the only step they repeat by hand with a command the script prints. Undoing would require deleting the account and revoking the key, and there is no route for that nor should there be one the installer calls on its own. The price is that an installation can end up half done; what it never does is end half done SILENTLY — each failure becomes a named line in a "What was left pending" block, at the end, where whoever installed is still looking. Taking down the whole installation because of the last step would trade half an installation for none. Idempotency is the HTTP CODE, and 409 is not a failure. Both routes answer 409 when the installation already has people — a second run, or a migration (RN-530) whose restore brought the users. That is the EXPECTED outcome: the step goes silent saying why, and does not enter the pending items. Any other code is a failure, and shows up with the code and the api's response alongside. 000 — the curl that never got to talk to the api — has its own treatment for the same reason: collapsing it with a response code would make "the api did not come up" read as "the api refused". And the agent step only runs when THIS run created the account: with a pre-existing user, registering a machine key would mint a durable credential for someone who asked for nothing in this round. The password touches neither disk nor argv. Read in the TTY without echo (stty -echo, with the terminal mode restored at the end), confirmed, and sent to the api via the curl's STDIN — never via --data on the command line, which /proc/<pid>/cmdline publishes to any user of the machine, and never via a file. The header with the BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN goes in a mode-600 --config, deleted right after: it is a secret too, and that secret already lives on disk, in .env, with the same mode. Without stty on the machine the step is refused, never degraded to asking with echo — promising no echo and delivering with echo is worse than not asking. The password does not go to .env, does not go to the marker and does not go to any log; the marker gains the email, which identifies and is not a secret, and MARCADOR_SCHEMA goes up to 3 together with the field, by the same rule that made it go up to 2 when gaining versao. The password refusal is repeatable, and the ceiling is 3. The policy is the domain's (RN-546), the same as normal registration, and it is only known AFTER the POST. Aborting the installation there would leave someone with the compose up and the second run falling into the migration path — so the loop is over the question+answer pair, and exhausting the ceiling becomes a named pending item instead of a refusal. A typed password different from the confirmation never leaves the machine. A tab in what was typed is refused and never silently removed: an installer that rewrites the password produces an account whose password is not the one the person typed. The refusal of service install --machine is the COMMON case on a developer's machine, and it arrives in its own words. install --machine refuses when there is a per-PROJECT unit installed, without --force (RN-545: "installing and warning would leave the wrong installation up"). The installer passes on the CLI's output WHOLE instead of summarizing it — it is what names the uninstall of each unit found, which is the gesture — and the pending item carries the exact command to repeat later. The key's name is the hostname, and the choice is this script's. RN-551 declares in writing that the CLI does not name: the name is a field of the record, and whoever names is whoever registers. Whoever opens the list of device keys needs to know WHICH machine to go to, and the hostname is the name the person already uses to talk about their machines — it is what the shell prompt shows. It is not a secret, it is not unique, and the api derives nothing from it. Quotes and slashes go (they would move out of place inside the JSON), the cut is at 80 (the DTO's @MaxLength(80), applied here so the refusal does not come from the api) and the total absence of hostname and uname returns a fixed name — empty would become a 400 by @MinLength(1), after the account already exists. The .parcial left over when the registration does not close STAYS where it is, and is named. The create writes the private key to a file with a .parcial suffix that the runner ignores by construction (RN-551), and if the registration fails it is left over. Deleting it would be the installer deciding it knows something it does not: a timeout after the api writes is indistinguishable from a timeout before, and the file may be the only copy of the private half of an already registered key. It is inert, the next device-key create names it and replaces it, and the message says both things. What this script does NOT do, and now says it right. The last line of the output announced, months after the functions existed, that it "does not pair the local agent" and that the key "still comes from the project screen". The text was rewritten: SMTP stays off by decision (MAIL_TRANSPORT=log, here as in production — and the account created is born verified precisely because of that), the LLM credential still belongs to whoever is going to spend (RN-058), and pairing through the project screen (ADR 0118) still exists for whoever wants it — what changed is that it stopped being mandatory. The --help suffered from the same defect in a place no test reached (it prints the HEADER, which is a comment, and the rule forbidding talk of "phase sessions" only read code lines): it said "THIS VERSION INSTALLS NOTHING". Fixed, and the fixed line range that cut it off silently became "up to the first line that is not a comment". What did NOT come in: a new route of any kind (the session is orchestration — if something were missing on the other side, the gesture was to stop and report); SMTP; LLM credential; a password written anywhere; and any path that creates an account without a TTY — without an interactive terminal the script reports and exits 0, at the step that already existed, before any write. Code: install.sh:1664 (fechar_a_instalacao, the chaining and the "always 0"), :1463 (perguntar_e_criar_a_conta, the consent, the loop and the ceiling), :1563 (parear_esta_maquina, the id becoming --id), :1640 (subir_o_agente_como_servico, the refusal passed on whole), :1366 (post_interno, the body via stdin and the header via the 600 --config), :1385 (criar_primeira_conta) and :1426 (registrar_chave_de_maquina) — the verdicts of the two routes —, :1441 (ler_sem_eco), :1345 (nome_da_maquina), :1586 (avisar_chave_parcial), :1208/:1215 (escapar_json/sem_controle), :108 (MARCADOR_SCHEMA=3), :1871 (the call, after the runner and before the marker), :1882 (the ownerEmail). Numbers re-read by symbol on 09/18 (AT-096), on 09/27 (AT-065, which added the Mac Intel branch in instalar_o_runner) and on 10/01 (AT-122); those of :966/:682 no longer matched on 09/17 Test: scripts/dev/install-fechamento.spec.ts — the shell functions run FOR REAL (the whole script loaded by source, minus the call to main) against a real node:http server and a stand-in brabo-runner: the account's happy path (body, service token and password arriving), 409/400/ 500/no-response with DIFFERENT verdicts, the password loop and the ceiling of 3, the order create → registrar → finish → service install with the --id being the api's id, the service install refusal passed on in its own words, the .parcial that stays when the registration fails, the create that refuses without anything being registered, and the closing without the agent's binary; scripts/dev/install.spec.ts (the printable plan, and the --help that stopped lying) Gap DECLARED: the end-to-end installation on a clean machine — real compose, real api, real runner binary, unit written and agent waiting for the first project — is the E2E of the phase's session 8, and only it can prove it. Here brabo-runner is a shell stand-in and the api is a test server; what is proven is the CHAINING, never the integration. And the main flow of install.sh (verifying its own origin against the signed checksums.txt) still has no coverage, for the reason install.spec.ts already recorded: no Release has that asset until the next final tag ADR: 0155 Origin: PHASE 30, session 6 — the phase's scope

documents.t: Session 8 of PHASE 30, the last — and the only one that could answer the question the whole phase pursues: on a clean machine, does install.sh end with the local agent up and paired, and does the person create the first project in Runner mode without going back to the terminal? Until now the answer was a written intention: RN-547 chained the five commands and declared, in writing, that in its tests brabo-runner is a shell stand-in and the api is a node:http — "what is proven is the CHAINING, never the integration". The harness was not born here: it was EXTENDED. .github/workflows/install-e2e.yml has existed since PHASE 29 (RN-534) and already runs the published installer on an ephemeral Actions runner — which is literally a clean machine, without Brabo, without .env, without a marker. What it proved stopped at .env: plan, state, the three promises to never delete, the path without a TTY, and the startup with a simulated TTY. A second workflow would duplicate the expensive side (waiting for the Release, downloading, verifying the signature) to measure the cheap side. It does NOT run on pull_request, and the consequence is declared instead of hidden. The installer verifies its own origin against a Release's signed checksums.txt (RN-526), which only exists after a final tag; the only way to make it run on a PR would be giving it a door to SKIP verification — the door ADR 0150 refuses, and which once opened would hold for anyone, not only for CI. Hence: the PR that wrote this E2E did not execute it, and its checks passed without exercising a single line of what it added. It is the same decision as the RAG golden-set (ADR 0138), for the same reason. Hence the half that RUNS on PRs, and it is the reason it exists. A workflow that only runs on tags is a workflow whose error shows up on the tag, when the release is already going out and nobody looks at the PR that broke it anymore. scripts/dev/install-e2e.spec.ts measures the two known ways for this E2E to rot silently: someone loosening the gate (putting pull_request in the trigger, or passing a skip-verification flag), and someone rewriting a sentence of install.sh — with which every grep of the workflow comes to match nothing, and the assertions do not fail, they VANISH. The prompts canary is derived, not memorized: the TTY answers go via file, in order, and a new read -r in the installer misaligns all the following ones — the base would become the password —, so the test counts the prompts and says to look at the answers file. What the E2E came to prove, and each assertion has an owner. The five links of RN-547, one by one, against a REAL api and binary — the account (RN-546), the pair generated on the machine and the stamped kid (RN-551), the registration of the public key (RN-552) and the per-machine unit (RN-545). Plus the invariant of RN-475 measured on the DISK and not in the output (the file the runner reads has kid, has d, and the .parcial vanished when finish closed), the password absent from .env, from the marker and from the log, and the ownerEmail present in the marker. The NEGATIVE proof is the one worth the most, and it is the absence of the pending block. RN-547 says to report each link that fails in a named final block — and exit 0 all the same. An E2E that looked at the exit code would go green with four of the five links broken. "No pending items" is the only way to assert that the five closed, including the ones the workflow does not know how to name. The signal that the agent is UP waiting is the LINE, never the manager's state — and that choice is this E2E's central decision. perguntarEstado maps activating to rodando (RN-088, with reason: "coming up" is not "stopped"), so both systemctl is-active and brabo-runner service status --machine answer up for a process that will die two seconds later. It is exactly the race a fixed sleep hides, and measuring the wrong artifact here — a binary on disk, a written unit — is the easiest way for an E2E to go green without proving anything. The chosen signal is the line the process writes when ENTERING the wait (RN-550): it only exists after the agent has read the machine key from disk, gotten a ticket, talked to the real api and received an EMPTY list — it proves pairing and waiting at once. And it is not state sampling: it is a fact already written to the journal, which does not undo itself. That is why waiting for it with a ceiling is not a race — either it shows up, or the ceiling blows and the step fails showing the whole journal. service status --machine comes in after it, as confirmation that the exit code answers what the operator will see, never in its place. The phase's outcome is measured through the API, and not the BROWSER. The subject of the assertion is the AGENT, not the page: what it observes is GET /runner/projects (RN-543), an api fact. A browser would create the project through the SAME route with one more layer that fails for reasons unrelated to the promise — and would not make the assertion stronger, because it remains the line in the agent's journal. The browser layer exists (e2e/, ADR 0120), answers another question (three origins, httpOnly cookie, CSRF), has its own lockfile and assumes the production compose up: dragging it here would make the installer's E2E depend on a second harness installed on a machine that should be clean. Proving the wizard is the web suite's job, and it is already covered there. What the step measures is the whole chain: the account born in the terminal gets through the login without any verification link, the personal workspace of RN-410 exists, the project is born runner, and the agent picks it up on its own within the 15s/30s/60s cadence of RN-550. Idempotency is measured by the half the E2E reaches without reinstalling. The api really answers 409 to a second first-account — with a GENERATED password, never a constant, because exigirSenhaValida runs BEFORE the conflict and a weak password would give 400, measuring the wrong thing. What the installer DOES with that 409 (go silent, and not become a pending item) is HTTP code classification, covered in install-fechamento.spec.ts against a test server: repeating it here would require a whole second installation, which goes through the MIGRATION path (RN-530) — proven backup, delete, recreate — and is its own delivery. The only divergence between this runner and a clean machine belongs to the ENVIRONMENT, and it is named. On a real machine whoever installs has a login session and systemd --user is already up; the Actions job runs non-interactively, without a session, and without it systemctl --user has no bus to talk to — the service install --machine would become a pending item for a reason that is not the product's, and the E2E would "prove" a lab failure. loginctl enable-linger brings the user manager up; it is not an installer flag, it skips no verification and does not change what the unit does. Two defects showed up while writing this, and both were invisible because the workflow never ran. The first was in the harness itself: the answers file started with nao-migrar, which on a clean machine falls into the MARKER question — it does not match s|S|sim|SIM, the script said "Nada foi gravado" and exited 0, and the marker assertion right below would have failed. The migration question is under if [ -n "$marcador" ] || [ -n "$sinais" ], and on a clean machine both are empty: it does not happen. Fixed to the SEVEN real answers. The second is a FINDING and was not fixed here, on purpose. The published install.sh cannot bring anything up on its own on a clean machine: it brings up the stack with docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.install.yml, a path RELATIVE to the directory it runs from — and that file is not a Release asset, does not enter the signed checksums.txt (RN-524), and the script does not download it anywhere (its only downloads are cosign, the manifest, its own hash and the runner binary). The compose also bind-mounts ./postgres/init.sql, so there are THREE files and not one. Whoever follows the runbook's sh -c "$(curl … install.sh)" dies in "no such file or directory" after having already verified the signature, chosen the base and written the .env. Fixing it means deciding whether the compose becomes a signed asset or whether the installer starts cloning — its own delivery, not something to do in passing inside the E2E that discovered the hole. The workflow brings the three by hand, from the tag, in a step that SAYS it is a finding; the PR test demands both halves (the step exists, and the installer keeps using the compose without downloading it), and the day the installer fetches them on its own the test fails — and the right thing then is to delete the step, not relax the test. What did NOT come in: any door to skip origin verification; apps/ untouched (the finding became a report, not a passing fix); no second installer E2E workflow; and no loosened gate — in particular, the E2E stays out of pull_request. Code: .github/workflows/install-e2e.yml:16 (the trigger that stays without pull_request), :111 (the finding's step — the three files the installer does not download), :172 (the systemd user session, the declared divergence), :204 (the full installation with the SEVEN answers), :241–:245 (the five links of RN-547, one per line), :253 (the negative proof — no pending items), :267–:274 (the kid, the d and the .parcial, measured on DISK and not in the output), :278 (the password that did not leak), :307 (the agent up, by the journal line and not by the manager), :354 (the first project via the api, and the agent picking it up), :415 (the 409 of the second account) Test: scripts/dev/install-e2e.spec.ts — the half that runs on PRs: the trigger read from the DOCUMENT (not from the text, which would match the comment that explains why pull_request is not there), the absence of a skip-verification flag in both files, the sentence contract between workflow and install.sh (the five links plus the usual four), the two lines of apps/runner the assertions depend on, the interactive prompts canary, the ORDER between the journal line and service status --machine, and the two halves of the compose finding. Verified by mutation: rewriting an installer sentence and putting pull_request in the trigger fail Gap DECLARED: this E2E does not run on the PR that wrote it, and none of its checks proves a line of what was added — the first real execution is the next final tag. Also left out, and not by forgetfulness: the second run of the installer through the MIGRATION path (RN-530) — backup, restore proof, delete and recreate —, macOS (the full step is Linux: launchd, and the Docker the hosted runner does not have), and the browser ADR: 0155 Origin: PHASE 30, session 8 — the phase's scope

documents.t: ExecutionModeSection was the only one of the five places in the product where one chooses a folder and the path was typed in the dark — the other four already opened FolderBrowserModal since RN-473/RN-504. The gap was declared in CLAUDE.md and the declared reason belonged to the other branch: onboarding a runner BEFORE the conversion saves registers a key in a project that is not yet runner, and ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase refuses with 400. None of that holds for mounted, and that is what this rule closes. Same component, same transport, no new rule. The mounted branch mounts FolderBrowserModal with origem: { tipo: 'api', workspaceId } — the same discriminated union NewProjectWizard uses for that mode (RN-533), because the folder lives inside the SERVER's base (ADR 0141) and it is the server that sees it. No new browser nor new endpoint is born, and the browser does not guarantee a valid path: what validates is still validarExecutionModeEWorkspacePath and the database CHECK. The runner branch does NOT get a browser, and that is a decision, not forgetfulness. Its transport ({ tipo: 'runner', projectId }) requires a runner connected to THIS project, and a project that is not yet runner has none — the wait would end in an error that looks like a bug. The order "convert, then onboard" remains a separate product decision. What changes is the screen now saying so in text instead of only not offering any button, which is the rule of ADR 0064: the control is removed, never the information. The base is a FOUR-valued state, and they do not collapse. The route GET workspaces/:workspaceId/projects-base (RN-500) may be in flight, have failed, have answered null or have answered a path — and each of those has its OWN text, by the rule of RN-088/RN-468: "I don't know" never becomes "it doesn't have". The button stays on the screen grayed out in the first three, with the reason stated in TEXT right below, and not by title (which on a disabled element does not open in Chromium). base state the button what the screen says in flight grayed out "querying this installation's projects base" the query failed grayed out it was not possible to KNOW whether it exists; reload answered null grayed out this installation did not declare a base answered a path live the base, NAMED, and that it is in it that the browser opens The mounted mode does not leave the selector when the base is missing, and that is the deliberate difference from the wizard (RN-513): a project that IS ALREADY mounted cannot see its own mode disappear from the control because of a query in flight. What disappears is the BROWSER, not the conversion. The minimum is the ENDPOINT's. PUT projects/:projectId/execution-mode and GET workspaces/:workspaceId/projects-base both require maintainer, read via roleAtLeast over ROLE_ORDER and never via a hand-written list of roles (RN-102) — the section did role === 'owner' || role === 'maintainer', which is right by accident while the minimum is high. Whoever does not reach the minimum does not fire the base query: it would end in a certain 403, and the "I don't know" it would produce would be about authorization, not about the base. The value chosen in the browser is treated as a TYPED value: it fills in the field and only goes to the api when someone confirms with the section's button. This section does not become autosave (RN-469). Closing it requires deciding the order "convert, then onboard", which is a separate product decision and remains without an owner. Update: the order was decided and measured in RN-612 — the runner branch gets onboarding AFTER saving, and the browser stays out for another reason, stated there ADR: 0111, 0141 Origin: AT-049 (EP-021/HS-033)
