documents.t: The section's fixed warning asserted "this migrates the agent's working folder", in both languages. ConvertProjectExecutionModeUseCase does not have a single line that copies or moves folder content: it moves permissions.json (the POLICY, with allow/deny/ask intact — RN-448), zeroes workspaceVerifiedAt (RN-450) and mirrorPath (RN-515), deprovisions the container when LEAVING container (RN-449) and writes the new workspacePath. materializarWorkspaceMontado only CREATES the new folder (RN-501). Whatever is in the old folder — uncommitted work included — stays there, orphaned. The orphan was already a declared gap in CLAUDE.md since RN-447..450. What this rule closes is not the orphan: it is the screen asserting the OPPOSITE of what the server does. This is an assertion fix, not a feature — migrating content between modes stays out, without an owner. Three facts, and not a paragraph, because they answer different questions: what the conversion REFUSES — a dev agent working or stuck right now becomes a 409, and the api's sentence is the one that shows up in the toast (the text that already existed and still holds); what it CARRIES — the project's policy changes scope with its content intact; what it does NOT carry — the folder's content, uncommitted work included, naming the old path. The warning NAMES the path because "stays on the old disk" without saying WHICH disk tells the person to go searching. The value is one line away (project.workspacePath) and disappears from the screen the instant the conversion saves. When there is no path to name — the project is container, and the old folder is a SERVER volume — the sentence is a DIFFERENT one, pointing to the managed folder: a variant with an empty {{caminho}} would say "whatever is in ", which is the screen refusing to name what it knows. It is the case in which the person has the LEAST means to guess. It does not promise detection. Asking the disk "is there uncommitted work?" is per-mode I/O and impossible to answer for runner from the api side: the folder lives on a machine the server does not see. It is not measured, it is not asserted (ADRs 0041/0042). And it blocks nothing: the conversion remains the same call, with the same refusals. The Alert's tone went from accent to warning, because the third fact is a LOSS of reach and not neutral information. It stays without role="alert": it is text that was already on the screen when it opened, and an assertive live region there would become an interruption without cause. Code: apps/web/src/routes/settings/ExecutionModeSection.tsx:333 (the three facts, one per line), :337 (the variant that names the old path × the managed folder one); apps/web/src/locales/pt-BR/settings.json:220 and apps/web/src/locales/en/settings.json:220 (executionMode.warning.*, the four texts in both languages — en is the app's default language (RN-425), and an honest warning only in Portuguese is the same lie with an accent) Test: apps/web/src/routes/settings/conversao-de-modo.test.tsx — the happy path (the warning containing the old path AND the words "uncommitted work"), the variant without an old path (a container project pointing to the managed folder, and the variant with a path NOT rendered), and the negative proof in BOTH language bundles: the migration promise survives in neither, and the four keys exist in both The CONDITIONAL consequences (AT-144). The question this rule left open — list ALL consequences or only the one that misled — was decided by the maintainer: only those that hold for THIS project. The warning adds, after the three facts, one line per consequence that applies, and NONE for what does not apply: line when it shows up the same condition as the use case the mirror destination is zeroed, NAMED mirrorPath filled in every conversion zeroes it (RN-515) the registered container is stopped and removed the project is container TODAY and the lifecycle exists outside removed removerContainerSeExistir only runs when LEAVING container (RN-449) "I could not read whether there is a container" the project is container and the lifecycle read FAILED — ("I don't know" never becomes "it doesn't have", RN-468) the folder confirmed on <data> stops being valid workspaceVerifiedAt filled in every conversion zeroes it (RN-450) The container line does not show up in mounted/runner even with a registered container, because the use case does not remove it there — the warning would say the opposite of the server, which is the defect this rule exists to close. The data are those the section already has (Project: mirrorPath, workspaceVerifiedAt, executionMode) plus the container lifecycle, which the section did NOT load: it comes from the route that ALREADY exists, GET projects/:projectId/container/lifecycle (viewer), queried only when the project is container — no new endpoint. While the read is in flight, the line simply does not show up. Code: apps/web/src/routes/settings/ExecutionModeSection.tsx:102 (consequenciasCondicionais), :118 (containerParaOAviso, the three states), :236 (cicloQuery, only in container), :344 (the four lines in the Alert) Test: the AT-144 describe in apps/web/src/routes/settings/conversao-de-modo.test.tsx — no condition (no extra line), registered container, a removed row that does not count, read FAILING with its own text, mounted with a mirror (the mirror line yes, the container one no, and the query does not even go out), runner with a confirmed folder (with the date), and the three conditionals in en ADR: 0111 Origin: AT-050 (EP-021/HS-034); the conditionals, AT-144 (EP-021/HS-034)

documents.t: The runner branch of the conversion was typed in the dark (RN-559) because the order was undecided: onboarding BEFORE saving registers a key in a project that is not yet runner, and ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase refuses the confirmation with 400. The maintainer's decision was to measure the other order with the MACHINE key (RN-543/RN-548) and implement it if the friction were acceptable. The measurement was done in the CODE (without bringing up the environment) and gave this: who will serve the project what happens after saving gestures MACHINE agent waiting (zero runner projects, RN-550) the next query of GET /runner/projects lists it and the agent connects on its own — 15/30/60 s cadence of espera-de-projetos.ts zero, within 60 s MACHINE agent already serving ANOTHER project the list is read ONCE, at start, with a live connection (RN-550) — the new project does not come in one: restart the service no machine key the same pairing as project creation (RN-473) pair + one command In all three cases the friction is that of project creation or less, so the conversion becomes two steps in the same section: saving to runner mounts, right below, the SAME RunnerOnboardingPanel as the Code tab and the wizard, with the projectId of a project that now IS runner — recognition of the paired machine, EsperaDoRunner and the ADR 0118 pairing come along, with no new rule. Above the panel the section SAYS the machine agent's asymmetry (waits on its own × restart), with the restart command for both platforms (systemctl --user restart brabo-runner.service, launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/dev.brabo.runner): the screen does not know whether the agent has another live connection, so it names both cases instead of asserting one. The panel shows up when the SAVED project is runner, with no pending mode change in the selector, and with the folder not yet confirmed — or until the end of the visit in which the conversion saved, so EsperaDoRunner shows the confirmation instead of disappearing the instant it arrives. An already confirmed runner project does not get it. The typed path is PROVISIONAL, and the screen says so. What decides the folder of a runner project is the runner: the confirmation OVERWRITES workspacePath (RN-423), and the machine agent does not even look at the typed value — it uses <base>/<workspaceDirName> (RN-544). The field stays mandatory because the database CHECK requires a non-null path outside container; the section does not invent a placeholder. The folder browser stays OUT of the runner branch, and now for the right reason. It is no longer the order: it is that the transport { tipo: 'runner', projectId } requires a runner connected to THIS project, and a connected runner has already confirmed its OWN folder (--dir, or the one derived from the base). Choosing another there would be a second runner → runner conversion the next reconnection would undo. Offering the button would be a control that controls nothing; the section says so in text (ADR 0064). documents.t: The procedure with the worst outcome in the Runbook now has a NAMED verification: a test walks through the whole rotation — encrypt with K1, publish K2, rewrap, discard K1 and still decrypt — against user_credentials and project_git_connections, with a real Postgres. Why integration, and not one more unit case. What already existed (envelope-encryption.service.spec.ts, the rotação da chave mestra describe) exercises encrypt/decrypt/rewrap in memory, and that does not prove the only thing step 3 of the runbook depends on: that the script walks through both tables. Converting half the holdings and reporting success, discarding the old key would make the other half unreadable forever. The proof of that is the assertion about the two rows — and it fails when the script's list of tables shrinks. Idempotency goes into the same test, because it is the property the runbook promises to whoever interrupts the script: the second round reports re-embrulhados=0 and já na chave atual=1 in both tables. An unreadable row does not abort the others. A record wrapped by a THIRD key — the case the runbook calls "came from another environment" — is counted, identified by table and id, and lets the others continue; its envelope stays untouched. What the test required of the code: rewrap-deks.ts was a main() fired at MODULE LOAD, so importing it from a spec would run the rotation. The core became reenvelopar(db, cofre, reportarFalha), exported, and main() — which reads the environment, opens the pool, prints and chooses the exit code — now runs only under require.main === module. The script's name and the runbook's invocation (node scripts/rewrap-deks.js) did NOT change. No key and no secret is literal in the test: both are born from randomBytes each round. A constant passphrase in a fixture is a string that looks like a secret going into history, and gitleaks sweeps branches. Code: apps/api/src/scripts/rewrap-deks.ts:93 (reenvelopar, the exported function), :100 (the list of the two tables, which is what the test pins), :209 (the require.main === module that prevents the import from rotating) Test: apps/api/test/scripts/rewrap-deks.spec.ts — the happy path (the sequence K1 → K1+K2 → rewrap → only K2), idempotency, and the failure case of the row from another environment, which also asserts that the report does NOT carry any secret Origin: AT-033 (EP-015/HS-022), finding BRB-010

documents.t: user_credentials and project_git_connections gain a nullable key_id text — the fingerprint of the master key that wrapped that DEK. With it, the question that decides step 3 of the rotation ("is there still a credential on the old key?") becomes a query: select count(*) from user_credentials where key_id is distinct from '<atual>' union all select count(*) from project_git_connections where key_id is distinct from '<atual>'; IS DISTINCT FROM, and never <>: with <>, the row with a NULL key_id — the holdings prior to this column — would disappear from the count, and "I don't know which key" would become "it is already on the current one", which is the reading that makes someone discard the old key too early. The value is HMAC-SHA256(chave derivada, 'brabo-master-key-id') truncated to 8 bytes, and not a counter in .env nor a hash of the passphrase. There is no new oracle, and that was MEASURED, not assumed: whoever reads the database already has a perfect verification oracle — the envelope itself is AES-256-GCM, which authenticates, so testing a candidate passphrase already cost one scrypt and one decipher. Testing it against the fingerprint costs the SAME scrypt. And there is no new variable for the operator to get wrong: the value is a pure function of the key they already published. The label is OBSERVABILITY, never AUTHORITY. decrypt stays byte for byte as it was — tries the current one, falls back to the previous one, GCM decides — and rewrap keeps deciding "it is already on the current key" by ATTEMPT. Trusting the label would make a row that LIES (label "current", envelope on the old key) be skipped silently, stay out of the re-wrapped count, and step 3 would make it unreadable forever. Incoherent metadata becomes secret loss; that is why the test that pins this rule is that of a lying row being re-wrapped anyway. What the label buys on failure: when NEITHER of the two keys opens, the message stops being generic and names the case — "came from another environment" (unknown label), "incoherent label or tampered record" (label says current and does not open) and "has no key_id" (row prior to this column) are different diagnoses with different actions. None of these messages carries the passphrase, derived key or secret content — only fingerprints. No migration of the holdings. The key_id is born at the next write (encrypt and rewrap write it). Today's rows stay NULL, and in an existing installation the query only becomes valid after the first rotation. Forcing a rewrap of everything just to fill the column would turn observability into a risky operation on all credentials. The operator needs the current fingerprint, otherwise the column compares against nothing: the api records it at boot in one line, and the rotation warning that already existed now names BOTH. Code: apps/api/src/infrastructure/security/envelope-encryption.service.ts:130 (impressaoDigital), :107 (the boot line), :113 (the warning with the two), :226 (the rewrap diagnosis), :251 (diagnosticoDaChave); apps/api/src/db/schema/llm.ts:259 and apps/api/src/db/schema/git.ts:76 (the column in both tables); migration apps/api/src/db/migrations/0059_key_id_no_envelope.sql Test: the key_id da chave mestra describe in apps/api/test/infrastructure/security/envelope-encryption.service.spec.ts — the happy path (stable and deterministic fingerprint, written by encrypt and by rewrap), the proof that the label does not decide (a lying row is re-wrapped), the legacy row without a label, and the two failure cases (message that names the key without leaking a secret; "no label" stated as such). The real SQL query is in apps/api/test/scripts/rewrap-deks.spec.ts, including the case of the NULL row counting as pending ADR: 0158 Origin: AT-034 (EP-015/HS-022), finding BRB-016

documents.t: The missing half of RN-519, declared in writing ever since in CLAUDE.md: "what remains open is only the SCREEN: apps/web has nowhere to list nor revoke, so whoever wants to revoke calls the route". Both routes exist — the DELETE since ADR 0118 and the GET since RN-519 —, and no screen used them. This RN is the screen, and it opens no new route: what the listing already returns is enough to draw everything that follows. Where it lives, and why PROJECT. It takes the Settings tab from 17 to 18 sections and is the 13th in render order (device-keys, group pessoas, right after access-tokens — the neighbor that does the same with PATs); the registry's order is the SAME as the barrel's, because it is what the scroll-spy uses. Project because the endpoint is /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys: an ACCOUNT screen would require a new route, and the scope is about the one that exists. The KIND shows up, and it is not decoration — it is the reach of the screen's only irreversible action. Since RN-543 the listing marks projeto | maquina, and a MACHINE key (null project_id) serves all the owner's projects and that is why it shows up in the list of ALL of them. Showing it without the mark would make the screen assert it is "this project's key", and whoever clicked revoke would think it takes down the local agent here when it takes it down in all of them — the screen would lie precisely about what can least be wrong. The mark is warning for the machine one and muted for the project one, and never success: green would read as "it's up", which is the arithmetic RN-548 already refused. The confirmation DEPENDS on the kind, and also states the collateral cost. Revoking opens a dialog with THREE sentences, and the middle one is the one that changes: the machine one names all your projects in runner mode (the loop of RevokeRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase over listRunnerModeReachableBy), the project one names its project. A single text for both would lie in one of the halves. The third sentence is the cost RN-520 declared and this delivery does not change: the disconnection target is {projeto, usuário} and never {chave}, so another runner of the same user on the same project also drops — even authenticated by a PAT or another key — and reconnects on its own if its credential is still valid. Recorded use is NOT an agent up, and the vocabulary is the SAME as RN-548. lastUsedAt is the data class of workspaceVerifiedAt (RN-468): the record of a confirmation, never a heartbeat. The caveat is stated in TEXT in the caption, and the status column talks about REVOCATION ("active"/"revoked", a fact about the row), never about connection — what knows about NOW is still the terminal's channel. Inventing a second vocabulary for the same distinction would be the screen saying the same thing in two ways, and one of the two would age. Five states, and none becomes the other (RN-088/RN-470). No key ("No device key of yours serves this project"), a REVOKED key (which stays in the list by RN-519's decision — making the row disappear would make the screen assert it never existed, and it gets no button because revoking again, even if idempotent in the api, would suggest an effect that did not remain), NULL lastUsedAt (the ORPHAN key of RN-473: registered by a tab that closed in the middle of the flow and never used by any runner — its own text, and an explanation below the table that only shows up when there is one, because explaining what does not occur is noise), "not loaded yet" and "I could not read". "I don't know" never becomes "it doesn't have". The role is the ENDPOINT's, and it is the project's EFFECTIVE one. The minimum is developer — what RunnerDeviceKeysController requires on the THREE routes (RN-102) — and the comparison comes from the SAME function RN-548 created (podeLerChavesDeDispositivo, over roleAtLeast), never a second rule and never a hand-written role === 'x' || role === 'y'. What changes in relation to RN-548 is the INPUT: there the panel read the WORKSPACE role and declared the gap, because it mounts in places that do not fetch project_members; here the data is at hand — the section lives in the same tab as MembersSection, with the SAME queryKey, and react-query deduplicates —, so the role is composed as in the use case (projectRole ?? workspaceRole, an OVERLAY in both directions, RN-471) and the gap closes instead of repeating itself. An ABSENT role is not an INSUFFICIENT role: while the member list is in flight the screen says it is verifying, and does not accuse the reader of not reaching developer. Whoever does not reach it still sees the whole section, what a device key is and what revoking the machine one costs — the CONTROL disappears, never the INFORMATION (ADR 0064) —, and the reason is stated ONCE in TEXT (title on a disabled element does not open in Chromium). Since the three routes require the SAME role, whoever does not reach it also does not see the LIST: the screen stops asking what the api would deny, instead of turning a predictable 403 into "I could not read". This is not a security boundary — what refuses is the RolesGuard. One at a time, and that is why there is no batch outcome. The screen does not offer "revoke all", so the rule of RN-469 — a UI action that becomes N calls is not a transaction, and the screen says so — does not apply: offering the batch would create a partial outcome to narrate for an action nobody asked for. A failure in revocation shows the api's OWN sentence and the row stays in the list. Code: apps/web/src/routes/settings/RunnerDeviceKeysSection.tsx:76 (the whole section; the effective role at :107, the query at :130, the confirmation by kind at :326); apps/web/src/routes/settings/sumario.ts:62 (the new entry, 13th in render order, of the 18); apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSettingsTab.tsx:86 (the composition, in the SAME order); apps/web/src/locales/{en,pt-BR}/settings.json (runnerDeviceKeys.*). It consumes listRunnerDeviceKeys/ revokeRunnerDeviceKey (apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts:431) and podeLerChavesDeDispositivo (apps/web/src/lib/agente-de-maquina.ts:68) without changing either of them Test: apps/web/src/routes/settings/chaves-de-dispositivo.test.tsx — the two kinds marked in the same list; the revoked one that stays, marked and without a button; the orphan with its own text and the explanation that does NOT show up without it; empty and failure with different texts; the caveat that recorded use is not an agent up; the reach warning in BOTH kinds, with the call going out only after confirming; cancel without revoking; the failure bringing the api's sentence with the key still in the list; viewer without calling the route and with the reason in text; the project role overlay in BOTH directions; and the absent role that says "verifying" instead of accusing Declared and NOT closed: (1) the revocation target remains {projeto, usuário} and never {chave} — the screen SAYS so and does not change it, because changing it requires a new column in runner_socket_tickets and a new auth contract (RN-520), its own front with an ADR; (2) in an installation without a PROJECT, the machine key freshly created by RN-552 remains unreachable: both routes are project ones, and without a project there is no one to ask — CLOSED in RN-611, with a route and section per ACCOUNT; (3) the maintainer view (list/revoke any user's) stays OUT by RN-519's decision, not by this screen's omission; (4) no browser E2E — what is proven here is what the screen ASSERTS, and that the component suite proves Origin: AT-012 (EP-003/HS-007)

documents.t: propose_container_start proposed blindly. dispatch_container_start/2 assembled the payload and called EngineApiClient.propose_action(...) directly — without a project read between one thing and the other, and with zero occurrences of execution_mode in the whole tool. In a runner project the proposal could only end in failure: since RN-507/ADR 0145 container_start does not serve that mode, because its payload ELECTS a candidate from the Arquiteto's routing (ADR 0131) and in runner there is no routing to elect against — that mode's type is container_start_via_runner. The rule is not new, and a second one was not born. The sibling tool already refused locally (RN-508) and the /containers page already branched by DESTINATION (RN-521, acaoDeSubidaDoModo): container and mounted come up via the BROKER, runner comes up via the local agent (ADR 0144/RN-503). What this rule does is give the missing tool the SAME rule — one project read (recusa_local_de_subida/2, which returns nil or a reason) and one CLAUSE per tool (recusa_por_modo/3). Two parallel rules would diverge on the first new mode of the enum. The refusal of container_start is an ALLOWLIST, like the broker's own: container/mounted pass, runner is refused NAMING the sibling tool, and a new mode in the enum is born refused with a message instead of proposed by omission. A nonexistent project also refuses — the same clause for both tools. The refusal is an INPUT to the loop (RN-163): tool RESULT text, which the model reads and uses to call the right tool. Never agent.error, never end of turn, never proposed_action — the api is not called. And it is not silence: the emit of tool.call now happens BEFORE the refusal in BOTH tools (in the sibling it was inside the branch that proposes), as in the generic dispatch_tool/2 of the same module — a refusal without a trace in the event log is the call vanishing from the human's timeline. The reads are LOCAL, and that is the decision. Project.get/1 and Engine.Runners.Registry.connected?/1 run in the SAME BEAM process as the Infra Lead; an HTTP call to the api here would put a network call inside the agent's loop. The cost declared in CLAUDE.md — "fixing it would require touching the Infra Lead's prompt/instruction" — was not confirmed: no prompt line changed, and the refusal text is what the model reads as a result. What this rule does NOT close, and it is half the gap: the blind proposal due to ABSENCE OF IMAGE remains possible in container/mounted. The refusal here is about MODE, and requiring a decided image would invert the order — electing the image is precisely what that proposal DOES (RN-491). /containers checks the THREE things (decided image, mode, confirmed folder) because it has a human clicking; the agent comes to check ONE. GetInfraContextUseCase stays without executionMode — enriching the Infra Lead's context is a separate front. container_stop/container_remove do not come in: they are proposed by the screen, never by an agent (RN-495). No ceiling changes: container_start remains a real proposed_action, maintainer, never seeded into auto-approval (until RN-671, which seeds it on accepting the Infra handoff), and container_remove stays at the absolute ceiling of git push/privileged command (RN-418). Code: apps/engine/lib/engine/infra/infra_lead_server.ex:599 (the dispatch of container_start querying before proposing), :902 (recusa_local_de_subida/2 — the SINGLE project read), :474 (the container_start clause: an allowlist), :477 (the refusal naming container_start_via_runner), :492 (the sibling's clause, with the second question — runner connected), :409 (the emit of tool.call moved to before the refusal); apps/engine/lib/engine/infra/tools/propose_container_start.ex (moduledoc — the tool stopped proposing blindly) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/infra/infra_lead_server_test.exs:422 (happy path in mounted — the broker serves both), :448 (failure case: runner refuses NAMED, propose_action never called, the tool.call narrated anyway), :538 (nonexistent project), :380 (the happy path of container, which now requires the row in the database) ADR: 0144, 0145 Origin: AT-048 (EP-020/HS-032) — the gap declared in CLAUDE.md since RN-494

documents.t: The signed checksums.txt (RN-524) is the precondition of two other rules: without it, GET /runner-releases/binary refuses with release_sem_manifesto (RN-525) and install.sh refuses itself (RN-526) — on all platforms, including those that attached a binary properly. A manifest that is late is not a late manifest: for whoever installs in that interval, it is an absent manifest. The measurement, against the three tags that exist. In v4.0.0, v4.0.1 and v5.0.0, the darwin-x64 target (macos-13) spent 24h00m01s in the queue and was cancelled by the Actions ceiling — the SAME number in all three, which says it never gets scheduled. The other four jobs end in at most 4m18s (linux-x64 in v4.0.1, 17:38:28Z → 17:42:44Z). The checksums job had needs: build: the always() guaranteed that it RAN (a cancelled dependency is covered), never WHEN. The rule: the manifest job does not depend on the matrix. It waits for the Release's ASSETS, not the JOBS — with a ceiling —, and publishes whatever exists, naming in the log what it does not cover. The absence of a target is a foreseen outcome (::notice::), never an error; the absence of the Release remains a named error, because this workflow only ATTACHES and never creates; and no attached binary remains an error, because an empty checksums.txt would assert that the release has no binaries when what happened was the whole matrix failing. The binaries ceiling is 1200s, and the number is not arbitrary: it is the timeout-minutes: 20 of the build job itself — the most a target with a runner can take after starting. What it deliberately does not cover is queue time, and not covering queue time is the whole point. The loop exits early when all targets arrive, which is the happy path. Nothing the job DOES changes. It still builds the manifest from the assets (and not from dist-bin/, empty there), signing with keyless cosign and verifying before attaching — RN-524 intact, one manifest and not five signatures. And a target that attaches AFTER the ceiling is not orphaned: the --clobber already existed for that, and redoing the manifest is a workflow_dispatch with the same tag. What this rule does NOT do: darwin-x64 still does not build. Changing the label, removing the platform or paying for a runner is the owner's decision, and the manifest cannot depend on it — it is precisely because it depended on it that it did not come out. Measured later, in AT-065 (2026-09-13, by a rehearsal workflow_dispatch): macos-13 is a label without a runner (image retired by GitHub in Dec/2025; 30min in the queue, cancelled, run 34769280227). macos-15-intel schedules in 3–22s and builds, but fails at --self-test-pty because, under Bun, the onData of node-pty does not deliver the child's output (oven-sh/bun#25822, open); the same proof passes under Node on the same runner (run 34770476634). The pending decision stopped being about the runner and became waiting for Bun or removing the platform. The rule above does not change because of that. Decided on 2026-09-27 (ADR 0174, AT-065): the platform left. The matrix went to FOUR targets, and ALVOS_ESPERADOS followed — it is against it that the absence is declared, and leaving darwin-x64 there would make every manifest announce, forever, a gap that is a decision. The Mac Intel stays with npm install -g @brabo/runner (under Node, where the same proof passes): install.sh says so without trying to download, the GET /runner-releases/binary proxy refuses darwin-x64 with its own 400 pointing to npm, and the browser panel does not even ask for the download. This RN's rule does not change: it keeps holding for any target left without a runner, and scripts/ci/alvos-do-runner.spec.ts fails when the matrix, the api's list, the installer's case and the browser's diverge. Code: .github/workflows/build-runner-binaries.yml:283 (the job, now without needs:), :318 (timeout-minutes: 40, which fits both waits), :335 (ALVOS_ESPERADOS at the JOB level, so both steps read the same list), :397 (the step that waits), :401/:402 (the two ceilings), :410 (the absent Release, which is an error), :433 (the binaries ceiling, which is a notice), :499 (the manifest naming what it does not cover) Test: scripts/ci/checksums-nao-espera-a-matriz.spec.ts — that the job has no needs:, that both ceilings exist, that the binaries ceiling is derived from the build's timeout-minutes (and not copied), that it fits in the job's own timeout-minutes, that the absence of a target is notice and the absence of the Release is error, that ALVOS_ESPERADOS matches the matrix, and the four guarantees of ADR 0149 this change does not touch (one signature, verifying before attaching, id-token: write, the install.sh in the manifest). It is STATIC, and the limit is declared at the top of the file: the job is only proven on a final tag, and it has never run on any Gap DECLARED: the matrix has THREE targets since ADR 0187 (win32-x64 left by the same mold as ADR 0174, and ALVOS_ESPERADOS followed) and the Release keeps receiving two — darwin-arm64 is proven in rehearsal (RN-688) and only needs a final tag to exercise it. The manifest will be born covering two and will say so, which is the difference between partial and silent. And, with the matrix failing entirely, the job spends both waits before refusing ADR: 0149 Origin: AT-051 (EP-009/HS-035)
documents.s: RN-565 — The signed manifest goes out with what the Release HAS, and does not wait for the platform that never builds

documents.t: decide() always returned a pair — policy and reason —, and the reason is written at every return point: insufficient IAM, the container floor (RN-492), agent_autonomy, the lines of permissions.json, the compound command, and each absolute ceiling. But ProposeActionUseCase only kept it in one place: rejectionReason, which initialStatusFor fills in only when the policy denies. On an auto-approval — the outcome that most needs auditing — the event log said "the policy decided" (RN-049) and never which rule. status made auto-approval distinguishable from a click; the reason is the next step. The rule: the payload of the SESSION event proposed_action.created gains reason, with the string from decide() as is, in all THREE outcomes — auto_approved, pending and denied. No second "structured" rule is born: the string is already the source, and a parallel enum would diverge from it on the first new ceiling. In denied the value is the SAME that becomes rejectionReason. The outbox does NOT gain the field, and that is a decision. The outbox row proposed_action.created is an api↔engine contract, and no engine consumer reads the reason; widening a contract without a consumer is the cut that ADR 0153 names. The session_event.appended row that AppendSessionEventUseCase writes for the same event carries only eventId/seq/type, so the reason also does not leak through it. Absent is not "no reason". An event written before this rule does not have the field, and there is no reprocessing nor new column: whoever reads treats an absent reason as "not recorded". Every new event has the field, because Decision.reason is a mandatory string in the type. Nothing in decide() changes — no ceiling, no verdict, no string. The screen also does not change in this rule: the reason comes to EXIST in the log, and showing it is another delivery. (Since RN-614 the screen shows it on the event's line in the log panel and in the ApprovalCard, through the same sentence.) What the reason does NOT say, declared: it names the rule, not the scope's ROOT — point 7 of ADR 0055 asked for which root authorized, and escopo: cd dentro da pasta do projeto does not carry the path. (The root started going in the event in its OWN field since RN-609, relative and never absolute.) In the compound command, the reason says all segments hit allow, without saying which pattern matched which segment. And the lines of permissions.json repeat the command's TOKENS in the text (the label of matchAgainstFile) — the same command that already lives in proposed_actions.payload and on the approval card. Code: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/propose-action.use-case.ts:259 (reason in the session event payload), :223 (the comment on the outbox without the field), :227 (the outbox payload, intact), :356 (the rejectionReason, which stays only on deny); apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts:278 (Decision, the string's source) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/propose-action.use-case.spec.ts:902 (happy path: auto-approval records agent_autonomy: auto_approve), :948 (require_approval by default and by the merge lock ceiling), :1047 (deny with the same text as rejectionReason), :999 (the outbox without reason) ADR: 0048, 0055 (point 7, partially) Origin: AT-066
documents.s: RN-567 — proposed_action.created says WHICH rule decided: the reason of decide() now survives when the action passes

documents.t: The Overview and the Executors tab build the roster with deriveAgentRoster over the session's LAST 200 events (useSessionEvents, latest: true). Two of the presence facts came from that window: gatesEverOpened (qa and secops come in when some pr.gate_changed/infra.gate_changed has already happened) and delegatedSubagents (an area member comes in with a recorded delegation). Both events are among the first of an execution — in a long session they leave the window, and QA, SecOps and qa-automacao vanished from the panel of an execution that kept running. It is the same class of defect that had already been closed for executionActivated, and the workspace summary (RN-090) already aggregated both facts over the whole session (bool_or and selectDistinct in projects-summary.repository.ts) — both screens loaded it and ignored those two fields. The rule: deriveAgentRoster/rosterFactsFromEvents accept an OPTIONAL agregado (AgregadoDaSessao), and both screens fill it with the summary. Four decisions, each with a reason: Absent is "I did not read", never "there was none". Without a loaded summary (first paint, error), the fact comes only from the window, exactly as before. An absent read never becomes "QA is not here". The aggregate ADDS to the window, it does not replace it (logical OR on the gate, union on the delegations). Both facts are MONOTONIC within a session — a gate that opened does not un-open, a recorded delegation does not disappear —, so the window only produces false NEGATIVES, never false positives. An aggregated false that disagrees with a gate SEEN in the window is a late summary (the two reads have their own poll cadences), and cannot hide QA. It only holds when the summary is of the SAME session the screen reads (latestSessionId === sessionId). The summary aggregates the project's most RECENT session; the Overview reads that same session, but the Executors tab reads the current EXECUTION session (RN-139). An ideation opened afterwards makes the two diverge, and then the aggregate would be of ANOTHER session — the screen goes back to deciding only by the window. Only PRESENCE changes. rosterFromFacts (the single rule, shared with the dashboard card) stays intact, and each agent's STATUS (gateStatus, subagentStatus) is still read from the window. No new request and the 200 ceiling does not change. delegatedSubagents came in through the SAME mold because it fits without changing a rule: the delegations table the summary reads and the delegation.* events the window reads are born together in RecordDelegationUseCase (one row, one event, the three outcomes), so the two sets describe the same thing. executionActivated (AT-130). It is the third fact of the same mold: the Executors tab read it from the summary WITHOUT the guard of item 3, so with a session newer than the execution one the summary (of it) said false and the dev agents vanished — or true, and they appeared without proof. Now it goes in agregado.executionActivated only when latestSessionId === sessionId, and deriveAgentRoster ADDS it (logical OR, monotonic) to the window and to the parameter, which also starts looking at execution.activated in the events. No new field in the API. Tests: ProjectExecutorsTab.test.tsx (summary of ANOTHER session, in both directions). Still open: with a long execution session AND the summary of another session, the event may have left the window and the tab goes back to deciding only by it — it is the cost of the guard, the same as for the other two facts. documents.t: ADR 0152 (decision 4) refused a backup of neo4j_data based on a premise — the graph can be discarded because it can be rebuilt — whose mechanism did not exist: grep for reprojet/reproject in apps/ and scripts/ came back empty, and application/graph-projection/ only had the FORWARD projector. While it did not exist, the graph was not discardable: it was lost. The rule: apps/api/src/scripts/reprojetar-grafo.ts (pnpm --filter api grafo:reprojetar; node scripts/reprojetar-grafo.js in the image) rebuilds the graph by sweeping the source. Five decisions, each with a reason: A single translator. The event → node/edge translation LEFT GraphProjector for GraphEventTranslator, and both paths call it — the projector reaches the source through an outbox row, the reprojection through a cursor. Two translators would diverge, and the divergent one would be the one that runs once a year. The projector's injection surface did NOT change (it builds the translator with the dependencies it already received). A test fails a new type in GRAPH_PROJECTABLE_EVENT_TYPES without a translation. The sources are two, and they are the real ones. handoff.offered, psychologist.hypothesis_proposed and anamnese.profile_updated come from session_events; the Interacao comes from sessions in closed/closed_abnormally, because closing a session is a pure transition and leaves no event in the log. PromptTemplate/PromptVersion do NOT come from the event log and are NOT reprojected — they come back through scripts/dev/seed-prompts.ts. Idempotent, in batches, and never deletes. Every write is a MERGE on a natural key; running again is the way to resume. session_events is swept in id order (ULID, the primary key), 200 per batch, and --after-event resumes after the printed cursor. With --project, only that project's sessions. It does not touch the outbox. The live projector keeps its progress in outbox_events.processed_at; the reprojection neither reads nor writes that table, and that is why it runs with the api up without stealing, reopening or marking rows. Never a silent success. A disabled graph is refused BEFORE reading the log (an empty scope "would pass" with zero projected); a Neo4j that drops midway stops with the last completed event; a nonexistent project is refused without writing anything; and an item with an incoherent payload is counted, named, and the process exits with 1. What this rule does NOT close: PerfilAnamnese is a snapshot per user + dimension, WITHOUT a project — the last to write wins —, so a round with --project may leave it at that project's value when another wrote later; the full round restores the global last one. There is no time measurement on a large event log (the only real round was the dev compose, 98 events, 2.5 s), and the proof on the local cluster that BRB-018 asks for was not done — it remains open. The first four require Neo4j up and SKIP without it — the api's CI does not bring up Neo4j. Origin: AT-032 (BRB-018) — the premise of ADR 0152 without a mechanism

documents.t: RN-549 measured, the first time the installer ran on a clean machine, that the published install.sh brought up nothing on its own: it called docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.install.yml, a path RELATIVE to the directory it ran from, and that file was not a Release asset, did not enter the signed checksums.txt and was not downloaded anywhere. Whoever followed the runbook's one-liner died in "no such file or directory" AFTER the script had written the .env with the secrets. The maintainer decided the way out on 2026-09-13 — a signed asset, and not a clone (ADR 0160). The rule: Four files travel with the installer, in the SAME manifest. The installation compose and the three the installation uses by relative path — the postgres/init.sql and the ollama/pull-models.sh that the compose bind-mounts, and the backup/test-restore-compose.sh that the migration (RN-530) executes — are published as brabo-install-* assets by the checksums job and enter the sha256sum that generates the signed checksums.txt. The fourth was not in the E2E's workaround and was found while implementing: in a folder without a checkout the migration would die there. The job checks each manifest line against the file (sha256sum -c --strict) before attaching. The table has two sides and a guard. The publisher reads scripts/ci/assets-do-instalador.ts; the downloader reads the case of destino_do_asset_do_instalador in install.sh (bash 3.2, without Node). The spec fails the divergence between the two AND derives from the compose every ./… bind-mount that is not in the table — which is exactly how the defect was born. Verifying comes right after its own origin, and before everything. The installer downloads the four and compares each sha256 against the checksums.txt that verificar_a_si_mesmo already verified (never a second download), by EXACT name equality. The three refusals are distinct — asset not published, manifest that does not cover it, hash that does not match — and all happen with the machine untouched. It never falls back to the relative path. COMPOSE_DE_INSTALACAO is born EMPTY and only gets an absolute path when the verified copies are put under the installation's folder, at the first instant they are needed (the migration or the startup). Whatever is already there is REPLACED, never read — with rm before the cp, so a symlink does not carry the write outside. What this rule does NOT close: the end-to-end proof only happens on the first final tag after the merge — install-e2e.yml does not run on PRs (ADR 0150) —, and no already published Release gains the assets: they stay with the old installer and the workaround of running it from inside a checkout at the tag. The adjacency ADR 0160 declared — test-restore-compose.sh called Compose without --env-file, and Compose looks for the .env in the compose's folder — closed in AT-102: the installer passes BRABO_ENV_FILE (--env-file, and not --project-directory, which would also change the project's name and the base of the relative paths) and the installation compose declares the backup_local volume that the backup service references, whose absence refused the whole file with the profile on. Covered by scripts/dev/prova-de-restauracao-env.spec.ts. documents.t: In a real installation (09/14) the dev agents "did not get past started the task". The event log had dev.started followed by dev.blocked_by_container, with the reason spelled out (RN-502). The team tree (timeline-tree.ts) had no translation for the block — what is not in TRADUCAO is discarded —, so the branch stopped at the previous milestone and the present sentence asserted work about a stopped agent. The team panel, on the same execution screen, already said aguardando for the same event (DEV_STATUS_EVENTS, RN-411): two screens, two tables, and only one of them was covered by the comparison with the engine's vocabulary. The rule, in three parts: Every dev.* type the engine emits has a decision in the tree — translated in TRADUCAO or declared in TRADUCAO_FORA with the reason (empty today). Omitting stopped being possible: scripts/ci/vocabulario-de-eventos-dev.spec.ts derives the engine's vocabulary through the same extractor as the event inventory and fails, naming the type, whatever is missing; and it also fails a translated dev.* type the engine does not emit. On the first round it found TWO missing (dev.blocked_by_container and dev.error) and ONE extra (dev.rearmed, which the api writes with actor user and which is why it never reached any branch — the tree only hangs milestones of actor agent). Whether a dev agent's last milestone is work in progress is not decided in the tree. For a dev.* milestone, the branch only stays ACTIVE when the panel gives trabalhando to the same event (statusDoEventoDev, read from DEV_STATUS_EVENTS). aguardando, ocioso, falhou and travado leave the branch stopped — and with them dev.idle, dev.blocked, dev.awaiting_gate, dev.awaiting_approval and dev.idle_tripped, which before also counted as active. A dev.* type the panel did not decide does NOT become active: when in doubt the screen does not assert work. The container block is its own milestone (espera, color warning, the same as the gate), with the engine's reason as detail — it is what says what to do. And dev.started stops saying "started the task": measured in the engine, it goes out on RECEIVING the order to work, before try_claim (DevAgentServer.handle_cast(:work)); it now says "looking for a task", and what asserts the task is dev.working, which now shows its title. What this rule does NOT do, and why: container.start_failed does not enter the tree. It is the reason for the block, but the actor is system (action-executor): hanging it on a dev agent's branch would be inventing authorship, and the only other place in the structure, the tronco, IS NOT RENDERED by any consumer (measured: AgentTimelineTree and the Activities section of the Shell only read ramos). The event stays in the chronological log, one click away, and the blocked branch already says, through the reason, that the container needs to be started. The tree's labels stayed in fixed pt-BR in this fix — migrating them was a change to the whole screen. AT-134 did that migration later, and it did NOT touch the rule above: the DECISION per type (whether it becomes a node, which MarcoTipo, which detail) stays in TRADUCAO, in the code, and it is what the spec compares with the engine; only the TEXT left, as a KEY (ChaveDeRotulo) resolved in executors:timelineTree.label.*, with the present sentence in timelineTree.now.* and the origin detail in timelineTree.detail.origin, in both languages (en is the default, RN-425). montarArvore receives the language as an argument (getFixedT), and the two consumers (AgentTimelineTree and the Activities section of the Shell) pass it from useTranslation — switching language rebuilds the tree. A key the table uses without text in one of the two locales fails in timeline-tree.test.ts. documents.t: In a real installation of v6.1.0 (AT-085), the wizard preselected mounted — install.sh always writes BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, and with a known base RN-513 preselected the mode. But the installation by Release has no container broker (the image is not published, decision 7 of ADR 0150), and container/mounted only start a container through the broker (RN-503). Result: six dev.blocked_by_container and two container.start_failed — nobody works on the project, forever (RN-502). The rule (ADR 0161): The api says whether there is a broker, on the route the wizard already reads. GET workspaces/:workspaceId/projects-base now returns brokerConfigurado next to projectsBase — the same question ("what mode does this INSTALLATION execute?"), the same minimum (maintainer), no new route. The source is ContainerBrokerPort.configurado(), the same as the read of the observed state. It says BROKER_URL exists, never that the broker answers. Three states, which do not collapse. Broker confirmed: RN-513 intact. Confirmed absence: container and mounted stay on the screen, inert (the control leaves, the information stays — RN-102), the reason is stated ONCE in text below the cards, and runner is the preselected one. I don't know (loading, failing query, absent field): does not become "it has" — mounted is NOT preselected, the revision of RN-513 — and also does not become "it doesn't have": no card locks and nothing is asserted in text; container stays selected, as before. The human choice does not point to what does not run. Whoever clicked a mode before the answer arrived, and the answer confirms it does not execute here, falls to runner — the same rule that already knocked mounted down when the base disappears. What this rule does NOT close: the mode conversion (RN-559) still offers container/mounted in an installation without a broker; the installer does not ask whether to turn the broker on, because its image cannot be obtained by a Release installation (measured — see ADR 0161); and in the development compose, which brings up the broker by default (RN-512) but leaves BROKER_URL empty until someone puts it in .env, the warning shows up — and it is right, because without the variable the api never calls the broker. documents.t: The same installation of AT-085 allowed approving, through the containers page (RN-521), two container_start that could only end failed with BrokerIndisponivelError. The page already refused locally what it knew would fail — no image, runner without a confirmed folder, role below maintainer — and did not know about this one. The rule (ADR 0161): The list says whether there is a broker, on every row. GET workspaces/:workspaceId/containers gains brokerConfigurado per row, with the SAME value in all of them, read ONCE per load — it is the installation's configuration, and swapping the list for an envelope would break the contract. A fourth refusal reason, sem_broker_na_instalacao, for container and mounted when brokerConfigurado !== true ("I don't know" does not become "it has"). It comes right after "already up" and BEFORE "no image decided": in an installation with nobody to start the container, telling to decide the image would be pointing to the wrong door. The text says what (this installation does not start containers for these two modes), why (no broker, empty BROKER_URL) and what is not affected (runner). runner never falls into it. What depends on the broker is decided by the SAME branching by destination of acaoDeSubidaDoModo (usaBroker), not by a second rule. What this rule does NOT close: stop and remove did not get the refusal (without a broker there is no registered container/mounted container up to stop, and the case was not measured), and the Infra Lead still does not know about an absent broker — it refuses by MODE (RN-566), and proposing container_start in an installation without a broker remains possible by the agent. documents.t: In an installation by Release, a container or mounted project never executed: what starts the container of those two modes is the broker (ADR 0144), and the installation did not have the service because the image was not published (ADR 0150, decision 7). ADR 0162 publishes the image as the fifth and puts the service in the installation compose, OFF; this rule is what decides when it turns on, because turning it on hands the machine's Docker socket to an installation service. The rule: Only a typed "s"/"sim" turns it on. The question comes after the base (the broker's second root derives from it) and before the .env, and SAYS in text what it grants — this machine's Docker socket, and that whoever commands the broker commands Docker — and what contains it. Enter, any other answer and the lack of a terminal leave it off, and the lack of a terminal is STATED, never decided silently. While the answer is not yes, Docker is not touched. The socket's group is MEASURED, from inside a container, with the broker's own image, no network, read-only rootfs and the socket mounted by --mount type=bind — which refuses a nonexistent source instead of creating a folder on the host, as -v would. It is the gid seen from inside that group_add needs (in Docker Desktop the host's says nothing). A measurement that fails, a path that is not a socket or a gid that is not a number are a named REFUSAL, which teaches to run again answering no — never the compose default's 999. The four lines go together or none goes: COMPOSE_PROFILES=container-broker, BROKER_URL=http://broker:8090, DOCKER_GID and PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT. A profile without a URL brings up a broker nobody calls; a URL without a profile points the api to a service that does not come up. escrever_env refuses to write the block without the measured gid — a defect of the script, not of the machine. BRABO_BROKER_IMAGE is ALWAYS written, on or not: Compose interpolates the whole file before filtering by profile. The managed folder's root is COMPUTED and then CHECKED. Before startup, <DockerRootDir>/volumes/brabo_project_workspaces/_data; after, compared with the volume's Mountpoint. Diverging, or the api not reaching the broker over the internal network, becomes a named PENDING item at the end — never a refusal, which would take down an installation that is up because of a step fixed by editing the .env. The decision shows up in the final summary, in both directions, and the sentence about what the installer does NOT do stops saying that only the Mounted folder stays without a container: container does too. What this rule does NOT close: the DOCKER_GID and the computed root were not measured on Docker Desktop for macOS, and the tag's E2E runs the interactive half only on Linux. Rootless or remote Docker does not have the socket at /var/run/docker.sock, which is the path the compose mounts, and falls into the refusal of item 2 — turning the broker on there is not offered by another path. documents.t: In a real installation (AT-088, 2026-09-14), a project without a repository — project_repositories, project_git_connections and repo_bootstraps empty — received three open_adr_pr from the Arquiteto and one open_infra_pr from the Infra Lead. The human approved all four, and all four ended failed with "Projeto sem repositório provisionado" (ExecuteAdrPrUseCase, ExecuteInfraPrUseCase). The person approved four actions that could only fail. It is not an edge, it is the common case. Since RN-541 creating a project does not create a repository, and the repository's trigger is accepting the handoff from the Arquiteto to the Dev Lead (RN-522). The Arquiteto works BEFORE that handoff — so in a new project every open_adr_pr failed by construction. The rule: both tools ask, BEFORE proposing, whether the project has a repository, and without it they REFUSE with a NAMED reason — what is missing, and when it comes to exist. The proposed_action is not born, and the approval queue does not receive what cannot succeed. The mold is that of RN-566, with no new rule and without touching the prompt. The refusal is a tool result (RN-163), an input to the loop — never agent.error, never end of turn —, and the model continues the turn reading the reason. The read is LOCAL, and the predicate is the SAME as the execution's. The engine already read project_repositories directly from Postgres (Engine.Projects.ProjectRepository, the consumers of default_branch/1 and remoto_de_trabalho/1), so there was no HTTP in the agent's loop to measure or justify: the new question, recusa_de_pr_sem_repositorio/2, is the SAME one ProvisionedRepositoryRepository.findByProjectId asks in the two use cases — there is a row for the project. If the two diverged, the tool would let through what the execution refuses, or would refuse what it would accept. Both tools use the SAME function, with the same text. In the Infra Lead the question comes before the HALT. propose_infra_pr does not propose on the spot: it interrupts the turn so finalize/3 runs the WorkflowsAgent and consolidates into a single PR. Refusing after that (in abrir_pr/3) would have spent a whole LLM loop and recorded two completed delegations for a PR that cannot exist. The refusal happens at the interception, and the turn CONTINUES. A durable trace in both. AT-048 found that a local refusal left no trace in the event log; RN-566 solved it by emitting the tool.call before the refusal, and here the same holds — in the Arquiteto dispatch_tool/2 already emitted it; in the Infra Lead the interception of propose_infra_pr emitted nothing and now emits, in the refusal branch, with the title and the PATHS (never the files' content). And the WHY goes along: a tool.result with ok: false and erro with the reason — the form the Criativo already uses —, because only the tool.call would say the call existed, not why it did not become a proposal. On the path that proposes nothing changes: its trace remains the proposed_action itself. The execution use cases keep refusing as before — defense in depth: the agent's refusal is a layer BEFORE, never in its place. What this rule does NOT decide: WHERE the repository should be born. The refusal text describes the current trigger, and it CHANGED: AT-092 was decided in RN-582 (ADR 0165) — the repository is born on accepting the handoff TO the Arquiteto, before its first turn, with the acceptance to the Dev Lead as a second door. The text changed along with it, as this rule promised: it names the new trigger and, since the Arquiteto only works after that acceptance, says the refusal means a FAILED provisioning (the repository.provision_failed) or a project prior to the rule, with the two ways out. It stopped being the common case; the refusal remains, because those two situations exist. open_infra_pr is also affected in a new project by another path (the Infra Lead is triggered by the Arquiteto's handoff, which can happen before the handoff to the Dev Lead); this rule only makes the proposal not be born, it does not reorder the handoffs. documents.t: The six conversational agents (Criativo, PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead, UX Designer and Staff) rebuild the history from the event log in init/1 — on restart and also when they come up in a session that already has a conversation (the PO at the Criativo's handoff). Measured on 09/13 (AT-073, against b61bc49cd), the six had the SAME copy of rehydrate/2, with three defects: They read the beginning. EngineApiClient.list_events/2 asks for limit=200 without latest, and the internal route — which did not even accept latest — returns the FIRST 200. In a conversation of 201 events the agent woke up without the message it was answering. The screen had already solved this with latest: true and a cut warning (RN-180); the engine had not inherited it. They rebuilt only chat.message and agent.response. The question asked via a form (chat.structured_question) and the tools called (tool.call/tool.result) disappeared. They cut silently. And the kickoff reads (PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead, UX Designer) and those of the product_brief rules (Criativo) filtered in memory the same FIRST 200 events of all types: in a long conversation with the Criativo, the brief was born after event 200 and the PO received "(no product brief available)". The rule: A single path. Engine.Agents.Reidratacao replaces the six copies; the six servers call historico/3 in init/1. The tail, with ADR 0060's ceiling. The read is latest=true&limit=200 — the route's MAX_LIMIT, neither more (the api would cut) nor less (it would leave out what it delivers for free). The ceiling did NOT become unlimited. What comes in. chat.message and agent.response as always (from any agent of the session — it is what the PO inherits from the Criativo); chat.structured_question as the agent's speech, with labels and options; tool.call/tool.result of the agent ITSELF as a text note with the tool, the arguments (cut at 1,500 characters) and the outcome — never as a role: "tool" message, because the event does not keep the call's id and a tool_result without the matching tool_use is refused by the provider. chat.structured_question_answered is left OUT on purpose: the api writes the same answers in a chat.message right after (AnswerStructuredQuestionUseCase reuses SendAgentMessageUseCase), and rehydrating both would duplicate the answer. The beginning that did not fit is stated, with the number. The seq is gapless and starts at 1, so the number of omitted events is the seq of the tail's first one minus one — SUBTRACTION, without an extra request. When it is greater than zero, the history opens with ONE system message that writes that number and brings the summary of the agent's most recent context compaction (when it was recorded) and the conversation's opening (the first six messages of the first 40 events, cut at 500 characters). Those are two more reads with a ceiling — three in total, and only one when the conversation fits. context.compacted records the summary from now on — summary, agent and messagesSummarized, next to the usual counts. A conversation compacted before this stays DECLARED ("compacted N time(s) before the summary started to be recorded; that summary was lost"), never rebuilt; the old events do not change. An unreadable history does not become an empty conversation. If the read fails, the agent receives a system message saying it could not read the history. Kickoffs and brief refs read BY TYPE, from the tail. The internal route gained types (up to 20, validated; malformed is 400) — a CONTRACT change, additive: without latest/types the response is the one from before. When the read by type hits the ceiling, the kickoff says there may be older items. Measured per agent: all six changed in rehydration (init/1). In the kickoffs, PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead and UX Designer changed; the Criativo changed in the product_brief refs and in the zero-rule guardrail; the Staff has no kickoff (ADR 0088). What this rule does NOT close: the text the tool returned was not in the log — closed by RN-589, from then on (an old session stays without it). InfraLeadServer (which rehydrates via Reidratacao.historico/3 since AT-150, without its own copy) and DevLeadTools.run_assessment/2 (which reads the TAIL, latest with the same 200 ceiling) also go through the common path; no reader of list_events/2 without latest remains in apps/engine/lib. Rehydration can bring MORE than the live context had (the whole tail, even what had already been compacted); the ContextManager compacts again on the next turn. documents.t: In a real installation of v6.1.0 (2026-09-14), answering the Criativo's questions form took 97.3 s, confirming readiness 97.3 s and confirming architecture ready 51.8 s — each click held by the agent's WHOLE turn, because the conversational's handle_call only answered the engine controller's GenServer.call when the turn's Task ended. A turn above the ceiling (120 s in the Criativo, 180 s in the others) became a 500 on a command that had worked. And the refusal of a second message with a turn in progress ({:error, :turno_em_andamento}) was discarded by the controller, which answered 202: a "Continue" typed during the Arquiteto's kickoff was accepted and never read, with no trace at all. The rule (ADR 0163, which generalizes ADR 0086): The acceptance goes out right away. TurnoAssincrono.iniciar/3 answers :ok to the from as soon as the Task comes up — after persisting agent.status: working, never before. It holds for the six conversational agents and for the four user routes that trigger a turn (…/agents/:agent/message and, through it, …/structured-question/:id/answer; …/readiness; …/agents/arquiteto/handoff-infra) and for returning a story (ReturnStoryUseCase). The api's status and body do NOT change (201 { ok: true }): they always meant "accepted"; what changed is when they arrive. The refusal BEFORE the turn comes up is synchronous and named. The engine answers 409 (turno_em_andamento, aguardando_aprovacao) or 422 (sem_regra_de_negocio) with {error, motivo}, and the api passes on the SAME status with the SAME sentence. turno_em_andamento gets a durable agent.error (origin politica); the other two already had one. The turn's outcome goes through the channel and the log, never through HTTP. A failure stays a durable agent.error, with the same origin as before. The screen stops treating "the call resolved" as end of turn. After the acceptance, it follows the end through the channel (agent.done) and, as a safety net, through the log's tail every 4 s: it closes when that agent's most recent persisted agent.status is not working. Without any agent.status of the agent in the window, it does not close — not knowing is not "it ended". The handoff to the Dev Lead keeps being born AFTER the Infra one. The :offer_dev_handoff that arrives with the Arquiteto's closing turn in progress stays pending and runs when the turn closes — success, failure, crash or cancellation. (Superseded by RN-672: the Arquiteto no longer offers to the Dev Lead, and the pending item ceased to exist.) What this rule does NOT close: the chat.message the api writes before asking the engine stays in the log when the engine refuses (now explained by the agent.error, before orphaned and mute); an engine restarted in the middle of the turn does not write idle, and the strip stays until "Stop" or a reload; and a message to infra via the composer fell to the Criativo through the final clause of AgentCommandController.message/2 — pre-existing, measured here and closed later by RN-584, which removed the default recipient. Revised for the MESSAGE by RN-673 (ADR 0191): the user's message that arrives with a turn in progress no longer receives turno_em_andamento — it enters the agent's queue and is read at the end of the turn. The refusal of item 2 still holds for the commands that are not speech (review, readiness, handoff offer). documents.t: The installation measured in AT-093 (v6.1.0, 09/14) showed ONE browser making 7,088 requests in 56 minutes — median of 118/min, peak of 263/min — against the 300/min of RATE_LIMIT_USER. Two visible tabs at the peak exceed the ceiling, and the 429 lands in the account owner's browser. Almost everything was a 3–5s poll from the Session screen over data that rarely changes (actions, handoffs and backlog came back 304 99% of the time), while the screen already kept the session:<id> channel with the engine open. The ceiling does NOT change: what drops is the request. The rule: The engine announces every confirmed write. The facade Engine.Sessions.EngineApiClient emits event.appended (only type and actorId, never the payload) after the api CONFIRMS append_event, append_event_returning, propose_action (proposed_action.created), create_handoff (handoff.offered) and create_epic/story/task (backlog.*_created). A refused write does not announce. Before, only ArtifactEmitter and the Infra Lead announced, by hand — and they announced even when the api refused the append. Since AT-157, the write the API does on its own also announces — the decision of a human in another tab, a session transition, the chat answered by the api's own model. AppendSessionEventUseCase and SendChatMessageUseCase (the only two points that write to session_events without going through the engine) call SessionChannelNotifier.eventAppended, which asks the engine POST /internal/sessions/:id/event-appended; the engine does the SAME event.appended (only type and actorId). The announcement goes out AFTER the commit of the outermost transaction (aposCommit in DrizzleUnitOfWork): an undone transaction does not announce, and announcing from inside it would make the web fetch before the event exists. A write that came from the engine (an /internal/* route, marked by OrigemEngineMiddleware) is NOT announced again by the api — the facade already announced. It is best effort and is not awaited: a lost announcement never fails the write, and the 15s fallback covers it. It is only those two points: another use case that starts writing to session_events without AppendSessionEventUseCase needs to call the notifier too. "Channel alive" is a CONFIRMED join. connectSessionHeartbeat marks the session alive on the join's ok and unmarks it on error/close of the channel or the socket and on cleanup. The state is per session and per tab, outside React, because the interval belongs to each OBSERVER and three observers (Shell, SessionPage, ContextAside) read the same events key. With the channel alive, the poll becomes a fallback. Events, actions, handoffs, backlog and the session itself go from 3–5s to 15s; the budget, from 5s to 30s. intervaloDaSessao is Math.max: whoever already polled slower does not speed up. A dropped channel brings back the short interval RIGHT AWAY — the screen never gets worse than it was. The announcement's TYPE decides what to invalidate, with a window. Every announcement invalidates the events and the budget; proposed_action.*/action.* also the actions, handoff.* the handoffs, backlog.* the backlog. Each target has a minimum window between two fetches (events 3s, actions/handoffs/backlog 2s, budget 10s): the first goes out right away, the following ones within the window become ONE at its end. Without that, a burst of tool.result would become one fetch per event. The rule of finding C remains, and only for the EVENTS: during a streaming turn they are not anticipated; the actions are. A hidden tab does not poll. refetchIntervalInBackground: false (TanStack v5's default, now written in OPCOES_PADRAO_DAS_QUERIES) — measured by test, not assumed. An empty body has a validator. A handler returning null went out with an empty body and WITHOUT an ETag (Express's res.send only generates an ETag with a body), so a 304 was impossible: sessions/:id/budget came back 304 in 0% of the 483 measured calls and execution/session in 22% (the time with active execution). The api writes the empty body's ETag when send goes out without a body — decided on what goes over the wire, not on the handler's value, so that a handler with @Res() that writes later never inherits the empty one's validator. A 304 does NOT reduce the rate limit count (the guard counts before the handler); it reduces bandwidth. It composes with following the turn through the log's tail (RN-578). The ACCEPTED turn keeps being followed by reading the tail every 4s (acompanharTurnoPeloLog) — it is the net against the lost agent.done, and the channel's announcement can be lost along with it, so the tick does NOT become a 15s fallback. What changes: the event.appended of the FOLLOWED agent's agent.status runs the read RIGHT AWAY (avisoPedeVerificacaoDoTurno), and the turn closes as soon as the log says it closed, without waiting for the tick. An announcement from another agent, of another type, or without a followed turn reads nothing extra. And the 3s poll of events stays PAUSED during streaming (findings 2/7): intervaloDaSessao only holds when the pause does not, and invalidation through the channel respects the same rule of finding C. Numbers (budget test, one tab on the Session screen, per minute): 123 with the channel down (the behavior from before, intact as a fallback) and 46 with it alive — of which 24 are from the Shell (projects summary and execution session, which do not belong to the session and stay at 5s). Two tabs: 246 → 92. Since RN-632 (AT-278) the PROJECT reads poll at the project pace (15s) and the Executors and Overview tabs go through the SAME criarInvalidadorDoCanal — the measurement with the real screens and two tabs lives there. What this rule does NOT close: the announcement of the write the api does on its own (item 1, AT-157) is best effort — if the engine is out or the announcement is lost, the screen gets there through the fallback, within 15s (it was 3s); the announcement goes to the engine node that received the call, and the Phoenix PubSub broadcast delivers it to subscribers on any node of the cluster (not measured in a cluster). The roster's working status still depends on the event.appended of the agent.status, which goes out after the api writes it. projects-summary and execution/session (Shell) stay at 5s. During an accepted turn, RN-578's 4s tail read adds up to 15 req/min, only while the turn lasts. It is not a consistency model change (no ADR): the source remains the GET, the channel remains only a trigger — as it already was since Phase 4a —, and what changes is the maximum latency of writes without an announcement.
