documents.t: In exp001 the heartbeat closed the session 30 seconds after the tab stopped, with the Criativo having just asked — and the event log kept receiving events for four minutes after closed_at. Two defects, one on each side of the closing: none of the pending-work signals of RN-064 saw a conversation waiting for the user (a Criativo that finished its turn is idle, without a handoff, without an action, without dev.*), and nothing — neither the events funnel, nor the conversation use cases, nor the engine — looked at the session's state before writing. The rule, on the heartbeat side: A conversation waiting for the user is pending work. It is the FIFTH signal of pending-work: the session's most recent end-of-turn event (agent.response, chat.structured_question or agent.error on the agent's side; chat.message or chat.structured_question_answered on the user's side) is the AGENT's, and the actor is a conversational one. agent.error counts as end of turn on purpose: by RN-059 the agent says in the thread what happened, and the next move is the user's. Speech from someone who does not converse (Psicólogo, dev agent) does not hold. It is the only signal with a CEILING: 8 hours, counted from the END of the agent's turn (the created_at of that event), not from the last heartbeat. The api returns the instant (aguardandoUsuarioDesde) and the engine applies the ceiling (SESSION_CONVERSATION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 28800000). Past it, the session closes closed with its OWN cause, conversation_idle_timeout — not heartbeat_timeout, because whoever reads termination_reason (the Psicólogo, a per-session metric) needs to separate the tab that vanished from the conversation nobody resumed. The TerminationClassifier reads it as :timeout: the api knows six causes in the hypotheses, and opening a seventh would be changing that contract. The ceiling also holds with the tab OPEN (AT-152): the SessionServer has its own clock (:conversation_idle_check, every 5 min — no environment variable, only the test hook :session_conversation_idle_check_ms), independent of the heartbeat — the tab's ping neither resets nor postpones it. On each round it reads the pending item and only CLOSES by ceiling (same cause, conversation_idle_timeout); api down, no pending item or a pending item without an instant only reschedule, because what closes due to api down is still the heartbeat. Before, the ceiling was only checked when the heartbeat expired, and an open tab (ping every ~10s) made it unreachable: an immortal session. A signal without a ceiling wins. With an offered handoff, a pending action, an agent in a turn or a dev agent working, the instant comes back null and the session stays without a ceiling, as it always did. That is why the signal is the LAST in the list. A present and unreadable instant is an ERROR, never nil. nil with pending: true is a pending item without a ceiling; a broken format would become an immortal session. As an error, it falls into the api-down path — it closes by heartbeat, saying why. The rule, on the closed session side: A closed/closed_abnormally session refuses a CONVERSATION event with a NAMED 409: { message, reason: "sessao_encerrada", status, type }. closing still accepts — the lock is on TERMINAL state. "Conversation" has two clauses, and both are necessary. The TYPE only exists as conversation (chat.message, chat.structured_question[_answered], agent.status, agent.activated, handoff.offered/accepted, readiness.confirmed, necessity.validated, architecture.readiness_confirmed), OR the ACTOR is a conversational agent (the six plus dev-lead and infra). An ALLOWLIST by type was measured and refused: those who legitimately write to a closed session are the CONSUMERS of the closing — the Psicólogo runs a ToolLoop against it and writes tool.call, agent.response, agent.error; the Anamnese writes its own outcomes —, and they speak the SAME generic vocabulary as the Criativo. The type is the same; who differs is the actor. The human decision about an action keeps coming in. action.approved/ action.denied and the execution outcomes are not conversation: the action is an item of a DURABLE queue that survives the session, and refusing the decision would leave a pending item impossible to resolve. The normal case does not even get here (a pending action holds the session, signal 2 of RN-064); it only exists when the session died through another door. The refusal leaves no trace. The state comes from the SAME UPDATE that reserves the seq (with no extra query on the hottest path, under the same row lock as the transition), and the refusal throws inside the transaction: the increment comes back, the seq stays without a hole. The human chat, which writes chat.message without the funnel, has the same lock. The use cases with an effect BEFORE the event refuse before the effect: CreateHandoff before creating the row, AcceptHandoff before marking accepted (which would activate the next agent), ActivateAgent before calling the engine. The closing STOPS the conversational agents. SessionLifecycleWorker, through which every closing goes (heartbeat, idle conversation, human, crash), stops the session's conversational agents on ALL nodes (Engine.Agents.Conversacionais, via :erpc — the registry is local and the job lands on any replica). The turn in progress is ABANDONED in the terminate/2 of the six servers (TurnoAssincrono.abandonar/1): the task dies without writing or broadcasting anything, because writing would be asking the api for what it refuses. There is no answer to give: since RN-578 (ADR 0163) whoever triggered the turn already received :ok on acceptance. For the same reason the offer_dev_handoff the Arquiteto kept for the turn's closing does NOT run when the closing is the session's — the handoff would be refused (since RN-672 there is nothing to keep anymore: the handoff to the Dev Lead comes from the Infra). The Infra Lead, which runs the turn inside handle_call, is killed if it does not exit within 5s. The refusal is never silent in the engine. Almost every caller of append_event/3 discards the return; the client logs the 409 sessao_encerrada as a warning, and the return stays the same. The screen recognizes the 409 by the CODE and says the session closed (AT-154). ehRecusaDeSessaoEncerrada checks status === 409 AND body.reason === "sessao_encerrada" — never the text, and never only the 409, which is also "turn in progress". In the four conversation actions (send a message, answer a structured question, confirm the readiness of the Criativo and of the Arquiteto) the screen shows its own sentence instead of the generic error, redoes the session read (it is the new status that makes the composer disappear) and does NOT lose what was typed: the message goes back to the draft and shows up read-only in place of the composer, and the form's answers stay in the fields. The sentence does not promise "Reopen" — the action does not exist. And the "Close" button stays inert in BOTH terminal states (sessaoEhTerminal, the mirror of isTerminal), not only in closed (AT-155). What this rule does NOT close: the ceiling is only checked when the HEARTBEAT expires — with the tab open and sending heartbeats, the session stays alive without a ceiling, as always (whoever is looking is not an idle conversation). The stateless human chat's answer to a turn that STARTED with the session open comes in even if it closes midway (the actor is the model, and the spend has already been measured). deploy/k8s/ does not carry SESSION_CONVERSATION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, and since AT-153 that is a DECISION written in the engine's Deployment, not a pending item: there nothing intercepts the environment, the absence is the runtime.exs default, and writing the number would make a second copy with no guard against diverging — changing the ceiling there is an env: item in the overlay's engine patch. The THREE composes map it with the code's default (the installation one only since AT-153, and until then the line in an installation's .env was inert), guarded by scripts/ci/teto-ocioso-nos-composes.spec.ts. Since AT-154 the screen handles the 409 with its own sentence (item 11); the screen's other actions that write to a closed session keep showing the api's message. documents.t: RN-001 said the terminal states have no way out. Since ADR 0183 there is ONE, and only one: the reopening, from closed or closed_abnormally to active, through its own path. The GENERIC transition keeps refusing closed → active with 409, and closing → active remains forbidden through any path. What comes back is the whole session. The event log is not touched — the conversation, the business rules, the answered questions, the handoff offers and acceptances. A conversational agent stopped at closing comes back through the idempotent start_agent on the first message and rebuilds the history (RN-580). The conversation comes in again because the refusal of RN-581 reads the session's state, which is now active. The previous closing is not erased. The sessions row loses closed_at and termination_reason; the NEW event session.reopened, in the same seq (RN-002) and with the human actor who reopened, carries {from, to, closedAt, terminationReason}. No event is edited nor renumbered, and the kind does not change (RN-097). A session with execution does not reopen — 409 sessao_com_execucao. Reopening a session with execution.activated would return it to findActiveExecutionSession (RN-139). The owner's decision, confirmed in ADR 0184. No deadline. Every closed session is reopenable (the owner's decision, ADR 0184). The engine is called before the transaction, as in activation: its failure leaves the session closed, with no event. Any non-terminal state is 409 sessao_nao_encerrada. The closing the reopening undid does not stop the live session. The SessionLifecycleWorker reads the session's status and ignores, with a log, the session.closed/session.closed_abnormally job of a session the api already says is non-terminal. The Psicólogo's second automatic analysis stays blocked by the alreadyAnalyzed that already existed; manual reprocessing continues. The second graph consolidation extends the window of the same Interacao. documents.t: POST projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId/reopen requires developer — the SAME role as the generic transition that closes the session: whoever can declare it finished can bring it back. It answers 200 with the session. viewer is 403. ADR 0183 had set maintainer as a provisional default; the owner decided developer on 2026-09-30 (ADR 0184), confirming along with it the other two decisions — no deadline, and a session with execution.activated refused. On the Session screen, the closed session's strip shows "Reopen session" with a sentence about what comes back. Below developer (roleAtLeast, WORKSPACE role — the gap of RN-471 already declared on the screen) the button stays inert and the reason is stated in TEXT. The api's refusal (409 for a session with execution, 403) becomes a toast with its sentence. The thread narrates session.reopened as "session reopened", with the cause of the previous closing when it was recorded. documents.t: It revises the TRIGGER of RN-522, which fulfilled the promise of RN-541. The mechanism does not change — the same ProvisionRepositoryUseCase, called by the same AcceptHandoffUseCase, always local, with the failure becoming repository.provision_failed and never taking down the acceptance. Structural decision in ADR 0165. What the real installation showed (AT-092, v6.1.0, 2026-09-14). The Arquiteto proposed open_adr_pr three times before the repository existed; the handoffs to infra and dev-lead were offered together, only the infra one was accepted, and POST /projects/:id/execution/activate answered 201. The tables project_repositories, project_git_connections and repo_bootstraps stayed empty — the project without a repository forever. Two defects: the trigger came AFTER those who need the repository (Arquiteto and Infra Lead write to it before the Dev Lead), and the only trigger was SKIPPABLE (activating execution does not require accepting to the Dev Lead). 1. The trigger is accepting the handoff to arquiteto. The Arquiteto is only activated by an accepted handoff addressed to it (canActivateAgent), and that handoff is born from the PO (offer_handoff(to_agent: "arquiteto")) or from the user (manual handoff) — both doors go through the same acceptance. Provisioning runs BEFORE activateAgent: the Arquiteto wakes up in a project that already has somewhere to write. Consequence: the Infra Lead, activated by a handoff FROM the Arquiteto, never again wakes up without a repository. 2. Accepting to dev-lead keeps provisioning, as a SECOND DOOR. It is the way out for a project that went through the Arquiteto before this rule (the exp001 of AT-092: Arquiteto accepted, Dev Lead offered) and the natural resumption of a provisioning that failed at the acceptance to the Arquiteto. With the created repository already up, the second call creates nothing — no repository, no session, no bootstrap row, no branch, no commit —, and that is proven by BOTH doors in sequence against the real Postgres and LocalGitProvider. 3. execution/activate without a repository is REFUSED with 409, right after the module_map check and BEFORE any effect (persisted budget, permissions.json, session, engine, event). The sentence is chosen by the state of the project's handoffs, read by HandoffRepository.findByProject (from all sessions — the handoff to the Arquiteto lives in the PO's): handoff to the Arquiteto offered → accept it; otherwise to the Dev Lead offered → accept it; otherwise one of the two already accepted → provisioning left no repository, see the repository.provision_failed and use the provisioning page (/projects/:id/provisioning?provider=local); otherwise → no handoff to the Arquiteto was accepted. A handoff offered to ANOTHER agent never becomes an acceptance instruction (accepting the Infra provisions nothing). An ADOPTED repository counts as a repository. Refusing and not provisioning here is a decision: provisioning inside activation would hide a git effect, and the agents before it would remain without a repository. 4. The screen removes the control and states the reason once, in text (the rule of RN-102 and ADR 0064). In the Execution section of the Overview, with GET .../git/repository answering a CONFIRMED null, "Activate execution" stays inert in place, the text says where the repository is born, and there is a link to provision. On the card of the handoff to the Dev Lead, inside the session, the "Activate execution" shortcut leaves and the card says that accepting that handoff provisions the repository. Loading or with an error, nothing locks — "I don't know" does not become "it doesn't have", and the backend refuses anyway. Accepting a handoff invalidates the repository query, because the acceptance may have created it. The technical session does not displace the working one (AT-131). The session the provisioning opens (repo_bootstraps.session_id, named git-bootstrap) is born in the MIDDLE of the Arquiteto's phase, and choosing "the most recent" only by createdAt put it in place of the working session until the next one was born (ADR 0165 left that declared). Now the two reads by createdAt of the workspace summary (latestSessionId and the cut of the unread ones) order by "is a bootstrap session" BEFORE createdAt, and the Overview (useLatestSession) does the same. The technical one is only the most recent when it is the ONLY one — in the manual provisioning flow it is in it that the project starts. The api reads the marker through repo_bootstraps; the web only has the session's NAME, and renaming it makes the two diverge (the Overview then treats the summary as being of another session and does not use it). The criterion does not change what ADR 0165 decided (where the repository is born), which is why there is no new ADR. Revised by RN-592 (AT-183): the web stopped reading the NAME — the session listing returns the technical marker, through the same link in repo_bootstraps, and renaming the session no longer makes the two diverge. The activation refusal does not tell to accept a handoff from a closed session (RN-581, AT-131). Accepting a handoff in a terminal session is 409 sessao_encerrada, checked BEFORE the handoff becomes accepted — so nothing is half provisioned. The refusal sentence now queries the state of the session of each offered handoff: only the one living in an OPEN session becomes "accept it"; if the only offered one is in a closed session, the sentence says so and points to the provisioning page. A session not found counts as open ("I don't know" does not become "closed"). The events provisioning writes do not fall under RN-581: the actor is system and the destination is the freshly created git-bootstrap session. What remains NOT covered: the Overview and the handoff card in the session read the state of the repository, not that of each session, and did not change. documents.t: The last clause of EngineWeb.AgentCommandController.message/2 did not look at the agent: it matched ANY name the clauses above had not caught and delivered the message to the Criativo. A message written to infra was read by another agent, the click answered 202, and the Criativo answered in the thread — nothing broke, and nobody saw. Found as an adjacency of RN-578 (AT-089) and fixed here (AT-098). The measurement, before the fix (the three sides, on dev at 72ee8cdcf): Destination Does the screen offer it? Does the api accept it? Did the engine have a clause? criativo yes (composer: the creative session's fallback and AGENTES_DE_CHAT) yes NO — it was the final clause, without a guard po, arquiteto, dev-lead, ux-designer, staff yes (AGENTES_DE_CHAT, the most recent agent.activated) yes yes, one each infra not in the composer (out of AGENTES_DE_CHAT since the 9-fix finding and RN-499) yes no — it fell to the Criativo any other name in the roster (qa, subagents, secops, psicologo…) only through the structured questions form, which answers the ACTOR who asked (agent={event.actor.id}); today only Criativo and PO ask yes no — it fell to the Criativo unknown name, or none no yes (the api does not validate the agent; only the sessionId becomes a checked URL segment, RN-128) no — it fell to the Criativo The rule: Each conversing agent has its OWN clause, the Criativo included ("agent" => "criativo"). The final clause stopped existing as a delivery: it is a REFUSAL. A name without a clause is a NAMED 422, {error, motivo} in the mold of RN-578: agente_sem_conversa, with a sentence that names the agent and says the message was recorded and no agent read it. The api passes on the 422 as UnprocessableEntityException with the SAME sentence (the postComandoDeTurno of RN-578, without new code), and the screen shows it through the mensagemDaRecusaDoAgente that already existed. Without "agent" in the body it is agente_ausente, and a conversing agent without text is mensagem_sem_texto — three reasons, because "does not converse" said to one who converses would be a lie. infra has its OWN refusal, with a sentence that says what it does: it works by proposal (the infra PR, starting the container), and what asks for a decision shows up in Approvals. It is not missing code, it is the same reading as RN-499 — the Infra Lead is propositional. And the user_message/2 that InfraLeadServer still exports does not serve for a clause: it runs the WHOLE turn inside handle_call (up to 180 s), without the acceptance of ADR 0163 and without "Stop" (via_for/2 does not know it). Wiring it would give back to the click the wait RN-578 removed. "Stop" also does not guess. cancel/2 without "agent" stopped the Criativo's turn; it becomes 422 agente_ausente. The api always sends the agent on both routes, so those two refusals only reach a broken caller. The screen keeps not offering infra in the composer — no UI change: AGENTES_DE_CHAT already excluded it, and what changed is that, if one day someone puts it there, the engine refuses with a name instead of delivering to another, and the CI guard fails it first. Since RN-617 (ADR 0175), items 3 and 5 no longer hold: the Infra Lead's turn migrated to TurnoAssincrono, and only then did it gain its own message/2 clause, the "Stop"'s via_for/2 and the place in AGENTES_DE_CHAT. Its agente_sem_conversa refusal left; the underlying rule of this RN — no default recipient, every name without a clause refused with a name — is the same. The guard that closes the class lives in scripts/ci/destinos-do-composer.spec.ts, because the destination is born in TypeScript and the clause lives in Elixir — neither of the two suites reads the other language. It DERIVES the destinations from the source (AGENTES_DE_CHAT, the agentParaEnviar = '…' literals of SessionPage.tsx and the roster's AgentKey) and requires: its own conversing clause and the "Stop"'s via_for/2 for each composer destination; no clause without a fixed agent in the head that delivers to an agent; the last clause of message/2 being a refusal; infra out of the composer and with its own refusal; and @agentes_de_conversa equal to the set of clauses that converse. Five mutations measured, all killed (the old catch-all back, infra in AGENTES_DE_CHAT, the Criativo's clause renamed, the Staff's via_for removed, the infra clause renamed). What this rule does NOT close, declared: Whether the Infra Lead comes to converse through the composer was a product decision, without an owner — taken in RN-617 (AT-141): yes. Giving it a clause requires, first, migrating its turn to TurnoAssincrono (the acceptance and the turno_em_andamento refusal of RN-578) and registering it in "Stop"; and requires deciding what a conversation does with an agent whose contract is to propose. Its user_message/2 stays exported and without a caller. The chat.message written by the api before the refusal stays in the log — and since RN-587 the engine writes the refusal's agent.error next to it, so the thread explains itself. The api does not validate the agent. Refusing there, before writing, would require a second list of who converses on the TypeScript side — and diverging it from the clauses is the defect this rule closes. What decides is whoever has the clauses (decision kept in RN-587). documents.t: Since ADR 0163 (RN-578) the turn of the six conversational agents runs in a Task, and the outcome the Task writes — agent.response, or agent.error when the api narrates budget, credential or binding in the final frame — goes out BEFORE the result reaches the agent's GenServer and zeroes turno_assincrono. A test that read the state right after the agent.error failed in ~1 of 4 rounds (AT-099: 8 of 30 measured). The question was whether the SAME window existed for the user: did the screen see the turn end and the next message hear 409 turno_em_andamento? It does not exist, and the rule is what makes it not exist: The two end-of-turn signals only come out of finalizar/1, which runs in the GenServer's process, inside the handle_info that HAS ALREADY zeroed turno_assincrono: agent.done on the channel and a persisted agent.status: idle. They are the two, and only they, that the screen uses to close the turn (onAgentDone and turnoTerminouNoLog, RN-578 item 4). The message from whoever saw one of those signals is served after that handle_info — the GenServer serves one message at a time —, so it finds the agent free and is accepted. What the Task writes is not an end signal. agent.response and agent.error show up in the thread with the turn still open in the agent. A screen or client that started closing the turn by them would reopen the window; emitting agent.done or idle from inside the Task too. There was no behavior change: the order was already this since RN-578. What this RN adds is the order WRITTEN and locked by a test in the six conversational agents — the test stops the GenServer with the Task finished and proves that neither of the two signals came out, without a timeout — and the fix of the PO's test, which now waits for the persisted idle instead of the agent.error. documents.t: Since RN-578 agent.status: working is written BEFORE the acceptance, and the end of the turn (agent.status: idle and agent.done) only comes out of finalizar/1, inside the agent's process (RN-585). If the engine falls in the middle of the turn, the process and the Task die together and nobody writes the end: the agent's last agent.status stays working forever (AT-156, reproduced — bringing up the server again over that log wrote nothing, in all six). The two readers of that signal take it for a turn in progress: the screen (turnoTerminouNoLog, RN-578 item 4) keeps the activity strip, and GetSessionPendingWorkUseCase counts pending work WITHOUT a ceiling (the third signal of RN-064), so the session does not close by heartbeat. Only the user's next message unlocked it, and only because it brings up the agent. The working left without a live turn is closed by a NEW event, never rewritten (an event is immutable): an agent.error with origin infra and reason: turno_interrompido_por_reinicio — the sentence says the engine was restarted, that the turn was not completed and that whoever decides to try again is the user (RN-059: a failure never becomes an empty response) — followed by a persisted agent.status: idle. The channel receives agent.error and agent.done, so the strip of whoever has the screen open goes away without reloading. It holds for those sharing TurnoAssincrono — six originally, seven since RN-617. The turn is NEVER re-executed. Redoing it would spend tokens on behalf of a message the user may have already forgotten, over a rebuilt history; no call to the model happens in the closing. Only each agent's LAST agent.status counts, and only working: idle is already closed, and awaiting_approval (suspended Dev Lead, RN-284) is a pending decision, not a dead turn. "Without a live turn" looks at the cluster, and when in doubt does not close. The agents' registry is local; in a rollout the old pod may be running the turn, and closing it from there would kill a healthy turn. A node that does not answer counts as alive. The drain's session handoff (RN-588, Monitor.expect_handoff/1) belongs to the SessionServer, not to the conversational agents: while the old pod is up its agent stays registered there, and the new pod's sweep sees it; the Adopter does not sweep — what reaches the orphan working after the old pod dies is the agent's init/1. Two entry points, one function (Engine.Agents.TurnoOrfao): the boot sweep in each rehydrated session (Rehydrator, off the readiness path — the boot does not wait for the api), which closes the turn even if nobody sends a message, and each server's init/1, a safety net for when the boot could not write (api still down). A read or write failure is logged and the agent comes up. Declared and not closed: the Infra Lead (infra) runs the turn inside handle_call, without TurnoAssincrono, and is left out — closed in RN-617, which put it in TurnoAssincrono and in TurnoOrfao; the read window is that of the session's 200 most recent agent.status; if the api is down at boot AND nobody wakes the agent, the working stays until its next startup; and the closing does not recover what the turn had already written before the fall. documents.t: The api writes the chat.message BEFORE asking the engine (the engine rebuilds the conversation reading the log, and the message needs to be durable even with it down). When the engine refused, the message stayed in the user's thread looking delivered and the reason lived only in the toast — the screen asserting what the source denied. The two originating RNs left that declared (RN-578, RN-584); this one closes it (AT-132). The measurement, before the fix, per refusal: Refusal Who produces it Durable agent.error next to the chat.message? 409 turno_em_andamento TurnoAssincrono (RN-578) ALREADY YES — emitir_recusa_por_turno_em_andamento/1, with a test 409 aguardando_aprovacao DevLeadServer.handle_call (RN-578) ALREADY YES — reason: "aguardando_aprovacao_de_plano" 422 agente_sem_conversa, mensagem_sem_texto, agente_ausente the controller (RN-584), without a *Server NO — the explanation lived only in the toast The rule: The engine is the source of the refusal AND of the record. The three 422 refusals write agent.error (origin politica, mensagem equal to the 422's sentence, reason equal to the motivo) and broadcast it on the session's channel — the same durable/ephemeral pair as the two 409s. The thread already draws agent.error (SessionPage.tsx, lerFalhaDeTurno), so no screen changed. There is only something to write with a named session. Without projectId/sessionId in the body (a broken caller) the refusal stays only as a response. The actor does not come from the route. infra and the six that converse come in as agent; any other name (which the public route lets through) is the system engine — a typed name never becomes an actor in the log. The chat.message is neither erased nor postponed. An event is immutable, and writing it only after the acceptance would reorder the log: the turn runs in a Task and the agent.response could precede the message it answers (and a failure between the acceptance and the append would run a turn over an unwritten message). The api still does not validate agent, and now that is a decision and not a gap. The validation AT-098 asked for is the engine's 422 refusal, and it is the SINGLE mechanism: the api passes it on (postComandoDeTurno) and the engine records it. A list on the TypeScript side would be the second copy that diverges on the first new agent, and a list GENERATED from the clauses would require parsing Elixir — with no gain for the user, who already sees the message and the explanation in the thread. documents.t: In the rollout, the old pod's drain stops the SessionServer and asks a peer to take over the session (Engine.Shutdown); the peer's init rewrites the row of engine.session_states. The :DOWN of the stopped process, however, reaches the old pod's Engine.Sessions.Monitor by message — and the Monitor is a single GenServer, which serializes each session's :DOWN with one DELETE per trip to the database, without waiting for the next handoff. When the :DOWN was processed AFTER the peer's upsert, the DELETE ... WHERE session_id — which does not look at owner nor generation — took the PEER's row: the session was left with an owner and without a row, invisible to the Adopter, the Rehydrator and the peer's drain's local_sessions/0. If the peer was ANOTHER old pod (.33 → .28 → novo), it did not see it when draining, and its SIGTERM killed it: active in the api and without an owner (AT-078, the rollout-test of propriedades.yml, ~3 orphans in 13 rounds). The rule: the drain marks the stop with Monitor.expect_handoff/1 (the usual expect_stop/1 PLUS "the row is not mine"), and the Monitor does NOT delete the row of a handed-over session — it records in Logger.info that it kept it. Without adoption, what deletes is the drain itself (terminate_unadopted), as it already was; the Monitor keeps deleting the row of every session that dies from another cause and that of the SessionLifecycleWorker's expect_stop/1 (the api has already closed the session). No migration: the row did not gain an owner column, and the mark lives in the Monitor's state, per session. Every deletion by the Monitor now leaves ONE log line with session, node and rows removed — the drain's log never reaches the pod's log (the preStop discards it), the Monitor's does. Inference that remains: the instant the row disappeared was never measured in k3d; the reading comes from the artifact of round 35452845830 (no row + a second old pod) and from the code, and the race was proven in ExUnit, not observed. The next k3d failure, if any, brings the Monitor's line. Code: apps/engine/lib/engine/sessions/monitor.ex:45 (expect_handoff/1), :119 (apagar_linha/1); apps/engine/lib/engine/shutdown.ex:130 (release/1, the drain marks the handoff) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/sessions/monitor_repasse_test.exs:52 (Monitor suspended: the late :DOWN does not delete the row rewritten by the peer), :67 (chain old → old → new: the second drain still sees the session), :87 (without adoption the row keeps going out through the drain), :100 (Shutdown.release/1 marks the handoff — swapping the call back to expect_stop/1 fails ONLY this test) Origin: AT-078 — intermittent orphan session of the engine rollout

documents.t: RN-580 declared it open: only the Criativo wrote tool.result, and without the text — in the other five the rehydration note said the log does not record the outcome, and the rehydrated agent knew THAT it called create_epic, not the id of the epic it answered. The rule: All six write. Criativo, PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead, UX Designer and Staff emit tool.result after EVERY call that returns text. The payload comes from ONE place, Engine.Agents.ResultadoDeFerramenta.payload/2: tool, ok and — on success — resultado; on failure, erro (as the Criativo already did). With a ceiling, and the ceiling states the total. The text is cut at 2,000 characters; when it cuts, resultadoTotal brings the REAL size (ADR 0060). The reason for the ceiling: the log is read by every project member and goes into the backup, and a listing (listar_backlog) can be large. Additive. A new field in an existing type, without a migration; tool/ok/erro stay as they were. An event is immutable: an earlier session stays without the text, and the rehydration note keeps saying so for the call without tool.result. Rehydration uses the text. desfecho: ok, devolveu: <texto> (with the warning [cortado; o total real tinha N caracteres] when there is resultadoTotal). It remains a text note, never role: tool — the event does not keep the call's id. propose_adr stopped writing its own refusal tool.result: the Arquiteto's server writes it for every tool, and the two would duplicate the event. What stays open: (a) and (b) closed in RN-593 — (a) the Dev Lead that SUSPENDS ({:pending, _}, propose_execution_plan/assess_implementability) did not write tool.result on suspension nor on action_settled; (b) InfraLeadServer had its own tool.result and did not go through this module; (c) the 2,000 ceiling is a CHOICE, not measured over the holdings — no real result was sampled; (d) pending product decision (human TODO of AT-151): the six's tools return ids, lists of rules/backlog/metrics and error messages — none reads a repository file nor command output —, but if such a tool is born, it would write its content to the log; the cut is the only containment. Code: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/resultado_de_ferramenta.ex:24 (payload/2), criativo_server.ex:382, po_server.ex:259, arquiteto_server.ex:336, dev_lead_server.ex:407, ux_designer_server.ex:232, staff_server.ex:198; apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/reidratacao.ex:224 (desfecho/1) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/reidratacao_test.exs:128 (text and cut warning in the note; :145 old session without tool.result), apps/engine/test/engine/agents/po_server_test.exs:252 (the recorded event, cut, with resultadoTotal) Origin: AT-151 — declared open in RN-580 (AT-073)

documents.t: ADR 0148 called the docs/ folder rebuildable and declared, in cost 3, that there was no reprojection command: deleting the folder did not rebuild it, because the outbox rows were already marked. It is the same gap RN-569 closed for the graph, in a second consumer. Measured by reading the code: a Postgres restore, the loss of the project_workspaces volume and the execution_mode conversion (which does not touch docs/) leave the folder absent or in the old place, and nothing rewrites it. The rule: apps/api/src/scripts/reprojetar-artefatos.ts (pnpm --filter api artefatos:reprojetar; node scripts/reprojetar-artefatos.js in the image) sweeps session_events and rewrites the folder. As in RN-569: A single translator. The event → agent folder, file name and Markdown translation LEFT ArtifactProjector for ArtifactEventTranslator; the projector reaches the event through an outbox row, the reprojection through a cursor, and both call it. The projector's surface (constructor, drainOnce) did not change. The list of what is projected remains ARTIFACT_PROJECTABLE_EVENT_TYPES — a new type goes in there and is translated in the same place, never in a second translator. Idempotent and never deletes. The name is a function of the event (versioned: <tipo>.md; append-only: with the seq), so running again rewrites the same files; resuming is running again, or --after-event from the printed cursor. A file the user put in docs/ stays. It does not touch the outbox (aggregate_type = 'artifact_projection'): it runs with the api up without stealing, reopening or marking rows. Never a silent success. Unlike the graph, there is no destination that stops everything (a write failure belongs to the ITEM, ADR 0148): each failure is counted and named with the event's id, the rest is written, and the process exits with 1. A nonexistent --project is refused without writing. What this rule does NOT close: (a) the versioned ones (module_map, module_routing, project_image, c4_diagram) show the LAST event in id order; --after-event starting between two versions may leave an older one — only the full round guarantees the current one; (b) it writes to the project's CURRENT location, and needs to see the same disk as the api; (c) it does not recreate qa_verdict/secops_verdict/task_blocked/infra_delegation_files, which were never a file; (d) no time measurement on a large event log; (e) it does NOT go into backup — it is derived, the argument of ADR 0152. Code: apps/api/src/application/artifact-projection/artifact-event-translator.ts:21 (ArtifactEventTranslator), :24 (projetarEvento); apps/api/src/application/artifact-projection/artifact-projector.ts:64 (the projector builds the SAME translator), :131 (delegates); apps/api/src/scripts/reprojetar-artefatos.ts:96 (reprojetarArtefatos), :115 (the translator), :137 (cursor sweep over session_events), :163 (the failure counted without aborting), :185 (lerArgumentos), :241 (only the direct invocation reprojects); apps/api/package.json:45 (artefatos:reprojetar) Test: apps/api/test/scripts/reprojetar-artefatos.spec.ts:215 (forward projector → delete the folder → reproject → same paths and contents; identical second round; outbox intact), :254 (never deletes), :265 (per project), :275 (nonexistent project — failure case), :289 (write failure counted without aborting the rest — failure case), :314 (unknown argument); apps/api/test/application/artifact-projection/artifact-projector.spec.ts (the forward projector, unchanged, over the extracted translator) Origin: AT-128 — the gap ADR 0148 declared (cost 3)

documents.t: RN-573/RN-574 (ADR 0161) taught project creation and the start in /containers to know the installation has no broker (empty BROKER_URL). The closing declared the rest out: the mode conversion, stop/remove and the Infra Lead. This rule takes the three doors, with the SAME source — ContainerBrokerPort.configurado() — and no new route. It says that the variable EXISTS, never that the broker answers (that remains naoObservado, RN-486). Mode conversion (ExecutionModeSection). The brokerConfigurado field already came in GET .../projects-base, which the section already reads. Converting to container/mounted with a CONFIRMED absence (false) leaves the button inert and states the reason in text; "querying", a failing query and an absent field do NOT assert anything — "I don't know" becomes neither "it has" nor "it doesn't have" — and do not block. Converting to runner, or to the mode the project already has, is never blocked. It is a SCREEN rule, like the creation one: the PUT projects/:projectId/execution-mode does not apply it. Stop/remove on /containers. container_stop/container_remove in container/mounted also go through the broker (RN-495), so without it they can only end in failure: the screen leaves "Stop"/"Remove" inert with its own text (sem_broker_para_parar), !== true as in the start. runner never falls here. The api refuses when proposing. ProposeActionUseCase answers 409 sem_broker_na_instalacao, BEFORE creating the proposal, for container_start/container_stop/container_remove in a project that is not runner when configurado() is false. It is the decision of HOW the Infra Lead knows without HTTP in the loop: the engine does not read BROKER_URL (a second source would diverge from configurado()), and the call the tool ALREADY made returns the refusal. dispatch_container_start/2 now delivers to the model the TEXT of the api's message (container_start recusado: …), as a tool result (RN-163), and not the raw tuple. RN-566 stays as it was: refusal by MODE, local. What it does NOT close: the blind proposal due to the absence of an IMAGE remains possible (RN-566 already declared it); the api's refusal also holds for whoever calls without being the agent, which is what is wanted — the approval would only end failed; and the PUT execution-mode keeps accepting the conversion by a direct call. documents.t: RN-582 (AT-131) made the provisioning's technical session — that of repo_bootstraps.session_id — stop displacing the working session as "the most recent", but with TWO criteria: the api recognized it by the link in repo_bootstraps, and the web by the NAME (git-bootstrap). The name is a label the user renames (RN-098), so renaming the session made the Overview and the workspace summary disagree about which was the working session. The api returns the marker. Each item of GET /projects/:projectId/sessions carries technical: boolean (SessionListItemResponseDto), true only for the session of repo_bootstraps.session_id of THAT project (one per project, unique(project_id)). It is the SAME criterion as the workspace summary (sessaoTecnicaDeBootstrap), never the name: renaming does not change the marker, and a working session called git-bootstrap does not become technical. Only the listing carries it. The marker is not a column of sessions nor a field of the Session entity: the GET of a session and the responses of create/rename/transition stay with SessionResponseDto, without it. It is the listing the screen sorts to find "the most recent". The screen reads the marker. sessaoMaisRecente (useLatestSession) skips the session with technical: true and only returns it when it is the ONLY one — the rule of RN-582 unchanged, with the source swapped. The web's SessaoListada type takes the field from the OpenAPI GENERATED type. What it does NOT close: the Overview and the handoff card in the session still do not query the state of each handoff's session (the gap RN-582 declared); deciding whether they start querying it is a separate decision, outside this rule. documents.t: RN-589 declared two open: the Dev Lead that suspends on an approval wrote tool.result at no moment, and InfraLeadServer only wrote the refusal one of propose_infra_pr, with a hand-assembled payload. In both cases the rehydrated agent (RN-580) read "the log does not record the outcome of this call" about a plan the user had already decided, or about every call of validate_infra_file and of container start. The rule: Dev Lead: the tool.result is born on RESUMPTION, never on suspension. When propose_execution_plan/assess_implementability suspends ({:pending, _}), the log stays with only the tool.call: there is no outcome, and writing "pending" there would be the same lie it would be for the model. When the {:action_settled, …} of the SAME action arrives, the server writes the tool.result with the SAME text that goes into the role: "tool" message. ok follows the partition of texto_do_desfecho/1: executed/auto_approved/approved are true; refusal, failure and a status the module does not know are false — ok: true on an outcome nobody classified would be asserting success without knowing. An outcome of ANOTHER action stays ignored and writes nothing. Infra Lead: every tool dispatched inline writes. validate_infra_file, propose_container_start and container_start_via_runner write tool.result through Engine.Agents.ResultadoDeFerramenta.payload/2 — a proposal accepted by the api is ok: true; a local refusal by mode (RN-566), the api's refusal (RN-591) and an absent runner are ok: false with the reason. The refusal of propose_infra_pr without a repository (RN-577) goes through the same module, with the payload from before (tool, ok: false, erro) and the cut. An accepted propose_infra_pr stays WITHOUT tool.result, on purpose: it does not emit tool.call (its trace is the proposed_action), and a result without a call would become an orphan note in rehydration. What remains open: a suspension crossed by an engine restart keeps losing the Wake subscription (ADR 0086) — there the tool.result is never born, and rehydration says the log does not have the outcome, which is true; the 2,000-character ceiling remains a CHOICE, not measured: no real holdings were sampled in this change (item (c) of RN-589); the output of validate_infra_file (hadolint/actionlint) may quote excerpts of the file the agent ITSELF wrote, and the cut is the only containment — it is item (d) of RN-589 with the first concrete case. Code: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/dev_lead_server.ex:313 (handle_info/2 of action_settled, the tool.result at :271), :719 (sentido_do_desfecho/1); apps/engine/lib/engine/infra/infra_lead_server.ex:1042 (registrar_resultado/4), :317 (the refusal of propose_infra_pr) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/dev_lead_server_test.exs:292 (the suspension does not write), :364 (the resumption writes the text the model read), :488 (refused is ok: false with the reason); apps/engine/test/engine/infra/infra_lead_server_test.exs:253 (the outcome of validate_infra_file), :409 (accepted proposal), :485 (refusal by mode), :863 and :910 (container_start_via_runner with and without a runner) Origin: AT-190 — declared open in RN-589 (AT-151)

documents.t: The broker comes up by default in the DEV compose since RN-512, but the api received an empty BROKER_URL (${BROKER_URL:-}, and the line came commented out in .env.example). The result, measured in the owner's test on 09/26: with the broker up alongside, brokerConfigurado came false and project creation only allowed runner (RN-573). Two rules close this: BROKER_URL has a default in the dev compose, and only there. The default is http://broker:8090 — the service and the port (BROKER_PORT) that the SAME file declares, and the test locks the two together: a default pointing elsewhere would swap "no broker" for "unreachable broker". The .env's value keeps winning. The PRODUCTION and INSTALLATION composes stay ${BROKER_URL:-}, on purpose: there the broker is under profiles: ["container-broker"], and whoever turns it on writes the URL (install.sh, asking — RN-575). A default there would make the api of an installation without a broker assert it has one. preflight.mjs REPORTS the managed folder, in the mold of DOCKER_GID. Without PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR, api and engine use the managed volume project_workspaces (without a host path), the broker is left without PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT — the dev compose DERIVES it from that one —, the stack comes up healthy and the container_start of the container mode, the default, ends refused. The report has four outcomes that do not collapse: ausente, ok, nao-absoluta (the ~: Compose expands it at the source of api/engine's bind-mount, but NOT in the variable the broker receives — measured with docker compose config) and divergente (an explicit PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT different from the folder api and engine mount, including when they mount the volume). Each message states the symptom and the fix. It NEVER refuses the startup and NEVER writes the .env: the answer is a path on someone's disk, and swapping the volume for the folder hides what is already in the volume (the data stay there, they just stop being seen) — the message says that too. What stays open: pnpm bootstrap does NOT offer the folder. Doing so would be a second consentir-base.mjs (asking in a TTY, creating the folder with the right owner, writing BOTH variables together, deciding what to do with a project_workspaces volume that already has data), and that is its own front. documents.t: In the owner's test on 09/26 the api logged 11 POST /workspaces/:id/projects → 400 in ~4 s, and the same runner project, created via the api with a path, came out 201. Measured by reading and reproduced in the wizard's vitest: there is no automatic retry (createProject is called directly, without useMutation), so each POST was a CLICK. The probable cause is the runner mode's "Browse folder...", which creates the project EARLY (RN-437): in the details step the path field is ABOVE the name, and clicking before typing the name sent { name: '', slug: '', executionMode: 'runner', workspacePath: '/workspace-a-confirmar' } — CreateProjectDto refuses a name with fewer than 2 characters and a slug outside kebab-case —, and the failure became only the toast "Could not prepare folder browsing right now", with no reason; clicking again was the only answer the screen suggested. A ONE-letter name passed Continue and came back 400 at "Provision" for the same MinLength(2). Three halves, all on the screen (the api is right to refuse): Do not send what is already known to be refused. nomeAceitoPelaApi mirrors the DTO (2+ characters, trimmed, and a non-empty slug) and becomes the name gate of the details step. In runner mode, "Browse folder..." stays INERT while the name does not pass, or while a TYPED path is not plausible (caminhoLocalParecePlausivel), and the reason is stated in text below the field (procurar-bloqueado, ADR 0064). An EMPTY path still does not block — the provisional placeholder of RN-437 covers it. It is the revision of RN-437's sentence "never blocking the click", which talked about the PATH and did not foresee the empty name. The name goes trimmed in the body. One creation at a time. criacaoEmVoo (a useRef) locks BOTH paths that create — "Browse folder..." and "Provision" —, because the disabled only reaches the button on the next render. In jsdom the disabled already holds the second click; the ref is what holds two events in the same browser frame. The refusal on the screen. The 400 failure of the early creation now puts the api's sentence (mensagemDaApi, the class-validator list joined) in the SAME step Alert that "Provision" already used (RN-170); other errors stay with only the toast. What was not measured: the api log of the owner's test did not survive the container restart, so the BODY of each of the 11 POSTs was not seen — the cause above is the only one that reading the code and vitest reproduce, and it does not prove it was it. The adjacency (RN-437) stays as it was: the project created early with the provisional path does not receive the refined path later at "Provision" (it is REUSED, not updated) — what fixes it is the runner when connecting (RN-423). documents.t: The broker's HTTP client applied ONE ceiling, 5 s, to the five operations. The docblock justified it by the screen READ path (RN-486), and it also held for exec — whose request CARRIES its own timeoutMs — and for start, which waits for the docker run and the image pull it does. Reproduced in AT-233: a fake broker answering an exec in 6 s, with a timeoutMs of 8 s, came back as BrokerIndisponivelError('sem-resposta') — "the container broker did not answer … The operation was aborted due to timeout". That is, every terminal command over 5 s in a container/mounted project with a running container (RN-492) failed saying the broker was down, while the command kept running. And the engine cut too: the container-exec call did not pass receive_timeout and fell back to Req's default, 15 s — the SAME default as TERMINAL_ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS. Reproduced with a fake api (Bandit) that answers in 16 s: {:error, %Req.TransportError{reason: :timeout}}. Raising the ceiling only in the api would fix nothing. The rule: inspect stays short (5 s) — it is the read of /containers and of the lifecycle route, and a screen that waits for the broker's worst case is worse than one that declares "not observed". exec DERIVES from timeoutMs (or from the broker's 15 s default, when it comes without one): broker context (10 s) + ps (30 s) + the larger of the command and the diagnostic docker version (30 s) + 5 s of margin. The broker cuts the command at timeoutMs and ANSWERS timedOut: true; the api has to be waiting when the answer arrives. start/stop/remove wait for the broker's OWN worst case: context + ps + the operation (the run with the pull; the stop with the 10 s of grace; rm --force) + the docker version it runs when it fails, plus the margin. Waiting for that is waiting for the broker's ANSWER, including its named refusal. The math was born with 105 s and forgot the SECOND ps of the resolver (the managed one and the namesake): the real worst case was 130 s. Since RN-605 it counts the six control calls of start and gives 195 s. The engine waits longer than the api: timeoutMs + 90 s. The chain is broker < api < engine, and the tests on both sides check it (the api mirrors the engine's slack as FOLGA_DO_EXEC_NO_ENGINE_MS, and the engine's test reads that number from the api's source). A blown ceiling has its own reason: BrokerIndisponivelError gains teto-excedido, distinct from sem-resposta (connection refused, DNS), and the message names the operation and the number — and, in the long ones, the consequence: the command may keep running in the container; the run/pull may have happened, so check /containers before repeating. In the screen's read teto-excedido falls into the SAME naoObservado: 'broker-sem-resposta' as always, with the text in detalhe — no new value in the DTO. The numbers on the other side (TIMEOUT_DE_CONTROLE_MS, TIMEOUT_DE_EXEC_PADRAO_MS, the TIMEOUT_MS of the broker's context client) are MIRRORED in named constants, not imported: the api does not consume the Docker port package. Nothing changes in the broker's containment (ADR 0130), in DockerPort nor in RN-502. Declared, not closed: A pull of more than 30 s keeps failing — in the broker. The pull runs under the Docker port's TIMEOUT_DE_CONTROLE_MS (30 s), and a big image does not come up on the first attempt. Since RN-605 the overflow has a NAME (PullExcedeuTetoError, origin infra) instead of "code -1" with origem: null; the ceiling itself did not go up, by the maintainer's decision. Node's fetch waits for headers for at most 300 s. An exec with timeoutMs above ~255 s is cut by undici before this rule's ceiling; the error comes out teto-excedido naming the 300 s. The outer hop (/internal/actions/execute, api → engine) also has no explicit ceiling and falls into the same 300 s, so TERMINAL_ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS above ~210 s does not arrive whole. A sick broker at ps (the docker ps taking the whole 30 s and the diagnosis another 30) may exceed the exec ceiling with a short command; it comes out teto-excedido, with the right name. documents.t: The Docker port's start did not pull: docker run did, internally, under TIMEOUT_DE_CONTROLE_MS (30 s). Reproduced in AT-234 with a double of the daemon (image absent, 45 s pull, without sleeping and without network): the overflow came out as ComandoDeDockerFalhouError — "docker run … ended with code -1: (no error output)" —, became a 502 with origem: null in the broker and reached the api without a name. And killing the CLI CANCELS the pull (measured on Docker 29.8.0, containerd): the image stayed absent for the following 60 s, so the sentence "the pull may continue in the daemon" did not hold. Of the four ways out measured (its own ceiling of ~300 s, asynchronous start, pull in advance at the image decision, only giving a name), the maintainer decided on D — only giving a name (2026-09-27). The rule: The pull is explicit. Before the run, image inspect; a present image is not downloaded again (the same --pull missing as the run). Absent, docker pull under the SAME 30 s control ceiling — no bigger ceiling. The overflow has a name. PullExcedeuTetoError, origin infra, with the image, the ceiling and the whole consequence: the pull was cancelled, the image stays absent, a big image does not come up through this path, and the fix is downloading it beforehand on the host. Before asserting that, the adapter checks the daemon (docker version): a daemon down remains DockerIndisponivelError. A pull that fails for another reason follows the usual path (ComandoDeDockerFalhouError, without an origin, ADR 0128). The name crosses over. The broker answers 504 with origem: 'infra', and the api passes it on in BrokerRecusouError — origem filled in, never null. In runner mode the same adapter runs on the user's machine and the message arrives in the container_start_result. The ceilings of whoever waits for the start count the whole worst case: the two ps of resolver, image inspect, pull, run and the diagnostic docker version — six control calls (CHAMADAS_DE_CONTROLE_NO_START). The api waits 10 + 6 × 30 + 5 = 195 s (TETO_DE_MUTACAO_MS); the engine, in RunnerRouter, 6 × 30 + 5 = 185 s on start and 4 × 30 + 5 = 125 s on stop/remove (it was 60 s, less than the resolver plus the operation). The engine's propose_action waits for the execution the api does inside it. Auto-approved container_start, container_start_via_runner and container_stop are EXECUTED in the same request (ProposeActionUseCase), and the call fell back to Req's 15 s default — a long start came back as a transport timeout even without a pull. Now it carries a receive_timeout of 225 s (the api's ceiling + 30 s), mirrored in the api as TETO_DO_PROPOSE_ACTION_DE_CONTAINER_NO_ENGINE_MS; the tests on both sides check broker < api < engine and runner < engine. container_remove stays out: it is never born auto-approved. No new dependency (ADR 0128), no field the caller writes (ADR 0130): the image keeps coming from the Arquiteto's decision, and pull is not a new broker operation — it is a step of start. Declared, not closed: A big image does not come up on the first attempt, neither through the broker nor through the runner — the maintainer's decision D. The outcome is now named; the fix is downloading the image beforehand on the host. In the worst failure case, the approval stays stuck for up to ~195 s: ExecuteContainerStartUseCase runs inside the approval POST, and neither the web nor the HTTP server has its own ceiling. It was not measured whether the layers downloaded before the cancellation are reused on the next attempt. documents.t: RN-567 put in the event the RULE that decided (reason) and declared what stayed out: point 7 of ADR 0055 asks for which scope authorized, and escopo: cd dentro da pasta do projeto does not say which folder the scope was that day. The root changes — mode conversion, a new base —, and the event is the only place that keeps what held at the instant of the decision. The rule: the payload of the SESSION event proposed_action.created of a terminal action gains scopeRoot, with three fields — executionMode, ancora and segmento: mode ancora segmento container raiz_gerenciada the workspace_dir_name — the root IS <PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT>/<segmento> mounted base_de_projetos the piece under BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, through the SAME segmentoSobABaseDeProjetos the broker uses mounted (without a base, outside it, or the base itself) indisponivel null runner nome_da_pasta the workspace_dir_name — identifies the folder without being relative to anything the server knows Never the absolute path, and that is the decision (AT-147, the maintainer's). The event log is read by every project member and an event is not rewritten; in mounted/runner the root is a folder on the user's machine, with their $HOME in the path. That is why indisponivel exists: falling back to the absolute path "so as not to lose information" would be exactly the leak. In runner the agent's local base never crosses the network, so there is no relative segment the server can compute — the ancora says the value is a NAME and not a path. Only in terminal. It is the only type in which decide() consults the scope (terminalNoEscopo); in the others the field does not exist, instead of existing saying something the decision did not use. The derivation is that of projectScopeRoot — raizDoEscopoNoEvento lives next to it, in the same file, and it is not a second rule: what it does is EXPRESS the same root without the absolute part. Additive, and absent is not "no root". An event written before this rule, or of another type, does not have the field; there is no reprocessing nor new column. The outbox does not carry it, for the same reason as RN-567 (no consumer in the engine). Nothing in decide() changes, no ceiling, and the screen does not change — where it shows up is another delivery (AT-148). (Since RN-614 the root shows up together with the reason, on the event's line in the log panel and in the ApprovalCard, always relative and with its own text for indisponivel.) The web reads the payload as a generic record, so old and new events go through the same read. Declared: in mounted, the segment is relative to the base configured AT THE INSTANT of the decision — if the base changes later, the old segment keeps saying what was true then, which is the point. And the separation between scope and permissions.json (RN-478) does not go into the field: it describes the SCOPE's root, never where the policy file lives. documents.t: RN-566 gave the Infra Lead's two start tools the refusal by MODE and declared the rest: /containers checks three things before offering the button (decided image, mode, confirmed folder) and the agent checked one. The maintainer's decision (AT-142, 2026-09-27) was to close that distance through local refusals at dispatch, in the mold of RN-566/RN-577, and NOT through enriched context — GetInfraContextUseCase does not change. recusa_local_de_subida/2 still reads the project ONCE. First the MODE (recusa_por_modo/2, RN-566's rule with no text change) — it is what says which tool to use, and answering "image missing" to whoever called the wrong tool would point to the wrong door. Then the STATE (recusa_por_estado/3), one clause per reason, in the SAME order as decidirSubida (apps/web/src/routes/containers-subida.ts), evaluated only until the first refusal: Clause propose_container_start container_start_via_runner Local read container already REGISTERED running/provisioning (ja_esta_de_pe) refuses refuses project_containers.status no image decided (sem_imagem_decidida) does not refuse refuses an artifact.project_image exists in some session of the project folder never confirmed (runner_nunca_confirmou) — refuses null projects.workspace_verified_at no runner connected now — refuses (already existed, RN-508) Engine.Runners.Registry Why propose_container_start does not refuse by image. Electing the image is what that proposal DOES (RN-491): requiring a decision before would invert the order. The screen checks image in both modes because its button elects nothing. container_start_via_runner does not elect — it starts the ALREADY decided image, and ExecuteContainerStartViaRunnerUseCase fails without it —, so there the clause holds. The predicate is the SAME as the api's (ObterContainerDoProjetoUseCase): the EXISTENCE of the event, never the validity of the payload, because the api degrades an unreadable payload to the default instead of treating it as absence. Why "already up" refuses, if the execution would not fail. SubirCicloDeVidaDoContainerUseCase is idempotent over provisioning/ running, so the approved proposal would be a nothing that spent a human decision — and in container/mounted worse than nothing: it would elect a new version of artifact.project_image that the container that is up, with the version frozen on the row (RN-245), would not use. Registered is not observed (RN-486): the text does not assert the container is alive, it says what to do when it died from outside. stopped, failed and removed do not refuse. A query error returns nil and falls into the usual path — "I could not look" never becomes a refusal. The texts, which are the tool result the model reads (RN-163) — never agent.error, never end of turn, with tool.call/tool.result (ok: false) in the event log through the same registrar_resultado/4 of RN-593: already up: "o container deste projeto já está REGISTRADO como <status> — subir não é a próxima ação, e <tool> não foi proposta. O registro não é observação (RN-486): se o container morreu por fora, ou se a imagem precisa mudar, diga ao usuário que parar ou remover é pela página /containers; só depois disso uma nova subida faz sentido. Não repita a chamada agora." no image: "nenhuma imagem de container foi decidida para este projeto (artifact.project_image, RN-105) — container_start_via_runner sobe a imagem JÁ decidida e não elege nenhuma, então aprovada ela só poderia falhar, e não foi proposta. Quem decide a imagem é o Arquiteto (choose_project_image): diga isso ao usuário e não repita a chamada até haver decisão." folder never confirmed: "a pasta deste projeto nunca foi confirmada por um agente local (workspace_verified_at vazio, RN-423) — nenhum brabo-runner jamais conectou a ele, e container_start_via_runner não foi proposta. Peça ao usuário para rodar brabo-runner --project <id> --dir <pasta> na máquina dele: a confirmação acontece quando o runner conecta." No prompt line changed, and no measurement with a real model was done in this rule: the premise that the model understands the refusal is that of RN-566. What NO clause checks, declared: an installation without a broker (the engine does not read BROKER_URL; what refuses is the api when proposing, with 409 sem_broker_na_instalacao, RN-591) and role/session (the agent is not the one who clicks). The folder clause uses the stamp, which is not a heartbeat (RN-468) — that is why the connected runner one stays after it. documents.t: The gap RN-552 and RN-561 declared in writing: "in an installation that has no PROJECT yet, listing and revocation — both via /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys — have no project to answer against". The one-line installation (RN-547) creates EXACTLY that situation: the account and the machine key are born before any project, and the key stayed alive and unreachable. The maintainer's decision (AT-118): yes, in the Account. Two new routes, and only two. GET /users/me/machine-device-keys lists and DELETE /users/me/machine-device-keys/:deviceKeyId revokes (204, idempotent). No @RequireRole, like users/me/credentials and users/me/preferences: the scope is the person THEMSELF, and there is no project nor workspace to resolve a role against. The userId comes from the session JWT and goes into the WHERE; no parameter names another person, and the maintainer view over someone else's key stays out by the decision of RN-519 — this route does not reopen it through another door. Only the MACHINE kind. The listing returns ONLY project_id IS NULL (especie: "maquina"), revoked ones INCLUDED (the rule of RN-519: making the row disappear would make the screen assert the key never existed). The PROJECT ones have a home — their project's device-keys section, where the reach of revoking them is stated — and bringing them into the Account would make the Account take down a project's pairing without naming the project. For the same reason, revocation via the account refuses a PROJECT key with 404, the SAME response as for a key that does not exist or belongs to another person: the question goes to the SAME listing as the screen, filtered by userId, so there is no way to ask about someone else's key and learn that it exists. What revoking actually takes down, and the target does NOT change. Revocation via the account is not a new revocation: RevokeMachineDeviceKeyUseCase checks that the key is among the caller's machine ones and DELEGATES to RevokeRunnerDeviceKeyUseCase, byte for byte. It writes the row and, for the machine key, asks the engine for a disconnectRunnerOfUser per project in runner mode the owner reaches (RN-520/RN-543). The target remains {projeto, usuário} and never {chave}: another runner of the same user in those projects drops along, even with a PAT or another key, and reconnects if its credential is still valid. In an installation without a project, the list of projects is empty and the revocation only writes the row — and that is enough: the machine agent waiting for the first project (RN-550) has no connection at all to take down, and the next ticket it asks for is refused. Changing the target remains its own front, with an ADR (AT-013). "Registering replaces the previous one" STAYS. RN-552 had two reasons to revoke the previous machine key on each registration: (a) the service token cannot manufacture durable credentials in series, and a reinstalled machine cannot leave behind a live key nobody remembers to revoke; (b) the orphan would be UNREACHABLE. This RN knocks down (b) and leaves (a) intact — it does not depend on a screen. What changes is that the replaced one now SHOWS UP, revoked, in the Account; and since nobody revoked it through the screen, the section says in TEXT that reinstalling revokes the previous one, so the row is not read as an incident. The screen lives in the Account (/account), the page that already existed for what follows the person across projects. It lists name, creation date, last use and status, and inherits the WHOLE vocabulary of RN-561/RN-548: lastUsedAt is RECORDED use, never connection, and null has its own text ("never used"); "active"/"revoked" talks about the ROW and never about an agent up — and "active" is not green, because the machine kind never gets green and there there are only those. There is no kind column: with a single kind it would repeat the same word on every row, and what it carried in the project section — the REACH — is stated in the caption and in the confirmation ("takes down the local agent in ALL your projects in runner mode; with no project at all, it only prevents the key from being used again"), together with RN-520's collateral cost. Loading, failed, empty, revoked and never used are five states with five texts (RN-088/RN-470). With no minimum role on the endpoint, the screen does not invent one: roleAtLeast here would lock out whoever can, the worse defect of the two. Revoking through one list invalidates ALL of them. The machine key shows up in the Account's list (['machine-device-keys']) and in that of EVERY project of the owner (['runner-device-keys', projectId], read by RunnerOnboardingPanel and by the device-keys section). invalidarChavesDeDispositivo invalidates the per-project one by PREFIX (every project in the cache) and the Account's always, and BOTH revocation screens call it — before, revoking through the project section invalidated only that of the open project, and the other lists kept announcing the revoked one. documents.t: RN-567 put in proposed_action.created the rule that decided (reason) and RN-609 put the scope's root (scopeRoot, only in terminal) — and both declared the screen did not change. Whoever audited through the screen an action that PASSED still did not know which rule let it through. The rule: the data shows up in TWO places (the maintainer's decision), and both say the SAME sentence, assembled by ONE function, fraseDaDecisaoDaPolitica: the event's line in the log panel — classifyEvent gains the branch for proposed_action.created (type permission, bad when denied), with the policy's outcome and, after the dash, the sentence; the ApprovalCard, on its own line right below the sentence of what happens (RN-096) — never inside the collapsed payload. The action (proposed_actions) keeps neither of the two fields: the screen reads them from the EVENT, which it already loads (decisaoDaPoliticaDaAcao, by actionId). That is why the card has THREE states, which do not collapse: a screen that does not read the event log (the "needs you" panel, PRs, containers) does not pass the data and the card goes SILENT; a screen that reads (the session chat and the Approvals tab's queue, both over the most recent session) and did not find the event in the loaded window says "outside the events loaded on this screen"; and the found event gives the sentence. The Insights tab has no ApprovalCard — a Psicólogo hypothesis is not a proposed_action. Since AT-336 (RN-656), each card of the Approvals tab has its OWN reason, read through the action when the loaded log does not cover it; the next paragraph is the state of AT-333, which it replaced — the single note remains only for the read that FAILS. Since AT-340 the same holds for the cards of pending items from OTHER sessions in the chat (RN-626), which before went silent: the thread's log never covers another session's action. In AT-333, the Approvals tab's queue started saying the gap ONCE. The queue is the PROJECT's (RN-638) and the events are those of ONE session, so there "outside the loaded events" came out on almost every card — a truth repeated per card, the tool explaining itself. The api does not expose the reason per action (the action does not keep it, and the events read does not filter by actionId: measured), and fetching without a window would require a new endpoint. The tab then starts COUNTING the pending ones without the event and saying, in a note above the queue, how many there are and why ("of these N actions", or "of N of the M actions below"), in the mold of RN-180; those cards go silent (the "screen that does not read" state), and the card whose event is loaded keeps showing the sentence. The note only counts with the log in hand: before the events arrive it asserts nothing. The session chat keeps the three states per card — there the cut is the thread's own. Absent is not "no reason", and the absolute never shows up. An event prior to RN-567 says "policy reason not recorded"; a terminal prior to RN-609 says "scope root not recorded"; another type, without scopeRoot, does not talk about a root (the scope is only consulted in terminal). The four anchors have their own text — managed folder, segment inside the projects base, folder name on the runner's machine, and indisponivel ("no relative form", without a segment). An anchor the screen does not know says it does not know, and does not print the segment: the screen rebuilds no path at all. The sentences are in en and pt-BR (approvals.json, key politica). documents.t: The fifth door of the ceilings line (RN-472, RN-556, RN-557), and the route ADR 0157 refused to open in passing. Until now WorkspacesController had no member @Delete, and offboarding was a write to the database. The maintainer's decision (AT-115/HS-006): the route is born, protected by a CLAUSE. The route. DELETE /workspaces/:workspaceId/members/:userId, owner (the SAME minimum as the upsert), 204, idempotent. The ceiling is inherited, with no new rule. remocaoEhAutoRebaixamento receives the actor's WORKSPACE role as today's effective one and null as the AFTER role — in the workspace there is no level above to catch the fall, so removing one's own row is always a fall to "no access", the branch the function already stated for a project without a workspace row. Removing ONESELF is always 403, with its own sentence: "Você não pode remover a si mesmo deste workspace: aqui não há papel acima para segurar a queda, e sem a linha você perde o workspace e todos os projetos dele. Voltar exige o owner que você estaria abandonando. Peça a outro owner." The last owner, by the SAME clause. Only owner calls the route; nobody removes themselves; so every successful removal leaves at least the CALLER as owner. Removing the last one would require them to remove themselves — the refused movement. The count stays refused (ADR 0157, point 2). The route's owner minimum is HALF of the proof, and that is why it is asserted in a test. movement outcome removing ONESELF from the workspace, whether or not there is another owner 403 removing ANOTHER owner passes — it is how ownership is revoked entirely removing the HOLDER (created_by), by another owner 409 criador_do_workspace — RN-616 removing any other person passes removing someone with no workspace row 204 — their project rows in the workspace go out the same The cascade, in one transaction. The workspace_members row; the project_members rows of the removed person in THIS workspace's projects (without them the projectRole ?? workspaceRole overlay of RN-471 would keep them inside every project in which they had their own row); and their credentials tied to those projects — PROJECT device keys and PATs —, revoked with the reason workspace_member_removed. After the commit, their runner's live connection drops in EACH project of the workspace through the path of RN-520, in a try/catch that only logs: an engine down does not take down the removal. Declared and NOT done: the MACHINE key (it belongs to the account and serves other workspaces; here it stops reaching because the role resolves to none); the already connected SESSION socket and the removed person's :web terminal (they stay until they drop; the new ticket is refused); a screen (there is no workspace members section in the apps/web). The HOLDER (workspaces.created_by) does not leave through this route — that is RN-616. documents.t: The maintainer's decision on the question RN-615 left open (AT-115, ADR 0173, point 7). workspaces.created_by authorizes nothing — what authorizes is the role (RN-472) —, but it is through it that the LLM credential the agents spend and the git one of agent actions are resolved (RN-058), as well as the owner of the spend report (RN-060). Removing the creator would leave the agents spending the credential of someone no longer in the workspace. The column comes to be called, in the rule, the holder. The refusal. DELETE /workspaces/:workspaceId/members/:userId with target = holder is 409 with code: "criador_do_workspace": "Não é possível remover o titular do workspace: a credencial de LLM que os agentes gastam, a de git das ações de agente e o relatório de gasto são dele (RN-058/RN-060). Transfira antes a titularidade para outro owner (PUT /workspaces/:workspaceId/owner-of-record) e remova depois." RN-615's ceiling comes first: the holder trying to remove themselves gets the self-removal 403. The transfer. PUT /workspaces/:workspaceId/owner-of-record, owner, body { userId }, answers the workspace (200). The destination must ALREADY be owner of the workspace, otherwise 409 titular_precisa_ser_owner ("A titularidade só vai para quem já é owner deste workspace: o titular paga o que os agentes gastam (RN-058). Promova a pessoa a owner antes, ou escolha outro owner."). It writes created_by in a transaction with the role read; transferring to the current holder is idempotent. Any owner can transfer, including to ANOTHER owner who did not ask — declared, it is the same authority that removes owners. The spend, from the commit on. ResolveCredentialOwnerUseCase returns the new holder: the agent turn looks for THEIR credential for the model's provider, and git actions for their git credential. Without a credential, the outcome is the one that already existed — the turn ends with "Nenhuma credencial cadastrada para " and the git remote read fails naming whose credential is missing. The transfer does NOT check this beforehand (declared in the ADR). The recorded spend does not move: token_usage does not keep the holder, and the whole report, history included, comes to belong to the new holder. No domain event: there remains a log line with from/to/who.
