documents.t: The decision RN-584 left open — "whether the Infra Lead comes to converse through the composer" — was taken by the maintainer (AT-141, 2026-09-27): yes, and it becomes the SEVENTH conversational agent (ADR 0175). The condition RN-584 wrote came first: its turn stopped running INSIDE handle_call/handle_cast and went through the SAME Engine.Agents.TurnoAssincrono as the other six; only after that was the message/2 clause born. Stage 1 — the turn. The Infra Lead's three turns come up in a Task — the kickoff (still a cast, only on the FRESH start of the accepted handoff), the gate correction ({:correct, _}) and the composer message. The message answers on ACCEPTANCE, with agent.status: working written BEFORE (RN-578); the outcome goes through the channel and, when it is a failure, through the durable agent.error. The user_message/2 that ran the turn inline LEFT: the name stayed and it is the acceptance. A second message with a turn in progress is 409 turno_em_andamento, with the agent.error of origin politica in the thread — including during the kickoff, which before held the message in the process's queue for the whole turn. "Stop" reaches the Infra Lead (via_for("infra") in cancel/2): it kills the Task — and with it the WorkflowsAgent, which runs inside the consolidation —, writes agent.error cancelado_pelo_usuario and returns idle. The consolidation with Workflows is part of the turn function and returns the state; the end signals (agent.done, agent.status: idle) only come out of TurnoAssincrono, in the server's process (RN-585). A gate correction that arrives with a turn in progress goes into a QUEUE (correcoes_pendentes) and comes up at the turn's closing, in order of arrival — the TurnoAssincrono without a from DISCARDS the request that finds a turn in progress, and the gate would be asking nobody for a change. The orphan turn of the restart closes through RN-586: infra entered TurnoOrfao (@agentes), at boot and in init/1. The history comes from Engine.Agents.Reidratacao (RN-580), as it already did, and the tool.result from ResultadoDeFerramenta (RN-593). The iteration ceiling is its own, 14 (the same as Arquiteto, Dev Lead, UX Designer and Staff), and exhausting it now emits toolloop.limit_reached (RN-166) — before, the 14th step ended silently. Stage 2 — the composer. message/2 has its OWN clause for infra, and its agente_sem_conversa refusal left — one name, one path. @agentes_de_conversa includes it; a message to an Infra Lead that is not up (engine restarted) brings it back up WITHOUT a kickoff, and it rehydrates in init/1. The screen offers it by the usual rule: infra entered AGENTES_DE_CHAT, so it is the recipient when it is the most recent agent.activated — with no default recipient (RN-584). Accepting ITS handoff stays in the dedicated card of RN-499; the thread's card excludes it by NAME (offeredHandoff), otherwise the invitation would show up twice and, being the oldest, would go back to hiding the Dev Lead's one (RN-136). The activity strip gained a sentence for its four tools. Conversing opens no external effect. The tools are the same four; the infra PR and the two container starts keep being born as proposed_action, with the local refusals of RN-566, RN-577 and RN-610 intact. The 180 s ceiling stopped mattering for the turn. It was smaller than the 225 s of the container propose_action (RN-605), and a message that led the model to propose container_start could blow the GenServer.call with the proposal up. With immediate acceptance, the GenServer.call only waits for the acceptance; the propose_action runs inside the Task, with nobody waiting synchronously. The 180 000 stayed, the same as the other six's, as the ACCEPTANCE ceiling. Does not change, declared: SOLO_CONVERSATIONAL_AGENTS (generated by pnpm --filter api gerar:areas) is the list of agents WITHOUT an area that manual handoff addresses; the Infra Lead is an area lead and stays out of it, and AGENTES_DE_CHAT is not generated. The Infra Lead did not gain structured questions nor backlog reading — conversing with it is conversing with what the kickoff gave it and with the four tools. documents.t: When an agent's context passes the threshold, the ContextManager swaps the old turns for ONE summary, written by another LLM call (the actor context-manager) and reinserted as a system message. That call's prompt is pt-BR and said nothing about language: in a conversation in English, or with two languages, the summary came out translated, and the next model read its own memory in the summary prompt's language — the language drift the language epic pursues, born outside the user's turn. The turn's language guidance does not protect this: it is never in messages, so it is never summarized, but it is also never seen by the summarizer. The rule is one sentence in the summary prompt, on BOTH tracks (the inline text and the versioned template prompts/context-manager-summarize.md, which goes up to version "2"): Mantenha cada turno no idioma original; não traduza citações nem código. The language is PER TURN, never a session language: in a session with two authors of different languages, both survive the summary. Quotes and code are literal text and are not translated — an identifier or an error message translated in the summary stops being findable. The sentence comes BEFORE the turns, so that the text of a turn at the end of the prompt is not read as its continuation. Cost: the addition is 76 bytes — 19 tokens by the engine's heuristic (bytes/4), at most 38 by a pessimistic rule of 1 token every 2 bytes —, within the ceiling of 50 input tokens per call the maintainer decided for the language guidance (AT-169, answer 8). The test fails a sentence that exceeds it by both rules. It is not agent_instructions: it is code text and versioned template text, outside the instruction_patch ceiling (RN-007), because the summarizer is not a project agent and has no per-project instruction. Decided without a baseline, declared: the maintainer decided to change the prompt right away, without waiting for the paid validation to show that the pt-BR summary drifts (AT-169, answer 4). The consequence is that AT-167's validation measures the WHOLE (guidance + new summary), without measuring the old summary in isolation. What this rule does NOT close, declared: With graph_templates_enabled? on, the ACTIVE version in the graph holds. A installation that seeded version "1" keeps sending the old prompt until it runs scripts/dev/seed-prompts.ts again — the body's hash changed, so the seeder creates the new version. With the flag off (the default) the inline one holds, which already has the sentence. Seeding again also removes from the body the documentation section that made the summarizer receive the turns twice (AT-244, see RN-413); the template is at version "3". The fallback for when the summarizer fails ("(N turnos anteriores omitidos)") is not a summary and does not get the sentence: there is no turn text in it. The sentence is pt-BR. It asks for each turn's language, not the prompt's; whether a model obeys it in a conversation in another language is what AT-167's validation measures. documents.t: Epic EP-028 was born from a conversation in Portuguese answered in Spanish. The maintainer's decisions of 2026-09-28 (AT-168, AT-169) fixed where the language of the ANSWERS lives — account, session and project — and the precedence among the sources. None of these rules touches the INTERFACE language (RN-432).
documents.s: The language of the agents' answers (RN-618..620, RN-622..624, ADR 0177)

documents.t: Open list, canonical form. The answers' language is any BCP-47 code whose language subtag the api's ICU recognizes, written canonically (pt-br becomes pt-BR) — never the interface's pt-BR/en enum, which stays closed. und, private use and free text are refused with a 400 that names the rule. A new account is born on AUTOMATIC. users.response_language is NULL ("automatic") until the person chooses; the api shows and accepts automatico as the name of that state. Interface and answers are independent. PATCH /users/me/preferences accepts locale and responseLanguage as OPTIONAL; sending one does not touch the other, a body with neither is 400, and an invalid responseLanguage refuses the WHOLE body before writing any field. The detected one only holds when confirmed. The language detected from the person's messages (detection is RN-624) only goes into users.detected_language together with detected_language_confirmed_at — a CHECK refuses one without the other. Detection alone changes nothing. A session override belongs only to whoever set it. PUT projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId/response-language (developer, the role for sending a message to an agent — the override only changes the answers to the person's own messages) sets a language in that session for WHOEVER CALLS; language: null (mandatory key) releases it and goes back to inheriting from the account. The GET (viewer) returns the caller's effective one. The key is the session×user pair: another participant of the same session is never affected, and there is no route to read or touch another person's. The precedence, resolved per person and never per session: session override > account choice > confirmed detected > users.locale. Since users.locale is NOT NULL, the chain always ends in a language, and the origin (sessao/conta/detectado/interface) travels with it. A one-off request inside a message ("translate to English") is not a step: what serves it is the model. Who consumes: since RN-622 the effective one reaches the model — the api calls ResolverIdiomaDaRespostaUseCase with the AUTHOR of each message to an agent and the session, and the engine puts the guidance at the end of each LLM call of that turn. The Account stopped saying the value "does not reach yet". documents.t: What it governs (the maintainer's decisions: AT-168 answer 8, AT-169 answer 1): the language of SHARED artifacts (product brief, business rules, ADRs) and of turns WITHOUT a human author (opening by kickoff, dev agents, gates, commit message, PR body). What an agent answers to a PERSON remains their answers' language (RN-618). Always a concrete language. projects.language is NOT NULL, a canonical BCP-47 code by the SAME rule as RN-618 — but without "automatic", which is resolving from a person's messages and does not fit what has no person. automatico and an unrecognized code are 400, and the project is not born (or does not change). New project: the language requested at creation, canonicalized; without a request, the EFFECTIVE answers language of WHOEVER CREATES (ResolverIdiomaDaRespostaUseCase, without a session: account choice > confirmed detected > interface language). The note's proposal was the creator's users.locale; the whole chain was chosen because whoever has already said in which language they want to work should not see the project be born in another — and, without a choice or detection, it IS the users.locale. Projects that already existed: migration 0062_idioma_do_projeto writes the language of the workspace HOLDER (workspaces.created_by, whose credential the agents spend — RN-058/RN-616), through the same chain. At the migration nobody had a choice or detection yet, so the value is their users.locale. The holder, and not "an owner" from workspace_members, because they are ONE and the migration cannot choose between two. Who changes it: PATCH /projects/:projectId with language (maintainer, the route's minimum), and the "Project language" section in Settings, with the control inert and the reason in text for whoever does not reach it (RN-102). The column's pt-BR default is only the net for whoever inserts outside the use case (seed, script, fixture). Who consumes, and what remains: since RN-622 the engine reads the column (Engine.Projects.Project, directly from Postgres) and sends it to the model in every LLM call of a turn WITHOUT a human author, and since RN-623 also as the language of the shared artifact an agent writes DURING a turn with a human author — the divergence this rule declared closed. documents.t: Next to the model selector, in another scope. The bar's model belongs to the SESSION and holds for everyone; the language belongs to the PERSON (GET .../sessions/:sessionId/response-language, resolved for the caller, RN-618). Changing it there is the session override — the maintainer's decision, AT-169 answer 2 — and never touches another participant's nor the Account. Never the value without the origin (the rule of RN-470): "set by you in this session", "chosen by you in the Account", "detected from your messages and confirmed by you" and "the interface language" are four texts, and none collapses into another. Loading and failed also have their own text — the failure does not pretend a language. The detected one never becomes an assertion about the person ("you are Brazilian"), only about the messages (AT-080). "Follow the Account" releases the override (language: null) and says in WHICH language that results — the same chain without the session step, derived on the client from the chain the route already returns, without a new endpoint. "Another code…" opens a field that only sets on the button (RN-469), and the api's refusal arrives in the toast with its sentence. A link leads to the Account, where the choice that holds in every session lives. Who changes it: the PUT's minimum (developer), via roleAtLeast over the WORKSPACE role (the declared gap of the screens that do not fetch project_members). Below it the value and the origin stay on the bar, the selector stays inert and the reason comes in text. What the bar does NOT assert: never "the agents answer in X" as a fact about the person — only the effective one and the origin. Since RN-622 that effective one reaches the model in the messages of whoever is viewing, and the warning "does not reach the agents yet" left the origin line. The line truncates at the bar's 60px and carries the whole text in the title — the text is on the screen, the title only returns what the ellipsis cut. On the narrow bar, the language CHANGES place and does not disappear (AT-317). The bar arranges itself by its OWN width (modoDaBarra, measured by ResizeObserver; an unknown width is the full bar): from 1720px everything stays inline; below that model, language and budget become ONE control whose trigger summarizes the model and the language code (below 920px only the icon, with an accessible name), and its panel brings the whole indicator with the origin WRAPPING instead of cutting. The detection question (RN-624) lives in the panel, and while it exists the trigger gains a mark and the accessible name announces it. The session title is the only item that shrinks (with a floor and the whole name in the title), and the buttons do not wrap — "Close" becomes an icon with an accessible name only on the minimal bar. documents.s: RN-620 — The session bar shows the answers language of WHOEVER IS VIEWING, with the origin, and changing it there is the override only for that person in that session

documents.t: RN-618..620 decided IN WHICH language the agent replies and showed it on screen; none of that reached the model. This rule is the transport (AT-164, on the specification from AT-081 and the mechanism verified per provider in AT-161). One role: "system" message at the END of the list, on every LLM call of the turn — tool iterations included —, and NEVER in the history: it does not enter state.messages, so it does not pile up turn after turn, is not summarized by compaction (RN-621) and vanishes with the turn. In OpenAI-compatible it goes at the end of the conversation; in Anthropic it is hoisted to the end of the top system (AT-161). It is not agent_instructions: it is code text, outside the instruction_patch ceiling (RN-007). One place only. The one that appends it is the EngineApiClient facade (llm_turn/5 and llm_turn_stream/6), through which EVERY LLM call of the engine passes — the seven conversational agents, the ToolLoop (dev agents and gates) and the Infra Lead. No server assembles the guidance. Turn WITH a human author (the message someone typed to an agent): the api resolves THAT person's language in that session (ResolverIdiomaDaRespostaUseCase, RN-618 — session override account > confirmed detected > interface) and sends it in the agent/message command as idiomaDaResposta, an OPTIONAL field. The agent's server puts it in the TURN state during handle_call, and the turn's Task inherits it from the process dictionary (TurnoAssincrono); the GenServer does not keep it for the next turn. Two authors in the same session each get their own. Turn WITHOUT a human author (kickoff, dev agents, gates, commit, PR body, the Dev Lead's resumption after approval): the PROJECT language (RN-619), read from projects.language on every call (maintainer decision, AT-169 answer 1). The compaction summarizer (context-manager) stays out: "reply in X" would translate the summary, and preserving each turn's language in it is RN-621. Failure never brings the turn down. A resolution that fails in the api becomes a log and the message goes on WITHOUT idiomaDaResposta; a turn with an author but no language goes on WITHOUT guidance — never the project's in place of the person's. A failing read of the project language in the engine becomes a warning and the call goes on without guidance. A value that does not have the shape of a BCP-47 code does not become guidance either: nothing that is not a code is interpolated into the prompt. The texts are code constants, one per language: pt-BR ("Responda em português brasileiro (pt-BR), salvo pedido explícito do usuário por outro idioma nesta mensagem."), en, and a generic one in English that names the BCP-47 code for any other language of the open list (AT-168 answer 2). The text does not depend on the model: switching models in the middle of the session changes nothing, and there is no per-model cascade nor a special case for DeepSeek. Cost — decided ceiling of 50 INPUT tokens per call (AT-169 answer 8). Measured with gpt-tokenizer, content only, cl100k / o200k: pt-BR 29 / 23, en 18 / 18, generic es-MX 26 / 26 and the WORST case (the generic one with the longest code the accepted shape allows) 42 / 42; the message frame adds ~4, so the worst case lands at ~46. The test locks the text at 160 characters as a watchdog of the ceiling. Measurement: the chat.message recorded by the api carries idiomaAlvo and origem when resolution succeeded — the event is immutable and says, forever, what was asked of the model in that turn (AT-082). What this rule does NOT close, declared: Human chat without an agent (SendChatMessageUseCase) stays out, by maintainer decision (AT-169 answer 3). Only the MESSAGE to an agent carries an author (and the answer to the structured question form, which reuses it). The other commands a person triggers — confirming readiness to the Criativo, accepting a handoff — start a turn without an author and fall back to the PROJECT language: the product brief from confirmReadiness comes out in the project language. Artifact of a turn with an author: this rule declared it following the language of whoever wrote; since RN-623 the same message gains the artifact clause, in the project language. Not measured: the DeepSeek and Anthropic tokenizers; whether the guidance is enough against the pt-BR system prompt is what the paid validation of AT-167 measures. In Anthropic, guidance hoisted to the top changes the cache prefix on every change of author or language — cache is not observable today. documents.t: RN-619 promised the project language for the shared artifact, and RN-622 put the AUTHOR's language in every turn with an author — so what an agent recorded DURING the conversation with a person came out in that person's language. Maintainer decision (AT-168 answer 8, AT-245): the artifact follows the PROJECT; the chat reply stays in the author's language. The mechanism is the same message from RN-622, with a second clause. In a turn with an author, when the call carries at least one tool that records a shared artifact and the project language (projects.language) DIFFERS from the author's, the guidance becomes "Responda em português brasileiro (pt-BR), salvo pedido… Artefatos do projeto: em en." — in the language of the base text: the pt-BR clause is in Portuguese, the others' in English ("Write project artifacts in X."). It is still ONE ephemeral system message at the end, assembled by the facade; what decides is the set of tools that the SAME call carries to the model, which the facade already has. Why the guidance, and not the tool description. The description travels on EVERY call, in every tool, whether the languages are equal or not; the clause exists only when they differ, and lives in the only place that already decides the language. Nothing is added when the languages are equal, when the call has no artifact tool, and in a turn WITHOUT an author (which already gets the project language). What a shared artifact is — what the tool PERSISTS is read by other people and by the next agents: emit_artifact (business_rule, note, decision_record) — Criativo, PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead, UX Designer, Staff; create_epic, create_story, create_task — PO; create_module_map, assign_story_modules, choose_project_image, create_c4_diagram, route_modules_to_infra, propose_adr (the ADR of open_adr_pr), emit_insight — Arquiteto; propose_execution_plan, assess_implementability — Dev Lead; propose_prototype — UX Designer; propose_rfc — Staff; propose_infra_pr — Infra Lead. The product brief does NOT pass through here: it is emitted by the SERVER in confirmReadiness, which is a turn without an author and already comes out in the project language (like the handoff and the revise, which this rule does not change). What is NOT: ask_structured_questions (it is a question to the PERSON of the turn), offer_handoff (carries no text), the read ones (listar_*, rag_*, read_file, search_workspace), validate_infra_file (only validates) and the proposals to start a container (they ask for a decision, they do not record an artifact). Dev agents and gates have no turn with an author. Failure never brings the turn down. A failing read of the project language becomes a warning and ONLY the author's guidance goes on — never without guidance, never the project's in place of the person's. An author with no resolved language goes on without guidance, as in RN-622. Cost — the 50 input-token ceiling from AT-169 applies to the whole message. Measured with gpt-tokenizer, content only, cl100k / o200k, over all pairs of pt-BR, en, es, es-MX and zh-Hant-TW: worst case pt-BR → zh-Hant-TW 42 / 36; en → pt-BR 26 / 26; generic es-MX → zh-Hant-TW 36 / 36. The clause only enters with BOTH codes in the short canonical form (idioma[-Escrita][-Região], e.g. pt-BR, zh-Hant-TW, es-419), because it is the FORM that holds the ceiling: its worst (pt-BR → a 12-character code) measures 44 / 37, ~48 with the message frame. A code outside that form gets only the author's guidance, and the log says so. The test locks every pair at 165 characters as a watchdog. What this rule does NOT close, declared: the list is by tool NAME — a new tool that records an artifact enters it in the same PR (the test ties each name to a spec that exists, but does not discover a new tool). Whether the model FOLLOWS both clauses in the same message is what the paid validation of AT-167 measures; the DeepSeek and Anthropic tokenizers remain unmeasured. documents.t: The paid validation of AT-167 found, for an author with en preference (C06/C12), the ask_structured_questions call with prose in English and the form questions in Portuguese — in treated DeepSeek, 8 of the 15 replies of C06+C12. The cause is the product's, and lives in one place only: the tool description said label was "the question text, in pt-BR". It was a SECOND language guidance, fixed, outside the facade of RN-622, competing with it on every call of the Criativo and the PO (both use the SAME spec). The mechanism is removing the competing guidance, not adding another. The description now says "the question text, in the language of your reply (also applies to options)", and the example, which stays in Portuguese, is marked "the texts follow the language of your reply". It does not name ANY language: WHICH language it is remains decided only by the ephemeral message of Engine.Harness.IdiomaDaResposta, and the EngineApiClient facade does not change. The RN-622/623 guidance stays byte for byte. Zero extra tokens in the 50 of the ceiling. ask_structured_questions stays OUTSIDE @ferramentas_de_artefato (it is a question to the person of the turn, RN-623 item 4), so an en author in a pt-BR project gets the questions in English — which is what is wanted. Cost, where it falls. The description travels on every call that carries the tool, with any author: measured with gpt-tokenizer, only the text that changed, +23 tokens in cl100k and +19 in o200k (the label line 18/17 → 29/27; the example's 8/6 → 20/15). It is not the guidance moving into the description — the sentence points to it without naming a language, and what went away was precisely the sentence that named one. Guard. No harness tool description (the 22 of Engine.Harness.Tools.*) may cite pt-BR, (en), "in English", "em português" or "em inglês" — that of emit_artifact, which requires the payload KEYS "in ENGLISH", is left out because it speaks of a contract, not of text for the person. What this rule does NOT close, declared: the paid before/after measurement did not run (no OpenRouter key on the machine of the change) — the "before" is AT-167's (treated DeepSeek: 8 of 15 replies of C06+C12 with the form in Portuguese), and the "after" is an owner's pending item: pnpm --filter @brabo/scripts idioma:validar --arquivo-de-chave ~/.config/brabo/openrouter-test.env --bracos tratamento --casos C06,C12 --rodadas 5 --teto-usd 0.5 --saida ~/.cache/brabo/validacao-idioma/at-282, followed by idioma:validar --relatorio --saida in the same folder and the review of the form (formulario label of idioma:revisar). Suggested ceiling US$ 0.50: the whole treated arm cost US$ 0.21 (DeepSeek) and US$ 0.94 (Haiku) over 17 cases, and these are 2. The script reads the description from the product file, so it measures the new text without a copy. If the form stays in Portuguese with the neutral description, the next step is a conditional clause in the guidance (only when the call carries ask_structured_questions), and it has to fit in the worst case of RN-623 (44 / 37), which is already at ~48 with the frame. documents.t: RN-618 left the "confirmed detected" step ready and empty. Maintainer decision (AT-168 answers 4, 6 and 7): detect, ASK whether the language is right, and the confirmed one becomes the default — per person, global, with the question on the screen where the language is already shown and corrected. The yardstick is ONE, and lives in the api. The heuristic of AT-080, measured by AT-160 (contrastive markers of pt/es/en, the stripping of code, log, quotation, URL and identifier), moved from scripts/idioma/ to apps/api/src/domain/iam/heuristica-de-idioma.ts, and the instrument REEXPORTS it from there — what the product runs is what the instrument measures. The rule of WHAT counts as evidence (only actor user; in the form, only the answers, and the echo with the agent's labels skipped) is also a single one, evidenciasDoAutor, used by the real-corpus extraction and by the detection. Local, no LLM, no new dependency. The sample comes from the event log, the hysteresis is recomputed. Detection reads the person's 11 most recent pieces of evidence across ALL sessions (the window of 10 plus the one the hysteresis recomputes) and decides when the TWO last evaluations of the sample point to the same language (idiomaConcordante). No detection state is stored: the evaluation of the previous message is recomputed with the window that ended at it. The read is served by a PARTIAL index (session_events_evidencia_de_idioma_idx, actor user and the two evidence types): measured with 200 thousand events, 0.056 ms through the index against 13.5 ms for the scan without it. The thresholds are PROVISIONAL. PARAMETROS_PROVISORIOS are the candidates of AT-080 with ONE difference, the minimum evidence of 10 words and not 20 — in the SYNTHETIC corpus, at 10 the coverage of decidable cases goes from 42.2% to 58.9% with the same three errors (all in a language outside the three). List at080; threshold 0.8, margin 0.3, sample 10 messages / 2,000 characters, hysteresis 2. The synthetic corpus was written by the same hand that wrote the heuristic: none of these numbers is calibrated, and the owner recalibrates them with the real corpus (pnpm --filter @brabo/scripts idioma:medir --real), changing the object, which is the only place the api reads them from. When it asks. GET .../sessions/:sessionId/response-language returns detectionQuestion with the language to ask about, or null. It does not ask when: the detection does not agree (short text, "ok", code, log, mixed); the effective one comes from an EXPLICIT choice — session override or Account —, because confirming would record a step BELOW them and the reply would not change; the detected one is already the effective one, compared by SUBTAG (pt does not diverge from pt-BR — the heuristic only knows the language); or the person already declined that language. Detection never changes anything on its own. Only POST /users/me/preferences/detected-language writes: confirm writes the pair detected_language + detected_language_confirmed_at (the CHECK of RN-618) and deletes the old decline of the same language — and it is 409 deteccao_mudou, without writing, when the messages no longer point to the language (the column says "detected" and cannot hold what the heuristic did not detect); decline writes the decline to detected_language_declines (one row per person and language, with the date), and THAT language is not asked about again. What is stored is the language and the person's decision — never country, nationality or proficiency. Where the question appears. In a small card anchored just below the language indicator of the session bar (RN-620): "Detectamos que você escreve em espanhol (es) — usar espanhol (es) nas respostas?", with "Usar", "Não" and "Agora não". No modal, without covering the composer; "Agora não" only hides it on this screen, without writing, and the question comes back on the next read. Sending a message (or answering a form) rereads the indicator, because the new message is the evidence that can make the question appear. Failure never blocks anything. Detection runs on the language READ, and not inside SendAgentMessageUseCase: the evidence is already in the event log, the question survives a page reload and appears in any session, and sending the message does not go through it — it gains no latency and has no way to fail because of it. On the read, any failure (database, heuristic) becomes a warning and detectionQuestion: null; the language keeps being shown. Cost: CPU measured on the synthetic corpus, on this machine — 11.6 µs to clean and classify a message, 110 µs per detection (11 messages, two evaluations), plus the indexed read of item 2. Zero tokens. What this rule does NOT close, declared: the heuristic knows three languages, and the language list is open — Galician and French can become es/pt (the synthetic errors), and under this rule the cost is a wrong question, which the person declines. A message in Spanish in a Portuguese window leaves the sample undetermined while it is in it (no question, no change). And the heuristic file cannot have import: the instrument runs it by type stripping, and scripts/idioma/ has its own tsconfig without verbatimModuleSyntax to accept the exports of a CommonJS module. documents.t: Maintainer decision (AT-236, 2026-09-28) and, on the criterion, of 2026-09-29: before each chat call of an agent, the api asks the Jev (typesafe/jev-1.13, OpenRouter's Decisions API) which tool fits the step, and the chat provider receives only the menu that the P3 policy derives from that answer. The mechanism is in ADR 0179; the adoption decision, with the numbers, too. When. Only with the turn model's provider equal to openrouter, with two or more tools in the request, with an agent in the turn (except the Anamnese and the compaction summarizer), without catalogoCompleto requested by the engine and with the workspace switched on (workspaces.tool_router_enabled, on by default, PUT workspaces/:workspaceId/tool-router, owner). Any condition fails: no call, no event. With a provider ≠ openrouter the workspace is not even read. The key is the workspace holder's, the same as the chat's (RN-058). The policy is P3 and it only restricts. Menu = {Jev's choice, previous tool of the SAME execution}. The Jev's responder_sem_ferramenta, or no previous tool in the step's catalog, leaves the WHOLE catalog. There is no tool_choice (the model can still reply in text) and there is no confidence threshold in v1: the confidence is recorded and it is up to AT-239 to propose one. Adoption criterion: 80%, owner decision of 2026-09-29 — Jev top-1 73% (66–79), P3 menu coverage 91% (85.1–94), top-2 90%; coverage is the CEILING of end-to-end accuracy (62%–91% in replay), and the real validation is AT-239. The state is what the product has before the step, cut from the messages the engine already sends, without a database read: agente = the agentId; contexto = the beginning (1,500 characters) of the system message that the ToolLoop puts in front (apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tool_loop.ex:98, system_msg, assembled by system_prompt/1 at :316); pedido = the last user message — in execution agents the initial message of the loop (apps/engine/lib/engine/dev/dev_agent_server.ex:484, initial_message/2, or the correction one at :523), in conversational ones the person's utterance; and passos_recentes = the last 6 tool calls after that message, one entry per call, argument and result cut at 500 characters — the result comes from the tool message the loop appends (tool_loop.ex:293, concluir_despacho/5, with toolCallId). The current execution is "after the last user" because ctx.messages restarts at each ToolLoop.run. Ceiling of 8 thousand tokens; exceeded, fallback estado_grande. The turn never fails because of the Jev. HTTP error, timeout (2,000 ms, TOOL_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_MS), network error, unexpected JSON, choice outside the options, large state and collision with the reserved name: the provider receives the whole catalog and the event carries motivoDaQueda and origemDaQueda (infra, modelo or codigo — RN-059), never silent. The policy does not change. The Jev does not approve, does not deny and does not choose a model. A chosen tool that requires approval still requires it; a call to a tool outside the menu is dispatched as always and the event only records foraDoCardapio. The iteration ceiling is the same as before (the call to the Jev is not an iteration). Per-step record. The engine writes tool_router.decided, in the EngineApiClient facade for all agents, with menu before and after, choice, confidence, second option, aplicado, fallback, latency, real cost and foraDoCardapio. The api writes ONE token_usage row for the Jev: actor = the agent itself (the spend goes into the area budget, ADR 0110), modelName = typesafe/jev-1.13, modelId null, estimated = false, costMicros = the usage.cost of the response, IMPLIED price per million (cost ÷ tokens) with price_implicit = true — keeps tokens × price = cost of RN-044 without inventing a catalog price. Without usage.cost in the response there is no row. The budget gate is not reconsulted between the Jev and the chat. Getting out of the dead end. Restricted menu and the model replies without calling a tool (not even in recoverable text), with no provider error: the facade repeats the step ONCE with catalogoCompleto: true, which skips the Jev. In the stream, only if nothing was written to the person. It asks for more tools, never one the agent did not have. What this rule does NOT close, declared: the screen (showing that the step was routed, with the confidence, and the "choosing tool" strip through the tool_routing_started frame) belongs to apps/web; the gain is AT-239's; a timeout that OpenRouter billed without returning usage.cost does not enter token_usage; the endpoint is ALPHA and the manual smoke (jev-tool-router.smoke.spec.ts, ceiling US$ 0.05) is what flags the change. documents.t: The real use of 2026-09-29 measured the cost of the owner talking in one session and the dev agents proposing in another: their approvals never appeared where he was, 45 of 173 clicks on "Sempre permitir" came back 409 (the card was still clickable after the action had already left pending), and reopening the session with a turn in progress gave back a free composer and the 409. The four fixes are SCREEN fixes — the api, the engine and every ceiling stay as they are. The card goes inert and says the api's sentence (AT-256). ApprovalCard holds the buttons while the decision is in flight (the double click was a certain 409) and, when the call returns a promise that rejects, shows the sentence the api sent ON the card — never a generic toast. A 409 (the action is no longer pending) leaves the buttons inert with the reason in text until the list swaps the card for the outcome line. The caller returns the promise and refetches the list EVEN on refusal (finally): it is ONE invalidation per click, no new poll, and the invalidation uses the channel and budget of RN-579. Reopening the session resumes the turn from the log (AT-268). The screen's turn state is local useState and was lost on leaving. On the first read of the events of an active session, turnoEmCursoNoLog looks at the most recent persisted agent.status of each agent (the same read as turnoTerminouNoLog, from RN-578); whatever is working reopens the strip and locks the composer through the same entry points as an accepted turn (iniciarTurnoDoAgente + acompanharTurnoPeloLog), and the read of the log tail closes it. It runs ONCE per mounted session (a recurring effect would rearm the strip with the old working still in the cache). The working left by an engine restart is closed by a new event at boot (RN-586), so what remains is a live turn. It does not queue messages: a message with a turn in progress is still refused with a named 409 — the queue is a pending decision of the owner (AT-267). Pending items of OTHER sessions of the project appear in the chat (AT-265). PendenciasDeOutrasSessoes reads GET /projects/:id/actions?status=pending (the same endpoint as the PRs tab and the "needs you" panel) and draws the ones that were NOT born in this session — this session's are already decided by the thread. It is a SHORTCUT and never a substitute (RN-467): the SAME ApprovalCard, the same endpoints, with the sessionId the action itself carries; onActivateAutoMode stays out (it is policy, not decision). The two queues — approvals and PR merges — have their OWN title and count and are never summed, and each row states the originating session. The drawing has a ceiling of 20 cards, and the excess is stated ("Mostrando N de M"): a declared cut, as in RN-180. The poll is the session's (5 s with the channel down, the 15 s fallback with it live — intervaloDaSessao), because the session channel does not announce another session's writes. "Mergear" on the card of the open PR (AT-266). Under the card of an executed pr_open, and only when the action.pr_open event carries the PR id and there is no live git_merge (pending, approved or auto-approved) for it, the button PROPOSES the git_merge through the same endpoint as the PRs tab (actor user, in this session). The proposal appears in the thread as the usual card, with Aprovar/Negar: the confirmation is the same and belongs to the human — merge into a protected branch remains unconditional require_approval (RN-418), without auto-approval, without "sempre permitir", without auto mode. The dedupe and the api's refusals (PR already merged, merge already proposed — RN-663) reach the owner as the api's sentence; a pending gate is not a refusal, it is a text notice next to the button. The role is the ENDPOINT's, and the gap is declared. Deciding an action and proposing an action require developer (actions.controller.ts); the screen uses roleAtLeast over the WORKSPACE role, because the Session does not fetch project_members — the same single gap of RN-471, declared here and not closed. Whoever does not reach it SEES the pending item and the button, with the controls inert and the reason in text (bloqueio of ApprovalCard): what is taken away is the control, never the information. What this rule does NOT close, declared: (a) "Mergear" does not propose AND approve in a single click — it is two clicks, the proposal and the confirmation, on purpose; (b) resuming the turn reads the window of events already loaded, and an agent.status outside it is not seen (not knowing is not "is working"); (c) the list of pending items from other sessions has the ceiling of 20 cards, and the rest stays in the Aprovações tab; (d) architecture pending items and the Psicólogo's hypotheses still have NO inline decision (there is no ApprovalCard for them). documents.t: qa-automacao runs several commands and each one may ask for human approval. The QaLeadServer already stopped the area when run/5 returned {:awaiting, _} (finding AB, ADR 0052), but the RESUMPTION (retomar/3, when the decision arrives) returned the result of a loop that could suspend ANOTHER time — and that second {:awaiting, _} went into the list of collected results as if it were a verdict. On consolidating, registrar_resultado/5 had no clause for it and the GenServer crashed (FunctionClauseError, measured on 29/09/2026: 06:55:01 and 07:00:10), leaving the three delivered tasks in awaiting_qa forever, with no verdict and no named outcome. A single place decides what to do with a subagent's result (tratar_resultado/6), whether it comes from run/5 or from retomar/3. {:awaiting, _} keeps the in-flight state (keyed by the new action), keeps the gate_states row in in_progress with the subagent and STOPS the area: no verdict, without blocking the task, without recording the delegation. The resumer is the same {:action_settled, _} of Engine.Dev.Wake (ADR 0086), as many times as needed. A result the lead does not know never crashes nor vanishes (RN-059): it becomes {:blocked, …} with origin codigo (a clause is missing here, it is not infra, model or policy), which registrar_resultado/5 records as a failed delegation and QaLead.consolidar/1 turns into a block of the task with the origin. Declared, not resolved: an engine restart with the lead suspended loses the Wake subscription (accepted gap of ADR 0086); the GateRescuer restarts the whole area (ADR 0067), it does not resume the ctx. This rule does not change ADR 0090 (the moment of QA-strategy) nor the subagent's iteration ceiling. documents.t: "Who is active" and "who receives the composer" came from the agent.activated seen in the 200-event window (latest: true). In a long session the activations of the Arquiteto and the Infra left the window; handoff offers addressed to them went back to looking acceptable and the "hi" went to the last agent that still appeared. It is the defect class of RN-180 (a silent ceiling makes the screen assert about what it did not read), already closed for the presence of QA/SecOps in RN-568. The rule: the project summary (RN-090) returns roster.activatedAgents — the agents with at least one agent.activated in the most recent session, one per agent, the most recently activated (by seq) first. Four decisions: The source is still the event log. No derived column, no index and no migration: the field enters the SAME per-session scan that already computes executionActivated/gatesEverOpened (array_agg ... filter), so the number of database round trips of the summary does not change (the constant-count spec still holds). The reserved migration 0066 was not used. No new HTTP per poll. The field travels in the summary the screens already read (RN-579). The client ADDS it to the window and only trusts it with the summary of the SAME session (latestSessionId === sessionId), as in RN-568: activation is monotonic (an activated agent does not deactivate), so the window only gives false negatives. A summary of another session does not count; with no summary, the window decides alone. The api says what happened, not who receives. The explicit, visible recipient in the chat (AT-251) and acceptance by handoffId (AT-253) consume this field in the web and are NOT part of this rule. Declared gap: this round only delivers the api CONTRACT. apps/web (session-readiness.ts, session-handoffs.ts) keeps reading the window until AT-251/AT-253 start consuming roster.activatedAgents. Closed in RN-631 (AT-251): the composer recipient and the handoff offers of the Session screen ADD roster.activatedAgents to the window, with the same-session guard. criativoActive/arquitetoActive (session-readiness.ts) still read only the window. Where it lives: apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.ts:212 (activatedAgents); apps/api/src/application/ports/projects-summary-repository.port.ts:32 (activatedAgents) Tests: apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.spec.ts ("activatedAgents cobre ativações anteriores à janela de 200 eventos" and "activatedAgents é da sessão MAIS RECENTE: ativação de sessão antiga não vale") Origin: AT-252

documents.t: Under --cap-drop ALL the container's root lacks CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE and cannot write to the project folder, which belongs to the operator's uid: npm install gave EACCES for every dev agent (AT-247, ADR 0180). The api measures, the broker composes. container-spec returns usuarioDaPasta (stat of the folder for the container/mounted modes; null if the folder is not reached, if the owner is root or if the project is runner). The broker copies it into spec.usuario and the adapter emits --user uid:gid and --env HOME=/tmp. It never comes from the requester. start has no body and the exec body ignores extra fields; exec inherits the container's user. The broker revalidates. Integers in 1..2^31-1; 0 is refused naming usuario.uid/usuario.gid (root is the absent one, "as always"). It does not loosen containment: --cap-drop ALL, one bind, a two-valued network and five operations remain. An already created container only changes when recreated. documents.t: The QA/SecOps gate ends in awaiting_user and nothing else touched the task's status: in the real use of 09/29 pr-6 was merged three times and the tasks stayed in in_review (AT-275). After the merge, never in its place. git_merge is still unconditional require_approval (RN-418); the rule runs INSIDE ExecuteGitActionUseCase, in the transaction that records the merge result, and only when the provider returned state: 'merged' (an open PR, or a merge that failed, does not touch the task). The task is found through the PR that opened it. Every pr_open of the project whose pullRequestId is that of the merged PR and that carries storyTaskId in the payload. A PR without a task (infra, ADR) changes nothing. Idempotent. TaskRepository.markDoneIfNotDone is an UPDATE … WHERE status <> 'done': a repeated merge of the same PR returns null, does not move it again and does NOT write the event. When it moves, it writes ONE immutable backlog.task_status_changed event (cause: 'pr_merged', pullRequestId, actionId), append-only, with no UPDATE on an events table. No migration. Declared boundary (AT-249). This rule does NOT refuse merging an already merged PR nor consult gate_status. Refusing the already merged PR (and the repeated proposal) came later, in RN-663, before the merge reaches here; the pending gate, by owner decision, is only a notice on screen. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/execute-git-action.use-case.ts:295 (settleMerge), apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/backlog.repository.ts:480 (markDoneIfNotDone) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/execute-git-action.use-case.spec.ts ("git_merge marca a tarefa como done": happy, repeated, open PR/failed merge, PR without task) Origin: AT-275

documents.t: The dark theme stops being petrol blue and becomes neutral black with a soft terracotta accent; the light one becomes the neutral of the same family (ADR 0181). The mechanism of RN-184 does not change — the pairs are measured in both themes, with the same floor —; what changes is what is demanded: The dark theme's debt became a floor. The five pairs that RN-184 left locked by number (3.89 / 3.10 / 3.88 / 3.88 / 4.41) pass 4.5:1 in both themes, and the test rejects whoever brings them back down — it no longer "records". The final value came from MEASUREMENT: the draft's --text-muted (#71717a) repeated the debt and was refused (#86868f in dark, #696972 in light), and muted stays BELOW --text-secondary on the three surfaces, which the test also demands. Text over a solid brand/state background passes AA. The dark theme's --on-accent is the neutral black (5.61:1 over the accent, 7.25:1 on hover, 7.65:1 over --success, 5.24:1 over --danger); the "known exception" of the primary button ceases to exist, and the accent's hue stays terracotta (10°–30°) in both themes. UI color only comes from a token. Whatever paints through a runtime library (Mermaid, xterm, minimap) reads the active theme's token and, without it, falls back to the default of TOKENS_PADRAO — a copy of :root that the test checks against design/tokens.css. Agent color is always var(--token); the three agents without a semantic one have --agent-* per theme, measured at 3:1. And no CSS module uses a var(--x) that nobody declares. documents.t: In the real use of 09/29, 45 of 173 clicks on "Sempre permitir" returned 409 (AT-310): the pattern was recorded BEFORE approving, and an action that had already left pending (double click, the same pending item in two panels, another tab) threw 409 with the pattern ALREADY recorded and WITHOUT the permission.granted event. Same transaction, after the transition. ApproveActionUseCase accepts an aoAprovar that runs INSIDE the decision's transaction, after assertTransition passes and before execution; it is through it that the pattern (permissions.json/allow or agent_autonomy, RN-509) and the permission.granted are recorded. "Approve first, record later" in separate transactions was refused: it would trade the defect for an approved (and even executed) action with the pattern failing afterwards. agent_autonomy and the event are atomic with the decision; permissions.json is a file and does not enter a transaction — it is only written after the transition is valid, and failing to write it undoes the approval. What remains, declared, is the window of the COMMIT failing after the file was written. The event goes with the recording, and only with it. A pattern that already exists is not rewritten nor narrated again (padraoGravado: false). An already approved action is a named success. If the transition is refused because the action is already approved/auto_approved/executed/failed, the response is 201 with desfecho: 'ja_aprovada' (the normal path returns 'aprovada'), without executing again, recording the pattern only if it is missing — with the event. An invalid transition coming from EXECUTION, after the decision has been confirmed, does NOT become ja_aprovada: it propagates as always. A DENIED action is still 409, named (reason: 'acao_ja_recusada'), without recording pattern or event: freeing forever what someone just denied is not idempotency. Ceilings intact. git push/PR/deploy, sudo/doas (motivoDeRecusaSempreAprovar, RN-418) and container_remove are still refused with 400 BEFORE any state read — including with the action already approved. The pattern is still the action's EXACT one (generalization by verb is AT-257, outside here). The ceiling TYPES too (AT-320). Measured in the audit of 09/30: the api only refused the git push TYPED in the terminal; the TYPED git_push passed and recorded GitPush() in allow (or module autonomy), and the ApprovalCard offered the button. TIPOS_SEM_SEMPRE_PERMITIR is the SINGLE list — git_push, pr_open, git_merge (whole: the GitMerge() pattern would apply to every target), container_remove, instruction_patch, parallelize, raise_max_parallel — and motivoDeRecusaDoSempreAprovar judges terminal by the command and the rest by type. The refusal is 400 with reason: 'teto_do_sempre_permitir' and actionType. The web hides the button through the copy in apps/web/src/lib/sempre-permitir.ts, checked against the api's by test; a terminal command keeps the button (repeating the parser on screen would be a second yardstick) and receives the api's refusal. When it was born, it did NOT change decide() nor the seeding; since RN-689 both change — git_push/pr_open are in the decide() ceiling and activation seeds only git_commit —, and the pattern the click would record for them would be inert. documents.t: The composer message's recipient was DERIVED: "the most recent agent.activated within the 200-event window" (finding 9-fix). It was a default recipient on the SCREEN side — the defect class that RN-584 closed in the engine — and it was INVISIBLE: the composer did not say who the message went to, and accepting a handoff on this screen changed nothing beyond the log. In the real use of 09/29 the session had handoff.accepted to the Infra and then to the Arquiteto, and the user's "hi" was answered by the Arquiteto without the screen saying so. And the acceptance card matched the offer to the event by the ACTOR/toAgent pair (e.actor.id === offeredHandoff.fromAgent), although handoff.offered has carried handoffId from the start (AT-251). The rule: The OPTIONS are the agents that converse (AGENTES_DE_CHAT) and that are already in the session: agent.activated in the window, roster.activatedAgents from the project summary (RN-630, the WHOLE session, only with the summary of the SAME session, in the mold of RN-568) or an ACCEPTED handoff (the list of handoffs has no window). The last two terms are RN-180: the agent does not vanish from the selector because the activation left the 200 events. In the creative session the Criativo is an option before being activated, because the first message activates it (finding 3). The recipient is what the person CHOSE — in the composer's "Para" selector, or by accepting a handoff ON THIS screen (the gesture of calling that agent; a failed acceptance changes nothing). Nothing in the log chooses for them: an acceptance made in another tab or through another path only adds an option. A SINGLE option is the recipient, and the composer names it before sending. It is not a default in the sense of RN-584 — there is no other agent the message could go to. Two or more options and no valid choice: no recipient. The "Enviar" (and Enter) is locked and the screen says in TEXT that a choice is needed — never "the most recent". Zero options is the session chat without an agent (SSE), and the screen says so too. Revised by RN-682: zero options also locks sending — the consultative session without an agent asks for an agent, and SSE to the raw model is no longer called by the screen. The choice is remembered per session in localStorage — a convenience for the viewer (without storage the screen just asks for the choice again), never product state. "Parar" stops the agent OF THE TURN (turnoAgentRef, streamingAgent, statusAgent), and only in its absence the recipient: changing the selector in the middle of another agent's turn must not stop the wrong one. The model shown in the topbar follows the recipient. The offer is matched by the payload's handoffId, never by the actor: each handoff.offered is the card of its own offer, with no pair to confuse nor a "most recent" to choose. Offers to an already activated agent (window OR roster.activatedAgents) do not become acceptable again. Every pending offer is actionable, and none hides another (AT-253). The card picked ONE offer (handoffs.find, the oldest pending), and the MANUAL handoff (ADR 0109, RN-441) — recorded with the PERSON as actor, and therefore never matched by the actor — had no "Aceitar" and hid the following offers. Now every pending offer to an agent that converses (except the Infra's, which has its own card, RN-499) has the button on its event; two pending ones to the SAME agent give a single button, the most recent one's, and accepting it removes the other through activeFor. The manual handoff pill says "Handoff manual" instead of the person's id. "Already in the session" is read from window-LESS sources scoped to the REQUESTED session (review of PR #759). The summary's roster.activatedAgents belongs to the project's MOST RECENT session, and activating execution CREATES a new session that becomes that one: the chat session lost the whole source and went back to depending on the 200 window. The sum now has THREE sources — the summary, only when it is this session's; the handoffs of THIS session (whoever received an accepted one and whoever OFFERED one, who was in it); and the per-agent spend of THIS session (GET .../token-usage, aggregated without a window: an agent with a row there ran a turn, and only an activated agent runs a turn). Each source only fixes false negatives, and spend is proof of PRESENCE, never of absence. Declared gap: an agent activated by a direct start, without a handoff, that never ran a turn, in a session that is no longer the most recent, still depends on the window — and whoever has a role below developer (the minimum of the spend route) lacks the third source. Closing it requires the activation aggregate PER SESSION in the api; it was not done here. A pending offer whose event left the window gets a button in the fixed strip above the composer (review of PR #759). The actionable card belongs to the handoff.offered, and the list of handoffs has no window: in a long session the offer stayed offered and without a button anywhere. The criterion is the CUT, not absence — the offer is older than the oldest event in the window (a just-created offer whose event has not arrived yet does not flash in the strip), and an empty window does not assert a cut. The strip has only the acceptance; the "Ativar execução" shortcut of the Dev Lead card stays in the thread. The guard of RN-584 (scripts/ci/destinos-do-composer.spec.ts) now reads DESTINATARIO_DA_SESSAO_CRIATIVA instead of the literal from SessionPage.tsx: every destination the composer can give still has its own clause in the engine. No api or engine change. Where: apps/web/src/lib/session-destinatario.ts:210 (agentesEmConversa), :237 (resolverDestinatario), :272 (useDestinatarioDoChat), :116 (useAtivadosNaSessaoInteira), :141 (ativadosSemJanela); apps/web/src/routes/SessionComposer.tsx:287 (destinatarioRow), :193 (ofertasForaDaJanela); apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx:350 (aceitarHandoff); apps/web/src/routes/session-timeline-montagem.tsx:547 (handoffIdDoEvento), :555 (origem); apps/web/src/lib/session-handoffs.ts:68 (activeFor), :120 (ofertasAcionaveis), :142 (ofertasForaDaJanela) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.destinatario-do-chat.test.tsx (choice → sent to the chosen one; two agents without a choice do not send and say why; single option; accepted handoff outside the window; summary of the same session and of another; acceptance that switches and acceptance that fails; remembered choice; session without agent; most recent execution session with the activation read from the handoffs and from this session's spend, and the refused spend; offer outside the window in the strip, and an offer in the window or newer than it outside it), apps/web/src/lib/session-destinatario.test.ts (ativadosSemJanela), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.handoff-inline-e-links.test.tsx (an old offer of ANOTHER handoffId stays mute), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.handoff-manual.test.tsx (the manual one gets "Aceitar"; the pending manual one does not hide the following offer; two to the same agent become one button) Origin: AT-251, AT-253

documents.t: Two reads of the Session screen left the handoff stale (AT-293, AT-294): The MANUAL handoff does not hide "Estou pronto para produzir" nor "Confirmar arquitetura pronta" (AT-293). prontidaoJaDeclarada and arquiteturaJaDeclarada only asked "is there a handoff leaving the Criativo/Arquiteto?", and the manual handoff (ADR 0109, RN-441) records as fromAgent the LAST activated agent (request-manual-handoff.use-case.ts): requesting a manual handoff to the Staff with the Criativo active hid the readiness button with no readiness at all declared. The manual one is recognized by the human ACTOR of handoff.offered (matched by handoffId, RN-631) — the api's Handoff does not carry the actor. Outside the 200 window the actor is unknown, and then: for the Criativo the artifactId counts (the readiness handoff carries the product_brief, criativo_server.ex; the manual one never carries an artifact); for the Arquiteto the two automatic ones carry no artifact, so the one of unknown origin keeps counting, as before. Declared gap: the durable mark would be the actor (or a manual mark) on the api's Handoff itself; it was not done here (the api belongs to the lifecycle lane, ADR 0182). An offer to an agent already ACTIVE in another session of the project is not actionable (AT-294). "Active" was the SESSION's: after "Ativar execução", the Dev Lead runs in the execution session, and the offer to him in the chat session still had "Aceitar". Now the offer (the thread card, the out-of-window strip and the Infra card) adds to "already joined this session" the summary's roster.activatedAgents, which is the project's MOST RECENT session — the execution one, once activated. activeFor is still THIS session's, because it is what the manual handoff selector uses. Declared gap: sessions that are neither this one nor the most recent are not seen; closing it requires a PER-PROJECT activation aggregate in the api, which does not exist. No api or engine change. documents.t: Execution runs in a NEW session (RN-135, RN-139), and the chat session the click came from may even close. The "Ativar execução" shortcut of the handoff card to the Dev Lead (RN-137) — and the merge with the acceptance (RN-161) — left the person in the chat session, looking at the place the work left from (AT-295). Now handleActivateExecution reads the sessionId that POST .../execution/activate returns and takes the screen to it, with the notice "Levando você à sessão de execução.". Without sessionId in the response, with the same id as the current session, or without anyone to navigate (the screen mounted outside the route), only the usual notice, and the screen stays. A refused activation does not navigate and shows the api's sentence. The one that navigates is the ROUTE (irParaSessao, the router's navigate): the screen does not depend on the router. documents.t: The real use of 09/29 hit the user's 300 req/min ceiling (RN-579) with two tabs open: 192 × 429 at 07:14, 106 of them on GET /projects/:id/sessions and 20 on GET /projects/:id, and three approve_always clicks refused in the middle (AT-278). RN-579 had put the SESSION screen reads under the channel; the PROJECT ones and the other screens that listen to the channel were left out. The ceiling does NOT change: what drops is the request. The rule: A project read that no channel announces polls at 15s (INTERVALO_DO_PROJETO_MS), UNCONDITIONALLY. The session:<id> channel only announces writes of its own session; the project's session list and the rail counters (approvals of the most recent session, pending merges of the project, stories to promote, architecture pending items, hypotheses) change by writes of ANY session — there is no notice to wait for, so the mechanism is a long poll, in the same fallback that RN-579 already accepts for the session. It applies to useProjectSessions/useLatestSession (they were 5s), to the five counters of the ProjectPage frame and to the architecture of the Executores tab. The tab that shows the data as its SUBJECT (Backlog, Arquitetura, PRs) keeps its own poll, and the fastest observer dictates the key's pace. Whoever writes in this tab still invalidates the key immediately. Whoever only needs the data on click does not poll. Each row of /containers reads its project's most recent session to PROPOSE stop/remove/start; at a 5s poll it was 12 req/min PER PROJECT — nine projects, 108/min from that page alone, the number that matches the 106 in the log. useLatestSession(projectId, false): mount and window focus are enough. Every screen that listens to the channel goes through criarInvalidadorDoCanal. The Executores and Visão geral tabs invalidated the events on EVERY event.appended, with no window: a dev agent in a burst (10 notices/s) made 630 event GETs per minute in the Executores tab alone. Now both use the SAME invalidator as the Session screen (window per target, the TYPE decides the target), and get as a bonus what was missing: the dev agent's action proposal invalidates the actions immediately, instead of waiting for the 15s fallback. The Visão geral requests the backlog on every notice (the blocked tasks come from it) through the extras parameter, with the same window. Waiting for the runner stops when it is over. EsperaDoRunner only stopped the GET /projects/:id probe (3s) at the CEILING; once the connection was confirmed, the ceiling's effect exited early and the probe kept going forever — 20 req/min while the panel was on screen, and, being the fastest observer of ['project', id], dragging the page's whole key. Now it stops at the ceiling OR on confirmation. Numbers (duas-abas.orcamento.test.tsx, the real screens — Shell, SessionPage, ProjectPage on the Executores tab, ContainersPage — over a fetch that counts per route; each tab measured alone, because two tabs are two JS contexts, and summed; req/min, dev → this rule): Scenario Before After session chat + Executores, live channel 70 + 138 = 208 70 + 72 = 142 same, dev agent in a burst (10 notices/s) 70 + 764 = 834 70 + 97 = 167 same, channel that never connects 155 + 186 = 341 155 + 120 = 275 /containers with 9 projects 132 (108 from /sessions) 24 What this rule does NOT close: with the channel DOWN in both tabs, 275/min is still close to the ceiling — the Session screen goes back to the usual 3s (RN-579: never worse than it was), and 25 req/min of slack vanish with a burst of clicks. The Shell keeps polling projects-summary and execution/session at 5s and, in the chat tab, the events of the EXECUTION session at 3s (the tab does not have its channel) — 44 of the 70 req/min of the chat tab. A session list created in another tab shows up here within 15s (it was 5s). The incident's number was MATCHED, not reproduced: the log did not say which tabs were open, and the reading that /containers was in one of them is inference from 106 ≈ 9 × 12. documents.t: handoffs only recorded offered/accepted, with no expiry, supersession or dedupe: a double click on "architecture ready" gave 2× Infra and 2× Dev Lead, and an offer to an already active agent stayed actionable forever (AT-291, ADR 0182). At most ONE offered per (project, target). decidirOferta decides: with no pending one, it creates; pending in the SAME session and with no new artifact (the new one is null or equal), it returns the existing one (desfecho: ja_oferecido, no row nor event); any other case creates the new one and replaces the pending one (substituiu_oferta) — returning the old one would lose the new artifact, or leave the requester with nothing to accept in the session they are in. Whoever replaces records. The row becomes superseded and a handoff.superseded event is born (handoffId, toAgent, motivo, substitutaId) in the session of the OLD offer, actor system, even with the session closed. The original handoff.offered is not touched. Serialized per target. CreateHandoffUseCase runs in a transaction with pg_advisory_xact_lock of the (project, target) pair: two tabs arriving together produce ONE row. Duplicates from before converge on the next offer or activation, with an event; the migration rewrites no row. An already active agent receives no offer: 409 reason: agente_ja_ativo, without row or event. Active = agent.activated in a NON-terminal session of the project. The message is the text the model reads: offer_handoff passes it on verbatim, and FalhaDeTurno.origem/1 classifies it as politica. Activating supersedes. ActivateAgentUseCase (acceptance and direct activation) and ActivateExecutionUseCase (per dev-<modulo>) supersede, after activating, every pending offer to the agent in any session of the project; the accepted one is not touched, and a refused activation supersedes nothing. "Architecture ready" is idempotent. OfferInfraHandoffUseCase does not trigger the target (infra, dev-lead) that already has a pending offer or is active; with both like that, it neither records nor calls the engine (desfecho: ja_oferecido, jaAtendidos with each one's reason). documents.t: The AppSec created three offers per story with run_design, to the same three targets — N stories, 3N pending offers (AT-292, which merges the vault's AT-273 by owner decision; ADR 0182). It asks in seAusente mode. criar_handoffs_appsec/3 calls EngineApiClient.create_handoff_if_absent/5, which sends seAusente: true to the SAME internal route. The api decides under the target's lock (RN-635): with a pending offer in ANY session of the project, it returns the existing one (desfecho: ja_oferecido) and does not supersede it; with the target active, 409 agente_ja_ativo. Asking beforehand, through the engine, would race with another offer. "Already handled" is not a failure. The two responses above go on without agent.error. A real failure (5xx, network) is still narrated per target, with origin (RN-116, RN-361). The artifact stays. The artifact.threat_model is recorded BEFORE and regardless; what stops being born is the repeated offer. documents.t: The visual survey of Round 29 (finding X3, AT-319) measured three defects in the thread cut of RN-177, all in the same function: (1) the "last 5" counted entries, and the handoff, approval and story cards counted as one message each — in a short conversation, the first question and the first answer went to the collapsed history; (2) the cut fell where the count said, possibly leaving the question collapsed and the answer open; (3) the history was grouped by origin, in the order of the origins, and the "LLM" group came before "Usuário" — expanded, the Criativo's answer appeared ABOVE the question that generated it. The rule, in the thread (the log panel does NOT change — there the axis is the layer): The cut counts MESSAGES: chat.message, agent.response and chat.structured_question (TimelineEntry.mensagem). Cards and dividers do not count; those that come after the cut stay open with the messages around them. A per-agent collapse (RN-138) and a "Passos do turno" are still ONE entry, and count as one message. The cut never splits a turn (RN-172): it backs up to the opening of the turn of the message that marked it, so the question always stays together with the answer. That is why the open ones may exceed five — never an exchange in half. The prologue (turn 0) has no opening and does not back up; if backing up reaches the start, there is no history. The history is ONE block, in chronological order, and DECLARES the cut (RN-180): the title says what the cut counts ("Antes das últimas 5 mensagens") and the trailing separates what stayed inside ("2 mensagens · 2 outras entradas"). The "LLM" label leaves the thread along with the per-origin groups. What was lost, declared: reopening only what the user said, without reopening the rest, was the reason for the per-origin groups in the thread. It does not survive chronological order — the log panel keeps offering that cut. documents.t: GET /projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId/actions ordered by ascending seq with a ceiling of 200, and usePendingActions never paginated: from the 201st action of a session on — which a real execution easily reaches, a dev agent proposes dozens of commands per task — the NEW pending one was outside the only page read and vanished from the thread, the Executores and Aprovações (AT-296), precisely when someone was waiting for it. The rule: The route accepts latest=true and status=pending. latest brings the limit actions with the highest seq, returned in ASCENDING order and without nextCursor, ignoring afterSeq — the same contract as the events' latest (ADR 0021). status only accepts pending (another value is 400, without querying); combined with latest, it brings the newest pending ones without the decided ones taking up the window. Without the two parameters the contract is the previous one. The screen asks two questions, and the second only when needed. buscarAcoesDaSessao reads the tail (200); only if it comes back FULL does it also request the pending ones and merge by id, in ascending seq. An old pending one that the tail pushed out is still a decision to be made and does not vanish for having waited too long. The short session — the common case — still costs ONE request, and a failing read of pending ones brings the query down (the screen says it failed, never pretends an empty queue — RN-088). What this rule does NOT close: with more than 200 PENDING ones in a session, the oldest beyond them stay out (the ceiling is the same limit); and what the thread shows as DECIDED is still the tail — an old decided action, outside the 200 newest, does not appear in the thread. Pending items of the WHOLE project are another read (RN-638). documents.t: The rail's Aprovações counter, the "needs you" panel (RN-467), the Aprovações tab, the Visão geral roster and the Código tab read the pending ones from useLatestSession — the session CREATED last —, which is only the execution one by coincidence. An ideation or a chat opened after the execution zeroed the counter and hid from the roster the dev agents waiting for a decision (AT-297). And the block of pending items from other sessions in the chat (RN-626) only existed in an active session, while the container_start that the Infra Lead proposes in the CHAT unblocks the dev.blocked_by_container that appears in the EXECUTION (AT-298). The rule: The queue is the project's. Those screens read useProjectPendingActions (GET /projects/:projectId/actions?status=pending, in any session), all through the SAME key ['project-pending-actions', projectId, undefined] — at the project pace of RN-632, and at 3s only in the Aprovações tab, which has it as its subject. The ProjectPage frame takes the PR counter (git_merge) from the SAME read, instead of a second query. The queues stay separate, each with its own badge — nothing is summed (RN-467). Each card decides through the session the action ITSELF carries. In the Aprovações tab, approve, deny, "sempre permitir" and the batch call the endpoint with action.sessionId, and invalidate the project queue by prefix and the actions of the action's session. The tab's PR and gate blocks read events and actions of the current EXECUTION session (RN-139), and only without it of the most recent one. Pending items from other sessions appear in any state. The chat block also shows in closed and technical sessions — deciding is about the action of the OTHER session, not conversation in this one (RN-581 keeps refusing conversation) —, and the Executores tab gets the SAME block for the execution session: the chat's container_start becomes visible where the block appears. The proposal arrives through the channel, without waiting for the poll. Every proposed_action.*/action.* notice from any session channel a screen listens to also invalidates the project queue (pendenciasDoProjeto in criarInvalidadorDoCanal, 2s window), and dev.blocked_by_container too — the proposal that unblocks it is born in another session, whose channel nobody there listens to (AT-299). No poll went up. The block fits in the column and shows all of them (AT-318). At the width of the thread and the composer (780px), collapsible, with the PRESENCE of each queue in the header — "Aprovações 3 · Merges de PR 1", each with its own number, never the sum (RN-467) — visible even when collapsed. Cards are born with the detail CLOSED (detalheRecolhido in ApprovalCard): open, they covered ~60% of the thread and left one card in view out of three. The origin label shows ONCE per session, with the time of the oldest — per card, it repeated between one card and the next. The ceiling of 20 cards and the declared cut (RN-180) remain. What this rule does NOT close: the notice only arrives where there is a screen listening to a session channel (Sessão; Visão geral, the most recent session; Executores, the execution one). In a tab without a channel (Aprovações, PRs, Backlog…) or for a proposal made in a session whose channel no open screen listens to, the counter arrives through the project poll, within 15s; opening a session channel in the frame would change the session lifecycle (the channel is RN-064's heartbeat) and was left out. The Aprovações counter still counts the pending git_merge, as before — the panel dedupes it into the PR queue. The gap of the WORKSPACE role in place of the effective one (RN-471) applies to the new Executores block as it does to the chat's. documents.t: Two screens showed a correct state with the text of another place (AT-323, AT-324 — findings P1 and K1/K2 of the visual survey of Round 29). The PRs tab and the image gate. The block is REAL and stays: the PR list and the diff go through the SAME funnel as the Código tab (ReadProjectCodeUseCase.alvo → portaoDoContainer), so without a decided image (RN-105, in all three modes by RN-494) the api responds 409 there too — measured, not assumed. What was wrong was the text: the PRs tab showed "A aba Code ainda não está liberada", speaking of ANOTHER tab and with a name ("Code") that is not the rail's ("Código"). Now ContainerImageGateNotice receives the blocked SURFACE ('code' | 'prs'), the PRs tab says "A lista de PRs ainda não está liberada" and explains that it reads the repository through the same path as the Código tab; and the tab names in the text come from nav:tabs.*.label, the SAME source as the rail — never a literal, which is how "Code" and "Código" diverged. The PRs tab note does NOT promise to unlock on its own: the Código tab asks for the state and revalidates, the PR list only discovers the 409 when the query fails. /containers without a container. Parar and Remover were already disabled with registrado: null (RN-521, "never provisioned") and with removed, but nothing said why, and the danger variant of Button had no disabled state — "Remover" came out in solid red, the same as the active one. Now the row states the reason ONCE in text (Nunca provisionado: não há container para parar nem remover. / Container removido: …), and .danger:disabled gets the same opacity as the other variants. A row with a running container gets no text at all. The long reason for the missing broker. The text that names BROKER_URL was nine lines long and tripled the height of the table row. The cell now shows ONE short sentence in a <summary>, and the long text (which still names the variable, for the operator) opens on demand in the <details> — native and keyboard accessible, never a title on a disabled button (ADR 0064). When the SAME missing broker blocks start AND stop/remove, it is ONE line only ("subir, parar e remover só terminariam em falha"), with both details behind the same <details>.
