documents.t: Three screens asserted "nothing" next to a screen that showed something (AT-325 — findings S2/D2/X6 of the visual survey of AT-290). Reproduction with the real engine was not possible in this environment (egress blocks repo.hex.pm and Alpine, and no image compiles); the three contradictions were MEASURED in the code and proven by tests that fail before the fix. The Dashboard one was born, in the survey, from a 500 of the engine stub in the workspace summary — but the text that turned it into "no activity" is the web's, and with the real engine any summary failure would produce the same. The sidebar read the EXECUTION session, and only it. The Atividades block (RN-198) requested the events of the current execution session (useActiveExecutionSession). In a project with only conversation sessions it is null, the list came back empty, and the sidebar said "Nenhum agente entrou em ação ainda" next to a Visão geral with the Criativo waiting. Now: with a current execution, the sidebar keeps reading IT (the dev agents and the -2 instances are what the grouping of RN-198 exists to show, and the queryKey is the Executores tab's); WITHOUT execution, it reads the SAME session as the Visão geral and the Dashboard card — the most recent working one (useLatestSession, the rule of sessaoMaisRecente). The states that collapsed into the same text separate (RN-470): loading (nothing is asserted), error (its own text), project without a session ("Este projeto ainda não tem sessão."), and the session read without an agent, with the text NAMING which one ("…na sessão de execução…" / "…na sessão mais recente…"). The session list is only requested without execution, and with the freshness of a project cycle (frescorMs in useProjectSessions): when the sidebar enables it the project frame has already brought it, and the request budget of RN-632/RN-645 does not grow. The Dashboard card had one text for four states. "Sem atividade ainda" came out with the workspace summary LOADING, with it FAILED (the survey's case: the summary responded 500 and the card of a project with sixteen events said there were none), with the project WITHOUT a session and with the most recent session empty. Now there are four texts: "carregando atividade…", "atividade indisponível", "Nenhuma sessão ainda" and "Sem atividade na sessão mais recente ainda". The row still reads the most recent working session (latestSessionId), the same as the Visão geral and the sidebar without execution — the api did not change. "Artefatos gerados 3" over a single group "PO 1". The section header counted the backlog TREE (epic, story and task: 3) and the per-agent group counted only the ROOTS (1). Both now count in the same unit — each item carries quantos (1, plus the descendants when it is a backlog root), the header is the sum of the items and each group is the sum of its own, so the sum of the groups IS the header, by construction. And the section's empty state says what it counts ("Nenhuma PR nem item de backlog nesta sessão ainda.") instead of the generic "Nada ainda.", which next to a brief or a rule of the same session seemed to deny they existed — the section's scope (PR and backlog, RN-159) does not change. documents.t: Three screens did work nobody saw (AT-301/AT-302). The Session screen re-rendered ENTIRELY on every token of a turn — the in-progress text lived in the state of the hook it called. The provisioning and adoption screens polled the bootstrap status and the technical session's events at 1 s, and the events never stopped, even with the repository ready. And /status hit forever a service that did not respond. The in-progress text lives in an external store. The consultative chat text and the turn's activity strip stay in a per-session store (criarStoreDoStreaming), subscribed via useSyncExternalStore only by the two components that draw them — the thread bubble and the strip. The page subscribes to ONE boolean question (has the turn shown content yet?), which is what the "thinking" timer (RN-131) needs and which changes once per turn. The strip's reducer is the same; what changed is who holds the state. The bootstrap is followed at 3 s. Status and events, on both screens. And it stops at the end. Status and events stop when the bootstrap converges (provisioned) and when the query errors (pollQueParaNoErro). FAILURE (provision_failed) is terminal in adoption and NOT in provisioning: there "Tentar novamente" triggers a new bootstrap and the screen needs to see its progress (RN-477). /status stops on error. A service that responds — including with 5xx, which becomes status: 'error' in a resolved body — continues every 5 s. A service that does not respond stops being asked by timer; window focus and remount ask again, and the first success resumes the pace. documents.t: The visual audit of Round 29 (AT-290, finding S1) measured that the product had no mobile layout after login: at 390px the sidebar (264px) and the project rail (180px) remained FIXED, adding up to 444px of frame, and the content was left with 0 to 126px or overflowed to the right. Configurações reached 114 truncated texts (validacao-visual.js). The rule: One cut, one source. The breakpoint is CONSULTA_MOVEL ((max-width: 767px)), read by useLayoutMovel. Whoever switches layout reads that hook and applies the mobile design through a CLASS; the CSS modules have no @media of their own for it. That way what the JS decides and what the CSS draws do not diverge at a boundary pixel, and the component test (jsdom, without CSS) proves the same cut the browser applies. Without matchMedia the layout is the DESKTOP one: mobile only applies when the query asserts it. The sidebar becomes a drawer. A bar at the top carries the menu button (aria-expanded, aria-controls) and the brand. The drawer is a modal dialog (role="dialog", aria-modal): on opening, focus enters it; Tab does not leave; Esc, the X and the backdrop close it and return focus to the menu button. It also closes on following any link inside it (the project tabs only change ?tab=) and when the route changes from outside. In the drawer the sidebar always appears EXPANDED, and the "Recolher menu" button disappears: manual collapse (RN-195) is a desktop preference, it stays recorded and applies again when the window crosses the cut back. The project rail becomes a horizontal bar. They are the same 12 leaves, in the same order, with the group headers inline and aria-orientation="horizontal". The arrows that move are left and right, and the active tab is scrolled into the visible strip. The bar scrolls INSIDE; the page does not scroll sideways. The project body becomes a column (the bar above the panel), and the Visão geral stacks the team and the activity instead of keeping the 360px rail beside them. Measured (390×844, dark theme, api seed, validacao-visual.js injected): the document's scrollWidth = 390 on all authenticated screens (dashboard, the 12 tabs, /containers, /account), and <main> with the whole 390px. In Configurações, texto-cortado dropped from 114 to 33. The rest is component text (tables and section labels), a matter of typography and space, not of frame. The fora-da-viewport left over in Visão geral and Aprovações are tabs of the horizontal bar beyond the edge, where internal scrolling reaches them. Revised by ADR 0211 (AT-404): item 3 no longer applies — the project rail left, and with it the horizontal bar. On the phone the project tabs live in the DRAWER (item 2), with the groups, the active one and the counters; choosing one closes the drawer. The project body no longer becomes a column: only the paddings shrink. What this rule does NOT close: the Código tab keeps the 48px rail of CodeShell and the editor in columns; it was not designed for the phone. The Session screen inherits the new frame, but the top bar and the thread still have findings X1–X3 of the audit. The duplication of tab navigation (drawer and bar) closed in ADR 0211. documents.t: The visual survey of Round 29 (finding G1, AT-321) went through the Configurações sections in ~40s and the project's whole page turned into "Limite de requisições excedido" — the 300 req/min ceiling is the USER's (RN-579). The script RELOADED the page per section, and one load of the tab cost 55 requests. Measured with the real screens, the defect had three parts, and none of them calls for raising the ceiling: The rule: CONFIGURATION data is valid for one minute (FRESCOR_DA_CONFIGURACAO_MS). With TanStack's staleTime: 0, every observer that MOUNTS after the first one refetches. The sections only mount after the project arrives, so GET /projects/:id, GET /projects/:id/git/repository and GET /workspaces went out TWICE on every load; and switching tabs and coming back remounted the 19 sections and redid 31 fetches. Configuration only changes by MUTATION, and every mutation of the tab invalidates its own key — invalidating ignores staleTime, so whoever saves sees the new value immediately. What the minute delays is a change made by ANOTHER person, which still arrives on window focus and on the next mount after the minute. Operational state stays out (container lifecycle, spend per agent and per key, device keys with lastUsedAt, bootstrap plan): there the question is "what is up now". Configuration does not poll. The proficiency profile and the instruction version history polled at 15s — 8 req/min against the ceiling for two lists that only change through their own section (which invalidates) or through an approved patch. The summary LIES DOWN above the sections, at any width. As a sticky column next to them it was the fourth vertical strip (sidebar 264 + rail 180 + summary 208): at 1440px ~740px of content remained and the models table cut the agent name at 79px and the model's at 91px (finding G2). The column had no way to pay its own price even on a wide monitor, because .body has a ceiling of 1040px (ADR 0078). Laid down, it gives the 208px back to the sections; the price is what the narrow window already paid — one loses the "where am I" STUCK to the screen, not the navigation. No token changed. Numbers (configuracoes.orcamento.test.tsx, Shell + ProjectPage on the Configurações tab over a fetch that counts per route; dev → this rule): Scenario Before After tab load (2.5s) 53 50 one minute idle on the tab 76 68 Configurações → Visão geral → back (configuration fetches) 31 0 tab load, with the resolved bindings in a BATCH (RN-654, AT-334) 49 30 The "After" of the first three rows were measured on the same base as the "Before"; integrated into dev with RN-638 (the frame reads the project queue only once), the load stood at 49 and the minute at 64. The fourth row is RN-654, measured on dev at 94e5dc721d: the 20 bindings resolved per key became ONE read, and the test holds the load at 30 and the minute at 64. What this rule does NOT close: until RN-654, 20 of the load's requests were the RESOLVED binding of each agent (17) and of each area (3), one route per key (GET projects/:projectId/agent-bindings/:agentSlug) — that part closed with the BATCH route. RELOADING the page per section, as the survey script did, still costs 30 per load (~10 loads per minute before the ceiling); navigating through the summary INSIDE the tab remounts nothing and costs zero. The 68 of the minute all come from the FRAME (the Shell polls projects-summary and execution/session at 5s and the execution session's events at 3s), common to every tab — the same gap that RN-632 declares. documents.t: RN-645 measured 49 requests on loading the Configurações tab, and 20 of them were the RESOLVED binding of each agent (17) and of each area (3), one route per key. Three sections read those keys — models per agent, models per area and best models per capability —, and the 300 req/min ceiling is the USER's (RN-579). The rule: GET projects/:projectId/model-bindings/resolved?agents=…&areas=… returns { agents: [{ key, binding }], areas: [{ key, binding }] }, in the requested order and without repetition. Each binding is EXACTLY what the individual route would respond for that key (GET .../agent-bindings/:slug, GET .../area-bindings/:key): the same cascade workspace › projeto › área › agente without a session, the same origins the screen turns into a chain (RN-470), the Criativo inheritance, and null when no level has a model. There is no new cascade: the use case calls ResolveModelBindingUseCase key by key, with the input the individual route would pass. The minimum role is that of the individual read routes, viewer. Whoever does not reach the project gets the SAME 403. The read is contained (ADR 0060): the keys come in a comma-separated list, with the slug alphabet (lowercase, digits, -, _), and are at most 64 combined (TETO_DE_CHAVES_NO_LOTE). A malformed key or a batch above the ceiling is 400 naming the reason, never a key silently discarded — the response would assert about fewer keys than the screen requested. The web reads the batch through ONE queryKey (['model-bindings-resolved', projectId]), served by one request to the three Configurações sections and, since AT-339, also to the Visão geral and the Executores tab (useBindingsDosAgentes): the roster agents the catalog knows come from that SAME key — the cache one tab warmed serves the other without a request —, and those the catalog does not know (the dev-<modulo>) come from ONE extra batch read, under the same prefix and in slices of the same ceiling. Every write of an agent or area binding rereads the whole batch by that PREFIX, which reaches both reads; no per-agent key is left to invalidate. The failure of these reads leaves the agent card without a model — "I don't know", never an asserted model — and does not fall back to the per-agent route. The batch failure does not become "no model". With a single read, the failure is of all keys at once: the section states the reason ONCE, with the api's sentence and the action to reread, and each row says "não lido" in place of the chain. While the batch does not respond, the row says "lendo…". "Sem modelo em nenhum nível" stays reserved for the null the api asserted. Numbers: the tab load dropped from 49 to 30 requests (configuracoes.orcamento.test.tsx, on dev at 94e5dc721d); the idle minute stays at 64, all from the frame. In AT-339, the Executores tab load dropped from 29 to 27 and the Visão geral's from 33 to 31 (duas-abas.orcamento.test.tsx, with the base roster of three agents — with team and modules, the drop is one per card), and going from Configurações to the Visão geral stopped fetching any binding (before, 3). What this rule does NOT close: the per-key routes still exist in the api (no screen reads them anymore). A dev-<modulo> whose key exceeds 64 characters would be refused by the batch format, and the read of the extras would fail entirely — not measured on a real project, and declared. documents.t: The "after" visual audit of Round 29 (docs/explanation/auditoria-visual-rodada-29.md, findings N1 and N3 to N8) measured, at 390px, what RN-643 had not reached: in the Session the "Contexto da sessão" panel kept ~320px and left ~70px to the thread (one word per line), and the bar pushed "Iniciar ideação" and "Encerrar" past the edge; in /containers seven fractional columns overlapped the headers and cut the actions; in "Modelos por agente" the agent name had 6px and the selector 0px; /status scrolled sideways (413px); the Dashboard search became "Bus"; the session name in the Criativo's list had 0px; and the mobile rail left the active tab cut off, with no sign that it scrolled. The rule (the cut is the same useLayoutMovel of RN-643, and the design comes through a CLASS or attribute that the component sets, never through @media): The Session context panel is born CLOSED on the phone and opens as a DRAWER over the thread, from the right: a modal dialog with the panel's name, focus on the X on opening, Esc, X and backdrop close it and return focus to whoever opened it. On desktop it is born open next to the thread, as always. Crossing the cut goes back to the new side's default — a panel open on desktop does not reappear squeezing the thread on the phone. The exception is navigation that COMES to the panel (highlightEvent, the Psicólogo's evidence chip): then it is born open on the phone too. The Session bar wraps, never cuts. Exit, state, title and the panel toggle stay on the first line; type, settings, "Iniciar ideação" and "Encerrar" go down, and go down again if needed. What the bar shows is still decided by its width (RN-620 item 6). Every Table becomes a stack of cards on the phone. Each row is a card and each cell carries the column label next to the value; the header disappears. A column without a label, or marked largaNoMovel (a selector, a block of actions), takes the card's width with the label on top. The page does not scroll sideways, and what identifies the row does not vanish. /status scrolls the table inside its own wrapper; the Dashboard search gets a full line; the session list row wraps with the name on top, whole. The mobile rail follows the active tab and says it scrolls. The active one is brought into the strip on mount, on switch, when the rail's CONTENT changes (the counters arrive later and widen the earlier tabs) and when the fonts finish loading — never on every render, otherwise whoever scrolled the strip by hand would be pulled back. The edge that hides tabs fades (data-rola-inicio/data-rola-fim). Measured (390×844, both themes, native api with the seed, validacao-visual.js injected): scrollWidth 390 on all seven screens; zero texto-cortado on the Dashboard, the Criativo's list, the Session (with and without the drawer), /containers and /status; in Configurações the 33 dropped to zero, and the rail's active tab stayed whole within the strip on the three tabs measured. What this rule does NOT close: in the minimal bar "Encerrar" still has only the icon and the accessible name (RN-620 decides that by the bar's width). The panel toggle moves up to the title line only in PAINTING (order): the Tab order follows the DOM's. The fora-da-viewport that the checker still reports in Configurações and Aprovações are decorative icons with position: absolute inside controls below the fold, not something cut off. documents.t: Until now every chat.message came out with the name and avatar of whoever was logged in: in a shared session, another person's utterance appeared with YOUR name, and an agent's with your e-mail (finding N2 of the visual audit of Round 29, hidden while the thread grouped the history by origin). The author now comes from the event's actor, which the api records with the sender's id (SendAgentMessageUseCase, SendChatMessageUseCase) and which the generic append-event route accepts of any kind. The outcomes do not collapse: The viewer (actor.id equal to the token's sub; without it, by the e-mail of the member row) — the name or e-mail of the member row, otherwise the session's e-mail, and only in the absence of both "Você". Another person the screen can name — their name, otherwise the e-mail, from TWO reads composed into a single list (comporMembros), the PROJECT one before the WORKSPACE one: GET projects/:id/members (minimum viewer), under the SAME queryKey as the Configurações tab, and since AT-335 GET workspaces/:id/members (RN-655), of the PROJECT's workspace. Whoever has both rows appears once, through the project one — the same order as the role overlay (RN-471). Another person the screen CANNOT name — "Outro membro": without a project or workspace row (someone who left the workspace and still has utterances in the log), or both reads failed or have not arrived yet. The read that fails does not erase the other, and neither of them breaks the thread. Until AT-335 this was the declared GAP of whoever joins only through the workspace role, which had no read route; the route was born by owner decision. Agent — nomeDoAgente and the agent's avatar/color, like agent.response. Unknown actor (absent, without id, system or a kind outside person/agent) — "Autor desconhecido", never "Você". The backlog.story_promotion_returned narration, which had the same defect (the viewer's name over whoever returned the story), goes through the same function. The composer's OPTIMISTIC message keeps the viewer's e-mail — it is always theirs. documents.t: The session thread (RN-652) only named whoever had a row in project_members; whoever joins the project only through the WORKSPACE role became "Outro membro", because there was no route that read the workspace members (owner decision, AT-335). The route is born next to the three member WRITE routes (POST/DELETE of member and PUT owner-of-record, all owner), and its minimum is NOT theirs: the minimum is the ENDPOINT's (RN-102), and reading the list is not maintaining it. It is viewer, that of the neighbouring reads (GET workspaces/:id, .../projects) and that of GET projects/:id/members, which it completes — whoever opens a session needs to know who spoke in it, and a workspace viewer already sees every project of the workspace. The response has the SAME shape as the project read — userId, name, email, role (the WORKSPACE role) — and nothing else: no createdAt, no account state. A nonexistent workspace is 404, and a non-member is refused by the RolesGuard (403). There is still no workspace members SCREEN: the read exists to name, and the write routes remain API-only. documents.t: The action does not keep the policy reason: it lives in proposed_action.created (RN-567, RN-609). The Aprovações tab reads the PROJECT queue (RN-638) and the log of ONE session, so since AT-333 it said in a single note how many actions were left without a reason (RN-614). Owner decision (AT-336): each card shows its OWN. What was measured. The two options for the card were an actionId filter on the events read or a route that read the event by action. The filter is the smaller: it reuses the route (GET .../sessions/:sessionId/events, viewer), the DTO and the use case, and the action already carries the sessionId of the session that proposed it. No index or migration is born: the predicate on payload->>'actionId' runs INSIDE the session, which the unique index (session_id, seq) already narrows. A PROJECT read by actionId would require a new route to find the session the card already knows. The rule in the api. actionId returns only the events whose payload.actionId is that action, in the requested session — it never crosses sessions. It combines with the other parameters and limit counts only the matching ones; seq stops being contiguous in the page, so whoever filters does NOT derive omitted ones by subtraction (RN-180). Empty is 400: a filter that vanishes with the wrong string would return the whole log to whoever asked for an action's reason. The rule on the screen. useDecisoesDaPolitica: an action whose event is in the log the tab ALREADY loaded uses that one, without a request; the others read by action, in their session, with staleTime: Infinity — an event is immutable, so each action costs ONE read while the cache lives and the queue polls without repeating any. Nothing is requested while the tab is still loading its own log. A read that responds WITHOUT the event gives the "motivo não registrado" sentence (never silent); only the read that FAILS leaves the card silent, and that one, and only that one, is what the top note counts ("de N das M ações abaixo"). Since AT-340 the cards of the pending items from OTHER sessions in the chat (RN-626, PendenciasDeOutrasSessoes, also in the Executores tab) go through the SAME hook and the SAME cache: every action there is from another session, so none is covered by the screen's log and each one reads by action — only the DRAWN ones, within the block's card ceiling, and one the Aprovações tab already read costs nothing there (and vice versa). A read that fails also silences the card and is stated once, at the top of the block. The "needs you" panel does NOT use this path: it reads no log and opening it does not trigger a query, so the card there stays silent, as RN-614 already said — a decision, not a gap. No ceiling changes. documents.t: The po → arquiteto offer that the engine creates (POST /internal/sessions/:id/handoffs) is accepted without a click, in the same request and AFTER the offer's transaction, when the four conditions hold (decidirAceiteAutomatico, pure): the offer is offered; the backlog is covered: the project has at least ONE business rule (artifact.business_rule) and NONE without a story that cites it in businessRuleIds — the SAME computeCoverage as the Backlog tab and the PO's read (RN-164). Zero rules is not covered; the repository is local and without credentials: the project has no repository (the acceptance provisions local) or has a local one, and has no git connection (OAuth) in project_git_connections; whoever opened the session still has developer in the project (effective role, RN-471) — the minimum of the human acceptance route. The acceptor is still AcceptHandoffUseCase: the repository is born there, before activateAgent (RN-582, ADR 0165), on behalf of whoever opened the session. The acceptance is auditable: handoff.accepted and agent.activated come out with the SYSTEM actor handoff-auto-accept, and handoff.accepted carries automatico: true, emNomeDe and the criterio (regras, cobertas, repositorio). A condition that fails records nothing — the offer stays with the usual button, and the response to the engine says the reason (regras_sem_historia, repositorio_nao_local, credencial_de_git_no_projeto…). A failure AFTER deciding "yes" does not bubble up: it becomes the handoff.auto_accept_failed event (origin infra) and the thread shows it. With the acceptance done, the offer_handoff tool tells the PO that the Arquiteto has already been activated. A remote repository or one with credentials still asks for the click, and the manual handoff (ADR 0109) too. documents.t: In the Executores tab, with execution active and the execution team on screen, a card offers to switch on auto mode (RN-153) for the team's agents at once (AT-315). It is ONE control, and it is an offer: the agents not yet in auto come checked, the person unchecks whoever they do not want, and nothing is recorded without the click on "Ligar". The click records the SAME wildcard (agent_autonomy, actionType: "*", auto_approve) through the SAME endpoint as the per-agent toggle (PUT .../agent-autonomy, maintainer) — one PUT per agent, in series, without aborting on the first refusal, with a PER-agent outcome in the three cases of RN-469 (all, none with the api's sentence, some with who stayed in manual). Switching off remains in the manual/auto toggle of each agent's card; there is no "switch off in batch". When all are already in auto, the card disappears. The card STATES, before the click, what auto mode does NOT unlock — the absolute ceilings still ask for approval (RN-154, RN-418): merge into a protected branch; git push, opening a PR and deploy; sudo/doas; container_remove; instruction_patch; parallelizing or raising the parallelism ceiling. Without maintainer the control stays inert and the reason is stated in text; the role read is the WORKSPACE one, with the same declared gap as the other auto mode screens (RN-471). documents.t: Owner decision (09/30, AT-312): the separate click to accept the PO goes away. The Criativo→PO handoff is born AFTER the click (it is the turn the click triggers that offers it, CriativoServer.executar_confirm_readiness/1), so the acceptance does not fit in the click's POST: it happens in the internal route that CREATES the offer (POST /internal/sessions/:id/handoffs), right after CreateHandoffUseCase, and goes through the SAME AcceptHandoffUseCase as the card. Measured before changing, acceptance through the card records: the row's transition to accepted, handoff.accepted (actor the person, {handoffId, toAgent}), agent.activated (actor the person, {agent}) and, by RN-635, the handoff.superseded of the other offers to the PO in the project. The implicit acceptance records exactly those, with the SAME human actor — whoever clicked, read from the marked readiness.confirmed —, and adds the mark implicito: { via: 'readiness.confirmed', readinessEventId } in the payload of handoff.accepted and of agent.activated. No event is edited, no system actor takes the person's place, and acceptance through the card stays without the mark. It is accepted only when ALL hold (decidirAceiteImplicitoDoPo): the offer is criativo → po, offered, of THIS session, and carries as artifact the product_brief born AFTER the most recent marked readiness.confirmed. Otherwise the offer stays offered and the card appears as always: a session prior to ADR 0185 (no mark), a brief prior to the click, and the MANUAL handoff, which never carries an artifact (RN-633 — "Estou pronto" stays on screen after it). A failed acceptance does NOT bubble up to the engine (the offer was created, and the Criativo would say "I couldn't offer" — false): it becomes a durable agent.error, actor system/aceite-implicito, with origin (infra or politica) and reason: aceite_implicito_falhou. The 400 for "not offered" is not a failure: someone decided the offer through another path in the interval, and that is already in the log. The screen hands the composer recipient to the PO on the click (the gesture of calling him, RN-631); until he joins, the choice does not count and the Criativo keeps receiving. No ceiling moves: accepting the PO does not provision a repository (only the Arquiteto and the Dev Lead, RN-582), does not merge nor push. documents.t: The product's branch policy has work born from dev (the bootstrap creates dev and qa from main, RN-582), but until now nobody pointed the agents at it: the dev agent's pr_open carried no targetBranch and the api filled in repo.defaultBranch (main); the Arquiteto's ADR PR was born from main and targeted main; the project's working tree opened default_branch; the gate computed the diff against it; and the QA context said "Repositório · branch main" (AT-250, item A4 of the real use of 09/29). Every agent PR skipped the dev → qa → main pipeline. Owner decision (09/30): the THREE now use dev, together — changing only one would leave the gate judging a diff that is not the PR's. The WORKING branch is dev and it is NOT the provider's default_branch (which remains the one promotion reaches last and is still read where it is the question): the project's working tree opens dev (ensure_remoto/2 ignores the remote's default_branch to choose the base), and each dev agent's worktree is born from dev EXPLICITLY, not from HEAD — a workspace initialized before this rule is stuck on default_branch (the ready mark prevents re-initializing) and gets the local dev from origin/dev, without a new fetch; the dev agent's pr_open carries targetBranch: "dev" in the payload, and the api, without the field (an action proposed before), fills in dev and no longer the defaultBranch; the ADR PR is born from dev and targets dev; the gate's diff is dev...HEAD, and the project context line says "Repositório · branch de trabalho dev". Repository WITHOUT dev (adopted without bootstrap, or a bootstrap that did not reach create_dev_branch): there is NO fallback to default_branch — it would be the agent working and the gate judging over a base that is not the PR's. Each point fails NAMED, through the behavior it already had for a missing branch, with one new exception: the working tree refused nothing and created an EMPTY LOCAL dev (the path of the bare that never received a push), marked ready and never re-initialized again. Now that path only applies to a remote WITHOUT any branch; with branches and without origin/dev, initialization raises with the named message (mensagem_sem_branch_de_trabalho/1, "o repositório do projeto não tem a branch dev… crie a branch… e tente de novo") and .git is undone (AT-112), so the next attempt, with dev created, initializes normally. The worktree refuses with the same message when there is neither dev nor origin/dev; the diff fails with git's error naming the revision; the provider refuses the PR (and the creation of the ADR branch) naming the ref. infra (open_infra_pr) did NOT change: it still is born from and targets defaultBranch. The value lives in TWO places, on purpose, one per language, and they change together: BRANCH_DE_TRABALHO in the api and branch_de_trabalho/0 in the engine. documents.t: It is RN-163 ("nothing is announced that the code will not execute") applied to the Infra Lead. In the real use of 09/29 (session be70, seq 282) he wrote that he would start the container "in parallel" to the infra PR, and no start tool.call came afterwards (AT-264). There were two causes in the code, and both close here: The response's whole batch is dispatched before the turn ends. An accepted propose_infra_pr ends the turn without a new trip to the model — it is the only point where the CODE cuts the loop with the model wanting to continue —, but it stopped dispatching in the MIDDLE of the batch: a propose_container_start (or container_start_via_runner) requested in the SAME response, after the PR, vanished without tool.call, without tool.result and without notice. Now it is the Dev Lead's form (propose_execution_plan): all calls of the response run, and only afterwards does the accepted PR end the turn. A second propose_infra_pr in the same response is refused with a reason (tool.call + tool.result with ok: false) — only the first consolidates with Workflows. The turn's closing says, with a SERVER sentence, when the start was NOT proposed — the form of the Criativo's consolidated outcome (encerrar/2). The decision is by what the loop executed (was any start proposal ACCEPTED by the api in this turn?), never by what the model wrote; its text is not read. It speaks in two cases: the turn ended through the PR and no start was proposed; or a start was attempted, refused, and no accepted proposal came afterwards. A turn that never touched the start (a question, a gate correction) gets no sentence at all, and neither does a container already REGISTERED running/provisioning (the same local read as recusa_ja_de_pe/2, without HTTP). The kickoff and the description of propose_infra_pr now say what the code does: the start comes BEFORE the PR or in the SAME response, because the PR ends the turn. That is help for the model, not the guarantee — the guarantee is the closing of item 2. Nothing here starts a container or proposes a start, with the refusals by mode and state intact (RN-566/RN-610). Since RN-671 (AT-260) the first start is a SERVER step in the kickoff, marked by the SAME registrar_subida: in the common case it was proposed and the closing of item 2 has nothing to say; it still speaks when the server's start was refused (or DENIED by the policy, which since then counts as a refusal) and when it was not up to the server (no routing, runner) and the model did not propose it. documents.t: The scope ceiling of ADR 0055 compared every command with the project folder on the HOST, including when the command runs INSIDE the container (RN-492/RN-502). In the real use of 09/29, the 37 "scope" requests were /work/... and /tmp compared with /home/<usuario>/projetos-brabo/<projeto> (AT-258). With a REGISTERED running container in a container or mounted project, the scope root is /work — the mount point, where the folder and the project's .worktrees live — plus the container's OWN /tmp. The cwd arrives as a host path and is translated to /work by the same engine rule (cwd_para_container/2): the root becomes /work, what is under it becomes /work/..., what is outside stays as it came and remains outside. In mounted the translation is bijective. Without a container, the root is still the project folder on the host, and the host's /tmp stays OUTSIDE. It applies to whoever is not on autopilot (the specific terminal rule): the autopilot does not go through the scope (RN-603, kept by RN-670). projectScopeRoot does not change nor merge with permissionsFilePath (RN-478); the auto-approval FLOOR remains only for container mode (RN-493). runner stays out, on purpose: the api does not know whether the runner will route to the container or to the host (RN-558). A command argument with a HOST path now counts as outside when there is a container — the engine translates only the cwd, and inside the container that path does not exist. documents.t: Owner decision of 10/01 (ADR 0189): RN-603 is NOT revoked. The wildcard *: auto_approve approves EVERYTHING, including the synthesized compound of permissions.json, paths outside the folder, git commit and creating a LOCAL branch. Still out, never auto-approvable: push/PR/merge/deploy through the terminal and sudo/doas (RN-418), merge into a protected branch, container_remove, instruction_patch and parallelism. An explicit deny wins, and an ask written in the file asks. The guarantee that this does not reach the Brabo's code is the container's containment — a single folder, at /work, strictly below the broker's root, without the Docker socket or privilege —, proven in apps/broker/src/contencao-do-brabo.spec.ts; what the proof does NOT cover is declared in ADR 0189. documents.t: Owner decision of 10/01 (AT-257, which closes AT-170 — point 6 of ADR 0055, the unit of generalization; ADR 0189). Until now the click recorded the WHOLE command, byte for byte (Terminal(<comando>)): the next command was almost never the same — 173 clicks in the real use of 09/29 —, and the compound became ONE pattern whose content only matched the FIRST segment, so cd src && npm test only freed cd src. Now each SEGMENT of the command (the same cut as decide(): &&, ||, ;, |, &) becomes a pattern, and the unit is: the verb alone (ls) → the verb; verb + word (npm test, git status, mix test, npx vitest) → both. A "word" starts with a letter, without /, ., =, glob or flag; an argument that looks like a word (cd src) stays as a subcommand — the NARROW side of the doubt, because telling the two apart would require a list of verbs, which is the space that findings Z/AD say does not converge; verb + argument that is not a word (cat src/x.ts, cd ../lib) → the verb; verb + FLAG (ls -la src, git -C /x status) → the EXACT segment: the form with a flag is where verb and invocation diverge, and generalizing there would be choosing a form from within the code; a unit that is a PREFIX of an RN-418 ceiling (git remote, gh pr) → the EXACT segment; and if even the exact one is a prefix (git alone), no pattern for that segment. Matching is still the usual one (token prefix), a click on a command with an external or privileged effect is still refused whole beforehand (motivoDeRecusaDoSempreAprovar, 400 teto_do_sempre_permitir), the decide() ceiling runs after the file, and the path scope still limits WHERE outside the autopilot (RN-669). Whoever can record is whoever already could (the endpoint's role, unchanged); the precedence with auto mode is that of RN-670. A module dev agent's "Sempre permitir" still goes to agent_autonomy (RN-509), without a pattern. Only the patterns that are MISSING are recorded and narrated; permission.granted carries patterns (the recorded list) and pattern (the same list joined by comma, for the timeline). documents.t: The real use of 09/29 measured both holes: pr-6 had THREE git_merge executed, and pr-4 was merged with the task in awaiting_qa. The api did not dedupe git_merge per PR (only the screen did, and only in the same list), and LocalGitProvider returned the already merged PR without error — the executor recorded a second executed for the same merge. Proposal. A git_merge of a PR that a previous execution already merged (executed with state: 'merged') is 409 pr_ja_mergeado; with a LIVE proposal of the same PR (pending, approved or auto_approved), 409 merge_ja_proposto. In both, nothing is created. Denied or failed do not count: whoever denied or saw it fail can try again. The comparison is by the payload's pullRequestId, across the whole project (any session). Approval. Approving a pending git_merge whose PR ANOTHER proposal already merged is 409 pr_ja_mergeado, before any effect, and the action stays pending for whoever sees it to deny. A merely LIVE sibling does not prevent deciding this one. Provider. LocalGitProvider refuses to merge an already merged PR with GitPullRequestAlreadyMergedError, and the target does not move — aligned with GitHub, which refuses the repeated merge. A pending gate is a NOTICE, never a refusal (owner decision, 09/30). The PRs tab and the chat's "Mergear" say in TEXT which gate is missing (qa-verificada with awaiting_qa or a gate not yet opened, secops-segura with awaiting_secops), and the button and the card stay active. awaiting_user, a done task and a PR without a task give no notice. The "blocked gate" (task blocked) stays as it was. No ceiling moves. Merge into a protected branch remains unconditional, human require_approval (RN-418, decide.ts): this rule only prevents proposing or approving when there is nothing to merge. Declared: two simultaneous proposals of the same PR are not serialized (there is no per-PR lock), and it is rule 2 that holds the second one. documents.t: Owner decision on 10/01 (ADR 0190), revising the "never seeded" of RN-491. In the real use of 09/29 the Infra announced the start "in parallel" and did not propose it; the container only started through /containers (AT-260). The seed. Accepting the handoff addressed to infra records, besides open_infra_pr: auto_approve and terminal: deny, the autonomy container_start: auto_approve. Only that one among the container ones: container_start_via_runner and container_stop remain never seeded, and container_remove remains in the absolute ceiling (RN-495). The trigger is the SERVER's. In the Infra Lead's kickoff, BEFORE the first trip to the model, if there is a current routing (artifact.module_routing roteado, with a candidate) and a container/mounted project, the server proposes container_start through the SAME path as the propose_container_start tool: the local refusals by mode and state (RN-566, RN-610), then propose_action, where the api refuses without a broker (RN-591), resolves the autonomy and, auto-approved, executes the start, electing the image through DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase with decidedBy: 'infra-lead' (RN-491). runner has no server step: it goes through container_start_via_runner, proposed by the model and decided by a human. The election is deterministic. The candidate with the most modules; on a tie, the routing's first. Network none, default resources, and a rationale that says it was the server. (Revised by RN-683: the resources are omitted and the api starts with the minimum derived from the module_map, not with the default.) The trail says who called. Durable tool.call (with origem: "servidor") and tool.result, and no tool message in the model's history; the kickoff says in text what HAS ALREADY happened (returned status, or the refusal reason). The closing of RN-668 stays true. The server's start marks the turn as the tool's would: proposed, the closing says nothing; refused, it says it was refused. A proposal DENIED by the policy (status denied, like a session opened by someone who is not maintainer) counts as a refusal, in both origins. No ceiling moves: the minimum role stays maintainer (the effective one of whoever opened the session), a deny in permissions.json still wins, and /containers does not change (it proposes as a human, and agent autonomy does not apply to it). Declared: the card's manual/auto toggle writes the wildcard, and the specific rule wins — putting the Infra in "manual" does not switch off this seed. documents.t: Owner decision on 10/01 (ADR 0190, AT-262). Until now "Confirmar arquitetura pronta" offered TWO handoffs — to the Infra and to the Dev Lead (FASE 14d, handoff-duplo in docs/fluxo.yml) —, and the Dev Lead could be accepted before the container in which the dev agents work existed (RN-502). In the real use of 09/29 both were born from the same confirmation (session be70, seq 252/254). The architecture confirmation offers only to the Infra. OfferInfraHandoffUseCase has one target (infra); the engine port's offerDevHandoff, the route POST /internal/sessions/:id/agent/offer-dev-handoff and the Arquiteto's :offer_dev_handoff/handoff_dev_pendente ceased to exist. ja_oferecido now means "the Infra already had an offer or was active". The one who offers the Dev Lead is the Infra Lead's server, through create_handoff_if_absent/5 (infra → dev-lead, ADR 0182): a pending offer in any session of the project comes back as is, and an already active Dev Lead (409 agente_ja_ativo) is not a failure. It is not a tool: the model does not decide when the Dev Lead comes in. Only with the container REGISTERED running (the local read of ProjectContainerLifecycle). The question is asked at two moments: at the end of every Infra turn (concluir) — the common case, because the server's start on acceptance (RN-671) runs inside the kickoff — and when the outbox's container.running arrives outside a turn (later approval, /containers, container_start_via_runner): Engine.Outbox.Drain now also enqueues Engine.Workers.InfraOfereceDevLeadWorker, which notifies the project's Infra Lead through PubSub. A failure that is not "already handled" is a durable agent.error with origin (RN-116), without bringing the turn down; the end of the Infra's next turn tries again. What stays as it was: the second repository door on acceptance to the Dev Lead (RN-582) — the acceptance is the same, only who offers changed — and the execution activation chained to the acceptance (RN-161). Declared: the outbox notice is at-most-once, like Engine.Dev.Wake; without an Infra Lead up at that instant, the offer waits for the end of its next turn. documents.t: Owner decision on 10/01 (ADR 0199, AT-261). Until now omitted resources became RECURSOS_PADRAO (2 cpus, 4096 MiB, 512 pids) and the server's start on acceptance (RN-671) always omitted it: every container was born at the default, with no notion of minimum. Each module declares its own. The module_map gains resources (cpus, memoryMb, pidsLimit) per module — what THAT module needs alone in the container. The create_module_map tool asks for it; the api accepts it absent and refuses with 400, on map creation: a HALF declaration (all three or none), a non-positive value or one above the ceiling, and a SUM across modules above the ceiling. The field lives in the artifact's JSON, without a migration. The minimum is the SUM, field by field. A project has ONE container (project_id UNIQUE in project_containers) and the modules run in it at the same time; the maximum across modules would undersize the container whenever two were up. A module without a declaration: floor at today's default. No number is invented. If there is a module without a declaration, the minimum is the larger of the sum of the declared ones and RECURSOS_PADRAO, field by field, and the rationale NAMES who did not declare. With no declaration at all (every map prior to this rule), and without a current module_map, the minimum is exactly today's default. The container_start execution resolves field by field. Omitted becomes the minimum (the server's start sends everything omitted); below the minimum is a named failed, without recording an image decision or starting; above is valid up to the ceiling, which does not change. The rationale of the recorded artifact.project_image gains "Recursos mínimos (RN-683): …" with the summed modules and the map version. A single yardstick. The api derives; the engine sums nothing and the server's start says in the rationale that the resources are the derived minimum. Out, declared: choose_project_image (the Arquiteto decides the image and its resources) and container_start_via_runner (starts the already decided image) do not change; the refusal below the minimum happens on execution, not on proposing. documents.t: In the real use of 09/29 the PRE-DEV test plan (RN-341) ended twice in toolloop.limit_reached 8/8 without emit_plano_de_teste: the loop read docs, empty RAG and folders until concluding that "the code does not exist yet". The owner decided (10/01) for option (b): the plan is born AFTER delivery. ADR 0192 revises 0090 on that point, and the rule has four parts: The plan is the first step of the review cycle. The QaLeadServer's run_area/3 obtains the delivery's plan BEFORE the subspecialties (plano_de_teste_da_entrega/5): it finds again in the session tail (rehydration ceiling, RN-580) the artifact.plano_de_teste of the SAME taskId — the correction round does not pay for another loop —, and otherwise runs QaEstrategiaAgent.run/6 with the dev's worktree as workspace_root, the task's business rules and the list of files the delivery touched (git diff dev...HEAD, up to 40 names). A diff that fails becomes text ("não consegui listar: motivo"), never an empty list. The plan is INPUT, never a verdict. It reaches the Automação at the END of its message, for the step of finding which test covers each rule; the verdict yardstick does not change (one coverageMatrix row per story rule, approved only with a green suite and every rule covered) and the external contract remains ONE qa_verdict per cycle. A plan that FAILS does not hold the review: the QA-strategy records agent.error with origin (RN-059) and the Automação receives the usual message, byte for byte. implementavel is judged over the story and the module_map. run_assessment/2 neither reads nor triggers a plan: it proposes the verdict on the FIRST call, over what the Dev Lead's kickoff already gives it, with payload storyId/parecer/justificativa. Gate, owner, severity warn and human approval do not change; only the entrada ([story-ready, module_map]). The appsec (RN-539) keeps triggering there, in design. The ceiling stays 8. "qa-estrategia" gets no clause in Iteracoes.tipo/1; what changed was the input. The agent now runs under the task_budget_micros that the subspecialties share (RN-036). run_design/3, Dispatcher.run_qa_estrategia/3 and QaEstrategiaContext were removed, and artifact.plano_de_teste now requires taskId. Declared and not decided here: whether the plan's executable criteria should become MANDATORY rows of the coverageMatrix (and therefore fail a delivery). documents.t: Owner decision (10/01), recorded in ADR 0193: a CREDENTIALED git operation runs on the runner's HOST, and the code runs in the container. It closes the half that RN-558 left open — the authenticated fetch in runner mode with the container up, which is the common path, always ended in the named refusal. The engine marks, and only at one point. RunnerGit.fetch!/3 dispatches the credentialed fetch through RunnerRouter.exec_git_credenciado/5, which puts gitCredenciado: true in the exec payload and requires a non-empty env by guard. The dev agent's terminal command goes through RunnerRouter.exec/4 and never carries the mark. Without credentials (provider local), the fetch goes without the mark. The runner runs on the host only with the CONJUNCTION: the literal mark true and a non-empty env. Then the command goes to executarComando (the env merged over process.env), even with an active container. The folder is the same: estado.dir is the bind-mount of /work. env without the mark does not get the host. With an active container, that pair stays REFUSED with the RN-558 mark and origin politica. Today no engine caller produces it; in practice it comes from a brabo-runner older than ADR 0193, which does not read the mark — and the engine's message says to update it. The mark without env changes nothing either: the command goes to the container. No containment changes: DockerPort.exec remains without env (ADR 0130), and RunnerReadiness (RN-507) stays byte for byte — the mark decides WHERE the runner executes, never WHETHER the engine dispatches. The log never carries the name or value of an env variable: the refusal gives the count, and the host path's log adds only [git credenciado, no host]. documents.t: Until now a message that reached a conversational agent in the middle of a turn was 409 turno_em_andamento (RN-578): recorded as chat.message (the api records before talking to the engine) and never read. The real use of 09/29 measured three in a single session — PO, Infra Lead and Dev Lead. Owner decision (10/01), for the SEVEN conversational agents through the same path: Queue, not refusal. With a turn in progress, the message enters the agent's queue (TurnoAssincrono.receber_mensagem/4), the agent records chat.message_queued (mensagemId, texto, idioma, posicao) and the click gets 202 with {entrega: "enfileirada", posicao}. Without a turn, the turn starts right away, as always (entrega: "lida"). The api route also returns the mensagemId — the id of the chat.message. N messages = 1 turn. At the END of the turn (finalizar/1, never suspender/1) the pending ones become ONE turn, in order of arrival, in a single text (FilaDeMensagens.texto_do_turno/1: one is itself; several, numbered), and the agent records chat.message_delivered with the ids. Delivery is a message to itself, after the server's closing (the Infra Lead's gate correction and the Arquiteto's handoff come first). A message that arrives between the end of the turn and the delivery goes to the END of the queue, and the queue is delivered right away. Ceiling of 10 pending per agent and session. The 11th is 409 fila_de_mensagens_cheia, with a durable agent.error of origin politica — it is recorded and will not be read. Cancel. POST …/agents/:agent/messages/:messageId/cancel (developer, the message route's minimum): only the SENDER (403 mensagem_de_outra_pessoa), only in a session that accepts conversation (RN-581). Whether it is still in the queue is decided by the agent's process, which serializes the race with the delivery: 409 mensagem_fora_da_fila when it was already read or cancelled. The engine records chat.message_cancelled on behalf of whoever cancelled; with the agent down, it records directly (the queue is the log). Persisted in the log, never in a table. Pending = queued and neither delivered nor cancelled — the same derivation in the engine and on the screen. The init/1 of the seven rebuilds the queue and schedules delivery; RN-580 removes from the history the cancelled one and the agent's own pending one; at boot, after closing the orphan turn (RN-586), the agent with a pending queue is woken up. The interrupted turn is still never redone. A turn suspended on approval (Dev Lead, RN-284) keeps refusing with aguardando_aprovacao — with no foreseeable end, queuing would promise a reading with no date. A queue that already existed waits for the resumption to finish. The screen. With a turn in progress the composer no longer locks for a message to an agent: the button becomes "Pôr na fila" and the message does not arm a new turn. In the thread, "na fila de " with Cancelar for the author, and "cancelada" struck through. The chat without an agent still locks. The turno_em_andamento refusal remains for what is not speech: the PO's story review, the Criativo's readiness, the Arquiteto's handoff offer. documents.t: Revises RN-161 (owner decision, 10/01): accepting the handoff to the Dev Lead no longer chains POST .../execution/activate, for EVERY role. The explicit "Ativar execução" shortcut of the card (RN-137) and the Visão Geral one remain — they are a click of their own, not the acceptance. The real use of 09/29 measured the inversion: execution was activated on handoff acceptance at 06:45:01 — the web chained the activation for maintainer/owner (session-acoes-de-handoff.ts, RN-161) —, and the Dev Lead's plan, proposed at 06:47:47, stayed pending and was never used. The plan had no consumer: propose_execution_plan had no execution pipeline and, approved, stayed approved forever. Measured on dev before changing: the acceptance backend (AcceptHandoffUseCase) NEVER emitted execution.activated; the only emitter is ActivateExecutionUseCase, called only by the execution/activate route. The rule: Accepting the Dev Lead only activates him to plan. handleAcceptHandoff accepts and nothing more; AcceptHandoffUseCase does not change — it keeps provisioning the repository as the idempotent second door (RN-582). Approving propose_execution_plan ACTIVATES execution. The action gained an executor in the api, ExecuteExecutionPlanUseCase, called by manual approval (ApproveActionUseCase) and by auto-approval (ProposeActionUseCase — the type is not in the absolute ceilings of decide.ts, so it CAN be configured auto-approvable). It records the tasks' module (RN-678) and calls the SAME ActivateExecutionUseCase as the button — no second yardstick: the 409 without a repository (RN-582), the 409 for execution.activated in a consultative session (RN-097) and the idempotent reactivation through findActiveExecutionSession stay there, untouched. Whoever activates is whoever APPROVED (decidedBy); on auto-approval, whoever opened the session — against whom decide() resolved the role. Both require maintainer, the same minimum as execution/activate, so resolving the effective role of the dev agents' git_* (the execution session's createdBy) does not change owner. The Dev Lead's session does NOT close (it is not passed as originSessionId, RN-135): it is there that he resumes the suspended turn and narrates the outcome. The outcome is named and durable. The action ends executed with { sessaoDeExecucao, modulos, tarefasAtribuidas } or failed with the motivo (the api's sentence, e.g. the 409 without a repository), plus the execution.plan_applied/execution.plan_failed event in the timeline. The Dev Lead reads the real outcome on resuming ("execução ATIVADA na sessão …" or "a ativação falhou: …"), never "plano registrado". Failing does not undo the approval: the human's decision is already recorded. documents.t: In the real use of 09/29 dev-input-keyboard picked up "Implementar loop de queda automática da peça" and dev-board-engine picked up "Mapear teclas…": the task had no module, the story had several, and claimNext let any dev of any module of the story pick up any of its tasks (s.module_ids ? $1). The rule: The task has a module — tasks.module, nullable text (migration 0068_modulo_da_tarefa). The one who assigns it is the Dev Lead, in the execution plan: propose_execution_plan gained tarefas: [{ taskId, modulo }], and his kickoff lists the pending tasks of the PROJECT backlog with the task_id and the story's modules. The valid set is the current module_map. The api reads the plan (lerPlanoDeExecucao, a pure function) on PROPOSAL and refuses with 400 plano_de_execucao_invalido, without creating the action, when: the plan has no tarefas; a task has no taskId or is without a module; the module (of the task or of the plan) is outside the module_map; the task appears twice; or it does not exist in this project. The sentence names the task, the module and the valid modules, and goes back to the Dev Lead as a tool error (loop input, RN-163), for him to fix. Approval rereads the plan against the module_map of that moment (it may have changed): a refusal becomes failed without recording anything and without activating. Passing, the modules are recorded BEFORE the activation, so that no freshly started dev agent looks for an ownerless task. Only that module's dev picks it up. claimNext and countClaimableByModule use the SAME predicate (daTarefaDoModulo): a task with a module belongs to whoever has that module, and nobody else — the story's module_ids no longer decide. A task without a module is only claimable when the story has ONE module only, and it is the dev's: it is the only case in which "that module's dev" is not ambiguous, and it is the path of whoever activated through the Visão Geral without a plan. A task without a module of a story with several waits for the next plan. Left out, declared: a task created AFTER the plan is born without a module (the PO does not assign); the task.became_claimable notice is still routed by the STORY's modules (waking one extra dev picks up nothing, it only costs a query); and the plan's per-module agentes stays informative — activation starts one dev per module of the module_map, as before, and extra parallelism still goes through parallelize (RN-083). documents.t: Owner decision on 10/01 (AT-277): switch the Anamnese back on with fixes. In the real use of 09/29 it ran six times and all six ended in anamnese.run_skipped ("no eligible member"), written by the MODEL after a paid call (8,933 micros), and the three accepted hypotheses stayed in the queue with no destination. See ADR 0196. Without an eligible subject, the round does not run. A subject is an EFFECTIVE member of the project (projectRole ?? workspaceRole, the yardstick of RN-471), outside the opt-out, with OWN interaction in what the round shows the model — an event of theirs with actor_kind: "user" in the window, or a decision of theirs. The guard comes BEFORE triage and not even the queued hypothesis gets past it. Without a subject: no LLM call and no RAG search; the reason goes NAMED to the engine log (sem_sujeito_elegivel, with nenhum_membro or nenhuma_interacao_propria and the numbers) and, in a manually requested round, also to the event log (anamnese.run_skipped with causa: "sem_sujeito_elegivel"). Through the tick it is only a log — it would be a notice every 15 minutes per project. The prompt now lists only the subjects. A project member is the EFFECTIVE one. Creating a project does not write project_members, and the Anamnese read only that table — the workspace owner was never a member. The Anamnese's three use cases now read listEffectiveMembers; listMembers remains only project_members. A hypothesis ACCEPTED by the person THEMSELVES becomes a profile fact. The psychologist.hypothesis_accepted carries projectId, sujeito (the author of the analyzed session), hipotese, sugestao and fatoDoPerfil, and the GraphEventTranslator — the same one as the projector and grafo:reprojetar — translates it into (:FatoDoPerfil {hypothesisId}), linked to the person (SOBRE) and to the project (NO_PROJETO). fatoDoPerfil is only true when the one who accepted is the subject: a fact about a person is never born from someone else's click, and the payload says why (motivoSemFato). A declined one is only recorded, as before. Acceptances recorded before this RN lack the fields and do not become facts. The fact enters the context of the agents that talk with the person. The author's message to a conversational agent carries THEIR facts in this project — read by QueryUserContextUseCase, scoped to the project, the 5 most recent, with the total beside them and the cut stated —, and the engine puts them in the turn as an EPHEMERAL system message, through the same path as the language (RN-622): never in the history, before the language guidance, with a ceiling of 2,000 characters. Graph down becomes a log, and the turn goes on without the facts. A turn without an author receives no facts. Switched back on. ANAMNESE_ENABLED returns to default true in runtime.exs and in the three composes; START_ANAMNESE does not change (the production one stays false, an already declared divergence). The Psicólogo stays paused. documents.t: Until now, a message in a consultative session without an agent went to the SSE of POST .../chat (SendChatMessageUseCase), which sends to the bound model only the current text — no history, no system prompt, no tool — and records the answer with the MODEL NAME as actor. Measured in the real use of 09/29: session 5d66 answered "I have no access to previous conversations". The owner's decision (10/01) is that, without an active agent, the consultative session asks to choose an agent — the same yardstick as RN-584 (no default recipient) reaching the last case that still had one: the raw model. The measurement, before the fix: the chat route had ONE client, the screen (handleSend, only when there was no recipient — which, since RN-631, only happened in the consultative session without an agent: the creative one always has the Criativo as an option). The curl the seed prints is a development hint, in a creative session. The use case has a SECOND legitimate consumer: the provider smokes (*-provider.smoke.spec.ts) use it directly as an end-to-end instrument (credential → call → metering) in a session without an agent. That is why the api's refusal lives in the ROUTE, and the use case does not change. The rule: The screen does not send without a recipient. "Enviar" and Enter are locked with zero options, as they already were with two and no choice; the SSE branch left handleSend. The recipient line SHOWS who can be called. Without an option, the manual handoff selector (RN-440) moves into it — "Para", the list, and "Chamar" —, and the selector above disappears so there is not the same choice in two places. The list is the agents that converse (AGENTES_DE_CHAT, those the engine matches with their own clause) and that the manual handoff reaches, minus whoever already joined and minus the Criativo: the consultative session promises in its invitation that he does not join, because opening the ideation is what the creative one does (RN-097). Chamar offers the handoff; accepting it in the thread makes the agent the recipient (RN-631). The api refuses the same case for any client. POST .../chat in a consultative session in which no agent.activated was recorded is 422 {reason: "destinatario_ausente"}, with the sentence that points to .../agents/:agent/message, BEFORE any effect: nothing is recorded and no model is called. The refusal goes out as an HTTP response and not as an error frame inside a 200 stream — the handler returns Promise<Observable>, and the rejection before the SSE header becomes the normal response. What this rule does NOT close, declared: The route still answers through the raw model outside that case: in a creative session without an agent (the seed's curl) and in a consultative one WITH an agent, for whoever calls it by hand. The screen calls it in neither; the owner's decision was about the consultative session without an agent, and closing the whole route is a separate decision. Free chat with history, the other option of AT-254, was not done. documents.t: Owner decision (10/01), recorded in ADR 0200. In the real use of 09/29, dev-board-engine spent 5 of its 24 tool steps reading other modules' worktrees to discover their interface: the module_map says who depends on whom, never what a module exposes. It applies RN-164 to the dev agents. The artifact is artifact.module_contracts, without a table, like module_routing and c4_diagram: the current one is the highest version, with ties broken by seq. Each declaration carries the WHOLE list and REPLACES the previous one; changing a contract is a new version by the Arquiteto. Per module, only what it EXPOSES: {modulo, expoe: [{tipo, assinatura, descricao}]}, tipo in funcao | rota | evento | dado, assinatura mandatory (up to 300 characters), from 1 to 40 items. What it CONSUMES is the dependsOn of the current module_map, derived on read — never retyped. The api refuses with 400 and the whole reason (which goes back to the model, RN-061): empty list, repeated module, module outside the current module_map (listing the valid ones) or no module_map, empty expoe or above 40, unknown tipo, empty assinatura or above 300. Nothing is recorded. An artifact SEPARATE from the module_map, never a field of it: revising one does not reissue the other. The dev reads through listar_contratos_de_modulos, :direct, in the Engine.Dev.Tools registry: project scope by the route, NO parameter, the dev's module coming from ctx.module. It shows in full its own and those it consumes; those that consume it and the rest, by name only; a ceiling of 120 items with the cut stated. A contract of a module that left the map is STATED, never attributed. The dev's kickoff says where to read another module's interface, and that it is not in another dev agent's worktree. Without a contract for a shown module, the tool says to implement from what the story and the task say and, if an interface is missing, report_blocked naming the module — never rereading the worktree. documents.t: Revises RN-520. Until now, revoking a device key brought down the runner's live connection by the {project, user} pair, because the credential's identity died in PatAuthGuard: a runner of the SAME user connected with a PAT or with another key went down too, and the MACHINE key (RN-543) multiplied that per project. Revoking a PAT brought down nothing. The ticket keeps WHICH credential requested it. runner_socket_tickets (an engine table) gains credential_kind (device_key | pat) and credential_id (the kid, which is the record's id — RN-475 —, or the PAT's id), both NULLABLE: the terminal ticket belongs to the web tab and has no device credential, and a runner one issued by an older api arrives without it. The PatAuthGuard annotates the credential AFTER authorizing (request.credencialDeDispositivo), the runner ticket carries it to the engine and the terminal one never does; an incomplete pair or an unknown kind becomes ABSENT, never an invented credential. The socket keeps the credential, and its id too. connect/3 sets assigns.credencial, and the id becomes runner_socket:<kind>:<projectId>:<userId>:<espécie>:<id> when it exists — the disconnect the channel broadcasts to its own id reaches only that credential. Revoking ONE credential: voids its PENDING tickets — a request made seconds before the revocation does not get in after it (consumed_at, the same "already used" state, no new state); asks EVERY runner in the cluster whether it was born from this credential — only the channel knows —, and only those born from it go down. The machine key is ONE request, and goes down in every project where it opened a connection, including one the api would not list; responds with a TALLY (derrubados, legados, intocados, semResposta, ticketsAnulados) — zero brought down is the normal case for an orphan key (RN-519). It applies to the three revocations: the key one (per project and through the Account, RN-611) and the two PAT ones (the owner's, RN-426, and the maintainer's, RN-427). It revokes FIRST, brings down afterwards, and bringing down is still a side effect that only LOGS — the DELETE stays 204 and idempotent. What already went down still goes down (the prohibition of AT-013). The LEGACY connection — a ticket without a credential — of the same owner, in one of the projects that a KEY revocation sends as scope (the row's, or the machine's candidates), goes down by the pair as before; the PAT gains no legacy scope, because it brought down nothing. And if the engine does not know the per-credential route (404 from an older engine), the key revocation falls back to the pair, disconnectRunnerOfUser, project by project. The {project, user} pair remains, with another owner: it is the target of member removal (RN-615), which removes the PERSON, with whatever credential. The screen states the precision (RN-561): the revoke confirmation — device keys in Configurações and machine keys in the Account — replaces "outro runner seu também cai" with "só cai o que se conectou com ESTA chave". The label changes, not the behavior. documents.t: Under Bun (the bun build --compile binary, ADR 0112), the tty.ReadStream with which node-pty reads the PTY's master side is an fs.ReadStream, and the first read with no data from the non-blocking fd RAISES as EAGAIN: the stream destroys itself, closes the fd, and no onData arrives after that (oven-sh/bun#25822). The binary's interactive terminal stopped after the first chunk of output on all THREE Unix platforms; Linux passed the proof only because the first read already brought the echo and the answer together. The rule: under Bun and outside Windows, node-pty's spawn runs with the tty.ReadStream swapped for its own reader that reads the SAME fd with fs.read and, on EAGAIN, WAITS and retries (from 4 ms, doubling up to 32 ms, back to the minimum on every piece of data); EIO or zero bytes is the end. The swap applies only DURING the spawn and is restored even when it throws; under Node the module comes back INTACT. The fd and the child process remain the real ones — nothing simulates output. And --self-test-pty makes TWO rounds, the second after a pause with nothing to read: it is the pause that forces the read through an EAGAIN, and it is through it that the old reader fails on Linux too. When it fails, the self-test says why (chunks, the child's output, a probe on a second PTY and the stream's events) — the verdict does not change. It was the probe that measured Windows: there the read side is ConPTY's named pipe, opened by node-pty as a net.Socket, without an fd the reader could take over, and the pipe ends after the first chunk — which is why win32-x64 left the matrix (ADR 0187) instead of getting a workaround. documents.t: The flow of ADR 0118 (RN-464..466) was RETIRED by owner decision (10/01, BRB-031): it was the only installation path that ended in a manual chmod +x, and install.sh already does its three things on the right side — it downloads the binary checked against the signed checksums.txt and installs it with install -m 0755 (RN-531), and creates the key ON THE MACHINE and registers it (RN-547, RN-551, RN-552). The rule: The RunnerOnboardingPanel shows the installer command (curl -fsSLO …/install.sh && bash install.sh, the SAME sentence as the runbook and install.sh, RN-526), copyable, with what it does stated in text, the caveat that it serves the installation's machine, and the EsperaDoRunner (RN-474) below. The command in the web is a COPY, and the copy is checked against the installer's constant. Once an active key that serves the project is recognized — machine (RN-548) or project (AT-107) —, the installer block LEAVES and the gesture is checking the service. The manual command with a PAT (--token) always stays in the <details>, named as the path for ANOTHER machine. There is no button to configure a folder, to download files, nor a platform selector, and the web no longer calls Web Crypto, File System Access nor the binary proxy. runner-bootstrap.ts was removed entirely. The api no longer has POST /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys. It was left without a caller. GET and DELETE stay (list and revoke); the internal machine route (POST /internal/machine-device-keys) stays. An ALREADY registered project key remains valid and revocable: nothing in the database changes, PatAuthGuard keeps accepting it (RN-465) and the CLI keeps reading the configured folder (RN-466). A runner configured through the browser before ADR 0203 does not break. Left out, declared: an installation with a TEAM loses the PAT-less path to pair a second machine (the machine key route is 409 with two or more people), and now uses the manual command; GET /runner-releases/binary is left without a production consumer and was NOT removed — that is a separate decision. documents.t: Revised by RN-713 (AT-385, 10/02): auto mode (the wildcard in auto_approve) now unlocks git_push and pr_open. Revises RN-418, by owner decision (10/01). Until now decide()'s external-effect ceiling only looked at actionType === 'terminal': a TYPED git push became require_approval, and the message said to use the typed action git_push — which, with the minimum role (maintainer) met, was born auto_approved through ANY of the three stages: the "*" wildcard of auto mode (RN-153, the autopilot of RN-670), a specific agent_autonomy rule (execution activation seeded git_push/pr_open as auto_approve for each dev-<modulo>) or an allow in permissions.json. Measured in decide.spec.ts before the fix: the six cases (two types × three stages) came out auto_approve. The rule: git_push and pr_open enter the block of absolute ceilings — if the verdict up to that point is auto_approve, it becomes unconditional require_approval, with the named reason ("teto de efeito externo (RN-418): … nunca é auto-aprovável"), which goes in proposed_action.created. deny has already returned before and still wins; the ORIGIN of the autonomy does not matter. The "sempre permitir" of both was already refused at the source (RN-642, TIPOS_SEM_SEMPRE_PERMITIR), and that is the half that keeps the ceiling from being decorative. The seeding follows along: DEV_AUTO_GIT_ACTIONS becomes only git_commit — on activation and on parallelization acceptance. Seeding push and PR would be recording an autonomy that decide() never honors, the screen promising what does not happen (the argument of RN-642). Already recorded rows stay in the database, inert. The dev agent follows the path of RN-050: commit executed, push and PR pending, agent in awaiting_approval holding the worktree until task.pr_settled; only then does the gate open. Left OUT, on purpose: git_merge (its own protected-branch ceiling); git_commit (stays on the machine, RN-670); open_adr_pr and open_infra_pr (they open a real PR on the provider, but the owner's decision does not cover them — open_infra_pr is seeded auto_approve on the Infra's acceptance, RN-671); the bootstrap actions (git_repo_create/git_branch_create/git_branch_protect, which do not go through decide()); and deploy, which is not a proposed_action type — it only exists as a target of the terminal command's message. documents.t: Measured in the real use of v7.0.0: the text the Anamnese's model writes during the round ("Analisando a janela do log… usuário (09824667-…)… Decisão de proficiência") appeared as a BUBBLE in the ideation session's thread, between the Criativo and the PO, with the user's raw UUID. The Anamnese does not converse with anyone: it analyzes the PERSON, and what it produces is the profile (RN-680). The rule: the round's text is recorded as anamnese.analysis, never as agent.response. The ToolLoop accepts response_event in the context (default agent.response, unchanged for every other consumer) and the Anamnese sets it. The session thread draws NO event whose actor is the anamnese agent — including the agent.response recorded before the fix. The session's log panel keeps showing its events; the result lives in Configurações › Perfil de proficiência, without a raw id. No "profile updated" marker enters the thread: it is left out until someone asks. documents.t: Measured in the code: until now the proficiency_profiles that the Anamnese records reached no agent at all — only the Psicólogo's FACTS accepted by the person (RN-680) went into the turn. The profile was screen-only. The rule: the api reads the message AUTHOR's level per competence in this project (listByUser) and adds it to the SAME perfilDoAutor text that the engine puts as an ephemeral system message in the turn (Engine.Harness.PerfilDoAutor) — no agent server changes. Only competência: nível goes, with the guidance to calibrate how many questions to ask; the rationale and the evidence do NOT go, and a level outside the scale is discarded. Ceiling of 12 competences, and the whole text stays under the 2,000-character TETO_DO_TEXTO. A read failure is a log, and the turn goes on without it, independently of the graph read. fatosDoPerfil in chat.message still counts only the Psicólogo's facts. Left OUT, and it is a pending product decision: what the Anamnese observes about the AGENT's behavior (the loop, the user cancelling the turn) becoming a product improvement signal, separate from the person's profile. TODO(humano): is the product improvement signal coming from the Anamnese an event (anamnese.agent_signal, with no person subject) or its own table, who reads it (Staff? an improvements screen?) and how long does it live? It is a new data boundary and calls for an ADR (0205 reserved).
