While blocked, the screen re-queries on its own every 15s — once decided, the image does not change without new human action, and re-querying a stable state would be the same family of unnecessary traffic as PÓS-FASE 15. The presentation of the fourth state was EXTRACTED to ContainerImageGateNotice (apps/web/src/components/ContainerImageGate.tsx) — a usage finding: the PRs tab (apps/web/src/routes/code/PrListAndDiff.tsx, consumed by ProjectPrsTab.tsx and by CodeDiffPanel.tsx) calls getCodePullRequests/ getCodeDiff, which go through the SAME funnel (RN-105) and can return the SAME 409 — but, unlike this tab, without asking first. It showed that 409 in the generic error banner with "Tentar de novo", the wrong affordance for a state only the Arquiteto resolves. isContainerImageGateError (apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts) identifies the cause by status === 409 — the only cause of ConflictException in ReadProjectCodeUseCase.alvo — and PrListAndDiff swaps the banner for ContainerImageGateNotice when it matches, without a pre-check of its own (it reacts to the 409 of the query that was going to run anyway). Where: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectCodeTab.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectCodeTab.module.css, apps/web/src/components/ContainerImageGate.tsx (shared presentation), apps/web/src/routes/code/PrListAndDiff.tsx (consumer reactive to the 409), apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts (isContainerImageGateError) Test: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectCodeTab.test.tsx ("o gate"), apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeDiffPanel.test.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectPrsTab.test.tsx ("o gate do container não é erro genérico") Edge case: the front-end check does NOT replace the api's — it is a UX convenience. If the api changes state between the gate query and the actual read, the read route still refuses with 409 (RN-105); the front only avoids the common case of showing the empty editor for an instant. The PRs tab does no pre-check: it discovers the block when the query has already failed, because there is no tree/file there for the "empty" instant that the Code tab's pre-check avoids. Origin: ADR 0065
documents.s: RN-107 — The Code tab has a FOURTH state: blocked by a pending decision

documents.t: Foundation of the blame gap declared in FASE 26 (no screen consumes it yet — it comes in the next wave). blame(ref, path) returns GitBlame | null, null meaning exactly what it already means in getFileContent/ listTree: file absent at that ref, or nonexistent ref. Two vocabularies of "does not exist" for the same tab would make the screen treat the same case in two ways — the same reason that already held for the two previous operations. Each provider computes by its OWN means, because there is no common endpoint: GitHub has no blame in REST (only GraphQL — the only provider operation that speaks GraphQL), GitLab has repository/files/:path/blame, and the local one comes from git blame --porcelain, the only one of the three tested against a real repository in this session (the other two only against the fake backends of the contract test — without GITHUB_TEST_TOKEN/GITLAB_TEST_TOKEN in the environment, what proves against the real API is the manual smoke). GIT_BLAME_LINE_LIMIT (2000) cuts a genuinely huge file — already cut by bytes on the content route, but blame reads the whole file from the provider before deciding. Where: packages/shared/src/index.ts (BlameInput, GitBlame, GitBlameLine, capability blame), apps/api/src/infrastructure/git/{github,gitlab,local}-provider.ts, apps/api/src/domain/git/git-read-limits.ts (GIT_BLAME_LINE_LIMIT), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/git/read-project-code.use-case.ts (method blame), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/git/code.controller.ts (GET /projects/:id/code/blame) Test: apps/api/test/contract/git-provider.contract.ts ("blame" block), exercised by the three provider specs — the local one against real git — and read-project-code.use-case.spec.ts ("blame" block) Origin: FASE 26b (foundation of the declared gaps of FASE 26/ ADR 0060)
documents.s: RN-110 — blame is the 13th operation of the GitProviderContract, with the same absence vocabulary as the other reads

documents.t: CodeDiffPanel.tsx consumes listPullRequests(state?) in a clickable list (id/number/title/author/state/branches, with a filter by state); clicking an item reuses the SAME diff-by-id flow that already existed — there is no new read path, only how to REACH the id without knowing it by heart. Whoever already knows the id (e.g.: came from Approvals) can still paste it directly. listPullRequests(state?) returns a SUMMARY per PR (GitPullRequestSummary: id, number, title, author, state, branches, updatedAt) — not GitPullRequest, which is the WRITE type (open/merge) and never had title or author because neither of the two operations needed them. A type of its own keeps the write from gaining fields only the read uses. local HAS PRs — the sidecar store of Fase 4a is already the source, and the assumption of the brief ("PR does not exist in the concept of a pure local repository") did not hold: the self-contained dev agents have created local PRs since then. The three capabilities are true. GIT_PR_LIST_LIMIT (100) is a single page, with no follow-up pagination — human navigation, not history synchronization. Where: packages/shared/src/index.ts (ListPullRequestsInput, GitPullRequestSummary, GitPullRequestList, capability pullRequestsList), apps/api/src/infrastructure/git/{github,gitlab, local}-provider.ts, apps/api/src/domain/git/git-read-limits.ts (GIT_PR_LIST_LIMIT), read-project-code.use-case.ts (method pullRequests), code.controller.ts (GET /projects/:id/code/pull-requests), apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeDiffPanel.tsx (clickable list, filter by state, reuse of the diff-by-id flow) Test: git-provider.contract.ts ("listPullRequests" block), read-project-code.use-case.spec.ts ("lista de PRs" block), apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeDiffPanel.test.tsx Origin: FASE 26b
documents.s: RN-111 — listPullRequests is the 14th operation of the GitProviderContract; the navigable list opens the same diff by id

documents.t: Foundation of the rich dropdown, now consumed by CodeBranchPicker.tsx (ahead/behind, PR badge — the wave after FASE 26b closed the gap that CodeShell.tsx declared). The decision was NOT to extend listBranches — the original 13th operation, which the Gitflow bootstrap calls without needing any of this: enriching costs an extra call to the provider PER BRANCH (two on GitLab, which has no endpoint returning both sides of a comparison in a single call, unlike GitHub's compareCommitsWithBasehead and git rev-list --left-right --count locally). Attaching that cost to every branch adoption/creation would turn the bootstrap into an expensive sweep. The two operations coexist in the contract: listBranches for the bootstrap, listBranchesDetailed (the 15th) for the Code tab — GitBranchDetail extends GitBranch only in SHAPE, never in the CONTRACT of the caller. ahead/behind are always relative to the repository's DEFAULT branch (ListBranchesDetailedInput.defaultBranch, which the caller already knows — asking for it again from the provider would be one more call just to rediscover what it already had). null in both when the provider cannot compute (orphan branch, unrelated history) is honest degradation, never an invented number. GIT_BRANCH_DETAIL_LIMIT (30) cuts for the same traffic reasons as item 34 of FASE 26 — without it, a repository with hundreds of branches would become hundreds of calls per dropdown opening. Where: packages/shared/src/index.ts (ListBranchesDetailedInput, GitBranchDetail, GitBranchDetailList, GitBranchPullRequestRef, capability branchesDetailed), apps/api/src/infrastructure/git/{github, gitlab,local}-provider.ts, git-read-limits.ts (GIT_BRANCH_DETAIL_LIMIT), read-project-code.use-case.ts (method branches), code.controller.ts (GET /projects/:id/code/branches); on the web, apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts (getCodeBranches) and apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeBranchPicker.tsx — the dropdown itself, opened from CodeShell.tsx Test: git-provider.contract.ts ("listBranchesDetailed" block), read-project-code.use-case.spec.ts ("branches detalhadas" block), apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeBranchPicker.test.tsx Edge case: the branches() method lives in the SAME use case as the other six reads (ReadProjectCodeUseCase), not near the bootstrap — it is a READ of the Code tab, with the same credential resolution and the same container gate (RN-105) as the others; treating it as a bootstrap operation would duplicate both. A ref outside the branch list (tag or sha) remains reachable — the dropdown footer has a manual field, because listBranchesDetailed does not enumerate those two things. Origin: FASE 26b (foundation); the next wave closed the UI
documents.s: RN-112 — listBranchesDetailed is an operation of its OWN, separate from listBranches

documents.t: The UI that consumes the foundation of RN-110 comes in here: the Code tab editor (CodeEditor.tsx) only calls getCodeBlame when the user turns on the "Blame" toggle — never together with the file read, which already fires by itself when opening a tab. The reason is the same as the composite-read budgets (ADR 0060): blame is a SECOND call to the provider per open file, and a file near the ceiling (GIT_BLAME_LINE_LIMIT, 2000 lines) is already expensive enough not to pay for it for free on every navigation. truncated (which RN-110 already exposes) becomes a visible warning, in the same pattern as the fileQuery.data.truncated warning. Consecutive lines of the SAME commit show author and short sha only on the FIRST line of the block — repeating the same text on each line of a block of dozens of lines would be noise, not annotation; the line only disappears from the text, never from the annotation (the element's title keeps the full date and the commit summary on any line of the block). Where: apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeEditor.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeEditor.module.css Test: apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeEditor.test.tsx Origin: UI wave of FASE 26b (blame — rich branch dropdown and PR list are UI from two other agents, with no collision risk)
documents.s: RN-113 — Blame in the editor is an ON-DEMAND annotation — a toggle, never embedded in the file read

documents.t: ANAMNESE_ENABLED (engine env var, boolean, default false as of this rule) decides whether a NEW Anamnese round can happen — periodic (AnamneseSchedulerWorker) or on demand (AnamneseCommandController). A PRODUCT decision by the user on 2026-08-10 ("hoje ele não está trazendo dados de muito valor"), not a bug — see docs/explanation/backlog.md. Disabled, NO existing data is touched: hypotheses, proficiency profiles and instruction patches already stored remain intact and visible, and the PER-MEMBER opt-out (RN-025) remains a separate concept — the pause belongs to the SYSTEM, not to individual profiling. AnamneseSchedulerWorker.kickoff/0 (called once at boot) does NOT schedule the periodic job when disabled, instead of scheduling it and letting perform/1 no-op on every tick — cheaper (the Oban queue does not receive a job every ANAMNESE_INTERVAL_SECONDS just to do nothing) and clearer for whoever inspects the queue. Correction on 2026-08-10 (a real finding in execution, not a hypothesis): the original version of this rule left perform/1 unconditional on purpose, so the chain between rounds would not carry the decision to turn on/off with it — but that meant a chain already scheduled BEFORE the flag existed (or before someone disabled it) kept rescheduling itself forever, running the Anamnese for real with the flag saying false. That is exactly what happened on a dev Postgres older than the original PR, remedied by hand by cancelling the scheduled jobs. perform/1 now checks enabled?/0 on every tick, like kickoff/0: if disabled, neither enqueue_projects/0 nor the rescheduling happens, and the chain dies there — which also SELF-HEALS the scenario of an old job that still fires once, without needing manual intervention. AnamneseCommandController.run/2 (on-demand route, "reanalisar agora" in Settings) answers 503 with body {"error": "anamnese_desativada"} when disabled — deliberately distinct from the empty 409 that already existed for "project without session" (the two were easy to confuse in a bare 409, and they are quite different causes). RunAnamneseUseCase, on the api side, converts the engine's 503 into ServiceUnavailableException with reason: "anamnese_disabled" in the body — never a generic 500 nor a reused 409. The web (ProjectSettingsTab.tsx) discovers the state on the first click of "Rodar agora" (there is currently no prior read of the global state) and, from then on, disables the button and keeps the explanation VISIBLE on screen — not just a toast that disappears (RN-088: never a silent or confusing failure). Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/workers/anamnese_scheduler_worker.ex (enabled?/0, kickoff/0), apps/engine/lib/engine_web/controllers/anamnese_command_controller.ex, apps/engine/config/runtime.exs, apps/api/src/domain/anamnese/anamnese-disabled.error.ts, apps/api/src/infrastructure/http-clients/api-to-engine-client.ts (runAnamnese), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/anamnese/run-anamnese.use-case.ts, apps/web/src/routes/settings/ProficiencySection.tsx Test: apps/engine/test/engine/workers/anamnese_scheduler_worker_test.exs (kickoff/0 does not schedule when disabled, schedules when enabled, default off; perform/1 disabled in the middle of the chain does no fan-out nor reschedules), apps/engine/test/engine_web/controllers/anamnese_command_controller_test.exs (503 distinct from 409, with and without session), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/anamnese/run-anamnese.use-case.spec.ts, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSettingsTab.test.tsx (ProficiencySection) Edge case: the flag is GLOBAL (all projects/workspaces), not per project — unlike the parallelism ceiling (RN-083) or the model inheritable per area (RN-102), which are per-scope decisions. Turning it back on is ANAMNESE_ENABLED=true and restarting the engine; there is no UI button for it (it is operational, not a project preference). Origin: no ADR — a reversible product decision, not a structural architecture change. See docs/explanation/backlog.md.
documents.s: RN-115 — The Anamnese can be paused globally; the pause belongs to the PRODUCT, it never deletes data

documents.t: PSYCHOLOGIST_ENABLED (engine env var, boolean, default false) decides whether a NEW Psicólogo round can happen — automatic (session closing, routed by Engine.Outbox.Drain) or on demand (PsychologistCommandController.reanalyze/2). The same PRODUCT decision by the user on 2026-08-10 already applied to the Anamnese (RN-115, "hoje ele não está trazendo dados de muito valor") — not a bug, see docs/explanation/backlog.md. Disabled, NO existing data is touched: analyses and hypotheses already emitted remain intact and visible. Unlike the Anamnese (whose automatic trigger is a periodic TICK that the flag itself decides whether to reschedule), the Psicólogo's automatic trigger is session closing — Engine.Outbox.Drain routes session.closed/session.closed_abnormally to PsychologistWorker only when PsychologistWorker.enabled?/0 is true (Drain.handlers_for/1); disabled, only SessionLifecycleWorker runs, and the Psicólogo job is not even born. PsychologistWorker.perform/1 remains unconditional on purpose — but it is NO longer "the same pattern" as AnamneseSchedulerWorker (see the 2026-08-10 correction in RN-115 above): there perform/1 started checking the flag because it ITSELF reschedules the chain on every tick, and an old job firing unconditionally reopened the Anamnese with the flag off. The Psicólogo has no chain that reschedules itself — each job is born from ONE event (session.closed), and what decides is the Drain at the moment it RECEIVES the event, not the worker at the moment it RUNS; a Psicólogo job already enqueued before turning the flag off is, at most, the last pending round, never an infinite chain. That is why the pre-existing suite of PsychologistWorker (which calls perform/1 directly) did not need to change. PsychologistCommandController.reanalyze/2 (on-demand route, "Reanalisar" in the Insights tab) answers 503 with body {"error": "psicologo_desativado"} when disabled, without even creating the job. ReanalyzeSessionUseCase, on the api side, converts the engine's 503 into ServiceUnavailableException with reason: "psychologist_disabled" in the body — never a generic 500. This discovers the pause when there is already an analysis to reprocess; the screen with NO hypothesis at all has its own prior read, which did not exist here — see RN-454. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/workers/psychologist_worker.ex (enabled?/0), apps/engine/lib/engine/outbox/drain.ex (handlers_for/1), apps/engine/lib/engine_web/controllers/psychologist_command_controller.ex, apps/engine/config/runtime.exs, apps/api/src/domain/psychologist/psychologist-disabled.error.ts, apps/api/src/infrastructure/http-clients/api-to-engine-client.ts (reanalyzeSession), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/execution/reanalyze-session.use-case.ts, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectInsightsTab.tsx Test: apps/engine/test/engine/outbox/drain_test.exs (session.closed only enqueues the Psicólogo when enabled), apps/engine/test/engine_web/controllers/psychologist_command_controller_test.exs (503 without creating a job, 202 with the job enqueued when enabled), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/execution/reanalyze-session.use-case.spec.ts, apps/web/src/routes/ProjectInsightsTab.test.tsx Edge case: the flag is GLOBAL (all projects/workspaces), like the Anamnese's. Turning it back on is PSYCHOLOGIST_ENABLED=true and restarting the engine; there is no UI button for it. Origin: no ADR — a reversible product decision, not a structural architecture change. See docs/explanation/backlog.md.
documents.s: RN-117 — The Psicólogo can be paused globally; the pause belongs to the PRODUCT, it never deletes data

documents.t: EngineWeb.SessionSocket.connect/3 refused the whole connection with only the session_id (UUID) needing to exist in the Registry — whoever discovered the UUID entered the session:<id> channel and received all the live broadcasts of the session. Closing this was a deliberate limitation documented in the module itself since Fase 3. POST /projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId/socket-ticket (scope: "heartbeat"|"terminal") issues an opaque ticket (32 bytes of CSPRNG, TokenFactory), TTL of 30 seconds, single use. scope: "heartbeat" requires the viewer role; scope: "terminal" requires developer — the same minimum role as MIN_ROLE_FOR_ACTION_TYPE.terminal in domain/actions/decide.ts (today no path really asks for terminal; the value is born right for FASE 25, the interactive terminal). The api persists only the HASH (plain SHA-256, not hashDeToken/HMAC — the engine does not have the api's pepper, and a 256-bit CSPRNG token does not need a pepper against a dictionary, the same reasoning that hashDeToken itself already records), never the raw token. Consumption belongs to the ENGINE, which reads session_socket_tickets directly (same pattern as Engine.Outbox.Event over outbox_events — never changeset/insert, only the narrow write that single use requires) in TWO steps: SocketTicket.validar/1 (peek, marking nothing — called by connect/3, which does not yet know which session_id will be requested) and SocketTicket.consumir/2 (conditional UPDATE requiring the topic's session_id to match the row's — called by SessionChannel.join/3, which also checks the ticket's project_id against the session's, defense in depth against a ticket of one project opening a channel of another). Without a ticket, or with an invalid one: the whole connection is refused ({:error, %{reason: "unauthorized"}}), not only the channel join. The web (session-channel.ts) fetches a NEW ticket before EVERY socket.connect() — including on automatic reconnection, which exists. The native reconnect of Phoenix.Socket would reuse the same params from construction (the old ticket, already expired or consumed), so it is neutralized (reconnectAfterMs that practically never fires) and reconnection becomes entirely manual, fetching a fresh ticket on each attempt. That neutralization holds for EVERY client of the socket, and not only for the web's — including the /runner socket, whose ticket (POST .../runner-ticket) is of the same caliber. It failed in TWO of the four Socket constructors in the repository, and the cost was measured in real execution: apps/runner/src/ channel.ts built the socket without the option — while the module's docblock CLAIMED the reconnect was "por isso neutralizado" — and the auto-reconnect repeated the same already-consumed ticket every ~5.13s (the ceiling of the phoenix.js internal backoff), yielding 61 REFUSED CONNECTION TO EngineWeb.RunnerSocket in a few hours. Added to the runner's OWN policy (index.ts, that one correct), the result was 530 requests in one minute against the ceiling of 300 of RATE_LIMIT_USER — and since the limit is per USER, the 429 showed up in the account owner's BROWSER. Two consequences, and the second is worse than the 429: while it is in that loop the runner is NOT connected, so RunnerReadiness (RN-507) refuses and the project looks like it has "no local agent". apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser-channel.ts had the SAME defect line (same single-use ticket, and no reconnection policy of its own — its onClose says "close and reopen") and was fixed along with it. What prevents the third instance is MECHANISM, not a comment: in the runner the Socket options became a type with a MANDATORY reconnectAfterMs (OpcoesDoSocket in channel.ts), and both sides gained a test asserting the OPTION PASSED to the constructor — a test that only checks "connects" would pass with the defect standing, and it did. Along with it, conectarERodar (index.ts) started to explicitly DISCARD the dropped connection (conexao.desconectar()): without it the Socket of the previous round survived the creation of the next one, and each drop left one more live object trying with the dead ticket. Where: apps/api/src/db/schema/sessions.ts (sessionSocketTickets), apps/api/src/domain/sessions/socket-ticket-scope.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/sessions/create-socket-ticket.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/sessions/sessions.controller.ts (route socket-ticket), apps/engine/lib/engine/sessions/socket_ticket.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/session_socket.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/session_channel.ex, apps/web/src/lib/session-channel.ts, apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser-channel.ts, apps/runner/src/channel.ts (OpcoesDoSocket, NUNCA_RECONECTAR_SOZINHO_MS), apps/runner/src/index.ts (conectarERodar, the discarding of the dropped connection) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/sessions/create-socket-ticket.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/domain/sessions/socket-ticket-scope.spec.ts, apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/session-socket-ticket.repository.spec.ts, apps/engine/test/engine/sessions/socket_ticket_test.exs (reuse fails, wrong session_id fails, concurrent race only one wins), apps/engine/test/engine_web/channels/session_socket_test.exs (without a ticket the connection is refused), apps/engine/test/engine_web/channels/session_channel_test.exs (ticket from another project: join fails), apps/web/src/lib/session-channel.test.ts, apps/runner/src/channel.spec.ts ("neutraliza o auto-reconnect do Phoenix.Socket — ticket de uso único nunca é repetido"; asserts the OPTION passed to the constructor, and fails without it), apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser-channel.test.ts (the same, in the folder browser's transport via runner) Edge case: the ticket is NOT the reused JWT — short TTL, single use, closed scope, and it is born from a route of its own that already checks the effective role, not from decoding the existing access token. Origin: no ADR — a one-off extraction/hardening, not a structural change.
documents.s: RN-108 — The session socket requires a single-use opaque ticket, not the reused JWT

documents.t: A project's physical folder in PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT was the bare UUID — unreadable when opened on disk. projects.workspace_dir_name (NOT NULL, UNIQUE) started storing the real name: <slug>-<8 chars do id> for a NEW project (workspaceDirNameFor in apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts), generated in code — the id is born from crypto.randomUUID() in CreateProjectUseCase, not from Postgres's defaultRandom(), because the folder name needs the id BEFORE the insert. The 8 characters follow the same convention as the session label (apps/web/src/lib/session-label.ts). The name is FROZEN at creation time and never recomputed: UpdateProjectUseCase allows editing the slug later, and that does NOT touch workspace_dir_name — renaming the physical folder, with a working tree and agent worktrees possibly open, is a real risk the decision avoids by construction, not by the caller's discipline. A project created BEFORE this migration (0042) kept the physical folder it already had: the backfill writes workspace_dir_name = id for every existing row — the same value that was already true on disk — and NEVER renames any directory. A BEFORE INSERT trigger (projects_workspace_dir_name_default_trg) applies the SAME fallback (id::text) to any insert that arrives without the field — a safety net for whoever forgets to write it (never the main path, which always writes it explicitly), and what keeps the dozens of existing test fixtures, which do not know this concept, working without needing to rewrite each one. Path derivation from the name (projectScopeRoot, RN-092/RN-075) started receiving workspace_dir_name instead of the raw projectId — same charset validation, same purity. The engine reads the SAME column (Engine.Projects.Project.workspace_dir_name/1) to resolve Engine.Actions.Workspace.workspace_dir/1, never recomputing the name from the id: the two derivations (api and engine) are, in practice, the same read against the same database — that is what guarantees RN-075 (terminal scope) and RN-092 (code reading) keep pointing to the SAME folder the engine really uses. Where: apps/api/src/db/schema/iam.ts (projects.workspaceDirName), apps/api/src/db/migrations/0042_tough_captain_midlands.sql, apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts (workspaceDirNameFor, projectScopeRoot), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/create-project.use-case.ts, apps/engine/lib/engine/projects/project.ex (workspace_dir_name/1, all_workspace_dirs/0), apps/engine/lib/engine/actions/workspace.ex (workspace_dir/1,2), apps/engine/lib/engine/dev/worktree_cleanup.ex Test: apps/api/test/db/workspace-dir-name-migration.spec.ts (trigger, equivalent backfill, uniqueness), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/create-project-semeia-areas.spec.ts (workspaceDirName is born <slug>-<8 chars>, two projects with the same slug in different workspaces do not collide on folder), apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.spec.ts Edge case: the parallelism ceiling and the merge gate do not change — RN-109 is only the folder NAME, never policy. Renaming the slug after creation does not rename the folder; the folder is only read through the stored workspace_dir_name. Origin: ADR 0066 (revises ADR 0055).
documents.s: RN-109 — The workspace folder name is frozen at creation, and an old project keeps the UUID

documents.t: RN-059 closed the empty bubble for the four conversational agents, but they do not go through Engine.Harness.ToolLoop — each one calls EngineApiClient.llm_turn_stream/6 in its own module. The ToolLoop (used by dev agents, QA Automação/Performance-Segurança, Infra-Workflows, Anamnese and Psicólogo) had the SAME defect on a different path: it emitted agent.response on every iteration, even when the model only called a tool without text, or ended the turn without producing anything — and the transport failure (provider down, timeout) became an agent.response with absent content, equally indistinguishable from success. Found live in a real execution session (dev agents): two bubbles with the RN-059 compatibility text ("resposta vazia — evento anterior...") appeared in a session created minutes earlier — they were not old events, they were the same defect happening again, only in the execution tab. Two fixes, at the STRUCTURAL point common to every ToolLoop consumer, not module by module: Empty content never becomes agent.response. An iteration that only called a tool is already narrated by tool.call/tool.result; an iteration that produced nothing (neither text nor tool call) leaves the outcome for the loop's caller to decide — ctx.last_error/{:ok, ctx} carry the information, and the consumer (e.g.: DevAgentServer.handle_outcome/4) already writes the durable event of its OWN domain (dev.blocked, with origem). A transport failure becomes a durable agent.error, with origem (Engine.Agents.FalhaDeTurno.origem/1 — the SAME helper the four conversational agents use, without duplicating classification) and mensagem in Portuguese — never again an agent.response without content. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tool_loop.ex (loop/1, emit_falha/2) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/harness/tool_loop_test.exs ("iteração só com tool call (sem texto) não grava agent.response vazio", "modelo termina o turno sem texto e sem tool call...", "falha de transporte... grava agent.error durável com origem") Origin: RN-059 (the rule this one extends) — found live in a real execution session with dev agents
documents.s: RN-129 — The ToolLoop never writes an empty agent.response; a transport failure becomes a durable agent.error

documents.t: ProjectExecutorsTab fetched the dev agent/QA events by the session that useLatestSession returned — the project's one with the most recent createdAt, without filtering by kind nor requiring execution.activated. It worked only by coincidence: the execution session tends to be the newest. As soon as any session is born after it — a new ideation, a consultative chat — the tab starts looking at that new session, empty of execution events, silently: no hint on screen said which session was being displayed. The correct read already existed in the backend: findActiveExecutionSession (SessionRepository) — the most recent active session that carries execution.activated — but it was only used internally by ActivateExecutionUseCase to decide whether to reactivate or create. The fix exposes the SAME criterion over HTTP, instead of duplicating it in the front: GET /projects/:projectId/execution/session (role:viewer) returns the current session or null — it never infers from the most recent; ProjectExecutorsTab swaps useLatestSession for useActiveExecutionSession (a new hook over the route above) as the source of the session the whole tab reads; the tab header always shows WHICH session is being displayed — its label (hashtag + name) linking to SessionPage, or "Nenhuma execução ativa" when null — never implicit again. The three states of RN-088 apply to the session fetch itself: loading, error (with trace_id) and empty (null) are three distinct renders, never an if (!sessão) return null that collapses them. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/execution/get-active-execution-session.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/execution/execution.controller.ts (getSession), apps/web/src/lib/hooks.ts (useActiveExecutionSession), apps/web/src/routes/ProjectExecutorsTab.tsx Test: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectExecutorsTab.test.tsx — shows the execution session even with a more recent session existing in the project, an explicit "nenhuma execução ativa" state, and a network error handled (not blank) Origin: finding from code investigation + live test — the same class of defect RN-088 closed for 429, now for "which session the screen is looking at"
documents.s: RN-139 — The Executors tab reads the CURRENT execution session, never the project's most recent one

documents.t: RN-074 locked the terminal output against {413, "request entity too large"}, but left the same door open through read_file: it read the WHOLE file, with no ceiling, and that content entered the loop history and traveled in every following turn. A PR with a large file (lockfile, bundle, generated file) was enough to lock up dev agents AND the Performance/Security QA — which only has ReadFile/SearchWorkspace (no Terminal, on purpose) to investigate a PR, so it had no escape route at all when the file was too large. The content is cut at READ_FILE_MAX_BYTES (default 32 KiB, the same value as RN-074 by coincidence of context, not by coupling — the two variables are independent) before becoming the tool result, with a marker stating the file and the two sizes: [arquivo package-lock.json truncado: mostrando 32768 de 1048576 bytes. Use search_workspace para localizar um trecho específico em vez de reler o arquivo inteiro.] The same three properties as RN-074 (the ceiling is > not >=; the cut does not split a multibyte character; the marker is addressed to the model, saying what to do). The truncation lives in the TOOL (Engine.Harness.Tools.ReadFile), not in Engine.Harness.WorkspaceFiles.read_file/2 — that is the generic file access base, shared by write_file/search_workspace, and truncating there would cut content of those who do not need that ceiling. search_workspace did not get the same treatment: it returns only the PATHS that matched (matched_content is a boolean), never the file content — the overflow vector that motivated this RN does not apply to it. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/read_file.ex (truncate/2), ceiling in apps/engine/config/runtime.exs (read_file_max_bytes) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/harness/tools/read_file_test.exs (describe teto de bytes do conteúdo) Origin: found live in the event log of a real execution — the 4 dev agents of a project and the Automação/Performance-Segurança QAs blocked with {413, "request entity too large"}, the same root cause as RN-074, a different door
documents.s: RN-141 — The content read by read_file also has a byte ceiling

documents.t: The session that receives execution.activated and the dev agents' tool-call events must be born with kind: 'criativa' — a structural rule (RN-097, garantirQuePodeAtivarExecucao), without which the event is refused. Since ProjectSessionsTab (the Criativo tab, RN-104) lists sessions filtering only by session.kind === 'criativa', the execution session appeared MIXED in the list next to real ideations — opening it in SessionPage.tsx shows a whole timeline of dev agent tool-calls, looking (to the user) like "the dev writing in the Criativo's chat". Confirmed live: a real session with 35+ dev agent events appeared normally in the list, next to real ideation sessions. The fix reuses the signal that RN-139 already exposes — useActiveExecutionSession/GET /projects/:projectId/execution/session — instead of the backend computing a new field per session (hasExecutionActivated or equivalent). The Criativo tab fetches the current session and excludes it from the rendered list: the fetch only runs on the Criativo tab (enabled off when kind !== 'criativa') — the Chat tab never made that call and still does not; the filter is by id, after the existing filter by kind — it does not change what the list IS, only what it EXCLUDES. Deliberate scope decision: this covers only the CURRENT execution, not OLD executions already closed (execution.activated written in a session that is now closed). Computing that would require the backend to annotate, per session, whether it has the event written — a change in the repository and in the listing endpoint, for a residual case: an OLD execution session appears with the closed badge, which already signals "this is not an active ideation" in a much less ambiguous way than the current one (which appeared active, indistinguishable from an ideation in progress). If this becomes confusing again in practice, the way out is the listing endpoint returning the signal per session — not one more filter in the front per old session. Where: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSessionsTab.tsx (ProjectSessionsTab) Test: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSessionsTab.test.tsx — the current one disappears from the Criativo list with normal sessions next to it, the Chat tab does not call the current-execution fetch, and without a current execution (null) the list appears whole Origin: finding from code investigation + live test — a real session with active execution appearing mixed in the Criativo tab
documents.s: RN-144 — The Criativo tab does not list the current execution session

documents.t: OfferInfraHandoffUseCase (POST .../agents/arquiteto/handoff-infra) already existed since Fase 4a — it writes architecture.readiness_confirmed and calls the engine, which offers the handoff to Infra and, in the SAME confirmation, to the Dev Lead (FASE 14d/ADR 0053). What was missing was the way to reach it: no place in the frontend called the endpoint. The "Confirmar arquitetura pronta" button exists for the Criativo since always ("Estou pronto para produzir", RN-131/RN-142) — the Arquiteto had no equivalent at all, and without the click the handoff was never born: the priority fix of the card in the thread (RN-125) had no practical effect, because there was nothing to show. arquitetoActive mirrors criativoActive (there is an agent.activated for the Arquiteto in this session) and arquiteturaJaDeclarada mirrors prontidaoJaDeclarada (there is ANY handoff leaving the Arquiteto — the proof that the confirmation already happened, since OfferInfraHandoffUseCase creates at least the Infra one in the same call). The button appears in the composer only when the first is true and the second is not — it disappears after the click for the same reason the Criativo's disappears after readiness. Unlike the Criativo, the Arquiteto has NO server guardrail blocking the confirmation without a module_map — ArquitetoServer.offer_infra_handoff refuses nothing, unlike CriativoServer.confirm_readiness (RN-142). The button is only disabled during streaming; not replicating here the Overview's disabled={!hasModuleMap} is a deliberate decision, by the same reasoning that already holds for "Ativar execução" on the Dev Lead card (RN-137) — when this card exists, the Arquiteto has already decided the architecture. Where: apps/api/src/interfaces/http/agents/agents.controller.ts (handoffInfra, pre-existing route), apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts (confirmArchitectureReadiness), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (arquitetoActive, arquiteturaJaDeclarada, handleArchitectureReadiness, "Confirmar arquitetura pronta" button) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.arquiteto-modelo-icone.test.tsx, describe "problema 1" — button absent without the Arquiteto active, the happy path calls the dedicated endpoint, failure shows an error toast, and the button disappears with the architecture already declared Origin: code investigation — the endpoint and the engine logic existed since Fase 4a/14d with NO UI path to them
documents.s: RN-145 — The Arquiteto also has a readiness button, and the SAME confirmation offers Infra and Dev Lead

documents.t: The model name only existed in token_usage, with no link to the specific agent.response event it produced — SessionPage.tsx showed the FIXED string "modelo" next to the agent's name, never the real name. The change crosses the three layers, all with the SAME field name (modelName), so no translation between them is needed: api — StreamLlmTurnUseCase/RunLlmTurnUseCase already resolved the model (resolveModelBinding → models.findById) to call the provider; the final frame/RunLlmTurnResult gain modelName: string | null. null only when the turn failed BEFORE resolving a model (no binding, or binding to a nonexistent model) — in the other cases, including budget exceeded, the binding had already resolved and the name travels even in the error frame. engine — the four conversational agents (criativo_server.ex, po_server.ex, arquiteto_server.ex, dev_lead_server.ex) extract Map.get(frame, "modelName") from the final frame and include it in the payload of emit_response/agent.response (%{content: content, modelName: model_name}). web — SessionPage.tsx reads event.payload.modelName. An event WRITTEN before this change does not have the key (undefined), and a turn whose api resolved no model writes null — both degrade to the generic label "modelo", never to undefined/null on screen; the same pattern that text === '' already uses for a response prior to RN-059. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/llm/stream-llm-turn.use-case.ts (LlmTurnStreamEvent), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/llm/run-llm-turn.use-case.ts (RunLlmTurnResult), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/dto/internal.response.dto.ts (LlmTurnResponseDto/LlmTurnStreamEventResponseDto), apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/{criativo,po,arquiteto,dev_lead}_server.ex (emit_response/3), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (the timeline's agent.response block) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/llm/run-llm-turn.use-case.spec.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/llm/stream-llm-turn.use-case.spec.ts (modelName on the happy path, on the provider error and without binding), apps/engine/test/engine/agents/{criativo,po,arquiteto,dev_lead}_server_test.exs (agent.response carries the model name; edge case of the frame without the key), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.arquiteto-modelo-icone.test.tsx, describe "problema 2" — real name, old event without the key, modelName: null Origin: code investigation — confirmed that the data already existed in token_usage, but never reached the event payload
documents.s: RN-146 — agent.response carries the name of the model that generated the response

documents.t: The Disclosure of timelineAgrupada (RN-138) received only the STRING of the name in titulo — each expanded message already has an avatar (.avatar + icon), and the collapsed header lost that visual cue precisely where it helps most to scan the thread. AvatarDoAgente reuses the SAME .avatar box as the expanded messages, but the chosen icon is the ROSTER's (AGENTS[id].icon) — the same source that already identifies "who is talking" in the streaming indicator (agenteExibido.icon, RN-131) — and not the per-event-TYPE icon each expanded entry uses (ModelIcon in agent.response, StackIcon in backlog.*_created, AlertCircleIcon in agent.error). A collapsed group can mix those entry types from the same agent; the header represents the AGENT, not its last entry, and only the roster icon is stable for that. Without id, or an agent outside the roster, it degrades to ModelIcon — never to an empty box. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (AvatarDoAgente, timelineAgrupada), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.module.css (.agentGroupTitulo) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.arquiteto-modelo-icone.test.tsx, describe "problema 3" — the collapsed header has the PATH of the PO's icon (UserIcon), not just a generic decorative SVG Origin: code investigation — Disclosure already accepted ReactNode in titulo; passing the avatar together with the name was what was missing
documents.s: RN-147 — The collapsed group header shows the agent's icon, not just the name

documents.t: The PO creates stories one by one, and each backlog.story_promotion_proposed (RN-126) became a standalone card in the timeline — in a batch of several stories, that stacked N identical cards competing for the same space, mixed with the rest of the narration. A batch is the set of promotion proposals STILL PENDING in the session, evaluated on each render — not "created in sequence without interruption". The criterion is the SAME one each standalone card already used on its own to decide whether it became an actionable card or a divider (no later backlog.story_transitioned/backlog.story_promotion_returned with the same storyId), only looked at at once for the whole session: 0 or 1 pending: nothing changes — the usual standalone card (the degradation is deliberate: a one-slide carousel gains nothing by becoming a carousel). 2+ pending at the same time: they become ONE Carousel (new in the design system, apps/web/src/components/ui/Carousel.tsx), inserted at the position of the FIRST proposal still pending; the others disappear as individual cards — each one becomes a SLIDE of it. Each slide shows the same sentence as the standalone card ("história … pronta, aguardando sua promoção"), a summary/RF if the payload carries one (today it does not — see below), and the Promover/Devolver buttons of that specific story, calling the SAME promoteStories/returnStory as always. "Aprovar todas" in the carousel header calls promoteStories with the ids of ALL pending ones in a single call — the endpoint was already a batch (promoteStories(projectId, storyIds[]), RN-048), so there was no contract change at all, only in who builds the list. A story resolved (promoted or returned) while the carousel is open leaves the batch on the next render (the events query is invalidated in both actions) — if only 1 pending is left, the carousel dissolves on its own and the card becomes standalone again. resumo/RF in the slide is a READY field, not used: CreateStoryUseCase today only writes storyId/epicId/title in the payload of backlog.story_promotion_proposed — no description nor functional requirements. The slide already knows how to display description/rf if the payload ever carries them (it degrades to the title alone until then); extending the payload was left out of this delivery, since it was not asked for. Where: apps/web/src/components/ui/Carousel.tsx (new component, generic navigation), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (promocoesPendentes, ehLevaDeHistorias, StorySlide, handlePromoteAll), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.module.css (.storySlide) Test: apps/web/src/components/ui/Carousel.test.tsx (navigation, ARIA, only the current slide mounted, index clamped when the list shrinks), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.carrossel-historias.test.tsx (3+ pending become a carousel; "Aprovar todas" sends the whole batch; single promotion and return keep working from a navigated slide; 1 pending degrades to the simple card; a resolved story leaves the batch and the carousel recomputes the count) Origin: user request — stories produced in batch by the PO were hard to decide one by one in the thread
documents.s: RN-148 — Stories with promotion pending at the same time become a carousel, not N cards

documents.t: create_c4_diagram (a new Arquiteto tool) generates the two Mermaid syntaxes of the C4 diagram (Context + Container, Simon Brown's model). The tool call carries only system_name/system_description/actors — the modules and the Container-level dependencies are NOT part of the input: the use case fetches the project's CURRENT module_map (ModuleMapRepository.findCurrent, the same read as GetArchitectureUseCase) and derives the Container level from it, with the SAME names and dependencies that create_module_map already validated without cycles. The obvious alternative — letting the model describe the modules again in the diagram's tool call, as it already does for create_module_map — was discarded on purpose: a second place where the model writes "the modules are X, Y, Z" is a second place where that list can diverge from the first, and the divergence would be SILENT — nothing would refuse a diagram with a module that no longer exists in the real map. Deriving from the repository closes that divergence by construction: the diagram can become OUTDATED if the module_map changes later (re-emitting is generating again, without a lock — see ADR 0068), but it never LIES about what existed at the moment it was generated. Without a current module_map, create_c4_diagram is refused with 400 — there is no Container level without modules to draw, and the error message instructs the Arquiteto to call create_module_map first (RN-061: the refusal comes back through the tool-result, with the whole reason). The artifact.c4_diagram artifact is versioned in the event log without a table of its own — the same design as artifact.project_image (ADR 0065): the current one is the one with the highest version, and revising is generating again, never overwriting. Where: apps/api/src/domain/architecture/c4-diagram.ts (gerarDiagramaContexto/gerarDiagramaContainer, pure), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/architecture/create-c4-diagram.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/architecture/get-c4-diagram.use-case.ts, apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/create_c4_diagram.ex, apps/web/src/components/C4DiagramView.tsx (rendering, three states — RN-088), apps/web/src/lib/mermaid-render.ts (mermaid stays isolated here, dynamic import()) Test: apps/api/test/domain/architecture/c4-diagram.spec.ts (valid Mermaid syntax from a sample module_map, dangling edge ignored, deduplicated ids), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/architecture/create-c4-diagram.use-case.spec.ts (without module_map it refuses with 400 and writes nothing; Container reflects the real modules/dependencies; versions on re-emitting), apps/engine/test/engine/harness/tools/create_c4_diagram_test.exs, apps/web/src/components/C4DiagramView.test.tsx (success becomes SVG, a syntax error becomes a readable Alert without breaking the screen, an empty diagram does not try to render) Origin: user request — the Arquiteto's C4 diagram in the project Overview (ADR 0068)
documents.s: RN-149 — The Container level of the C4 diagram is derived from the module_map, never retyped by the model

documents.t: Found in a PR review: search_workspace (dev agents and the two QA/gate agents, qa_tools.ex and qa_performance_seguranca_agent.ex — the latter only has read_file/search_workspace, without Terminal, on purpose) returned ALL search results, with no ceiling at all — the same class as finding S (Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor.truncate/2) and as the read_file fix (Engine.Harness.Tools.ReadFile.truncate/2): the result stays in the loop history and travels in every following turn, and a large tree is enough to blow the provider's {413, "request entity too large"}. Two independent ceilings, because the search overflows in two different ways: Hit count — a tree with thousands of files matching the term produces thousands of - caminho lines even if no individual file is large. Truncating only by BYTES at the end would still pay the cost of scanning and reading the content of each of those files before building the string. That is why the count ceiling (SEARCH_WORKSPACE_MAX_HITS, default 500) lives in WorkspaceFiles.search/3, which already STOPS consuming the search as soon as it finds enough hits — the pipeline runs over a Stream, and Enum.take(stream, max_hits + 1) only reads from the source what it needs to produce the first max_hits + 1 results. The "+1" is what allows saying there WERE more without continuing to scan the rest to count the exact total — counting the total would pay again the I/O the ceiling exists to avoid, so the marker says "showing the first N" and never invents a total. Bytes of the final text — even with limited hits, very long paths can produce a large string. Byte ceiling (SEARCH_WORKSPACE_MAX_BYTES, default 32,768), same pattern as terminal_output_max_bytes/read_file_max_bytes — its OWN variable, it does not reuse the other two: same class of overflow, diverging one should not require touching the others. The truncation marker is addressed to the MODEL, not to the human: it says what was cut (hits and/or bytes) and instructs to refine the search term — the same spirit as the TerminalExecutor/ReadFile markers. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/workspace_files.ex (search/3, take_capped/2), apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/search_workspace.ex (truncate/3, marca_de_truncagem/5), apps/engine/config/runtime.exs (search_workspace_max_hits, search_workspace_max_bytes) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/harness/workspace_files_test.exs (search/3 with max_hits cuts the COUNT and marks truncation only when there are more than the ceiling), apps/engine/test/engine/harness/search_workspace_test.exs (a search with few results is not altered; a search with more hits than the ceiling is truncated with a clear warning; a final text larger than the byte ceiling is also cut) Origin: PR review finding — the second real cause of the 413 in reviews, after the read_file fix
documents.s: RN-150 — search_workspace has a ceiling on hit COUNT and on BYTES, each with its own marker

documents.t: The number next to each project's name in Shell.tsx came from useProjectsUnread — latestSeq (the most recent seq already written in the session) minus the "last seen" cursor the browser keeps in read-state.ts. That counts ANY new event — tool.call, agent.response, chat — not only a pending decision. A test project showed "392" in the sidebar (accumulated activity from a real execution) while the Approvals tab of the SAME project showed "8" (the real count). A number that does not correspond to anything actionable when clicked is worse than none. The dashboard read model (ProjectsSummaryRepository.summarizeForWorkspace, RN-090) gained pendingApprovalsCount: COUNT(*) of proposed_actions with status = 'pending', aggregated by project_id in one more query in the existing Promise.all — same format as storiesAwaitingPromotion (RN-048), without growing the number of database round trips per project. The sum is over the WHOLE project, all sessions — deliberately different from the Approvals tab (ProjectApprovalsTab.tsx), which shows only the pending items of the MOST RECENT session: the badge is per PROJECT, not per session, and a pending item in an old session is still a pending item. Shell.tsx stopped importing useProjectsUnread — its only consumer there was this badge. Dashboard.tsx/ProjectCard.tsx gained the same wiring: the unreadCount prop of ProjectCard never had a caller (ProjectCardContainer did not pass it), and became pendingApprovalsCount with the same value as the sidebar — two screens, one number, one source. Where: apps/api/src/application/ports/projects-summary-repository.port.ts (ProjectCardSummary.pendingApprovalsCount), apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.ts (summarizeForWorkspace, aggregate query over proposed_actions), apps/web/src/routes/Shell.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/Dashboard.tsx, apps/web/src/components/ProjectCard.tsx Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/projects-summary.repository.spec.ts (pendingApprovalsCount soma o projeto INTEIRO..., only pending counts, does not leak between projects, the number of queries stays constant), apps/web/src/routes/Shell.test.tsx (pending approvals badge) Origin: user finding while navigating the app — sidebar badge showing "392" against a real "8" in the Approvals tab of the same project
documents.s: RN-151 — The project badge in the sidebar is pending approvals, not unread activity

documents.t: CodeBranchPicker already listed every branch of the repository, including those of the dev agents (feature/task-XXXXXXXX, Engine.Dev.AgentIo), but with no hint at all of who created it — only the raw name. ReadProjectCodeUseCase.branches solves this without an extra call to the git provider: the 8 chars after feature/task- are exactly the first hyphenated group of the task's uuid ("feature/task-" <> String.slice(to_string(row.task_id), 0, 8), not an arbitrary substring), so they match against TaskRepository .findByProjectAndIdPrefix (join by PROJECT, so an 8-char prefix never leaks a task from another project). The task's assignedTo is the agent_id (dev-<modulo>/dev-<modulo>-2, RN-087); the module is resolved by comparing against the project's CURRENT module_map with the SAME functions that generated them (devAgentId/extraDevAgentId in activate-execution.use-case.ts) — never by reverse regex, which would degenerate into ambiguity for a module name with a special character. producedBy: { agentId, moduleId } | null is honest degradation, the same way ahead/behind already are: null for a branch without the pattern (the user's manual one, or main/dev/qa), and also when the pattern matches but the task/module are no longer resolvable (task deleted, module removed from the current map) — never an invented value. In the dropdown, each branch produced by a dev gets the agent's icon and color (AGENTS/agents.ts, RN-087), reusing the SAME degradation that apps/web/src/lib/agent-status.ts already uses for the live roster: a module without a fixed key in AGENTS inherits the icon/color of dev-backend. Where: apps/api/src/application/use-cases/git/read-project-code.use-case.ts (branches/producedBy/moduloDoAgente), apps/api/src/application/ports/backlog-repository.port.ts (TaskRepository.findByProjectAndIdPrefix), apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/backlog.repository.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/git/dto/code.response.dto.ts (CodeBranchProducedByResponseDto), apps/web/src/lib/api-types.ts (CodeBranchProducedBy), apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeBranchPicker.tsx (IconeDoAgenteProdutor/defDoAgenteProdutor) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/git/read-project-code.use-case.spec.ts (describe "producedBy da branch de task" — task resolved with module and with the extra agent -2, a branch outside the pattern never gets producedBy even with a task of matchable prefix, prefix without a task in the project, module removed from the current map and task without an owner yet degrade to null), apps/web/src/routes/code/CodeBranchPicker.test.tsx (a task branch shows the owning dev agent's badge; a branch without the pattern gets no badge at all) Origin: user request — no visual hint of who created the branch in the rich dropdown of FASE 26b
documents.s: RN-152 — A task's branch says which dev agent and module it belongs to, in the Code tab dropdown

documents.t: Revised by RN-603 (ADR 0167): decide() started receiving also the ORIGIN of the autonomy, and auto mode (the wildcard in auto_approve) no longer goes through the path scope ceiling. What follows below about decide() "not changing" describes the original design. Before this RN, agent_autonomy only knew how to grant autonomy per (projeto, agente, TIPO de ação) — one row per type, upsert of ONE rule at a time (SetAgentAutonomyUseCase, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/set-agent-autonomy.use-case.ts). Trusting an agent broadly required one row per type — terminal, write_file, pr_open… — and a new type was born without a rule, back to require_approval. "Auto mode" is the special value actionType: "*" in the SAME table and the SAME endpoint (PUT /projects/:projectId/agent-autonomy) — it is not a new mechanism, it is the existing column (agent_autonomy.action_type, free text, no enum nor FK — apps/api/src/db/schema/agents.ts) accepting one more value. The wildcard means "autonomy for any action type of THIS agent" and is resolved in DrizzleAgentAutonomyRepository.findMode (apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/agent-autonomy.repository.ts): it fetches the SPECIFIC rule and the wildcard in the same query, and the specific one always wins — writing terminal: deny with "*": auto_approve already on keeps denying terminal for that agent, and releasing the rest. decide() (apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts) does not change: it receives the PermissionPolicy already resolved in ctx.autonomyMode, exactly as before the wildcard existed — that is why the absolute ceilings hold without needing to know that "auto mode" exists (see RN-154). The ApprovalCard (apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.tsx) gains the "Modo automático" button next to "Sempre permitir", visible only when: (a) the action is pending, (b) whoever proposed it is an AGENT (actor.kind === 'agent' — there is no agent autonomy to grant to a user) and (c) the caller (ProjectApprovalsTab.tsx/SessionPage.tsx) has already confirmed the maintainer/owner role in the workspace — the same requirement as the endpoint (@RequireRole('maintainer'), unchanged). The onActivateAutoMode prop is undefined for whoever lacks the role — the card HIDES the button instead of showing it disabled, and the check lives in the caller, not in the card (a presentational component, with no query of its own). Turning it off reuses the manual/auto toggle the agent card already had (Fase 8d) — no new screen. AgentTeamGrid.tsx starts looking for the agent's wildcard rule BEFORE the representative one (autonomyActionTypeFor): if it exists, the card's toggle reflects and edits the WILDCARD, no longer the representative type — turning off is writing the same wildcard as require_approval, and the toggle on the agent card is exactly that "turn off". Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts (AGENT_AUTONOMY_ALL_ACTIONS, AgentAutonomyActionType), apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/agent-autonomy.repository.ts (findMode with precedence specific > wildcard), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/actions/dto/set-agent-autonomy.dto.ts (accepts "*"), apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.tsx ("Modo automático" button), apps/web/src/components/AgentTeamGrid.tsx (the toggle starts prioritizing the wildcard), apps/web/src/routes/ProjectApprovalsTab.tsx and apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (handleActivateAutoMode, role gate via useCurrentWorkspaceWithRole) Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/agent-autonomy.repository.spec.ts (precedence specific > wildcard; the wildcard is per agent; turning off is rewriting the wildcard as require_approval), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/propose-action.use-case.spec.ts (auto mode auto-approves a common action WITHOUT hitting permissions.json; a specific rule in deny beats the wildcard), apps/api/test/interfaces/http/actions/agent-autonomy.controller.spec.ts (PUT/GET still require maintainer; the DTO accepts "*" and refuses a string outside the list), apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.test.tsx (button disappears without onActivateAutoMode; click calls the callback; the note explains the ceilings that keep asking for a decision) Origin: user request — "Sempre permitir" only writes a specific command pattern, and agent_autonomy only covered one action type at a time; what was missing was trusting an agent broadly with a single click
documents.s: RN-153 — "Auto mode": the ApprovalCard turns on autonomy for ANY future action of an agent

documents.t: Revised by RN-603 (ADR 0167): the ceilings listed here remain in force in auto mode; what stopped holding for it was the PATH SCOPE ceiling (ADR 0055), which was never on this list. The design of "auto mode" (RN-153) is deliberately incapable of piercing the three ceilings that already existed in decide() — they are applied LAST, over current.policy, without looking at where the permissiveness came from (agent_autonomy with a specific type, wildcard, or permissions.json — the function never knew how to distinguish the origins, and still does not): Merge into a protected branch (git_merge with target in dev/qa/rc/main, RN-006) — the merge lock (isProtectedBranch) downgrades auto_approve to require_approval always, even with "*": auto_approve on for the agent. instruction_patch (RN-007) — changing another agent's instruction requires the human to see the diff; auto mode does not change that. parallelize/raise_max_parallel (RN-086) — raising the parallelism ceiling, or asking for more agents above it, remains the user's decision; an agent with auto mode on cannot self-grant more spending power. The proof is by CONSTRUCTION, not case by case: since the three ceilings check only current.policy === 'auto_approve' — never the origin —, and "auto mode" can only reach current.policy === 'auto_approve' through the SAME path that a specific agent_autonomy rule already used (ctx.autonomyMode), the ceilings that already contained agent_autonomy keep containing the wildcard without needing new code. The real risk was not the ceiling — it was someone, when generalizing agent_autonomy to accept "*", inserting the wildcard check BEFORE the ceilings and reopening the door; that is why AGENT_AUTONOMY_ALL_ACTIONS was resolved entirely in the REPOSITORY (before decide() runs), and decide() itself gained no new line — only enough to have no place where the wildcard could pierce. Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts (the three ceiling blocks, lines ~207–258, unchanged by this feature) Test: apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/propose-action.use-case.spec.ts ("auto mode NÃO auto-aprova merge em branch protegida", "... instruction_patch", "... parallelize/raise_max_parallel" — all three with agent_autonomy "*" written as auto_approve and the verdict remaining require_approval) Origin: design constraint confirmed by the user when asking for "auto mode" — the three ceilings are the guarantee that cannot regress
documents.s: RN-154 — The three absolute ceilings keep blocking EVEN with "auto mode" on

documents.t: Product owner decision on 2026-09-26 (AT-226, ADR 0167): with "Modo automático" on for an agent — the "*" wildcard of RN-153 resolved as auto_approve —, the agent runs ANY terminal command without asking for approval, INCLUDING outside the project folder. The path scope ceiling of ADR 0055 stops holding for that agent. Measured on exp001 (mounted mode, container up): 51 commands asked for approval with the mode on, 47 only for citing /work or /tmp — the dev agent runs in the container and the scope compares against the HOST root. decide() starts receiving the ORIGIN of the autonomy (ctx.autonomyOrigin: 'especifica' or 'curinga'), resolved by the SAME repository that already resolved the precedence — findMode became a read of resolve, not a second rule. Only the wildcard in auto_approve is auto mode (modoAutomaticoDoAgente); an absent origin counts as specific. In auto mode, two prompts cease to exist: the SCOPE ceiling and the require_approval that the COMPOUND command synthesizes when a segment has no rule at all in permissions.json (the file with no opinion, which never downgrades an earlier stage) — without the second, cd /work && npm test would keep asking. Everything remains as it was, in auto mode too: deny (from the file, from the built-in patterns or from specific autonomy) wins; an ask WRITTEN in the file asks; the external-effect/privileged-command ceiling (push, PR, deploy, sudo/doas, RN-418) runs first and does not look at the origin; merge into a protected branch, instruction_patch, parallelize/raise_max_parallel and container_remove are never auto-approvable (RN-154). A specific rule for the type beats the wildcard in the repository and arrives as 'especifica': terminal: require_approval with the wildcard on keeps asking. Turning off (the agent card's toggle writes the wildcard as require_approval) restores the ceiling. Since RN-670 (ADR 0189) the specific auto_approve under the auto_approve wildcard — what a dev agent's "Sempre permitir" writes — resolves as the WILDCARD, and no longer turns off auto mode; and, outside it, the scope compares against the REAL execution folder (RN-669). The screen says, before the click, what the mode releases and what keeps asking: the ApprovalCard note appears in BOTH variants (chat and Approvals queue), and the agent card shows a sentence under the toggle — only when the WILDCARD is on, because the toggle over the representative type writes a specific rule, which does not release the scope. Where: apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts:295 (modoAutomaticoDoAgente), apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts:370 (the synthesized verdict of the compound ignored), apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts:455 (the scope ceiling skipped), apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/agent-autonomy.repository.ts:25 (resolve, with the origin), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/actions/propose-action.use-case.ts:216 (autonomyOrigin), apps/web/src/components/AgentTeamGrid.tsx:108 (autonomyHint), apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.tsx:313 (the note in both variants) Test: apps/api/test/domain/actions/decide.spec.ts ("modo automático libera o escopo de caminho (RN-603)": out of scope and compound auto-approve; push/sudo/deny/written ask remain; a specific rule and a wildcard turned off do not release; the other ceilings do not change), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/actions/propose-action.use-case.spec.ts (end to end with the real repository), apps/api/test/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/agent-autonomy.repository.spec.ts (resolve returns the origin), apps/web/src/components/AgentTeamGrid.test.tsx, apps/web/src/components/AgentCard.test.tsx, apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.test.tsx Origin: product owner decision (AT-226) after the test on exp001
documents.s: RN-603 — Auto mode releases the path scope, and only it

documents.t: The timeline of SessionPage.tsx orders events and proposed actions by a single comparable numeric axis. For events, it is event.seq (gapless, per session). For actions, it is the seq of the correlated proposed_action.created event (found by payload.actionId === action.id, written by ProposeActionUseCase in the SAME transaction that creates the action) — never action.seq, which is a unique and global bigserial of the whole proposed_actions table, shared by all sessions and projects of the system, and therefore incomparable with event.seq (a deliberate contrast, see apps/api/src/db/schema/actions.ts). Comparing the two directly produced an unpredictable order every time an ApprovalCard entered the mix with normal events. Actions without that link (only the Gitflow bootstrap — git_repo_create/git_branch_create, which only write outbox) degrade to a position interpolated by createdAt, anchored on the last previous event. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (ordemDaAcaoNaTimeline) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.ordenacao-e-avisos.test.tsx Origin: finding from PR #286 — approval cards appeared out of order in the timeline, mixed with normal events
documents.s: RN-155 — timeline ordering uses the proposed_action.created link, never the raw action.seq

documents.t: The indicator that appears after 5s without a response (pensandoVisivel) shows the fixed sentence "Reunindo informações...", without the agent's name interpolated — it replaces the previous text "{Agente} está escrevendo…". The agent's name is already visible in the header as soon as the real text streaming starts; repeating it in the wait indicator did not help reading. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.pista-e-status.test.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.ordenacao-e-avisos.test.tsx Origin: finding from PR #286 — the previous text named an agent that was already visible in the header
documents.s: RN-156 — the 5s wait indicator has fixed text, without interpolating the agent

documents.t: The backlog.epic_created/backlog.story_created events no longer render as a full message bubble (.message/.bubble, 32px avatar — the same visual weight as a real agent response) and start using the same compact notice format that .handoffDivider/.handoffPill already uses for the baton pass: a centered line with a horizontal rule and a compact pill, keeping the "Ver no Backlog" link. agentId remains populated in the TimelineEntry — unlike the handoff divider, this does not mark a transition between agents, it is an action by the PO within their own turn, and it remains eligible for per-agent collapsing (RN-138). Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.handoff-inline-e-links.test.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.ordenacao-e-avisos.test.tsx Origin: finding from PR #286 — the full bubble had visual weight equal to a real agent response, for a metadata action by the PO
