documents.t: agent.response in the Session thread renders a subset of Markdown (bold **texto**, italic *texto*/_texto_, inline code `texto`, heading #/##/###, list -/1., link [texto](url) and code fence ```linguagem), via its own regex parser (apps/web/src/lib/markdown.ts), with no new dependency. chat.message (text typed by the user) stays literal — Markdown only applies to the OUTPUT of an agent/LLM, never to human input. Security: the parser never produces HTML — it returns a data tree that MarkdownMessage.tsx converts into React elements directly (never dangerouslySetInnerHTML). A link only becomes a clickable <a href> when the URL scheme is http, https or relative (/..., #...); any other scheme (javascript:, data:, etc.) degrades to the link text, never to an executable href. Code inside a fence gets per-token highlighting, reusing highlightLine/highlightFile from apps/web/src/routes/code/highlight.ts — the same function that already colors the Code tab. sh/bash gained their own shell keyword vocabulary (before, they only had the # line comment mapped and fell into the JS fallback). Fences ```sh/```bash get the visual aesthetics of a terminal ($ prompt per command line), consistent with the $ comando that ApprovalCard already uses for the terminal action. Where: apps/web/src/lib/markdown.ts, apps/web/src/components/ui/MarkdownMessage.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/code/highlight.ts Test: apps/web/src/lib/markdown.test.ts, apps/web/src/components/ui/MarkdownMessage.test.tsx, apps/web/src/routes/code/highlight.test.ts, apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.markdown-resposta.test.tsx Origin: PR #288 — agent responses with lists, code and links arrived as raw text in the thread, with no structure at all
documents.s: RN-158 — Light Markdown with highlighting in the chat

documents.t: The Session's "Artefatos gerados" panel (ContextAside in SessionPage.tsx) lists dev PRs (pr_open), the Arquiteto's ADR PRs (open_adr_pr) and epics/stories created by the PO (backlog.epic_created/backlog.story_created), grouped by agentId — who generated each artifact — with the same collapsible Disclosure pattern of RN-138 (agent name + count, expandable to the title of each artifact). Each artifact navigates to the place where it lives: a PR (dev or ADR) opens the real URL (executionResult.pullRequestUrl, the same field that ProjectOverviewTab.tsx already reads for an ADR PR); epic/story navigates to /projects/:projectId?tab=backlog (the same Link pattern already used in the PO's compact notices in the main thread, RN-124/ RN-157). A PR still without pullRequestUrl (pending execution) appears in the panel without becoming a clickable link. Out of scope, by a decision recorded in a code comment (ContextAside in SessionPage.tsx): module_map/C4 — they are the project's CURRENT state (one current version, overwritten on each generation), not an artifact dated per SESSION like PR/epic/story; the Overview tab (ProjectOverviewTab.tsx) is already their place today, without an anchor of their own — addressing that is out of the scope of this delivery. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (ContextAside) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.artefatos-gerados.test.tsx Origin: PR #288 — the panel did not distinguish who generated each artifact nor covered ADR PRs and epics/stories, only dev PRs
documents.s: RN-159 — Generated Artifacts grouped by agent

documents.t: The "Confirmar arquitetura pronta" button (Arquiteto→Dev Lead handoff, via confirmArchitectureReadiness) is born disabled until the project's backlog has at least 1 story with a status other than draft — that is, already promoted by PromoteStoriesUseCase/TransitionStoryUseCase (RN-048), having a captured business rule not being enough. in_progress/done also count, because one only gets there having gone through ready. The source is the SAME the Backlog tab already uses (useBacklog, ProjectBacklogTab.tsx, the same queryKey ['backlog', projectId]) — no new round trip. While there is no promoted story, the button shows the hint in title explaining the reason. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (hasPromotedStory, button render) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.readiness-arquitetura-exige-historia.test.tsx Origin: user request — the Arquiteto→Dev Lead handoff button had no gate at all It only held on the CLIENT: a direct HTTP call ignored the rule. Closed by RN-404 (ADR 0094), which revalidates on the backend.
documents.s: RN-160 — "Confirmar arquitetura pronta" requires at least 1 promoted story

documents.t: Revised by RN-677 (ADR 0194, owner's decision on 10/01): accepting the handoff to the Dev Lead stopped chaining the activation of execution, for EVERY role — the acceptance only brings it to PLAN, and what activates is the APPROVAL of its plan (propose_execution_plan). The text below describes the fusion as it was. handleAcceptHandoff (SessionPage.tsx) chains activateExecution automatically when toAgent === 'dev-lead' AND the EFFECTIVE role of whoever accepts — read from the same useCurrentWorkspaceWithRole() that already authorizes "Auto mode" (RN-153) and the Approvals/Settings screens — is owner or maintainer. For developer (or a role not yet resolved), the current flow remains untouched: accepting activates nothing, and "Ativar execução" remains as a second button. The check is client-only — POST .../execution/activate still requires maintainer on the backend (RN-137); the fusion only avoids a redundant click for whoever already had both roles. It reuses the SAME handleActivateExecution that the "Ativar execução" button already calls, which handles its own error (toast + mensagemDaApi) and never rethrows — it avoids a late activation error being reported as "não foi possível aceitar o handoff". Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (podeFundirHandoffComExecucao, handleAcceptHandoff) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.handoff-devlead-e-colapso.test.tsx, describe "problema 4" Architectural decision: ADR 0069 Origin: user request (approved design)
documents.s: RN-161 — Accepting the handoff to the Dev Lead chains execution activation when the effective role already authorizes it

documents.t: The Criativo can, when it asks SEVERAL questions in the same response, emit the list in a STRUCTURED format instead of letting the user answer item by item in free text — a new tool ask_structured_questions (apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/ask_structured_questions.ex, :direct), registered next to emit_artifact. Schema: { questions: [{ id, label, type?, options? }] } — id unique and non-empty, label non-empty, type ∈ text|textarea|select (default text), options mandatory and non-empty when type: select. It writes chat.structured_question. The frontend (StructuredQuestionCard, SessionPage.tsx) renders a form with one field per question — Input/Textarea/Select from the design system, according to type. POST .../agents/:agent/structured- question/:questionSetId/answer (AnswerStructuredQuestionUseCase) validates that every question has a non-empty answer, writes chat.structured_question_answered (referencing questionSetId = the id of the question event) and REUSES SendAgentMessageUseCase — the answers become a concatenated message ("1. {label}: {resposta}\n2. ..."), as if the user had typed in the thread; there is no new "the agent reads the structured answer" channel. A set of questions can only be answered ONCE: resubmission is refused with 409, and the form does not even reappear — the card becomes read-only as soon as there is a later chat.structured_question_answered with the same questionSetId. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/ask_structured_questions.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/criativo_server.ex, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/agents/answer-structured-question.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/agents/agents.controller.ts, apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (StructuredQuestionCard) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/harness/tools/ask_structured_questions_test.exs, apps/engine/test/engine/agents/criativo_server_test.exs, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/agents/answer-structured-question.use-case.spec.ts, apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.perguntas-estruturadas.test.tsx Origin: user request — no precedent of structured input in the chat
documents.s: RN-162 — The Criativo's structured questions

documents.t: Each Criativo turn runs a bounded tool-use loop, with a ceiling of 12 trips to the model — the same design the PO and the Arquiteto already had. Before, the model was called ONCE per turn: the tool result was appended to the in-memory history and nobody read it again, so the sentence "vou corrigir e tentar de novo" — literal in the code — was only fulfilled if the user sent another message. For whoever used it, the Criativo simply stopped answering after saying it was going to fix it. Four consequences, and each one is a rule: A tool error is input, not the end of the line. The reason goes back to the model as a tool message and the loop calls the model again, which re-emits it corrected WITHIN the same turn. Nothing is announced that the code will not execute. The retry sentence is decided after dispatching the tools and knowing how many rounds are left: with a round available, the agent says it will fix it; without a round, it does not promise. The tool failure became a durable agent.error, with origin (RN-059) — it was an agent.response, indistinguishable in the event log from a normal response. origem: infra when the api refused the append_event; origem: modelo for the payload the model wrote (wrong key, origin that is not a list, duplicated rule, system-emitted type). The payload carries tool and retentativa. An exhausted ceiling does not end in silence. It becomes an agent.error with reason: "limite_de_iteracoes" and origem: modelo, the same reading as the ToolLoop's toolloop.limit_reached. The event name is NOT reused: this agent does not run inside the ToolLoop, and the event would lie about who produced it. Two boundaries of the loop, both deliberate: a successful ask_structured_questions ends the turn (the ball is with the user, and the answers come back in a future turn — RN-162); and a turn that had a failure in some round closes with a CONSOLIDATED outcome in the thread, so the last word is not the error of a round that was already corrected later. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/criativo_server.ex (run_turn_capturing/3, continuar/4, emit_falha_de_ferramenta/4, emit_falha_limite/2) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/criativo_server_test.exs (a loop that really corrects, an exhausted ceiling narrated, origin infra vs modelo, a structured question that ends the turn) Origin: real use in the exp001 project — "o Criativo não respondeu depois de dizer que iria corrigir e tentar de novo"
documents.s: RN-163 — The Criativo keeps the promise to try again

documents.t: REVISED by RN-421 (ADR 0104): workspace_mode/local became an execution_mode of THREE values (container/mounted/runner, migration 0048) — the rest of this entry is history, faithful to what held until the revision. A project is born with a workspace mode (projects.workspace_mode, migration 0043), and it is what decides where the scope root is derived from: container (DEFAULT, and the behavior that always existed): the folder MANAGED by the product, join(PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT, workspace_dir_name) (RN-109); local: a folder OF THE USER, at the absolute path of projects.workspace_path. The pair is tied by a CHECK in the database ((workspace_mode = 'local') = (workspace_path IS NOT NULL)), and not only by the use case: the column is read by TWO processes (api and engine) and written by seed/backfill scripts that do not go through it. local without a path would be a terminal scope pointing nowhere; container with a path would be a second source of truth waiting to diverge from the first. The derivation remains unique — projectScopeRoot started receiving the location ({workspaceDirName, workspaceMode, workspacePath}) and picks the branch; none of the four consumers (RN-092) gained validation of its own. The engine resolves the same locator in the QUERY (folder name in container, absolute path in local) and distinguishes the two by the leading slash, which is unambiguous because the folder name is validated against ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$. Two explicit consequences of the local mode: The Arquiteto's image gate (RN-105) does NOT apply. REVOKED by RN-494 (ADR 0135): the exemption ended — the three modes now require the image decision before opening the Code tab. The rest of this item is history. A Local project does not start a container, so the Code tab unlocked without waiting for a decision that was never going to happen. The exemption lived in the same funnel as the gate in the api, and the screen agreed: ProjectCodeTab did not even ask for the container state (RN-107) when the project was Local — if only the api exempted it, the tab would remain blocked on screen by a nonexistent decision. The permissions.json lives in the user's folder, together with the code — because the policy has to be read from the SAME root that the terminal scope authorizes. workspace_mode is not to be confused with the GitProviderName 'local': one says where the CODE lives on disk, the other where the git REPOSITORY lives, and the two choices are orthogonal. Where: apps/api/src/db/schema/iam.ts (projects), apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts (projectScopeRoot), apps/api/src/domain/iam/project.entity.ts, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/git/read-project-code.use-case.ts (portaoDoContainer), apps/web/src/routes/ProjectCodeTab.tsx, apps/engine/lib/engine/projects/project.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine/actions/workspace.ex (workspace_dir/2), apps/engine/lib/engine/dev/worktree_cleanup.ex (which was the second hand-written derivation, and started using the single one), apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.tsx Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.spec.ts (describe "projectScopeRoot no modo local"), apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/fs-permissions-file-store.spec.ts (the permissions.json in the user's folder), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/create-project-modo-de-workspace.spec.ts, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/git/read-project-code.use-case.spec.ts (a Local project does not go through the gate), apps/api/test/interfaces/http/iam/project-dto-modo-de-workspace.spec.ts (the mode is frozen: PATCH does not change it), apps/web/src/routes/ProjectCodeTab.test.tsx (the screen also exempts the gate), apps/engine/test/engine/actions/workspace_test.exs (describe "workspace_dir/2 com o localizador já resolvido"), apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.test.tsx Architectural decision: ADR 0072 Origin: user request (their decision, with the free-path variant explicitly chosen)
documents.s: RN-169 — The project chooses where the code lives: Local or Container

documents.t: REVISED by RN-422 (ADR 0104): creation validation started to DIVERGE by mode — mounted (the renamed local) keeps touching the disk as described here, runner validates only the LEXICON, without I/O — the rest of this entry is history, faithful to what held until the revision. Creating a project in local mode with a path the api cannot reach produces a project that hangs later — on the first tool of the first agent, far from the screen where the decision was made. That is why creation refuses with 400, and the message says what needs to be done. The path must be: absolute, with no .. or . in any segment (the stored path is the path that is read; /srv/app/../../etc is /etc and does not look like it); existing and a folder inside the api container; writable by the process (access(W_OK|X_OK)) — the images run non-root (ADR 0024), and a host folder with another owner arrives mounted as read-only in practice; outside the root and the system folders (/, /etc, /usr, /var, /data… and everything below them): the project root is the scope that AUTHORIZES the agent's terminal (ADR 0055), and a project rooted at /etc turns "the agent writes in its project" into "the agent rewrites the container"; with no overlap with the Brabo checkout, in BOTH directions — the folder that CONTAINS the monorepo and the folder INSIDE it. The second case is the problem that ADR 0055 reports actually happening. The stored path is the normalized one, not the raw string: validating one string and storing another is how validation stops holding the next day. A workspacePath sent together with workspace_mode: container is REFUSED, not ignored — a field silently discarded becomes "but I configured it". The LEXICAL part (items 1, 4 and 5) runs also on read, on each derivation of projectScopeRoot: the only way to bypass creation is to write directly into the database, and what is gained there is a terminal scope at /. The DISK part (items 2 and 3) runs only at creation, where the user can still fix it. The refusal for a missing folder brings the mount instruction — the file, the two services and the line (- <caminho>:<caminho>), with the pointer to the runbook. Mounting only in the api produces a project the api accepts and the engine does not see: it validates what it sees, and has no way of knowing what is mounted in the other container. Where: apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts (validarCaminhoDeWorkspaceLocal, CaminhoLocalInvalidoError), apps/api/src/application/use-cases/iam/create-project.use-case.ts (caminhoValidado), apps/api/src/interfaces/http/iam/dto/create-project.dto.ts, apps/web/src/lib/wizard.ts (caminhoLocalParecePlausivel) Test: apps/api/test/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.spec.ts (describe "validarCaminhoDeWorkspaceLocal"), apps/api/test/application/use-cases/iam/create-project-modo-de-workspace.spec.ts (describe "a criação RECUSA o caminho que travaria depois"), apps/web/src/lib/wizard.test.ts, apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.test.tsx Architectural decision: ADR 0072 Origin: a guard required by the free-path variant (ADR 0072)
documents.s: RN-170 — A Local path is validated at CREATION, and the refusal teaches

documents.t: The PO gained two READ tools — listar_regras_de_negocio and listar_backlog (:direct, with no parameter at all) — served by two internal routes scoped to the project: GET /internal/projects/:projectId/business-rules and GET /internal/projects/:projectId/backlog. The first returns every artifact.business_rule of the project's sessions with the whole description, which stories already cite each rule and the uncoveredCount; the second returns the SAME epic → story → task tree as the Backlog tab, through the same ListBacklogUseCase (three reads per project, never N+1). The text returned to the model puts the UNCOVERED rules first and the ORPHAN epics before the tree — that is what generates work. What the rule fixes: until now the PO had four tools, all of them write tools. Its context was built once, at kickoff, from the 200 last events of the session — from then on it did not know which rules existed, which it had already covered, nor what it had already created. The scope is the project and not the session on purpose: a rule captured in a previous session is exactly what the per-session read hid. Reading does not become a proposed_action (it is not an external effect), but it is CONTAINED in the sense of ADR 0060: neither of the two routes accepts a parameter beyond the project id — no search, no pagination, no filter —, the cost per call is constant, and the text delivered to the model has a line ceiling stating the real total when it truncates. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/listar_regras_de_negocio.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/listar_backlog.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/po_server.ex, apps/engine/lib/engine/sessions/engine_api_client.ex, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/backlog/list-business-rules.use-case.ts, apps/api/src/interfaces/http/internal/internal-projects.controller.ts Test: apps/engine/test/engine/harness/tools/listar_regras_de_negocio_test.exs, apps/engine/test/engine/harness/tools/listar_backlog_test.exs, apps/engine/test/engine/agents/po_server_test.exs, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/backlog/list-business-rules.use-case.spec.ts Origin: real use in the exp001 project — "crie ferramenta para o PO conseguir listar as regras de negócio"
documents.s: RN-164 — The PO READS what already exists, scoped to the project

documents.t: When the PO ends a turn having created an epic and no story for it, that becomes an EXPLICIT outcome: a durable event backlog.epic_without_story (with origem: "modelo", the ids and titles of the epics and the message) plus the agent.error broadcast — the pattern of RN-059: the log is what survives, the broadcast is the agent saying it in the thread. The call-out is per OCCURRENCE: once reported, the pending list is emptied, and it does not become an alarm that repeats on every turn. What counts is the creation that succeeded: a create_story refused by the api (nonexistent business_rule_id, for example) does not settle the epic. Treating it as if it did would be trading one silence for another. The pending epics live in the PoServer state and are NOT rehydrated: the call-out is about the obligation assumed in the turn, and rebuilding it from the event log would reopen an old epic the user has already resolved some other way. Along with it came the two pieces that were missing for the PO to have a way out other than stopping: ask_structured_questions — the SAME tool as the Criativo's (RN-162), just advertised in po_server — and the kickoff instruction saying, in so many words, that an epic without a story blocks execution and that when information is missing, one ASKS, never stops nor invents. The previous instruction did not say a word about what to do in the face of a gap, and in the face of a gap without instruction a model chooses between inventing and stopping. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/po_server.ex (anotar_obrigacao/4, encerrar_turno/1, obrigacoes/0), apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/create_epic.ex (id_no_resultado/1), apps/web/src/lib/activity.ts Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/po_server_test.exs (describe "RN-165"), apps/web/src/lib/activity.test.ts Origin: real use in the exp001 project — a backlog without stories, hence without tasks, hence execution stuck without a visible error
documents.s: RN-165 — An epic without a story is called out, and the PO asks when it does not know

documents.t: Once the iteration ceiling of the PoServer tool loop (12) is exhausted, the turn emits toolloop.limit_reached with {iteration, max_iterations} — the SAME type and the same payload that Engine.Harness.ToolLoop already emitted since Fase 3. Before, the clause returned the state and that was it: from outside, an exhausted loop was indistinguishable from a turn that simply ended. Reusing the identifier instead of creating a po.* is deliberate: it is the same fact (the loop hit the ceiling), and whoever reads the event log should not need to learn a second name because the conversational agent has its own loop instead of using the ToolLoop. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/agents/po_server.ex (run_turn/2, clause remaining <= 0) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/agents/po_server_test.exs ("teto de iterações emite toolloop.limit_reached") Origin: investigation of the exp001 hang — the loop ended silently
documents.s: RN-166 — The PO's iteration ceiling leaves a trace

documents.t: In the session thread, the offered handoff and the approval card appear AFTER the last utterance of the turn in which they were born — never in the middle of it. This does not fix ordering: RN-155 remains fully in force, and the timeline stays ordered by the event log's seq. What the log records is the truth: po_server.ex (run_turn/2) emits, in the SAME iteration, the turn's agent.response, THEN the tool.call of offer_handoff (which writes handoff.offered) and ONLY THEN recurses to the closing agent.response. The handoff's seq is honestly lower than the last utterance's. The same holds for proposed_action.created, which is born in the middle of the turn while the agent still has something to say. Showing "passed the baton" or "approve this" in the middle of the conversation is a wrong reading of correct data — so the rule is about PRESENTATION, applied in a separate and explicit pass (afundarDesfechos), after the sort by seq, and not hidden in a three-term comparator. Different turns never mix. An outcome sinks to the end of the stretch right below it and stops at the first entry that fails any of the three conditions: same turn — the turn is the seq of the last OPENING before the entry, and an opening is an event with actor user (chat.message, agent.activated, story promotion/return). It protects the case in which the boundary between two turns has no VISIBLE entry at all: agent.activated opens a turn and does not become a thread item. same author — in an EXECUTION session several agents write without the user speaking a single time, and all of them stay in the same turn; one's outcome cannot cross another's utterance. is not an outcome — two consecutive outcomes preserve the order between them (the Infra's handoff.offered before the Dev Lead's, in the same confirmation). The system actor does NOT open a turn: it is infrastructure noise in the middle of the thread, not a decision of whoever is conversing. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (aberturasDeTurno, turnoDoSeq, afundarDesfechos, and the autor/turno/desfecho fields of TimelineEntry) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.ordenacao-e-avisos.test.tsx (describes "RN-172 — turno e desfecho (unidade)" and "RN-172 — a sequência REAL do engine, renderizada") Origin: real use on exp001 — "a passagem de bastão do PO para o arquiteto está aparecendo acima da última mensagem do PO" and "a mensagem de aprovação apareceu acima do chat do arquiteto até ele finalizar a resposta"
documents.s: RN-172 — Handoff and approval are the OUTCOME of the turn

documents.t: The chat scrolls to the end when the content grows — and not only when a new event arrives. The two timeline sources are SEPARATE queries (events and actions), and the height still changes without either of them: opening/closing a Disclosure (per-agent collapse of RN-138, the approval card's "Detalhes"), Markdown reflowing, a diagram rendering later. That is why there are two mechanisms: the effect's dependencies cover what React knows (events.length, actions.length, streamingText), and a ResizeObserver over the thread's CONTENT covers what only the layout knows. The guard remains unchanged and deliberate: it only scrolls whoever is already less than 120px from the end. Whoever scrolled up to reread the history is not dragged — the thread follows the conversation, it does not hijack the reading. In the same thread, the approval card no longer takes up the whole 780px of the column: it gets a ceiling of 560px and is centered, as .handoffCard/.handoffDivider already are. Indenting 45px like the bubbles would be wrong — the card is nobody's utterance, it is a decision asked of the user. The Approvals tab queue does not change: there the card MUST fill the grid column. Since AT-322 the card is ONE single card on every surface and fills the container — what applies the ceiling and the centering in the thread is its container (.acaoNoFio), no longer a variant of the card. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (acompanharOFim and the two effects that call it); apps/web/src/components/ApprovalCard.module.css (.card) and apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.module.css (.acaoNoFio) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.ordenacao-e-avisos.test.tsx (describe "RN-173 — o fio acompanha o que cresce", with the case of the user having scrolled up) Origin: real use on exp001 — "o scroll do chat deve ficar sempre no final seguindo o chat" and "aprovação mal diagramado deve ficar ao centro"
documents.s: RN-173 — The thread follows everything that grows, and only for whoever was already at the end

documents.t: A type: "select" question of ask_structured_questions (RN-162) accepts an answer outside the list. The field is allowOther, and the default is true: whoever declares nothing offers the way out. Closing the list requires an explicit allowOther: false, and only makes sense when it is genuinely closed ("Sim"/"Não"). The open default is not a style preference. A list closed by the model's OVERSIGHT locks the whole conversation and the user has no way to unlock it from outside — that is exactly what real use found: the model offered an option of the kind "Escreva você mesmo" and the form had nowhere to write, because the tool schema did not know how to express "besides these, whatever you want". A list opened by mistake, in the worst case, offers one field too many. The two errors do not cost the same. For the same reason the tool description forbids creating an "Outro" option inside options: the form already offers it by itself, and two escape hatches in the same list confuse. allowOther only exists in select — in text/textarea the field is already free text, and the engine normalizes these two to false instead of writing a meaningless state in the event log. On screen, choosing "Outra (escrever)" swaps the Select for an Input: the interface sentinel (__outra__) never travels to the backend, and what goes is the typed TEXT. The submit button keeps requiring ALL questions filled — AnswerStructuredQuestion UseCase refuses with 400 listing what is missing, so enabling it with an empty field would only produce a server error —, and being on "Outra" with the text still blank does NOT count as filled. The card also stopped being the only item in the thread aligned to nothing: it is now centered with the same 560px ceiling as the ApprovalCard in the chat variant (RN-173) and gets the agent's avatar and color, which is what makes it read as SOMEONE's utterance instead of an orphan form. Before, it was born pushed to the left with a 480px ceiling, while the bubbles start 45px inward. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/ask_structured_questions.ex (schema, validation and normalizar/1), apps/web/src/lib/api-types.ts (StructuredQuestion.allowOther), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (StructuredQuestionCard, OUTRA_RESPOSTA, permiteOutra), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.module.css (.structuredQuestionCard, .structuredQuestionCabecalho) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/harness/tools/ask_structured_questions_test.exs (open default, explicit false, non-boolean allowOther refused), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.perguntas-estruturadas.test.tsx (describe "saída por texto livre no select") Origin: real use on exp001 — "sempre dê a opção de input do usuário quando ele seleciona Escreva"
documents.s: RN-171 — The list question has a free-text way out, by default

documents.t: The "the agent is working" indicator (the three dots after 5s, RN-131/RN-156) only appears while streaming or statusAgent hold, and they were turned on in three places: the composer (handleSend), the readiness confirmations and the Phoenix channel. Every screen action that triggers a synchronous turn in the engine now arms it too. There are two, and neither of them is the composer: Answering the structured questions form — AnswerStructuredQuestionUseCase reuses SendAgentMessageUseCase (RN-162), and the call only resolves after the whole turn. Returning a story to the PO — ReturnStoryUseCase calls reviseStory, which is handle_call({:revise, …}) in po_server: the HTTP response waits for the PO to rewrite the story. The Phoenix channel does not cover the gap, and that is what makes the fix necessary rather than redundant: when it has not finished connecting yet (ticket + join, RN-108) the agent.status "working" broadcast has no listener and is lost — the screen stays in absolute silence for dozens of seconds, which is indistinguishable from "nothing is going to happen". The pair is iniciarTurnoDoAgente(agente) before the await (the channel's agent.status may arrive first, and without the agent pinned the indicator would be born without knowing who is speaking) and finalizarTurnoDoAgente() in the finally — on BOTH paths, because an error that left streaming on would lock the composer until the next turn. Resolving the call is a signal of the end of the turn as reliable as the channel's agent.done, and finalizarTurnoDoAgente is idempotent. The 5s deadline does not change: a turn that answers quickly still shows nothing. Where: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (iniciarTurnoDoAgente, handleReturnStory, StructuredQuestionCard) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.perguntas-estruturadas.test.tsx and apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.promocao-inline-e-volta.test.tsx (RN-174 describes, with the failure case proving the indicator does not get stuck) Origin: real use on exp001 — "caso a web, api e engine demore mais de 5s para ter uma resposta, a web deve apresentar uma animação no chat mostrando que o agente está pensando"
documents.s: RN-174 — An action that triggers an agent turn arms the thread indicator

documents.t: agent.response carries modelName in the three producers of the event, and not only in the four conversational agents: producer who goes through there before the four conversational ones (criativo/po/arquiteto/dev_lead) chat already wrote it, since RN-146 Engine.Harness.ToolLoop EVERY execution and gate agent — dev-*, QA, SecOps, Infra-Workflows, Psicólogo, Anamnese never wrote it SendChatMessageUseCase (api) chat without an active agent, in which the one answering is the model never wrote it No new call: RunLlmTurnUseCase already returns modelName in the body and StreamLlmTurnUseCase already puts it in the final frame — the value is the name of the model of the resolved binding (model.name), not the provider's echo. It is null when the turn failed before resolving the binding, and absent in an event written before this rule. On screen, the model stopped being the loose word modelo in mono 10px --text-muted next to the agent's name — which reads as if the model were CALLED "modelo", and which fails the reading-text contrast. It became a chip with the model icon, --text-secondary over --surface-2, and the unknown label became "modelo não registrado". The screen does not guess the model from the agent's CURRENT binding when the data is missing: attributing to an old response a model that perhaps did not even exist when it was generated would be inventing provenance, and invented provenance is worse than absent — the same argument as the frozen price in token_usage (RN-044). Out of scope, declared: agent.error still lacks the model in the four servers, even when the api sent it in the error frame (budget exceeded, for example). It is a change to another event, with another question to answer. Where: apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tool_loop.ex, apps/api/src/application/use-cases/llm/send-chat-message.use-case.ts, apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx (the chip in agent.response), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.module.css (.messageModelo) Test: apps/engine/test/engine/harness/tool_loop_test.exs, apps/api/test/application/use-cases/llm/send-chat-message.use-case.spec.ts, apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.arquiteto-modelo-icone.test.tsx, apps/web/src/design-contraste.test.ts (the chip's pair) Origin: real use on exp001 — "PO não mostrou o modelo que estava utilizando; todos os agentes devem apresentar o seu modelo ao lado do nome"
documents.s: RN-175 — Every agent response says which model it was generated with

documents.t: The chat's light Markdown (RN-158) now recognizes a GFM table and renders it with the design system's Table — the same component as Settings, Spending and Executors, not a <table> of its own: "how Brabo draws a table" is a single decision. Before, the Module Map table that the Arquiteto writes in the response came out as a paragraph with literal pipes. What distinguishes a table from prose with | is the separator line, and it is mandatory as in GFM: without it the block remains a paragraph, so "escolha entre a | b | c" does not become a table by mistake. The header rules the number of columns — a short line gets an empty cell, a long line loses the excess —, an escaped \| stays inside the cell, and the alignment comes from the separator's colons. Zero new dependency: the parser remains its own, regex-based, and the data tree keeps becoming React elements directly (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML). The artifact.module_map artifact remains OUTSIDE the thread, and the choice is deliberate: it is the project's CURRENT state, not an artifact dated per session — the same decision already recorded in RN-159 —, and it lives in the Overview. What the user asked for was the table inside the message, and that is what is now drawn; the fix serves ANY agent that writes a table, and not only the Module Map. In the bubble, the table scrolls horizontally instead of squeezing columns: the thread is ~700px and a module_map has 4 columns. Where: apps/web/src/lib/markdown.ts (table block, celulasDaLinha), apps/web/src/components/ui/MarkdownMessage.tsx (TabelaMarkdown), apps/web/src/components/ui/MarkdownMessage.module.css Test: apps/web/src/lib/markdown.test.ts (describe "tabela (RN-176)"), apps/web/src/components/ui/MarkdownMessage.test.tsx Origin: real use on exp001 — "a tabela dentro da mensagem do Mapa de Módulos do arquiteto tem que ficar bem estruturada em formato tabela, utilizar design system do próprio Brabo"
documents.s: RN-176 — A Markdown table in the thread becomes a real table

documents.t: The activity feed hid six event types (tool.call, tool.result, agent.response, agent.delta, agent.status, context.compacted) without offering any alternative: whoever wanted to see what the agent and the harness exchange had to open the database. The filter remains, and remains off by default — its reason has not changed (116 of 193 real events were of these types, see isMachineEvent) —, but it became a choice: a "Eventos de máquina" button on the same rail as the type chips. Showing everything only solves half: a long session becomes a list nobody goes through. That is why the 5 most recent stay open and the rest goes into collapses by ORIGIN — a NEW classification, which does not replace the ActivityKind: kind says which SUBJECT the event talks about (commit, PR, permission) and decides icon and color; origem says which LAYER it came from, and it is what makes the history readable in handfuls. The six come from the data that exists — actor.kind and the type prefix —, never from assumption: origin what falls into it harness tool.*, toolloop.*, agent.status, context.compacted llm agent.response, agent.delta, llm.* usuario any event with actor.kind === 'user' sistema any event with actor.kind === 'system' agente remaining agent.*, handoff.*, delegation.*, an agent's chat.* eventos the domain event log (backlog, git, PR, artifact, bootstrap…) The precedence is what makes the classification predictable, and it is in the order of the ifs: mechanism (harness, llm) beats actor, because a tool.call belongs to the harness whatever the actor; and actor beats agent prefix, because chat.message exists on both sides and what distinguishes them is who spoke. A type that nobody foresaw falls into eventos — it never disappears, never invents a category. The same rule holds in the session THREAD, with the axis inverted: the thread is ascending (the newest next to the composer), so the last 5 entries stay open at the bottom and the collapsed history stays at the TOP. The cut is over the list already grouped by agent (RN-138) — what counts is what the user sees, and a collapse of twelve messages is ONE entry on screen. Revised in the thread by RN-644: there the cut counts only MESSAGES, goes back to the opening of the turn and the history is ONE chronological block, not groups by origin (which put the answer above the question). The log panel remains as described here. Where: apps/web/src/lib/activity.ts:94 (OrigemDeEvento), :125 (origemDoEvento), :152 (agruparPorOrigem); apps/web/src/components/ActivityFeed.tsx:34 (the cut of 5), :66 (the toggle); apps/web/src/routes/session-fio.tsx:119 (the thread cut), :291 (dividirFio); apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx:516 (fio) toggle); apps/web/src/routes/session-fio.tsx:119 (the thread cut), :291 (dividirFio); apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx:516 (fio) Test: apps/web/src/lib/activity-origem.test.ts, apps/web/src/components/ActivityFeed.test.tsx (describe "ordem, agrupamento e o toggle de máquina"), apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.painel-e-agrupamento.test.tsx (describe "RN-177") Origin: real use on exp001 — "em log de eventos mostrar também log do sistema, concentrar a mensagem em grupo, ou seja mantém as últimas 5 mensagens mas abaixo vira o grupo de log de eventos, sistema, llm, harness, agente, usuário"
documents.s: RN-177 — The log shows everything, and the history collapses by ORIGIN

documents.t: The four sections of the context panel (business rules, generated artifacts, touched files and event log) were ascending: they opened at the start of the session. In a session of thousands of events that delivers the wrong screen — whoever opens the panel wants what just happened. All four became descending, including inside the backlog tree (RN-179). A consequence that came along: the feed's "Carregar mais antigos" button (RN-099) switched sides. It was ABOVE the list because the list was ascending and the past was at the top; with the order inverted the past is at the end, and a button at the top would ask to scroll in the direction opposite to what it loads — the same argument as before, with the sign flipped. And above 5 rules the list paginates, instead of growing endlessly: the panel has the width of one column and an ideation session goes past twenty rules effortlessly. The current page is resolved by clamp (min(pagina, total - 1)) and not by a synchronization effect: a new rule arriving through the poll lengthens the list, and a useEffect would render once with the invalid page before correcting it. With 5 or fewer, the paginator does not exist — a control that paginates nothing is noise taking up height. Where: apps/web/src/routes/ContextAside.tsx:109 (REGRAS_POR_PAGINA) and the ordering of the four sections in the same file; apps/web/src/components/ActivityFeed.tsx:98 (the descending sort) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.painel-e-agrupamento.test.tsx (describe "RN-178"), apps/web/src/components/ActivityFeed.test.tsx Origin: real use on exp001 — "mostrar log de eventos, arquivos tocados e regras de negócio sempre em ordem do último para o primeiro de acordo com a data" and "caso as regras de negócio ficar acima de 5, deve-se paginar"
documents.s: RN-178 — The session panel reads from last to first, and the rules list paginates

documents.t: The "Artefatos gerados" panel (RN-159) listed epic and story side by side, flat, and ignored backlog.task_created — precisely what a dev agent picks up to work on. The three now form a tree, with the child inside a collapse of the parent, and tasks are born CLOSED: an epic with thirty tasks would take over the whole panel without anyone having asked. The parentage comes from the link the event already carries — backlog.story_created writes epicId, backlog.task_created writes storyId —, never from proximity in the log. A node whose parent is not among the loaded events rises to the root instead of being hung on the nearest epic: inventing parentage is worse than showing the loose node, and a task whose story fell outside the window is a normal case, not an error. Each level remains a link to the Backlog, and the children's collapse comes BELOW the line instead of inside the header — a Disclosure header is a <button>, and an <a> inside a <button> is invalid HTML and an ambiguous click target. The section header's counter counts the WHOLE tree, not only the roots: saying "3" with eighteen tasks inside would be the same kind of number that corresponds to nothing that RN-151 removed from the sidebar. Where: apps/web/src/lib/session-backlog-tree.ts:68 (montarArvoreDeBacklog), apps/web/src/routes/ContextAside.tsx:210 (the roots become items), :225 (the tree count) Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.artefatos-gerados.test.tsx (cases "épico/história/tarefa do PO viram árvore" and "nó sem pai carregado aparece na raiz") Origin: real use on exp001 — "mostrar também as tarefas criadas no artefato do PO, mas abaixo do épico e ter opção de colapsar"
documents.s: RN-179 — The PO's artifact is a TREE: epic → story → task

documents.t: useSessionEvents fetches { limit: 200, latest: true }, and the context panel read that slice through a prop. Consequence: in a session of thousands of events the four sections showed the tail as if it were the whole session — a business rule captured at the beginning of the ideation simply did not exist, without any warning. The panel started reading the same paginated history that the Overview's Activity tab already used (RN-099), with the tail's queryKey shared with the thread — zero extra requests in the poll cycle (RN-090/RN-091). Two things changed with that: The feed gained the pager the component always had. The props onLoadOlder/hasOlder/loadingOlder are optional since RN-099 and this call site never passed them — that was why the session lost its beginning silently. A note counts how many events are missing. The number comes from SUBTRACTION over the seq (gapless and per session): menor seq baixado − 1. Never from one more request — the same mechanism as the bell's "+ N mais antigos" (RN-100). Reaching the start of the session, the note disappears, instead of asserting a zero. The derived sections read baixados (everything that has already come) and not events (the feed's window of 100): they do not paginate item by item, and cutting them at the window would make them show LESS than they showed before this change. It is the same button that feeds both. pausarPoll goes down through useSessionEventHistory to useSessionEvents, and it is not a detail: the refetch interval belongs to each OBSERVER, not to the query. A second observer of the same key with the timer on would resurrect the poll that the screen pauses during the turn — and with it the visual duplicate of the bubble in streaming. Where: apps/web/src/lib/hooks.ts:262 (the history's pausarPoll), :388 (baixados); apps/web/src/routes/ContextAside.tsx:154 (eventosAnteriores) and the ActivityFeed with the pager, at the end of the same file Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.painel-e-agrupamento.test.tsx (describe "RN-180") Origin: review of the round itself — the ceiling of 200 existed silently in the four sections
documents.s: RN-180 — The panel says what it is NOT showing

documents.t: When an area (QA, Infra) delegates to subagents and consolidates the verdict, the three outcomes the lead records — delegation.completed, delegation.failed and delegation.dispensed — only existed in the log panel. Whoever followed the session saw the gate open and close without any sign that there was a second attempt underneath. The three are now narrated in the thread as a compact notice, in the format of RN-157 — not a bubble: it is a notification of what happened inside the area, not an utterance. The SENTENCE comes from classifyEvent, the same as the panel's, because two wordings of the same event diverge on the first payload change; and it already names the subagent and the area, so the lead is not prefixed (it would produce "QA Lead QA Automação concluiu a delegação (qa)"). The area's external contract does not change (ADR 0038): the thread does not start addressing subagents, it only narrates what the lead has already recorded. The failure origin travels along in delegation.failed, for the same reason as RN-059 — it is what says whether the next step is changing the key, waiting for the provider or opening a bug. Where: apps/web/src/routes/session-timeline-montagem.tsx:754 Test: apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.painel-e-agrupamento.test.tsx (describe "RN-181") Origin: real use on exp001 — "quando houver uma nova tentativa e consolidação de algum agente deve apresentar no chat"
documents.s: RN-181 — Area delegation appears in the thread

documents.t: The light theme exists in design/tokens.css since the beginning, under [data-theme='light'], and nothing in apps/web wrote that attribute: the only way to see the light theme was to type the attribute in DevTools. It now becomes reachable. The preference lives in localStorage['brabo.theme'], accepts only 'dark' or 'light', and the default is dark — the design system's primary theme. What applies it is apps/web/public/theme-boot.js, synchronous in the <head> and before the bundle: data-theme decides the colors of the whole tokens.css, and applying it after hydration would make the light-theme user see a dark flash on every load. It is a file, not an inline script, and the reason is the same that made the fonts self-hosted (ADR 0036): the production image serves under script-src 'self' (docker/web/nginx.conf), without 'unsafe-inline' and without a nonce. Inline would work in pnpm dev:web and would be blocked in the published image — the worst failure mode possible, because it only shows up after the deploy. The whole path degrades instead of breaking: localStorage can throw (private mode, storage blocked in an iframe) and theme is a preference, not a function; an unknown value falls to the default instead of becoming a data-theme that the CSS does not know and that would render with no theme at all. Where: apps/web/public/theme-boot.js:41, apps/web/index.html:53 Test: apps/web/src/lib/tema.test.ts (describe "contrato com o script de boot") ADR: 0074
documents.s: RN-182 — The theme is chosen, persisted and applied before the first paint

documents.t: Reading, writing, toggling and observing the theme is apps/web/src/lib/tema.ts — the button lives in the shell and consumes that API, it never writes data-theme on its own. Three decisions inside it: temaAtual() reads the ATTRIBUTE first, and only then localStorage and the default. The attribute is what the screen is showing; falling back to the stored preference before it would make the UI assert a theme different from what is seen, in the exact case where the boot failed. lerTemaSalvo() returns null, not the default, when there is no stored preference. Whoever never chose may one day follow the operating system (prefers-color-scheme), and erasing that distinction here would take the information away from whoever decides that later. observarTema() covers the storage event, which the browser fires in the OTHER tabs of the same origin. Without it two open tabs would stay in different themes until the next reload. The key and the default are repeated in public/theme-boot.js because it runs before the bundle and cannot import anything. It is the only duplication able to diverge silently, and that is why the test reads the boot file and fails if the two stop matching. Where: apps/web/src/lib/tema.ts:73 Test: apps/web/src/lib/tema.test.ts ADR: 0074
documents.s: RN-183 — The theme preference has one source, and the <html> attribute is the truth

documents.t: While the light theme was unreachable (RN-182), measuring only the dark one was honest: measuring a screen nobody can open is measuring an intention. With the theme button, no longer measuring the light one would hide half of the product's visible surface — so the pairs are now enforced in both themes, with the same floor (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for interface elements). For that, six light-theme tokens changed value. The most demanding background of the light theme is --code-bg (paper, #efe4d2, one step away from the surfaces), and whatever passes against it passes against the rest: --accent 3.56 → 4.81, --warning 3.15 → 4.98, --success 3.89 → 5.12, --violet 4.16 → 4.95, --text-muted 2.76 → 5.17, and --accent-hover followed the accent one step below. The dark theme did not change a single value, and its known debt remained locked by the same five numbers (3.89 / 3.10 / 3.88 / 3.88 / 4.41) until RN-640 (ADR 0181), which closed it with the neutral palette and turned it into a floor. The light theme's --text-muted was not debt: at 2.40:1 over --surface-2 it failed even the interface element floor, which is the lowest that exists. It was a defect, and the light theme has no reason to be worse than the primary one. Where: design/tokens.css:208 Test: apps/web/src/lib/contraste.test.ts, apps/web/src/design-contraste.test.ts, apps/web/test/design-contraste.test.ts ADR: 0074
documents.s: RN-184 — Contrast is measured in BOTH themes

documents.t: The highlighting palette was three tokens of its own (--syntax-function, --syntax-comment, --syntax-operator) and five reuses of semantic ones (--accent, --warning, --violet, --success, --text-primary). It is this reuse that made the palette measured only in the dark theme: in the light one the semantic tokens failed against the paper --code-bg. It now has the handoff's eight roles, with the --syntax-* prefix the repository already uses, and each with its own value per theme. Naming the eight is what lets highlighting diverge from the semantic tokens on the day it needs to. The handoff's value only comes in when the measurement approves. Against the handoff's own --code-bg, five of the eight fail the 4.5:1 that code text requires — --syn-cm 4.09:1 in dark and 2.32:1 in light, --syn-kw 4.34:1, --syn-str 4.20:1, --syn-fn 4.14:1, --syn-op 4.00:1. Where the handoff fails, the measured number holds: it is the same rule as ADR 0036 — the handoff's intention holds, the mechanism (or the number) that breaks the product does not. The five semantic tokens are still what paints (SyntaxTokens.module.css did not change in this delivery) and that is why they are measured alongside the eight: as long as they are the real pixel, the floor is enforced on them. In the light theme each role today has the SAME number as the semantic token that paints it, on purpose — two sources with different numbers for the same pixel would diverge on the first fix made on one side only. Where: design/tokens.css:111 Test: apps/web/src/lib/contraste.test.ts (describe "contraste — paleta de sintaxe sobre --code-bg") ADR: 0074
documents.s: RN-185 — The eight syntax roles, and the handoff's value only comes in measured

documents.t: Shell.tsx had a fixed width (248px) and no way to shrink. It now toggles between --sidebar-w (264px) and --sidebar-w-collapsed (62px) — the two tokens that Onda 1/frente A had already created in design/tokens.css — with transition: width .18s ease. Collapsed, it becomes a vertical rail: a square of initials per project (border in the identity color, RN-197) plus an Activities icon; clicking a project in the rail re-expands the bar, opens that project and navigates to it. The preference belongs to the user and survives a reload: brabo.sidebar.collapsed ('1'/'0') in apps/web/src/lib/sidebar-state.ts. It is manual only (colapsadoManual): there was a second, automatic state (autoColapsado), ORed in by the Code tab, and it was removed by ADR 0126 — see RN-201. No screen collapses the sidebar on its own; what is seen collapsed was requested by the user, and is stored. Where: apps/web/src/routes/Shell.tsx:340-351 (state and toggle), apps/web/src/routes/Shell.module.css (.sidebar, .colapsado .sidebar, .trilha*), apps/web/src/lib/sidebar-state.ts (lerColapsado/gravarColapsado) Test: apps/web/src/lib/sidebar-state.test.ts (describe "colapso"), apps/web/src/routes/Shell.test.tsx Origin: PROGRAMA 28, Onda 2, frente B — design_handoff_brabo/README.md section "Navigation shell"
documents.s: RN-195 — The sidebar collapses into an icon rail, with the preference persisted

documents.t: Each project in the sidebar gets a chevron: clicking it expands the row and reveals that project's tab list (Visão geral, Executores, Criativo, Chat, Code, Backlog, Aprovações, Insights, Gastos, Configurações), each one a link to /projects/$projectId?tab=<chave>. Several projects can stay open at the same time — the state is a Set<string> of ids, persisted in brabo.sidebar.open. The tab list and the labels come from ABAS_DO_PROJETO (apps/web/src/routes/project-tabs.ts, owned by frente C, running in parallel in this same wave) — the sidebar only reads the exported array, it never rewrites tab names. Shape assumption, to be checked against what frente C delivered: AbaDoProjeto has key: string, label: string and count?: (contagens: ContagensDeAba) => number | undefined, with ContagensDeAba = { promocoesPendentes, aprovacoesPendentes, hipotesesPendentes }. The sidebar can only fill aprovacoesPendentes for free (pendingApprovalsCount already comes in the dashboard summary, RN-151); promocoesPendentes/hipotesesPendentes come in as 0 — computing them would require a new query PER PROJECT OPEN in the sidebar, the same class of N+1 that RN-090/091 closed in the dashboard. The two badges remain correct within the rule of ProjectPage itself; only the preview in the sidebar is partial, and it is a deliberate omission, not a bug. The project of the CURRENT route always appears expanded (projetosAbertosEfetivo), even without being in the persisted Set — opening "for free" through the route writes nothing; only the explicit click on the chevron goes into brabo.sidebar.open. Since ADR 0211 (AT-404) this list is the project's ONLY navigation: the vertical rail left and it received everything only the rail had — the three groups with headers, the active tab marked, the vertical tablist named by the project, the keyboard (ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End with wraparound, crossing groups) and the FIVE counters, each on its own tab and never summed. The deliberate omission above still holds for a CLOSED project and for the project open outside the frame (in the Session, for example): only Approvals, from the summary. With the project frame mounted, the five numbers come from the SAME hook it uses (useContagensDoProjeto), without a new request. Collapsed, the square of the open project opens a flyout with the same tabs. Where: apps/web/src/routes/Shell.tsx:557 (projetosAbertosEfetivo), :505 (useContagensDoProjeto), :512 (irParaAba), :527 (flyoutAberto), :215 (contagensDoResumo); apps/web/src/routes/AbasDoProjeto.tsx:78 (AbasDoProjeto), :34 (itensDasAbas), :95 (aoTeclar); apps/web/src/lib/contagens-do-projeto.ts:22 (useContagensDoProjeto), :70 (publicarAbaAtiva), :86 (pedirAba); apps/web/src/lib/sidebar-state.ts (lerProjetosAbertos/gravarProjetosAbertos) Test: apps/web/src/lib/sidebar-state.test.ts (describe "conjuntos"), apps/web/src/routes/Shell.test.tsx (describe "Shell — abas do projeto aberto (ADR 0211)": the 12 tabs, the five separate counters, the active one, the click and the arrow navigating, the collapsed flyout, the drawer on the phone and the failure case — without the frame mounted, only the summary's number), apps/web/src/routes/AbasDoProjeto.test.tsx (groups, active, counters, keyboard, roving tabindex, link per project), apps/web/src/routes/project-tabs.test.tsx Origin: PROGRAMA 28, Onda 2, frente B; ADR 0211 (AT-404)
documents.s: RN-196 — Expandable projects reveal the project's tabs, N at the same time

documents.t: The handoff asks for a "project color dot" on the expanded row and the same color principle on the collapsed rail. The product already had a dot there — NavStatusDot — but it is status (budget/recent activity, derived without its own query from useProjectsSummary/useProjectsStatus, RN-039), not identity: its color CHANGES over time. Decision, documented instead of resolved: the expanded row keeps showing only NavStatusDot (it is actionable information; duplicating a second dot next to it would be noise). The IDENTITY color — stable per project, a deterministic hash of the id over a fixed palette of tokens (corDoProjeto, no new table, the same idea as AGENTS[key].color) — appears only on the collapsed rail, as the border of the initials square, which is where there is no room for the two dots and where identity (not status) is what helps to find the right project among several similar squares. In the same way, the handoff asks for a "badge with the total of last iterations" on the project; the product uses pendingApprovalsCount since RN-151, which is later than the handoff and fixes a real defect (a number that did not correspond to anything actionable when clicked). This badge does not change — RN-151 remains in force, and it is the handoff that diverges here. Where: apps/web/src/lib/sidebar-state.ts (corDoProjeto), apps/web/src/routes/Shell.tsx (NavStatusDot, comment on the divergence) Test: apps/web/src/lib/sidebar-state.test.ts (describe "corDoProjeto") Origin: PROGRAMA 28, Onda 2, frente B — divergence between design_handoff_brabo/CHECKLIST-CONFRONTO.md and RN-151
documents.s: RN-197 — Two project colors, two purposes: identity is not status

documents.t: The sidebar's Activities section is the same grouping logic as AgentTimelineTree.tsx/timeline-tree.ts (already used in the project's Overview), moved to a new place — not rewritten. montarArvore already groups by evento.actor.id; the novelty is agruparPorInstancia (apps/web/src/lib/timeline-tree.ts), which decides which branches form a two-level visual group. The "instance" is not a renumbered counter (-01/-02) — it is the REAL agent_id the product already writes: devAgentId/extraDevAgentId (apps/api/src/application/use-cases/execution/activate-execution.use-case.ts:27-38) produce dev-<modulo> and dev-<modulo>-2 (suffix always exactly -2, because the ceiling is TWO per module, RN-154). A branch only becomes an "extra instance" of another if the base agent (without the suffix) ALSO has a branch in the same list — otherwise it is the agent itself. An agent with one instance opens directly on the events; with two, it reveals a second level, one row per instance, each with its own count — reusing getAgentLastSeenSeq/setAgentLastSeenSeq (read-state.ts) which already existed for the tree's novelty counter. Scope: only the project of the CURRENT ROUTE (pathname), not all projects of the workspace — aggregating all would require an events query PER project, the same class of N+1 that RN-090/091 closed in the dashboard. It reuses the SAME pair of hooks that AgentTimelineTree/SessionPage already use (useActiveExecutionSession + useSessionEvents, same queryKey) — zero new requests when the two screens are mounted together. What opens/closes is persisted in brabo.sidebar.agents, with the handoff's format adapted to the real ids: agenteBase (open group, e.g.: dev-backend) or ${agenteBase}/${instancia} (a specific instance open, e.g.: dev-backend/dev-backend-2). Where: apps/web/src/lib/timeline-tree.ts (agruparPorInstancia, GrupoDeAgente), apps/web/src/routes/Shell.tsx:237-311 (GrupoDeAtividade, InstanciaDeAgente), apps/web/src/routes/Shell.tsx:376-399 (scope and persistence) Test: apps/web/src/lib/timeline-tree.test.ts (describe "agruparPorInstancia"), apps/web/src/lib/sidebar-state.test.ts Origin: PROGRAMA 28, Onda 1/frente B0 (finding, no code) and Onda 2/frente B (implementation)
documents.s: RN-198 — Activities groups by REAL base agent/instance, never by an invented counter

documents.t: The sidebar footer gets a sun/moon button that consumes the API of apps/web/src/lib/tema.ts from Onda 1/frente A (temaAtual, alternarTema, observarTema) without reimplementing anything — only the BUTTON is new. It works collapsed (62px): the text label disappears, but aria-label/title keep describing the current theme and the click keeps toggling. Where: apps/web/src/routes/Shell.tsx:130-148 (BotaoDeTema) Test: apps/web/src/lib/tema.test.ts (the API, unchanged by this RN) — Shell.test.tsx does not duplicate the theme suite, it only mounts the Shell Origin: PROGRAMA 28, Onda 2, frente B
documents.s: RN-199 — Theme button in the footer, functional when collapsed

documents.t: The two route-less items of the nav footer ("Chat global"/"Configurações", title="em breve") are removed. The handoff is explicit: only Projects and Activities are GLOBAL items — everything else is scoped to a project. "Configurações" still exists, as a project TAB (RN-196) inside the expanded row — what goes away is the loose item with no destination. Where: apps/web/src/routes/Shell.tsx (the .globalNav/ .inertNavItem block from FASE 17a was removed, with no global replacement) Test: apps/web/src/routes/Shell.test.tsx (describe "sem itens globais inertes") Origin: PROGRAMA 28, Onda 2, frente B — design_handoff_brabo/README.md section "Navigation shell"
documents.s: RN-200 — Only Projects and Activities as global items

documents.t: Two final handoff keys: brabo.project (the active project) and brabo.tab (the active tab) — written when the user clicks a tab link IN THE SIDEBAR (LinhaDeAba/the project name link). ?tab= in the URL only counts as an INITIAL deep link (project-tabs.ts, FASE 24) — switching tabs inside ProjectPage.tsx is local state and does not write to the URL after the first load, so these keys are the only way for the preference to survive from one navigation to another. This half never changed. The Code tab's auto-collapse LEFT (ADR 0126). Until then the Code tab collapsed the sidebar by itself to give width to the editor, without writing a preference: AutoCollapseContext/useAutoCollapseSidebar in sidebar-state.ts, registered by ProjectCodeTab.tsx (the only caller) and ORed with the manual collapse inside the Shell. The context, the hook, the autoColapsado state, the Provider around <Outlet /> and the disabled of the collapse button — which existed only to protect that path — were all removed. The reason is structural: with the project's vertical rail (routes/ProjectRail.tsx, removed in ADR 0211) always present, keeping the auto-collapse would put the Shell's icon rail right against the project rail — TWO adjacent, permanent vertical rails, on the heaviest tab of the product. What now holds: the sidebar collapse is a decision of the USER, and only theirs. It stays manual, stays persisted in brabo.sidebar.collapsed (RN-195), and no screen collapses the sidebar on its own. The cost, accepted and declared: the Code tab now opens with the sidebar EXPANDED (264px) + the project rail (180px) + the rail of the CodeShell itself (48px) — 492px of frame before the first character of code, MEASURED in the browser, against ~110px before (62px of collapsed sidebar + 48px of the Code rail). Collapsing manually remains possible and still produces the Shell rail next to the project rail — the difference is that now it was the user who chose, not the system. Revised by ADR 0211 (AT-404): the project rail left, and the Code tab frame became 312px with the sidebar expanded (264 + 48 of the CodeShell) and 110px collapsed (62 + 48) — with no double rail in either case. The collapse remains the user's only. The active tab the sidebar marks comes from the project frame (publicarAbaAtiva), not only from brabo.tab. Where: apps/web/src/lib/sidebar-state.ts:80-105 (lerProjetoAtivo/gravarProjetoAtivo, lerAbaAtiva/gravarAbaAtiva, and the comment recording the removal), apps/web/src/routes/Shell.tsx:366-369 (only colapsadoManual is left), apps/web/src/routes/ProjectCodeTab.tsx (no collapse call) Test: apps/web/src/lib/sidebar-state.test.ts (describe "projeto e aba ativos"), apps/web/src/routes/Shell.test.tsx (describe "Shell — colapso da sidebar": the preference is only born from a click on the button and is always written). The "useAutoCollapseSidebar" describe was removed together with the hook. Origin: PROGRAMA 28, Onda 2, frente B — design_handoff_brabo/CHECKLIST-CONFRONTO.md section 1; the auto-collapse half was revised by ADR 0126
documents.s: RN-201 — Active project/tab persist across pages; the sidebar collapse is ONLY the user's

documents.t: The most recent design handoff of PROGRAMA 28 calls the consultative tab "Chat RAG" (designs/Brabo Chat.dc.html), but the product does not have that functionality: there is no per-project indexing pipeline, no vector index, no source citation UI. ADR 0075 put embed in the LLMProvider contract — the operation exists and is PROVEN on Ollama —, but nothing CONSUMES it yet. Today's sessions tab is the ordinary consultative Chat of RN-104: an agent answering with the session context, without producing backlog, with no RAG at all behind it. Labeling the tab "Chat RAG" today would announce a capability that does not exist — the same mistake that ADR 0042 already refuses for a catalog model ("não ativar modelo descoberto automaticamente"). The label changes on the day the functionality arrives, together with the data behind it — never before. Where: apps/web/src/routes/project-tabs.ts:144 (entry key: 'sessions') Test: apps/web/src/routes/project-tabs.test.tsx (describe "abas do projeto derivam de um registro só", 'RN-202 — a aba \sessions` continua "Chat", nunca "Chat RAG"'`) ADR: 0078
documents.s: RN-202 — The sessions tab stays "Chat", never "Chat RAG"

documents.t: The design handoff lists 7 project tabs (Visão geral, Criativo, Código, Chat RAG, Gastos, Aprovações, Configurações); the registry (apps/web/src/routes/project-tabs.ts) has 10. The three extra ones — executores (RN-121), backlog (RN-048) and insights (the Psicólogo's hypotheses awaiting a decision) — were born AFTER the handoff was designed, all with real data, a counter derived from a query and at least one RN of their own with a test. The handoff fixes how each screen should LOOK — colors, typography, spacing, the design of the frame —, and that part was followed to the letter in this same change (header, ruler, scrolling, content width). It does not freeze the tab inventory on the day it was written. Deleting the three to "match" the handoff would destroy information the product already knew how to show, for the wrong reason. Where: apps/web/src/routes/project-tabs.ts:91 (the REGISTRO) Test: apps/web/src/routes/project-tabs.test.tsx (describe "abas do projeto derivam de um registro só", 'RN-203 — as 3 abas que o handoff não previu continuam no registro') ADR: 0078
documents.s: RN-203 — The handoff is a visual reference, not a ceiling on how many tabs the product has

documents.t: The "Melhores modelos por capacidade" block (Settings) has no score column. The handoff shows a score per capability (code 9.4, image 9.1…), but it is FICTITIOUS mock data — no provider publishes "code quality" and the product does not measure that anywhere. Computing a number here would be the same "guess dressed up as data" that ADR 0041 forbids for MODEL capability, now about quality. Instead, "recomendado"/"alternativa" come from two real signals, among the models THIS workspace's curation marked for that capability (uses, RN-057): first the ones most used by agents of THIS project — the same cascade that resolves the current binding of each agent —, cost (from the catalog, ascending) as tiebreaker. "What the team has already chosen" is the most honest signal available without inventing a score. A capability with no curated model shows "sem cobertura curada" — it never hides the row, the same pattern that the Origin column of ModelsSection already uses for the skipped binding. Where: apps/web/src/routes/settings/MelhoresModelosPorCapacidadeSection.tsx Test: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSettingsTab.test.tsx (describe "MelhoresModelosPorCapacidadeSection") ADR: 0077
documents.s: RN-210 — "Recommended" is real usage and cost, never a computed score

documents.t: The handoff asks for daily bars stacked by provider and a breakdown by provider. The repository's dataviz skill requires validating a categorical palette by script before using it, never by eye: validate_palette.js fails every combination of 3+ tokens from design/tokens.css against at least one of the two themes — --accent+--violet is the only pair that passes in both (several --syntax-* are literally the same hex as --warning/--violet/--success, measured). With 9 providers (ADR 0043) and 2 validated colors, cycling the palette is the anti-pattern the skill itself names ("a 9th series is never a generated hue"), and inventing a new hex would violate this frente's instruction. The breakdown by provider becomes a Ranking — the same piece as "Por modelo"/"Por projeto"/"Por agente e pessoa", without identity by color. The DAILY series per provider is not delivered: sumGroupedBy (ADR 0076) groups by one dimension at a time, and there is no cross aggregation day×provider in this wave's backend. Where: apps/web/src/lib/spend.ts ("Gasto por PROVIDER na tela" block), apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSpendTab.tsx (GastoDoWorkspace) Test: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSpendTab.test.tsx (describe "a audiência do owner" — 'mostra os cinco recortes do workspace, incluindo provider') ADR: 0076
documents.s: RN-211 — Spending per provider on screen is a Ranking, not an invented categorical palette

Three readings: loading (silent, avoids flashing before the role resolves the audience below), no budget defined (a text note, no CTA) and error (silent — in practice almost always a 403 from someone who has a WORKSPACE role but is not maintainer on the PROJECT, and showing a banner on purpose would be a false alarm for most members, the same pattern already used by the compact TokenMeter of ProjectPage.tsx). No new business rule — purely presentation of data that already exists. documents.t: TokenMeter already has savingsBRL/savingsPct ready to receive the number, and they remain unfed on purpose. The card would require a COUNTERFACTUAL price — how much the same call would have cost on a paid model — that does not exist anywhere in the product: the catalog (ADR 0042) only freezes the price of the model ACTUALLY used (RN-044), and there is no declared mapping "local model X ~ paid model Y". Inventing it here would be the same class of "score dressed up as data" that RN-210 already refused for the capability ranking.
