documents.t: This document is the phase's scope: what it pursues, what it refuses, and in what order. The decisions live in ADR 0149, 0150, 0151 and 0152 — whatever is here and not there is intention, not decision.
documents.s: FASE 29 — the one-line installation

documents.t: Brabo installs today in three disconnected gestures, and none of them knows about the others: gesture where what it requires of the installer bring up the services docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.prod.yml export five secrets by hand (RN-114, ADR 0059) and have the checkout put the runner on the machine browser (ADR 0118) download the binary, manual chmod +x (BRB-031), repeat per project choose where the code lives pnpm bootstrap (ADR 0146) have a development checkout — the menu doesn't exist outside it FASE 28 refused in writing the one-line installer, and the reason still holds: "a one-line installer without a signature is worse than the current download" (fase-28-pasta-do-usuario.md, BRB-005). A curl | sh that downloads an unsigned artifact turns any compromise of the channel into code execution on the installer's machine — and the product today signs nothing it publishes. That is why this phase starts with the signature and not with the installer. The order is not a preference: without ADR 0149, ADR 0150 would be the thing FASE 28 refused.
documents.s: The problem

documents.t: Each layer with a single mechanism, and none inventing new authority: layer where mechanism provenance release.yml, build-runner-binaries.yml keyless cosign (Actions OIDC) on images and binaries; signed checksums.txt installation versioned install.sh, obtained from GitHub Releases verifies its own origin, detects what already exists, asks, writes a marker data docker/backup/ backup and restore that run against compose, without a cluster live folder the runner's guard.ts one consented base; each project is a subfolder inside it The fourth layer exists for a physical reason FASE 28 had already named: a bind mount doesn't cross the network nor reach a path outside what was mounted. The brabo-runner is the process that already lives on the user's machine — what is missing isn't an agent, it's for it to be born with a base instead of a loose path.
documents.s: The design, in four layers

documents.t: The point the four ADRs need to declare, and which decides the installer's design: Choosing a base, writing a .env, creating a folder and installing a service are configuration consented to by the user in their own terminal — not an agent asking to act. None of it becomes a proposed_action, and routing it through there would fall under the path scope of ADR 0055, become a queue of routine approvals and erode precisely the ceiling that gives the click its meaning. The corollary holds both ways, and it is what separates this phase from an ordinary installer: consent does not waive verification. The user consents to the base and to the installation; they have no way to consent to the provenance of a binary they cannot inspect. That is why signature verification belongs to the mechanism, never a question on screen — and failing it is a named refusal, never a warning one can accept by clicking.
documents.s: Configuration consent ≠ action approval

documents.t: The repository's prose counts remain in known drift: the frontmatter of docs/adr/index.md announces a number of ADRs the disk doesn't confirm. No session of this phase trusts a number written in prose. The method, which every session of this phase repeats before reserving any number — and which FASE 28 already ran, plus a second half that was missing: # ADRs e RNs em dev — o piso git ls-tree --name-only dev docs/adr/ | grep -oE '^[0-9]{4}' | sort -n | tail -1 git grep -h -E '^### RN-' dev -- 'docs/business-rules.md' 'docs/business-rules/*.md' \ | grep -oE 'RN-[0-9]+' | sed 's/RN-//' | sort -n -u | tail -1 # o que está EM VOO — branches locais e remotas ainda não mergeadas for b in $(git branch --format='%(refname:short)'; git branch -r --format='%(refname:short)'); do git merge-base --is-ancestor "$b" dev 2>/dev/null && continue echo "$b: $(git ls-tree --name-only "$b" docs/adr/ | grep -oE '^[0-9]{4}' | sort -n | tail -1)" done Measured at the start of session 1, against dev: 147 ADRs (highest 0147) and 382 RNs (highest 521). And in flight, at the same moment: ADR 0148 allocated by two branches at the same time, and RNs 510, 522 and 523 — 522 and 523 also duplicated between two branches each. The range reserved for the phase is RN-524 to RN-538, and the ADRs are 0149, 0150, 0151 and 0152. The jump over 510/522/523 and over 0148 is deliberate. Recording the three observed collisions is the point, not a detail: FASE 28 wrote that counting only dev would return an already allocated number, and this session found the same failure mode happening three times at the same time. Counting dev is a necessary and not sufficient condition; the second half of the command above is what was missing, and that is why it comes in here. All three were resolved later, and the criterion was the date. Whoever allocated first keeps the number: the three branches from 2026-09-06 kept ADR 0148, RN-522 and RN-523, and those from 2026-09-08 renumbered to ADR 0153, RN-539 and RN-540 — above this phase's range, out of reach of anything in flight. One of them was already the second renumbering of the same RN: it was born 522, became 523 to escape a collision, and fell into another — because that sweep covered the remote branches, and the one waiting for it was local. It's worth repeating why a collision survives so long: docs:build doesn't catch a duplicate anchor. onBrokenAnchors: 'throw' fails a link to an anchor that doesn't exist; with two identical anchors Docusaurus resolves the first and the second becomes unreachable, silently.
documents.s: Numbering — counted, not inherited

documents.t: This phase's plan was born from a scope written before the measurement. Five points of it didn't survive the disk, and they are recorded because a plan that rewrites itself to match the result stops teaching: workspace.verified doesn't exist — not as an event, not as a channel message, not as a route. What exists is workspace_confirm, and it is one-way: terminal_channel.ex:356-373 replies {:noreply, socket} and pushes nothing back to the runner. A pair with a reply has another mold in the repository, that of exec/exec_result. Point 5 of ADR 0146 doesn't version any install.sh — it versions scripts/dev/consentir-base.mjs. The principle ("never generated by the api, never downloaded at run time", with the corollary that the api gets no route that emits a host script) is generalizable, and ADR 0150 extends it; but citing it as if it already spoke of the installer would be attributing to the ADR a sentence it doesn't have. docker-compose.prod.yml doesn't consume GHCR. Every service points to brabo-*:prod with a local build: block, and the file's header says of itself: "what this file is NOT: a hardened production manifest". The only consumer of .release/images.json is kustomize. make test-restore is a Kubernetes path (it requires kubectl and the brabo-backup CronJob), and docker/backup/backup.sh covers only Postgres. Treating it as "the migration proof" in a compose installation would be promising what the disk doesn't sustain — hence ADR 0152 existing. The BRB register doesn't belong to the repository. It lives in the maintainer's vault, with 33 items and a definition of done per item; here only two ids appeared, in prose. Measuring the six the phase inherited: BRB-032 and BRB-033 describe defects that no longer reproduce, and BRB-004 is not what the id suggests — it asks for third-party images by digest, not the tag #419 pinned. Hence this repository's register keeps the evidence (measured state, file:line) and not the finding. "One runner per project" is enforced in five independent places, not only in the Registry: the terminal:<projectId> topic, the socket id runner_socket:<kind>:<project_id>:<user_id>, the project-scoped ticket, the runner_device_keys.project_id NOT NULL column and the service unit name. That is why the per-machine runner left this phase.
documents.s: What the measurement corrected in the scope

documents.t: One deliverable each. The table is reading order, not precedence — the "depends on" column is what orders, and FASE 28 recorded the case where the real order diverged. # deliverable depends on its own prohibitions 1 this document, ADRs 0149-0152, the BRB register and the RN range — doesn't touch apps/, docker/, scripts/, .github/, deploy/; doesn't edit an accepted ADR 2 signing in release.yml and build-runner-binaries.yml; checksums.txt; verification in the runbook 1 doesn't write install.sh; doesn't change what the images contain; doesn't touch the api proxy (see below) 3 install.sh: origin verification, detection, question, marker — and the GET /runner-releases/binary proxy starts verifying 2 brings up nothing — not compose, not migrate, not runner 4 install.sh: GHCR × local build source, secrets, installation compose, verified startup 3 doesn't install the runner; doesn't migrate a previous installation 5 volume backup and restore, running against compose 1 doesn't touch the k8s CronJob nor deploy/k8s/test-restore.sh 6 install.sh: migration of a previous installation, proven with session 5 4, 5 doesn't delete the user's base nor the mirror folder, under any circumstances 7 runner: consented base in guard.ts; install.sh installs the runner 4 doesn't touch per-project pairing; doesn't create a new credential 8 protocol: capability and folder-creation message, its own predicate 7 doesn't change RunnerReadiness; doesn't introduce proposed_action 9 ✅ web: picker via fs_list_dir in runner mode, wait with three states (RN-533) 8 doesn't touch the mounted mode path (RN-504, through the api) 10 ✅ E2E on a clean machine, install.sh in the signed manifest, docmap, docs:check (RN-534) 6, 9 doesn't loosen a gate for the E2E to pass The two sides of verification don't come in together, and the split is the real dependency. Session 2 delivers whoever produces the signature; the consumers come in at 3, because the two that exist — install.sh checking its own hash, and the GET /runner-releases/binary proxy checking the binary it serves — read the same signed checksums.txt and can only be written after it exists. Until 3 closes, the proxy keeps serving bytes from GitHub without verifying anything, exactly as before: session 2 doesn't worsen that path, and doesn't fix it either. Session 4 doesn't call docker/smoke.sh, and the change is deliberate. The plan said "migrate, smoke". Neither survived contact with the disk, and for opposite reasons: migrate isn't a step because compose already chains it (api depends on migrate-api with service_completed_successfully, and up --wait waits) — a second place ordering migration would be the second source of the same truth; and smoke.sh builds the images (--build) and tears down the stack at the end, which is the opposite of what an installation wants. In its place, the installer asks before asserting: it hits /health on the api and the engine and only then says it installed — the rule reset-total.sh learned the hard way (BRB-033).
documents.s: The sessions

documents.t: Declared in the four ADRs, and repeated here because it is what gives meaning to the rest: decide.ts and the absolute ceilings of the permissions policy — none gets an exception, not even a configurable one proposed_action as the origin of every external effect of an agent the immutability of the event log the image gate in the three modes (ADR 0135) the mirror (RN-515/516/517) — the folder binding is another thing, with another message; don't merge them the five containment layers of the broker (ADR 0130) docker-compose.prod.yml, which remains the validation compose for the images
documents.s: What this phase does NOT touch

documents.t: The per-machine runner — the five couplings above. Declared as the scope of the next phase, with the measurement already done. git credential discarded in docker exec in runner mode — ADR 0130/0145. The initial clone through the new message runs on the HOST, through the path that already carries the credential, and is therefore not affected; the gap stays where it was. Revocation reaches {project, user}, never {key} (RN-520). With per-project pairing preserved in this phase, the cost doesn't change — but when FASE 30 makes the runner per-machine, revoking will bring down all the projects of that machine. Cost declared here so it isn't discovered there. The broker isn't published — docker-bake.hcl has four targets and scripts/ci/images-manifest.ts accepts four. In a GHCR installation the container-broker profile is unreachable, and mounted mode brings up a container through the broker (ADR 0144). ADR 0150 decides what the installer does about it. BRB-017 (GPL obligation of the tools bundled in the engine image, P1) stays where it was — and the phase makes it more concrete, not less: the installer distributes that image to third-party machines. BRB-004 (third-party images by digest) is touched: the installer resolves its OWN images by digest, while neo4j, pgvector and ollama remain by tag. See the BRB register.
documents.s: Gaps the phase touches and doesn't solve

documents.t: This document is the phase's scope: what it pursues, what it refuses, and in what order. The decisions live in ADR 0154 and in ADR 0155 — where this and they disagree, the ADR wins.
documents.s: FASE 30 — the machine's local agent

documents.t: Install Brabo in one line and use it. Today FASE 29 delivers almost that: the install.sh verifies its own origin, brings up compose, installs the runner binary with install -m 0755 and writes the base. And then it stops, at two points that the product itself already declared in writing. The first is the local agent. The installer's last line says it doesn't pair the agent with a project, and that the device key still comes from the screen. Whoever wants to use the installed binary goes back to the browser and ends up pasting into the terminal the command that apps/web/src/lib/runner-bootstrap.ts:398 builds. The comment next to it explains why the screen can't avoid it — "a web page doesn't run a binary on anybody's machine" — and it's right. What it doesn't cover is that the installer is not a web page: it runs in the terminal, with a TTY, and ADR 0150 refused curl | sh precisely so it could ask. The second is that nobody can get in. Measured in this phase: the generated .env has no email variable at all, MAIL_TRANSPORT falls to log (docker/docker-compose.install.yml:200), and registration requires verifying the email — which, as the docblock of apps/api/src/scripts/provisionar-usuario.ts already recorded, "with the log-only MailSender doesn't close on its own". The one-line installation ends by saying "Done" and leaving the person to fish a verification link out of docker compose logs api. Both are solved in the same place, and that is what makes a single phase.
documents.s: What the phase pursues

documents.t: FASE 29 took the per-machine runner out of scope with a measurement: "one runner per project is enforced in five independent places". Re-measuring with file:line, three of the five don't need to change — and that shrinks the phase by half. # where what it enforces this phase 1 terminal_channel.ex:204 topic terminal:<projectId> doesn't touch 2 runner_socket.ex:73 socket id with project_id doesn't touch 3 Engine.Runners.SocketTicket ticket carries project_id doesn't touch 4 apps/api/src/db/schema/auth.ts:325-326 project_id NOT NULL becomes nullable 5 apps/runner/src/servico.ts:264,391 unit brabo-runner-<projectId> becomes one per machine The reason is in ADR 0154: items 1, 2 and 3 describe a connection, not a process. A process that opens N connections — one per project — satisfies them byte for byte, and preserves the refusal of a second runner on the same project, which is a real guarantee and not an accident. What remains is what belongs to the process: the credential (4) and the unit (5). Nothing in the engine changes in this phase. That was the measurement's most useful finding, and it is what keeps RunnerReadiness (RN-507), the mirror (RN-516) and workspace_create (RN-532) byte for byte.
documents.s: What the measurement changed in the scope

documents.t: One deliverable each. The "depends on" column is what orders. # deliverable depends on its own prohibitions 1 this document, ADRs 0154/0155 and the RN range — doesn't touch apps/, docker/, scripts/, install.sh; doesn't edit an accepted ADR 2 CLOSED — api: nullable project_id, machine key accepted in runner-ticket, GET runner/projects (RN-543) 1 doesn't touch the engine; doesn't loosen any route's role 3 CLOSED — runner: N connections, one per project, discovered through the route (RN-544) 2 doesn't touch RunnerReadiness, the mirror or workspace_create 4 CLOSED — runner: per-machine unit in service install, coexisting with the per-project ones (RN-545) 3 doesn't remove the per-project unit; doesn't change Restart=on-abnormal 5 CLOSED — api: POST /internal/first-account, verified account + personal workspace, 409 with any user (RN-546) 1 doesn't create a public route; doesn't touch normal registration 6 CLOSED — install.sh: consent, account, machine key and service install (RN-547) 4, 5 doesn't write the password anywhere; without a TTY it reports and exits 0 7 CLOSED — web: the project screen recognizes an already paired machine agent (RN-548) 3 doesn't remove the ADR 0118 flow 8 CLOSED — E2E on a clean machine, docmap, docs:check (RN-549) 6, 7 doesn't loosen a gate for the E2E to pass
documents.s: The sessions

documents.t: The api half is standing: runner_device_keys.project_id is nullable, the PatAuthGuard resolves the role against the requested project when the credential names none, and GET runner/projects exists. Two things the scope's measurement didn't anticipate and the implementation forced a decision on, both recorded in RN-543: The RN-519 listing started returning both kinds, marked. A machine key that appeared in no listing would be invisible and permanent — the defect RN-519 closed, reborn in the new kind. Revocation got a PLURAL target. revogar of a machine key has no projectId to pass to the engine; no longer bringing it down would reopen RN-520 across N connections. One {project, user} per project in the owner's runner mode, without touching the engine. And what remains declared, not done: no api route CREATES a machine key yet — whoever registers it is install.sh (ADR 0155 point 4), in session 6. The route is born in the PR that has the first real caller.
documents.s: What session 2 closed, and what it left declared

documents.t: The local agent opens N real connections, and the scope's measurement was confirmed: nothing in the engine changed, and the runner's handlers (tratarExec, tratarMirrorSync, tratarWorkspaceCreate) didn't change a line — what forced the design were the four PER-PROJECT fields of EstadoDoRunner, which became N states with docker and base shared by value. The old mode stayed byte for byte, and the new gate is narrow: machine credential and consented base. Three things the scope didn't anticipate, and RN-544 records them: One refused project doesn't bring down the others. The attempt ceiling and the join refusal stopped belonging to the PROCESS and started belonging to the PROJECT; only when none remain does the process exit with 1, with each one's outcome. In single-project mode the old behavior stays identical, by the inverted reasoning: with ONE connection, nothing remains to serve. The list is queried only at start. Re-querying would let a list that comes back SMALLER — deleted? converted? transient 500? — bring down a live connection through ambiguity. The process says so when it starts, and the gesture is to reconnect. An empty list is a NORMAL state, with exit 0. It is the state of every new installation, and Restart=on-abnormal doesn't bring it back up on purpose. (Revised when splitting session 6, RN-550: with ZERO connections the agent now STAYS UP and re-queries — the "only at start" half stays intact for whoever has a live connection.) And what remains declared, not done: the apiUrl in machine mode comes from --api-url/BRABO_API_URL/default, and never from brabo-runner.config.json, which is per PROJECT — whoever writes the flag is the per-machine unit, from session 4. The unit remains per project: this session changed the PROCESS, not the service.
documents.s: What session 3 closed, and the three decisions it had to make

documents.t: The fifth and last coupling of the table above closed: service install --machine installs brabo-runner.service / dev.brabo.runner, without a suffix, and brings up the process session 3 created. The per-project unit was neither removed nor renamed, Restart=on-abnormal stayed byte for byte (changing it would also undo session 3's decision to make an empty list exit with 0), and nothing in the api, the engine or the web was touched. One measurement changed the mechanism, and it contradicts the letter of ADR 0154 point 5. The ADR wrote "service install without --project installs the machine unit"; resolverProjeto has two sources, and today's normal path is to run install with no flag at all from inside the folder the browser configured — it is brabo-runner.config.json that answers. Taken literally, the ADR would silently convert the installation of whoever already uses the product, which is the opposite of what the same point 5 promises. So the discriminator became the --machine flag, explicit opt-in, with both project sources intact. The three decisions the scope left open, recorded in RN-545: status answers about the kind asked, and the code doesn't add up. The four states and the four codes (RN-088) don't become eight; the other kind appears in TEXT, as presence read from disk, saying its state was not asked of the manager. Without --machine and without a resolvable project, the answer is about the machine — the only unit whose name needs no argument. install REFUSES when the other kind is already installed. It removes nothing, writes nothing, and names the uninstall of each unit found. No --force: the two together would be two processes competing for the same project, and the server would deny one of them. Point 5's guarantee (an already installed unit keeps working) stays intact — what is refused is creating the overlap now. uninstall without a named kind removes nothing, and lists what exists. It doesn't inherit status's default on purpose: reading the wrong kind costs a wrong line, removing the wrong one costs a service and a key. Two refusals of install --machine's own weren't in the scope and are measured: the folder cannot have brabo-runner.config.json (the service would start in PROJECT mode, silently, serving only one) and the base must be consented to (without it the agent exits in uso() on first boot). The unit freezes XDG_CONFIG_HOME — it is what decides where the base file lives, and neither of the two managers passes on the shell's environment — but never the base's value. And what remains declared, not done: install --machine doesn't know whether the key in that folder really is a machine one (on disk both kinds are the same file, and whoever knows is the server), so a folder with a project key installs the unit without error and the refusal shows up on first boot. And nobody CREATES a machine key yet — that is session 6.
documents.s: What session 4 closed, and the three decisions it had to make

documents.t: Session 5 closed with a decision ADR 0155 hadn't faced, and it applies to whoever picks up session 6: provisionarUsuario refuses to run with NODE_ENV=production, and the installer runs exactly there. Instead of BRABO_FORCE_SEED, the core became ProvisionarUsuarioUseCase and the refusal stayed in the script — what it protects is a KNOWN password created WITHOUT human interaction, and the route is another category. Session 5 also added what the ADR didn't say and RN-410 requires: the personal workspace is born in the same transaction, otherwise the installation would close with a login that gets through and a dashboard where "New project" has nowhere to create.
documents.s: What session 5 closed, and the decision ADR 0155 didn't have

documents.t: The kind marker session 2 added to the listing — "without them in the list, a machine key would be invisible on every screen" — got a consumer. The runner onboarding panel now recognizes an active MACHINE key and, with it, stops telling you to pair: what is missing isn't pairing, it's the agent running. Nothing in the api, the engine or the runner was touched. The three decisions the scope left open, and what each became (RN-548 has the whole why): Where it appears: in the PANEL, and therefore in the three mounters at once — but not with the same result. Recognition is per PROJECT, because the route is GET /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys: TerminalPanel and FolderBrowserModal always have a project, and NewProjectWizard only after early creation (RN-437). Without projectId there is nobody to ask. AmbienteDoProjeto was CONSIDERED and refused: its docblock already declares that runner presence is first-hand knowledge of the channel, and a line about a registered key there would be a third proxy competing with a stronger signal — and about the MACHINE, not the project. With a key and no live connection — the most common case — the screen says the two things it knows and names the two it doesn't. It announces the pairing (with the key names and the date of last use), and next to it: a registered key is not an agent running and the list belongs to your ACCOUNT, not this browser. It is the workspaceVerifiedAt rule applied one step earlier, accent tone and never success included. The gesture it offers is to check the SERVICE on the paired machine, and whoever answers for the now is still EsperaDoRunner, reused. The kind appears through its COST, not as a label. The panel doesn't list keys nor revoke — it says a machine key serves every project of the owner, and that revoking it brings down the local agent in all of them. And what remains declared, not done: nobody CREATES a machine key yet (that's install.sh, session 6), so today the screen can only be exercised with a key registered by hand. The command offered is brabo-runner service status --project <id>, the form that exists today — the per-machine one arrives with the session 4 unit (closed later, AT-106: with a recognized machine key the panel offers brabo-runner service status --machine; with a project key, it keeps --project <id>). An active PROJECT key doesn't change the panel: that's the sibling defect, one scope below. And the screen to list/revoke keys still doesn't exist.
documents.s: What session 7 closed, and the three decisions it had to make

documents.t: Session 6 would touch apps/api, apps/runner and install.sh at once, and a delivery across three workspaces is where a session gets lost. It was split into three: the two pieces below, disjoint and in parallel, and install.sh after them, as orchestrator and nothing more — session 6 remains open, with that smaller scope. Neither of these two is a numbered session of the phase, and in particular neither is session 8, which is the E2E and remains open in the table above. The two pieces that were missing on the agent side, and both come from ADR 0155. The first is a REVISION of session 3, and the decision is ASYMMETRY (RN-550): with zero connections the agent stops exiting and starts WAITING, re-querying GET runner/projects at 15s/30s/60s until the first project appears; with a live connection, the list keeps being read only at start, byte for byte. Session 3's argument stays whole where it holds — a list that comes back SMALLER is ambiguous, and bringing down a live connection through ambiguity trades a certain state for a guess —, and with zero connections there is nothing to bring down. What fell was the exit 0 argument ("an active service that does nothing"), because the process started doing something and saying it does. Measured in this session: Restart=on-abnormal doesn't look at the exit code — it restarts on signal, watchdog or timeout —, so nothing in the two units changes, and the effect is that the machine unit is genuinely active (running). Waiting has no ceiling; failing does (ten queries in a row, exit 1 naming the number). The second closes the gap sessions 2, 3 and 4 declared — "nobody CREATES a machine key yet" — through the half that belongs to the agent (RN-551): brabo-runner device-key create|finish generates the Ed25519 pair on this machine. The decision here is the CUT: the CLI does not talk to the api, because whoever registers is the installer with the BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN, and giving that secret to the agent would widen what it can do far beyond what it needs — each side keeps a secret and neither sees the other's. From that follows the two-step design: the kid is the id of the REGISTRATION and only exists after it, so create writes a .parcial that the reader ignores and finish writes the real name. The file the runner reads never exists without a kid — the defect of RN-475, impossible by construction. What remains declared, not done: the ROUTE that registers the machine public key and the install.sh that chains the three commands are still session 6. And the API half of the same split (RN-552): POST /internal/machine-device-keys, engine-service, body { name, publicKeyJwk } and a response with the id that becomes the private key's kid (RN-475). The credential was decided and the cost is declared: the service token, because requiring a credential from the freshly created user would force the installer to open on the machine exactly the live session that ADR 0155 point 5 refused to open — and would give a second use to the password RN-546 discards on purpose. The price: a leaked BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN can now manufacture a lasting access credential, not just talk to internal routes. Three containments live in the route, not in the text: there is no userId in the body (the owner is the installation's SINGLE user, and zero or more than one is 409 without writing anything — RN-546's condition in another form, about the INSTALLATION and never about the argument); registering REPLACES the owner's active machine keys in the same transaction, so a reinstalled machine passes and a thousand keys are impossible by clause, with no number that ages; and a JWK with d is refused by name, with the shape rule becoming ONE, in the domain, called by both registrars. What remains declared, not done: in an installation without a PROJECT, no screen reaches a machine key — listing and revoking are both through /projects/:projectId/... —, and that is why registering replaces instead of leaving an orphan: an orphan there would be alive and unreachable.
documents.s: What the split of session 6 closed — and why it isn't session 8

documents.t: With the smaller scope, session 6 was orchestration and nothing more: no line of apps/ changed, no route was born, and the four pieces install.sh chains already existed, tested. The hole the phase opened at the start — "in a new installation nobody can get in" — closes here, and the promise of point 5 of ADR 0155 starts happening for real: the agent starts without a project, waits, and picks up the first one the person creates on the web. The four decisions, recorded in full in RN-547: When a middle link fails, nothing is undone and everything is reported — and the script always exits 0. The links already done are useful on their own (with the account the person gets in, with the key the machine is paired), undoing would require deleting an account and revoking a key, and there is no route for that nor should there be one the installer calls on its own. The price is an installation that may end halfway; what it never does is end halfway SILENTLY — each failure is a named line in a final block, with the command to repeat. Idempotency is the HTTP CODE, and 409 is not a failure. A second run, or a migration whose restore brought the users back: the step goes quiet saying why and doesn't enter the pending items. 000 — the curl that didn't talk to the api — has its own handling, otherwise "the api didn't come up" would be read as "the api refused". And the agent step only runs when THIS run created the account: with a pre-existing user, registering a machine key would mint a lasting credential for someone who asked for nothing in this round. The key's name is the hostname. RN-551 declared that the CLI doesn't name — it is a registration field, and whoever names is whoever registers. Whoever opens the key list needs to know WHICH machine to go to, and the hostname is the name the person already uses to talk about their machines. The .parcial left over when the registration doesn't close STAYS, and is named. Deleting it would be the installer deciding it knows something it doesn't: a timeout after the api writes is indistinguishable from one before, and the file may be the only copy of the private half of an already registered key. Two things changed that weren't in the scope. The password is sent through curl's STDIN, with the service token in a 600 --config — /proc/<pid>/cmdline is readable by any user on the machine, and a password in argv would be exposed during the request. And --help lied: it prints the header, which is a comment, and the rule forbidding talk of "phase sessions" to installers only read code lines — so "THIS VERSION INSTALLS NOTHING" survived for months after the script started bringing up compose and installing the runner. Fixed, with a test on the OUTPUT of --help, and the fixed range of lines that silently cut it became "up to the first line that isn't a comment". And what remains declared, not done: the end-to-end installation on a clean machine — real compose, real api, real runner binary, unit written and agent waiting — is session 8's E2E, and only it can prove it. In this session's tests brabo-runner is a shell stand-in and the api is a test server: what is proven is the CHAINING, never the integration. And install --machine still doesn't know whether the key in that folder really is a machine one (the gap of RN-545) — the difference is that now there is a path that CREATES a machine one there, so the refusal on first boot stopped being the probable outcome.
documents.s: What session 6 closed, and the four decisions it had to make

documents.t: The last of the phase, and the only one that could answer the question the whole phase pursues. Session 6 declared in writing that its tests prove the CHAINING and never the integration — brabo-runner a shell stand-in, a fake api —, and that is the gap that closes here. The harness wasn't born in this session: .github/workflows/install-e2e.yml has existed since FASE 29 (RN-534) and already ran the published installer on an ephemeral Actions runner, which is literally a clean machine. What it proved stopped at the .env. The session extended it, and what it proves now are the five links of RN-547 against a real api and binary, the agent standing and waiting, and the first project in Runner mode being picked up without anyone going back to the terminal. The three decisions, recorded in full in RN-549: The signal that "the agent is up" is the LINE it writes, never the manager's state. perguntarEstado maps activating to rodando — with reason (RN-088: "starting" is not "stopped") —, so systemctl is-active and service status --machine answer up for a process that is going to die two seconds later. The RN-550 line only exists after the agent has read the key from disk, taken a ticket, talked to the api and received an EMPTY list: it proves pairing and waiting at once, and it is a RECORDED FACT, not a sampling of state — that is why waiting for it with a ceiling isn't a race. status comes in after it, as confirmation, never in its place. The outcome is proven through the API, not the browser. The subject is the AGENT, and what it observes is GET /runner/projects. A browser would create the project through the same route with one more layer that fails for unrelated reasons — and wouldn't make the assertion stronger, because it would still be the journal line. The browser layer exists (e2e/, ADR 0120), answers another question and assumes the production compose is up: bringing it in would make the installer's E2E depend on a second harness on a machine that should be clean. The half that runs on PRs is a TEST, not the workflow. The E2E stays out of pull_request — opening that door would give the installer a way to skip the origin verification, which is what ADR 0150 refuses. But a workflow that runs on a tag is a workflow whose error shows up on the tag: scripts/dev/install-e2e.spec.ts guards the two ways it can rot silently — the loosened gate, and the install.sh sentence rewritten, which makes the assertions not fail but VANISH. Two defects showed up, both invisible because the workflow had never run. The first was in the harness and was fixed: the TTY answers file started with nao-migrar, which on a clean machine falls into the MARKER question — it doesn't match s|S|sim|SIM, the script said "Nothing was written" and exited 0, and the marker assertion would have failed. The second is a FINDING and stayed a finding: the published install.sh brings up nothing on its own on a clean machine — it uses docker/docker-compose.install.yml, which isn't a Release asset, doesn't enter the signed checksums.txt and it doesn't download anywhere (with ./postgres/init.sql included, that's three files). Whoever follows the runbook's curl … install.sh dies at "no such file or directory" after having already verified the signature and written the .env. The workflow brings them by hand, from the tag, in a step that says it's a finding; fixing it means deciding between a signed asset and a clone, and it's a delivery of its own. And what remains declared, not done: this E2E doesn't run on the PR that wrote it — the first real run is the next final tag, and no PR check proves a line of it. Left out, by decision: the second run through the MIGRATION path (RN-530), macOS (the full step is Linux — launchd, and the Docker the hosted runner doesn't have) and the browser. Reserved range: RN-543..555. ADRs 0154 and 0155. RN-541 is already allocated in an unmerged branch — the jump is deliberate, by the criterion FASE 29 recorded when it resolved three collisions by date.
documents.s: What session 8 closed — and the three decisions it had to make

documents.t: Eight sessions, plus the two pieces that came out of splitting session 6 and are not numbered sessions. What the phase promised at the start — install Brabo in one line and use it — started happening: The local agent's identity stopped being per PROJECT and became the MACHINE's. The two couplings the scope's measurement said needed to change did change: runner_device_keys.project_id is nullable (RN-543) and the unit is one per machine (RN-545). The other three didn't change, and the measurement that saved them is the phase's most useful finding: topic, socket id and ticket describe a CONNECTION, and N connections satisfy them byte for byte. Nothing in the engine changed. RunnerReadiness (RN-507), the mirror (RN-516) and workspace_create (RN-532) stayed byte for byte, and so did the runner's handlers. A new installation stopped being born with nobody inside. MAIL_TRANSPORT is still log and the installer still doesn't turn on SMTP — what changed is that the first account is born in the TERMINAL, already verified (RN-546/RN-547), with the personal workspace in the same transaction. Fishing for a verification link in docker compose logs api stopped being the path. The agent comes up paired and WAITS. The Ed25519 pair is born on the machine (RN-551), only the public key travels (RN-552), the registration id becomes the kid (the invariant of RN-475, now impossible to violate by construction), and with zero projects the process stays up re-querying (RN-550) instead of exiting. The screen recognizes who is already paired (RN-548), without ever claiming the agent is running — a registered key proves pairing, not a live process. And the whole is measured end to end (RN-549), against a real api and binary, on a clean machine. What the phase did not close is right below, in "Gaps the phase touches and doesn't solve", and none of them changed size along the way — except the key list/revoke SCREEN one, which became larger on purpose: the phase added a kind of key to list and didn't build the screen. Add to that the compose finding session 8 measured, and the install --machine gap, which still doesn't know whether the key in that folder really is a machine one — on disk both kinds are the same file, and whoever knows is the server.
documents.s: What the phase delivered, as a whole

documents.t: Declared in both ADRs, and repeated here because it is what gives meaning to the rest: decide.ts and the absolute ceilings — none gets an exception, not even a configurable one proposed_action as the origin of every external effect of an agent; creating a folder and pairing an agent remain consented configuration, not agent action (the RN-516 line) the immutability of the event log RunnerReadiness (RN-507) and its three preconditions — and never a "skip container" flag, for the reason in ADR 0147 point 4 the mirror (RN-515/516/517) and workspace_create (RN-532): both are per project and travel in the join grant of that connection normal registration with email verification, and the MAIL_TRANSPORT=log default the browser configuration flow (ADR 0118)
documents.s: What this phase does NOT touch

documents.t: Revocation still reaches {project, user}, never {key} (RN-520) — and it now costs more: revoking brings down the agent in all the projects of that machine. FASE 29 declared this cost in advance; here it arrives. Closing it requires changing the revocation's target, which is its own front. There is no screen where device keys are listed and revoked. RN-519 opened the GET in the api; the web never got the screen. The phase adds a kind of key to list and doesn't build the screen — the gap gets larger, and declared. RN-548 starts CONSUMING that listing in the onboarding panel, which doesn't close it: reading to recognize is something else than listing to revoke. Single point of failure. One process per machine instead of N: the service going down takes the agent out of every project. It's the price of the design, not carelessness. The git credential remains discarded in docker exec in runner mode (ADR 0145) — this phase doesn't touch it, and nothing here makes it worse. BRB-031 closes by maintainer decision, not as a consequence: the phase creates the path without chmod and keeps the browser one. Choosing to retire the second is a separate decision. BRB-017 (GPL obligation of the engine image, P1) stays where it was, and this phase makes it more concrete for the same reason as FASE 29: more installations on third-party machines.
documents.s: Gaps the phase touches and doesn't solve

documents.t: A gate is a point in the flow where work stops until someone — person, agent, or script — says it can proceed. The product has thirteen, and until PHASE 15a none of them existed as a list: they were scattered across pure rules, use cases, tests and CI workflows. Answering "which gates exist" required reading six files. docs/gates.yml is that list. This document explains what it is, and — more importantly — what it is not.
documents.s: The gates, and how they're measured

documents.t: No gate becomes enforced because of the file. Changing severidade in it doesn't change any behavior: who blocks a merge is still decide.ts, who judges a PR is still the QA agent, who fails a backmerge is still the CI workflow. It's the easiest assumption to get wrong, so it's worth repeating: the registry is an index, not policy. The branching policy still lives in branching-policy.md; the entrada and entregavel fields are a sentence in Portuguese, and onde points to the code that really governs. What the registry buys is something else: making gates enumerable. The lesson from Phases 10 and 13 — metric extracted by script, never annotated by hand — can't be applied to what can't be listed.
documents.s: The registry describes; it doesn't execute

documents.t: verificacao answers how you prove this gate passed, not who judges it. script means there's a mechanical artifact — an event, a test, a job — that serves as proof. That's why qa-verificada is script even though it's an LLM issuing the verdict: the artifact is the pr.gate_changed with veredito. Who judges lives in dono. aprovacao_humana: true means the decision belongs to the user — directly by a click, or delegated by a policy the user wrote themselves. That's what lets acao-aprovada coexist with status: auto_approved: the policy deciding on its own is the user having decided beforehand. merge-protegida is the case where not even delegation exists, because the ceiling downgrades auto_approve to require_approval even with autonomy on. In the four gates the constitution declares manual, this field is invariant and locked by a test (RN-071).
documents.s: The two fields that age if left undefined

documents.t: type when what the locator brings event_log the outcome becomes a domain event event types + payload filter teste the guarantee is an assertion spec path ci the gate lives in the repository workflow + spec The two cases that forced the field to exist: merge-protegida doesn't emit its own event. It's a ceiling applied last on top of the already-computed verdict, which downgrades auto_approve to require_approval; the outcome shows up as a pending proposed_action.created, indistinguishable from any other pending item. What guarantees the block is the test. backmerge lives outside the application: it's a required check, with state versioned in .release/gate.json on main. Without evidencia, the rule "a block gate without proof fails" would turn the product's two hardest locks permanently red.
documents.s: Three forms of evidence, because not every proof lives in the log

documents.t: The registry is validated in two layers, and the split is not cosmetic: layer what it asserts who runs it validarRegistro claims about the content — block needs script, the four human gates stay human, active needs evidence, no duplicate id, no orphan entrada anyone who reads the registry, including the api at runtime validarLocalizadores the teste/ci target file exists the test against the real file, and phase 2 of validacao-gates.ts — never the api The first is true wherever the registry is read. The second is a claim about the repository, and it only makes sense inside a checkout. The two used to be one function, and the api's loader called it. The consequence was measured on the installed v6.1.0: GET /gates answered 500 with RegistroDeGatesInvalido listing all eleven targets as "does not exist" — twelve 5xx responses in about 55 minutes. Nothing was wrong with the registry. The production image carries /app/docs/gates.yml and nothing else from docs/; apps/api/test/, scripts/ci/ and .github/ never enter it, so a repository claim evaluated against that tree fails for every gate, in every installation. Nothing was loosened. The rule still exists, still covers the same targets, and a target that disappears still fails — it just runs where the question means something. Two guards keep it that way: the test that climbs to the repository root and checks every locator, and a loader test that rebuilds the image's tree on disk (a root with docs/gates.yml and nothing else) and asserts the registry loads. Putting the check back in the loader turns that second one red with the exact message the installation produced. And the api serving the registry is now exercised against the production image: docker/smoke.sh calls GET /gates and GET /internal/gates (service token) and requires the registry back from both. The body check is one shell function, checar_registro_de_gates, which scripts/ci/smoke-gates.spec.ts runs against the three bodies without bringing the stack up. No unit suite could have caught the original failure — vitest and ExUnit run from a checkout, where the targets exist.
documents.s: Two validations, and only one of them runs in production

documents.t: qa-verificada and secops-segura are not two event types: both record pr.gate_changed, discriminated by payload.gate. Worse — the same type is recorded when the gate opens, without a veredito. A registry that stored only the type name would count opening as passing and measure double what actually happened. Hence the filter, and hence the veredito: presente sentinel. The same applies to the two infra PR gates, which share infra.gate_changed. The test asserts that no pair (event_types + filtro) repeats in the registry. That uniqueness is what makes the measurement mean anything. The filter only reaches the payload, on purpose: accepting an arbitrary column in the YAML would open up the entire query. Who promoted a story — a person or the PO — lives in the actor_kind column and stays outside the declarative vocabulary.
documents.s: The shared-type trap

documents.t: pnpm --filter api validacao:gates # full report pnpm --filter api validacao:gates -- --sem-banco # registry and locators only pnpm --filter api validacao:gates -- --projeto <uuid> Three phases, in this order: registry (loads and validates), locators (does the teste/ci target exist?) and event log (latest passage, with event id). The first two never touch the database — that's what makes the script useful in CI without Postgres. Phase 2 reports every locator in the registry, not just the ones on active+block gates. It used to have its own narrower loop while the api's loader had a wider one, and rag-acertivo — active, warn, citing both a workflow and a test — never showed up in the table. One rule now, validarLocalizadores, shared with the test. exit code when 0 valid registry and locators in place 1 invariant violated, target missing, or gate with no passage when --projeto was given 2 invalid usage The asymmetry is deliberate. Registry and locators are claims about the repository: they always hold. Event-log evidence is a claim about an execution, and only exists if one happened — without --projeto, phase 3 is just a report. Requiring a passage on a freshly created database would make the script exit 1 always, and a script that always fails becomes noise nobody reads.
documents.s: Measuring

documents.t: Before measuring anything, writing the list found two things nobody was seeing: QA and SecOps's judgment on infra PRs, which has its own path (infra.gate_changed, with no backlog task behind it) and wasn't in the spec; promotion-check was a required check with no spec of its own, unlike pr-police and approval-ladder. The evidence pointed to the script, with the gap written right there, and the item went to triage — the phase declares and measures, it doesn't fix. Triage closed it: scripts/ci/promotion-check.spec.ts exists, and the gate's evidence now points to it. It's the cycle working as designed — enumerating found it, triage prioritized it, another phase fixed it. The third finding came from the measurer's first run: the story-promovida filter pointed at actor_kind, which is a column and not payload, and the gate showed up as "never passed" on a database where it had passed hours before. A registry nobody runs is a registry that lies.
documents.s: What enumerating already paid off

documents.t: implementavel (owner dev-lead) was born planned in PHASE 14d, alongside the rest of the target org chart that docs/gates.yml/ docs/fluxo.yml already described with no code behind it. The ADR 0090 activated it — and the exercise is worth using as an example because nothing about the registry's shape changed: status: planned → active plus the evidencia block (pointing to proposed_action.created filtered by actionType: assess_implementability) are the ONLY two lines a warn gate needs to gain to stop being an aspiration. severidade stays warn — the comment in the file already said "born warn even when activated," and activating isn't the same decision as promoting to block (that would require measuring real passages first, same discipline as PHASE 15a). The real work sits outside the file: the Dev Lead needed a new tool (assess_implementability) that proposes the assessment as a proposed_action, and QA-strategy — until then a proposto role in docs/fluxo.yml, with the separation criterion already written there ("can be the qa-lead itself in a second moment") — had to exist to feed the assessment with a real test plan. The registry only started describing what the code now does. That input did not survive real use. ADR 0192 (RN-674) moved the test plan to AFTER the dev's delivery — written PRE-DEV it had no code to read and ran out of iterations — and the gate's entrada changed from plano-de-teste to module_map: the Dev Lead judges the story and the module map it already has. The plan now feeds qa-verificada, as input to the one verdict that gate already gives. Same lesson in the other direction: the registry line changed because WHO DELIVERS WHAT TO WHOM changed, not to make a gate pass.
documents.s: Activating a planned gate is the same work as any other

documents.t: implementavel is the example of a gate that needed new code to leave planned. paralelismo-autorizado is the opposite: the mechanism (RequestParallelizationUseCase, RN-083) has been in production since PHASE 14d — it was the registry that fell behind, declaring planned over something that was already active in the sibling docs/fluxo.yml and in the code. The fluxo.yml × code audit (finding A1/B5, auditoria-fluxo-vs-codigo.md) found the divergence; the fix was just the same two lines implementavel also gained — status: active plus evidencia pointing to proposed_action.created filtered by actionType: parallelize. Worth noting why this changed nothing on the team panel's PR track: paralelismo-autorizado is fluxo: execucao, and the screen only derives steps from fluxo: pr gates (see "Consumption" below) — a gate can become active in the registry without appearing anywhere in the UI, if its flow is a different one.
documents.s: A registry can age in the wrong direction — stale, not inactive

documents.t: implementavel and paralelismo-autorizado are the two examples of a gate that already existed (declared planned or stale) and gained its registry entry AFTERWARD. necessidade-validada (RN-406, ADR 0095) is the third pattern: mechanism and registry were born in the SAME change, because the gate itself didn't exist anywhere — not planned in the file, nor code behind it. The choice of severidade: warn follows the same reasoning as implementavel, but for a different reason. implementavel is warn because promoting to block would require measuring real passages first (PHASE 15a). necessidade-validada is warn because NOTHING in the product today checks its passage before letting the PO continue — the Creative→PO handoff already happens inside confirm_readiness, before this gate even exists. block would promise a lock that doesn't exist; warn describes exactly what the gate is: a measurement that a human validated the need's merit, not a gate that blocks the next step. workspace-verificado (RN-423, ADR 0104) is the fourth example, and the clearest of the four about why warn isn't a "weak lock": what really locks things down HERE isn't the gate, it's the explicit refusal in Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor.decisao_de_execucao/1 — without a verified workspace or a connected runner, the command is refused unconditionally, deep inside the code, without going through the registry. The gate exists only to give EVIDENCE of when the confirmation happened (project.workspace_verified in the event log); promoting it to block would describe a lock that already exists somewhere else, the same way necessidade-validada would have lied about one that doesn't exist anywhere. rag-acertivo (RN-490/RN-498, ADR 0132/ADR 0138) is the fifth example, and the reason it stays warn changed shape once, which is worth telling in full. It was born warn for the plainest reason of the five: there was no CI that ran a real LLM — the golden-set it measures (17 questions composed from real RNs/ADRs, checked against a curated real corpus through the actual HybridSearchUseCase) only ran by hand (mix golden_set.rag), the same posture the QA Automation golden-set (ADR 0123) still carries today. That stopped being true: .github/workflows/golden-set-rag.yml now runs mix golden_set.rag for real, against a real Ollama service — it only calls the embedding model, CPU, deterministic, never a chat model doing judgment. (The claim that the QA golden-set was not tractable the same way was later measured, and the clock turned out not to be the obstacle — see the next section.) What kept severidade: warn from becoming stale isn't that the gate stayed manual — it's that the workflow is scheduled (nightly cron plus workflow_dispatch), never triggered by pull_request. block would still promise a check that gates a merge, and a scheduled run gates nothing: a regression becomes visible within a day, never at PR time. The reason moved from "no CI can run this" to "this CI doesn't sit on the merge path" — warn keeps describing exactly what's true, just not the same truth it described before.
documents.s: A gate can be born active directly — when the mechanism and the registry arrive together

documents.t: The golden-set of the QA Automation agent's semantic judgment (ADR 0123) is what would give qa-verificada's semantic step a trend signal. ADR 0123 and ADR 0138 both stated, without measuring, that running it in CI needed an API LLM secret or new infrastructure (a GPU runner). On 2026-09-13 (AT-067) it was measured, in the exact mold of golden-set-rag.yml: ubuntu-latest, no GPU, the same pinned pgvector and ollama service images, qwen2.5-coder:latest pulled into the job's own Ollama (with the dev compose's OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=1h/OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=16384), the api and the engine up as servers — the engine is extra relative to the RAG job, because it is the engine, called by the api through POST /internal/actions/execute, that runs the npm test the QA asks for. run model pull setup until the mix task mix golden_set.qa whole job score 34769447405 15 s ~3 min 19 min 15 s 22 min 09 s 0/6 34770869429 13 s ~3 min 22 min 53 s 25 min 45 s 0/6 A chat turn of the 7B model on that runner's CPU took a median of ~20 s (10–34 s over the 23 turns the api log kept). The clock fits: a nightly or weekly job of under half an hour, no secret, no GPU. The "new infrastructure" half of the old sentence is refuted by measurement. What does not fit is the instrument. Both runs scored 0/6, below the recorded floor of 1/6 — and not because of the model's judgment. The event log of the second run shows why: every npm test the QA proposed was auto-approved (permissions.json allow: npm test) and then refused by the engine, because since RN-502 (ADR 0143, 2026-09-04) a container project with no running container does not run terminal commands anywhere. The seed script dates from 2026-08-30 and never registers a container. So no case can ever see exit 0, and emit_qa_verdict refuses approved without one — three of the six expected verdicts became impossible. The refusal message says "bring the project's container up (Infra proposes container_start)", and the model did what it read: in three cases it asked the terminal for container_start or docker-compose up (left pending, so awaiting_approval), and in one it repeated npm test sixty times until toolloop.limit_reached (blocked(modelo)). The remaining two stalled on their first call with an empty command — the unreliability ADR 0123 already recorded for this model, independent of RN-502. Nothing here is CI-specific: the same refusal applies to a local run. That is why no golden-set-qa.yml was committed. A scheduled workflow that is red on every run for a reason unrelated to what it measures is worse than none — background red teaches people to ignore red. The design that was measured stays in the repository history (the workflow as of commit e7d7d1b16, including a temporary diagnostic step). Making it measure again meant deciding how the golden-set runs the suite under RN-502, and that was a decision for a human. Relaxing the refusal so the harness passes was never one of the options: it would weaken the isolation RN-502 exists for, to make a test pass.
documents.s: The QA golden-set in CI: the clock fits, the instrument measures, and it runs weekly

documents.t: On 2026-09-27 the maintainer chose the first path: the seed brings up a real container through the broker and registers it running, by the production path. RN-502 is untouched; what changed is that the seed now satisfies its precondition. For each case, after cloning the skeleton into the project's managed folder, apps/api/scripts/golden-set-qa-container.ts walks the same use cases a real project walks, in its own consultiva session: CreateModuleMapUseCase (one module), RouteModulesToInfraUseCase (one candidate image), ProposeActionUseCase for container_start with actor agent/infra, and ApproveActionUseCase as the project owner. The approval runs ExecuteContainerStartUseCase, which records the election as a new artifact.project_image through DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase (so validarDecisaoDeImagem judges the image), calls ContainerBrokerPort.start and registers provisioning → running through the state machine. The seed proposes and approves instead of calling the execution use case directly because two rules live on the proposal side — the named 409 sem_broker_na_instalacao (RN-591) and decide()'s policy for container_start — and a harness that skipped them would stop following production the day either changed. The image is node:24.11.1-bookworm-slim, pinned by the multi-platform index digest in the seed (the ADR 0159 rule, although that file sits outside the trees imagens-pinadas.ts scans). Debian rather than Alpine because the broker keeps the container alive with sleep infinity. The geometry that makes the three sides see the same code: the worktree is the managed project folder (projectScopeRoot), the broker mounts <PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT>/<workspace_dir_name> at /work, and the engine translates the QA's cwd into /work before the exec. In the CI job the api, the engine and the broker all run natively on the runner, so PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT (api, engine) and PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT (broker) are the same path; the broker is the only process that talks to Docker. A case whose container does not come up now fails the seed with ContainerDoGoldenSetNaoSubiuError, naming the step and the reason the product gave, and the ExUnit module fails when the api is up but the seed fails. Before, it returned {:skip, _} from the test body — which ExUnit does not treat as a skip: the test passed, green, having measured nothing. Measured with a temporary push-triggered workflow on the branch (removed before the PR, as AT-067 did): run model pull image pull container up (proposal → executed) mix golden_set.qa whole job score 36291440108 15 s 6 s 0.20–0.28 s per case 48 min 29 s 52 min 38 s 3/6 36294037297 15 s 6 s 0.22–0.30 s per case 83 min 16 s 86 min 16 s 3/6 Against the three criteria, in both runs: the event log has zero RN-502 refusals (no terminal action and no session event mentions it); npm test ran inside the container with exit 0 in five of the six cases in the first run and in all six in the second (the gaps are empty commands the broker refused by name — the model unreliability ADR 0123 already recorded); and the score is reported as it came, 3/6 twice, against the floor of 1/6. case expected 36291440108 36294037297 rf-covered approved ✓ approved ✓ approved rf-uncovered changes_requested ✓ changes_requested ✓ changes_requested rf-single-clean approved ✗ changes_requested ✗ blocked(modelo) rf-mismatched-filename approved ✗ changes_requested ✓ approved rf-partial-coverage changes_requested ✗ blocked(modelo) ✗ blocked(modelo) rf-skipped-test changes_requested ✓ changes_requested ✗ approved Same total, different cases: the misses are now the model's judgment and its variance, which is what the golden-set exists to measure — rf-skipped-test approved once, counting a test.skip as coverage, and rf-single-clean ran npm test 30 times in the second run before ending blocked(modelo). The runs got longer (48 and 83 min against 19–23 min) because the cases now do the work: they read files and reason about coverage instead of stopping at the refusal, and a case that repeats itself now repeats real executions. A scheduled job needs a timeout-minutes above the 86 min seen here. Two things were seen and not changed here: the api→broker call has a 5 s ceiling for every operation, start included, so a container_start whose image is not yet in the daemon would time out while the pull continues (the job pulls the image first; not measured without it); and the engine's heartbeat closed the idle sessions (heartbeat_timeout) about 30 s after the seed, while the QA kept proposing and running commands in them (the QA runs in the mix process, outside any session process), with no visible effect on the round.
documents.s: The decision, and the second measurement (AT-076)

documents.t: On 2026-09-27 the maintainer chose the cadence: weekly (ADR 0168). .github/workflows/golden-set-qa.yml is the AT-076 design made permanent — api, engine and broker native on the runner, only the broker talking to Docker, the same managed folder on the three sides — on schedule plus workflow_dispatch, never pull_request, the same posture as golden-set-rag.yml. Weekly and not nightly like the RAG job, for two measured reasons. The RAG run costs ~20 minutes and is deterministic, so yesterday's drop is a real drop. This one costs 52 to 86 minutes and varies: the two AT-076 runs reached the same 3/6 through different cases. A nightly run would spend hours of runner a week to read the same trend with more noise; one run a week is what the ratchet floor needs to show a fall, and workflow_dispatch answers right away after a change to the QA prompt or the seed. It runs on Saturday at 01:17 UTC: away from the RAG's daily 06:00, the property proofs' Sunday 04:00 and the external-link check's Monday 06:00; on Saturday so that a red run waits for the week to start; at minute 17 because Actions delays, and may drop, schedules at the top of the hour. timeout-minutes is 150: the 86 min measured plus room for a run in which more than one case hits the iteration ceiling. That is the model's variance, and the job does not measure the clock. The verdict is the test's own: below the passRate that floor.json records for the model, ExUnit fails. The workflow only adds two instrument guards — the score line must exist (the test skips when the api is down, and a skip in an unattended run is a green that measured nothing) and the event log must hold no RN-502 refusal (the AT-067 signature) — and on failure it prints the logs, as the RAG job does. The image to pre-pull is read from the seed's own constant (IMAGEM_DO_GOLDEN_SET_QA), not from a second literal: the broker's docker run runs under the Docker port's 30 s control ceiling (RN-604), and a job that pulled one image while the seed asked for another would put the pull inside that ceiling. The proof run, with a temporary push trigger on the branch removed before the PR: run model pull image pull mix golden_set.qa whole job score 36327281774 15 s 5 s 10 min 13 s 13 min 41 s 3/6 Zero RN-502 refusals in the event log, all six containers running before the first case. The same 3/6 once more, through yet another set of cases — rf-covered, rf-uncovered and rf-skipped-test hit; rf-single-clean and rf-mismatched-filename got changes_requested where approved was expected, and rf-partial-coverage was approved with partial coverage. The run took a sixth of the AT-076 ones (10 against 48–83 minutes of mix golden_set.qa): no case this time repeated itself until the iteration ceiling. The timeout stays sized by the slowest run measured, not the fastest.
documents.s: Scheduled, weekly (AT-149)

documents.t: deployavel is the fourth pattern, and the least flattering: it was declared as area-infra's gate_saida in docs/fluxo.yml and was absent from docs/gates.yml altogether — not planned, not stale, simply not there. The team model has three pieces (catalogue, flow, registry) and nothing yet cross-checks them, so a gate can be a deliverable in one and not exist in another. This is the second finding of that shape; the first was paralelismo-autorizado ageing in the opposite direction. It enters as planned/warn, with no evidencia block and no verification script, because RN-070/ RN-071 forbid block without one — and because what blocks it is not code. The infrastructure exists (overlays, GHCR images by digest, smoke/rollout/restore scripts); what is missing is a production environment with real traffic and someone maintaining it. See ADR 0153, which also stops ten documents from citing DEPLOY_ENABLED as if it were a variable that exists in the code.
documents.s: A gate can be missing from the registry while fluxo.yml already assigns it

documents.t: The PR track on the panel — Dev → QA → SecOps → You — used to be a list written into the component. Since PHASE 15b it comes from the registry, via GET /gates. What changes in practice is one property, not the appearance: a gate that leaves the registry leaves the screen on its own. Before, deactivating SecOps left a dead step on the track until someone remembered to edit the code — exactly the kind of aging that motivated the registry to exist. Three decisions worth explaining: The route is separate from the internal one. /internal/gates is service-to-service, with a service token, and serves the measurement script; /gates belongs to the logged-in user and serves the screen. Same registry, different audiences. No projectId. The registry is a fact about the PRODUCT: the same gates apply to every project. Attaching it to a project would suggest it's possible to have different gates per project, which is exactly what ADR 0054 deliberately left undecided. Only active gates. A planned gate describes a future role (dev-lead, platform). On a screen that says what's happening now, it would appear as if it were happening.
documents.s: Consumption: the screen derives, it doesn't repeat

documents.t: Each step's label (QA, You) and which step each gate represents stay in the component. It's not an inconsistency: the registry describes policy, and what to call things for the user is a screen decision. What left it was the LIST — which steps exist. A PR gate the registry brings that the screen doesn't yet know how to draw is ignored, with a test asserting it: an undefined step in the middle of the track would be worse than its absence.
documents.s: What the screen still decides on its own

documents.t: ADR 0054 — the decision ADR 0048 — the decision in the event log, without which there'd be nothing to measure RN-070, RN-071

documents.t: Immutable record of Brabo's completed phases, moved from CLAUDE.md on 2026-08-23 without rewriting. The product's CURRENT state lives in CLAUDE.md, in the RNs (docs/business-rules.md) and in the ADRs — this file answers "how we got here", never "what holds today". An accepted ADR is never edited; the ADR corrections recorded in this text remain valid where they are.
documents.s: Phase history

documents.t: FASE 1 (MVP) — COMPLETED: IAM/RBAC, sessions with an immutable event log, chat with an LLM router (Ollama + APIs), token metering/budget, proposed_actions pipeline + permissions.json, Elixir/OTP engine with supervision and a termination event. FASE 2 — COMPLETED: GitProvider (Local/GitHub/GitLab) with a contract suite and capabilities, encrypted credentials, idempotent Gitflow bootstrap resumable through the pipeline, wizard with live progress. FASE 3 — COMPLETED: Harness (PromptAssembler, ToolLoop, ContextManager, InstructionFiles, Hooks), explicit handoffs, Criativo, PO and Arquiteto agents with artifacts and validations in the domain. FASE 4 — COMPLETED: execution agents (dynamic per-module devs in isolated worktrees, QA and SecOps as PR gates, proactive Infra), protected-merge lock, live team panel; real Psicólogo and Anamnese with a closed loop. Gates validated by real execution (ADR 0020). FASE 5 — COMPLETED: non-root production images and CI (ADR 0024), Kubernetes with Kustomize, HPA by Oban queue, NetworkPolicies and ESO (ADR 0025), graceful shutdown + OpenTelemetry + dashboards (ADR 0026), backup with tested restore, runbooks and hardening (ADR 0027). FASE DOC — COMPLETED: docs/ as the single source with Diátaxis, a Docusaurus site in website/ reading from docs/, generated references, docs/.docmap.yml + drift check (docs:check) in CI, a community layer, MIT verified, mechanism documented in docs/explanation/documentation-workflow.md. FASE 6 — COMPLETED: mechanized branch policy (ADR 0030) — pr-police, approval-ladder with both modes, promote/tag-release with a calculated version and a tree anchor, backmerge gate with automatic back-propagation, versioned rulesets. Pipeline exercised end to end (v0.1.0 → v0.2.0) and the hotfix chain validated by real execution. FASE 7 — COMPLETED: first-party auth replacing Keycloak — argon2id, Ed25519 access, refresh rotation with family revocation, progressive lockout, account tokens and a log-only MailSender (ADR 0031, RN-030..033); atomic cutover with its own issuer, RBAC untouched, /internal/* with a service token, httpOnly cookie + CSRF, user migration and total removal of Keycloak (ADR 0032, RN-034/035); OpenAPI on the 23 controllers with type-locked DTOs, a table test requiring metadata, docs/reference/api/ generated with a hash manifest (ADR 0033). FASE 8 — COMPLETED WITH A CUT: agent hierarchy — areas with a single lead as the external contact, private internal delegations (table delegations, area as TEXT), consolidated verdict with traceability, failure with origin; QA as an area (Lead + Automation + Performance/Security, the gates' external contract unchanged — the Fase 4 suite green without modification); Infra as an area with a Workflows subagent generating CI per provider; team panel by area and Psicólogo/Anamnese targeting subagents (ADR 0038). SCOPE CUT of the time, REVOKED by FASE 14d: agent_areas/agent_area_members exist since then, per project, with configurable max_parallel — it was the dev area, the first DYNAMIC one, that forced it. What remains cut is only the budget per area (real budget ceilings remain project, session and task). The apps/web/src/lib/agents.ts list survived for color, icon and the addressing RULE; dev members come from the table. FASE 9 — COMPLETED: LLMProvider contract suite running against the existing ones, OpenAICompatibleProvider base on node:http with an INACTIVITY timeout, error normalized by code, capabilities in two layers (ADR 0041); catalog sync with a discovered model coming in disabled, a vanished model marked instead of deleted, price frozen in token_usage with append-only auditing (ADR 0042); ModelPicker regrouped by origin with curation. The six 9b providers came in through Fase 11 (ADR 0043). FASE 10 — COMPLETED: Bitbucket + GenericGitProvider delivered VIA dogfooding (the first real run of Brabo building Brabo itself, in a fork with a manual seed, batches with a restart between tasks, Criativo mandatory in the chain). Harvest written in Fase 12d, in docs/explanation/primeiro-dogfooding.md — the 17 findings with file:line are real; the QUANTITATIVE half (restarts, interventions, cost) stayed as não medido, because the observation table was never filled in. The three operability P1s were closed by Fase 12. The other 14 remain open and listed in the harvest — don't fix them in passing. FASE 11 — COMPLETED: the six Fase 9b providers as config on top of the base, each one investigated from scratch against the official docs (inheriting quirks forbidden); LLM_PROVIDER_NAMES from 3 to 9; credential DTO and connection tester deriving from a single list; capability only declared when proven, with two live reversals (DeepInfra and Vultr); a single new hook in the base (parseErrorFrame, +31 lines) proven necessary by OpenRouter (ADR 0043). Pending smokes with a real credential: absorbed by FASE 13. FASE 12 — COMPLETED: post-dogfooding operability, the three P1 findings closed and proven in a single run (ADR 0047). 12a — adoption of an existing repository: its own route, getRepo validating access before writing, origin (created|adopted) in both tables, and the PLAN as the gate — a dry-run that describes the divergence and changes nothing while the decision is null; re-adopting converges (ADR 0044, RN-045/046). 12b — event-driven rescheduling of the dev agent: a persisted state machine (working|awaiting_gate|idle|idle_tripped) reacting to two events of the existing outbox, awaiting_gate retaining the worktree (which is per AGENT, not per task) until the gate ends, and a circuit breaker with explicit rearm (ADR 0045, RN-047). 12c — story promotion with the user's authority: story_promotion per project with manual as the NEW DEFAULT (a targeted backfill puts the existing projects in auto), proposed_ready as a proposal and not a state, promotion reusing TransitionStoryUseCase (dead code from finding #13) and refusal returning to the PO with the reason pinned in its session (ADR 0046, RN-048). 12d — the Noop entered the 12b state machine; the script pnpm --filter api validacao:fase-12 that exits != 0 when the criterion doesn't close and extracts the evidence from the database; Fase 10 harvest written; docmap covering engine/dev and engine/agents. Pending items (running the validation; Local/Noop limits declared): absorbed by FASE 13. Don't refactor what is done without an explicit request.
