documents.t: No new feature. The phase closes the declared pending items, proves what the Local/Noop validation admittedly doesn't prove, and turns the 19 open findings into a prioritized plan. Lesson incorporated: the manual table of Fase 10 was never filled in — in this phase EVERY metric is extracted by script from the event log/token_usage, never noted by hand.
documents.s: FASE 13 — COMPLETED on 2026-08-07 (prove it for real and triage)

documents.t: COMPLETED on 2026-08-07: pnpm --filter api validacao:fase-12 exits 0 and the table of event ids is in docs/explanation/validacao-fase-12.md (the TODO(humano) came out). It cost four fixes — three to the INSTRUMENT (the guinea pig was born in /tmp, invisible to the engine; the Noop didn't open the gate; the Noop died at pr_settled) and one to the PRODUCT (finding W: the dev agent died when the queue emptied). PARTIAL on 2026-08-07: the OpenRouter smoke ran with a real credential and closed (real cost US$ 0.000005, read from token_usage). The other five remain skipped — there is no key for them in the environment. The smoke had rotted against ADR 0049 and had never run; fixed along with it. Dated result in docs/explanation/aceite-providers.md
documents.s: 13a — Close the declared pending items

documents.t: The whole chain proven against REAL GitHub (daneiel/test), in ten runs: remote adoption → plan with the user's decision → manual promotion of ONE story → real dev agent writing code → commit, push and REMOTE PR → gate opens → area delegates and dismisses with justification → subagent SUSPENDS on approval → the user's refusal RESUMES the loop → changes_requested verdict by LLM. Zero engine restarts. Merge out, by design (RN-014). 3. The script is pnpm --filter api validacao:real, with phases split by COST (--ate adocao|backlog|execucao) — the cheap one runs alone first, and that is how configuration errors showed up before costing money. It requires running FROM INSIDE the api container: the policy is a file in a shared volume, and from the host it is born in a filesystem the engine doesn't see. 4. pnpm --filter api medir:execucao is the instrument, and it is PROVEN: it reproduces on its own the numbers the previous dogfooding had noted by hand (18 calls, 292,211 tokens, ~US$ 0.03). 5. Result in docs/explanation/validacao-real.md, with the ten runs and what each one taught. SEVEN P1s closed along the way, all found by EXECUTION and none by test: W (dev agent died with an empty queue), Y (the search didn't distinguish empty from not-found), AA (git credential resolved by whoever clicks, not by whoever pays — RN-082), AB (the gate called a pending decision an infra failure — ADR 0057), AC (redirection made any command unapprovable), the ReDoS in the path scope (CodeQL HIGH), and the postgrex CVE. Of the findings the phase opened, X closed later (FASE 14d, RN-085 — the iteration ceiling became per agent TYPE). TWO remain open, and their argument is worth more than the numbers: Z and AD (the verb allowlist does NOT converge: verb, form and invocation are distinct spaces, and runs 6/7/8 got stuck on one of each), and AE (the QA agent tries to fix the code it judges, against its own prompt — contained by two independent barriers, allowlist and scope). Neither of them is a bug to fix: they are a product decision, and are in docs/explanation/achados-execucao-real.md. The conclusion the phase delivers, and that matters more than the PR: the path to autonomy does NOT go through loosening policy. It goes through the agent WAITING for the decision instead of dying — what ADR 0057 did for the gates, extending 0052.

The 19 findings are closed (19 of 19). The document stays alive and received the new findings from 13b. 6. Triage session: read docs/explanation/primeiro-dogfooding.md and classify the 19 findings into P1/P2/P3 with a proposed grouping into cohesive phases (by theme and dependency between them), estimated relative cost (S/M/L) and the risk of waiting. The output is a PROPOSAL — the priority decision is the user's. 7. Consolidate the full backlog into a living document (docs/explanation/backlog.md or equivalent): triaged findings + old items — budget per area (ADR 0038; the areas apparatus and the Dev Lead left the backlog with ADR 0053, implemented by FASE 14d), manual handoff to an agent of choice, MFA/social/OIDC/federation (ADR 0031), real SMTP in MailSender, deploy (DEPLOY_ENABLED + Environments), return of rc/rcfix (ADR 0030), community mode of approval-ladder, "N agents online" on the dashboard, currency preference with a manual rate.
documents.s: 13c — COMPLETED: the triage became docs/explanation/backlog.md

documents.t: The hello world run didn't get past the first turn and revealed defects that no suite caught, because everything before ran with a LOCAL model. The fixes are already in; what remains is a feature decided by the user during the run.

documents.t: A turn failure became a DURABLE agent.error with origin, and the agent SPEAKS in the thread; the four conversational ones stopped writing an empty agent.response (RN-059). The error path narrated in the final frame, which emitted no event at all, also closed. The Criativo chat opens with an invitation instead of empty: it is activated and waits for the user to speak first, and the screen now says so — including that technology and code are NOT its job. The key the agent spends is the workspace OWNER's (RN-058). Before, the turn looked for the credential by the agent's SLUG in a UUID column: no agent ever used a provider with a credential, and only ollama worked. Key spend report, only for the owner, with agent separate from person (RN-060). Gitflow bootstrap on GitHub: a freshly created repo answers 409 on the whole Git Data API, and the first commit goes through the Contents API. The tests' fake backend lied (404 where GitHub answers 409) — fixed along with it, it is what made the suite stay green with the product broken.

documents.t: One branch per agent, from the first milestone to what it is doing NOW, derived 100% from the event log the screen already fetches. The chronological feed remains, in the activity column: it answers "what happened", the tree answers "who is doing what". Revisited after FASE 26 (no new phase, same spirit of a targeted fix as 12d/POST-FASE 15): the default opening criterion went from just "active/stopped" to the 5 agents with the most RECENT activity — active keeps priority (RN-118); each collapsed branch got its own NOVELTY counter, with a per-agent "last seen" in read-state.ts (same mechanism as the bell, now granular); and tool.call/tool.result/agent.response started expanding INDIVIDUALLY (args, result, iteration), grouped by ToolLoop iteration boundary.

documents.t: Delivered in four PRs (#181, #182, #183, #184). ADR 0053 became ACCEPTED, revoking for good the three cuts (Dev Lead, dynamic areas via module_map and the generic areas apparatus). Areas became data: agent_areas/agent_area_members per project, with max_parallel default 2. What forced it was the dev area — the first DYNAMIC one, whose members are one per module of the module_map. What is not enumerable in code has to be data. The ceiling is the SESSION's, not the module's (RN-083). Counting per module would allow N modules × 2 without any authorization — the previous hole under another name. Above the ceiling it becomes a proposed_action. Configurable per area in Settings, requiring maintainer for the same reason as activating execution: changing the ceiling is deciding how much the product spends without asking. The Anamnese proposes raising it when authorizing has become routine — three approvals and NO denial (RN-086). One denial kills the signal: if you ever refused, the ceiling is doing its job. The Dev Lead exists (RN-087), conversational, receiving the handoff from the Arquiteto in the same confirmation that already delivers to Infra, and proposing the plan: how many agents per module and why. The dev-<modulo> stopped being addressable by handoff — the rule of ADR 0038 starting to apply to dev as it already did to QA and Infra. Finding X was closed here (RN-085): TOOL_LOOP_MAX_ITERATIONS became a ceiling PER TYPE — 8 conversational, 60 execution and gate. The criterion of who goes up is NOT "who works a lot": it is who has token_budget_micros underneath holding the spend. infra-workflows uses a heavy tool and stays at 8, because it runs without a budget. Three gaps of the phase itself, found by me while writing the next slice, and all the same failure: the ceiling rule came in with green tests and the product didn't exercise it — no route called the use case, approving the action executed nothing, and the type could be auto-approved by permissions.json (closed by RN-086). Testing the piece is not testing the path to it. Out of scope, by declared decision (ADR 0053 item 5): the "Activate execution" button changing owner. The Dev Lead → dev-<modulo> delegation through the delegations table with area = "dev", which this same item also declared, STOPPED being out of scope — closed by ADR 0094 (fluxo.yml × code audit, Wave 2, RN-405). The button remains reversible; execution remains on the current path, and the post-gate fix still goes straight to the dev who opened the PR.
documents.s: 14d — COMPLETED: parallelism decided by the LEAD, authorized by you

documents.t: No NEW gate. The phase extracts into docs/gates.yml the gates that ALREADY exist implicitly in the product, with script verification and severity, in the same spirit as docs/.docmap.yml. An agent gate that doesn't exist (dev-lead, platform) comes in as status: planned referencing the backlog — never active. The gates' external contract does NOT change.
documents.s: FASE 15 — COMPLETED on 2026-08-07 (gates as data)

documents.t: docs/gates.yml with the existing gates (see ADR 0054, which extends ADR 0048 — the decision in the event log is what makes passing a gate measurable), schema validated by test. Loader in the api reading the registry; internal read endpoint. Script pnpm --filter api validacao:gates that extracts from the event log the last pass of each active gate and exits != 0 if some block gate has no evidence of script verification. Not every gate has proof in the event log, and the registry says where it lives: merge-protegida is guaranteed by TEST (the lock in decide.ts emits no event of its own) and backmerge is CI, with state in .release/gate.json. That is why each gate declares evidencia: event_log | teste | ci with the locator — demoting them to warn would be lying about the product's hardest locks.
documents.s: 15a — COMPLETED: declarative registry

documents.t: The team panel shows the gate each story/PR is waiting on, derived from the registry (not hardcoded). docs/explanation/gates.md explaining the mechanism, in the docmap.
documents.s: 15b — COMPLETED: consumption

documents.t: Not a planned phase: it is what USE found after 15, and it is here because the origin of each item matters. None of this came from a script — it came from browsing the app in Chrome and reading the security panel. UI defects, found while browsing (RN-088..091): 429 turned into a WHITE SCREEN and the app answered with more traffic. The rule became general: every screen distinguishes THREE states — loading, error (with trace_id and a button) and empty. if (!dado) return null collapses all three. The dashboard made one request per project: 3,824 → 12 req/min, with GET /workspaces/:id/projects-summary. The bell was the missing half: 289 → one request per cycle (RN-090/091). Security hardening, with both panels at ZERO: ADR 0058 — CSP closed in the api (default-src 'none'), revising item 7 of ADR 0027; and the projectId contained in the root (RN-092), which hit not only permissions.json but the scope that AUTHORIZES the terminal. ADR 0059 — GIT_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET without a default in production (RN-093). The default was PUBLIC (.env.example) and the production compose supplied it as a fallback: requiring "not empty" would have caught nothing, because on the real error path the variable was DEFINED. An alert that didn't hold up was DISMISSED with a written justification, never silenced — and dismissing is the user's decision, not the agent's. Three operational lessons that cost a CI cycle, and hold as a rule: Green CodeQL on a PR doesn't prove an old alert closed — the PR check reports a NEW alert. An alert closes on the scan of the DEFAULT branch, that is, only after the fix reaches main. Gitleaks scans commits reachable from refs/heads/*, not the tree. A high-entropy value committed once fails CI forever on that branch; fixing on top does NOT clean it. The way out is for the commit to stop being reachable (rebuild from dev and DELETE the old branch BEFORE opening the new PR) — never an allowlist, which blinds the scanner on that path for every commit. PR refs are out of scope. A fixture that represents a secret is born WITHOUT entropy. A barrier that lives in another function CodeQL doesn't see — hence the three js/path-injection surviving the fix. The centralized check was kept (RN-092) and the price was paid on the panel: duplicating it in each caller would be a check that one day diverges.
documents.s: POST-FASE 15 — COMPLETED on 2026-08-08 (v2.5.0 and v2.5.1)

documents.t: Eleven requests born from the FIRST real browsing of the app after the database reset. It's not a script: it's use. Three discoveries from the investigation defined the size and the ORDER of the program, and it's worth recording each one, because none was in the original request: There is a COMPLETE design handoff in design_handoff_brabo/ — 8 high-fidelity screens, tokens, typography and brand. The decision was to adopt it WHOLE and FIRST: that way the eleven requests are born in the new look instead of being done twice. The Code tab's terminal became an ARCHITECTURE decision. Each project now has its own container, and it is the ARQUITETO who decides the image. Inside it the agent is free; git push, PR and deploy remain human. This pays off the product's biggest open debt — today the agent runs in the SAME container as Brabo's monorepo, and ADR 0055 says of itself that it is policy, not isolation. Two real defects showed up along the way, and neither was requested: agent_areas is NEVER written (upsert without a caller, the API returns []), and the bell drawer orders seq ASC in SQL — it shows the OLDEST. Execution ceiling: at most FOUR subagents in parallel. The phases were cut by CONTESTED FILE, not by theme — that is what makes parallelism possible. The backend's limiter is apps/api/src/db/migrations/meta/_journal.json and the drizzle snapshots: ONE migration per wave, because resolving a snapshot conflict by hand is a path to a divergent schema. RN ranges and ADR numbers are PRE-ALLOCATED before the wave starts: two parallel phases writing RN-094 make one renumber at merge, and a renumbered RN breaks the #rn-0xx links that pnpm docs:check fails.
documents.s: PROGRAMA 16–26 — what browsing asked for (in progress)

documents.t: None of the eleven requests delivers here. The phase exists because three of them touch the SAME four points of router.tsx/ProjectPage.tsx, and another three run into the lack of a common piece. Without it, the waves collapse into serial execution. design/tokens.css gets --violet (agents/AI) and whatever else the handoff defines. The fonts REMAIN self-hosted — following the handoff there would break the app under nginx's CSP (ADR 0036). The contrast test covers the new pairs, and the known debt of 4 pairs stays locked. The tab stops being a closed list in TWO places: a single registry from which PROJECT_TABS, type TabKey, the ruler and the render start to derive. A test that fails a key present in one place and absent in the other — that's the real defect. Disclosure in the design system, with the semantics of the most complete implementation that already exists (ModelCatalogSection). COMPONENT ONLY: none of the six ad-hoc implementations migrates here, otherwise the phase would open the three most contested files of the program. The session label becomes a helper and the five inline slice(0, 8) migrate. It is this migration that keeps FASE 20 from colliding with 19. CLAUDE.md enters the definition of done (see the Documentation section), with a warn rule in the docmap. DELIVERED: the rule is claude-md in docs/.docmap.yml, triggered by package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, apps/*/package.json, apps/engine/mix.exs, docs/adr/*.md and docs/gates.yml — the sentence "today it has ZERO coverage" that was here described the state BEFORE the phase and kept lying after it.
documents.s: FASE 16 — COMPLETED: foundations (unblock parallelism)

documents.t: Visual fidelity BEFORE behavior, so as not to redo work. No business rule changes: if a screen needs data that doesn't exist, that becomes a declared pending item, not a hitchhiking feature. 6. Login and App/project list. 7. Project and Session, preserving the three states of RN-088 (error before empty). 8. Approvals and Settings — Approvals is the visual base of FASE 19. 9. Proof that fidelity happened: contrast measured on the tokens and layout verified by scripts/dev/validacao-visual.js on ALL the screens touched. The .dc.html is a reference, NOT code to copy — the handoff's own README says so.
documents.s: FASE 17 — COMPLETED: the 8 screens per the handoff

documents.t: AgentAreaRepository.upsert has NO caller at all, so four use cases operate on an empty table. Provision on project creation + backfill, with a test that proves a freshly created project HAS areas — it's the same failure as FASE 14d: testing the piece is not testing the path to it. Collapse the THREE copies of the areas list (api, web, engine) into one source.
documents.s: FASE 18 — COMPLETED: the area exists in the database (a defect, fixed first)

documents.t: Kill the generic fallback of ApprovalCard, which dumps chave: JSON.stringify(valor) — the likely cause of "hard to read". Every type gets a SENTENCE in pt-BR; a type without a sentence shows verb + "see details" and the raw payload is born COLLAPSED, never dumped. Collapse in THREE places: Approvals, Insights and the card in the chat, with verb and sentence coming from ONE module. Project constraint: the collapse does NOT introduce a new required prop in ApprovalCard. That is what keeps SessionPage.tsx untouched and removes the edge with FASE 20.
documents.s: FASE 19 — COMPLETED: an approval you can read

documents.t: sessions gets kind and name in the SAME migration — two migrations on the same table collide in the journal and the snapshots. Reconcile with the event-based derivation: kind classifies the creation INTENT, execution.activated keeps classifying execution STATE, and neither rewrites the other. execution.activated in a consultative session is an explicit error, not a silent conversion. Rename preserving the hashtag; without a name, it degrades to the hashtag alone. A back-to-dashboard button — today SessionPage.tsx imports neither Link nor useNavigate, and NO navigation leaves the screen. Destination revised in a later round: the button goes back to the session's PROJECT (/projects/:projectId), no longer to the root dashboard — a session is always born inside a project.
documents.s: FASE 20 — COMPLETED: the session gets an identity

documents.t: useSessionEvents remains the CURRENT STATE (latest, four consumers: roster, tree, execution, Approvals). The HISTORY became useSessionEventHistory, only for Activities, with the afterSeq the endpoint already returned. No new route, no new parameter. The anchor is the TAIL, not the start of the session: the endpoint pages forward and there is no beforeSeq, but opening the feed on event #1 of a session with thousands delivers the wrong screen. So the first page is the same latest read (SAME queryKey, deduplicated) and each click goes down a fixed window backwards. The bell orders DESC in SQL. The "read" cutoff did NOT change semantics, and that's why there's no ADR: a cutoff by seq marks a PREFIX and the drawer shows a SUFFIX, so "mark the 50 shown" is inexpressible without a per-event read table. What changed is the drawer no longer hiding what the advance swallows — total per project, + N older, and the button saying how many it marks. The missing number comes from SUBTRACTION (latestSeq minus the cutoff), not from a request. The RN-090/091 savings didn't regress: one request per cycle, and the first "load older" costs ZERO — the latest read brings 200 and the window shows 100. An old page has staleTime: Infinity and no refetchInterval: a closed seq window over an immutable event doesn't change.
documents.s: FASE 21 — COMPLETED: the volume of events (RN-099/100)

documents.t: Delivered as the Spend tab (ADR 0063, RN-101). 22. The missing AGGREGATIONS came into a single method — sumGroupedBy(dimensao, escopo) with model, project, actor, session and day. provider is NOT one of its dimensions, and the absence is structural: breaking down by provider is breaking down by CREDENTIAL, and that is what keeps the member's view from gaining the axis by carelessness — there is no argument to pass. 23. No charting library: daily bars and a ranking in inline SVG. The daily series comes DENSE from the api (a day without spend comes in with zero), otherwise three calls in three weeks become three bars stuck together. 24. The collision was resolved by separating the QUESTIONS, not the filters. The per-CREDENTIAL report stays exclusive to the owner (RN-060) and gained alongside it the workspace breakdown by model/project/actor/day, also owner. The member's view is by ACTOR, in tokens and estimated cost, without provider and without credential — and the actor comes from the authenticated TOKEN, with no parameter where one could write another person's id. An agent doesn't count in the member's account: token_usage records who spent, not who ordered the spending. No migration, but WITH measurement: at 525 thousand rows the queries take 55 ms and 38 ms by seq scan, and an index on token_usage(created_at) would bring them to 32 ms and 19 ms. The number is in the ADR; the index comes in the wave that has the slot.
documents.s: FASE 22 — COMPLETED on 2026-08-09 (spend with two audiences)

documents.t: The area scope entered the cascade (session > agent > area > project > workspace), BETWEEN agent and project: it is the default that lead and subagents share, and the agent diverges by overriding it (ADR 0064, RN-102). The incoherence resolved BEFORE coding: the agent binding was GLOBAL (scope_id = plain slug, the route's :projectId ignored since Fase 9a) and area is per project since ADR 0053. A per-project scope above a global scope would make the same agent resolve different models only where there was an area. Decision: the agent binding became per project too — the scope_id of agent/area became composite, <projectId>:<slug|chave> (RN-103) — and not the area below the agent, which would contradict "inheritable default" (almost every binding today is an agent's). The UI shows who INHERITS and who DIVERGED (AreaModelsSection and the Origin column of ModelsSection, in ProjectSettingsTab.tsx); "go back to inheriting" is a DELETE on the agent/area binding, never writes into it the model of the level below — copying would become a copy that diverges on its own at the area's next change. The maintainer role to change the area's model (same rule as the parallelism ceiling, RN-083); the agent's stays developer.
documents.s: FASE 23 — COMPLETED on 2026-08-09 (model inheritable per area)

documents.t: Two tabs on the PROJECT screen, each listing the sessions of its kind and creating in that kind without asking again. The Session remains its own screen — the tab did not become a chat container. The collision was resolved with "Sessions" LEAVING the ruler. What remained of it is the deep-link KEY: Chat carries key: 'sessions', and that is what makes an old ?tab=sessions open on Chat with the tab MARKED. An alias resolved only in the panel would open the right panel and leave the ruler without a selection, because Tabs compares active with key and whoever writes active is ProjectPage — one of the two files the wave kept closed. Verdict on "Start ideation": it STAYS. Half the problem had already closed in FASE 20 (the button vanished from the consultative session, RN-097), and the other half wasn't redundancy: it is what brings the Criativo, and from there on the owner's key is spent (RN-058). What was wrong was the PLACE — the invitation spent a paragraph pointing at the topbar. Now the action lives INSIDE the invitation while it is on screen, and goes back to the topbar when it isn't; conviteVisivel is the only question the two share, so that it neither shows up twice nor disappears.
documents.s: FASE 24 — COMPLETED: Chat and Criativo as places (RN-104)

documents.t: The biggest architectural change of the program, and the one that pays the debt Phases B and F already pointed at separately. Delivered 25a (the Arquiteto's decision and the gate) and 25c (the external-effect boundary); 25b (the container's lifecycle) was CUT and declared — not half-implemented (ADR 0065, RN-105 and RN-106). 30. COMPLETED: the ARQUITETO decides which image comes up for the project, as its artifact (artifact.project_image in the event log, versioned, without a table) — auditable, not hidden configuration. Until it decides, the Code tab answers 409 and doesn't unlock (RN-105). 31. NOT DELIVERED AT THE TIME, declared: per-project lifecycle (provision, recycle, clean, resource ceiling actually applied), with the agent's worktree living inside the container. Container state is MUTABLE and asked for its own table — improvising it in the event log just so as not to wait for the migration slot would produce the fix right after. PARTIALLY REVOKED by Wave 4/front F1 of PROGRAMA 28: the state TABLE (project_containers, ADR 0081) arrived. What is still missing, without softening, is the half that made the table worth anything: no real orchestrator calls Docker yet, and the agent's worktree remains outside the container. The "inside, the agent is free" half of the terminal policy has NOT CHANGED YET — ADR 0055 keeps holding as it is until the container actually comes up. 32. COMPLETED AT THE TIME, REVISED by the local runner (ADR 0102/0103, RN-418): the external-effect boundary. git push, PR and deploy don't go out through the terminal — not even inside the project scope —, and the rule WAS deny (not require_approval, because of "always allow"), with the message redirecting to the TYPED action (git_push/git_merge/ pr_open), which is born a proposed_action (RN-106, revised). The deny became an ABSOLUTE CEILING (unconditional require_approval, never auto-approvable) — the product owner's decision, "always allow" closed at the source so it wouldn't become decorative (see the local runner section). Merge into a protected branch remains manual (RN-014), untouched. Network and spend have their own verdict in the image ARTIFACT (network: none/egress, a cpus/memory/pids ceiling that refuses instead of silently downgrading) — decided ONCE, not command by command, for the same reason Z and AD proved that a verb allowlist doesn't converge. Closing Z and AD itself depends on 25b (the physical wall), which hasn't come up yet.
documents.s: FASE 25 — COMPLETED WITH A CUT: Container per project (the boundary stops being just policy)

documents.t: COMPLETED (26a): GitProviderContract gained listTree and PR diff (11th/12th operation), capability declared ONLY when proven by the suite. COMPLETED (26b): the four routes of code.controller.ts — tree, file, search and diff — behind the CENTRALIZED check of RN-092/095, with a ceiling and cache on the search (which is COMPOSITE, not a contract operation). COMPLETED: the screen (ProjectCodeTab/code/*), registered in project-tabs.ts without touching router.tsx/ProjectPage.tsx. Rail (Explorer/Search — the only ones with real data), explorer loaded by DIRECTORY, editor tabs with breadcrumb, real search with filesScanned/truncated, PR diff by known id (with patch: null treated as "no text", never "no change"). Syntax highlighting is its OWN regex tokenizer (code/highlight.ts) — ZERO new dependency, against the 15-90 KB of Prism/highlight.js/Shiki for what the tab needs; three new color tokens (--syntax-function/ -comment/-operator) calibrated at 4.5:1 against --code-bg in BOTH themes. The fourth state of RN-088 — blocked by the Arquiteto's pending decision (RN-105) — became RN-107, asked BEFORE trying to read code, with its own re-query every 15s while blocked. Pending items DECLARED, with no real data behind them: interactive terminal (FASE 25b, which remains cut — an honest empty state in the tab), blame, list of PRs inside the tab (the diff is only reachable by known id, coming from Approvals) and a Problems/lint/tests panel. Line virtualization was also left out at the time — the handoff itself calls the code tab "the most costly of the program"; the 512 KB per file ceiling (GIT_BLOB_MAX_BYTES) limited the worst case until then. CLOSED by Wave 4/front E2 of PROGRAMA 28 (RN-239..242): only the visible window becomes a DOM node, and the minimap reuses the same tokenization without a second pass.
documents.s: FASE 26 — COMPLETED: Code, read-only

documents.t: The phase started as ONLY the API layer, and the sentence "no UI" that stayed here described the state of the FIRST batch — it aged and started teaching wrong. The THREE UIs exist: the rich branch dropdown (item 38, CodeBranchPicker.tsx), the on-demand blame toggle (CodeEditor.tsx, RN-113) and the list of PRs inside the tab (CodeDiffPanel.tsx), the last two delivered in v3.0.0. The three declared pending items of blame, rich branch dropdown and PR list would touch the SAME files (contract, the three providers, the use case, the controller, the contract suite) if attacked separately by agents in parallel; the decision was to deliver all three together, at once, and leave the UI of each to three following agents with no risk of collision. 36. GitProviderContract gained blame, listPullRequests and listBranchesDetailed (13th, 14th and 15th operation — RN-110/111/112), capability declared only when proven by the contract suite against the three providers (local against real git; github/gitlab mocked — the real smokes remain skipped without GITHUB_TEST_TOKEN/GITLAB_TEST_TOKEN in the environment, same situation as FASE 13a). listBranchesDetailed is its OWN operation, not an extension of listBranches (RN-112) — enriching costs an extra call to the provider PER BRANCH, and listBranches remains the Gitflow bootstrap's, which doesn't pay that cost. 37. Three new routes in code.controller.ts (GET .../code/blame, GET .../code/pull-requests, GET .../code/branches), same role: viewer and the same central path check (RN-095) as the four earlier ones. apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts/api-types.ts gained the corresponding functions and types (getCodeBlame, getCodePullRequests, getCodeBranches) for the next wave to consume — CodeShell.tsx and CodeDiffPanel.tsx were NOT touched beyond the comment documenting that the foundation already exists. 38. COMPLETED: the rich branch dropdown (RN-112) — CodeBranchPicker.tsx, opened from CodeShell.tsx, replaces the plain text field with a selector listing each branch with ahead/behind relative to the default and the associated PR, when there is one (aberta/mesclada/fechada). A ref outside the list (tag or sha) remains reachable — listBranchesDetailed doesn't enumerate those two, so the dropdown's footer has a manual field. The program's freeze: each phase declares what it doesn't do, and the hardest is 26's — code READ-ONLY, no saving through the tab. Editing is the next phase, and when it comes, writing is an external effect: it is born a proposed_action.
documents.s: FASE 26b — COMPLETED: blame foundation, navigable PRs and a rich branch

documents.t: Same spirit as POST-FASE 15: not a planned phase, it is what USE asked for. Stories with pending promotion at the same time (RN-048/RN-126) became N loose cards in the PO session's timeline when it produced several in one batch. Carousel (apps/web/src/components/ui/Carousel.tsx) is the design system's first item-by-item navigation component — 2+ pending become ONE navigable carousel (arrows, dots, keyboard), with "Approve all" promoting the whole batch in a single call (promoteStories was already a batch, no contract change); 1 pending remains the usual simple card. The decision of when a "batch" forms is re-evaluated on each render — the set of promotions STILL PENDING in the session, not "created in sequence without interruption" — so that resolving a story in the middle of the carousel recomputes the batch on its own, with no state of its own to synchronize. Local or Container project (RN-169/RN-170, ADR 0072). The product owner's request: "cross the boundary of only writing code in the container and be able to write code from a user folder", with the freely typed path variant chosen by him, aware that it only works mounted in the container. projects gets (workspace_mode, workspace_path) in migration 0043, with container as the default — nothing changes for whoever doesn't choose. ADR 0072 REVISES part of 0065 and touches the ground of 0055, which decided the opposite direction (the container wall), and so the consequence is written without softening: the STRUCTURAL containment of join(env, coluna) — no corrupted column leaving the managed root — ceases to exist for a Local project, and what remains is the creation guard plus the lexical revalidation on read. FASE 25b remains cut: a Local project runs in the SAME container as today, only the folder changed. The Arquiteto's C4 diagram (RN-149, ADR 0068). New deliverable: create_c4_diagram generates Context + Container (Simon Brown) in Mermaid, rendered in the Overview. The Container level is DERIVED from the current module_map by the use case — never retyped by the model — so as not to open a second source that diverges from the first; only the Context (system name and external actors) comes from the tool call. artifact.c4_diagram is an artifact without a table, versioned in the event log, same design as artifact.project_image (ADR 0065). mermaid came in as a new RUNTIME dependency of apps/web — the first of its kind (the docs site already uses Mermaid, but at build time) — isolated behind apps/web/src/lib/mermaid-render.ts with dynamic import(); vite build confirmed that only the entrypoint loads eagerly and Mermaid's heavy chunks stay on demand, and none of them uses eval/new Function — the closed CSP of ADR 0058 stayed intact, with no configuration change.
documents.s: POST-PROGRAMA 16–26 — what use asked for afterwards (RN-148)

documents.t: Not a phase: it is 17 points USE found in a live test session on the exp003 project, fixed in five waves sequenced by CONTESTED FILE — four of them converging on SessionPage.tsx, which forced serialization. The origin matters: none of these was found by a test. What the round taught, worth more than the list: the biggest fix (RN-155) was invisible to any suite because the defect was in comparing two DIFFERENT numeric spaces that happen to both be number — the event.seq (gapless, per SESSION) against the action.seq (proposed_actions.seq, a global bigserial of the WHOLE table, shared by every project and every session in the system, and documented in the schema as a deliberate contrast). The order only seemed right while the table was small. The fix didn't invent a field: it used the proposed_action.created event that ProposeActionUseCase already writes in the SAME transaction, with payload.actionId pointing back. Engine and contained reading (RN-150) — search_workspace returned ALL the hits, without a ceiling: the second real cause of the 413 in PR review, after the read_file fix. Two INDEPENDENT ceilings, because the search blows up in two ways — number of hits (SEARCH_WORKSPACE_MAX_HITS, 500, over a Stream that STOPS scanning at max_hits + 1) and bytes of the final text (SEARCH_WORKSPACE_MAX_BYTES, 32,768). Their own variables, not reused from the other two: same class of overflow, diverging one shouldn't require touching the others. The truncation mark is addressed to the MODEL (it tells it to refine the term) and never invents a total, because counting the total would pay again the I/O the ceiling exists to avoid. Numbers that lie (RN-151) — the project badge in the sidebar counted ANY unread event: exp003 showed 392 while the Approvals tab of the same project showed 8. A number that doesn't correspond to anything actionable when clicked is worse than none. It became pendingApprovalsCount in the read model that already existed (RN-090), in one more aggregation in the Promise.all — never N+1. Traceability of what the agent produced (RN-152) — the feature/task-XXXXXXXX branch in the Code tab's dropdown now says which dev agent and module it belongs to. The module comes from the current module_map through the SAME functions that generated it, never by reverse regex on the name; without a link, it degrades to null instead of guessing. Auto mode (RN-153/154, see Conventions) — the actionType: "*" wildcard. What matters is where it lives: resolution is the REPOSITORY's (findMode), and decide.ts didn't gain a line — that is what makes the three absolute ceilings true by CONSTRUCTION, and not by one more if that one day someone forgets. The session thread you can read (RN-155..159) — ordering (above); the 5s indicator with the fixed text "Gathering information..." instead of interpolating the agent, which already appears in the header (RN-156); the PO's epic/story creation becoming a compact notice instead of a bubble with the same visual weight as a real reply (RN-157); light Markdown with highlighting in the chat by its OWN regex parser, zero new dependency and no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and only the agent's OUTPUT is rendered — what the human types stays literal (RN-158); and "Generated artifacts" grouped by agent with the Disclosure of RN-138, each artifact navigating to where it lives (RN-159). The module_map/C4 stayed OUT by recorded decision: it is the project's CURRENT state, not a session-dated artifact. Order of authority (RN-160/161, ADR 0069) — "Confirm architecture ready" only enables with at least 1 PROMOTED story (having a captured rule isn't enough); and accepting the handoff to the Dev Lead chains the activation of execution when the effective role of whoever accepts already authorizes it. The fusion is only on the client: the backend still requires maintainer (RN-137), so it avoids a redundant click without moving the authorization boundary. Structured input (RN-162) — ask_structured_questions, the Criativo's: the model declares the questions in a schema, the form is rendered by StructuredQuestionCard, and the answer REUSES SendAgentMessageUseCase instead of opening a second message path. Answering is a single act — resending is 409, not an overwrite.
documents.s: RODADA exp003 — COMPLETED (RN-150..162, PRs #278–#293)

documents.t: Same spirit as the other rounds: it came from USE, not from a script. The report was "the Criativo didn't reply after saying it would fix it and try again", and the sentence was literal in the code — run_turn_capturing/1 called the model ONCE, dispatched the tools and returned. The tool's result went into the in-memory history and nobody read it again, so the promised fix only happened if the user sent another message. The Criativo was the only conversational one without a tool-use loop; it got the same as the PO, with its own ceiling of 12. What matters beyond the fix: whoever decides what is announced became the ceiling, and not a fixed text — the retry promise only enters the sentence when there is still a round to keep it. An exhausted ceiling became a narrated agent.error (po_server ended silently in that case, and that was the next obvious debt — closed just below by RN-166), and the tool failure stopped being an agent.response — in the event log it was indistinguishable from a normal reply and stated no origin at all, exactly what RN-059 closed for turn failure.
documents.s: RODADA exp001 — the Criativo keeps its promise (RN-163)

documents.t: Not a phase: it is a defect found by real USE, and the origin matters because no suite would catch it. The backlog came out with an epic and no story — hence no task, hence execution stuck with no error at all. The investigation found four stacked causes, and the first three are the same: the PO had no way to know and no way to warn. The PO had four tools, all of them WRITE tools. The context was built ONCE, at kickoff, from the last 200 events of the SESSION — from then on it never re-read anything: it didn't know which rules existed, which it had already covered, nor what it had itself already created. In came listar_regras_de_negocio and listar_backlog (RN-164), served by two internal routes scoped to the PROJECT — and the scope is the point: reading per session was exactly what hid the rule captured earlier. They reuse the plumbing that already existed (listByTypeForProject, ListBacklogUseCase, computeCoverage); what was missing was the route, the client method and the tool. Nothing demanded the story after the epic and the loop ended silently. An epic without a story became an EXPLICIT outcome — backlog.epic_without_story, durable, in the pattern of RN-059 (RN-165) — and the PoServer's iteration ceiling started emitting toolloop.limit_reached, the SAME type as the ToolLoop, which the conversational agents never emitted because they have their own loop (RN-166). The kickoff instruction didn't say a word about what to do when information is missing — and faced with a gap without instruction a model chooses between inventing and stopping. Stopping is what it did. The third way out came to be written, with the tool to exercise it: ask_structured_questions, the SAME one as the Criativo's (RN-162), now advertised to the PO too. Two design decisions that hold beyond this case: only a create_story that succeeded discharges the epic's obligation (a story refused by the api covered nothing, and treating it as if it had is trading one silence for another); and the demand is per OCCURRENCE, reported once, never an alarm that repeats every turn until someone learns to ignore it.
documents.s: RODADA exp001 — the PO reads what already exists and is held to account (RN-164..166)

documents.t: Same origin as the others: USE, not a script. Four complaints about the Session screen — the PO's handoff appearing ABOVE its last line, the approval going up into the middle of the Arquiteto's reply and only coming down when it finished, the approval card "badly laid out" and the scroll that didn't follow the conversation. The investigation found that the ordering was RIGHT, and that is the round's lesson. RN-155 is faithful to the event log; what the log says is that po_server.ex#run_turn/2 emits, in the SAME iteration, the agent.response, THEN the offer_handoff tool.call and ONLY THEN recurses into the closing line — so the handoff's seq is honestly SMALLER than the last line's. The same for proposed_action.created. The fix, therefore, isn't about ordering: it is a declared PRESENTATION rule (RN-172), in a separate pass (afundarDesfechos) AFTER the sort by seq — not a comparator with three terms nobody would be able to justify a year later. What keeps turns from mixing are three barriers, and each one exists because of a real case: turn (the boundary between two turns may have no VISIBLE entry — agent.activated opens a turn and doesn't become a thread item), author (in an execution session several agents write without the user speaking even once, and they all stay in the same turn) and non-outcome (two outcomes in a row preserve the order between them — Infra before the Dev Lead). RN-173 closes the other two complaints, and they were the same: the scroll effect depended only on [events.length, streamingText], and actions is a SEPARATE query — a card arriving pushed the conversation off screen without scrolling anything. Dependency fixed, plus a ResizeObserver on the content for what NO dependency list reaches (Disclosure collapse, Markdown reflowing). The guard of 120px from the end stays intact, on purpose: the thread follows the conversation, it doesn't hijack the reading of whoever scrolled up.
documents.s: RODADA exp001 — the thread reads as the turn happens (RN-172/173)

documents.t: Same origin: USE. Four complaints about the Session screen, and three of them share the same lesson — the product knew the information and didn't show it. The question at the center, and with a way out (RN-171). The report was literal: "always give the user the input option when they select Write". The model offered a "Write it yourself" kind of option and the form had nowhere to write — the ask_structured_questions schema couldn't express "besides these, whatever you want". allowOther came into select with default true, and the asymmetry is the argument: a list closed by FORGETFULNESS locks the conversation and the user can't unlock it from outside; a list opened by mistake offers one more field. The interface sentinel never travels to the backend, and the submit button still requires everything filled in (the backend refuses with 400 either way). The box also became centered with the 560px ceiling of ApprovalCard and got an avatar: it was the only thread item aligned to nothing. An action that triggers a turn arms the indicator (RN-174). The "thinking" animation already existed — what was missing was COVERAGE. Two actions on the screen trigger a synchronous turn in the engine and armed nothing: answering the form (AnswerStructuredQuestionUseCase reuses SendAgentMessageUseCase) and returning a story to the PO (ReturnStoryUseCase calls reviseStory, which is handle_call({:revise, …})). The Phoenix channel doesn't cover the hole: with the join still in progress (RN-108) the "working" agent.status has no listener and gets lost. The model, for EVERYONE (RN-175). The premise that the defect was the PO's didn't hold: the four conversational ones have written modelName since RN-146, with a green test. Whoever never wrote it was the ToolLoop — the path of every execution and gate agent — and the chat without an active agent in the api. No new call: RunLlmTurnUseCase already returned the field in the body. The screen stopped writing the loose word "model" (which reads as if the model were called that) and became a readable chip; without the data, it SAYS it wasn't recorded — guessing from the current binding would attribute to an old reply a model that maybe didn't even exist, the same error RN-044's frozen price avoids. A Markdown table becomes a table (RN-176). Two ways out were possible, and the chosen one was to support tables in the chat's Markdown, with the design system's Table. Rendering artifact.module_map in the thread was REFUSED by a decision already recorded: it is the project's CURRENT state, not a session-dated artifact (RN-159), and it lives in the Overview. Besides, the request was about the table inside the message — and the fix serves any agent that writes one, not just the Module Map. The separator line remains mandatory (GFM), so prose with | never becomes a table by mistake.
documents.s: RODADA exp001 — the thread says who speaks, with which model and what it asks (RN-171/174/175/176)

documents.t: Same origin as the others: USE, not a script. Five complaints about the context panel and the Session log, and the round's lesson is a single one — the panel showed a slice as if it were the whole, in three different dimensions at once: it hid six event types without offering an alternative, read from oldest to newest, and cut the session at 200 events without saying so. Origin as a new classification (RN-177). ActivityKind answers "what SUBJECT the event is about" and decides icon and color; origem answers "what LAYER it came from", and it is what makes the history readable — eventos, sistema, llm, harness, agente, usuario, derived from the data that EXISTS (actor.kind and the type prefix). The precedence is what makes it predictable and is in the order of the ifs: mechanism beats actor (a tool.call belongs to the harness whoever it is), and actor beats agent prefix (chat.message exists on both sides). The 5 most recent stay open and the rest collapse by origin, in both places — in the log panel and in the thread, where the axis is inverted (the thread is ascending, so the history stays at the TOP). The machine-noise filter stays on by default: its reason didn't change (116 of 193 real events), what changed is that it became a CHOICE instead of a done deal. Order and pagination (RN-178). The four sections became descending, and the "Load older" button switched sides as a consequence — the argument from before, with the sign flipped. Business rules above 5 paginate, with the page resolved by clamp and not by a synchronization effect. The PO's tree (RN-179). backlog.task_created never entered the panel; now epic → story → task form a tree, through the LINK the event already carries (epicId/storyId), never by proximity in the log — a node without a loaded parent goes up to the root instead of being hung by guesswork. The ceiling that started showing (RN-180), and it is the item worth most. The panel read 200 events by prop and had no way to say there were more. It started reading the paginated history of RN-099 (same queryKey as the tail, ZERO extra requests — RN-090/091), got the pager ActivityFeed always had and no call site passed, and the note counts how many are missing by SUBTRACTION on the seq, like the bell of RN-100. The derived sections read baixados (everything already fetched) and not the feed's window, otherwise they would start showing LESS than they showed before. Delegation in the thread (RN-181). delegation.completed|failed|dispensed only existed in the log panel: the gate opened and closed with no sign at all that there was a second attempt underneath. They became a compact notice in the RN-157 format, with the sentence coming from classifyEvent — the same as the panel's. The area's external contract doesn't change (ADR 0038): the thread narrates what the lead recorded, it doesn't start addressing a subagent.
documents.s: RODADA exp001 — the panel groups, orders and says what it doesn't show (RN-177..181)

documents.t: The light theme existed in design/tokens.css, had a parity test and was described in design/README.md as if it were a screen — and nothing in apps/web wrote data-theme. The only way to see it was to type the attribute in DevTools. The two contrast tests knew and said so: one asserted by expect that THREE light pairs fail, "a record of what is inherited, not a guarantee of what is rendered". While it lasted, the argument was honest — measuring a screen nobody can open is measuring an intention. With the theme button arriving, it flips sign. The boot is a FILE (apps/web/public/theme-boot.js), synchronous in <head>, before the bundle. The handoff says to use an INLINE script; the image serves under script-src 'self' (ADR 0058), so inline would work in pnpm dev:web and be blocked in production — ADR 0036's failure with another subject. tema.ts is the API the shell consumes; the button doesn't live in it. A localStorage that throws degrades to "paints and doesn't persist", and an unknown value falls to the default. Six light-theme tokens changed value (ADR 0074), because the light theme's most demanding background is the paper --code-bg: accent 3.56 → 4.81, warning 3.15 → 4.98, success 3.89 → 5.12, violet 4.16 → 4.95, text-muted 2.76 → 5.17, plus accent-hover one step below. The DARK didn't change any, and its debt stays locked at the same five numbers. Two side effects recorded: the five pairs that are debt in the dark PASS in the light, and the "known exception of the design system" (--on-accent over --accent, 3.20:1) disappears in the light — the fix the test's comment described, darkening down to --terracota-500, is what the light theme now does. Five of the handoff's eight --syn-* values were REFUSED by measurement (the worst, --syn-cm, gives 2.32:1 in the light). Where the handoff fails, the measured number holds: it's the same rule as the fonts. The eight roles now exist with the prefix --syntax-*; the five semantic ones that still paint are measured alongside them.
documents.s: PROGRAMA 28 — Wave 1, front A: the theme stops being unreachable (RN-182..185)

documents.t: The containment changed nature, and that is what matters — not the new axis. provider became a dimension of sumGroupedBy again, revising ADR 0063 by the product owner's decision. Before, the member couldn't reach the breakdown by CREDENTIAL because it didn't exist — ADR 0063 wrote "there is no argument to pass". Now it exists, and whoever contains it is the TYPE: two overloads, and the scope that carries actor (the only one of the member's view) only accepts Exclude<SpendDimension, 'provider'>. The guarantee went from "impossible to express" to "impossible to compile", which is weaker — and that is why the barriers are TWO and independent: the member's route also has no dimension parameter at all. No if on the combination, on purpose (same lesson as RN-153/154), and the proof was by INVERSION: without the @ts-expect-error, tsc flags TS2769 on the exact line. porOwner/porAgente are a partition of porAtor by actor_kind, with no extra query; system stays out of both and remains in the total. The index on token_usage(created_at) that ADR 0063 measured and postponed came in in migration 0044. The SCREEN didn't change — that's a later wave.
documents.s: PROGRAMA 28 — Wave 1, front D0: spend by provider (RN-186..188)

documents.t: The handoff asked for two things that depended on the SAME data the product doesn't have: a quality score per capability (mock: "code → claude-sonnet-4 / qwen2.5-coder:14b (9.4)") and an "ideal" badge in ModelPicker when the model covers "all the capabilities required by the agent". The investigation confirmed twice that this second data doesn't exist: ModelsSection itself had already renamed the "Agent · capabilities" column to just "Agent" for that reason, and the agent-binding ModelPicker reads GET /projects/:id/models (role viewer) — the curation (uses, ADR 0051) only exists in ModelComCuradoria, from a maintainer-only route. The badge was NOT built; the "Best models per capability" table WAS, with two real signals: how many of the project's agents already resolve, through the cascade, to each curated model, and the catalog cost as a tiebreaker — never a calculated score.
documents.s: PROGRAMA 28 — Wave 2, front H2: model ranking without an invented score (RN-210, ADR 0077)

documents.t: 264px/62px with an icon track when collapsed; expandable projects revealing the tabs (read from project-tabs.ts, never hardcoded); the Activities section grouped by REAL base agent/instance — the -2 suffix of extraDevAgentId, never an invented -01/-02 counter (finding of Wave 1/front B0) —, scoped to the current route's project, not all of them, so as not to open N+1 event reads. Theme button in the footer; the two inert global items go, only Projects and Activities are global; auto-collapse of the Code tab via AutoCollapseContext (sidebar-state.ts), without saving a preference. Persistence centralized in sidebar-state.ts, the handoff's six brabo.* keys. Two divergences from the handoff documented and NOT resolved (RN-197): the project badge remains pendingApprovalsCount (RN-151 wins, it's more recent) and the handoff's identity color only appears on the collapsed track — the expanded line keeps only the existing status dot (RN-039), two dots would be noise.
documents.s: PROGRAMA 28 — Wave 2, front B: the sidebar collapses (RN-195..201)

documents.t: The four literal fixes of the handoff's "screen frame" checklist: .headerTop got min-height: var(--header-h) — a FLOOR, not a ceiling, because the project header (identity + compact TokenMeter) is richer than the generic header of the handoff's 6 internal screens, and forcing 60px would cut the budget alert, the same class of error RN-088 forbids; the active tab with box-shadow: inset 0 -2px 0 var(--accent) instead of border-bottom; horizontal scrolling on the ruler; a content container with max-width: 1040px on the document-shaped tabs (not on the semRespiro ones). The ruler's spacing values that lived as a descendant CSS override in ProjectPage.module.css since FASE 16 migrated to Tabs.module.css, now with the same owner. The part that required a decision, not just CSS: the handoff lists 7 project tabs and the registry (project-tabs.ts) has 10. executores (RN-121), backlog (RN-048) and insights (Psicólogo hypotheses) were born AFTER the handoff, with real data and their own RN, and they STAY — the handoff is a VISUAL fidelity reference, not a ceiling on how many tabs the product has (RN-203, ADR 0078). And the sessions key remains labeled "Chat", never "Chat RAG" as the handoff's most recent version asks (RN-202): "Chat RAG" would describe a feature that doesn't exist — the embeddings contract is ready (ADR 0075) but nothing consumes it yet, with no indexing pipeline and no citation UI — and renaming the tab today would be the same error ADR 0042 already refuses for a catalog model: announcing a capability before it exists. No export SHAPE changed (AbaDoProjeto, ABAS_DO_PROJETO); only the code label went from "Code" to "Código".
documents.s: PROGRAMA 28 — Wave 2, front C: screen frame (RN-202/203, ADR 0078)

documents.t: Select, Modal (close button) and ProjectCard got :focus-visible with the same calibrated treatment as Input.module.css, including the forced-colors block: none of the three had a focus indication reachable by keyboard alone. The Modal close button went up from 30px to 32px, the desktop touch-target floor. Table and Badge were audited and did NOT need change — neither exposes an interactive affordance of its own: a Table row is pure presentation (whoever needs a clickable row already uses <button>/<a> inside the cell, via render) and Badge is not used with onClick anywhere in the product.
documents.s: PROGRAMA 28 — Wave 2, front H1: visible focus (ADR 0036)

documents.t: The handoff asks for 4 status seals for the session's 5 real states (created/active/closing/closed/closed_abnormally). closed_abnormally→ aborted and created→waiting are direct; closing was NOT merged with "closed" — it gets its own seal ("closing", accent tone, pulsing), because in closing the outcome isn't known yet and calling it "closed" would lie about that. The pill filters (only 4, for the same reason) group created and closing by TRAJECTORY, not appearance: created falls in "Active" (still in play), closing falls in "Closed" (on the way to closing without error) — the row's seal is never rewritten by the filter, only the grouping changes. Of the 4 KPIs, two are honest about missing data: "cost this month" REUSES getMySpend (same queryKey as the Spend tab, the member's view/RN-101) and never shows the project total — which is the owner's data (porProjeto), and the Criativo tab is seen by any member; "ideation → commit rate" is DECLARED absent (shows "—"), because there is no link between session and commit in the product today — inventing the calculation would be the same class of error ADR 0042 already refuses for a model score.
documents.s: PROGRAMA 28 — Wave 3, front H3: the Criativo tab gets KPIs without faking data that doesn't exist (RN-227..230)

documents.t: On top of the chunks table from Wave 3 (ADR 0079): MANUAL indexing (no watcher, POST .../rag/reindex, idempotent full rebuild — deletes the scope/session before recreating) of the three honest scopes — docs/adr via ReadProjectCodeUseCase (same credential/gate/path check as the Code tab) and session only from chat.message/agent.response. Chunking by heading/paragraph, 1200 characters with 150 of overlap — documented as a starting point, not a calibration against real data (there isn't, yet, a body of questions run against the index). Hybrid search is TWO independent queries (vector via HNSW, lexical via GIN), fused by a weighted sum (0.6/0.4) and cut at a threshold (0.2) — numbers that are also a starting point. When the embedding provider (fixed: ollama) doesn't answer, the pipeline writes the chunks WITHOUT a vector and declares the gap in the report — it never fakes complete indexing, and the search degrades to lexical-only with a warning. The screen (RAG Chat as its own tab) belongs to Wave 5; this front is just the backend.
documents.s: PROGRAMA 28 — Wave 4, front G2: the RAG Chat gets an indexing pipeline and hybrid search (RN-231..238, ADR 0080)

documents.t: See item 31 of FASE 25 (PARTIALLY REVOKED): project_containers (migration 0046) writes the mutable STATE — provisioning → running ⇄ stopped, failed reachable from all three, removed only leaves by reprovisioning — distinct from artifact.project_image (the Arquiteto's immutable DECISION). Confirmed by investigation (grep, zero occurrences): NO service of the product mounts /var/run/docker.sock nor runs privileged — both use cases only WRITE and READ, no real call to Docker. The first transition requires the image already decided (RN-105) and FREEZES version/resources in the row; a local project (ADR 0072) is refused, because it doesn't bring up its own container. The resource ceiling (cpus/memory_mb/pids_limit) is DECLARED, not applied — no screen asserts "the container is limited to X", only "the recorded intention was X". No new HTTP route at the time: without a real consumer yet, exposing one would be guessing a contract — closed by Wave 5/front F2 just below.
documents.s: PROGRAMA 28 — Wave 4, front F1: the container lifecycle becomes a table, without an orchestrator (RN-243..248, ADR 0081)

documents.t: The screen that RN-202 (Wave 2/C) had postponed — "Chat RAG" would describe a capability that didn't exist yet — arrives together with the backend of Wave 4/G2: key: 'rag', a NEW tab (ordem: 28, between Code and Backlog), NEVER renaming sessions. The distinction stays the same, only the reason changed: sessions is a conversation with an ACTIVATED agent (spends the owner's key per turn, RN-058); rag is a search over an already built index, with no agent at all in between, read-only by nature. The screen consumes the three contracts of ADR 0080 without guessing shape and shows the two honest degradations the backend already declared and no screen read — vectorAvailable: false becomes a visible warning, and the coverage never invents "reindexed Xmin ago". A citation with session origin navigates to the exact EVENT, reusing the mechanism the Psicólogo's evidence chips already use; file origin shows path/heading as text, without a link — the Code tab has no deep link by path today, out of scope here.
documents.s: PROGRAMA 28 — Wave 5, front G3: the RAG Chat gets its own tab (RN-252..254, ADR 0082)

documents.t: The original plan for this front was the complete interactive terminal. The investigation confirmed that FASE 25b remains cut: no service mounts /var/run/docker.sock, and even after ADR 0081 nothing in production transitions project_containers — there is no real container to open a terminal INSIDE it. Implementing a faked terminal, or one running in the same container as Brabo's monorepo (the debt ADR 0055 already describes as policy, not isolation), would invent capability — the same error ADRs 0041/0042 refuse for an LLM provider and a catalog model. The real delivery: GET /projects/:projectId/container/lifecycle (role:viewer), the first HTTP exposure of the lifecycle (revises ADR 0081, which had postponed the route for lack of a consumer), and the Terminal tab showing that state — translated badge, failure reason — UNDER the explanatory text that already existed, never in its place, fetched only while the tab is open. null (never provisioned) is the honest and most common result today.
documents.s: PROGRAMA 28 — Wave 5, front F2: the real consumer of the container lifecycle (not the terminal) (RN-267/268, ADR 0083)

documents.t: Explicit request from the product owner, aware of the security consequences — the prohibition goes away only for GitHub/GitLab; MFA, OIDC provider and generic federation remain out of scope (see "What NOT to do"). SocialLoginCallbackUseCase ends in the SAME EmitirSessaoUseCase as the password login — no second session format. It reuses the existing OAuth client, but the state has its OWN purpose (purpose: 'social_login', checked BEFORE any other field): it never accepts the state of the git CONNECTION flow to a project, which would be privilege escalation. New table social_identities (migration 0047), key (provider, provider_user_id) — never email/login. A three-step decision: known identity → login; email matches an existing account AND verified by the provider → links (and verifies the account's email if it wasn't yet); email matches but NOT verified → refuses — a typed email isn't proof of ownership, accepting it would open account takeover; no matching account → provisions a new account without a password, same "pending" state as the Keycloak migration. It reuses the SAME OAuth app as the git connection — zero new environment variables, only different redirect_uri/scope per flow; the OPERATOR's action of registering the second callback in the provider is what justifies the breaking/ branch.
documents.s: PROGRAMA 28 — Wave 5, front I: social login revokes the prohibition from the ADR 0031 backlog (RN-272..283, ADR 0084)

documents.t: Not a planned phase: it closes the divergence a read-only audit of docs/fluxo.yml × code found (finding A2, docs/explanation/auditoria-fluxo-vs-codigo.md) — the flow already declared the dev-lead's plano-de-paralelismo output as via: proposed_action since ADR 0085, and the code was never adjusted to match. The product owner decided the code was wrong. propose_execution_plan entered decide.ts (minimum role maintainer), DELIBERATELY outside the absolute ceilings block — it can be configured to auto-approve, unlike parallelize/raise_max_parallel. The Dev Lead is the FIRST conversational agent (they all run a synchronous turn via GenServer.call of up to 180s) to suspend waiting for a human decision — the pattern already existed for the dev agent (ADR 0052) and the QA/Infra gates (ADR 0057), but those two are triggered by cast and never had to deal with a pending synchronous from. TurnoAssincrono.tratar_resultado/2 gained a branch: when the :aguardando_aprovacao key is present (checked by VALUE, not by presence — the Dev Lead carries it as nil since init/1), it replies to from the same way and at the same time as always, but emits only agent.status: awaiting_approval instead of agent.done — the turn hasn't ended. LiveBroadcast.agent_status/4 got the new status in its guard. The resumption uses the SAME Engine.Dev.Wake that QaLeadServer already reuses for the QA subagents (delivery is per AGENT, not per type). Accepted gap, declared: without its own state table, an engine restart while the Dev Lead is suspended loses the subscription — the decision remains recorded and visible in Approvals, but it doesn't narrate the outcome on its own. Closing this would require the same persistence mechanism as ADR 0052; out of scope for this fix, which only aligns the behavior with what docs/fluxo.yml already declared.
documents.s: fluxo.yml × code audit — the Dev Lead's plan becomes a real approval (RN-284, ADR 0086)

documents.t: It's not a triggered separation trigger — docs/fluxo.yml always declared "when the MANAGED project has its own interface to design" as the criterion, and it didn't fire: the design system remains static input. A CONSCIOUS decision by the product owner to bring the role forward anyway. Engine.Agents.UxDesignerServer mirrors DevLeadServer — a GenServer per session, ceiling of 14 iterations, activated by an accepted handoff addressed to "ux-designer" through the already existing GENERIC mechanism (no line changed in ActivateAgentUseCase). SOLO: no area, no subagents. The kickoff reads the most recent artifact.product_brief — the SAME "business need" the Criativo produces, without a new artifact — and the design system (design/tokens.css, design/COMPONENTS.md) is DESCRIBED in the agent's identity (Engine.Harness.Agents), static text: the conversational agents have no tool to read repository files. propose_prototype is the ONLY tool (personas, jornadas, prototipo with telas/anotacoes, resumo). It writes artifact.prototipo_navegavel without a dedicated use case in the api — unlike choose_project_image/create_c4_diagram, which need one because they have content DERIVED from another artifact or a shared domain refusal; neither reason holds here, so the shape validation lives in the engine (ArtifactSchemas) and the write uses the generic append_event_returning the api already exposes, the same path as artifact.product_brief. One single artifact, two handoffs about it — to "po" and to "dev-lead" — never a second artifact for "spec-visual": the prototype (screens + annotations) IS the visual spec, and duplicating it would risk the two copies diverging later. It reuses the half of ADR 0086's design that survives without its suspension: a successful propose_prototype ends the turn, so the model doesn't propose again and duplicate the artifact — without the "aguardando_aprovacao", because proposing a prototype has no external effect. apps/web/src/lib/agents.ts got the entry (color: var(--accent), the least reused semantic token of the roster; icon: PencilIcon). uxDesignerActive entered the roster in BOTH sources RN-090 requires in sync — the team panel (agent-status.ts) and the dashboard card (projects-summary.repository.ts, the same infraActive query widened, no new query). Out of reach, declared: teste-de-usabilidade requires a real human user — no agent replaces that. metricas-de-uso remains a gap even with analytics active (ADR 0089): the funnel report measures session→commit→PR→merge, not feature adoption by the FINAL users of the project Brabo builds — "evidence of adoption per feature" is DECLARED as a metric with no path to exist today, not a pending item to close next round.
documents.s: UX Designer — the fifth conversational agent, brought forward (RN-285..287, ADR 0087)

documents.t: Not a planned phase: docs/fluxo.yml declares the Staff/Principal Engineer as status: planned since ADR 0085 ("contract ready, activation decided, waiting for a trigger"). A CONSCIOUS decision by the product owner: bring the CODE forward knowing the AUTOMATIC trigger (the Anamnese noticing a RECURRING systemic problem) won't fire — the Anamnese is paused (ANAMNESE_ENABLED=false, decision of 2026-08-10). Dormant for automatic triggering, not for MANUAL invocation. The sixth solo conversational agent (Engine.Agents.StaffServer), alongside Criativo/PO/Arquiteto/Dev Lead/UX Designer, mirroring the Arquiteto (bounded loop, ceiling 14) with two differences: NO kickoff/1 (there is no session artifact to summarize — it comes up and stays idle until the first user_message, which is how whoever addressed the handoff explains the problem) and activated by the GENERIC path of canActivateAgent (an accepted handoff addressed to "staff"), without entering USER_STARTED_AGENTS — investigation confirmed that no domain change in the api was necessary, because assertHandoffTargetAllowed only refuses an area subagent and the Staff has no area. The only tool, propose_rfc (problem, options with trade-offs, recommendation, disposable PoC), writes artifact.rfc_staff DIRECTLY via append_event_returning — the same tableless pattern as emit_insight, and not that of artifact.c4_diagram (which derives the Container level from the module_map in the api) — and returns the handoff to the Arquiteto in the SAME tool call, without a proposed_action (recording a document is not an external effect). staffActive entered the team panel roster and the dashboard card (ProjectCardSummary.roster), same criterion as infraActive, so as not to open the divergence the RosterFacts comment already warned about. Declared, not hidden: SessionPage.tsx/AGENTES_DE_CHAT were not touched — the same pattern already accepted for infra (a REAL and ACTIVE lead also outside that list). The end-to-end usage path today is the internal route (POST .../agent/message, agent: "staff"), not the Session screen; the generic "manual handoff to an agent of choice" UI remains in the backlog.
documents.s: Staff — code ready, dormant for automatic triggering (RN-305/306, ADR 0088)

documents.t: A conscious decision by the product owner to bring forward the trigger docs/fluxo.yml already foresaw ("when the implementavel gate activates") — the trigger HERE is the very work of building the mechanism, not a usage symptom waiting to happen. docs/gates.yml, implementavel: status: planned → active (owner dev-lead, severidade: warn untouched — the registry already said "it's born warn even when it activates"). QA strategy stops being a proposto role: it is the qa-lead ITSELF, in a second MOMENT — same process, a deliverable separate from the PR verdict, exactly as docs/fluxo.yml already declared ("it may be the qa-lead itself in a second MOMENT, not necessarily a new agent: the separation is by deliverable"). Engine.Gates.QaLeadServer.run_design/3 is a NEW and ADDITIVE entry point (without touching run/2, the usual path, tied to DevAgentState.find_by_task_id), triggered by Engine.Gates.Dispatcher.run_qa_estrategia/3 (the same test-swappable indirection run_qa/2/run_secops/2 already use). Engine.Gates.QaEstrategiaAgent is a STATELESS module (not a GenServer), the same shape as QaPerformanceSegurancaAgent — a registry without Terminal (ReadFile, SearchWorkspace, EmitPlanoDeTeste) —, but the CONTEXT is different: Engine.Gates.QaEstrategiaContext.fetch/3 fetches ONLY the story (from list_backlog) and the current module_map (from get_infra_context, reused only for the moduleMap field — zero new route), without dev_state or worktree_path, because the gate runs PRE-DEV: there is no dev agent, worktree or task_id yet. None of the three tools goes through the ActionPipeline (only terminal/write_file do), so this agent NEVER suspends — run_design/3 runs synchronously inside its own handle_cast. The iteration ceiling stays at 8 (conversational), not 60 (gate) — ON PURPOSE: with no token_budget_micros underneath (there is no task, PRE-DEV), the same reason infra-workflows stays at 8 even while using a tool (RN-085). The deliverable (emit_plano_de_teste: synthesis, executable criteria, a GENERIC automation strategy with no framework) becomes artifact.plano_de_teste in the event log of the calling session. assess_implementability, a new Dev Lead tool, reads the most recent artifact.plano_de_teste of the story in its OWN session's history: with no plan yet, it triggers the assessment and returns an error asking for a retry (a tool error is loop INPUT, not the end of the line — RN-163); with a plan, it proposes the opinion (implementavel/inviavel + justification, plan embedded in the payload) as a proposed_action, the SAME three-outcome pattern as propose_execution_plan (ADR 0086) — maintainer, DELIBERATELY outside the absolute ceilings block of decide.ts. appsec stops being proposto — the SecOps second moment comes in the next section.
documents.s: The implementavel gate active — QA strategy as the qa-lead's second moment (ADR 0090)

documents.t: docs/fluxo.yml (id: appsec, camada_seguranca) declared in advance "same pattern as QA: two MOMENTS, not two agents for now" — a conscious decision by the product owner to bring the activation forward, without waiting for the implementavel gate (front qa-estrategia, same conceptual ADR 0090) that the registry itself cited as the trigger. Engine.Gates.SecOpsAgentServer.run_design/2 runs in the SAME process as the PR secops (same Registry key), without any Diff/Scanner/ DevAgentState: it fetches the story from the backlog + the current module_map (Engine.Gates.AppSecContextBuilder, without dev_state/worktree_path) and calls Engine.Gates.AppSecAgent.run/3 — a STATELESS module (not a GenServer, the same shape as QaPerformanceSegurancaAgent), a tool registry WITHOUT Terminal, running a STRIDE-lite checklist via ToolLoop.run/1 over the story's DESIGN, never over code. It ends by emitting artifact.threat_model and creating a handoff to the three declared leads (arquiteto, dev-lead, infra — the addressable AGENT of the id area-infra, RN-361). Declared gap, not a bug: run_design/2 is INVOKABLE, but nothing invokes it on its own yet — the natural trigger is the Dev Lead's assess_implementability (front qa-estrategia), out of scope for this delivery, which was kept self-contained (decide.ts/docs/gates.yml/dev_lead_tools.ex untouched).
documents.s: appsec gets the secops second moment (RN-360/361, ADR 0090)

documents.t: A conscious decision by the product owner to BRING FORWARD two roles of the target model (docs/fluxo.yml, status: proposto) without waiting for the organic trigger each one already declared. The shape is the one the flow itself prescribed: analytics "absorbed by medicao" until a PRODUCT metric becomes mandatory PO input, delivery-metricas "never becomes an agent — it becomes a REPORT of medicao". Both become a single SCRIPT — apps/api/scripts/analise-funil.ts (pnpm --filter api analise:funil -- --projeto <uuid> [--json]), in the SAME format as medir-execucao.ts (Fase 13b): a pure read via Drizzle, zero writes, no GenServer, no LLM agent. It measures FOR REAL, over proposed_actions.execution_result of the dev agent's three git actions (git_commit/pr_open/git_merge, only status: 'executed'): a real funnel (how many sessions produced a commit / opened PR / merged PR, and the conversion between stages — it counts SESSIONS, not actions), real lead time (first commit to the session's first merge, by the EXECUTION's updated_at, not the proposal's) and real deployment frequency (merge into a PROTECTED_BRANCHES branch, per day, cross-referencing the backmerge gate of docs/gates.yml — whose evidence is CI, out of reach of a script that only reads the database). Three metrics stay in a "Not measured, on purpose" section — a PERMANENT declaration, not a gap to close next round: the complete product funnel ideation → commit (sessions without storyId, RN-230, would require a new schema — no migration in this front); evidence of adoption per feature (it's not data that is missing collection — Brabo doesn't instrument the projects it BUILDS, with no path at all for that telemetry to exist today); MTTR and change failure rate (they require a real production INCIDENT signal, the same dependency as secops-runtime/platform — another front).
documents.s: analytics/delivery-metricas become a report (RN-320..322, ADR 0089)

documents.t: A decided bringing-forward by the product owner of the secops-runtime role (docs/fluxo.yml, camada_seguranca, previously proposto), without waiting for the declared trigger ("production with real traffic, after DEPLOY_ENABLED + platform active"). Only what the trigger does NOT require comes in: pnpm --filter api relatorio:seguranca-runtime reads rate_limit_hits — the data that the ADR 0027 RateLimitGuard already writes, including under dev/CI traffic — and produces a ranking of buckets (user:<uuid>/ip:<endereço>, the only two formats written; no route or reason, which the table never stored) and a temporal distribution in fixed slices. It's a SCRIPT, not an LLM agent nor a GenServer: there's no decision to make about the data, only aggregation.
