Automatic incident detection, incident response and security postmortem remain OUT — they depend on the same trigger that didn't fire — and the report lists them in a PERMANENT "not measured" section, without simulating an example incident nor inventing a number (same principle as ADRs 0041/0042/0077). The retained window is short by design (DomainGaugesCollector.pruneRateLimit deletes hits older than 2 × RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS, 240s by default), and the report declares both windows — CONFIGURED and OBSERVED — never letting the second pass for a longer history than it is.
documents.s: secops-runtime as a report script (RN-375..377, ADR 0091)

documents.t: A conscious decision by the product owner to bring forward part of the platform role (docs/fluxo.yml, camada_plataforma) — whose status remains planned and whose ativacao remains synchronized with DEPLOY_ENABLED, which doesn't exist. pnpm --filter api relatorio:telemetria [--projeto <uuid>] [--json] is a SCRIPT (not an LLM agent, not a GenServer) that reads, on demand, the SAME questions DomainGaugesCollector already collects for the Prometheus scrape — active/closing sessions per project, blocked tasks per project, state of the last backup (always GLOBAL, never per project, because the product backs up the whole database) — and ends after printing. The SQL queries are REPLICATED, not imported from the collector: its methods are private and end by writing to a Prometheus gauge, with no pure "just the query" half to reuse without coupling a CLI script to the lifecycle of an @Injectable. The output always includes "where to see more" (the versioned dashboards in deploy/k8s/observability/dashboards/*.json, the alerts in deploy/k8s/observability/alerts/brabo-alerts.yaml, docs/runbook.md #observabilidade, pnpm dev:obs for local observability) — a link, never duplication — and a "not measured" section that DECLARES, without inventing: no numeric SLO is defined in the product, a postmortem depends on a real incident that didn't happen, and telemetry back into the product in a closed loop is what would make platform active — the trigger (DEPLOY_ENABLED) remains absent. The role's gate_saida: { id: operavel, status: planned } doesn't change; docs/fluxo.yml only gets a nota on the telemetria-consolidada output saying the manual/on-demand version is already real.
documents.s: platform gets a first delivery: an on-demand telemetry report (RN-385/386, ADR 0092)

documents.t: Of the fluxo.yml dbre role, only two of the four deliverables depend on real data volume (plano-de-capacidade, tuning — they remain a gap, with no deadline). The other two don't need a real load: parecer-de- migracao is pattern recognition in SQL text (apps/api/scripts/lint-migracao.ts, scans apps/api/src/db/migrations/ *.sql, flags DROP TABLE/TRUNCATE/DROP COLUMN/ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE/ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL without DEFAULT, != 0 if it finds something — today it finds 3 occurrences in migrations already merged and accepted, informative, not fixed in passing); backup-restore-testado was already real since Fase 5 (CronJob + backup_runs + make test-restore executed, RTO ~40s) — all that was missing was an on-demand report (relatorio:backup, the same read as DomainGaugesCollector.collectBackup()). Neither of the two goes into CI yet: the linter scans the whole repository, not the diff of a PR, and would become a gate that fails a PR for a finding that isn't its own — see ADR 0093 for the scoping technique (pr-police.ts) when that changes. The "one migration per wave" rule (meta/_journal.json) stopped being called the "mechanized version" of this role: it avoids snapshot conflicts between agents in parallel, a concern orthogonal to "this SQL has a risky pattern".
documents.s: dbre becomes two mechanical scripts (RN-400..403, ADR 0093)

documents.t: The first of the six waves of the audit plan (section D, docs/explanation/auditoria-fluxo-vs-codigo.md) to close — Waves 3, 4 and 5 had already been brought forward out of order (analytics/DORA, the implementavel gate, QA strategy/appsec); this one is only metadata, no ADR, no line of production code. docs/gates.yml (paralelismo-autorizado): status: planned → active, with evidencia in the SAME format as the neighboring implementavel gate — event_types: [proposed_action.created/approved/denied], filtro: { actionType: parallelize }, onde: request-parallelization.use-case.ts (finding A1/B5 — fluxo.yml already said ativo since ADR 0053/FASE 14d, only gates.yml lagged behind). docs/fluxo.yml got three more fixes from the audit, all of citation or label, none of behavior: the dev's state machine went from 4 to 5 states (awaiting_approval came in, Fase 12e/ADR 0052 — A3); the RN-160 citation left the Arquiteto's backlog-promovido input and went to where it really applies, the handoff-duplo output (the "Confirm architecture ready" button it locks — A4); the RN-161 citation left handoff-duplo and became a note on the Dev Lead's input (it is the step of ACCEPTING the handoff that chains execution activation, not the double handoff itself — A5); and the origin of the dev's worktree-por-agente stopped saying harness (Engine.Dev.WorktreeManager is not one of the 4 components of the harness role — A8). docs/explanation/backlog.md was also updated: the line about the outdated gates.yml left the table of pending items (closed here), together with the implementavel gate (B3, already closed by ADR 0090 before this wave, without anyone having removed it from the table) and the part of B7 (deployment frequency/lead time) that analise:funil (ADR 0089) already actually delivers — MTTR/change failure rate remain out, but as a PERMANENT gap already declared in fluxo.yml, not an engineering pending item. Verification: pnpm --filter api validacao:gates -- --sem-banco (valid registry, no ativo-sem-evidencia) and pnpm docs:check green. Phase 3 of the script (real evidence in the event log) requires --projeto <uuid> against a database with data — out of reach of this fix, which is metadata only. Pending items of the same plan, not of this wave: Wave 2 (Dev Lead → dev delegation, RN-160 revalidated in the backend) and Wave 6 (the necessidade-validada gate, which requires an ADR and a product decision before coding).
documents.s: fluxo.yml × code audit — Wave 1: fluxo.yml/gates.yml up to date

documents.t: The second of the six waves of the audit plan (section D), the TWO items of largest scope after Wave 1 — the other four (3, 4, 5 brought forward out of order; 6 still pending, requires an ADR and a product decision). Both live exclusively in apps/api; no change in engine/web was necessary. B6 — RN-160 revalidated in the backend. The rule ("Confirm architecture ready" requires at least 1 promoted story) was only guaranteed on the CLIENT (SessionPage.tsx, hasPromotedStory) — a direct HTTP call to POST /agents/arquiteto/handoff-infra ignored the rule entirely. OfferInfraHandoffUseCase.execute now queries StoryRepository.findByProject and refuses with BadRequestException BEFORE writing the event or calling the engine, when no story has status !== 'draft'. B1 — the Dev Lead → dev delegation becomes data. ADR 0053 (item 5) already foresaw this and declared it out of scope at the time — CLAUDE.md listed it as a reversible cut. Closed here: AcceptParallelizationUseCase.execute (API side, covers both the direct AND the approved-for-free paths, because both already converge on it) writes delegations with area: 'dev', leadAgent: 'dev-lead', subagent = the id of the freshly activated dev-<modulo>. Unlike QA/Infra (which write on the ENGINE side, because that's where the subagent produces an opinion), status: 'completed' was REDEFINED for this area: it means "the delegation was CARRIED OUT" (the agent came up), not "opinion issued" — and parecerArtifactId points to the project's most recent artifact.module_map (via SessionEventRepository.listByTypeForProject, an already existing method, no new query). Without a module_map in the project — it shouldn't happen —, the delegation isn't written with a fake id: it only logs the unexpected state and moves on, because the dev agent's activation is already a success when that write is attempted; a failure in RecordDelegationUseCase also doesn't bring down the activation, for the same reason. Decision recorded in ADR 0094, which also revokes the cut of ADR 0053 item 5. docs/fluxo.yml (dev-lead, output delegacao): status: lacuna → status: ativo, regra: RN-405.
documents.s: fluxo.yml × code audit — Wave 2: RN-160 in the backend and Dev Lead → dev delegation (RN-404/405, ADR 0094)

documents.t: It closes the LAST of the six waves of the audit plan (section D, docs/explanation/auditoria-fluxo-vs-codigo.md) — all six closed: 3, 4 and 5 had been brought forward out of order (analytics/DORA, the implementavel gate, QA strategy/appsec, ADRs 0089/0090); 1 and 2 closed in the previous PRs (fluxo.yml/gates.yml up to date; RN-160 in the backend + Dev Lead → dev delegation). This is the 6th: the necessidade-validada gate (Criativo → PO), declared proposto since ADR 0085 with no mechanism at all behind it. modelo-de-time.md already recorded why it stood still: the Criativo (the model) deciding on its own that the need it produced itself is validated would be self-validation, not a real gate. The product owner's decision was a SEPARATE human confirmation — a third button in SessionPage.tsx, "Confirm need validated", in the SAME pattern as "Confirm architecture ready" (RN-160): a dedicated route (POST .../agents/criativo/validate-necessity), a dedicated use case (ValidateNecessityUseCase), its own event (necessity.validated). It never reused confirm_readiness/RN-142 (which remains just the structural floor, "≥1 captured rule") nor the PO's acceptance of the handoff (AcceptHandoffUseCase, structural, without judgment of content). The chaining chosen: the button only enables AFTER confirm_readiness has consolidated the artifact.product_brief (hasProductBrief) — it makes no sense to "validate" a summary that doesn't exist yet, and it is the most consistent reading of docs/fluxo.yml (the gate is the Criativo's OUTPUT, the moment its work has already delivered a concrete artifact). Unlike OfferInfraHandoffUseCase, this confirmation does NOT signal the engine — the Criativo→PO handoff already happened inside confirm_readiness itself, so the new event is only the record of MERIT, with no trigger at all waiting for it. docs/gates.yml gets the necessidade-validada gate: active, aprovacao_humana: true, but severidade: warn — nothing in the product today CHECKS the passing of this gate before letting the PO proceed, unlike the block ones of story-promovida/plano-de-adocao, which have a real code lock behind them. docs/fluxo.yml (criativo, gate_saida): status: proposto → status: ativo, regra: RN-406.
documents.s: fluxo.yml × code audit — Wave 6 (last): the necessidade-validada gate (RN-406, ADR 0095)

documents.t: It closes item B4 — the last line of the table "Team model backlog (ADR 0085)" in docs/explanation/backlog.md; the table is EMPTY after this fix, and the fluxo.yml × code audit ends here. No new ADR: it follows the same pattern already established by RN-164 (agent read scoped to the project, no external effect, no proposed_action), just with a new RN. docs/fluxo.yml (role po, input metricas-de-produto): status: lacuna → regra: RN-407. The DATA already existed since ADR 0089 (analise:funil — real funnel session → commit → PR → merge, real lead time, real deployment frequency); all that was missing was for the PO to be able to READ that report within the turn. The PO's third read tool, listar_metricas_de_produto (GET .../product-metrics), the exact same design as the two siblings of RN-164 — :direct, no parameter, scope closed to the project. The pure CALCULATION functions and the query (calcularFunil/calcularLeadTimes/ leadTimeMedioMs/deploymentFrequencyPorDia/buscarAcoesGitDoFunil) migrated from apps/api/scripts/analise-funil.ts to apps/api/src/application/services/funil-metrics.ts — a MECHANICAL and necessary refactoring (scripts/ can't live in src/, and src/ doesn't import from scripts/): the script started to RE-EXPORT from there, without changing signature or behavior, and the script's regression test stays green without being touched. The JSON body has no field for the three permanent absences the script already declared only in text (complete product funnel ideation → commit, evidence of adoption per feature, MTTR/change failure rate) — the PO's tool cites them by name in the TEXT it returns to the model, always, so it never concludes from the omission of the numbers that there is no gap.
documents.s: fluxo.yml × code audit — B4 (the LAST pending item): the PO reads product metrics (RN-407)

documents.t: An item of the previous backlog ("Community mode of approval-ladder") became a record correction, not an implementation: investigation confirmed that the community mode already exists in code since FASE 6 (scripts/ci/approval-ladder.ts), tested on both sides, only turned off by APPROVAL_MODE=solo (default). The backlog's sentence ("it becomes a change of aprovacao_humana in the gates registry") came from a SPECULATIVE line of ADR 0054 — not edited, by rule, but the imprecision is recorded in docs/explanation/backlog.md: the aprovacao_humana of the aprovacoes-da-escada gate is already a fixed true in both modes, with no field at all in the Gate schema that reacts to APPROVAL_MODE. What was really missing was another TODO(humano), in docs/explanation/branching-policy.md: the criterion for who goes into each approvers list (devs/po/gestão) — who comes in, who leaves, based on what. GOVERNANCE.md (repo root, new) closes that: the MECHANISM stays in branching-policy.md (the ladder, distinct people, the step by step of the variable switch), the CRITERION now lives in GOVERNANCE.md. It's a proposal, not a functioning committee — the project still has a single maintainer, and the document is explicit about it: most of it describes what comes into force WHEN there are more people, not a structure already active. A new warn rule in the docmap (governanca) demands a review when approval-ladder.ts/ branching-policy.md change — separate from the existing block rule (politica-de-branches) for the same reason checks-e-rulesets is separate from it: MECHANISM follows from the code, CRITERION is a human decision.
documents.s: GOVERNANCE.md — the criterion of the community mode, not its mechanism

documents.t: It closes the backlog item open since the Keycloak cutover (ADR 0032, "real SMTP remains future config"). nodemailer over pure SMTP transport (a LINE protocol with state/MIME/STARTTLS/AUTH, unlike the HTTP JSON APIs the rest of the product integrates), behind MAIL_TRANSPORT — log (default, INCLUDING in production: sending real email is the operator's opt-in) or smtp, selected by useFactory in AuthUseCasesModule without touching any use case (RegisterUseCase, RequestPasswordResetUseCase, LoginUseCase, the migrate-keycloak-users.ts script keep just injecting MailSender). SMTP_HOST/SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASSWORD/SMTP_FROM follow the RN-114 pattern in production when the mode is smtp — but WITHOUT the public default the four original RN-114 ones have, so the rule only kicks in when the operator opted for smtp; the validation runs in the constructor of SmtpMailSender, exercised by the useFactory when the provider graph is assembled (the same design as CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY), not by an eager call in main.ts. Body in PLAIN TEXT, never HTML — the port carries no structure for a rich body, and a template engine would be injection surface with no gain at all. Investigation found a real gap before coding: email_verification had no web route at all — verificarEmail existed in apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts since Fase 7a with NO caller, so the verification email's link would lead nowhere as soon as SMTP started sending real email. /verificar-email (VerifyEmailPage.tsx) closes that, mirroring SetPasswordPage.tsx — the same validateSearch pattern in router.tsx, the same single response for a nonexistent/expired/already used link — with one difference: no form, the confirmation fires on its own on mount, so the screen needs the three states of RN-088 (loading/error/success), not just two.
documents.s: Real SMTP in MailSender (RN-408, ADR 0096)

documents.t: An item of the previous backlog closed. Prior investigation confirmed there was no liveness aggregate at all, neither per project nor per workspace — only HISTORICAL presence (RosterFacts, "has appeared at some point") and real live status only on the client, derived from the event log, only when a project is OPEN. ProjectCardSummary.onlineAgentCount adds two mechanisms by the SAME rule ("not idle, not stuck"): dev agents (engine.dev_agent_states.status NOT IN ('idle', 'idle_tripped'), aggregated in batch in the engine) and conversational agents (the last agent.status of the most recent session with status !== 'idle', a payload that only accepts working/idle/awaiting_approval). QA/SecOps never count — they don't emit agent.status, a single verdict per invocation, with no notion of "idle" between calls. The architecture decision worth recording: the query reads engine.dev_agent_states DIRECTLY, via raw SQL batched by workspace, inside the SAME Promise.all that already adds up eleven queries of the RN-090 read model (TWELVE → FOURTEEN, still CONSTANT) — instead of opening a new internal HTTP route in the engine. api and engine share the SAME physical database, separated only by Postgres schema, and there was already a precedent (apps/api/scripts/medir-execucao.ts already reads engine.oban_peers); this decision raises the pattern from a manual script to TESTED production code (a minimal, declared fixture of the engine table in test/support/global-setup.ts). Consequence accepted and declared in ADR 0097: the query assumes whoever operates the product migrates both sides together (db:migrate AND engine:migrate), and fails loudly/visibly if only the api migrated — no try/catch hiding the error.
documents.s: "N agents online" on the dashboard — LIVE status, never historical presence (RN-409, ADR 0097)

documents.t: A fix for a defect found in a REAL execution session, not a script item: five dev agents came up, became idle_tripped (RN-047, the circuit breaker) stuck waiting for the user to unblock task by task, and the session's 30s heartbeat (Engine.Sessions.SessionServer) closed the session underneath while the manual unblocking went on. The third signal of GetSessionPendingWorkUseCase (RN-064) only reads agent.status, the conversational agents' vocabulary — dev agents speak dev.* (Engine.Dev.AgentIo) and never emit agent.status, so no dev agent ever held the session through that signal. The fourth signal reads the last dev.* event of each dev-<modulo>/dev-<modulo>-2 in the session: dev.working/dev.blocked/dev.idle_tripped hold the session (stuck waiting for a human decision IS pending work); only dev.idle (truly drained) doesn't hold it. dev.awaiting_gate/dev.awaiting_approval ENTERED the rule through RN-412 — see below; the residual gap this paragraph described was closed.
documents.s: An execution session no longer closes with a pending dev agent (RN-411)

documents.t: Found while browsing: the dashboard's "New project" button did NOTHING, with no error. Root cause: RegisterUseCase and SocialLoginCallbackUseCase (in the branch that provisions a new account) created a user and a credential but NEVER a workspace — EVERY new sign-up hit that wall, and it only didn't show before because seed.ts always creates a workspace along with the demo data. Both points now create the workspace and add the user as owner in the SAME transaction that already creates the account. Name/slug come from a single pure function, nomeESlugDoWorkspacePessoal (domain/auth/personal-workspace.ts), so the rule doesn't diverge across two files; the slug is always suffixed with userId.slice(0, 8) (the same pattern as extraDevAgentId) to be unique without a round trip to the database (RN-410).
documents.s: Automatic personal workspace on sign-up (RN-410)

documents.t: Not a planned phase: a fix requested by real USE ("on PRs it's always blowing up with entity too large") plus the sibling defect of the Executors tab showing up empty with real work going on. Investigation found the two chained: the gate dies with 413 → devs get stuck in dev.awaiting_gate → that state didn't hold the session (the gap of RN-411) → the 30s heartbeat closes the session underneath → the tab requires an active session and vanishes with the whole roster. The cause of the 413 was Brabo's API, not the LLM provider — the comments that attributed the error to the provider (runtime.exs, terminal_executor.ex, docker-compose.yml) were wrong; FalhaDeTurno.origem({413, _}) already classified it as "codigo", and was right. apps/api/src/main.ts never configured Express's body limit — the 100 KB default applied, far below the 8 MB that Phoenix accepts, in the transport's heaviest direction (engine → api, POST /internal/sessions/:sessionId/llm-turn, which resends the WHOLE history on each ToolLoop iteration). API_JSON_BODY_LIMIT (default 10 MB) closes the transport end. The second end, without which raising the limit would only postpone the overflow: the engine's ContextManager (ADR 0098) had TWO defects that kept compaction unreachable before the body overflowed — estimate/1 counted only content, so assistant messages full of toolCalls cost ~zero tokens in the estimate; and the compaction window used only context_window (128,000 tokens in the gate agents), which gave ~350 KB before compacting — well after any reasonable transport ceiling. The EFFECTIVE window is now min(context_window, teto_de_transporte), with the cut always on a ToolLoop ITERATION BOUNDARY (never separating an assistant with toolCalls from the role: "tool" ones that answer it — it would break the provider's tool-use protocol). RN-412 extends RN-411: DEV_PENDING_TYPES gained dev.awaiting_gate (the original argument — a gate can die and lock the dev agent in that state indefinitely) and also dev.awaiting_approval, by a new argument found in the investigation: the approval decision writes proposed_actions.status SYNCHRONOUSLY, but the dev agent's resumption via outbox/Oban is ASYNCHRONOUS — in the window between the two, nothing held the session, the same defect as RN-411 one level deeper. The Executors/Overview tab had the sibling defect on the web side: executionActivated was derived from events.some(...) over the window of only 200 events of useSessionEvents — execution.activated is among the FIRST events of a session and left the window in any real execution, erasing the whole roster. The correct value already existed, aggregated over ALL the events, in the workspace summary (RN-090, projects-summary.repository.ts) — the two screens started consuming that value. A bonus finding along the way: ExecutionSection (Overview) recomputed activated again, independently, over the same window — a long execution went back to offering "Activate execution" as if it had never started; fixed along with it. gatesEverOpened suffers from the SAME class of defect and was DECLARED as a known limitation, not fixed here — fixing it would require changing the signature of deriveAgentRoster/rosterFactsFromEvents, out of scope for this targeted fix.
documents.s: 413 on PRs and Executors "without execution" — the two ends and the chain (RN-412, ADR 0098)

documents.t: The product owner's request: Neo4j + ollama-model-loader (gemma:1b, yi-coder:1.5b, nomic-embed-text), explicitly inspired by the repository ErickWendel/neo4j-ai-experiments — acknowledgment recorded in ADR 0099 and in prompts/README.md, for the concrete inspiration of the "prompt as a versioned file, not a string stuck in the code" pattern and of the graph as agent memory. Two responsibilities, one foundation: versioned prompt templates (PromptTemplate/PromptVersion, idempotent by hash — RN-413) and relational memory (interactions, Psicólogo hypotheses with evidence, Anamnese profiles, handoffs — real consumption is a future wave, this delivery only builds the mechanism). The graph is DERIVED memory, never a source of truth; pgvector remains the chunks' vector index, without duplicating embeddings in two databases. The neo4j-driver driver in the api (not in the engine) — the api already owns all persistence and the RAG, the engine consumes through internal HTTP with a service token, as always. rag_search (RN-414) closes the biggest gap of the existing RAG: no agent queried it, only the web "Chat RAG" tab. A new tool in the engine, its own ceilings (RN-150), degradation always visible at the start of the text to the model. ollama-model-loader (RN-415) closes a separate real bug: nomic-embed-text was never pulled automatically and the RAG degraded to lexical-only silently in any clean environment. First batch of templates extracted to prompts/*.md (ux-designer, Psicólogo, Anamnese, ContextManager summarization).
documents.s: Neo4j as a knowledge graph — the foundation (RN-413/414/415, ADR 0099/0100)

documents.t: InstructionFiles gained a :graph source (db > graph > dir > root — the user's instruction_patch still beats everything), and THREE agents started TRYING to resolve the template from the graph before the inline text, which became a mandatory fallback: ux-designer (graph_instruction_templates_enabled?), Psicólogo and Anamnese (graph_templates_enabled?, the same key for the two). Two flags, not one — they would collide with OPPOSITE defaults between parallel fronts if they shared the key; both defaults are false. Only context-manager-summarize (of the four templates in the batch) was left without a consumer at the time — a gap ADR 0101 declared open and that closed later, through the FOURTH consumer of the SAME graph_templates_enabled?: the ContextManager's summarization prompt (prompt/1, see RN-417). Psychologist.ContextBuilder/Anamnese.ContextBuilder gained a SECOND context source — rag_search, with a query derived from the analysis trigger — in COMPOSITION with the usual recent/time-window read, never as a replacement: with no hit, the behavior is identical to before. The excerpts go into the EXISTING Triage budget, and the RAG's degraded: true is always visible in the context, never hidden. The graph writes itself: GraphProjector (api) drains a SECOND outbox line (aggregateType: 'graph_projection', same transaction, a value the engine's filter — IN ('session', 'task') — never matches, avoiding the race with Engine.Outbox.Drain, which already drains 'session' in ~2s) and calls the already existing write use cases. The engine NEVER writes to the graph directly — it preserves the event log as the single source of truth; the graph can be rebuilt by replay. A real finding during verification, recorded because it teaches: the body limit test of RN-412 (apps/api/test/main.spec.ts) had a LATENT bug — AppModule imported STATICALLY at the top of the file evaluates DrizzleModule (which creates its connection pool at MODULE scope, not in a Nest factory) BEFORE beforeAll can point DATABASE_URL to the test database. It stayed masked while the local dev database was also migrated (same table, so the query "found" it even pointing at the wrong place); it got unstuck as soon as the dev database was recreated empty (by this very wave's real smoke test against Neo4j+Postgres). Fixed with a DYNAMIC await import(...) inside beforeAll, after DATABASE_URL is already set — it is the pattern to follow whenever a test needs to redirect DATABASE_URL to a real AppModule.
documents.s: Graph consumption — templates without touching GenServers, relevance without replacing recency (RN-416/417, ADR 0101)

documents.t: The product owner's request: an agent running on the USER'S MACHINE, in the project's local folder, through the user's default terminal — plus a real interactive terminal in the Code tab. Two changes, one depending on the other. Policy (ADR 0102 — a GLOBAL decision, explicitly confirmed by the product owner after an automatic security warning about the change): git push/PR/deploy (RN-106) and sudo/doas (new) leave the unconditional deny and become an ABSOLUTE CEILING — unconditional require_approval, in the SAME block and SAME pattern as the neighboring ceilings (current.policy === 'auto_approve'), never auto-approvable by agent_autonomy (wildcard "*") nor by permissions.json. The gap the original deny plugged by force was closed at the SOURCE: ApproveAlwaysActionUseCase/patternForAction refuse to write an allow pattern for an action with a git external effect or a privileged command — "always allow" approves only the instance, never the pattern, for those two cases. Without that second half, the ceiling would be decorative. sudo/doas match by VERB in comandoPrivilegiadoNoComando (external-effect.ts), scanning all the command's segments, same principle as efeitoExternoNoComando. Runner (apps/runner, a new Node/TS workspace, ADR 0103): a CLI (brabo-runner --project <id> --dir <pasta> --token brb_...) that the user runs on their own machine, connects to the ENGINE through a NEW Phoenix channel (/runner, topic terminal:<projectId>) authenticated by a SINGLE-USE ticket (same pattern as RN-108, but a ticket ISSUED BY THE ENGINE — schema "engine", its own migration — and requested by the api through an internal HTTP route, inverting the session ticket's flow). It runs exec (an ALREADY APPROVED agent command — the routing in TerminalExecutor only happens AFTER the usual decide()/proposed_action pipeline, never before) in the user's $SHELL, and an interactive PTY mode for the Terminal tab (pty_open/pty_data/ pty_input/pty_resize/pty_close — the engine does pure RELAY, never interprets the bytes). Only ONE runner per project (Engine.Runners.Registry, :global, exclusivity of :global.register_name/3); runner mode WITHOUT a verified workspace or WITHOUT a connected runner REFUSES explicitly — it never falls into System.cmd/bind-mount, which doesn't exist for a runner project (revised by ADR 0104/RN-423, see above; the fallback to the usual path remains valid, but only for container/mounted). PTY is an action of the authenticated USER, it doesn't go through proposed_action, but it audits (terminal.session.started/ended in the event log, even when the tab drops without an explicit pty_close). The runner's security boundary is NOT sandboxing — it is authentication (the CLI presents a Personal Access Token of the user's ACCOUNT) + the usual approval pipeline + the consent of the user running the CLI on their own machine, with their privileges. apps/runner/src/guard.ts validates cwd inside the root by lexical resolution, but it is declared BEST-EFFORT, not the real guarantee. The PAT closed the automation token gap (ADR 0105/RN-424..426). The real finding of Wave 1 — "the product has no LONG-LIVED account token mechanism for automation, so the runner replicates the browser login (cookie/CSRF persisted in ~/.brabo/runner-credentials.json)" — was closed in Wave 2: personal_access_tokens (brb_…, HMAC-SHA256+ pepper hash via hashDeToken(), never argon2 — wrong for a HIGH-entropy secret) is issued in the project's Settings, scoped to ONE project, revocable, with optional expiry. apps/runner/src/auth.ts lost completely the interactive login, cookies and the credentials file — it only validates the format and passes on --token/BRABO_ACCOUNT_TOKEN, NEVER written to disk by the CLI. The PAT never authenticates outside POST .../runner-ticket, by CONSTRUCTION (IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY/ @RequirePatAuth() + PatAuthGuard) — never a branch in the global JwtAuthGuard, which would let RolesGuard authorize the PAT for any route of the user's role. maintainer revokes another user's PAT (RN-427), closing the item ADR 0105 had declared out of scope for now (incident response — a dismissed dev with a leaking token). An extension of the same model, without a new ADR: SEPARATE routes (GET .../personal-access-tokens/all, DELETE .../personal-access-tokens/:tokenId/admin), scope by projectId instead of userId — each user's self-revocation (RN-426) doesn't change. @xterm/xterm/@xterm/addon-fit (web) and phoenix/node-pty (runner) are the four new dependencies — the same exception rule as mermaid (ADR 0068): dynamic import(), no eval/new Function confirmed by grep in the installed package (not a formal guarantee against obfuscation, only strong evidence — declared as uncertainty, not asserted as certainty). ADR 0104 — Wave 1 COMPLETED (RN-421/422/423): ADRs 0072 and 0103 never talked to each other — RN-170 required a bind-mount at creation, and the routing to the runner (RN-420) reused the same workspace_mode == 'local' flag without any bind-mount, so actually using the runner was still forced to go through the mounted-folder validation. workspace_mode (2 values) became execution_mode (container/mounted/runner, migration 0048) — RN-170 (now RN-422) applies only to mounted; runner is born with a path validated only LEXICALLY (no I/O) and workspaceVerifiedAt: null, promoted to verified when a runner connects and confirms the path on the HOST (POST /internal/projects/:projectId/workspace-verification, RN-423) — the runner is the SOURCE OF TRUTH of the path, overwriting what was typed in the wizard. Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor.decisao_de_execucao/1 gained FOUR outcomes: it routes only with a verified workspace AND a connected runner; without either of the two, it REFUSES explicitly — it never falls into mounted's System.cmd/bind-mount, which doesn't exist for a runner project. A finding of the implementation, correcting the ADR (which is not edited — the correction lives here and in backlog.md): ADR 0104's sentence that converting between the three modes of an existing project "is now allowed without recreating the project" is INCORRECT. UpdateProjectDto still excludes executionMode/workspacePath on purpose — it isn't a trivial PATCH (worktree, permissions.json and the engine cache point to the old scope). Wave 1 delivered only the three-value field at CREATION; converting an existing project is a future wave, with its own design, not yet planned. Runner backlog: Wave 2 (PAT, ADR 0105) closed the item that blocked npm publish @brabo/runner, and Wave 3 (ADR 0106) delivered the distribution itself — tsup bundles apps/runner into a single dist/index.cjs (node-pty as a mandatory external, native binding), published on each final tag by its own workflow (publish-runner.yml), parallel to release.yml. A real finding tested empirically: the auto-run guard of index.ts needed realpathSync on process.argv[1] — without it, main() never ran when the CLI was invoked through the bin installed via npm install -g (a symlink, which process.argv[1] never resolves by realpath but import.meta.url always does). Declared operational pending item: the actual publication requires the product owner to create the npm Automation Token and configure the NPM_TOKEN secret — without it, the workflow warns and skips, never fails. Exclusivity by {project_id, machine_id} remains postponed until a second real simultaneous dev; best-effort guard.ts is a REAFFIRMED invariant, not a gap. See ADR 0104/ ADR 0105/ ADR 0106.
documents.s: Local runner — execution on the user's machine (RN-418/419/420, ADR 0102/0103)

documents.t: A terminal menu in scripts/dev/bootstrap.sh grouping what is done day to day: Docker, K8s, Database and Test. It exists because those commands live in THREE places that don't talk to each other — package.json, Makefile and scripts in deploy/k8s//docker/ — and memorized knowledge rots. It reimplements nothing: each leaf calls the command that already exists. The --print-commands mode resolves the whole tree without a TTY and without executing, and it is on it that the test runs (scripts/dev/bootstrap.spec.ts) — a TUI can't be unit tested, but the menu→command mapping can, and that's what goes wrong. Zero new dependencies; the colors come from design/tokens.css in 24-bit ANSI with degradation to 256 colors and to none. The output of a running command is SCROLLABLE (mouse wheel in SGR, j/k, PageUp/PageDown, G to go back to the end). What was missing wasn't reading the wheel: it was OFFSET — tail -n only knows how to show the end —, so the window became a slice with sed -n 'a,bp', testable without a TTY through --print-window. Two consequences the footer announces: scrolling back FREEZES the window (like less +F, otherwise the 5 Hz redraw undoes the scrolling) and mouse tracking, turned on only on the execution screen, is turned off on EVERY exit — \e[?1006l\e[?1000l in restaurar_terminal, which the EXIT trap covers. The escape parser is a generic CSI one (reads up to the final byte): reading two fixed bytes left the rest of the sequence in the buffer, and since the menu treats [1-9] as a choice, a wheel turn fired menu items. Three recorded decisions: Create provisions from scratch and Deploy publishes into an environment that already exists (that's why only Deploy has a per-service choice); in K8s only All works, and Api/Engine/Web appear DISABLED instead of vanishing, because the menu should say what the product doesn't do; and Database › Delete recreates the pgvector extension, since docker/postgres/init.sql only runs on the volume's first initialization — a plain DROP SCHEMA would make the next migration fail, and since the engine shares the same database, recovering requires db:migrate AND engine:migrate. Docker › Reset total (scripts/dev/reset-total.sh) adds up that whole sequence into a single leaf — preflight, up --build --wait (the --wait of Compose v2.17+ is the "until everything is healthy", with no health loop written by hand), the same DROP SCHEMA as Delete, db:migrate + engine:migrate and the seed — with its OWN confirmation screen (confirmar_reset, requires typing RESET), distinct from Delete's (which requires the database NAME) and without Delete's "postgres already up" precondition, because it is the command itself that brings up compose from scratch. The seed (apps/api/src/db/seed.ts) gained a step that activates a provider credential from .env, reusing the SAME <PROVIDER>_TEST_KEY variables that the LLM smokes already use (apps/api/test/infrastructure/llm/*.smoke.spec.ts) — a single naming convention, two consumers; a provider without a defined variable doesn't come in, without error, and the credential stays with the OWNER (RN-058). Two findings when running the reset for the first time, and not about the item itself — neither of them is hypothetical, both broke the real run: gemma:1b doesn't exist in the Ollama registry (manifest unknown — only gemma3:1b exists), so ollama-model-loader always failed and the --wait never closed green. Fixed in the six places that carried the wrong value as CODE — docker-compose.yml/.prod.yml, .env.example, docker/ollama/pull-models.sh, scripts/dev/verificar-modelos-ollama.sh, deploy/k8s/base/ollama/job-model-loader.yaml and RN-415 in docs/business-rules.md — without touching ADRs 0099/0100 (accepted) nor the historical narrative of this same section of CLAUDE.md, which describe what was requested/decided at the time, not the current operational value. More serious, and older — Database › Delete (item 3.4, existing since the menu was created) never really dropped: DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE doesn't reach engine.* (Ecto/Oban lives in its OWN schema, engine) nor drizzle.__drizzle_migrations (drizzle-kit's control lives in its OWN schema, drizzle). Result: mix ecto.migrate hit duplicate_table on the engine tables that survived, and pnpm db:migrate — worse, WITHOUT any error — saw drizzle-kit's control intact, concluded it had already run everything and recreated NO api table. Delete/Reset total now drop engine and drizzle too, in that order, before public.
documents.s: DEVELOPMENT TOOL — pnpm bootstrap

documents.t: Five independent waves, run in parallel by contested file, coming from real use of the project screen — none planned in advance. The sixth wave of the same program (complete translation of product and documentation, i18n) is bigger than the five together; its FOUNDATION (Wave 6a — mechanism, no content translation yet) has already closed: react-i18next+i18next on the web (en became the app's default language, pt-BR kept — RN-425), a locale column in users embedded in the login/refresh payload, a new AccountPage (/account) proving the mechanism, and Docusaurus with i18n.defaultLocale: 'en'/locales: ['en', 'pt-BR'] — the current pt-BR snapshot of docs/ is already preserved in website/i18n/pt-BR/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/current/. Wave 6b (mass extraction of the interface + translation of docs/) advanced a lot on 2026-08-22, in four parallel fronts — see CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased/ Documentation) for the detail of each — but it has NOT YET closed: missing are docs/business-rules.md (only the front-matter was translated; the body, with hundreds of RNs, remains 100% in Portuguese — it is the largest file of the whole doc and grows faster than it can be translated in passing) and a residual slice of smaller .tsx components. When it really closes, this section gets the final summary and the rest of CLAUDE.md (Stack, "Documentation") is fully revised to record English as the real primary language. Grouped tab ruler: 11 loose tabs became 6 at the top — Overview, Agents ▾ (Executors, Criativo, Chat, Insights), Dev ▾ (Code, PRs, Approvals), Documentation ▾ (Backlog, Architecture), Spend, Settings — via a new GroupedTabs (apps/web/src/components/ ui/GroupedTabs.tsx), built ON TOP of the generic Tabs, which remains without groups for the other screens. ChaveDeAba remains flat — only the presentation became grouped, so as not to touch the ?tab= deep link. Chat and RAG Chat become ONE tab (ProjectChatShell.tsx) with an internal segmented control ("Converse"/"Search") — the business distinction between the two (RN-202: conversing activates an agent and spends the owner's key per turn; RAG is a read over an index, without an agent) didn't change, only the UI container. PRs tab, project-wide: ProjectApprovalsTab scoped "PRs under review" to the most recent session — the review of a PR from a previous session vanished from the screen as soon as a new session proposed another one. The new prs tab lists straight from the git provider (never per session) and cross-references with a pending proposed_action via findPendingByProject, new, alongside the already existing session-scoped method — the decision uses the sessionId of the action ITSELF, never latestSession (RN-423). It is the first real producer of git_merge through the UI; the protected-branch lock (RN-154) remains absolute and untouched — the "Merge" button only PROPOSES, human approval remains the only way to execute. Architecture tab: extracted from the Overview (module_map, C4 diagram, ADRs, pending items), which keeps a condensed summary + link. The design system's first lightbox — Modal gained size="full" — to enlarge the C4 diagram (SVG, without quality loss) (RN-424). Local folder navigation via the Runner (RN-422, ADR 0104): revises ADR 0072 (which had explicitly refused a folder picker) WITHOUT editing it — navigation exists, but through the Runner, which already runs with the user's real privilege on their machine, never through the api enumerating the container's filesystem. Two new events on the already existing channel (fs_list_dir/fs_home_dir), pure relay by the engine, same pattern as the PTY. FolderBrowserModal works where the project already exists. At creation (NewProjectWizard.tsx), the gap stayed declared until ADR 0108: in mounted mode the project is still only born at confirmation (the path validation touches disk there), but in runner mode "Browse folder..." now creates the project IN ADVANCE — reused by an identity snapshot instead of duplicated on each click — so it can anchor the channel ticket before the confirmation (RN-437, ADR 0108). A new RunnerOnboardingPanel (shared with the Terminal tab) replaces the raw <code> from before. apps/runner got a README — actually publishing to npm/packaging a signed binary remains out of scope, declared in the README. The folder explorer itself became three columns (shortcuts, a list where one click selects/double click enters, a details panel — RN-436), following the product owner's visual reference. The PO's carousel bug fixed (RN-421): the batch of pending promotions depended on a scan over the last 200 events (useSessionEvents) — in a long session, the proposal left the window and the carousel degraded to a single card or vanished. The same class of bug that RN-180 had already fixed for ContextAside; the source is now useBacklog (complete, no window), with a per-story fallback when the backlog hasn't answered yet.
documents.s: Grouped tabs, project-wide PRs, local folder via Runner, the PO's carousel (2026-08-20)

documents.t: It closes the backlog item open since FASE 13c. CreateHandoffUseCase remains the ONLY place that writes toAgent (ADR 0038) — it only gained an optional actor?: Actor, defaulting to the usual {kind:'agent', id: fromAgent}. RequestManualHandoffUseCase (a new route, POST .../sessions/:sessionId/handoffs, role developer) validates toAgent against addressableAgents() — a CLOSED catalog (area leads ∪ SOLO_CONVERSATIONAL_AGENTS), stricter than assertHandoffTargetAllowed (which only refuses a subagent) — resolves fromAgent through the session's most recent agent.activated (sentinel "usuario" when there is none), and writes actor: {kind:'user'}. The handoff is born offered just like an automatic one: the already existing acceptance card (SessionPage.tsx) picks it up on its own, zero change in the acceptance path. Investigation BEFORE coding found ux-designer (ADR 0087) in the SAME situation as the Staff (ADR 0088) that motivated the item: a message/2 clause ready in agent_command_controller.ex, no human path to it. Both entered AGENTES_DE_CHAT in the same change — infra/qa remain out, the same pattern already documented there (leads without kickoff/1 or a message clause). Declared, not hidden: the mirror of SOLO_CONVERSATIONAL_AGENTS on the web side (apps/web/src/lib/agents.ts) is NOT cross-checked by test with the api's — diverging produces, at worst, a stale option in the selector that the backend still refuses with 400.
documents.s: Manual handoff to an agent of choice (RN-440/441, ADR 0109)

documents.t: An approved backlog item ("Older backlog", docs/explanation/backlog.md). agent_areas gets budget_micros/spent_micros, mirroring exactly max_parallel — same row, same decision owner (maintainer), without a new table. It is a THIRD ADDITIVE ceiling alongside project and session (CheckBudgetGateUseCase checks all three in parallel, any one blocked already refuses), not the model binding cascade of ADR 0064 (session > agent > area > project > workspace, "the most specific wins") — the two mechanisms share the word "area" and nothing else; not confusing the two is the central point of ADR 0110, in the same way RN-101/ADR 0063 already separates the owner's view from the member's view in the spend report. spent_micros always adds up when the actor belongs to an area (lead or member, via areaDo — a pure function, without touching the database for an actor without an area), with or without budget_micros configured (null is the default, no ceiling).
documents.s: Budget per area — closes the cut of ADR 0038 (RN-443, ADR 0110)

documents.t: A backlog item of ADR 0104 ("standalone binary, pkg/bun build --compile"), companion of ADR 0106 (distribution via npm). The product owner's explicit decision: a truly SINGLE binary, a complete matrix with Windows since v1 — the cheaper alternative ("binary + a node-pty-native/ folder next to it") was offered and refused. bun build --compile embeds node-pty's native .node through with { type: 'file' } and extracts it to a REAL TEMPORARY directory at runtime (native-pty-loader.ts) — necessary because node-pty resolves its own addon through a require() of a COMPUTED path (lib/utils.js#loadNativeModule), which Bun can't embed on its own (the build passes, the runtime throws Cannot find module, tested before designing the fix). Five platforms (linux-x64/linux-arm64/darwin-x64/darwin-arm64/win32-x64), each one built on its NATIVE runner (.github/workflows/build-runner-binaries.yml, final tag trigger, same pattern as publish-runner.yml), the binary attached to the already existing Release. Honest validation, per platform: only linux-x64 was actually executed in this environment (build:bin+smoke:bin green, repeatedly — it was by running the real binary that the two bugs below showed up). The other four — Windows especially, with THREE native files instead of one — were reasoned about by reading node-pty's source code, never executed on a real machine of that OS; their first real run is the NEXT version tag, not this PR. No per-platform fallback was applied preventively — nothing in this investigation PROVED that any of the five doesn't work this way; if a real tag shows that it does, that becomes a new item, not today's assumption. Two defects found only by running the compiled binary, not by reading the API: --external node-pty needs to be in the bun build command even without any static import of node-pty in the code — the fallback await import(...) (used only outside the binary) is discovered and embedded by Bun anyway, and fails at runtime with a misleading error; and the auto-run guard (ADR 0106) needed a second branch — process.argv[1] inside the binary is a VIRTUAL path (/$bunfs/root/...) that realpathSync can't reach, throwing ENOENT outside any try/catch before main() is attempted.
documents.s: The runner's standalone binary (2026-08-23, RN-451/452, ADR 0112)

documents.t: It closes the correction that the runner's Wave 1 (ADR 0104) had recorded in docs/explanation/backlog.md: item 4 of that ADR said that converting execution_mode between container/mounted/runner in a project that already exists "is now allowed without recreating the project", and that was false until here — UpdateProjectDto still excludes both fields on purpose. PUT projects/:projectId/execution-mode (maintainer, ConvertProjectExecutionModeUseCase) is a DEDICATED route, not a loosened PATCH: it orchestrates the migration instead of just switching the column. It refuses with 409 while any dev agent of the project (in ANY session, read straight from engine.dev_agent_states by project_id, the same path as RN-409) isn't idle — idle_tripped COUNTS as active here, unlike RN-409's "online" criterion, because the agent still has workspace_root captured in memory waiting for human unblocking (RN-447). PermissionsFileStore gained move(from, to): the content of permissions.json never changes, only the physical path, because projectScopeRoot derives from the (mode, path) pair (RN-448). Leaving container with a provisioned container, the lifecycle (ADR 0081) is taken to removed — via stopped first if it was running — BEFORE the column changes, because RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase refuses a transition outside container mode; entering container never auto-provisions (RN-449). workspaceVerifiedAt is reset on every real conversion, including going back to runner with a path that looks the same (RN-450). The same (mode, path) as today is a no-op — it doesn't even check for an active dev agent. Declared consequence, not hidden: the conversion NEVER copies the code already written between the old root and the new one. That is safe for what was already COMMITTED — the engine derives the worktree from the bare repo from scratch (Engine.Actions.Workspace.ensure!/4) whenever the destination folder isn't yet marked ready, so the next agent rebuilds the working tree in the new root from the real git. What does NOT survive is an UNCOMMITTED diff in the abandoned worktree — it stays orphaned on the old disk, never migrated nor deleted. The active dev agent ceiling (RN-447) reduces the risk (it never converts with a working agent) but doesn't eliminate it: an idle agent between tasks may be sitting on a dirty diff, and nothing here inspects the working tree's cleanliness before converting.
documents.s: Converting the execution_mode of an existing project (RN-447..450, ADR 0111)

documents.t: The product owner's request: attach a folder from the user's OWN machine to a project as a READ reference for the agents — without the brabo-runner CLI (ADR 0103). Explicitly NOT project execution/workspace: execution_mode: runner (ADR 0104) needs the CLI because it needs a real HOST path for the container to route commands; this is more like "attaching files to a conversation". The browser reads the CONTENT (File.text()) and the RELATIVE path (File.webkitRelativePath) of the chosen files — never an absolute host path (the File API doesn't expose one, to any site), and that's why ADR 0113 is explicit that it is NOT a revision of what ADRs 0072/0107 refused: those refused RESOLVING a host path from the browser; here there is no path at all to resolve, only bytes the browser already had the right to read. chunks.scope (ADR 0079/0080) gains a FOURTH value, 'local' (migration 0052, ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE, additive — the two CHECKs of migration 0045 are already written as "it's session or it isn't", so local falls on the same side as docs/adr without a new CHECK). IndexLocalFolderUseCase mirrors IndexProjectDocsUseCase closely — Markdown-aware chunking for .md/.mdx, RagEmbeddingService, a chunk without a vector instead of failing when the embedding drops (RN-233) — but REJECTS (400) the whole upload when the AGGREGATE ceilings overflow (number of files, summed bytes), never truncates silently: it's a SINGLE gesture by the user with a folder picker on screen, not a background scan. An individual file that's too big or has an unrecognized extension is only SKIPPED (filesSkipped), never brings down the batch (RN-456). origemDoChunk didn't need any new branch: local carries sourcePath like docs/adr, falls into the kind: 'file' that the citation already knew how to render. It never enters the generic "Reindex now" (RN-457): ReindexProjectUseCase reindexes by reading from a source the SERVER can revisit (the project's repository, the event log); local has no source at all to revisit — the text only exists in the browser of whoever attached it. Reattaching the folder (a new upload to POST .../rag/local, maintainer) IS the resync mechanism, a deliberately separate button, with a cross-comment in both use cases pointing at each other and at ADR 0113, so that a future "fix" doesn't wire the two back together and erase the user's material. The coverage (RagCoverage.local) has its OWN shape — there's no "total in the repository" to compare — and lastAttachedAt is the ONLY real exception to the "never Xmin" rule (RN-237): a real MAX(chunks.created_at), not a guess (RN-458).
documents.s: A local folder attached as a RAG Chat reference (2026-08-23, RN-455..457, ADR 0113)

documents.t: The product owner's request: the Session screen starts showing, ABOVE the composer, a strip that narrates in human language what a conversational agent (Criativo, PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead, UX Designer, Staff) is doing DURING the turn — visual reference: Claude Code's status line. The thread only receives the reply bubble AFTER the turn ends; the rule belongs to the CHAT (Phoenix channel) and applies only to the six conversational ones — the consultative chat without an active agent (SSE, streamChatMessage) keeps the usual streaming bubble, untouched. Mechanism: the six servers already emitted a DURABLE tool.call; they now also broadcast(state, "tool.call", %{tool: name, agent: @agent}) — EPHEMERAL, without args (RN-096/RN-412) — for the channel to deliver in real time. There is no shared behaviour/macro between the six dispatch_tools (four distinct structural shapes, confirmed by a complete read) — the change was six edits adapted to each one's local shape, not a refactoring. On the web side, a PURE reducer (reduzirAtividadeDoTurno/lib/atividade-do-turno.ts) accumulates the agent.delta as current text; when tool.call arrives, it archives the non-empty current text as a narration line, resets it, and always adds a tool line with fraseDaFerramenta(tool) (a dictionary of the 19 tools, lib/narracao-de-ferramentas.ts, without its own RN). Its OWN flag (turnoViaCanal, never derived from statusAgent/streamingAgent, which go through legitimately null windows in the middle of the turn) decides whether the strip appears or the old bubble — never both. Presentation rule (history): agruparNarracoesDoTurno, a new pure pass after afundarDesfechos (RN-172) in the same useMemo — consecutive agent.responses of the same turno+autor become a compact Disclosure ("Turn steps · N"), only the last stays intact outside it. turno === 0 (the sentinel prologue of turnoDoSeq) stays OUT of the grouping — old fixtures stack agent.response without a turn boundary to test another mechanism (RN-138/RN-177), and without the exclusion the new grouping would produce a Disclosure inside a Disclosure there. afundarDesfechos itself didn't change. A finding along the way, scope extended by the product owner's decision: the investigation found that FOUR of the six servers (Arquiteto, Dev Lead, UX Designer, Staff) ended SILENTLY at the iteration ceiling — defp run_turn(state, remaining) when remaining <= 0, do: state, without any event, contradicting the permanent rule that an agent loop doesn't end silently. Only the PO already emitted toolloop.limit_reached (RN-166); the Criativo deliberately diverges with agent.error (a decision documented in the code itself). The four fixed now emit toolloop.limit_reached, the same event as the PO (RN-459).

documents.t: It closes what RN-491 declared pending: Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor gets the FIFTH outcome, :executar_no_container — an execution_mode: container project with a REGISTERED running row (Engine.Containers.ProjectContainerLifecycle, a direct read, the same pattern as Engine.Projects.Project) — and the command crosses engine → api (POST internal/projects/:projectId/container-exec, ExecutarComandoNoContainerUseCase) → broker (ContainerBrokerPort.exec, the FIRST real caller of the last of the five operations of ADR 0128/0130), running via docker exec instead of a local System.cmd. cwd is translated from the HOST path to inside /work in the engine, BEFORE the call — confirmed in code to be the SAME physical directory Workspace.ensure!/4 already writes (the dev agent's worktree changes neither place nor mechanism). BrokerRecusouError/BrokerIndisponivelError/a transport failure become a normal failed_result, never a crash nor a silent fallback outside the container (RN-486: a registered running never guarantees the container is up). A terminal INSIDE the container gets an auto-approval FLOOR (ProposeActionUseCase/decide.ts, containerExecutionActive) — the five absolute ceilings and the usual lexical scope keep running on top, byte for byte

documents.t: container_start/container_stop/container_remove get a SECOND execution path, branched by executionMode: container keeps going through the broker (unchanged); mounted/runner now ask the connected RUNNER, through THREE new pairs on the Phoenix channel (container_start/_result, container_stop/_result, container_remove/_result, the same mold as exec/exec_result) — EngineWeb.ContainerCommandController passes it on to the RunnerRouter, which the runner serves with DockerViaCli (ITS Docker, @brabo/docker-port, which gets real use beyond --self-test-docker). The image is READ (ObterSpecDeContainerUseCase, the same use case as the broker's), never re-elected. "No runner"/"timeout" (RunnerNaoConectadoError) and "runner refused" (RunnerRecusouContainerError) become a named failed, never an exception. Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor didn't get a new outcome — it already routed every command of a connected runner project to the channel unconditionally; the host-vs-container choice is INTERNAL to the runner (EstadoDoRunner.containerAtivo, tratarExec routes via docker exec with cwd translated by prefix swapping, cwdParaContainer). guard.ts/RN-434 now covers the bind-mount without ANY new validation — the mount IS the root already confirmed at the CLI's startup
