documents.t: offeredHandoff filters the thread's card by AGENTES_DE_CHAT, which excludes infra — and the filter is RIGHT (the engine has no message clause for the Infra Lead; widening it would make the screen offer a thread that doesn't exist and the composer send a message to the Criativo). The defect was the consequence, which the code's own comment recorded as accepted: acceptHandoff had ONE consumer only, behind that filter, so the OfferInfraHandoffUseCase handoff stayed offered forever, the Infra Lead was never activated, propose_container_start was never called and NO project in any mode ever got a container up. Fix: its OWN actionable card, outside the thread, on the fixed strip between the scrolling area and the composer — the same one that already hosts the manual handoff and declares itself the place for handoff actions that aren't conversation —, calling the acceptHandoff that already existed, closed by the same activeFor. The Infra handoff.offered remains NARRATED in the thread as a mute divider
documents.s: The Infra handoff could be accepted by no screen at all (D0) (RN-499)

documents.t: Creating a mounted project required a bind-mount line written BY HAND in api AND engine plus a restart of both — which kills every agent turn, terminal socket and LLM call in flight in the installation, to onboard ONE project. BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE is born: ONE base, configured once by the operator, mounted by IDENTITY ($X:$X) in both services, with all mounted projects inside it and NOTHING edited per project. Identity and not a fixed mountpoint because workspace_path is typed by the user and shown back to them — and it is what keeps projectScopeRoot/workspace_dir/2 correct without new code. Its OWN variable (a namespace collision with the UNIQUE workspace_dir_name would git init in another project's folder; opposite owner; the base is browsable and the managed root shouldn't be). ABSENT is normal: projectsBase: null (GET workspaces/:id/projects-base, maintainer) and the mode isn't offered. And pnpm dev REFUSES to start with the base overlapping the checkout — the only possible check, because the api compares against /workspace. Two declared costs: a symlink under the base and a single base
documents.s: The single base of mounted projects (PR 1, BREAKING) (ADR 0141, RN-500)

documents.t: A mounted project couldn't get ANY container, because of two independent blocks — the api sent every non-container mode to the RUNNER (which requires a connected brabo-runner) and the broker refused non-container at the source. The two were about GEOMETRY, not the mode's name, and ADR 0141's single base changed the geometry. The branching becomes by DESTINATION: container AND mounted → broker, only runner → runner (and container_stop/_remove change TOGETHER with _start, otherwise it comes up on the server and stops on the user's machine). The ADR 0130 invariant doesn't move — no absolute path crosses the network: the broker gets a SECOND root (BRABO_PROJECTS_HOST_BASE) and the api sends a DISCRIMINATED locator (gerenciada |montada |indisponivel) saying against which root the relative segment applies. THREE variants because indisponivel has two different fixes (runner × a legacy mounted outside the base), and a missing root is NEVER supplied by the other one. mounted ELECTS the image like container — the broker composes from artifact.project_image, so an unrecorded election is an inert election (ADR 0133 in a second mode)
documents.s: Container for a mounted project (PR 3) (ADR 0144, RN-503)

documents.t: In a real run of exp001, TEN dev tasks got stuck at once — and the finding wasn't the folder that failed, it was that nothing ordered container before dev agent. Engine.Dev.AgentIo.try_claim/2 — the SINGLE claim point — now queries ProjectContainerLifecycle.running?/1 (the predicate ADR 0134 already had) BEFORE calling the api: without a REGISTERED running row, the agent falls into :idle, persists and emits dev.blocked_by_container. In the ENGINE and not only in the api's activate-execution because REHYDRATION reaches try_claim/2 without going through any route (init/1 → finish_restart_recovery/1). :idle and NOT a new status, for the reason try_claim/2's own docblock already recorded since Fase 12b — it is the only state from which a wake still rescues, and all the guards of handle_info/2 rely on that; whoever distinguishes "empty queue" from "no container" is the EVENT, never the status. The wake comes through the outbox: RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase publishes container.running in the SAME transaction that writes the arrival at running, in a NEW aggregate_type (container, the third one Engine.Outbox.Drain reads) instead of borrowing task, with the PROJECT as the aggregateId; the message delivered is the {:wake, :became_claimable} that already existed. Second half: TerminalExecutor stops degrading silently — container without running fell into System.cmd INSIDE the engine process, and now it REFUSES, with mounted in the same branch
documents.s: Dev agents only after the container (PR 7) (ADR 0143, RN-502)

documents.t: The rule "promotion is --no-ff" was broken THREE times (#367, #394, #464 — the third was the PR that fixed the first two). The finding: the detection ALREADY existed and ALREADY worked (tag-release failed the first two with the right message) — what was missing was WHOM to ring, because a push workflow that fails on a permanent branch has no PR to go red on and the repo had zero issues. tag-release gets the avisar job, which opens an issue (and comments on the already open one, never duplicates) with github.token and never with the PAT — an invalid PAT is one of the failures it reports — and that stopped being hypothetical: the BRABO_BOT_TOKEN expired on 2026-09-03 at night, failed two tag-release runs, and was rotated on 2026-09-04; v4.0.0 stamped and TRIGGERED the Release, which only happens with a valid PAT (a tag created with GITHUB_TOKEN doesn't trigger a workflow). The rule now covers dev NARROWLY: the only defect is a PR that brought a NEW EDGE (head was a merge whose second parent wasn't in the base), never the squash of a work PR, which is the convention. Turning off squash in the repo was MEASURED and refused (it would tax every PR and touch changelog.mjs, which runs --no-merges)
documents.s: A pipeline merge alarm with a recipient (ADR 0139)

documents.t: decision_record reuses the GENERIC pattern of emit_artifact/ArtifactSchemas (the same as note/business_rule) instead of the dedicated one of project_image/c4_diagram — a decision is an append-only log, never a "current" one that gets replaced. PO, Arquiteto, Dev Lead, UX Designer and Staff get the tool (alias + tool_specs + run_tool/3 + the same sentence in system_prompt/1); the Criativo already had emit_artifact since Fase 3b and only got the new type, with no change to it. Distinct from open_adr_pr (only the Arquiteto, a real commit + PR + human approval): the two COEXIST for different scales of decision. Out of scope, declared: execution agents (ToolLoop, without a common harness) and the tie-in with the Infra Lead — emitting decision_record when proposing container_start_via_runner — which depends on a tool from another front of the same plan, in a separate branch
documents.s: The conversational agents' decision artifact (Front 3, generic slice) (RN-505)

documents.t: Clicking "always allow" on an action of a dev-<modulo> wrote to permissions.json, the WHOLE PROJECT scope — it released the same command for any other agent. It now writes to agent_autonomy(projeto, agente, tipo), the SAME mechanism already used for the 3 git actions seeded on execution activation. dev-lead (leads the area, isn't a member of it) and any non-modular actor keep going to the usual permissions.json; the two absolute ceilings (a terminal with an external effect/privileged command, container_remove) keep refusing the whole click BEFORE the new branch. No migration: old entries remain in permissions.json, a conscious decision
documents.s: "Always allow" separated per module Dev Agent (RN-509)

documents.t: runner routed every approved terminal to the CLI as soon as a verified workspace connected runner matched, without checking for a running container — without Docker up, the runner fell on its own to the pure HOST, the SAME silent fallback that ADR 0143 had already closed for container/mounted. Engine.Runners.RunnerReadiness unifies the THREE preconditions (verified, connected, running container) with two consumers: TerminalExecutor and the materialization of the dev agent's worktree, which stops trying a LOCAL File.mkdir_p!/git init against the HOST path (the gap open since RN-478) and starts running INSIDE the real container, on the user's machine, through the SAME exec/exec_result channel (Engine.Actions.Workspace.RunnerGit, new) — WorktreeManager forks by the same criterion, and the periodic cleanup job silently SKIPS a runner project without a ready runner now. The exec protocol gets an optional env for the git credential (ADR 0056) to travel in the environment of the HOST's child process — merged over process.env, never passed on to docker exec nor logged. container_start stops serving runner (its payload, with image election, never made sense there); container_start_via_runner is born — a schema with only rationale, it brings up the already decided image —, with the Infra Lead's new tool refusing LOCALLY (without HTTP) before proposing blindly
documents.s: Docker becomes a real prerequisite of Runner mode (RN-507/508, ADR 0145)

documents.t: The "decision artifact" and the "always allow per Dev Agent" merged 2 minutes apart, each one allocating RN-505 without seeing the other; "always allow per Dev Agent" was renumbered to RN-509 (docs/business-rules.md, CHANGELOG, the comment in approve-always-action.use-case.ts and in ApprovalCard.test.tsx), freeing the {#rn-505} anchor for the decision_record. Found along with it: the 505→507/506→508 renumbering done during the conflict resolution of another PR (Docker/runner, ADR 0145) had been left INCOMPLETE — three mentions of "RN-505" remained in this very file, also fixed to "RN-507"
documents.s: RN-505 duplicated in dev, fixed

documents.t: The join of the terminal:<projectId> channel was mute on BOTH sides — the runner sent {} and the server did _params —, so the server had no way to know whether the binary on the other side understands a new message, and the defect was the worst possible: the message arrives, the handler doesn't exist and NOTHING happens, without error and without log. Now the runner DECLARES in the params (Engine.Runners.Capacidades, vocabulary exec/pty/espelho) and the server GRANTS the intersection with what it KNOWS, in socket.assigns and NEVER in a table (a capability is a property of that CONNECTION). The runner declares only exec and pty — declaring espelho without implementing it is exactly the defect the negotiation prevents; it comes in as a vocabulary NAME and nothing more, and session 6 implements it. Absent/empty params are the LEGACY binary and grant {exec, pty} — a FACT, not benevolence: they are the two functions the runner was born with, and refusing legacy would be breaking/ and MAJOR. Unknown is IGNORED (a runner NEWER than the engine connects); required-and-not-declared refuses the join NAMING the missing one, BEFORE the Registry — a mechanism implemented and tested that today does NOT fire (runner requires exec, which every binary has; nothing requires espelho yet), and that is the design. The half that delivers value TODAY: a message without the capability is REFUSED with a named reply — exec replies in the exec_result format (126 + cause) instead of the RunnerRouter waiting for the timeout, and pty_* becomes pty_error in the tab instead of vanishing. RunnerReadiness byte for byte as it is
documents.s: FASE 28 (session 5) — the local agent's join stops being mute (RN-514, ADR 0147 point 1)

documents.t: The espelho capability goes from a vocabulary name to code on BOTH sides. The DESTINATION travels in the join GRANT (the reply stops being empty for :runner: %{espelho: %{destino: ...}}), lives only in that connection and the runner REFUSES mirror_sync for a destination not granted — never global configuration nor a variable, which would make project B's artifact land in project A's folder. A non-null mirror_path now REQUIRES the capability, and that is the FIRST real firing of RN-514's refusal mechanism: an old binary in a project with a destination STOPS connecting, named and fatal — opt-in, cost declared in the ADR. espelho-guard.ts is born a SIBLING of guard.ts (reuses the three helpers and the double pass, inherits the TOCTOU caveat in writing) and refuses the ADR's three things; a finding while implementing: realpathMaisProximo falls back to the ancestor, and since the destination almost never exists, collapsing both sides would make /base-outra and /base become / — the second pass resolves the ancestor and PUTS BACK the suffix. ONE direction and it NEVER deletes: a file deleted at the origin STAYS at the destination (the user's folder is accumulation, not a replica). What gets copied is the GIT LIST (tracked + untracked-not-ignored), with no exclusion list of its own; a failing git becomes a NAMED error, never a fallback cp -r; a nested git repo (the dev agent's worktree) comes back as ONE entry and isn't descended into, and a symlink at the origin is skipped. Its OWN predicate (Engine.Runners.Espelho), TWO preconditions and NEVER RunnerReadiness with a flag — runner_readiness.ex stays byte for byte. Trigger: the COMMIT, a named moment, fire-and-forget and never a watcher; "end of an agent turn" stays DECLARED and not wired, because there is no unambiguous hook
documents.s: FASE 28 (session 6, half B) — the mirror comes into existence (RN-516, ADR 0147 points 2/3/4/8)

documents.t: RN-512 took the broker out of profiles so it would be up in dev, and it NEVER came up: corepack prepare ran as ROOT at build (cache in /root/.cache), the container runs as uid 1000, and without a cache corepack tries to DOWNLOAD pnpm in a service whose only network is internal: true — EAI_AGAIN registry.npmjs.org, Exited (1) five seconds later. Without a healthcheck, up --wait said Healthy and the reset total announced "reset complete" with the process dead; while there was a profile, whoever brought up the broker was someone already watching it. The fix takes the registry out of RUNTIME and does NOT open the network (the first of the five layers of ADR 0130): COREPACK_HOME prepared at build with the runtime uid's owner, pnpm install as a BUILD step, and — because the three node_modules volumes cover what the image installed and Docker only seeds an EMPTY volume — an entrypoint that reconciles them against a copy outside /workspace, stamped with the sha256 of the build's lockfile (the same stamp WARNS that the image fell behind, without refusing to start). A healthcheck on the service, from inside the container. Production didn't suffer from this and doesn't change
documents.s: The broker that never came up (fix of RN-512) (RN-512, ADR 0130/0146)

documents.t: brabo-runner service install|uninstall|status, and the precedent was ZERO (no mention of systemd/launchd in apps/runner/; the model was foreground killed by SIGINT). USER level always — systemd --user/LaunchAgent —, and root is a REFUSAL, not a warning: guard.ts's docblock declares "runs with HIS privileges" as the premise of the three real boundaries, and a root service would leave the best-effort cwd guard as the only thing between an approved command and the disk. Windows is a NAMED refusal (a third mechanism, not a variation of the two). One unit per PROJECT because the server already enforces one runner per project — naming by folder would create two units that never come up together, and the second would appear as a connection failure instead of an installation error; on Linux the file goes where systemd LOOKS ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user, otherwise ~/.config). Restart=on-abnormal and NEVER on-failure (in the plist, KeepAlive/Crashed): the runner's exit 1 is a fatal join refusal (RN-514) or an exhausted attempt ceiling, and restarting would be the loop the CLI refuses to do on its own. The service authenticates by DEVICE KEY and never by token — writing it into a unit would leave it on disk, and this CLI never wrote a credential to disk. uninstall removes the THREE by reading the UNIT's folder and never the cwd (without a unit, only with --dir — guessing would delete another project's key), and SAYS that the key left the disk and was NOT revoked on the server. status answers FOUR states with their own sentence and code (0/3/4/5), and the first answer comes from DISK — that's why it stays right on a machine without a manager; a failed spawn never becomes "the manager said no". BRB-031 does NOT close here
documents.s: FASE 28 (session 7) — the local agent becomes a user service (RN-518, ADR 0147 point 5)

documents.t: container_start_via_runner (RN-508, ADR 0145) ended failed 100% of the time — "container specification refused at projectId: expected non-empty text, got undefined" —, and in a real run of exp004 what was seen was the EFFECT: ten dev tasks with no agent claiming them. That block was RIGHT (RN-507 and RN-502/ADR 0143 refuse without a REGISTERED running container); what was wrong was the previous step. EspecificacaoDeContainerParaRunner was born with NINE fields and especificacaoValidada (packages/docker-port) always required TEN — the data was at hand in SpecDeContainer.projectId and simply wasn't copied; the engine passes the map on OPAQUELY, so nothing was lost in the middle. By contrast the BROKER always worked because it FETCHES the spec from the api and receives the whole SpecDeContainer — that's why only runner mode broke. Three green suites didn't catch it because each link built its own fixture: nobody tested the CHAIN. It comes in — the payload the REAL use case composes crossing the REAL validator, and the SET of fields locked (raizDoProjeto is the only one the api doesn't send) — in the api suite, through a RELATIVE import, the only place where both sides exist alive; the api-nao-consome-docker-port invariant stays green and was EXTENDED to fail a relative import from src/. Siblings checked and RIGHT: container_stop/container_remove send only workspaceDirName, which is all that nomeDeWorkspaceValidado asks for
documents.s: The runner's spec went without projectId, and the path NEVER brought up a container (RN-508, ADR 0145)

documents.t: Anamnese and Psicólogo had been PAUSED since 2026-08-10 and three places called the pause reversible — the docblocks of AnamneseSchedulerWorker.enabled?/0/PsychologistWorker.enabled?/0 ("Turning it back on is X=true and restarting the engine") and docs/reference/configuration.md. It wasn't reversible in ANY environment: the environment: of the engine service mapped the THIRTEEN Anamnese/Psicólogo variables — all cost CEILINGS — and neither of the two PRODUCT ones, and docker compose does NOT pass on the host's environment, so ANAMNESE_ENABLED=true in .env was inert and runtime.exs fell back to the "false" default SILENTLY. Measured in the dev container: [true] [] []. Likely origin: when the default became false, nobody needed the variable to TURN IT OFF — only whoever tries to TURN IT ON discovers the wire doesn't exist, months later. The EIGHT boolean flags (System.get_env("X", "true"|"false") == "true") go into BOTH composes with the SAME default as the code — the four extra ones (START_MODEL_SYNC, START_GATE_RESCUE, the two GRAPH_*) because they are the same defect, found by the mechanism itself, and excepting them would require four excuses. Zero change in behavior: the product decision to keep both off stays byte for byte, what comes into existence is the SWITCH. The mechanism is scripts/ci/flags-do-engine-no-compose.spec.ts, which DERIVES the list from runtime.exs (the other 50 variables are ceilings with a good default and release things, legitimately absent) and demands an equal default only in the DEV compose — the production one turns off the background agents on purpose. deploy/k8s/ does NOT change, for coherence: the layer that breaks doesn't exist there
documents.s: The pause that couldn't be undone (RN-540)

documents.t: Installing Brabo is THREE disconnected gestures (compose with five secrets by hand, runner through the browser with chmod +x, pnpm bootstrap that only exists in a checkout), and FASE 28 refused in writing the one-line installer while the artifacts weren't signed (BRB-005) — that's why the phase signs BEFORE installing. Four Proposed ADRs: keyless cosign signing by DIGEST plus ONE signed checksums.txt, never five signatures (0149); the installer invoked by sh -c "$(curl …)" and NEVER curl|sh, because with the pipe the script IS the stdin and consent dies (0150); the runner's consented base, reusing dentroDoEscopo and the per-SEGMENT loop refusal of espelho-guard.ts instead of a fourth copy of the rule (0151); and backup/restore against compose (0152). The measurement corrected FIVE points of the original scope: workspace.verified does NOT exist (what exists is workspace_confirm, and it is ONE-WAY), point 5 of ADR 0146 versions consentir-base.mjs and not an install.sh, docker-compose.prod.yml doesn't consume GHCR and declares itself a VALIDATION compose, make test-restore is a Kubernetes path with a Postgres-only backup, and "one runner per project" is enforced in FIVE independent places — which took the per-machine runner out of this phase, to FASE 30. Its own finding: git_local_repos isn't in any backup, and losing it is losing the code of the local projects. docs/reference/brb.md is born — and the finding is that the BRB register isn't the repository's: it lives in the maintainer's vault, with 33 items, and here only two ids appeared in prose. Measuring: BRB-032 and BRB-033 describe defects that no longer reproduce, and BRB-004 isn't what the id suggests — it asks for third-party images by DIGEST, not the tag #419 pinned. The file here keeps the EVIDENCE (measured state, file:line); the vault remains the owner of the finding. Range RN-524..538 and ADRs 0149-0152, skipping what is IN FLIGHT: three collisions observed at the same moment (ADR 0148 ×2, RN-522 ×2, RN-523 ×2), resolved later by the DATE criterion — whoever allocated first kept the number, and the branches of 08/09 became ADR 0153, RN-539 and RN-540
documents.s: FASE 29 (session 1) — one-line installation, planning only (ADR 0149-0152, fase-29-instalacao-de-uma-linha.md)

documents.t: The product signed nothing: cosign/sigstore/attestation didn't exist in .github/, scripts/ or docker/, and the only provenance was the --provenance of the runner's npm package. release.yml published the four images without id-token: write; build-runner-binaries.yml uploaded the five binaries with gh release upload and nothing more — while the sha256sum -cs that already existed verify third-party binaries, the pattern the repository knew how to apply and never applied to itself. Now the images are signed by DIGEST (never by tag, a moving pointer) and the binaries get ONE signed checksums.txt, in a checksums job that waits for the matrix — not five signatures, because whoever verifies four and forgets the fifth doesn't know they forgot. The job is if: always() on purpose (fail-fast: false in the matrix) and names what the manifest doesn't cover. Both workflows verify before publishing. Keyless because of the house's history: a private key would be one more CI secret, and a PAT has already expired silently (ADR 0139). A verification procedure in the runbook, with the two --certificate-* flags mandatory — without them cosign accepts a valid signature from ANYONE. Closes BRB-005 for images and binaries; left out, declared, are OS code-signing and the download proxy
documents.s: FASE 29 (session 2) — the pipeline signs what it publishes (RN-524, ADR 0149)

documents.t: install.sh is born at the ROOT, versioned and served by the Release. The form is sh -c "$(curl …)" and never curl|sh, for a MECHANICAL reason: with the pipe, the process's stdin IS the download, and every read reads bytes of the script itself or hits EOF — an installer that doesn't ask would choose on its own where to create a folder on someone's machine. It VERIFIES ITS OWN ORIGIN (the signature of RN-524's checksums.txt, and its own hash INSIDE the verified manifest), with cosign pinned and checked by sha256sum against the hash written in the script; DETECTION names what it found before asking; without a TTY it reports and exits 0; and it never deletes a user folder — the projects base and the mirror folder stay outside any confirmation, by the mirror's rule (RN-516). A marker in $XDG_STATE_HOME/brabo/, never in ~/.brabo/, which is PER PROJECT. It doesn't install anything in this version, and SAYS so instead of ending silently. --print-plan/--print-state expose the decision without a TTY, without network and without effect — the mold of bootstrap.sh's --print-commands, tested the same way. Two bash bugs found while running, both of the same kind: under set -e+pipefail, a [ cond ] && assignment that is false KILLS the script, and an ls that doesn't match brings down the whole substitution — in a function whose normal case is "found nothing". The repository ROOT wasn't covered by any docmap (the root globs are literal names); the instalador rule is born
documents.s: FASE 29 (session 3) — the installer that doesn't install yet (RN-526, ADR 0150)

documents.t: docker/docker-compose.install.yml is born, GENERATED from the production one and different in three points: the four images come from a mandatory variable (${BRABO_API_IMAGE:?…} — with a default, a missing variable would bring up half the stack with an image nobody chose, and the error would become strange behavior instead of a refusal), no build: survives, and the broker service does NOT exist because its image isn't published (the bake has four targets) — with --source=ghcr, mounted doesn't bring up a container, and the compose SAYS so in the BROKER_URL comment. docker-compose.prod.yml stays intact: it declares itself a VALIDATION compose and is what smoke.sh uses building locally. The cost of the two files is declared and the ceiling is MECHANICAL — composes-em-conformidade.spec.ts fails an extra service/volume/port, a surviving build: and a loosened third-party image. Two things from the plan died on contact with the disk, for opposite reasons: migrate isn't a step (compose chains api→migrate-api with service_completed_successfully, and two places ordering migration would be two sources of the same truth) and the smoke.sh isn't reused (it BUILDS what the installation downloaded by digest, and tears down the stack at the end) — in its place, the installer ASKS before asserting, hitting /health on both
documents.s: FASE 29 (session 4) — the installation comes up from its own compose (RN-527, ADR 0150)

documents.t: Installing over an existing installation isn't offered — either it migrates, or it stops: up over another version's volumes is damage that gives no warning. The order is backup → PROVE → ask → delete → install → restore, and the middle step is what gives the installer the right to delete: a backup nobody tried to restore is a file, and the time to find that out isn't after the down -v. The proof runs test-restore-compose.sh (the SAME three validations of ADR 0152); a backup or proof that fails stops the migration without deleting anything. The destination is a HOST folder — the compose default is the backup_local volume, which down -v would delete ALONG with what one wants to preserve. The Postgres dump is NOT restored on its own over a populated database (it's destructive, and brabo-restore never touches the origin); the local git repos are, because they would be born empty
documents.s: FASE 29 (session 6) — migrating requires a PROVEN backup (RN-530, ADR 0150/0152)

documents.t: The installer asks for the base ONCE and writes it in BOTH places: BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE in .env (server, ADR 0141) and the base field of runner.json (local agent, RN-529) — what differs between mounted and runner is WHO executes, not where the code lives, and two bases for the same folder would be the collision ADR 0141 refused. A refusal in BOTH directions against the checkout, and ~ isn't expanded on purpose (the value goes into a configuration file, where ~ is read literally). The runner binary is checked against the same checksums.txt the script already verified to check itself — downloading it again would be two chances to get different manifests, and the second wouldn't be verified — and installed with install -m 0755. BRB-031 closes here: it survived FASE 28 because the installation didn't come from a versioned artifact, and whoever reached service install had already needed the chmod. A Release without the platform's binary does NOT interrupt the installation
documents.s: FASE 29 (session 7) — one base for both sides, and BRB-031 closes (RN-531, ADR 0150/0151)

documents.t: 8 (RN-532): the workspace_create/_result pair is born in the mold of exec/exec_result, and the confirmation REUSES the workspace_confirm that already exists — no new write route, the engine still doesn't write the table. The predicate is its OWN for a stronger reason than the mirror's: there the third precondition would be circular — a runner project only has a running container after the runner brings it up, and the container comes up ON the folder that this message creates. The workspace capability is the only one whose declaration depends on STATE (consented base), not on the binary's version. 9 (RN-533): the picker goes back to reading the user's disk through fs_list_dir, and the decision NOT to hide the mode without a runner is symmetric to RN-513, not contrary — there the api HAS a signal and without a base the creation ends in 400; here there's no presence signal ( RN-521 already declares it), and hiding would be deciding "doesn't have" from "don't know". Finding: the screen decided by matching the SENTENCE 'Nenhum runner conectado' that lives in an engine .ex — it became a discriminated reason. 10 (RN-534): the install.sh enters the signed checksums.txt (without it the verification it does of ITSELF was a dead letter) and is exercised on a clean machine, with a TTY simulated by script -qec and never by a pipe — the pipe is what kills consent. It does NOT run on PRs, for the same reason as the signature
documents.s: FASE 29 (sessions 8-10) — the protocol, the picker and the E2E (RN-532..534, ADR 0149/0150/0151)

documents.t: RN-529 built the BASE and declared in writing that nothing consumed it. In comes the workspace_create/workspace_create_result pair, in the REQUEST WITH REPLY mold of exec/exec_result — and NEVER in that of workspace_confirm, which is ONE-WAY ({:noreply, socket}, pushes nothing back), a precision that the phase had already recorded along with "workspace.verified does NOT exist". Only the relative SEGMENT crosses the network (the invariant of ADR 0130/0144: whoever has the root is whoever executes), and an ABSOLUTE segment is refused lexically. The confirmation REUSES the workspace_confirm that already existed, and that is what saves a whole front: no new write route is born, the engine still doesn't write the table, and the only path that stamps workspace_verified_at remains a single one — with ORDER as the mechanism (confirm BEFORE the result, because both reach the same channel process in order and the confirm handler is synchronous). The workspace capability enters the vocabulary IN THE SESSION IN WHICH THE CODE COMES IN, on both sides — RN-514 made the opposite bet with espelho and it only paid off because someone demanded it —, and it is the ONLY one of the four whose declaration depends on the STATE of that execution: the runner only declares it with a consented base, and it is through that line, and no other, that the server KNOWS a base exists (the engine doesn't read the user's disk). NOBODY requires it at join, on purpose: requiring it in runner would be breaking/ and MAJOR for a function that project may never use. Its OWN predicate (Engine.Runners.PastaDoProjeto), TWO preconditions, RunnerReadiness byte for byte — and here the third would be worse than unnecessary, it would be CIRCULAR: a runner project only gets a running container after the runner brings it up, and the container comes up on the folder this message exists to create. It also doesn't ask about workspace_verified_at (here that's the RESULT) nor the mode. The TWO preconditions are answered in different places because "consented base" is a property of the CONNECTION (socket.assigns, never a table): the channel refuses BEFORE pushing, with motivo: "sem-base" through the same ref, in the format the module expects — never a timeout. Five named reasons that don't collapse, idempotency with its OWN outcome (ja-era-repositorio is a success), and estado.dir does NOT change. It isn't a proposed_action and no ceiling gets an exception
documents.s: FASE 29 (session 8) — the local agent's base gets a consumer (RN-532, ADR 0151 points 3–6)

documents.t: The backup covered ONE database and ran in ONE place: make test-restore is a Kubernetes path (it requires kubectl, a cluster and the CronJob) and docker-compose.prod.yml had NO backup service at all — migrating a compose installation had no proven path. The decision starts by REFUSING the easy move ("back up all the volumes") and CLASSIFYING the seven: neo4j_data and project_workspaces are derived, ollama_data can be re-obtained, brabo_projects_base is the user's — copying them gives an impression of coverage without adding recovery. The sources of truth are TWO, and the finding is the second: git_local_repos wasn't in any backup, and a project with the local provider keeps its bare repo there — it isn't rebuildable from Postgres (the event log keeps the NARRATIVE, not the git objects), so losing the volume is losing the agents' code. The runbook's prose asserted the opposite ("the real repositories live in GitHub/GitLab") and it is what explains the years without coverage: it holds for github/gitlab, and for local there's no upstream. The file's guarantee is DECLARED and smaller than a "snapshot" — consistency by REFERENCE (git writes objects before moving the ref, and swaps the ref by atomic rename), without a global instant and without git fsck (the image has no git, on purpose); a concurrent gc becomes a FAILURE and not a partial file, with the tar status captured in a FILE because in POSIX sh a pipe's status is that of the last command. The five S3 variables stop being mandatory and become the configuration of ONE destination (BACKUP_DIR chooses disk; absent, S3 — the inference is what keeps the CronJob INTACT). make test-restore-compose triggers a REAL backup and calls the SAME brabo-restore with the SAME three validations: the WRAPPER changes, never the judgment, and deploy/k8s/test-restore.sh stays INTACT (unifying would make the compose one depend on kubectl); restore.sh still doesn't touch the ORIGIN database. Restoring the repos is a SIBLING command (brabo-restore-git, verifies by default, writes only with --restaurar) and not a phase of the other — two artifacts, two judgments, and joining them would make a git failure fail the event log validation. A finding while RUNNING, which reading wouldn't give: the volume is shared by three images with different uids and carries the owner of whoever mounted it first (measured 1000:1000, mode 0755), while the image runs as uid 70 — the extraction died halfway leaving the volume half done; now it refuses BEFORE the tar naming --user 0:0, and what's extracted as root goes back to the DIRECTORY's owner, otherwise the volume would come back intact and USELESS (api and engine, non-root, unable to write to what was just restored). Neo4j gets REPROJECTION and not backup — not built here (BRB-018): a migrated installation is born with the graph EMPTY, a named degradation and not data loss (the RAG lives in pgvector, inside the dump)
documents.s: FASE 29 (session 5) — the backup starts covering what hurts to lose (ADR 0152, RN-528)

documents.t: FASE 29 delivered installing in one line and STOPPED at two points the product itself already declared in writing: the local agent was still paired per PROJECT (whoever wanted to use the installed binary went back to the browser to paste a command into the terminal), and nobody could get in — the generated .env has no email variable, MAIL_TRANSPORT falls to log and registration requires verifying the email, so the way out was fishing the link from docker compose logs api. Both were solved in the same place, and that's what made a single phase. The finding that defined its SIZE came from re-measuring with file:line FASE 29's claim that "one runner per project is enforced in five places": three of the five didn't need to change, because topic, socket id and ticket describe a CONNECTION, and a process that opens N connections — one per project — satisfies them byte for byte, preserving the refusal of a second runner on the same project, which is a real guarantee and not an accident. Nothing in the engine changed in the whole phase, and that's what kept RunnerReadiness, the mirror and workspace_create intact. What remained was what belongs to the PROCESS: the credential (runner_device_keys.project_id becomes nullable, RN-543 — and the listing starts returning the TWO kinds, marked, otherwise a machine key would be invisible and permanent, the defect RN-519 closed, reborn) and the unit (RN-545, service install --machine, one per machine, COEXISTING with the per-project ones). Two decisions contradicted the letter of the ADRs and both were MEASURED: the unit's discriminator is the --machine flag and not the absence of --project (resolverProjeto has two sources, and the normal path is to run install without a flag from inside the folder the browser configured — taken literally, the ADR would silently convert the installation of whoever already uses the product), and install REFUSES when the other kind is already installed, without --force, because the two together would be two processes competing for the same project. Session 6 would touch three workspaces at once and was SPLIT into three, with the two disjoint pieces going out first and install.sh after them, as orchestrator and nothing more. From that split came the phase's most interesting revision: with ZERO connections the agent stopped EXITING and started WAITING, re-querying at 15s/30s/60s (RN-550) — RN-544's argument against re-querying stays whole where it holds (a list that comes back SMALLER is ambiguous, and bringing down a LIVE connection through ambiguity trades a certain state for a guess), and with zero connections there's nothing to bring down; what fell was the exit 0 argument ("an active service that does nothing"), because the process started doing something and SAYING it does. Measured: Restart=on-abnormal doesn't look at the exit code, so no unit changed and the effect is that the machine one is genuinely active (running). The other piece (RN-551) closes "nobody CREATES a machine key" from the agent's side, and the decision there is the CUT: the CLI does not talk to the api, because whoever registers is the installer with the BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN — each side keeps a secret and neither sees the other's. From that follows the two-step design, and from it follows the invariant: the kid IS the registration id and only exists after it, so create writes a .parcial the reader ignores and finish writes the real name — the file the runner reads never exists without a kid, the defect of RN-475 made impossible by construction. The api half (RN-552) declared the cost instead of hiding it: the credential is the service token, and a leaked token can now MANUFACTURE a lasting credential — that's why three containments live in the ROUTE and not in the text (there's no userId in the body; registering REPLACES the owner's active machine keys in the same transaction, so a reinstalled machine passes and a thousand keys are impossible by clause, with no number that ages; and a JWK with d is refused by name). Session 6 (RN-547) chained the five commands and fixed three rules: a middle link that fails undoes nothing, becomes a named line in a final block and the script ALWAYS exits 0 (undoing would require deleting an account and revoking a key, and there's no route for that nor should there be one the installer calls on its own); idempotency is the HTTP CODE, and 409 is an EXPECTED outcome and not a failure, with 000 handled apart so "the api didn't come up" isn't read as "the api refused"; and the password travels through curl's STDIN, never through argv, because /proc/<pid>/cmdline is readable by any user on the machine. A finding of that session: --help had been LYING for months ("THIS VERSION INSTALLS NOTHING") because it prints the header, which is a comment, and the rule forbidding talk of "phase sessions" only read code lines. Session 7 (RN-548) gave the kind marker a consumer, and the decision was one of HONESTY: with a key and without a live connection — the most common case — the screen says the two things it knows and names the two it doesn't (a registered key isn't an agent running, the list belongs to your ACCOUNT and not this browser), accent tone and never success. Session 8 (RN-549) is the only one that could prove the whole, and it EXTENDED the workflow that FASE 29 already had instead of creating a second one. Its central decision is the SIGNAL: perguntarEstado maps activating to rodando — with reason —, so systemctl is-active and service status --machine would give green to a process that's going to die in two seconds; the chosen signal is the LINE the agent writes when entering the wait, which only exists after it has read the key, taken a ticket, talked to the api and received an EMPTY list, and which is a RECORDED FACT and not a sampling of state. The outcome is proven through the API and not the browser, because the subject of the claim is the AGENT and what it observes is GET /runner/projects — a browser would create the project through the same route with one more layer that fails for unrelated reasons, and the assertion would still be the journal line. And the E2E stays OUT of pull_request, with the consequence declared instead of hidden (the PR that wrote it didn't run it): opening that door is giving the installer a way to skip the origin verification, which is what ADR 0150 refuses — hence the half that runs on PRs being a TEST (scripts/dev/install-e2e.spec.ts), guarding the two ways the workflow can rot silently, the loosened gate and the rewritten install.sh sentence (which makes the assertions not fail, but VANISH). Two defects showed up, both invisible because the workflow had never run: the TTY answers started with nao-migrar, which on a clean machine falls into the MARKER question and made the script exit 0 saying "Nothing was written"; and the FINDING that stayed a finding — the published install.sh brings up nothing on its own on a clean machine, because docker/docker-compose.install.yml (with ./postgres/init.sql along) isn't a Release asset, doesn't enter the signed checksums.txt and it doesn't download it anywhere, so whoever follows the runbook's curl … install.sh dies at "no such file or directory" AFTER having already verified the signature and written the .env. Fixing it means deciding between a signed asset and a clone, and it's a delivery of its own. What the phase left DECLARED and not done: revocation still reaches {project, user} and never {key}, and now it costs more (it brings down the agent in ALL the projects of that machine); there's no screen to list and revoke a device key, and the phase added a kind to list without building the screen — the gap became LARGER, on purpose; one process per machine is a single point of failure, the design's price; and install --machine still doesn't know whether the key in that folder really is a machine one, because on disk both kinds are the same file and whoever knows is the server
documents.s: FASE 30 — the machine's local agent (ADRs 0154/0155, RN-543..552, closes in session 8 with RN-549)

documents.t: Two deliveries, one human decision between them. AT-067 had measured that the clock fit in an ubuntu-latest without a GPU and that the instrument didn't measure: since RN-502 the npm test of a container project without a running container is refused, and the seed never brought one up — 0/6 by construction. The maintainer chose "path 1" and AT-076 delivered it: the seed brings up each case's container through the PRODUCTION path (module_map → routing → container_start proposed by Infra and approved by the owner → ExecuteContainerStartUseCase → broker → running through the state machine), with node:24.11.1-bookworm-slim pinned by digest, RN-502 intact, and a container that doesn't come up becoming a NAMED error that fails the ExUnit (before, the body's {:skip, _} passed green silently). Two runs in CI gave 3/6 and 3/6 against the 1/6 floor, with different cases, in 52 and 86 min of job. AT-149 closed the cadence: WEEKLY (Saturday 01:17 UTC, plus workflow_dispatch, never pull_request), in golden-set-qa.yml, in the mold of golden-set-rag.yml. Weekly and not nightly because a run costs up to 86 min and VARIES — the same total through different cases —, and once a week is enough for the floor to flag a drop. timeout-minutes: 150 for the worst measured case. The verdict is the test's own; the workflow adds only two INSTRUMENT guards (the score line must exist, and the event log can't have an RN-502 refusal) and, on failure, prints the logs like the RAG one — no issue. The image to pull before the seed is READ from the seed's constant, never from a second literal, because the broker's docker run runs under the 30 s control ceiling (RN-604). The proof run, with a temporary push trigger removed before the PR, was 36327281774: 3/6 again, zero RN-502 refusals, 10 min of mix golden_set.qa and 13 min 41 s of job. Declared: the CI broker doesn't have the compose's five layers, the heartbeat closes the seed's sessions while QA is still working on them (with no visible effect), and a PR that touches the workflow doesn't run it.
documents.s: The QA golden set measures again and runs on a schedule, weekly (AT-076/AT-149, ADR 0168)

documents.t: RN-584 (AT-098) removed the chat's default recipient and left the product question in writing: does the Infra Lead converse? The maintainer said yes on 2026-09-27, with the condition RN-584 itself had set — the turn first. The Infra Lead's turn ran ENTIRELY inside handle_call/handle_cast: without acceptance, without "Stop", outside TurnoOrfao, with the loop's 14th step ending silently and a 180 s ceiling smaller than the 225 s of the container propose_action (RN-605). The kickoff, being a cast, didn't hold a click, but it held the process — 8.4 min measured in AT-089 —, and a message in the meantime would wait in the queue. Stage 1 put the three turns (kickoff, gate correction, message) into TurnoAssincrono, with the Workflows consolidation inside the Task; a gate correction arriving with a turn in progress got a queue, because TurnoAssincrono without from would discard it. Stage 2 gave infra the message/2 clause (the agente_sem_conversa refusal went away), the via_for of "Stop" and a place in AGENTES_DE_CHAT; the acceptance of its handoff stayed in RN-499's own card, and the thread card excludes it by name. SOLO_CONVERSATIONAL_AGENTS didn't change: the Infra Lead is an area lead. Declared: it didn't get structured questions nor backlog reading.
documents.s: The Infra Lead converses through the composer (AT-141, ADR 0175, RN-617)

documents.t: 2026-10-01, round 36. RN-558 had closed the SILENCE half — the authenticated git fetch in runner mode, with the container up, stopped running with empty variables and started being refused with the mark credencial-nao-atravessa-o-container — and declared the other half as a pending ADR, because every known option touched the containment port of ADR 0130. The owner's decision (01/10) chose the one that doesn't touch it: credentialed git operation on the HOST, code in the container. Measured before: the engine's only exec with env was RunnerGit.fetch!/3's fetch; there was no credentialed push nor clone through exec (the folder-creation clone already ran on the host, RN-532); and the folder is the same on both sides (estado.dir mounted at /work). The chosen discriminator was an explicit MARK from the engine (gitCredenciado: true, set only by RunnerRouter.exec_git_credenciado/5), and not the env that already existed — with env as the key, any command with env would escape the container. RN-558's refusal survived shrunk, for env without the mark, and in practice came to mean "runner older than ADR 0193". The proof is AT-111, on both sides: on the runner, a real git credential fill and git fetch origin with GitAuth's helper succeed on the host with the container active; on the engine, the chain through the real TerminalChannel ends in {:ok, _}. The ExUnit tests didn't run in the delivery environment (repo.hex.pm 403) and were left for CI.
documents.s: Credentialed git runs on the runner's host, the code in the container (AT-116, ADR 0193, RN-676)

documents.t: 2026-10-01, round 36. In the real use of 29/09 a consultative session without an agent answered "I don't have access to previous conversations": the message without a recipient went to the SSE of POST .../chat, which sends the bound model only the current text — no history, no system prompt — and writes the reply with the model's name as the actor. The owner's decision (01/10) was to ask for an agent instead of giving history to the free chat. Measured before: the screen was the only client of the route (the curl printed by the seed is a development hint, in a creative session), and the SendChatMessageUseCase use case had a second legitimate consumer, the provider smokes, which use it as an end-to-end instrument in a session without an agent. That's why the api's refusal lives in the ROUTE, in its own guard, and the use case stayed intact. On the screen, the recipient line started carrying the manual handoff's own selector when there's no agent — the same usual gesture, now in the place where it is the only way for the message to have a destination —, and the Criativo stayed off the list because the consultative session promises it doesn't come in.
documents.s: The consultative session without an agent asks for an agent (AT-254, RN-682)

documents.t: 2026-10-01, round 36. RN-520 had made revocation reach the live connection, with the {project, user} target because the credential's identity died in PatAuthGuard; ADR 0154 put "revocation by key" among what it didn't do, and PR #534 gave the machine key the same pair applied project by project. AT-013 stayed blocked by scope and by decision until the owner chose (01/10): by KEY, with an ADR, touching the engine. Measured before: the ticket was born from {userId, kind}, the socket kept only project/user/kind, and the channel compared the user — the same user's runner with a PAT or another key fell along; the machine key's connection in a project outside the api's list stayed up; a ticket issued before the revocation got in after it; and revoking a PAT brought down nothing. Delivered: two nullable columns in the ticket (an Ecto migration, the table is the engine's — Drizzle's journal stayed at 0068), the guard annotating the credential after authorizing, the socket id gaining the kind and id of the credential, and a runner/disconnect-credential route that voids the pending tickets and asks every runner in the cluster whether it was born from it. The AT-013 prohibition (not ceasing to bring down what used to fall) became two transition pieces: the legacy connection falls through the pair in the row's projects, and an engine without the route makes the api go back to the pair. The pair stayed as the target of member removal. The screen changed only the confirmation text (RN-561). The runner didn't change. The ExUnit tests didn't run in the delivery environment (repo.hex.pm 403) and were left for CI.

documents.t: Brabo speaks four languages in the documentation and in the interface, and Brazilian Portuguese is the source and the default of both products (ADR 0216). All new text is born in pt-BR; the other languages are translations of it.
documents.s: Localization

documents.t: language code plural forms (Intl.PluralRules) note Português (Brasil) pt-BR one, many, other (+ mandatory _zero in the interface) source English en one, other English notes Русский ru one, few, many, other Russian notes 简体中文 zh-Hans other Chinese notes The codes are the same in Docusaurus, in i18next, in <html lang> and in users.locale. The site's local search uses its own (pt, en, ru, zh). On the site, the language selector sits in the top bar (localeDropdown in website/docusaurus.config.ts), with the labels above, and takes you to the same page in the chosen language; each language lives under its own path (/en/, /ru/, /zh-Hans/; pt-BR at the root of the stage).
documents.s: Languages and codes

documents.t: The choice saved in the account always wins and is never overwritten by detection. Without a choice, the browser language suggests (resolverIdiomaDoNavegador, apps/web/src/lib/idioma.ts): pt* → pt-BR; zh, zh-CN, zh-SG and zh-Hans* → zh-Hans; ru* → ru; en* → en; anything else — German, traditional Chinese (zh-TW, zh-Hant) — → pt-BR. The language of the agents' REPLIES is another preference, with its own mechanism (ADR 0177), and does not depend on the interface language.
documents.s: Resolving the interface language

documents.t: On the site, a page without a translation in a locale is served from the pt-BR source, at the same address, and a banner at the top SAYS so in the reader's language. A translated page whose source changed after the translation states the translation date and that the original changed. In the interface, text is never missing: key and plural parity is measured, and fallbackLng is pt-BR. Every translated page carries traducao_de: <SHA> in its frontmatter — the last commit of the source it translates. That is what separates "up to date" from "stale". Today's measurement is in Translation parity, generated by pnpm docs:generate. The Reference sidebar labels and the top bar labels come from website/sidebars.ts and each locale's navbar.json/current.json; since ADR 0219 the content of the reference/ pages is translated too, generated block included, and only the parity page stays out.

documents.t: AT-160 (EP-028, HS-053). The heuristic being measured is the one the AT-080 specification proposed ("A — own heuristic, no dependency"). Since AT-163 (RN-624) the product runs it: the api detects the author's language with it and ASKS before anything changes. The product's thresholds are provisional — see The product's provisional thresholds.
documents.s: Measuring the language heuristic

documents.t: The instrument lives in scripts/idioma/ and runs with the repository's Node (type stripping, no build step). No new dependency: the heuristic is marker lists and regular expressions, and the extraction talks to Postgres through psql inside the database container. The heuristic itself lives in the api — apps/api/src/domain/iam/heuristica-de-idioma.ts — and scripts/idioma/heuristica.ts only re-exports it, so the instrument measures exactly the code the product runs. That direction is forced: the api reaches neither scripts/ nor any runtime package without a build step, and packages/shared is types only. The file has no imports, so Node runs it from scripts/ by type stripping (the idioma:* commands silence the "typeless package" warning that comes with it), and scripts/idioma/ has its own tsconfig.json — the only difference is turning verbatimModuleSyntax off, which rejects every export of a CommonJS module such as the api's. A .mts file was tried first: it passed both typechecks and the build, and broke every ts-node script of the api. The rule of what is evidence (evidenciasDoAutor) moved with the heuristic, and the real-corpus extraction uses the same one. file role heuristica.ts re-exports the api's heuristic: cleaning, contrastive scoring, the candidate and the provisional parameters, the 10-message sample, the hysteresis and the evidence rule corpus-sintetico.jsonl the versioned synthetic corpus — every line hand-written for the instrument, origem: "sintetico" sequencias-sinteticas.json synthetic conversations for the sample-and-hysteresis path medicao.ts / medir.ts the instrument and its CLI extrair.ts extracts the real corpus from the local event log, to a file outside git rotular.ts assisted labeling of the real corpus, in the terminal
documents.s: What exists

documents.t: The maintainer's decision (AT-168, answer 5) is real + synthetic. They have opposite storage rules: Synthetic — versioned, reviewed like code. It covers the nine mandatory cases of AT-080 (typos, legitimate Spanish, English, mixed text, "ok", code, logs, quotations in another language) plus Portuguese full of English jargon, inline identifiers, and languages outside the three (French, Italian, German, Galician, Catalan, Dutch) — the language list is open (AT-168, answer 2). Real — the user's own messages from the local event log. It never enters git, a fixture, a CI log or a PR body. extrair.ts and corpus.ts refuse any destination inside the checkout, and the file is written with mode 600 under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/brabo/corpus-idioma/ (else ~/.cache/…). The report never prints an item's text — only ids, labels and counts — so its output can be pasted into a PR. What the extraction takes as evidence follows the AT-080 cleaning: only events whose actor is the user (the agent's reply is never evidence, so a Spanish answer from the model cannot feed the detection back), and, for the structured form, only the answers — the concatenated chat.message the api writes right after it, whose labels are the agent's text, is skipped. The labeling assistant does not pre-fill the heuristic's guess: accepting it with ENTER would anchor the label on the thing the label exists to measure. ENTER accepts the language the owner declares with --padrao. Labels: a BCP-47 code (pt-BR, es, fr…), und (nothing to decide: "ok", only code, only a log) or mul (mixed, no dominant language). Scoring: pt/es/en must get their own language; und, mul and any other language must get indeterminado — the only correct answer a three-language heuristic can give them. An indeterminado on a decidable item is lost coverage (the known preference stays); a wrong language is an error, and falso es is counted apart because it is the defect the epic exists to remove.
documents.s: The two corpora, and where each one lives

documents.t: # synthetic corpus (the default) pnpm --filter @brabo/scripts idioma:medir # the owner's real corpus, on the owner's machine pnpm --filter @brabo/scripts idioma:extrair --container brabo-dev-postgres-1 pnpm --filter @brabo/scripts idioma:rotular --padrao pt-BR pnpm --filter @brabo/scripts idioma:medir --real --container runs psql inside that container with one read-only SELECT on session_events (--usuario/--banco default to the compose's brabo/brabo); --database-url <url> uses a host psql instead. Re-running the extraction keeps existing labels and appends new messages unlabeled.
documents.s: Running it

documents.t: 123 labeled items, 7 sequences, candidate parameters of AT-080 (20-word minimum, threshold 0.8, margin 0.3, 10 messages / 2,000 characters, hysteresis 2). Two marker lists: at080 is the specification's list verbatim; ampliada is a larger list written by this instrument before it was run against the corpus (frequent function words absent from the other two languages). Same corpus, so ampliada is not validated by these numbers — the real corpus is what can tell. Per message, candidate parameters: label n at080 correct at080 indeterminate ampliada correct ampliada indeterminate pt 56 26 (46.4%) 30 30 (53.6%) 26 es 20 6 (30.0%) 14 7 (35.0%) 13 en 14 6 (42.9%) 8 6 (42.9%) 8 und 15 15 (100%) 0 15 (100%) 0 mul 5 5 (100%) 0 5 (100%) 0 other languages 13 10 0 9 0 Wrong-language verdicts: none on a pt/es/en item, in either list. All of them are on languages outside the three — at080: French → pt (the ê of arrêté), Galician → es (the one falso es), Dutch → en; ampliada: French → es, German → pt and → en, Dutch → en. The cleaning removed more than half of the words of zero decidable items. All seven synthetic sequences end where expected with at most the allowed number of switches, in both lists — including Portuguese with a long Spanish quotation, one whole Spanish message in the middle of Portuguese, and Portuguese dense with English jargon. CPU on this machine: at080 11.7 µs per message and 49 µs per evaluation of the 10-message sample; ampliada 16.8 µs and 60 µs. It varies with the machine; the order of magnitude is the point.
documents.s: Numbers on the synthetic corpus (2026-09-28)

documents.t: With the at080 list, the threshold and the margin never bind. 66 of the 67 items that score at all score for one language only (confidence = 1.0), so sweeping the threshold from 0.5 to 1.0 changes nothing. The word minimum is the only knob that acts: per message, decidable items reach their language 42.2% of the time at 20 words, 58.9% at 10 and 66.7% with no minimum — at 20 it throws away every short and typo message and most of the technical ones. Dropping the minimum lets mixed text decide. With no minimum, at080 turns three of the five mixed messages into en or pt, and ampliada also decides two und items as en — unfenced code (const total = itens.reduce(…)) and pnpm output (ELIFECYCLE Test failed. See above for more details.) pass the cleaning, which only knows fenced code and the log shapes AT-080 listed. The margin of 0.3 is redundant with the threshold of 0.8 in any list: with three languages, a winner at ≥ 0.8 is at least 0.6 above the second. The unit that matters is the sample, not the message — in the sequences the 10-message window reaches the language with messages that alone would be indeterminado. A single Spanish message in a Portuguese window turns the sample indeterminado for as long as it stays in the window (sequence q03): no switch, but no confirmation either. The open language list is where the errors are. With three languages, a Galician or French user can be told they write Spanish or Portuguese. Under the AT-168 rule the detection only asks, and the user confirms, so the cost is a wrong question — but it is still the heuristic's only failure mode here. These are synthetic numbers: the corpus was written by the same hand that wrote the heuristic. The thresholds of AT-163 should come from the real corpus.
documents.s: What the numbers say

documents.t: AT-163 had to ship with some numbers before the real corpus exists, so the api reads PARAMETROS_PROVISORIOS — provisional, not calibrated, and declared so in RN-624: parameter provisional AT-080 candidate why marker list at080 — ampliada gains 4 points in pt and gets German wrong twice; neither is validated by real data word minimum (over the sample) 10 20 coverage of decidable items 42.2% → 58.9% with the same three wrong verdicts (French, Galician, Dutch — languages outside the three); below 10, mixed text starts to decide threshold / margin 0.8 / 0.3 0.8 / 0.3 they never bind on the synthetic corpus, so there is no better number to pick yet sample 10 messages / 2,000 characters same — hysteresis 2 2 — The hysteresis is recomputed, never stored: the api reads the last 11 pieces of evidence and asks whether the last two evaluations of the sample agree. CPU on this machine, synthetic corpus: 11.6 µs to clean and classify one message, 110 µs per detection (11 messages, two evaluations). The read is served by a partial index on session_events: 0.056 ms against 13.5 ms for a sequential scan, measured over 200,000 events. To recalibrate: run the real corpus (idioma:medir --real), then change PARAMETROS_PROVISORIOS in the api — it is the only place the product reads them from, and the instrument imports the same file (its report still sweeps the AT-080 candidates).
documents.s: The product's provisional thresholds

documents.t: The protocol is AT-082's, with the decisions of AT-169: budget US$ 5, 5 rounds per case and arm, acceptance threshold "in the treated arm, zero Spanish answers where pt-BR is expected, and correct language ≥ 95% in C01–C04 and C06–C15", model under test deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash, comparison model anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5, incremental cost ceiling 50 input tokens per call. Code at d48f99f8e (the dev of 2026-09-29).
documents.s: Paid validation of the language orientation (AT-167, 2026-09-29)

documents.t: A script outside the product, scripts/idioma/validar.ts (the pure part — matrix, judging, report — in validacao.ts, tested by validacao.spec.ts). It calls OpenRouter directly and writes nothing to the database. What the product sends to the model is read from the product's files at every run, never copied — the read throws, naming what it missed, if a file changes shape: the orientation (RN-622/623): @textos, the generic sentence, the artifact clause, @forma_curta and @ferramentas_de_artefato of apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/idioma_da_resposta.ex, sent as the LAST message, role: "system", in every call of a treated turn (tool iterations included) and never kept in the history; the summary prompt and its language sentence (RN-621) of apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/context_manager.ex; the Criativo persona (CRIATIVO_INSTRUCTIONS), its two tools with the real descriptions, and the tool results the product returns. Declared differences from the product: the system prompt is only the persona (no ContextBuilder layers); compaction is forced before the fifth turn of C04 (keeping the last two messages, the product's keep_recent), with the model under test as summarizer; resumption (C15) is the history rebuilt as text, the shape of Engine.Agents.Reidratacao; at most 4 model calls per turn (the Criativo allows 12); and max_tokens is capped at 4000 (the product sends none). The upstream provider was not fixed — recorded per call as a confounder. Baseline = the code before RN-621/622: no orientation and the old summary prompt (AT-169 answer 4: the validation measures the set, there is no isolated baseline of the old summary). The resolved language of each message's author is part of the case: pt-BR for Ana (C01–C05, C07–C11, C13–C15), en for Bob (C06 as a confirmed detected en, C12 as an explicit en preference writing Portuguese); project language pt-BR. C05 expects pt-BR: under AT-168 answer 4 detection only asks, so the author's resolved language stays pt-BR until confirmed. A first passo-zero run with max_tokens 1000 was discarded: DeepSeek's reasoning used the whole cap in 7 calls and the answer came back empty (two summaries became the product's fallback text). Its records are kept apart in the output folder; an empty answer now counts as falha, never indeterminado.
documents.s: Where it runs, and what is (and is not) the product

documents.t: Baseline only, deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash, C01–C04, 5 rounds: 0 Spanish answers in 35 judged answers (35 pt, 0 indeterminate). The 13/09 report (Spanish from Portuguese input) is not reproduced, so no improvement on that defect can be claimed from the treatment. The run continued because the AT-169 threshold is absolute on the treated arm and the other cases (C05, C06, C12, C16, C17) do show the baseline answering in the wrong language.

documents.s: Results by case × arm × model

documents.t: model Spanish where pt-BR expected (treated) correct in C01–C04, C06–C15 (strict, classifier) verdict by the classifier deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash 0 82/95 (86.3%), 8 indeterminate does not pass anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5 3 (all C05) 81/95 (85.3%), 0 indeterminate does not pass The 13 DeepSeek misses are two groups. The reading below was the agent's, made BEFORE the review; the review (next section) corrected it — the 8 indeterminates are not all English prose: the 8 indeterminates (C06 ×2, C12 ×6) read as English prose — the ampliada list scores English poorly ("Great starting point — …"); the 5 C11 misses answer the translation request with the English translation inside a Portuguese frame, which the orientation allows ("unless the user explicitly asks … in this message" covers the translation, not the frame). The protocol's "translation in en" does not say which of the two is right. If the review accepts both groups, DeepSeek reaches 95/95 and passes; if it rejects C11, 90/95 (94.7%) and fails by one answer. Haiku fails either way: with the explicit en preference and Portuguese messages (C12) it answered in Portuguese in 10 of 10 treated answers, and it answered 3 of 5 Spanish messages in Spanish (C05). A hypothesis, not measured: for Anthropic models OpenRouter lifts the trailing system message into the top system prompt, where it loses the recency it has at the end of the list. (Measured afterwards, and not confirmed: see the diagnosis below.) The answers to review (every indeterminate or divergent one, every C11 translation, and a deterministic 1-in-10 sample of the concordant) are 146 of 560, listed in revisao.md in the output folder.
documents.s: Against the threshold

documents.t: Paired prompt_tokens of the first call of each conversation (identical input in both arms but the orientation), from OpenRouter's usage, never an estimate: model orientation pairs Δ input tokens DeepSeek pt-BR (108 characters) 75 32 (every pair) DeepSeek en + artifact clause (128 characters) 15 27 Haiku pt-BR 75 30 Haiku en + artifact clause 15 27 All under the 50-token ceiling. At catalog input price that is about US$ 0.0000096 per call on DeepSeek and US$ 0.00003 on Haiku — an upper bound, since DeepSeek served most of the input from cache (cached tokens are returned; the per-call cost with cache is inside usage.cost, not separated per message). The orientation goes in every call of a turn, so a turn with tool iterations pays it once per iteration.
documents.s: Incremental cost of the orientation

documents.t: The cost of the validation is the sum of usage.cost of each response, kept per call in chamadas.jsonl: US$ 2.3071 in total — US$ 2.2629 in the counted runs (DeepSeek 0.1526 baseline + 0.2133 treatment; Haiku 0.9526 + 0.9443; 865 calls), US$ 0.0281 in the discarded step zero and US$ 0.0162 in a one-case smoke. The GET /api/v1/key counter moved from 1.8301 to 4.1578 (Δ 2.3277) over the same period, but the key is shared with other paid lanes running at the same time and the counter lags, so that delta is context, not this validation's spend. Generation ids were not recorded, so the per-call cost was not cross-checked against GET /api/v1/generation. The product's own metering (token_usage) was not involved: the script bypasses the api.

documents.t: Two offline-or-cheap follow-ups to the paid validation, both on the same run (respostas.jsonl, 560 judged answers): the human review of the 146 answers the classifier flagged (Part A, no spend), and the test of the "OpenRouter hoists the trailing system message" hypothesis for Haiku (Part B, US$ 0.1485). Neither changes the product.
documents.s: Human review and the Haiku diagnosis (AT-167 follow-up)

documents.t: Every one of the 146 answers in revisao.md was read, one by one, by the agent that wrote this section (not by a second human; the label file is kept for anyone who wants to contradict it). For each: the real language of the text the user reads, whether it is correct for the case, and a one-line reason. The files live outside git with the answers — ~/.cache/brabo/validacao-idioma/2026-09-29/revisao-feita.md (the 146) and amostra-lida.md (the sample below). pnpm --filter @brabo/scripts idioma:revisar reads them and prints every table of this section; the labels are data, the arithmetic is code (scripts/idioma/revisao.ts, tested). The labels are four, because the reading found a fact the classifier cannot see: sim / nao: the answer is / is not in the expected language; formulario: the prose is in the expected language, but the questions of the structured form (ask_structured_questions, the substance of a first answer) came out in Portuguese for an author whose language is en; c11: a translation into English inside a Portuguese frame — the owner's decision, see below. of the 146 correct incorrect prose right, form in Portuguese C11 (owner's decision) all 42 81 8 15 baseline arm (89) 18 64 1 6 treated arm (57) 24 17 7 9 The 14 answers the classifier called indeterminate were, once read: 3 English answers (Haiku's plain English translations of C11), 2 incorrect (DeepSeek C12, Portuguese and English sentences interleaved in the prose), 8 English prose with the form in Portuguese, and 1 C11. So the agent's earlier sentence — "the 8 indeterminates read as English prose" — was half right: the prose was English, and so was not the form in 6 of the 8. The classifier's error, measured. On the 118 definitive verdicts (pt/es/en) among the 146 read answers, the reading contradicted 0. The classifier never called an answer right that was wrong, nor wrong that was right; its only failures are the 3 "indeterminate" that were plain English. For the 414 answers that were not flagged (all concordant with the expectation), a sample was read: 60 drawn with random.Random(20260929).sample(range(414), 60) over the answers in respostas.jsonl order, plus the 14 unflagged C06/C12 answers with expected en that the draw missed (they decide the threshold, so they were read whole) — 74 read, 0 divergent (Wilson 95% upper bound 4.9%). Together with the 39 concordant answers that the 1-in-10 hash had already flagged and were read too, the random part is 0 in 99 (upper bound 3.7%): at most ~15 of the 414 could be wrong, and the sample suggests none. Two slips seen in the sample are one-word insertions ("What falta for us…", "reminders automáticos") that do not change the language of the answer. What the classifier cannot see is the form: clf=en on an English answer did not tell that its questions were in Portuguese (it flagged those answers as indeterminate only when the mix was heavy). That is why the sample read the C06/C12 answers whole, and why the two readings below exist.
documents.s: Part A — the review of the 146

documents.t: Treated arm, C01–C04 and C06–C15 (n = 95), Spanish counted on the real language of every treated answer where pt-BR is expected (C05 included). Wilson 95% interval. Two independent readings: C11 (the owner's, open) and form (prose right, form in Portuguese — the agent resolved it as a fact about what the user reads, and shows the other side so it can be contradicted). model C11 counts form counts hits rate 95% interval Spanish (pt expected) verdict DeepSeek yes yes 93/95 97.9% 92.6–99.4% 0 passes DeepSeek yes no 87/95 91.6% 84.3–95.7% 0 does not pass DeepSeek no yes 88/95 92.6% 85.6–96.4% 0 does not pass DeepSeek no no 82/95 86.3% 78.0–91.8% 0 does not pass Haiku yes (any) 85/95 89.5% 81.7–94.2% 3 (C05) does not pass Haiku no (any) 81/95 85.3% 76.8–91.0% 3 (C05) does not pass The pass threshold is 91 hits of 95 (94.7% fails). Reading the table: Haiku fails in every reading: 3 Spanish answers in C05 (the zero-Spanish clause alone) and, with everything accepted, 85/95. DeepSeek passes in exactly one cell: C11 accepted and English prose with a Portuguese form accepted. Reject either one and it fails — by 4 answers if the form is rejected (87 of the 91 needed), by 3 if C11 is (88). Reject both and it is the classifier's number, 82. The C11 decision therefore only matters if the form is accepted. With the form counted as a miss, DeepSeek fails whatever C11 is, and the finding to act on is not C11 but the form: in the treated arm, 8 of DeepSeek's 15 C06+C12 answers carry Portuguese text inside an English answer (6 form-only, 2 interleaved), while 7 are clean English, forms included. The model can write the form in English — it does so about half of the time. Where it came from (AT-282, RN-667): the tool's own description told the model the label was "o texto da pergunta, em pt-BR" — a second, fixed language instruction outside the facade, competing with the trailing orientation in every call. It now says "no idioma da sua resposta" and names no language; the orientation itself is unchanged. The after-measurement was not run (no OpenRouter key on the machine that made the change) and is pending the owner — C06 and C12, treated arm, 5 rounds, with the budget cap in the RN. What C11 is, in the data. DeepSeek's 5 treated misses: 3 have the English translation quoted in a Portuguese frame ("Registrei a regra… A tradução que você pediu: > …"), and 2 have no translation in the recorded text — the run keeps only the last message of a turn, and these turns called emit_artifact first, so the translation was in an earlier message of the same turn (10 calls for 5 conversations, two per conversation), so the translation was presumably in an earlier message of the same turn, and was not kept. Both are counted as frame-only, i.e. as hits under "C11 counts". Haiku's 4 treated misses are an English translation with a Portuguese note or Portuguese alternatives around it. TODO(humano): Does a translation into English inside a Portuguese frame count as correct in C11? It decides the C11 axis of the table above: accepted → DeepSeek 93/95 and passes (if English prose with a Portuguese form is also accepted; 87/95 if not); rejected → DeepSeek 88/95 (or 82/95) and fails. Haiku fails either way. Recommendation, in one sentence: accept it — the orientation's exception covers only the requested translation and the frame stays in the author's language, so rejecting it would penalise exactly the behaviour the orientation is meant to produce. (The second question, the form in Portuguese, is a product-scope question and is stated as a finding above; it was not put to the owner because the agent resolved it as a fact — what the user reads.)
